result.strongestDefect: L-19 — the "Prune empty" confirmation dialog names a count computed from a ≤50-row client page while the endpoint it authorises deletes every empty user in the corpus. Chain, fully quoted: useAdminUsers.ts:59 fetches listUsers(token, 50) and discards res.total (PaginatedResponse.total, types.ts:127) → AdminPane.vue:33 passes the page's .length as :total-users → AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 computes emptyCount from that array → :289-291 renders "Prune {N} empty users? This will permanently delete {N} users … This cannot be undone." → api/admin-users.ts:69 POSTs /admin/users/prune-empty with no body → api/src/modules/admin/service/users.ts:232 findEmptyUserSlugs() over the whole collection and deleteMany(slugs) in one transaction → AdminUsersPanel.vue:303-308 then prints the SERVER's count back. With 400 users of which 137 are empty and 3 fall in the first 50, the admin confirms "3" and loses 137 users plus every one of their sessions, unrecoverably. This is a library-structure defect in the exact sense the seat exists to find: the panel is not wrong to render emptyCount, it is wrong to POSSESS it, and it possesses it because a typed pagination contract is thrown away one module below the component. L-1 (the inverted composable→SFC dependency, now measured at four madge cycles) is the strongest purely structural defect, and L-24 is why it survived four passes: no import/no-cycle, no madge installed, and boundary lint rules aimed at a directory deleted at W43.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but four things on this axis are SOUND and were proved, not assumed — recorded so no wave wastes effort re-auditing them. (1) THE PUBLISHED SURFACE IS DOGFOODED HONESTLY. `grep -rEoh "from \"(@mkbabb/value\.js[^\"]*|\.\./+src/[^\"]*|/src/[^\"]*)\"" demo --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts" | sort | uniq -c` → 24 @mkbabb/value.js/color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize; ZERO relative ../src/ reaches, ZERO @src/* reaches, ZERO bare-root-barrel reaches. Cross-checked against `node -e "Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports)"` → ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize — every specifier used is a published subpath. The Vite self-alias set is GENERATED from package.json#exports with anchored regexes (vite.config.ts:37-50), so it is structurally incapable of resolving a specifier a real consumer could not write. AdminUsersPanel imports value.js not at all. This is the fourth consecutive pass to reach that conclusion by an independent instrument. (2) THE API/TRANSPORT LAYER IS CORRECTLY SHAPED — demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts takes the token as a parameter, delegates to one adminRequest, and PUBLISHES the pagination and search contract (limit/offset/q/total) that the layer above discards. The L-19/L-20 rot is entirely in the composable; do not send a fix into api/. (3) THE BARRELS THAT EXIST ARE CORRECTLY FORMED — browser/index.ts, browser/admin/index.ts, browser/card/index.ts are named re-exports per PI-6 with the SFC-scoped-style tree-shake rationale stated in-file. The seam FORM is right; only its enforcement (L-15), coverage (shared/ui has no barrel) and membership (L-21) fail. (4) NO RUNTIME CYCLE EXISTS — the offending edge (useAdminUsers.ts:14) is `import type` and verbatimModuleSyntax erases it, so the four madge cycles are type-graph and ownership cycles, not boot-order bugs; stated explicitly so the cure is not mis-scoped. Also sound and checked: import type discipline in the subject (:199 is the only type-only import and is correct; SAFE_ACCENT_KEY/ADMIN_PORT_KEY are runtime Symbols, correctly value-imported); Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure with a default at :205-220 (edict 7); vj-celebrate is tokenized in demo/styles/animations.css:142-165, nothing deleted or inlined (edict 6); Badge variant="secondary" at :102 IS valid (glass-ui Badge declares variant, unlike Button — a mechanical variant sweep touching Badge would be a regression); the role="button" disclosure row's `target === currentTarget` guard at :345 is load-bearing and correct; and no a11y finding is filed — all four Safari matrices report pageErr 0 / consoleErr 0 / overflowX 0 / main 1 on /#/admin/users with the 4 small tap targets all in the dock, and the MT-F022 two-engine keyboard delta is confirmed out of scope for this axis.

result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier declared at spawn. Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-34 — PaletteCard's Export→SVG menu action emits an unescaped, attacker-shaped SVG document (reproduced live: a colour string broke out of `fill=` into an `onload=` attribute, a palette name injected a full-canvas `<rect>`), because the concept "serialize a palette to a document" has two homes and the wrong one won the wiring. The correct home — `demo/palettes/export/` (contract-governed, ships `xmlEscape` + `canonicalColor`, the feature's only `@mkbabb/value.js` export edge) — is imported by nothing but `demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts`, whose green test literally reads "escapes the display name and never renders text/font/script". A green gate certifying code the product does not load.

defects.defect: The card's Export→SVG writes attacker-controlled markup into a downloadable document, because the escaping implementation lives in the app-dead contract module. Two live implementations of palette serialization: `demo/palettes/export.ts` (wired to the card menu via usePaletteExport) interpolates `c.css` and `palette.name` into SVG with no escaper; `demo/palettes/export/` (12 files, PALETTE-CONTRACT Appendix W51, ships xmlEscape + canonicalColor + the only value.js edge) is imported only by the test suite.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/export.ts:66-67 (`fill="${c.css}"`) and :73 (`<text …>${palette.name}</text>`) — no escaper anywhere in the file. Correct home: demo/palettes/export/svg.ts:16,19 uses `xmlEscape(...)`. Consumer census: `grep -rn "usePaletteExport|export/serializers" demo` → BrowsePane.vue:198, PalettesPane.vue:152 (legacy), demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23 (contract) — ZERO app consumers of the contract path. Green test asserting the cure: demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:187 `it("escapes the display name and never renders text/font/script")`. Live output measured (probe-L4b.mjs): `{"escaped": false, "injectedElementCount": 3, "rawColorAttrPresent": true}`; emitted file contains `<rect x="0" y="0" width="60" height="80" fill="#ff6b6b" onload="0" />` and `…fill="#333">Ridge</text><rect x="0" y="0" width="999" height="999" fill="#f0f"/><text></text>`. Artifact: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/evidence/L4b-ridge-text-rect-x-0-y-0-width-999-height-999-fill-f0f-text.svg
defects.mechanism: dual-path / unique-semantic-ownership violation — one concept, two homes, the unsafe home wired and the safe home unreachable; the test suite's greenness conceals it
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/probe-L4b.mjs — seeds one local palette named `Ridge</text><rect x="0" y="0" width="999" height="999" fill="#f0f"/><text>` with colour `#ff6b6b" onload="0`, drives PaletteCard's own menu → Export → SVG Swatch on http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, reads the downloaded file back. defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/palettes/export.ts and demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts outright; rename demo/palettes/export/serializers.ts → index.ts (the header's stated reason for the odd name dies with the legacy module); route the card's five export actions through the contracted serializers. Do NOT add an escaper to export.ts — that preserves two homes for one concept, which is the actual defect.

defects.defect: The interaction register PaletteCard's root comment claims (`the cartoon-surface atom owns the hover/press choreography`) is measurably absent — zero computed-style change on hover — and the producer's own typed documentation says it was never there. Owner mark MT-F036 (missing hover), root-caused to glass-ui.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:7-15 claims the register. The WHOLE of the utility, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css:1: `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }` — no :hover, no :active, no transition. `grep -rno "data-cartoon" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/**/*.css` → no matches. Producer typing, dist/components/card/Card.vue.d.ts: `/** Static Memphis edge treatment; it does not add command behavior. */ cartoon?: boolean;`. MEASURED live (probe-L4.mjs §A, WebKit, computed style at rest vs during hover() over boxShadow/translate/scale/transform/borderColor/backgroundColor/filter/opacity): `"hoverDelta": {}`. Press works only via inline JS: `"pressDelta": {"scale": {"rest": "none", "press": "1.0091 0.9512"}}`. Witnesses: audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-11, OM-12.
defects.mechanism: string-coupling to a design-system internal — the class name was copied into the template as a literal, so when glass-ui 7.0.0 shipped it decoration-only nothing failed loudly and the migration comment kept asserting a register that does not exist
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/probe-L4.mjs — section A_rootRegister, field hoverDelta
defects.proposedCure: BJ ask (never a local patch, per owner law): seat an interaction register on glass-ui's `Card` — e.g. `<Card interactive>` — carrying hover lift + shadow step + :active squash on producer easing tokens, composable with `cartoon` and every material/tier. glass-ui already ships `.hover-lift{,-md,-lg}` (dist/styles/utilities/components.css); the ask is to seat that register on Card so consumers stop hand-rolling it. Demo companion: adopt `<Card cartoon material="well" as="div">` in place of the hand-rolled root.

defects.defect: The hard-edged faceted shadow slab is three ZERO-BLUR producer shadow layers, and the demo hand-rolls the class outside the primitive that arbitrates against double shadows. Owner mark MT-F036 (shadow artifacts), root-caused to glass-ui.
defects.evidence: Measured resolved box-shadow on the live card root (probe-L4.mjs §A): `oklab(0.28 0.01676 0.024882 / 0.32) -3px 3px 0px 0px, oklab(… / 0.26) -5px 5px 0px 0px, oklab(… / 0.18) -7px 7px 0px 0px` — three layers, blur radius 0px, offsets -3/-5/-7px. Token is producer property: dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css `--shadow-cartoon-md: -3px 3px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-lead), -5px 5px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-mid), -7px 7px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-contact);`. The primitive guards the stack — dist/card-Bk96VI2R.js passes `shadow: n.shadow && !n.cartoon` to Surface — but PaletteCard.vue:19 applies `cartoon-surface` by hand alongside its own `bg-well border-card-edge` fork, so nothing arbitrates. `.cartoon-cast` re-measured inert this pass: {"position":"static","zIndex":"auto","boxShadow":"none","display":"inline","w":0}. `--cartoon-press-t` resolves `0` while the card writes `--card-press-t: 0.0000`.
defects.mechanism: same string-coupling as L-36 — applying a producer class by literal bypasses the primitive's own compensation logic; the artifact itself is a producer token tuned for a different scale
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/probe-L4.mjs — section A_rootRegister, fields rest.root.boxShadow, rest.vars.shadowCartoonMd, rest.cast. Visual witnesses OM-11-palette-card-shadow-artifacts.png, OM-12-palette-card-shadow-artifact-closeup.png
defects.proposedCure: BJ ask: retune the cartoon shadow ramp at the producer — fewer layers, or non-zero blur on the trailing layers, or a size-aware ramp — and make the `shadow && !cartoon` arbitration reachable by consumers who do not go through `<Card>` (or make going through `<Card>` the only supported path). defects.defect: A leaf presentational card hard-requires an APP-ROOT BOOT provider through a non-null-asserted inject; the dependency runs backwards and no lint rule can observe it because it travels via provide/inject. Each card mount also increments a module-global epoch that invalidates a module-global tint cache for every surface in the app.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:229 `const { safeCss } = useSafeAccentFn("well");` (unconditional, setup top level) → demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:347 `const ambient = inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)!;`. Sole provider: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:92 `provide(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, derivedLightness)` — demo/color-picker/ IS the app root. This is the edge G-DEMO-1 exists to forbid (its own message: 'the shared color layer must never import app-root boot (demo/color-picker)'). Epoch thrash: useContrastSafeColor.ts:76-81 `bumpProbeEpochOnMount()` registers a per-instance onMounted that increments module-global `probeEpoch`; :239-249 keys module-global `liveTintCache` on (darkClass, epoch), each miss costing a getComputedStyle + two canvas getImageData readbacks. BrowsePane pages 50 rows. The value bought is `safeFirstColor` (PaletteCard.vue:230), read ONLY inside the `v-if="expanded"` subtree (PaletteCard.vue:143).
defects.mechanism: direction-of-dependency inversion laundered through provide/inject — invisible to no-restricted-imports, and the rule that would have caught the import form is itself dead (L-39)
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "provide(INK_AMBIENT_KEY" demo → demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:92 only; grep -n "inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)!" demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts → :347. Latent-crash path: mount PaletteCard outside the boot tree, then expand — the first safeCss() call throws on `ambient.value` (undefined).
defects.proposedCure: Certified ink for a palette's first colour is a property of the palette ROW, not of the card chrome. Hoist it to the list owner (usePaletteStore / PaletteCardGrid) and pass it as a plain prop, or compute it lazily inside PaletteCardSwatches where it is actually read. One instrument instance serves the whole grid; the epoch bump happens once; the card stops reaching up into boot and becomes mountable in isolation.

defects.defect: A host wraps PaletteCard in a native `<button>` while the card ships interactive descendants — invalid HTML content model. The card's public surface (role=article + a root @click + interactive children) never states that it contains interactive content, so hosts read it as a clickable tile.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 — `<button v-for="palette in savedPalettes" type="button" :aria-pressed="…" @click="togglePalette(palette)"> <PaletteCard :palette="palette" :css-color="''" /> </button>`. Measured interactive descendants of a collapsed card (probe-L4.mjs §C): `collapsedInteractiveDescendants: 1` (the aria-label="Palette menu" trigger, a real <button> from glass-ui). Plus a slug-copy <button> at PaletteCardSwatches.vue:13 whenever show-slug is set. HTML Living Standard §4.10.6: <button>'s content model is phrasing content 'but there must be no interactive content descendant'.
defects.mechanism: ambiguous activation contract — the component publishes a root click emit AND interactive children without declaring the latter, so hosts over-wrap it (mirror image of pass-1 L-3 / pass-3 L-32, where hosts under-wire it)
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS on the live-nesting axis. probe-L4.mjs §B navigated /#/mix and measured `{"articles": 0}` — the mix source list did not surface the seeded palettes on that route, so the nested DOM was not captured. Established instead by source reading (MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268) plus the measured descendant count (probe-L4.mjs §C = 1).
defects.proposedCure: Activation belongs to the card. Drop the root `click` emit; make the title row the single activator (a real <button> around the name); hosts pass @activate. Selection state becomes a prop the card renders, not a wrapper element the host invents — glass-ui's Card already ships `variant="selection"` + `selected` (Card.vue.d.ts) for exactly this.

defects.evidence: Measured root: rootClass "group rounded-card cartoon-surface border-card-edge bg-well cursor-pointer"; role "article"; tabIndex -1; onkeydown false. PaletteCard.vue:5-27. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5: "A palette card is a bounded entity article, not a clickable role=article ... The card body owns no expand, inline rename, action menu, transient result or hover-only swatch-action path." §3.1/PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.12: exact tuple {sm, content, quiet, opaque, shadow:false, grain:false, specular:off}, "no cartoon/grid/selected variant", root is a "noninteractive container". glass-ui 7.0.0 ships the contract: dist/components/card/Card.vue.d.ts exposes size/material/shadow/surface/grain/specular.
defects.mechanism: Hand-rolled div shell reaching past the design system, with activation on the container instead of a named seat.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/palettes with any saved palette; Tab through the page — no card is ever focused. document.querySelector('[role="article"]').tabIndex === -1 and .onkeydown === null.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose to the canon shape: <Card> with the frozen tuple as a noninteractive container plus one native <button type="button" aria-pressed> seat spanning specimen+identity. Delete the premise of the current root rather than patching it.

defects.defect: MT-F036(a): the card trails a hard-edged three-facet shadow slab, and pairs it with an almost invisible 12%-alpha edge.
defects.evidence: Measured computed boxShadow: "oklab(0.28 .. /0.32) -3px 3px 0px 0px, oklab(.. /0.26) -5px 5px 0px 0px, oklab(.. /0.18) -7px 7px 0px 0px". Token: --shadow-cartoon-md = three 0-blur offsets at -3/-5/-7 (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css:1). Applied by @utility cartoon-surface { position:relative; border-width:2px; box-shadow:var(--shadow-cartoon-md) } (dist/components/card/styles.css:1). Measured borderTopColor oklab(0.216128 0.00350075 0.00518669 / 0.12). glass-ui's own idiom pairs these shadows with a solid outline: :where(.shadow-cartoon-sm,-md,-lg){border:2px solid var(--border)} (dist/styles/utilities/components.css:1). Owner witnesses OM-11/OM-12.
defects.mechanism: Three discrete zero-blur offset copies of the border-box staircase at the bottom-left corner — MT-F027's class — hung off a 2px stroke at 12% alpha, so the card ships cel shadow without cel line.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/palettes with a saved palette at 1440; read getComputedStyle(card).boxShadow, or view docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-12-palette-card-shadow-artifact-closeup.png.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the canon tuple's shadow=false and delete cartoon-surface from this consumer. Do not tune the offsets and do not add a consumer box-shadow:none override — that is the per-instance patch edict 5 forbids. If the resulting matte slip does not read against the glass workspace, that is a producer composition question (BJ ask), not a consumer shadow.

defects.defect: MT-F036(b): the interactive container has no hover, press, or focus register at all — a glass-6→glass-7 regression, and the source comment documenting the choreography is now factually false.
defects.evidence: Enumerated every rule in the running document (53 stylesheets / 5351 rules) whose selector mentions 'cartoon': only .cartoon-surface{position;border-width;box-shadow}, .shadow-cartoon*, and .liquid-enter.is-cel > .cartoon-cast. Every :hover/:active rule whose SUBJECT is one of the root's six classes: only three EMPTY declaration blocks '.group-[.destructive]:hover:*{}'. Measured transitionDuration "0s". PaletteCard.vue:7-18 claims cartoon-surface "owns the hover/press choreography (translate/scale on --ease-cartoon-punch @ --duration-normal, shadow bezier md→lg, :active squash, 2px border)" — glass-ui 7.0.0 implements three declarations, none of them motion.
defects.mechanism: W44 adopted glass-ui 7.0.0 whole; the producer atom this consumer depended on lost its interaction register and the consumer was never re-verified.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/palettes with a saved palette, hover the card: no visual change. Programmatically: walk document.styleSheets for any rule with :hover/:active whose subject compound matches .cartoon-surface/.rounded-card/.bg-well/.border-card-edge — result is three empty blocks.
defects.proposedCure: BJ ask to glass-ui, never a local hover: utility — the canon palette entity slip needs a producer-owned interactive register (resting → hover → pressed → focus-visible) on Card or on the named pressed seat, in the glass motion vocabulary, PRM-gated at the producer. Under the canon shape it attaches to the <button aria-pressed> seat, which also fixes the root being hoverable but never focusable.

defects.defect: A dead <span class="cartoon-cast"> and a dead JS spring drive ship on every rendered card — legacy left behind by the glass-7 adoption. (This also CORRECTS pass-1's claim that the cast is a live fourth caster.)
defects.evidence: Measured computed style of PaletteCard.vue:30's span: {display:"inline", position:"static", boxShadow:"none", zIndex:"auto", borderRadius:"0px", translate:"none", scale:"none", rect:{width:0,height:0}}. It matches NO rule — the only .cartoon-cast selectors in the document are '.liquid-enter.is-cel > .cartoon-cast' and the root carries neither class (the bare rule lives in dist/styles/glass/glass-atom.css, unreachable from the @mkbabb/glass-ui/styles entry graph). Measured inline style on every card root: "--card-press-t: 0.0000; --flex-vel: 0.0000;". `grep -rn "card-press-t" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no matches; `grep -rn "card-press-t" demo/ src/` → only PaletteCard.vue:29 (comment), :260 (comment), :264 (pressVar). The producer's cast reads --cartoon-press-t (@property, initial 0). useLiquidPress is imported at exactly one site in the whole demo.
defects.mechanism: The press variable name never matched the producer's, and the styled-cast rule is not in the shipped entry graph — so a per-card spring clock and six pointer handlers write two custom properties nobody reads into an unstyled 0x0 element.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/palettes with a saved palette; getComputedStyle(card.querySelector('.cartoon-cast')) returns display:inline / position:static / boxShadow:none, and card.getAttribute('style') is "--card-press-t: 0.0000; --flex-vel: 0.0000;".
defects.proposedCure: Delete the .cartoon-cast span and the useLiquidPress call outright (owner edict 2 — no legacy, no dead dual paths). Press feedback arrives with D-4's producer register on the named seat.

defects.defect: Radius concentricity error: the colour strip paints the card's OUTER 16px radius 2px inside the border box, producing the crescent artifact visible in OM-11.
defects.evidence: Measured: card x 33, borderTopLeftRadius 16px, borderTopWidth 2px; strip x 35, borderTopLeftRadius 16px. Correct inner radius = outer − border = 14px. Source: PaletteCard.vue:33-37 applies `rounded-t-card` (the outer radius token) to a child inset by cartoon-surface's 2px border.
defects.mechanism: Two 16px arcs offset by 2px are not parallel, so up to 2px of bg-well shows between the strip's arc and the border's inner arc at both top corners.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/palettes with a saved palette; compare getBoundingClientRect().x and borderTopLeftRadius of the card root vs its .rounded-t-card child. Visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-11-palette-card-shadow-artifacts.png at both cards' top-left corners.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the strip radius from container radius and border in one place. Under the canon tuple the strip becomes a full-bleed child of a producer-clipped surface and the arithmetic disappears entirely.

defects.defect: The expand/collapse motion is untokenized, forks easing token values as literals, animates layout-forcing `height` with three explicit reflows, and completely ignores prefers-reduced-motion (including an unconditional smooth scrollIntoView).
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts: DEFAULT_EXPAND_DURATION=350, DEFAULT_COLLAPSE_DURATION=250, EXPAND_EASING="cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)" // matches --ease-out-expo, COLLAPSE_EASING="cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)" // matches --ease-standard; `htmlEl.style.transition = \`height ${expandDuration}ms ...\``; `void htmlEl.offsetHeight` x3; `htmlEl.scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth", block:"nearest"})`. Header comment admits "no exact glass-ui canon match — 350ms sits between --duration-normal 300ms and --duration-slow 450ms". `grep -rn "prefers-reduced-motion|matchMedia" demo/palettes/browser/card/` → one comment in ShadowPalette.vue:25, nothing else. Contrast: the vj-* families ARE globally neutralised at demo/styles/animations.css:184. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: "Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry and stable chromatic state."
defects.mechanism: Inline style.transition written at runtime is structurally unreachable by the global PRM media-query guard the sibling animation families rely on.
defects.reproduction: Set OS/browser prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; open /#/palettes and click a card. The row still animates its height over 350ms and the viewport still smooth-scrolls.
defects.proposedCure: The expand disclosure is deleted by the canon shape (detail moves to the selected inspector). Any surviving local disclosure uses the producer spring register through the vj-* CSS families with interpolate-size/grid-rows instead of height, inheriting the global PRM guard for free.

defects.defect: The reorder handle is an unnamed, unfocusable 16x16 <svg> with a grab cursor — an operable ornament with no name, no keyboard grab, and below every tap floor.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:47-50: `<GripVertical v-if="draggable" class="drag-handle w-4 h-4 ... cursor-grab active:cursor-grabbing" />` — no role, no tabindex, no aria-label, no key handling. Measured {w:16, h:16}. Canon §3.1/PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.12: "An optional reorder handle is a separate named control." §5.2 requires Space-grab keyboard reorder with `position of total` announcement. §5.5: "Decorative controls and operable ornaments without names are forbidden." PR-07 names the family.
defects.mechanism: A styled glyph substituted for a control; there is no element for focus, name, state, or key handling to attach to.
defects.reproduction: Open /#/palettes with draggable enabled; Tab — the handle is never reached. document.querySelector('.drag-handle').getBoundingClientRect() → 16x16; it has no role/aria-label attribute.
defects.proposedCure: A named <button type="button"> seat carrying the grip glyph, with the Space-grab protocol and an ordinal announcement; or remove the glyph if reorder is not a shipped affordance this tranche. Do not leave an operable ornament.

defects.defect: Operation truth — including failure — is a 2.5-second transient held inside the child and injected imperatively through a component-ref map.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:238-244 `defineExpose({ showFeedback })`. demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:209 `const cardRefs = reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`; :230 `card.showFeedback("Saved!", "success")`; :239 `card.showFeedback(result.message, "error")`; :249 and :264 likewise; demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:207 likewise. ActionFeedback.vue:23-47 auto-dismisses at autoDismissMs=2500. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5: "Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace. A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth." PR-08.
defects.mechanism: State lives in the child's local refs and is reachable only by an imperative method call, so it cannot be rendered, replayed, or tested by the owner and dies with the card on sort/filter/page.
defects.reproduction: On /#/browse trigger a failing publish/save; the error chip appears for 2.5s and then no record of the failure exists anywhere in the UI. Re-sorting the wall before it dismisses destroys it immediately.
defects.proposedCure: Owner-held per-entity operation state ({pending | ok | failed(reason)}) rendered in the selected inspector's durable status region; the card may keep a silent celebration. Delete defineExpose and the cardRefs map.

defects.defect: The six-file decomposition is not along seams — it is a god module distributed across six files; two children own no state and one has no root element at all.
defects.evidence: Line counts: PaletteCard.vue 364, PaletteCardMenu 228, PaletteCardSwatches 96, PaletteRenameInput 66, PaletteCardMeta 64, ActionFeedback 58 (876 total). PaletteCard retains 11 props, 17 emits, a 19-entry string-keyed action table (:293-313), four composables, and two pieces of UI state. PaletteCardSwatches owns NO state and takes 8 props / re-emits 8 events, all forwarded straight back into useHoverPopover. PaletteCardMeta has no root element — five sibling root nodes (:8,16,26,36,43) laid out by the parent's flex row; measured parent row reports metaChildren:8 with the meta chips as direct children. Source comments record the history: "T.W5 PP-8 cap cure", "the H.W3 sub-component precedent". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 names the result: "seven-mode omnibus" — and the prop list is literally seven modes (expanded, isOwned, editableName, isAdmin, showSlug, draggable, layout).
defects.mechanism: A line-count cap was met by relocating markup rather than by moving responsibility, so the coupling surface (16 members for Swatches; the parent's own flex context for Meta) was preserved intact across a file boundary. The Meta extraction actively CAUSED D-1: the shrink-0 decision that starves the title now lives in a file that cannot see the title.
defects.reproduction: Read the six files; count props+emits on PaletteCardSwatches (8+8, zero state) and root nodes on PaletteCardMeta (5, no wrapper). At runtime, the parent's identity row reports metaChildren:8 — the child's chips are the parent's flex items.
defects.proposedCure: Subtraction, not re-cutting. The canon anatomy — Card(frozen tuple) > button[aria-pressed] over specimen+identity, plus one named reorder handle — with expand/rename/menu/transient-result/swatch-actions moving to the selected inspector DELETES PaletteCardSwatches, PaletteRenameInput, ActionFeedback and most of PaletteCardMenu from the card, and dissolves D-1, D-7, D-9 and D-17 as a side effect. Per feedback_kiss_no_contrivance the fix is not a seventh file or a shared/ dir.

defects.defect: Seven verbatim hand-rolled copies of the icon-button recipe survive in the sibling files while the parent uses the glass-ui Button atom.

The recipe is verbatim: `p-1.5 rounded-sm hover:bg-accent active:scale-95 active:bg-accent/70 transition-colors cursor-pointer focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40`. defects.reproduction: Run the two greps above; then measure getBoundingClientRect() on the '…' menu button (36x36) versus a swatch popover action button (~28) inside one card.
defects.proposedCure: All seven consume the glass-ui Button atom (owner edict 4/5). PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.12 also requires glyph size, target size and layout reservation be separate quantities — the hand-rolled p-1.5 conflates them.

defects.defect: Per-instance override of a glass-ui Badge from consumer scoped CSS, with a redundant duplicate declaration, on top of a demo-root fork of the producer's gold token.

defects.defect: The folder is split-brain on the Vue 3.5 props idiom — three files use reactive props destructure, three use withDefaults + props.x.

defects.proposedCure: One idiom across the folder (owner edict 7). Reactive destructure is the 3.5 idiom; the two withDefaults sites become `const { x = default } = defineProps<...>()`.

defects.defect: `swatchClass` is a raw Tailwind class string exposed as a public prop — a per-instance styling override channel with a name.

defects.reproduction: Read PaletteCard.vue:194-197 and ExtractWorkbench.vue:150.
defects.proposedCure: A closed `size` token ('sm' | 'md') resolved inside the component, matching how the producer's own Card/Button take size (owner edicts 3 and 5).

defects.defect: The documented "designed empty-state swatch" never paints; a zero-colour palette renders a 40px void band instead of a designed empty state.

defects.defect: The activation region is defined by exclusion — four @click.stop descendants punch invisible dead zones out of an otherwise fully clickable card.

defects.reproduction: Open /#/palettes and click across a card: the title row toggles, the swatch area and menu area do not, with no visual boundary between them.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Seat declared, not inherited; matches the explicit Opus 5 spawn declaration.

defects.defect: The component addresses glass-ui 7's Button through a `variant` prop that does not exist in that component's API. Five sites pass variant="outline"/"ghost"; they land as dead fallthrough HTML attributes while the real axes render emphasis=secondary tone=neutral. The file's own comment at :107-111 claims variant="ghost" quieted the per-row destructive (the W5-12/F-8 cure) — that mechanism does nothing; the observed quieting comes from hand-rolled utility classes. This CORRECTS a pass-2 'verified clean' attribution. Also bypassed: iconOnly (the icon-seat cure), loading (the pending-state cure), tone (the destructive cure).
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts — ButtonProps = {emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class}; no `variant`. demo/ui/button/index.ts:1 is a bare re-export. Live Chromium DOM (probe-D4a): `attrs: data-slot=button | data-emphasis=secondary | data-tone=neutral | data-size=sm | … | variant=outline | style=…`; `border: 0px rgb(28,25,23)` — no outline renders. Sites: AdminUsersPanel.vue:22,33,58,114,123. Systemic scope: `grep -rn '<Button' -A2 demo | grep -c 'variant='` -> 51 across 22 files.
defects.mechanism: producer API never read; consumer back-fills the missing styling with per-instance utility classes
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D4/probe-D4a-computed.mjs against localhost:9000/#/admin/users — read the pasted `variant=outline` attribute next to `data-emphasis=secondary`.

That one move also deletes the five per-instance class strings (D-24), the hand-rolled spinner (pass-2 D-13), the undersized icon seat (pass-2 D-15) and the font-display override (pass-2 D-6). Relay the 51-site systemic finding to the glass-ui BH inbox — the consumer cut is producer-coordination work.

defects.defect: Five per-instance geometry overrides of a root that carries a `size` axis passed on the same element — and they are inert. `h-7` (28px) loses at every measured viewport.

defects.defect: One toolbar status sentence counts two different populations: `{{ totalUsers }} users` is bound to the UNFILTERED roster while `· {{ emptyCount }} empty` is computed over the SEARCH-FILTERED prop. A middot joins a numerator and denominator that do not belong to each other — and it is that numerator the prune confirmation then quotes.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:8-13; :241 `users.filter(...)` over the prop; AdminPane.vue:28 binds the prop to pm.filteredAdminUsers (filter at useAdminUsers.ts:29-35) while AdminPane.vue:33 binds totalUsers to the unfiltered pm.adminUsers.length. Pass-2 probe-D3f output shows it: `toolbar: ["5 users","· 1 empty"]` with `renderedRows: 1`.
defects.mechanism: truth derived at two different altitudes inside one sentence

result.strongestDefect: New to this pass: D-23 — the component has never rendered its own declared design. glass-ui 7's Button has no `variant` prop; the five `variant="outline"|"ghost"` props at AdminUsersPanel.vue:22,33,58,114,123 land as dead fallthrough HTML attributes (measured `variant=outline` sitting beside `data-emphasis=secondary data-tone=neutral`, `border-width: 0px`). Every downstream hand-roll (dead `h-7` geometry, hand-rolled spinner, undersized icon seat, font-display type) is back-fill for an API call that silently failed at all five sites. Overall across all three passes the strongest remains pass-2 D-1: an irreversible bulk deletion whose confirmation understated its scope 3x in a single reproduced run, with the captured request (POST /admin/users/prune-empty, postData null) proving the client cannot scope it at all.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative proof is owed; recorded here are the attacks that failed, so a later seat does not re-litigate them. (1) `min-w-0` is NOT missing from the forked row despite AdminListItem carrying it — :68's `overflow-hidden` zeroes a grid item's automatic minimum size identically; corroborated by overflowX 0 on all four REPORT.md admin/users rows and all six STATES.json state rows. (2) verbatimModuleSyntax (edict 8) clean — :199 is the only type-only import and is correct; SAFE_ACCENT_KEY/ADMIN_PORT_KEY are InjectionKey values. (3) Vue 3.5 idioms (edict 7) clean — reactive props destructure with default at :205-220; no template refs owed; no defineModel round-trip. (4) Animations (edict 6) clean — vj-celebrate is one of the three sanctioned families, nothing deleted, global keyframes in demo/styles/animations.css; its max-height leg resolves none->none here because the site sets no --vj-celebrate-collapse/-expanded, so pass-2 D-16's 105px displacement is layout participation, not the transition. (5) The panel does not contribute to the smallTapTargets count at mobile — its own controls measure 108x54 and 80x54 at 390; the 4 belong to dock/search chrome. (6) No page or console errors on any admin/users capture. (7) main = 1 on every admin/users row. (8) The icon-only delete's aria-label works — admin routes are absent from the 18 namelessButtons. (9) The WebKit/Chromium keyboard-reachability delta is MT-F022 Full Keyboard Access and is not counted; the one a11y finding raised here (D-29) is reproduced byte-identically in both engines. defects.defect: MT-F036(b) — the interactive card container ships NO hover state, and the nine-line 'producer CARTOON REGISTER' comment at PaletteCard.vue:7-15 documents behaviour that does not exist in glass-ui 7.0.0. The comment claims cartoon-surface owns 'the hover/press choreography (translate/scale on --ease-cartoon-punch @ --duration-normal, shadow bezier md→lg, :active squash, 2px border)'. Of five claims only '2px border' is true.
defects.evidence: Shipped rule in full, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css: `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }` — three declarations, no transition, no :hover. Live probe: `probe('cartoon-surface')` → {"transitionProperty":"all","transitionDuration":"0s","transitionTimingFunction":"ease"}. Full computed snapshot of the live card root → real Playwright .hover() → re-snapshot → diff: {"isHovered":true,"diff":{}} — ZERO computed-property change under :hover. `grep -rno "cartoon-surface:hover[^}]*}" --include="*.css" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist` → no output. `grep -rn cartoon-surface demo/styles/ demo/**/*.css` → no output (no local override). Token --shadow-cartoon-hover exists and is referenced by nothing.
defects.mechanism: demo prose asserting producer behaviour that the installed producer version does not implement; glass 7.0.0 adoption removed/never-shipped the hover leg and no gate reads prose
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → snapshot getComputedStyle of [role='article'].cartoon-surface → Playwright locator.hover() → re-snapshot → diff is empty. Also: cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css | grep -o '@utility cartoon-surface[^}]*}'
defects.proposedCure: MARKED BJ ASK, per the owner's instruction that a missing glass variant never becomes a local patch. glass-ui grows the hover leg of cartoon-surface (--shadow-cartoon-hover already ships as an unused token) plus the transition legs the demo's own O-16 oracle already asserts it has. A :hover in PaletteCard.vue's scoped block would violate edicts 4 and 5 and fork the register into the demo. The false comment must be deleted with the fix — it is why three audit passes and one e2e oracle assumed the register existed.

defects.defect: MT-F036(a) — the hard-edged faceted shadow slab, plus `.cartoon-cast` is inert dead markup wired to a CSS variable nothing in the repository ever writes. Three sub-mechanisms: (i) --shadow-cartoon-md is three ZERO-BLUR offset copies at 3/5/7px with stepping alpha, which facets by construction; (ii) the standalone .cartoon-cast rule lives in dist/styles/glass/glass-atom.css which the demo never imports, so the hand-authored <span class="cartoon-cast"> is a 0×0 styleless inline node; (iii) useLiquidPress is configured pressVar:"--card-press-t" while .cartoon-cast reads --cartoon-press-t — a name mismatch, so the press drive is connected to nothing even if the sheet loaded.
defects.evidence: Live card root box-shadow: `oklab(0.34 0.0115 0.0277 / 0.46) -3px 3px 0px 0px, oklab(… / 0.38) -5px 5px 0px 0px, oklab(… / 0.26) -7px 7px 0px 0px`, border-radius 16px — blur 0, spread 0, three discrete steps = the terrace in OM-11/OM-12. Live .cartoon-cast computed: {"tag":"SPAN","display":"inline","position":"static","boxShadow":"none","zIndex":"auto","borderRadius":"0px","translate":"none","scale":"none","rect":{"width":0,"height":0}}. Walking all 53 loaded stylesheets: the only .cartoon-cast rules present are liquid-enter.css's `.liquid-enter.is-cel > .cartoon-cast`; the card root carries no .liquid-enter.is-cel. `grep -rn "card-press-t|cartoon-press-t" demo/ src/` → only PaletteCard.vue:29, :260, :264 (all writers of --card-press-t); zero writers of --cartoon-press-t. Live root inline style permanently `--card-press-t: 0.0000; --flex-vel: 0.0000;`, cast --cast-travel 0px / --cast-spread 1. Every other producer consumer passes a name its own CSS reads: --glass-btn-press-t, --dock-press-t, --timeline-press-t.
defects.mechanism: a consumer hand-authoring a producer's internal element and guessing its contract — wrong custom-property name, and a stylesheet the card entrypoint does not distribute
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.cartoon-cast')) → all-default; then getPropertyValue('--cartoon-press-t') → '0' on both card and cast while the root inline style carries --card-press-t. Witnesses: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-11-palette-card-shadow-artifacts.png and OM-12-...-closeup.png
defects.proposedCure: Delete the <span class="cartoon-cast"> and the pressVar override outright — demo markup must never hand-author a producer internal, which is exactly how the variable name drifted. MARKED BJ ASK for the rest: (a) --shadow-cartoon-* must stop faceting (the zero-blur triple stack is MT-F027's mechanism class, fixed at the token, at root); (b) if the cast/press choreography is wanted it arrives whole from Card surface=cartoon — emitting its own child, under its own variable name, with its own CSS distribution.

defects.defect: The press choreography fires for every pointerdown INSIDE the card, not for pressing the card. v-bind="press.handlers" sits on the root and pointer events bubble, so opening the dropdown, touching a swatch, grabbing the drag handle or clicking into the rename field all drive the card's spring.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:24 `v-bind="press.handlers"` + :25 `:style="press.pressStyle.value"`. Dispatching pointerdown on the 'Palette menu' button of a 462×100 card and reading the ROOT's inline style: at rest `--card-press-t: 0.0000; --flex-vel: 0.0000;` → +60ms `--card-press-t: 0.7103; scale: 1.0068 0.9652;` → +180ms `--card-press-t: 1.0120; scale: 1.0092 0.9512;` (4.9% vertical squash of the whole card). Swatch pointerdown +80ms → `scale: 1.008 0.9591`.
defects.mechanism: gesture-scope error — an interaction affordance bound to a container that is not the gesture's subject
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → card.querySelector('button[aria-label="Palette menu"]').dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerdown',{bubbles:true,button:0})) → read card.getAttribute('style') after 180ms
defects.proposedCure: Folds into the existing pass-2 C-4 cure: once the expand disclosure is a real focusable <button aria-expanded> on the header row, press.handlers belong on THAT element, and the inner controls carry their own press (glass-ui Button already does). Do not stopPropagation per control — that is a patch that must be maintained at every new child.

defects.defect: The cardRefs instance map retains fully-unmounted PaletteCard instances forever. Pass 2 filed this as an argument it could not photograph; it is measurable from the map itself. Second, sharper consequence not previously drawn: showFeedback dispatched at a retained-but-unmounted instance writes a ref on a destroyed component, so the truthy guards report success and the user gets NO verdict and no error.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:94 and PalettesPane.vue:84 both use `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[k] = el)"` — Vue calls the function ref with null on unmount and the `el &&` guard makes that a no-op. Measured by filtering /#/palettes to zero rows: {"before":{"refs":5,"dom":5},"after":{"refs":5,"dom":0},"retainedWhileFiltered":[5 × {"isUnmounted":true,"elInDoc":false}],"restored":{"refs":5,"dom":5}}. Silent-failure sites: BrowsePane.vue:229 `if (card) card.showFeedback(...)`, :238, :249 `cardRefs[palette.slug]?.showFeedback(...)`, :264.
defects.mechanism: imperative defineExpose handle forcing every host to build an identity map, with a truthiness guard that swallows Vue's unmount signal
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → walk card.__vueParentComponent.parent until setupState.cardRefs → type a non-matching string into input[type=search], dispatch 'input' → Object.keys(cardRefs).length stays 5 while document.querySelectorAll("[role='article'].cartoon-surface").length is 0; each retained value has $.isUnmounted true
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a delete-key fix. Feedback is state ABOUT A PALETTE, not about a component instance: lift {slug, message, variant, at} into the pane's palette manager and pass it DOWN as a prop. defineExpose({showFeedback}), both cardRefs maps, both `(el: any)` casts, the retention AND the silent-no-verdict all delete together — and the duplicated broken idiom across two panes (edict 2, no dual paths) goes with them.

And my P1 shows probe('cartoon-surface') returns transitionProperty 'all'/duration '0s', so census.cartoon['translate'] is undefined and expect(undefined).toBe('0.3s') would throw if reached. Separately: `grep -rln "PaletteCard|ActionFeedback|useHoverPopover|useHeightTransition|SwatchHoverMenu" test/ demo/test/` → no output (zero unit tests); the three e2e flow specs assert only that a network call fired (vote-toggle.spec.ts:44-46 polls voteCalled).

defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o16-computed-cascade.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line
defects.proposedCure: Exact green-keeping mutation to record: delete .cartoon-cast, delete the press wiring, ship the ActionFeedback truncation, double every shadow layer, leak the whole cardRefs map — all still green. Cure: assert census.liveCards (non-empty AND per-leg), and split R2's pane-transition drift out of the same test so a spatial-family regression cannot shadow the cartoon register. The deeper cure is that a motion register asserted only by class-probe cannot notice a producer version bump that deletes the rule — the oracle needs the live element as its primary referent, not its footnote.

defects.defect: CONVERGE with pass 2 C-2, independently re-measured at a second viewport with a real mouse hover: `.floating-panel` has no CSS rule anywhere in the repo or the producer, so the teleported swatch action panel computes position:static, its correct inline top/left are inert, and it renders entirely off-screen. Add/Edit/Copy on a palette swatch is unreachable on the hover path.
defects.evidence: After a real Playwright .hover() on the first swatch of an expanded card at viewport 390×844: {"inlineStyle":"top: 493.867px; left: 65px; transform: translateX(-50%);","computedPosition":"static","rect":{"x":-195,"y":844,"w":390,"h":40},"swatchRect":{"x":47,"y":535.9},"visible":false}. positionPanel computed the correct anchor (top = swatch top − 42, left = swatch centre) and it is discarded. `grep -rn "floating-panel" --include="*.css" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist` → one prose comment in demo/styles/animations.css:2. `grep -rn "floating-panel" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no output. Same node: {"ariaHidden":"true","focusableInside":2} — focusable buttons inside an aria-hidden subtree (axe aria-hidden-focus).
defects.mechanism: dangling class — the rule was deleted on the claim that glass-ui provided it; it does not, and no gate reads for undefined classes
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → click a card to expand → Playwright hover the div.relative wrapping a .watercolor-swatch → getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.floating-panel')).position === 'static', getBoundingClientRect() → {x:-195,y:844}
defects.proposedCure: MARKED BJ ASK, and do NOT re-add a demo-local floating-panel.css — that re-forks what glass-ui was meant to absorb. An anchored hover/press action panel is a component type the producer owns; retire the hand-rolled Teleport + getBoundingClientRect + inline top/left branch and drive one producer panel from useHoverPopover's open state on both pointer classes. That single removal kills positionPanel, floatingStyle, the aria-hidden lie, and the e.currentTarget defect.

defects.defect: CONVERGE with pass 2 C-1: glass-ui 7.0.0 WatercolorDot sets inheritAttrs:false and consumes only attrs.class/attrs.style, has no `tag` prop, and hardcodes aria-hidden="true" + pointer-events:none. So SwatchHoverMenu's tag="button", :aria-label and @click.stop are all silently dropped. The entire expanded card exposes exactly ONE interactive element.
defects.evidence: dist/watercolor-dot.js: `inheritAttrs: !1`, `props: { color:{}, variant:{default:"solid"}, animate:{...}, cycleDuration:{...}, range:{...}, seed:{default:""} }` (no tag), setup reads only `n.class`/`n.style`, render root `o("span", { "aria-hidden": "true", …, style: u([f.value, { …, pointerEvents: "none", … }]) })`. Live expanded card: {"dotCount":5,"dotAriaLabel":null,"dotAriaHidden":"true","dotPointerEvents":"none","firstDotOuter":"<span aria-hidden=\"true\" class=\"… cursor-pointer watercolor-swatch\" style=\"…; pointer-events: none; …\">"} and interactive descendants = [{"tag":"BUTTON","name":"Palette menu","w":36,"h":36}] — one element.
defects.mechanism: a decorative producer primitive being asked to also be an interactive one; attrs silently dropped rather than rejected
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → expand a card → document.querySelector('.watercolor-swatch').outerHTML shows a span with aria-hidden=true, no aria-label, pointer-events:none, while carrying the consumer's cursor-pointer class
defects.proposedCure: MARKED BJ ASK for the producer half: WatercolorDot needs an `as`/`tag` prop with attr passthrough and a conditional aria-hidden, so the dot can be the button its consumers already ask it to be. Consumer half, and the KISS answer if the producer declines: SwatchHoverMenu renders its own <button type="button" :aria-label> and mounts <WatercolorDot> inside as pure decoration — at which point the hardcoded aria-hidden and pointer-events:none become correct by construction.

defects.defect: CONVERGE with pass 2 C-6, third independent reproduction at a third timing: ActionFeedback's auto-dismiss watcher fires only on a CHANGE of props.visible, so a second showFeedback while the chip is already up is a no-op write — no new timer — and the second message inherits the first's remaining countdown.
defects.evidence: ActionFeedback.vue:39-47 `watch(() => props.visible, …)`; PaletteCard.vue:238-242 showFeedback writes feedbackVisible.value = true. Measured, showFeedback twice 1500ms apart against a promised 2500ms: t=51 'FIRST', t=1502 'FIRST', t=1752 'SECOND', t=2504 'SECOND', t=2755 null → SECOND lived ~1005ms. Consistent with pass 2's 2250ms offset → 613ms and pass 1's vitest harness: one law, second message lifetime ≈ 2500 − offset. BrowsePane.vue:226-265 fires showFeedback from five async paths against the same card.
defects.mechanism: boolean-keyed lifetime for a value-keyed concern — the chip's clock is owned by a flag, not by the message
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → card.__vueParentComponent.exposed.showFeedback('FIRST','success'); setTimeout(()=>showFeedback('SECOND','success'),1500); poll card.querySelector('.feedback-chip').textContent every 250ms
defects.proposedCure: Make showFeedback push a value, not set a flag: {id, message, variant} watched as an object so a new id restarts the clock by construction. Add role="status" aria-live="polite" (the sole surface reporting four async outcomes currently announces to nobody) and onScopeDispose(() => clearTimeout(timer)). A clearTimeout bolt-on inside showFeedback would re-fork the timer across two files.

defects.defect: CONVERGE with pass 2 C-5, with finer sampling that pins the window: choosing 'Rename' from the palette menu focuses the rename input, then reka's dropdown focus-restore-on-close yanks focus back to the menu trigger between 100 and 300 ms. The user types into nothing and their first Enter re-opens the menu.
defects.evidence: Sampled document.activeElement after clicking the Rename menuitem: t+0 INPUT.input-bar-field, t+100 INPUT.input-bar-field, t+300 BUTTON[aria-label=Palette menu], t+600 same, t+1000 same; inputFocused:false. Same run: menuStillOpen:false — which falsifies the comment at PaletteCard.vue:291-292 ('keep the menu open visually until the input takes focus'), because startRenaming() (:280-283) sets menuOpen.value=false on its first line, making the `if (action !== "rename")` guard at :317 dead code guarding nothing.
defects.mechanism: two unsynchronised focus writers — PaletteRenameInput's onMounted focus and reka's async close-restore — with no arbitration
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → click button[aria-label='Palette menu'] → click the 'Rename' [role=menuitem] → sample document.activeElement at 0/100/300/600/1000ms
defects.proposedCure: One party writes focus. Drive the rename open from the menu's own close completion — @close-auto-focus.prevent on DropdownMenuContent, focusing the input in that handler — which is the idiomatic reka seam. Not a setTimeout. Delete the dead guard at :317 and the false comment above it.

defects.defect: CONVERGE with pass 2 C-10/C-11 plus one NEW target: three controls in this folder are below the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 24×24 CSS-px floor. The vote button at 23.6px is new — it misses by 0.4px, exactly the kind of near-miss an eye passes and a measurement does not.
defects.evidence: Measured by rendering each control's exact class string through the LIVE cascade: copy-slug button (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:13-19, p-0.5 + w-3 h-3) = 16.0 × 16.0; rename submit/cancel (PaletteRenameInput.vue:18-30, p-0.5 + w-3.5 h-3.5) = 18.0 × 18.0; vote heart (PaletteCardMeta.vue:43-54, px-1.5 py-0.5 + w-3.5 h-3.5) = 47.2 × 23.6; popover actions (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:41-62, p-1.5 + w-4 h-4) = 28 × 28 OK; palette menu (PaletteCard.vue:96-104, glass-ui Button icon-only size=sm) = 36 × 36 OK. Pass 2 measured 16×16 and 17.5px (same box, different DPR rounding).
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled icon-button recipes; the size floor is being restated per call site instead of owned by the design system
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000 → append a hidden div containing each button's verbatim class string → getBoundingClientRect() on each
defects.proposedCure: PaletteCard.vue:93-95 already performed this exact lift once — 'the 3rd copy of the hand-rolled icon-trigger recipe dies onto the glass-ui atom; the sm square also cures the ~24px touch target' — and it was never propagated to the other three. Consume `Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm"` (already imported in the parent) at all three sites. The floor is a design-system property, not a per-site p-1.5.

defects.defect: Decomposition verdict: the six-file split distributed a god module rather than dissolving it. PaletteCardSwatches.vue is a wrapper that earns nothing — 96 lines, 8 props in, 8 emits out, zero state, zero logic, every value forwarded verbatim between a composable and its consumer one component apart. PaletteCard.vue's script still holds all the state for all six files.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue: 8 props (colors, isLocal, displaySlug, safeFirstColor, openPopoverIndex, canHover, floatingStyle, swatchClass) all forwarded verbatim to SwatchHoverMenu; 8 emits (hover, leave, cancelLeave, swatchClick, popoverTouch, popoverAdd, popoverEdit, popoverCopy) all re-emitted verbatim — every one a member of the useHoverPopover() destructure at PaletteCard.vue:246-255 and its handlers at :149-156. PaletteCard.vue's script (163-335) = 172 lines holding 10 props, 16 emit variants, 4 refs, 4 composables and an 18-entry string-keyed dispatch table (:293-313) whose wire to its own child is an untyped `action: [action: string]` (PaletteCardMenu.vue:225) with `if (!fn) return;` (:316) silently swallowing unknown verbs. NEW: PaletteCardMenu renders TWO items labelled 'Publish' (:27-40 for kind==='saved', :48-60 for remote && isOwned && !isPublic) emitting different events. PaletteCardMeta is a 4-root fragment, not a component.
defects.mechanism: splits drawn to satisfy a line-count cap (PaletteCardMeta.vue:2-4 and PaletteCard.vue:76-77 both name it: 'T.W5 PP-8 cap cure') rather than along state seams
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural, established by reading all six files; wc -l gives 364/228/96/66/64/58 = 876 total
defects.proposedCure: Move useHoverPopover() INTO the swatch row — its state is entirely local there, and the only reason the parent holds it is one line (onBeforeCollapse at :277) that an @collapse emit covers. That takes PaletteCardSwatches to 4 props / 3 emits and makes it a component instead of a conduit. Type the menu seam as the card's own event union so the 18-entry table and the `!fn` masking fallback (edict 2) both become unreachable and deletable. Fold PaletteCardMeta back or give it the vote mutation. Two of six files should not exist in their current form, and the file that was supposed to shrink did not.

defects.defect: CORRECTION against my own first reading. I statically read certifyAccentInk's `if (!accent) return css` guard and recorded a negative result — 'no parseCssColor crash class here'. That inference holds only for input parseOklch returns falsy for. It is false for the empty-argument colour-function class, where parseCssColor THROWS and bypasses the guard entirely. Pass 2's C-3 is right and my negative is withdrawn.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/ink.ts:135-136 `const accent = parseOklch(css); if (!accent) return css;`. Pass 2 reproduced end-to-end through the remote browse feed: colors[0].css = "oklch()" → 2 articles → 0, pane replaced by 'This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace)', innocent neighbour palette destroyed, pageErrors and consoleErrors both EMPTY because the boundary absorbs the throw. Reachable because api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:28 is `css: z.string().min(1).max(200)` with no colour validation. I did not re-reproduce it — my environment's API was unreachable, so no remote wall existed to poison.
defects.mechanism: a total function advertised where a partial one ships; the correct degenerate exists one line up and the throw jumps over it
defects.reproduction: NOT RE-RUN IN PASS 3 (API unreachable). Pass 2's procedure: seed a one-palette browse wall with colors[0].css='oklch()' plus a neighbour palette, expand the first card. Recorded here so pass 3's negative-results section cannot be read as contradicting it.
defects.proposedCure: Three layers, none a shim. LIBRARY: parseCssColor must return {ok:false} for the empty-args class — this is the π gate's R1, still live; certifyAccentInk already HAS the correct degenerate. API: the schema should validate a colour, not a 200-char string. DEMO: `??` → a trimmed `||` so the documented EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH fallback is actually reachable for empty strings. Nothing about PaletteCard's structure needs to change.

result.strongestDefect: C3-2 — the card hand-authors a producer internal (<span class="cartoon-cast">) whose stylesheet the demo never loads, and drives it through pressVar:"--card-press-t" while the rule that would consume it reads --cartoon-press-t. Four compounding mechanisms — an unloaded sheet, a wrong variable name, a zero-blur triple-stacked shadow token that facets, and a nine-line comment asserting all of it works — produce exactly the artifact the owner marked in OM-11/OM-12. It is the clearest instance of the folder's general disease: the demo describing producer behaviour it does not have, in prose, where no gate can read it (C3-1's diff:{} is the same disease at the hover leg; C3-10 is the gate that should have caught both and cannot reach its own assertion). Across all three passes the single most severe finding remains pass 2's C-3 — one malformed colour string on the public wall destroys the Browse pane for every visitor — which pass 3 does not displace and, on re-reading, corrects itself in favour of.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded for completeness, the four things I checked and found SOUND, so a fourth pass does not re-spend the probes: (1) Interrupted expand/collapse does NOT corrupt state — this bounds pass 2's C-18 hypothesis. Clean expand → inline:"", panel 66.5px, 3 dots, card 191.5px; collapse then re-expand 80ms into the 250ms collapse → inline:"", 66.5px, 3 dots, 191.5px. Byte-identical; Vue's v-if remount recovers and the transitionend listener dies with the removed node. (2) The press spring is PRM-correct and disposes — dist/useSpring-9u2_shxV.js defaults `respectReducedMotion: u.respectReducedMotion !== !1` and registers onScopeDispose; no ungated rAF originates in these nine files. Pass 2's C-7 PRM finding concerns useHeightTransition's inline transition string and scrollIntoView, a different mechanism, and stands. (3) verbatimModuleSyntax: PASS, verified file by file across all six components and three composables — every type-only import is `import type` or an inline `type` specifier. (4) useTemplateRef used correctly at PaletteRenameInput.vue:48. Brief hazard sweep: no defineModel (stale-read N/A), no HSV roundtrip (stableHue N/A), no ValueUnit construction, no reka slider, no WebGL.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (AdminUsersPanel.vue, area palettes, route #/admin/users)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context), the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the unguarded expand race renders user A's palettes under user B's row, and the admin delete written from there deletes A's palette while debiting B's count. It is the only row that writes wrong data to the server. Measured end-to-end (probe/dbg3.mjs): DELETE /admin/palettes/azure-one-11aa issued from crimson-owl-77's region; azure left reading 4 with 3 palettes, crimson zeroed while still owning 1.

defects.defect: toggleUserExpand awaits pm.loadUserPalettes(slug) and assigns unconditionally — no request key, no re-check after the await, no abort. Two expands (or an expand-then-collapse) resolve in completion order, so one user's palettes render under another user's row; the card's admin-delete is wired to the ROW's slug (`:150`), so the delete goes to the leaked palette while the count is debited from the wrong owner.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-365 and :150. probe/aup-probe.mjs R3, chromium AND webkit byte-identical: `R3 t+2.4s expanded row = "crimson- owl-77 1 Palettes"` / `AZURE rows visible under it: true | CRIMSON visible: false`. End-to-end, probe/dbg3.mjs: `CALLS: [... ,"DELETE /admin/palettes/azure-one-11aa"]` issued from crimson's region; `BADGES: ["azure-fox-014Palettes","azure-fox-01","crimson-owl-77"]` — azure still reads 4 with 3 palettes, crimson's row lost role=button because useAdminUsers.ts:118-121 decremented crimson 1→0.
defects.mechanism: async write into shared component state without carrying the request's identity through the await (mechanism A: value sourced from a different authority than the one that acts on it)
defects.reproduction: VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:9124 npx vite --port 9124; node probe/aup-probe.mjs chromium R3 (and webkit); node probe/dbg3.mjs — delay /admin/users/azure-fox-01/palettes 1500ms, crimson 30ms, click azure then crimson 100ms later, then open the leaked card's ADMIN > Delete (admin).
defects.proposedCure: Replace the imperative fetch with a keyed, self-invalidating resource in the admin port — useAdminUserPalettes(slugRef) driven by watch(slugRef) with an AbortController cancelled on key change, returning {palettes, loading, error} bound to the key it was fetched for, so a response for a non-current key is unrepresentable. Take the delete's owner from palette.userSlug (already returned by the API), not from the row. This also supplies C-4's missing error cell and deletes the whole defineExpose back-channel.

defects.defect: The prune confirmation quotes emptyCount, computed over the search-filtered, first-50-only client list, while POST /admin/users/prune-empty takes no scope and the server deletes every empty user in the corpus plus their sessions. The dialog's number and the request's effect have different authorities.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 + :288-299; demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:69-71 (no body, no filter); api/src/modules/admin/service/users.ts:228-237 (`users.findEmptyUserSlugs()` → deleteMany, unbounded). probe/aup-probe.mjs R5, chromium AND webkit: dialog = "Prune 1 empty users? This will permanently delete 1 user…"; request sent = ["POST /admin/users/prune-empty"]; result banner = "Pruned 2 users".
defects.mechanism: a destructive verb's stated scope derived from a view of the data while it executes against the corpus
defects.reproduction: node probe/aup-probe.mjs chromium R5 (and webkit) — 4 users, 2 empty; type "verdant" in Search users…; press Prune empty → Prune. Server answers {pruned:2}; the app promised 1 and then printed 2.
defects.proposedCure: Make the count and the act the same object: either the server answers a preview (GET /admin/users/prune-empty → {count}) that the dialog quotes and the button gates on, or the client sends the explicit slug list it just described. Renaming the computed does not fix it.

defects.defect: onConfirm fires the action and only then sets confirmOpen=false; nothing disables the footer button, nothing clears confirmAction, and the Dialog plays a leave transition — so the destructive control stays mounted and hit-testable after it fires. One double-click = two whole-corpus prunes.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:283-286. probe/aup-probe4.mjs H2 (a single dblclick): `H2 prune POSTs after ONE dblclick: ["POST /admin/users/prune-empty","POST /admin/users/prune-empty"]`. Independently reproduced from a different harness than the r2 seat's.
defects.mechanism: a control outlives its own activation (mechanism C)
defects.reproduction: node probe/aup-probe4.mjs chromium H2 — open Prune empty, then a single dblclick on the dialog's Prune button.
defects.proposedCure: onConfirm becomes async with the footer button bound :disabled to the pending state (visibly inert the instant it fires), and confirmAction is taken out of the ref before invocation so a late event has nothing to call. Store it in shallowRef. The whole 33-line confirm engine (:254-286) is the natural extraction out of a 391-line SFC.

defects.defect: NEW. A request that never answers leaves the prune control terminally spinning: `pruning` is set true at :295 and cleared only by onPruneDone, which only runs after the awaited port call settles — and there is no AbortController, AbortSignal or timeout anywhere in demo/. The identical shape strands loadingUserPalettes and the disclosure skeletons.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:295,304,359-364; usePalettePorts.ts:121-124; demo/platform/transport/client.ts:67-92 (fetch(input, init) with no signal, inside a retry loop). `grep -rn "AbortController\|AbortSignal" demo/ | wc -l` → 0. probe/aup-probe4.mjs H1: `t+1000ms {"disabled":true,"spinner":true}` / `t+5000ms …true` / `t+10000ms …true`.
defects.mechanism: work started with no bounded termination (mechanism C) — an unbounded promise is the sole clearing path for a UI flag
defects.reproduction: node probe/aup-probe4.mjs chromium H1 — route POST /admin/users/prune-empty to never fulfil; the button spins, disabled, indefinitely; only a reload recovers.
defects.proposedCure: Put the deadline in the transport once: give fetchWithRateLimitRetry an AbortSignal.timeout(ms) composed with any caller signal, so all ~30 API wrappers inherit a bounded wait and ApiProblem/ApiUnavailableError become reachable on a hang. The panel then derives `pruning` from the port's in-flight state instead of hand-toggling it at two call sites — the same move C-1's keyed-resource cure already needs. A per-component setTimeout watchdog would be the contrivance.

defects.defect: NEW. The tail-priority slug pill splits the identifier into two spans inside a flex container; flex items compute display:block, so the identifier is two block boxes. Selecting and copying a slug yields "azure-\nfox-01", innerText carries a newline, and the row's accessible name is announced as two words. This is the measured root of the mangled accName strings both prior seats recorded as probe noise.
defects.evidence:
AdminUsersPanel.vue:97-101, :243-252. probe/aup-probe2.mjs F4, chromium AND webkit byte-identical: {"pillTitle":"azure-fox-01","pillInnerText":"azure-
fox-01","pillTextContent":"azure-fox-01","selectionToString":"azure-
fox-01
","rowInnerText":"azure-⏎fox-01⏎4⏎Palettes","childDisplays":["block","block"],"pillDisplay":"flex"}.
defects.mechanism: a presentation transform destroys the datum it presents — visual truncation implemented by DOM surgery on the string rather than by CSS on one text node (new mechanism D)
defects.reproduction: node probe/aup-probe2.mjs chromium F4 (and webkit) — selects the pill's contents via a Range and reads window.getSelection().toString(), i.e. what the clipboard receives.
defects.proposedCure: Keep one text node and do the tail-priority truncation in CSS: direction:rtl; unicode-bidi:plaintext; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis on a single span. The F-13 intent (two prune candidates stay distinguishable on a phone) is preserved; slugHead/slugTail/SLUG_TAIL (:243-252) delete with it, and the rule lands on the existing .slug-pill recipe at demo/styles/foundation.css:585-587 rather than per instance.

defects.defect: NEW. The app ships a working Idempotency-Key replay store (server middleware mounted globally, covering /admin/*; both transport helpers forward the header) and uses it on palette saves — while EVERY admin destructive verb (prune-empty, deleteUser, deleteUserPalettes, deletePaletteAdmin, featurePalette) sends un-keyed mutations. C-15's double-fire therefore reaches the server as two genuinely distinct prunes, not one replayed request.
defects.evidence: api/src/app.ts:69-73 (`app.use("*", idempotency)`); api/src/platform/http/idempotency.ts:93-99 (opt-in per header); demo/platform/transport/client.ts:112-114 and :145-147 (header forwarded). `grep -rn "idempotencyKey" demo/palettes/api/` → only palettes.ts:80,145,161 (crypto.randomUUID()); `grep -rln idempotencyKey demo/palettes/api/admin-*.ts | wc -l` → 0. demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:69-71 is the un-keyed prune.
defects.mechanism: one concern (mutation replay safety) with two contradictory implementations in one directory — the server-side half of mechanism C, already built and simply not called
defects.reproduction: The greps above are exact. The consequence is measured by node probe/aup-probe4.mjs chromium H2 (two distinct POSTs from one gesture). Rider, source-derived and labelled: the replay key scopes on `c.var.sessionToken ?? c.var.userSlug ?? "anon"` (idempotency.ts:108), which a Bearer-authenticated admin may collapse to "anon" — I did not run the server.
defects.proposedCure: Two lines per admin mutation — { method: "POST", idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID() } — using the header, helper and middleware that already ship; add the admin identity to the server's scope key. Zero new modules. It does not replace C-15's UI cure; it makes the failure of that cure survivable, which is what a destructive console requires.

defects.defect: The nested palette load costumes an error as empty: loadUserPalettes catches and returns [], and :138 renders EmptyState "No palettes." for an empty array. The file's own header comment at :49-50 declares the opposite law ("error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as an empty roster") and honours it for the roster only.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:49-50 vs :138; demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:152-162 ("Returns [] on failure"). probe/aup-probe.mjs R2, chromium AND webkit: `R2 after 500 on /palettes: "· 2 empty | Palettes | · NONE PINNED · | No palettes. | …"` / `R2 shows any error affordance: false`.
defects.mechanism: error-to-neutral coercion at the port boundary (mechanism B): `return []` destroys the failure before the UI can see it
defects.reproduction: node probe/aup-probe.mjs chromium R2 (and webkit) — route /admin/users/*/palettes to 500, expand a user with 4 palettes.
defects.proposedCure: The keyed resource of C-1 returns {palettes, loading, error}; the expanded region renders the same EmptyState variant="error" + Retry the roster already uses at :51-62. One species selector used at both levels — the correct grammar already exists in the file and is merely unreachable from this path.

defects.defect: A failed prune is reported with a success-shaped sentence. onPruneEmpty swallows every error and returns 0; onPruneDone maps 0 to "No empty users to prune" — so a 500, a missing credential and a genuine no-op are one string, printed while the toolbar next to it still reads "· 2 empty".
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:186-199 (two `return 0` paths); AdminUsersPanel.vue:303-309. probe/aup-probe.mjs R4: `[console.error] status 500` then `R4 after a 500 the panel says: "No empty users to prune"` / `R4 still lists empty users: true`.
defects.mechanism: error-to-neutral coercion (mechanism B); onPruneDone(count: number) is the signature defect — a number cannot express failure, so no downstream code can
defects.reproduction: node probe/aup-probe.mjs chromium R4 — route POST /admin/users/prune-empty to 500, prune 2 empty users.
defects.proposedCure: onPruneEmpty returns a result union ({ok, pruned} | {error} | {unauthenticated}); onPruneDone takes it and routes failure into the EmptyState error register the panel already owns.

defects.defect: With no admin token loadAdminUsers returns before touching loading or usersLoadError, so the state ladder falls through to the success-with-no-data plate: an unauthenticated visitor sees "· ROSTER CLEAR · No users found." with no mention of authentication, and the Refresh button issues zero requests forever with no feedback.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface

result.strongestDefect: L-12/L-1 — the component's interactive surface is dead. `@mkbabb/glass-ui`'s `WatercolorDot` is a declared *paint* primitive (`inheritAttrs: !1`, root `<span aria-hidden="true">`, inline `pointer-events: none`, zero slot machinery, six props with no `tag`); the demo mounts it as its primary *control* at 6 sites. Every prop, listener, aria-label and child is silently discarded. Measured: the "Add current color" vnode carries prop keys `["aria-hidden","class","data-testid","data-variant","style"]` — no `onClick` exists to fire — and on an iPhone-13 profile the component's own `.swatch-row` yields 3 swatches with `aria-expanded: null` / `data-state: null`, so Edit/Copy/Remove are unreachable on every touch device. This pass converted that touch BLOCKER from a mechanism inference (all prior probes ran at 1440×900 desktop, where the `!canHover` Popover branch never mounts) into a reproduction.

Every demo import is one a real consumer could write verbatim through the published exports map — T.W1's dogfood keystone holds. This is precisely why the colour-identity and colour-model findings are surface GAPS, not boundary violations. (2) The brief's named suspect "three parallel useDark stores" is CURED — all 10 sites route to `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dark`; the `useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:76` pointer is stale. (5) All four Safari matrices report /#/palettes at overflowX 0, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0, main 1, and none of the 8 smallTapTargets belong to this component — which is itself the finding: the broken controls are aria-hidden and pointer-events:none, so they are invisible to the very probe that would have flagged them.

Playwright, devices["iPhone 13"], savedColors seeded via addInitScript, scoped to CurrentPaletteEditor's own `.swatch-row`: {"swatchRowFound":true,"solidDots":3,"rootTag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"ariaExpanded":null,"dataState":null,"pointerEvents":"none","editCopyRemoveVisible":false,"afterTap":{"editBtn":false,"copyBtn":false,"removeBtn":false}}. `aria-expanded: null` + `data-state: null` are reka-ui's own trigger attributes — their absence proves the as-child merge reached the DOM with nothing.

defects.evidence: demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:206-211 serializes in the colour's OWN space for all 13 members of CSS_PICKER_SPACES (:92-95). savedColorStrings (useColorPipeline.ts:166-168) and cssColorOpaque (:104) both route through it. Measured against dist: ONE physical colour (pure red) -> rgb: 'rgb(255 0 0)' / oklch: 'oklch(62.795536392143% 0.257683303805 29.233880279628deg)' / hsl: 'hsl(0deg 100% 50%)'; savedColorStrings.indexOf(cssColorOpaque) -> -1.

Then delete all three demo predicates and give membership exactly one home in the palette store.

defects.evidence: Three homes: useSwatchActions.ts:63 (indexOf on opaque strings) -> `reordered.push(...)` END at :66; usePaletteWiring.ts:85-89 (serializePickerColor ===) -> `savedColors.unshift(...)` FRONT at :98; useColorPipeline.ts:215-217 (toCSSColorString ===) -> `savedColors.push(...)` END at :220. addCurrentColor handles a hit itself (END) but delegates a miss to emit('addColor') -> emitAddColor -> unshift (FRONT). Wiring confirmed at PalettesPane.vue:45 `@add-color="(css) => colorTarget.emitAddColor(css)"` and :44 `@apply="(colors) => colorTarget.emitApply(colors)"` -> usePaletteWiring.ts:65-73 -> onPaletteApply.
