defects.reproduction: Code-path trace with all three sites and the full emit wiring pasted. Behavioural repro NOT driven — the ordering contradiction is derived from the three call sites, not observed in the UI. Labelled a hypothesis at the behavioural level.
defects.proposedCure: Collapse to one `paletteMembership` module in demo/palettes/ owning both the predicate and the insertion policy, consumed by the swatch UI, the wiring layer and the pipeline alike; delete the three private copies.

defects.defect: The palette wire contract has no single home. It is declared independently in api/src/modules/palette/format.ts (FormattedPalette — the authority, constructed by formatPalette) and hand-transcribed in demo/palettes/types.ts (Palette — what BrowsePane and every pm.* member is typed against). 20 of 22 fields diverge. The transport asserts the transcription without validation. The server publishes a literal discriminant (isLocal: false); the client widens it to boolean, which forces every server-guaranteed field to become optional.
defects.evidence: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe-L4/typediff.mjs` → `DIVERGENT: 20 of 22`. api/src/modules/palette/format.ts:19-47 vs demo/palettes/types.ts:15-71. Unchecked assertion: demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:39-41 `Promise<CursorPaginatedResponse<Palette>>` over `request()`. defects.defect: Three focusable buttons live inside an `aria-hidden="true"` container (axe-core `aria-hidden-focus`, WCAG 4.1.2). Because the panel is teleported to body, they sit at the very end of the tab order, actionable but unannounceable, targeting a swatch the user cannot identify.
defects.evidence: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:40-50 (aria-hidden="true" on the panel) hosting CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:46-54 (three <button>s). probe-B.mjs: {"floatingPanel":{"ariaHidden":"true","buttonsInside":3,"focusableInsideAriaHidden":3}}.
defects.mechanism: aria-hidden used as a fig leaf over a broken second render path rather than the path being fixed
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe-B.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by C-4 — a real Popover needs neither the aria-hidden fig leaf nor a second render path.

defects.defect: The Save button is nameless — icon-only <Button> wrapping a bare <Check> with no aria-label, title or text, while every other icon-only button in the same file carries one. This is the component's contribution to the visual REPORT's namelessButtons count on /#/palettes.

The repo's own e2e documents it in prose instead of failing on it: e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts:40-41 'the icon-only Save button next to the Input lacks an aria-label'.

defects.defect: The duplicate-name refusal is silent to assistive tech: the '"X" already exists.' message has no aria-live / role=status ancestor and focus does not move, so a screen-reader user sees the save simply do nothing.

defects.defect: `swatchKeys` put the array index inside the identity (`${color}::${i}`), so ANY removal or reorder re-mints EVERY key. TransitionGroup therefore never observes a move — it tears down and remounts the whole remaining row, replaying the enter animation and rebuilding a fresh feTurbulence numOctaves=5 SVG filter per surviving swatch.
defects.evidence: useSwatchActions.ts:43-59; consumed at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:24-32. Deterministic re-execution of that exact code: initial ["#f00","#0f0","#00f","#ff0"] -> [0,1,2,3]; after removing index 0 -> [4,5,6] (all three re-minted). Move-to-end reorder (the branch addCurrentColor performs at useSwatchActions.ts:64-68): [0,1,2] -> [3,4,5]. After 200 churn cycles map.size=5, counter=1000. The pre-flush prune at :54-59 deletes exactly the moved entries, guaranteeing the re-mint.
defects.mechanism: lossy projection at a layer boundary — identity re-derived from position instead of carried on the model
defects.reproduction: node -e '<verbatim re-implementation of useSwatchActions.ts:43-59>' (pasted in the report); output as above
defects.proposedCure: Mint an id at insert time on the model: give ColorModel.savedColors entries a crypto.randomUUID() where they are pushed (useColorPipeline.ts:220) and key the v-for on it. That deletes swatchKeys, the Map, the counter and the prune watcher — 17 lines replaced by the field that should have existed.

defects.defect: `colorsFromStrings` projects to `{ css, position }` only, dropping PaletteColor.name and PaletteColor.weight. Because confirmUpdatePalette feeds it into a wholesale `updatePalette(id, { colors })`, updating an extracted palette erases every per-colour name and every quantizer population weight, collapsing PaletteColorStrip to uniform segments.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:243-245 (projection) and :272 (emit "updated"); demo/palettes/types.ts:1-11 declares name?/weight? with weight documented as the quantizer population share that PaletteColorStrip sizes from; usePaletteActions.ts:79-81 `deps.updatePalette(id, { colors })`. Measured in the C-3 store diff — the target's entire colors array, metadata included, was replaced.
defects.mechanism: lossy projection at a layer boundary — the current buffer is string[] and structurally cannot carry metadata
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe-C.mjs (keys storeBeforeUpdate / storeAfterUpdate)
defects.proposedCure: Either merge by position against the target's existing colors on update, or lift the current palette to PaletteColor[] end to end so the lossy projection disappears entirely.

defects.defect: `addCurrentColor` tests colour identity with a raw string `indexOf`, but savedColorStrings serialize in each colour's OWN space while cssColorOpaque serializes in the CURRENT space. After any space switch the same physical colour fails to match, so both the move-to-end branch and the no-op guard become unreachable and the click appears to do nothing.
defects.evidence: useSwatchActions.ts:63 `savedColorStrings.value.indexOf(cssColorOpaque.value)`; useColorPipeline.ts:166-168 vs :104. probe-E.mjs (saved reds in rgb, live colour in oklch, same physical red): {"savedColorStrings":["rgb(255 0 0)","rgb(0 255 0)"],"cssColorOpaque":"oklch(62.8% 0.2577 29.23deg)","indexOfResult":-1}. The fall-through emit is then swallowed downstream by a DIFFERENT predicate — useColorPipeline.ts:213-217 uses canonical toCSSColorString.
defects.mechanism: two identity predicates answering one question; display-string used as an identity key
defects.reproduction: node .../probe/probe-E.mjs
defects.proposedCure: One canonical colour identity exported from the pipeline (toCSSColorString or a space-agnostic key) and used at both comparison sites.

defects.defect: `useLeaveTimer` registers no onScopeDispose, so a pending 250ms close callback survives component unmount.

defects.mechanism: unowned timer in a composable advertised as shared

defects.proposedCure: onScopeDispose(cancel) in useLeaveTimer — or delete the composable entirely under C-4.

defects.defect: The three swatch-action buttons still carry the exact per-site strays the file's own comment declares retired (`active:scale-95`, `transition-colors`), plus `focus-visible:outline-none` which SUPPRESSES the root focus ring in favour of a bespoke one — the same regression this file calls out by name elsewhere. defects.defect: Vacuous gate stack: there is no test that would fail if the component were broken — and it IS broken, while every gate is green. Zero unit coverage; vue-tsc is blind to the whole C-1/C-2 family by construction; CI invokes no Playwright at all, so the one e2e spec written for this flow is RED and unobserved.
defects.evidence: vitest.config.ts:21 includes only test/**/*.ts + demo/test/**/*.ts; `grep -rn "CurrentPaletteEditor|swatchKeys|duplicateTarget|saveCurrentPalette|useSwatchActions" demo/test test` -> 0 hits. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` -> exit 0, zero output at HEAD. `grep -rn "playwright" .github/workflows/*.yml` -> no hits (ci.yml runs lint, vue-tsc x2, build, npm test, api tsc, api test). e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts fails at :37 with a 30s locator timeout.
defects.mechanism: gates that cannot observe the failure class they nominally cover — the mutation that keeps everything green is the shipped code itself
defects.reproduction: npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit ; grep -rn "playwright" .github/workflows/*.yml ; npx playwright test e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts --project=smoke
defects.proposedCure: (1) Wire the existing Playwright smoke suite into ci.yml as a HARD step — it already catches C-1 with zero new assertions. (2) Add a mount-level vitest asserting the three role queries the flow depends on (Add current color / Save current palette / Color swatch) — each fails on HEAD. (3) Add the 20-line 'every template class resolves to >=1 CSS rule' walk from probe-D.mjs, which kills C-4 and C-5 as a family.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design: visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; running as declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D3-04 — the gestalt: `CurrentPaletteEditor` puts five distinct jobs (identity, specimen, status, action, a second action of a different grammar) on one flat `<div>` that is materially a Card (measured `--shadow-cartoon-sm` + `1px dashed` edge + `--well-bg` + `radius:16px`), and sites it inside the Library field — a region the ratified composition (`OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:40`) defines as exactly "owner-state selector; resource field; selected inspector/actions" with "Field, lane, empty state and inspector have zero Cards". It is a compose-and-commit instrument parked in a browse surface. Every other defect in the file — the dead verbs, the three action species, the double dashed empty invitation, the uncapped growth to 38% of an 844px viewport, the unreachable disabled arm — is downstream of that one siting decision.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded as correct rather than defective, with positive evidence: reduced motion resolves to final geometry via the global guard at `animations.css:184-192`; narrow-viewport reflow is clean at 360px with measured `docOverflowX: 0`; the motion family name `vj-enter` is one of the three sanctioned names and animates only opacity/transform, forcing no layout; the singular/plural count copy at `:21` is correct.)

defects.defect: GESTALT — five jobs on one flat div, in a route composition with no seat for any of them. The `.dashed-well` root renders identity (`:5-23`), specimen+action (`:24-113`), status `role="alert"` (`:116`), action (`:117-143`) and a SECOND action in a different grammar (`:144-167`). It is materially a Card inside a region whose Card count must be 0, and it carries two boundary devices at once (dashed edge AND cast shadow). Consequence: on the empty route the pane shows two dashed empty invitations ~200px apart (the well and `EmptyPaletteMark`), and once populated the scratch tray holds the only saturated colour on a route whose actual protagonist (the saved field) is empty.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:5-167 (five zones). Live measured on the well: box-shadow = three-step `--shadow-cartoon-sm`, border `1px dashed oklab(0.216 … / 0.12)`, background `--well-bg`, border-radius 16px. Growth measured: 1440px empty 462×113.88; 390px empty 105.59 → populated 322.2 (38% of an 844px viewport); 360px 308.2 with a 170px swatch block. Action species measured: icon circle 32×40, `Update` 61.8×36, `Cancel` 59.2×36. Canon: OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:40 ("owner-state selector; resource field; selected inspector/actions … Field, lane, empty state and inspector have zero Cards"); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.2 ("one protagonist, one identity line, at most one persistent action/status region"); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:19, :34, §3 law 2 ("≤15% of the stage or disappears"); PR-05, PR-06. Frames: frames-D3/pop-desktop-1440.png, frames-D3/pop-mobile-390.png.
defects.mechanism: composition/siting — an instrument-class component (compose→name→commit) was authored inline into a browse-class field, so it had to invent its own housing, its own action grammar and its own status seat rather than consuming the three regions the ratified composition already provides.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with an empty tray → two dashed invitations visible simultaneously in one column. Seed localStorage["color-picker"]={inputColor,savedColors:[12 lab colours]} and reload at 390×844 → the well measures 322.2px tall, 38% of the viewport, for a scratch surface.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a patch. Split by job into regions that already exist: the draft tray (identity + specimen row) becomes the Library's draft-lane/empty-state content and collapses to a tray when empty; naming+commit moves into the selected inspector/action region where VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 already puts rename/lifecycle/durable operation state; the collision decision becomes a confirmation inside that same region in the one glass-ui action set; the backend status leaves the palette editor entirely. That split simultaneously dissolves D3-02, most of D2-19, PR-05's double boundary, PR-06's three action species, and the duplicate dashed invitation.

defects.defect: One palette, two irreconcilable specimen species, visible on one screen. The same twelve colours render as twelve discrete seeded organic WatercolorDot faces (measured 48×48, per-face `border-radius: 28.1208% 33.6845% 57.986% 49.3693% / 79.1234% …`, per-face feTurbulence/feDisplacementMap) inside the well, and — directly below, after saving — as one continuous hard-edged 40px band with `border-radius: 0` and raw `backgroundColor` segments. The most important state change on the route (draft → saved) is expressed by silently swapping the visual language for the object.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:36 `size-class="w-11 h-11 sm:w-12 sm:h-12"` → measured 48×48 seeded faces; PaletteColorStrip.vue:8-24 `flex h-10 w-full` (=40px), per-segment `backgroundColor: color.css`, no radius, `aria-hidden="true" role="presentation"`. Both species simultaneously present in the live frame frames-D3/duplicate-state.png. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:18 — "Watercolor/data | swatches, active mark, pastel Palettes identity | the only ornamental color-bearing species"; :5 — the product's job is that a person "leaves with an understood … color artifact"; :102 authorises "the card's compact swatch strip … noninteractive data" but not a second rendering technology.
defects.mechanism: visual-language fork — two independently-authored renderings of the same domain object, so the transition between them carries no shared shape, size, edge, rhythm or unit and therefore transmits no identity.
defects.reproduction: Seed localStorage["color-picker"]={inputColor,savedColors:[12 lab colours]}; load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; type a name; press Enter. The 12 blobs in the well and the single 40px band on the new card are on screen together. Frame captured at frames-D3/duplicate-state.png.
defects.proposedCure: One species per object. Either the saved card's compact strip becomes the same seeded WatercolorDot row at a smaller glass-ui rung (the constitution's "compact swatch strip" clause), or the well adopts the band and drops the blobs. Decide once what a palette looks like — the same decision that resolves the dead-host BLOCKER, so it belongs to the same owner.

defects.defect: The "nothing to save" state is not designed, and the control that would express it is structurally unreachable. `:118 v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0"` and `:138 :disabled="savedColorStrings.length === 0"` are complementary predicates on the same expression, so the disabled arm can never evaluate true. Worse than the dead branch: when the tray empties, the entire naming-and-commit region vanishes rather than resting, so the two-step grammar the interface teaches (collect → name and commit) deletes its own second step exactly when a new user is looking at it.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:118 vs :138. Live: with 12 colours the sole well button reports `disabled:false`; with 0 colours the empty-state outerHTML ends `<!--v-if--><!--v-if--><!--v-if-->` and `wellFocusables` is `[]`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 — "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value … are explicit"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.5; owner edicts 2 (no masking fallbacks) and 3 (KISS).
defects.mechanism: dead guard + state-by-removal — a defensive predicate was written against a condition its own mounting guard already excludes, and the state it pretended to cover was then expressed by unmounting the surface instead of resting it.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with an empty tray → no input, no button, `wellFocusables: []`. Populate the tray → both appear, `disabled:false`. There is no frame in which the button renders disabled.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `:disabled` — it is a lie — and keep the save region mounted and genuinely disabled at zero colours, with the count line reading `0 colors` rather than the header swapping to a different sentence. One region, one identity line, one resting action (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.2). Falls out for free once D3-04's split lands.

defects.defect: A design-system context provider is instantiated per component instance, around a control that cannot fire it. `TooltipProvider :delay-duration="200"` is declared inside the leaf template, so this one control's tooltip timing is a local opinion that cannot by construction agree with any other tooltip in the app. Four nodes of design-system machinery (Provider/Tooltip/Trigger/Content) support zero reachable behaviour, because the `as-child` target renders as an inert `<span aria-hidden pointer-events:none>`.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:88-111. Live: the `as-child` target measures `{tagName:"SPAN", tabIndex:-1, aria-hidden:"true", pointer-events:"none", aria-label:null}`, so the trigger can never fire. Canon: owner edict 5 (style/configure at the root component level, never per-instance) and edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.6 — "do not compensate for an unnecessary action with tooltip proliferation. Subtraction precedes explanation."
defects.mechanism: design-system boundary crossing — a context owner (not a leaf primitive) instantiated at a leaf, making a system-wide property into a per-site value.
defects.reproduction: Read CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:88. Live at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: hover the add slot for 3s → no tooltip appears (pointer-events:none measured); no other tooltip in the app shares this provider instance.
defects.proposedCure: One `TooltipProvider` at the app root; delete this one. Once the add slot becomes a real named `<button>`, the tooltip is redundant with the button's own accessible name and should be removed rather than relocated.

defects.defect: Every verb the component owns is written onto a decoration. All 13 WatercolorDot faces (12 colours + the add slot) render as `<span aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" style="pointer-events:none">` with the consumer's `aria-label` and default-slot `<Plus>` glyph both dropped — glass-ui 7 executed the `P051` abrogation at VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91 and this consumer never executed its half. Add, edit, copy, remove and select are unreachable by pointer, keyboard and AT simultaneously.
defects.evidence: Live probe: 13/13 faces `{tagName:"SPAN", tabIndex:-1, ariaHidden:"true", pointerEvents:"none", ariaLabel:null}`. `page.click(".add-slot-ghost",{force:true})` ×5 with slider nudges between → swatch count 0 → 0. Empty-well outerHTML contains only the watercolor filter svg and the ghost-stroke span — no lucide `<Plus>` node. Populated `wellFocusables` = `[INPUT "<<NO ACCESSIBLE NAME>>", BUTTON "<<NO ACCESSIBLE NAME>>"]`: 12 colours × 3 verbs = 36 actions, 0 reachable. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91 — "V abrogates a selection outline and interactive host on WatercolorDot. P051 removes the public tag=\"button\"/interactive-host branch"; the file still passes `tag="button"` at :98 and SwatchHoverMenu.vue:15,32.
defects.mechanism: unexecuted producer ruling — the design system removed the interactive-host branch; the consumer kept writing activation semantics onto the ornamental face, so the semantics land on nothing.
defects.reproduction: node probe (docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/probe-D3-pass3-a.mjs): load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, click `.add-slot-ghost` five times with force:true → `document.querySelectorAll('.dashed-well [aria-label^="Color swatch"]').length` stays 0.
defects.proposedCure: Give every verb a named geometric seat as the constitution already specifies ("Selection, activation, drag and keyboard focus belong to a named enclosing geometric button/seat", :91): a real `<button type="button">` wrapping each face, with the face aria-hidden inside it. Delete `tag="button"` from every WatercolorDot call site. This is the same decision as D3-01 and lands with D3-04's split.

defects.defect: The desktop swatch action menu is styled by a phantom class. `.floating-panel` has zero rules anywhere in the live CSSOM, so `position` resolves to `static`, the inline `top/left` computed by `useHoverPopover.positionPanel` are inert, and the Teleported menu renders as an unstyled full-width strip at the very bottom of the document — 900px below the swatch it describes — with no background, shadow, radius or z-index, while growing document scrollHeight 900 → 940. This is exactly the `inv-N-7` phantom-class failure that `.dashed-well` was minted to cure (utils.css:86), recurring uncured.
defects.evidence: Live CSSOM walk over every stylesheet including nested rules: `cssRulesDefiningFloatingPanel: 0`. Computed on the live panel: `position:"static"`, inline `"top: 305.156px; left: 791px;"`, rect `{x:0, y:900, w:1440, h:40}`, `background rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `boxShadow "none"`, `borderRadius "0px"`, `zIndex "auto"`, `aria-hidden "true"`; `docScrollH 940` vs `viewportH 900`. Repo-wide grep for `floating-panel` returns only SwatchHoverMenu.vue:42 (the usage), useHoverPopover.ts:7 (a comment) and animations.css:2 (a comment) — no rule. Frame: frames-D3/hover-panel-full.png shows the pencil/copy/trash glyphs at the document's bottom-left corner.
defects.mechanism: phantom style atom — a class name is applied and positioned by JS but was never defined in CSS, so absolute positioning silently degrades to static flow at the end of `<body>`.
defects.reproduction: node probe (probe-D3-pass3-b.mjs): seed 12 colours, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 1440×900, hover the first swatch, read `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.floating-panel'))` → position static, rect y=900. Frame at frames-D3/hover-panel-full.png.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-rolled hover/Teleport path entirely and consume the glass-ui Popover the touch branch already uses — one accessible, producer-positioned surface for both modalities. Retiring the fork also retires `useHoverPopover`'s hardcoded `offsetY = -42` magic offset, its lack of scroll/resize repositioning inside an `overflow-y-auto` pane, and its viewport-edge collision blindness.

defects.defect: The name-collision state — a destructive overwrite prompt — is announced to nobody, associated with nothing, and speaks a third action grammar. The `"{name}" already exists.` line is a bare `<span>` with no `role`, no `aria-live`, no association to the input (`aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid` absent), and focus does not move. A screen-reader user presses Enter, the save silently does not happen, and nothing is said.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:144-167. Live with the collision on screen: live regions inside the well = only the ApiOfflineChip `role="alert"`; `document.activeElement` = the same INPUT; the message span carries no role/aria-live. Confirm controls measured `Update` 61.8×36 and `Cancel` 59.2×36 — two 36px text pills adjacent to a 32×40 nameless icon circle, i.e. three action species in one column. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 ("Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit") and §5 ("Commit uses one glass-ui action set"); PR-06, PR-08. Frame: frames-D3/duplicate-state.png.
defects.mechanism: failure state authored as decoration — an error was rendered as prose next to two ad-hoc pills rather than as an associated, announced, focus-managed state of the field that produced it.
defects.reproduction: Seed 12 colours, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, name the palette `Dup` and press Enter; reload, name it `Dup` again and press Enter. The collision row appears with no live region and focus unchanged (measured `active: INPUT/Palette 2`).
defects.proposedCure: Make the collision a state of the field: `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` pointing at a `role="alert"` message, focus moved to the decision, and the Update/Cancel pair expressed in the one glass-ui action set the commit control already uses. It relocates into the selected-inspector action region under D3-04's split.

result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — but the following were interrogated and could not be broken, and are recorded as INFO so the next seat does not re-spend the time. (1) The brief's hazard list is genuinely absent from this component: grep over BrowsePane.vue finds no `defineModel`, no `requestAnimationFrame`, no `ValueUnit`, no WebGL, no IntersectionObserver/ResizeObserver, no setTimeout/setInterval, no addEventListener, no slider — the stale-defineModel, PRM-RAF, ValueUnit-nesting, reka pointer-capture and WebGL-context-loss classes do not apply here. `verbatimModuleSyntax` is honoured (`import type { Palette, Tag }` at :197). (2) Tap-target and accessible-name geometry: BrowsePane's contribution is ZERO. On a fully-loaded six-card wall at 1440x900 in Chromium I measured `smallTargets: []` and `namelessButtons: 0` scoped to `main`; the pane's own search field measures 375x38. The `{"w":160,"h":23,"tag":"input","label":""}` row in REPORT.json for /#/browse is NOT BrowsePane's — the same four small targets appear on all fifteen routes (the dock's slug widget). (3) Keyboard reachability was deliberately NOT born-RED, per MT-F022: the route's 7/12 Chromium gap is roving-tabindex-shaped and this seat ran one engine. The focus finding filed (N-2) is not reachability — it is a measured focus DESTRUCTION on activation ("More from the commons" -> BODY), which no roving-tabindex design produces. (4) The `<Transition>` state machine is sound: three mutually exclusive branches correctly keyed (developing/error/wall), `mode="out-in"` legal with a single child at a time, and the load-more block correctly sits outside it. (5) The generation guard on the fetch itself is CORRECT: `loadRemotePalettes` discards stale responses (useBrowsePalettes.ts:73, 78, 84) and repeated racing probes never produced an out-of-order `remotePalettes` write — the C-2 bug is the guard's SCOPE (extended to a flag it does not own), not its absence.

result.negativeProof:
Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this records what I attacked and could NOT break — including one finding I had drafted and then killed with my own pixels.

1. THE SEATED FIELD'S FOCUS RING PAINTS — my own draft BLOCKER, killed. First measurement supported "no focus indicator": focused, `.search-seated` computed box-shadow gained two layers of `oklab(0 0 0 / 0) 0px 0px 0px 0px` — transparent and zero-sized. The pixels refuted it: blur-vs-focus screenshot diff over the field gives bbox (6,0,484,63), max channel delta 68, 2019 pixels differing > 8 — against a ring perimeter of a 462x36 box at 2px of ~1992px. The null layers were a mid-transition serialisation (`.input-bar` carries `transition: box-shadow var(--duration-fast)` and I sampled in the same tick as .focus()). The `--focus-ring-shadow` token resolves correctly on the bar, and `.search-seated:focus-within` correctly COMPOSES rather than replaces the cartoon stamp — utils.css:140-142 explains why, and it works. Standing trap recorded: a computed box-shadow read inside a transitioning element's first frame is neither its resting nor its settled style.

2. REDUCED MOTION IS HONOURED AT THIS SITE. Under reducedMotion:"reduce", `.vj-morph-enter-active` computes transition-duration 0.1s, animation-name none. STATES.json records rafPer1500ms: 0 for /#/browse against 270 at rest — the renderer loop actually stops, which getAnimations() is structurally blind to (the MT-F022 instrumentation earned this).

3. NO HORIZONTAL OVERFLOW ANYWHERE, INCLUDING RTL. overflowX 0 in all six state matrices and all four Safari matrices; clipped: [] in every one. My own probes at 1440, 390, 320 and the 200% arm independently reproduce overflowX 0. I tried to produce one and could not. The corrected state matrix handed to this seat is accurate.

4. NO DUPLICATE TAG FETCH ON ROUTE ENTRY — a plausible-looking finding, killed by measurement. Entering #/browse issues exactly ONE API request: /palettes?limit=50&sort=newest. `onMounted(() => pm.tagEdit.loadAllTags())` (BrowsePane.vue:222-224) produced no second read; the shared port's catalog is already resolved.

5. verbatimModuleSyntax IS HONOURED. BrowsePane.vue:197 — `import type { Palette, Tag }`. No mixed type/value import in the file.

6. MOTION IS TOKENIZED AND NO ANIMATION IS DELETED (owner edict 6). BrowsePane defines no local keyframes, removes none, and names only producer tokens (duration-fast, the vj-morph family).

7. KEYBOARD REACHABILITY NOT BORN-RED (MT-F022 honoured). I did not raise the 7/12 figure. The one keyboard consequence I record is a concurrence with pass-2's D-11, and it is engine-invariant by construction — PaletteCard.vue:5-25 is a `<div role="article">` with no tabindex and no key handler, so no engine can focus it — and it is not a roving group: my Chromium walk shows 25 individually-tabbable stops inside the pane (every vote chip and every card menu), which is the opposite of roving.

LABELLED HYPOTHESIS (not claimed as a finding): the dark structural plate may violate VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2's restrained-neutral-pole law — sampled rgb(66,55,47), hue 25deg, HSV saturation 28.8% in dark against rgb(233,225,217), hue 30deg, 6.9% in light, i.e. ~4x more chromatic. But HSV saturation on a translucent surface composited over a live chromatic aurora does not measure the surface's own tint, and pass-2's H-2 already flags the captured field as seed-dependent rather than scheme-dependent. A real finding needs the plate's own background-color token sampled against a neutral ground, in two seeds.

OPERATOR DISCLOSURE: to reach the populated wall (no prior pass had rendered it from production rows in this seat's evidence set) I ran a read-only GET-only CORS mirror on :9101 and a second Vite dev server on :9010 with VITE_API_URL set. The second instance shares node_modules/.vite and its optimiser replaced the deps directory under the owner's running :9000 server, which then served 504 (Outdated Optimize Dep). I detected it, stopped both probe servers, and restarted :9000 exactly as it had been running (npx vite --port 9000 --strictPort); verified recovered (textLen 324 on /#/browse, HTTP 200). No repository file outside docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/ was touched.

defects.defect: The component was orphaned by a single commit and the sweep gate that should have caught it was defeated by the barrel that exists to protect it. `95993197` (T.W0 legacy sweep) deleted `PaletteDialog/components/PaletteControlsBar.vue`, the sole render site. The same commit correctly cascaded-deleted `ImagePaletteExtractor.vue` for the identical reason but stopped one component short — and its §8 *improved* the orphan (iconOnly migration, geometry delta flagged) in the same commit; `f2c8f565` then touched it again. 243 lines maintained across two tranches with zero render path.
defects.evidence: `git log --oneline -S"<PaletteSlugBar" -- demo` → `95993197`. `git show 95993197 -- demo | grep -n PaletteSlugBar` → lines 800 (`-        <PaletteSlugBar`), 874 (`-import PaletteSlugBar from …`), 921 (`-const slugBarRef = …`), all deletions inside PaletteControlsBar.vue, plus line 36 = the §8 improvement note. `git log --oneline -- demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue` → f2c8f565, a61094e3.
defects.mechanism: Dead-module retention behind a live-looking barrel: a text-grep liveness gate cannot distinguish (a) a barrel re-export of the module under test or (b) an `import type` edge (erased at build) from a real consumer. Both survivors existed here, so `grep all imports before delete` returned non-empty and the cascade halted.
defects.reproduction: `git log --oneline -S"<PaletteSlugBar" -- demo` then `git show 95993197 -- demo | grep -n PaletteSlugBar`; and `grep -rn "PaletteSlugBar|palette-slug-bar" demo src test e2e` → 4 hits, none a mount.
defects.proposedCure: Fix the gate, not just the file. Replace the text-grep liveness protocol with a reachability sweep: start from the entry module + the router component map, walk template/h()/dynamic-import edges, print every `demo/**/*.vue` never reached — discounting, by construction, barrel re-exports of the module under test and all `import type` edges. Run it in CI. At HEAD it prints PaletteSlugBar.vue and demo/palettes/browser/index.ts. Then delete demo/palettes/browser/slug/ entire (SFC + 3-line barrel) and browser/index.ts:44.

defects.defect: The gh-pages production build emits ZERO application code. The entry chunk is 698 bytes containing only Vite's modulepreload polyfill. Root cause candidate: the demo has no entry module — its composition root is an inline `<script type="module">` in index.html, and no main.ts has ever existed in repo history. Consequence: no component in this demo, orphan or live, can be certified against a production artefact, and both this run's and run 1's tree-shake/byte-cost questions are unanswerable at HEAD.
defects.evidence: `npx vite build --mode gh-pages --outDir <scratch>/ghp --emptyOutDir` → `✓ built in 8.14s`. `ls -la <scratch>/ghp/assets/*.js` → `698 index-Dezn_h7o.js` + `11774 quantize-worker-*.js`; `find <scratch>/ghp -name '*.js' | wc -l` → 2. `grep -n 'createApp|App.vue|app.mount' <scratch>/ghp/index.html` → no match (exit 1). Probes for "Switch account", "My Palettes", "EMPTY PLATE", "unique identity", "enter slug or token" across all emitted js → all 0. Committed dist/gh-pages is identical (same chunk name, same 698 bytes, mtime Jul 27 18:46). Source: demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213. `git log --oneline --all -- demo/color-picker/main.ts` → empty.
defects.mechanism: Missing module boundary at the composition root. "Where does the application begin" is answered inside a markup file, so the root has no place in the module lattice: not typechecked as an entry (tsconfig.demo.json includes demo/, not HTML), not importable by a test, invisible to every rule in eslint.config.js. Vite serves inline modules in dev (60 healthy dev captures in the visual audit) but the build consumes the block and emits none of its graph — dev/prod divergence with the root as the fault line. This is the W44 §F 'gh-pages prod-preview empty-mount' carry, now localised.
defects.reproduction: `npx vite build --mode gh-pages --outDir /tmp/ghp --emptyOutDir` then `ls -la /tmp/ghp/assets/*.js` and `grep -c createApp /tmp/ghp/assets/index-*.js` → 698 bytes, 0. Falsifiable next step (not run — this seat may not edit demo/): extract demo/color-picker/main.ts with those 7 lines, point `<script type="module" src="./main.ts">` at it, rebuild, assert the entry chunk > 698 bytes and contains createApp.
defects.proposedCure: Create demo/color-picker/main.ts as the real entry, referenced by src=. The fouc-guard boot script (index.html:159-203, pre-paint, intentionally inline/blocking) stays inline; the APPLICATION root becomes a module — typechecked, importable, testable, present in the graph. Add a 3-line CI gate asserting the emitted entry chunk contains createApp, which would have failed the wave this landed in.

defects.defect: The demo's declared @mkbabb/value.js surface is wider than the published exports map by three specifiers and narrower by one. tsconfig.demo.json declares the bare root, /parsing and /units — none published, and neither src/subpaths/ nor dist/subpaths/ contains parsing or units — while omitting /css, which is published and imported by 10 demo files. This is a live false proof of the public API: a demo author can write an import that typechecks here and that no consumer of the published package could write.
defects.evidence: `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports))"` → ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize'] — 7 keys, no '.'; `main: undefined types: undefined` (so bare-root import = ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED). tsconfig.demo.json:42-49 declares 8 keys including `@mkbabb/value.js`, `/parsing`, `/units`, and omits `/css`. `ls src/subpaths/` → color,css,easing,math,quantize,transform,value (no parsing, no units). Its own comment at tsconfig.demo.json:37-41 calls it 'a CLOSED 8-key set'.
defects.mechanism: Asymmetric derivation. The Vite alias set is GENERATED from package.json#exports (vite.config.ts:37-50, with an explicit comment that this makes drift impossible), while the tsconfig paths are hand-rolled — so the type surface silently drifted from the runtime surface by 3 phantom keys + 1 missing live key when the exports map was narrowed.
defects.reproduction: `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports))"` vs `sed -n '42,49p' tsconfig.demo.json` vs `ls src/subpaths/ dist/subpaths/`. Blast radius today is zero: `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"|/parsing|/units' demo src test e2e` → no hits (all 49 demo imports use the 5 real subpaths: color 24, css 10, math 6, easing 5, quantize 4).
defects.proposedCure: Generate the tsconfig paths from package.json#exports exactly as the Vite aliases already are — a prebuild step emitting a generated tsconfig.paths.json that tsconfig.demo.json extends — making drift structurally impossible instead of comment-enforced. Then rule explicitly on the bare root: either add '.' to exports or delete it from the paths map. Today it is claimed and unshipped.

defects.defect: `.slug-pill` is a demo-local design primitive that glass-ui should own (glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes ./chip and ./badge), with a per-instance `:style` ink contract documented only in a CSS comment. result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue (area: palettes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the 1M-context variant. Spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration and served by it; nothing inherited or delegated.
result.strongestDefect: C-3 — the filter popover has no height contract: `max-height:none`, `overflow-y:visible`, no scroll container, and it ignores the `--reka-popper-available-height` variable reka publishes for it. With a populated tag catalog the content is 670.8px and "Clear all filters" is FULLY off-screen at 1440x1000, 1440x800 and 390x664; a real Playwright pointer click failed for 30s with "element is visible, enabled and stable ... element is outside of the viewport". At mobile the entire "Find by Color" section — the component's reason to exist — is below the fold with no scrollbar. Root cause is in glass-ui 7's `PopoverContent` root class list, which the same design system's Combobox family already fixes with `max-h-[min(24rem,var(--reka-combobox-content-available-height,60dvh))]`. It is strictly worse in reach than C-1 and it explains why C-1 and C-2 survived this long: the surface that would expose them falls off the bottom of the screen.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field records the probes that came back clean — including four hypotheses I formed and then killed by measurement, so the next seat does not re-spend them. (1) `pr-16` survives glass-ui's `.field-control`: paddingRight 64px, text-lane right edge 580.0 vs Search-button left edge 587.4 = 7.4px clearance (overlapPx -7.4); the `class` prop merges onto Input's single `<input>` root, so no wrapper mis-targeting. (2) No colour-text autofill at popover open — I predicted MiniColorPicker's `{immediate:true}` hex watcher would stamp `#4488cc` into the field; measured `{"inputValue":"","placeholderShown":true}`. RETRACTED. (3) Typed text survives close/reopen: "rebeccapurple" -> "rebeccapurple". (4) `miniPickerOpen` does not leak across the outer popover's unmount — open mini (wrappers 2, sv 1) -> outside click (0,0) -> reopen (wrappers 1, sv 0, miniAutoOpened false). RETRACTED. (5) The nested popover does not dismiss its parent: outer stays open through open + a 12-move SV drag (outerStillOpen true both times). (6) No `<label>` double-fire: clicking the row text gives clicksOnControl 1, stateChanges ["checked"]. (7) Radio wiring is correct (modelValue/update:modelValue match the .d.ts; `value=""` round-trips as `update:tier: [[""]]`) — this is what makes C-1 an asymmetry rather than a harness artifact. (9) No repo-record local hazards: no rAF (PRM-RAF clean), no WebGL, no ValueUnit wrapping, no defineModel (so the stale-read hazard does not apply), no timers/listeners/observers/cleanup owed/unbounded growth. defects.defect: The tag-filter checkboxes are bound to `:checked` / `@update:checked`, a prop and an emit glass-ui 7's Checkbox does not have (its contract is `modelValue` / `update:modelValue`). `:checked` degrades to an inert DOM attribute, the listener waits for an event nobody emits, and the checkbox runs UNCONTROLLED. Selecting a tag filters nothing — while the control fills in and sets `aria-checked="true"`, announcing success to sighted and AT users simultaneously. The badge, which reads the never-changing `selectedTags` prop, stays empty in the same frame — the component contradicts itself.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Contract: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts (CheckboxProps has modelValue/defaultValue/disabled/value/id/class; emits {"update:modelValue": (value: CheckedState) => any}) — no `checked`, no `update:checked`. LIVE reproduction with a 3-tag catalog (probes/probe-C2.mjs, evidence/probeC2.json): before {states:["unchecked","unchecked","unchecked"], badge:"", checkedAttr:["false","false","false"]} -> after click {states:["unchecked","checked","unchecked"], aria:["false","true","false"], badgeText:""} and netAfterTagClick = the UNCHANGED boot triple [GET /colors/approved, GET /palettes?limit=50&sort=newest, GET /colors/tags] — not one request fired. Family is 2 of 2: grep -rn "<Checkbox" demo/ -> TagEditPopover.vue:27, SearchFilterBar.vue:51; both miswired identically.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui 7.0.0 whole-major API drift, unmigrated: pre-7 shadcn-vue `checked`/`update:checked` surface left pointed at a component whose surface is now `modelValue`/`update:modelValue`. Vue silently accepts unknown props as fallthrough attrs, so the miswire is invisible without strictTemplates.
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/probe-C2.mjs  (dev server live at :9000; the probe route-mocks /colors/tags to [{name:pastel},{name:neon},{name:earth}] and neuters assertApiAttemptAllowed so localhost may reach the mocked API). Read the `checkbox`, `checkboxAfter` and `netAfterTagClick` keys.
defects.proposedCure: Bind the real contract: `:model-value="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)"` + `@update:model-value="() => toggleTag(tag.name)"` (toggleTag already derives the next array, so the CheckedState payload is discardable here). Apply identically at TagEditPopover.vue:28-29 where the payload IS used: `(v) => onToggle(tag.name, v === true)`. The gestalt cure is the C-7 transposition — turn on `strictTemplates` so this whole class becomes a compile error instead of a silent runtime lie.

defects.defect: The filter popover can neither shrink nor scroll. `max-height: none`, `overflow-y: visible`, no scrollable ancestor, `scrollHeight === clientHeight`, and it never consumes the `--reka-popper-available-height` variable reka publishes for exactly this purpose. With a populated tag catalog the content is 670.8px tall and "Clear all filters" — the only escape hatch from a bad filter state — is FULLY off-screen at every viewport tested, unreachable by pointer. At 390x664 the popover renders SORT, TIER and the bare word TAGS; the tag list, the entire Find-by-Color section and the Clear row are all below the fold with no scrollbar and no affordance hinting more exists.
defects.evidence: probes/probe-C4.mjs -> evidence/probeC4.json. 1440x1000: content 670.8px, maxHeight "none", overflowY "visible", scrollableAncestor null, scrollHeight 669 == clientHeight 669, --reka-popper-available-height 569.01px, bottomOverflow 101.8px, clearRect.top 1036.4, clearFullyOffscreen true. 1440x800: 670.8px, available 469.01px, overflow 201.8px, clear top 936.4, fully offscreen. 390x664: 630.4px, available 371.02px, overflow 259.4px, clear top 858.1, fully offscreen. Discovered by a REAL pointer click failing: `locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded ... locator resolved to <button ... variant="ghost" ...> - element is visible, enabled and stable - scrolling into view if needed - done scrolling - element is outside of the viewport` (62 identical retries). Screenshots: evidence/C-r2-overflow-{desktop-1440x1000,laptop-1440x800,mobile-390x664}.png. Root cause — glass-ui PopoverContent root class list (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js): "popover-content z-popover w-72 glass-floating [--overlay-pad-inline:1rem] [--overlay-pad-block:calc(var(--overlay-pad-inline)*1.272)] px-(--overlay-pad-inline) py-(--overlay-pad-block) glass-reveal"; `grep -c available-height` on that module = 0; `grep -oE 'max-h-[^ ]*'` = no output. Self-indicting asymmetry — the same system's Combobox does it right in dist/styles/components.css: `.max-h-\[min\(24rem\,var\(--reka-combobox-content-available-height\,60dvh\)\)\]{max-height:min(24rem,var(--reka-combobox-content-available-height,60dvh))}`.
defects.mechanism: A floating overlay primitive with no height contract: the design system's PopoverContent declares neither a max-height bounded by the viewport nor an inner scroll container, so content height is unbounded and floating-ui's collision shift is the only (insufficient) mitigation. Compounded in this file by glass-ui's RadioGroupItem carrying a 44x44 hit target inside a 31px label row — 5 radios = 285px of the 670.8px.
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/probe-C4.mjs  (runs 1440x1000, 1440x800, 390x664; opens the Filters popover, selects Tier=Featured to mount the Clear row, measures and screenshots). Or, for the pointer-unreachability proof directly: probe-C3.mjs, which throws `locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded ... element is outside of the viewport`.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a patch on this file: add the height contract to glass-ui 7's `PopoverContent` root — `max-h-[min(var(--reka-popover-content-available-height,80dvh),80dvh)] overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain` — mirroring the Combobox rule the same package already ships. This fixes every glass Popover in the constellation at once. defects.defect: The "Find by Color" text field is decorative. `applyColorSearch` masks every input that is not an exact 6-digit hex — 3-digit hex, 8-digit hex, hsl(), oklch(), named colours, whitespace, the empty string, outright garbage — replacing it with `pickerHex.value` (default #4488cc), then setting `colorSearchActive = true` and emitting. The badge increments and the wall filters, so the user is shown a SUCCESSFUL search for a colour they never asked for. The placeholder advertises the capability it discards (`placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)"`).
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225, the ternary `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;` (line 218) — a masking fallback, a direct violation of owner edict 2. LIVE (probes/probe-C2.mjs, evidence/probeC2.json): typed `totally-not-a-color`, clicked Search -> {"badgeText":"1", "fieldStillReads":"totally-not-a-color", "swatchLabel":"Open color picker, current color #4488cc", "errorTextPresent":false, "clearAllPresent":true}. The guard is also unnecessary: hexToOklab (line 205) calls parseColorIn -> demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:11 -> parsePickerColor -> parseCssColor (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113), which parses all of the rejected inputs correctly and throws a typed PickerColorError on genuine failure (picker-color.ts:112) — the exact signal a 'no such colour' affordance needs, discarded.
defects.mechanism: A masking fallback substituted for an error path: a narrowing regex in front of a parser that is already total, with the rejection routed to a silent default instead of to the user. The component has no error surface at all, which is why the fallback exists and why it cannot be fixed by deleting the regex alone.
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/probe-C2.mjs ; read the `garbageSearch` key. By hand: open http://localhost:9000/#/browse, click the Filters button, type `hsl(120 100% 50%)` into the colour field, press Enter — the wall filters against #4488cc and the badge reads 1.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the regex and the fallback; parse the text and surface the failure. `const text = colorText.value.trim(); if (!text) { parseError.value = "Enter a colour."; return; } try { const {L,a,b} = cssToOklab(text); parseError.value = null; colorSearchActive.value = true; emit("colorSearch", L, a, b); } catch (e) { parseError.value = e instanceof PickerColorError ? "Not a CSS colour." : "Search failed."; }` — with parseError rendered into the aria-live region C-8 independently requires. Net: one regex and one fallback out, one honest branch in. Rename hexToOklab -> cssToOklab (see C-13); it was never hex-only.

defects.defect: Zero test coverage, and all three gates are structurally blind to the two API-drift blockers. No spec anywhere references this component; the visual gate never opens the popover, so 12 of its 13 controls are outside its reach; `strictTemplates` is unset, so vue-tsc accepts unknown props and unknown on* handlers as fallthrough attrs and reports the file clean. Any mutation is vacuous.

With one config line added (probes/tsconfig.strictTemplates-probe.json adds "vueCompilerOptions":{"strictTemplates":true}): 271 error TS lines demo-wide, 8 on this file — (5,25) TS2353 'variant' does not exist; (52,38) 'checked' does not exist; (53,38) 'onUpdate:checked' does not exist; (89,46) TS2322 Type 'string | number' is not assignable to type 'string'; (93,37) 'aria-label'; (95,38) 'onKeydown'; (112,29) 'variant'; (115,30) 'onClick'. Full text at evidence/C-r2-strictTemplates-SearchFilterBar.txt. Visual gate blindness: audit/visual/REPORT.json safari-desktop-light /#/browse records "dialog": 0 and 4 small tap targets (input 160x23 + three 22x22 buttons "Switch to slug"/"Generate new slug"/"Cancel") — all PaletteSlugBar's; the popover is never opened.
defects.mechanism: A gate set that cannot see the failure mode the codebase actually has. vue-tsc's default strictTemplates:false makes component prop/emit contracts unenforced precisely when a design system takes a major version; the visual matrix samples only default route state, so overlay-resident UI is unaudited; and there is no unit or e2e coverage to fall back on.
defects.reproduction: Vacuous-mutation proof: delete the entire <PopoverContent> subtree (lines 16-122) and replace <script setup> with `const emit = defineEmits<{}>()` — `npm test` and `npm run test:e2e` both stay green. Gate-blindness proof: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` (clean) then `npx vue-tsc -p docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/tsconfig.strictTemplates-probe.json --noEmit` (8 errors on this file, 271 demo-wide).
defects.proposedCure: Set "vueCompilerOptions": { "strictTemplates": true } in tsconfig.base.json — the single highest-leverage repair here, converting the entire prop/emit-drift class (2 Checkbox sites + 51 Button sites + the rest of the 271) from silent runtime breakage into compile errors. It has one honest prerequisite, measured: 3 of this file's 8 errors are glass-ui DECLARATION GAPS, not demo defects — aria-label and onKeydown on Input, onClick on Button all reach the DOM at runtime (Input sets inheritAttrs:false and spreads forwardedAttrs onto its <input> root; the a11y tree reports textbox "Search by CSS color"; the Clear button's click demonstrably fires). So glass-ui must declare its native attribute surfaces on InputProps/ButtonProps first — a BH/BI relay item. Separately: add an e2e spec that opens the popover and asserts a tag click changes the result set, and extend the visual matrix with an overlays-open pass.

defects.defect: The loading state is dead code. `applyColorSearch` is declared `async` but contains no `await`, so it runs to completion synchronously and `searching` goes true->false inside one call, before Vue's scheduler gets a turn. The spinner can never mount, `:disabled` can never apply, and the reentrancy guard protects against a reentrancy a synchronous function cannot have.

defects.mechanism: An async ceremony wrapped around a synchronous computation — five pieces of machinery (async keyword, ref, try/finally, :disabled binding, Loader2 import) that transact nothing, because the work they model happens in a parent computed rather than over the network.

defects.defect: "Clear all filters" unmounts itself while focused. It lives under `v-if="activeFilterCount > 0"`; activating it zeroes the filters, `activeFilterCount` falls to 0, and the focused button is removed from the DOM mid-activation. Focus falls to <body>, which trips reka's dismissable-layer focus-outside handling, so the ENTIRE filter popover closes as a side effect of clearing filters.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:110-120 (v-if wrapper), :227-232 (onClearAll), BrowsePane.vue:329-332 (onClearFilters). LIVE (probes/probe-C2.mjs, evidence/probeC2.json), focus set then activated — exactly what keyboard activation does: clearAll {"active":"Clear all filters"} -> clearAllAfter {"activeTag":"BODY", "activeText":"->BrowseToolsBrowsePalettes Login  @mbabb", "clearStillPresent": null, "badgeText":""}. `clearStillPresent: null` means no popper content wrapper remained in the DOM — the panel dismissed itself.
defects.mechanism: Conditional rendering of a control keyed on state that the control itself resets: the element destroys its own focus anchor, and in a focus-scoped overlay that destruction reads as focus-outside and cascades into a dismissal. Compounds with C-3: because the Clear row is off-screen at every tested viewport, the only reachable activation path is the keyboard, so a keyboard user must Tab to a control they cannot see (WCAG 2.4.7, 2.4.11), activate it blind, and then have focus dumped to <body> (2.4.3).

defects.proposedCure: Keep the row mounted and disable it: `:disabled="activeFilterCount === 0"`. KISS, it preserves the focus anchor, and it stops the popover resizing under the pointer — which also removes one of the two states C-3 has to fit. If the row must stay conditional, move focus to the popover content root before the state change.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure under demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, as declared at spawn. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: LP2-1 by severity: the Tags filter is inert — `:checked`/`@update:checked` are not glass-ui 7's Checkbox surface (it declares `modelValue` + `update:modelValue`), so `toggleTag` is never invoked and the control silently does nothing; Vue's attribute fallthrough makes it invisible to vue-tsc. LP2-3 is the strongest NEW finding (neither pass 1 nor the prior library-audit seat has it): the published `toRgba8` is not channel-symmetric — three mathematically identical RGB channels project to `[77,76,77]` because `roundHalfEven`'s magnitude-scaled epsilon (~1 ulp at byte scale) resolves per-channel what is one decision; 67/255 of the half-byte ladder yields non-neutral bytes from a colourless input, including `hsv(0,0,0.5/255) -> [1,0,0]`.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but two negatives are load-bearing and were proven, not assumed — on the axis the CHALLENGE-L premise most directly names, the structure is RIGHT. (1) The demo's consumption of @mkbabb/value.js is genuinely honest: `grep -rn 'from "\(\.\./\)*src/' demo --include=*.ts --include=*.vue` returns ZERO hits across the entire demo tree. The five specifiers in use (`/color` x24, `/css` x10, `/math` x6, `/easing` x5, `/quantize` x4) are all real keys in package.json#exports, and vite.config.ts:38-49 GENERATES the self-alias set from that exports map with anchored regexes, resolving to dist/subpaths/*.js — the built artifact, not src/. A real npm consumer could write every import the demo writes. Pass 1 proved the same via `tsc --traceResolution`; two independent methods agree. This is a true proof of the public API. (2) No wrong-direction edge from this component: its five targets are demo/ui/* (sibling infra), ./MiniColorPicker.vue (own cluster), ../../types (own area), @lucide/vue (leaf), ../../../color-session/color-utils (peer/spine, downward). It reaches nothing in demo/color-picker/ (boot), demo/shell/, or src/ internals. (3) glass-ui composition uses the design system's own contract: SearchFilterBar is slotted into glass-ui SearchBar's default slot (BrowsePane.vue:15-26); SearchBar's compiled definition ends in `A(n.$slots,"default")` after its own input. No glass-ui internal reached, no variant forked into demo/ui/, scoped styles use only tokens (--font-serif, --type-small, --radius-md, --duration-fast, --ease-standard, --accent) with no hard-coded colour and no glass-root override. (4) verbatimModuleSyntax clean (:144 `import type { Tag }`, the only type-only import); Vue 3.5 idioms correct (reactive props destructure :147; useTemplateRef MiniColorPicker.vue:82-83). (5) Visual matrix: /#/browse is clean for pageErrors(0), horizontalOverflow(0), main(1), namelessButtons(0) in all four Safari matrices (REPORT.md:120-121,135-136,150-151,165-166); the 4 smallTapTargets on that route are PaletteSlugBar's (input 160x23 + three 22x22 "Switch to slug"/"Generate new slug"/"Cancel"), NOT this component.

defects.defect: The Tags filter section is completely inert: SearchFilterBar binds `:checked` and `@update:checked` on glass-ui's Checkbox, but glass-ui 7.0.0 declares neither. Both bindings fall through to $attrs, so `toggleTag` is never invoked and `update:selectedTags` is never emitted; the control is additionally uncontrolled (modelValue undefined) so it can latch visually while selectedTags stays empty forever.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55 binds `:checked="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)"` + `@update:checked="toggleTag(tag.name)"`. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts:4-11 declares `CheckboxProps { modelValue?: CheckedState | null; defaultValue?; disabled?; value?; id?; class? }` — no `checked` — and :21 declares the emit map `{ "update:modelValue": (value: CheckedState) => any }` — no `update:checked`. Blast radius measured: `grep -rn 'update:checked\|:checked=' demo --include=*.vue` returns exactly 4 sites in 2 files, both in this cluster (TagEditPopover.vue:28-29, SearchFilterBar.vue:52-53).
defects.mechanism: Markup written against a retired design-system API. Vue permits arbitrary fallthrough attributes on a component, so vue-tsc cannot reject an ABSENT prop (it is not wrong, it is missing) — the toolchain is structurally unable to see it. Same mistake disables tag filtering in the browse bar and tag editing in the popover.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED by type declaration, not by click — the Playwright MCP profile was held by a concurrent seat ("Browser is already in use for .../mcp-chrome-83447af"). Pass 1 (challenge-L-library-pass1-c654824e.md, its L-1) reports measuring it live; the declarative evidence is independently sufficient since the named prop and emit do not exist in the installed package.
defects.proposedCure: Immediate: `:model-value` + `@update:model-value`. Structural (preferred): the component should own no tag-selection state at all — hoist all four filters into one `useBrowseQuery` store (see LP2-5 lattice) so the bar becomes a stateless view over `v-model:query` and a desynchronised control becomes unwriteable.

defects.defect: NEW — the published `toRgba8` (@mkbabb/value.js/color) is not channel-symmetric: an achromatic colour projects to a tinted byte triple. Three mathematically identical RGB channels round to [77,76,77] (#4d4c4d), a magenta cast on what must be neutral grey.
defects.evidence: src/color/operations.ts:305-312 `roundHalfEven` gates the half-even branch on `Math.abs(fraction - 0.5) < Number.EPSILON * Math.max(1, Math.abs(value))` — approx 1.70e-14 at 76.5, i.e. ~1 ulp. Measured against dist/subpaths/color.js: for hsv(0,0,0.30000000000000004) the three rgb channels are 76.500000000000042633 / 76.500000000000014211 / 76.500000000000028422, whose |frac-0.5| are 4.2633e-14 / 1.4211e-14 / 2.8422e-14 against tol 1.6986e-14 -> branches false/true/false -> bytes 77/76/77. toRgba8 returns [77,76,77,255]. Rate over UI-emittable ladders: v=k/10 accumulation 2/11; v=k/100 0/101; v=k/255 0/256; v=(k+0.5)/255 67/255, including hsv(0,0,0.5/255) -> [1,0,0] (pure red from a colourless input). 0/200000 over random v — rare-but-exact, which is why sampling tests miss it.
defects.mechanism: Two faults compounding: (1) hsv->rgb is not channel-symmetric at s=0, emitting three channels 1-3 ulp apart instead of bit-identical; (2) roundHalfEven's tolerance is scaled by the value's magnitude, so at byte scale it cannot distinguish 'exactly .5' from '0.5 + 2 ulp of upstream conversion error', and it resolves PER CHANNEL what is logically one decision. Net: the library's most depended-on projection is not a pure per-channel map. Structurally this is why the duplicated colour engine (LP2-4) has survived every prior audit — the canonical path is WORSE than the copy on the neutral axis, so nothing ever forced convergence.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED against the published surface: `node` importing dist/subpaths/color.js, scripts at scratchpad/gray.mjs plus inline `node -e` probes (all pasted in report §3 LP2-3). UI reachability is a labelled HYPOTHESIS: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:70 sets `:step="0.001"`, and canonical step quantization puts the V-slider .700 detent at `0.001*700 === 0.7000000000000001` (verified in node), which yields bytes [179,178,179] = #b3b2b3 — the value pickerColorToHex (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:212 via color-model.ts:64) would hand the hex readout and clipboard. I could not confirm reka-ui computes the detent as step*n (no browser).
defects.proposedCure: Make achromaticity structural rather than arithmetic: hsv->rgb at s===0 must emit the value channel three times bit-identically, not compute it three times. Replace roundHalfEven's magnitude-scaled epsilon with one shared rounding decision over the triple (or accept plain half-even on exact .5 and stop treating a float-error window as equality). Add the missing invariant as a property test: for every AnyColor whose RGB channels are equal, toRgba8 returns equal bytes. This must land BEFORE the LP2-4 engine merge.

defects.defect: `variant` is not a key of glass-ui 7's ButtonProps. `variant="ghost"` falls through to $attrs as a literal DOM attribute while `emphasis` takes its declared default `primary`, so buttons authored as the quietest register render at the loudest.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:5 (`variant="ghost" icon-only`) and :111-114 (`variant="ghost" size="sm"`). node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:4-19 declares `ButtonEmphasis = "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"` and `ButtonProps { emphasis?; tone?; size?; iconOnly?; loading?; type?; disabled?; class? }` — no `variant`; the d.ts default block shows `emphasis: ButtonEmphasis` defaulted. Measured surface: `grep -rn 'variant="ghost"' demo --include=*.vue | wc -l` = 28; `grep -rln ... | wc -l` = 19 files.
defects.mechanism: Consumer-side drift across a design-system major, laundered by demo/ui/'s re-export barrels (LP2-7) — the one layer where a migration could have been noticed is the layer that hid it. Vue attribute fallthrough again defeats vue-tsc.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED by type declaration. Pass 1 reports the rendered `data-emphasis="secondary"` measured live. I DISPUTE pass 1's count of "51 sites / 20 files" — I cannot reproduce 51; the ghost-specific figure is 28 occurrences across 19 files (commands pasted in report §2). Likeliest explanation for the divergence is counting all `variant="..."` values (glass-ui Badge DOES declare `variant`, exported via demo/ui/badge/index.ts, so some variant= sites are correct) or including non-demo/ trees. I also DOWNGRADE this from pass 1's BLOCKER to MAJOR: it degrades appearance deterministically but no command stops working, unlike LP2-1.
defects.proposedCure: `emphasis="quiet"` at all 28 sites, migrated in the same pass that deletes demo/ui/ (LP2-7) — removing the laundering layer is what makes this class of drift visible at the point of use in future.

defects.defect: NEW MEASUREMENT — the component's second colour engine and the library disagree on 27.37% of a 14 641-point HSV grid. MiniColorPicker hand-rolls HSV->RGB, a hex serializer, and the hex->HSV inverse inside the demo of a colour library whose published product IS that conversion.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue:85-105 (sextant switch + `:103 const toHex = (c) => Math.round(c*255).toString(16).padStart(2,"0")`) and :110-125 (hex->HSV inverse). Transcribed verbatim and diffed against hsv()->toRgba8() from dist/subpaths/color.js: `samples=14641 mismatches=4007 (27.37%)`, e.g. h=0 s=0.0 v=0.3 local=#4d4d4d library=#4d4c4d; v=0.9 local=#e5e5e5 library=#e6e5e6. Four homes already own this: the library (hsv/convertColor/toRgba8, src/subpaths/color.ts), demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:212 (pickerColorToHex), convertPickerColor(_, "hsv") used 6x in useColorPipeline.ts/useColorParsing.ts, and glass-ui's oklchStopToHex/cssToOklch (@mkbabb/glass-ui/color). `grep "toString(16)"` over demo/+src/ returns 5 sites; MiniColorPicker.vue:103 is the only colour serializer not routed through toRgba8.
defects.mechanism: Ownership inversion — one concept, multiple homes, no forcing function toward convergence. The 27.37% splits into a deliberate rounding-policy fork (local Math.round half-up vs library banker's) and the LP2-3 asymmetry. Note the direction: on the neutral axis the demo's copy is RIGHT and the library is WRONG, which is exactly why the copy has never been deleted.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED — scratchpad/hsv.mjs, importing dist/subpaths/color.js so it exercises the published surface; output pasted in report §3 LP2-4.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both local conversions: `currentHex` becomes pickerColorToHex(convertPickerColor(hsv(hue,sat,val),"rgb")) and the incoming-hex watcher becomes convertPickerColor(parsePickerColor(hex),"hsv") — MiniColorPicker loses ~45 lines and becomes a pure gesture surface (two pointer-drag regions), which is the only thing a demo component should own. SEQUENCING IS LOAD-BEARING: LP2-3 must land first, or convergence onto today's toRgba8 makes neutral greys measurably worse than the hand-rolled copy produces.

defects.defect: NEW — seam discipline is inverted: seven barrels guard a leaf feature while the shared colour spine has none. demo/color-session/ has no index.ts, yet 57 files outside it reach 18 distinct raw internal modules of it; SearchFilterBar's own `../../../color-session/color-utils` is one such reach.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:145 `import { parseColorIn } from "../../../color-session/color-utils"`. `ls demo/color-session/` = 24 files, no index.ts. Measured surface: `grep -rho 'from "[^"]*color-session/[^"]*"' demo --include=*.ts --include=*.vue | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` -> 26 keys, 19 picker-color, 16 color-model, 11 useContrastSafeColor, 6 color-utils, 5 ink, 4 color-names, 4 generate-color, 3 color-chips, 2 colorSpaceInfo, 2 color-space-meta, 2 ColorSpaceSelector.vue, +6 more = 18 distinct modules incl. one raw .vue. `grep -rl 'color-session/' demo --include=*.ts --include=*.vue | grep -v '^demo/color-session/' | wc -l` = 57. Against that: demo/palettes/browser/ carries SEVEN barrels (browser/index.ts + card/ admin/ search/ dialog/ slug/ status/) and browser/index.ts:1-18 is eighteen lines of prose about seam law.
defects.mechanism: Effort spent inverse to risk. color-session is simultaneously a peer feature and the shared spine, so it has the surface discipline of neither — nothing declares what of it is public, therefore all of it is. Meanwhile a leaf feature carries five sub-barrels that are the 'new shared dir that does not already exist' contrivance the KISS edict forbids.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED — commands and counts above are pasted in report §3 LP2-5.
defects.proposedCure: Invert the effort. Create demo/color-session/index.ts — the one barrel that matters, named exports only (parseColorIn, colorToCss, colorToRgb255, pickerColorToHex, convertPickerColor, parsePickerColor, PICKER_* tables, keys) — and route the 57 consumers through it. Collapse the leaf's seven barrels to the one at browser/index.ts. While doing it, fix the throw-vs-Result inversion the barrel would otherwise enshrine: picker-color.ts:103 parsePickerColor converts the library's explicit Result into an exception, which is precisely why the component wrote a regex instead of reading a failure (pass 1's L-5).

defects.defect: NEW — `searching` is dead state. `applyColorSearch` is declared `async` but contains no `await`, so searching.value is set true and false within one synchronous tick and Vue never observes true; the Loader2 spinner and the disabled state can never render.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 — `async function applyColorSearch()` sets searching.value=true, runs an entirely synchronous body, and resets in `finally`, with no await anywhere. Consequently :98 `:disabled="searching"` never binds, :102 `<Loader2 v-if="searching" class="... animate-spin"/>` is unreachable, and :99's `disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:pointer-events-none` are dead classes.
defects.mechanism: Residue from an intended server call. The search is synchronous because it is the client-side Array.filter of pass 1's L-3 (the colour filter never reaches the wire), so the async signature and its spinner describe an architecture that was never built.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED by reading — no await token exists between :213 and :225; the claim is structural, not timing-dependent.
defects.proposedCure: Ordered: fix pass 1's L-3 (send colorL/colorA/colorB via currentFilterOpts) and the async-ness becomes real and the spinner earns its place. If L-3 is deferred, delete `searching`, the Loader2 import and both dead attribute sets. Edict-6 check: animate-spin is a Tailwind utility on a never-rendered node, not an authored keyframe — removing it deletes no animation and demo/styles/ is untouched.

defects.defect: NEW MEASUREMENT — demo/ui/ (19 directories, 19 files, 29 lines, zero implementation) imposes shadcn-vue's 2023 directory taxonomy on glass-ui 7's own subpath lattice and funnels every component through the ROOT barrel, past the granular entry points glass-ui ships.
defects.evidence: All 19 barrels are one-line re-exports (`demo/ui/button/index.ts`: `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`); `wc -l demo/ui/*/index.ts` = 29 total. glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes 70 subpaths including ./button ./popover ./card ./select ./slider ./switch ./tooltip ./separator ./label ./collapsible ./dropdown-menu ./dialog ./badge — 13 of demo/ui's 19 names have a dedicated entry point, and only demo/ui/input reaches a real subpath (@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms). Measured transitive closure of the unbundled dist: root barrel 66 modules / 224,193 bytes; button.js 11 modules / 17,224 bytes; popover.js 7 modules / 13,960 bytes. Vite dep pre-bundle confirms the funnel: node_modules/.vite/deps/ contains @mkbabb_glass-ui.js at 231,357 bytes and NO @mkbabb_glass-ui_button.js or _popover.js.
defects.mechanism: An alias layer with no encapsulation, forbidden by the no-legacy/no-aliases edict. Its unconditional cost is taxonomic: from a call site demo/ui/button and demo/ui/input are indistinguishable, so the design system's real boundaries are invisible at the point of use — and that laundering is the mechanism by which LP2-2's 28-site drift went unnoticed.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED — barrel dump, wc, closure computation and the .vite/deps listing are pasted in report §3 LP2-7. HONEST SCOPING, stated in the report so the number is not overclaimed: the root chunk loads anyway (three demo files import writeClipboard/useClipboard/useTouchGate from bare glass-ui) and sideEffects:["*.css"] lets Rolldown tree-shake production, so the 231 KB is a DEV-mode cost, not a shipped one. The taxonomic cost is unconditional.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ outright; import glass-ui at the point of use through the granular subpath where one exists (`import { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/button"`). Removes 19 directories, kills the alias layer, replaces ../../../ui/popover with a bare specifier at every depth, and makes the design system's boundaries visible in the import block. Migrate LP2-2's 28 variant sites in the same pass.

defects.defect: NEW — `hexToOklab`'s defensive throw on "none" OKLab channels is unreachable dead code.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:205-211 throws `new Error("Hex color produced missing OKLab channels")` if any of L/a/b === "none". Both callers (:184 and :219) can only pass a 6-digit hex or pickerHex.value; `none` channels arrive only from CSS `none` keywords, which the :218 regex gate excludes by construction.
defects.mechanism: Type narrowing wearing runtime-error clothes, because the Channel = number | "none" policy has no single home (pass 1's L-8 documents four divergent guards).
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED by call-graph inspection — the two call sites are the only ones and both are gated by :218.
defects.proposedCure: Disappears once the "none" policy gets one home: a library-side `resolveChannels(c): Result<[number,number,number]>` (pass 1's L-8 cure), narrowed once at the parse boundary so the component holds a value that is already total.

defects.defect: STRONGER PROOF of pass 1's L-11 — the barrel-seam invariant that demo/palettes/browser/index.ts declares as machine-enforced law is absent from the effective lint configuration entirely, not merely unable to match.
defects.evidence: `npx eslint --print-config demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue` -> `no-restricted-imports` = "<ABSENT>"; same for demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue. Root cause: eslint.config.js:232-239 scopes G-DEMO-3b to demo/@/components/** and demo/@/lib/**, :275-278 scopes G-DEMO-3a to demo/@/composables/**, and W43 (RF-15, quoted at vite.config.ts:66-72) deleted that tree — `ls -d demo/@` -> No such file or directory; `grep -rn '"@components' tsconfig*.json vite.config.ts vitest.config.ts` -> nothing; `grep -rn 'from "@components' demo | wc -l` -> 0. Corroboration that the seam is already bypassed inside its own tree: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:193 imports `../status/ApiOfflineChip.vue`, a raw .vue reach past status/'s barrel — exactly the crossing G-DEMO-3b names — and eslint is green.
defects.mechanism: Documentation-as-enforcement. A prose invariant plus a barrel plus a lint rule whose selector rotted when the tree was renamed; every subsequent reader, including this component's author, inherits a boundary they believe is machine-checked. Pass 1 inferred this from the globs; the --print-config output measures it directly.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED — both --print-config invocations and the three corroborating greps are pasted in report §4.
defects.proposedCure: Re-target the globs to physical homes (demo/palettes/**, demo/picker/**, demo/workbenches/**, demo/scenes/**, demo/shell/**) and re-express the ban against physical paths. Better and cheaper to keep true: replace the bespoke no-restricted-imports encoding with a declarative boundary map (import/no-restricted-paths zones or eslint-plugin-boundaries) where each area declares its allowed targets once, so a directory rename cannot silently unhook it — which is precisely what happened.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (component: demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue, ~243 lines, area palettes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context arm). Declared by the seat brief, not inherited. Not Fable/Sonnet/Haiku.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the component has no design because it has no place: it renders on ZERO of 15 routes (no `<PaletteSlugBar` tag exists anywhere; its only references are two barrels and one erased `import type`), and its job is constitutionally assigned elsewhere — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:222 rules "Account is one modal side Dialog opened from the Dock, not a route chassis or second main." Three live siblings (ProfileSection / SlugEditLayer / MobileMenuDropdown) already discharge it in the Dock. The proof of cost is D-2: its login form cannot submit at all, a regression that landed in the glass-7 commit f2c8f565 and was never noticed because nothing renders it.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (One negative was proven and reported honestly: the shortest AUTHORED error string does NOT bleed the viewport at 320px — measured errBleedsViewport = -36.92px — so no horizontal-overflow claim was made for it; the overflow finding D-3b rests only on the measured 758px-in-286px case for a real server message. The `vj-morph` motion-family usage was also examined and found CORRECT — ratified family, globally PRM-guarded, no layout-forcing property — and is stated as such in §D-10.)

defects.defect: The component has no render path anywhere in the repository, and its composition contradicts the ratified topology: an inline account/identity bar inside the `My Palettes` pane header, where the constitution assigns Account to one modal side Dialog opened from the Dock. It also adds a second, unrelated identity line above the pane's real identity line, violating the one-identity-line card law.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "PaletteSlugBar" --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts" . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v docs/tranches` returns exactly 4 hits: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:6 (`import type`), :30 (unbound ref), demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:44 (barrel), demo/palettes/browser/slug/index.ts:3 (barrel).
