Checkbox `checked="false"` fallthrough per D2-B1. Sibling UserSortMenu.vue:9 passes `size="xs"` with no geometry override and renders a true 28.4x28.4 circle on /#/admin/users.
defects.mechanism: Pre-glass-7 (shadcn/radix) idioms survived the 7.0.0 adoption as no-ops because Vue fallthrough attributes never warn. The design defect and the legacy-code defect are the same defect: the surface looks styled while nothing was applied. `p-0` and `h-8 w-8` are additionally per-instance overrides of producer roots — wrong to write and lost anyway. Net visual consequence: an `iconOnly` button whose contract is square geometry renders as a 32x40 vertical stadium seated in a 374x24.6 input row.
defects.reproduction: node -e with playwright against /#/browse, read `[...document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Filters"]').attributes]` and `getComputedStyle(popoverContent).padding`; or `npx vue-tsc` with strict template checking, which would surface the undeclared props.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose onto DropdownMenu/DropdownMenuTrigger and pass only declared axes: `emphasis="quiet" size="xs" iconOnly`. Delete `variant`, `p-0`, `h-8 w-8`, `:checked` and `@update:checked` outright — no shims. Enable strict template type-checking on demo/ so an undeclared prop is a compile error rather than a silent DOM attribute.

defects.defect: Two option lists of the same species sit in one 240px menu at 57px and 33px pitch — a 1.73x rhythm fork — and the Sort section is 42% dead vertical space.
defects.evidence: Chromium measurement, popover open: glass-ui RadioGroup computes display:flex, flexDirection:column, gap:26px; .filter-option row ink = 31.0px; option y = 441.9 -> 498.9 -> 555.9, i.e. 57.0px pitch. The hand-authored tag list (SearchFilterBar.vue:49 `flex flex-col gap-0.5`) computes gap:2px over identical 31.0px rows, i.e. 33.0px pitch. Sort section rect h=197.5 carrying 21.6 (label) + 3x31.0 (rows) = 114.6px of ink. Visible in shots/tall-desktop-light-open.png.
defects.mechanism: Category error: RadioGroup's 26px is a FORM-field stack gap sized for labelled form rows; these are MENU option rows. The component consumed the wrong producer default for one list and then hand-authored the sibling list at its own gap, so the same menu speaks two rhythms. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.7 (no spacing fork) and PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.8 (real rendered relation wins over token intent); it is also the direct cause of ~134px of D2-B2's overflow.
defects.reproduction: Playwright evaluate on /#/browse with the popover open: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[role=radiogroup]')).gap -> "26px"; getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.max-h-28')).gap -> "2px"; then read the .filter-option rects.
defects.proposedCure: Use `DropdownMenuRadioItem` and `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` for both lists, as UserSortMenu.vue:22-33 already does — the menu rhythm then comes from the producer and neither list carries a local gap.

defects.defect: The radio species has no focus indicator at all in either scheme, and the popover exhibits four different focus vocabularies — including Chrome's default blue-grey outline on a hand-rolled button.
defects.evidence: probe6.mjs, CHROMIUM (per audit/visual/states.mjs:6-9), tallest state, light and dark. button[role=radio].radio-group__item: outline "none 3px …" (style none, not painted), boxShadow "none", hasVisibleRing FALSE in both schemes. button[role=checkbox].checkbox: boxShadow "… 0 0 0 2px". input.field-control: boxShadow "… 0 0 0 2px". button.block (swatch, :75): cartoon shadow. button.absolute (hand-rolled Search, :97): outline "auto 1px rgb(176,192,210)" — the UA default. Also measured: unchecked checkbox edge = 1px color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.12) light and 1px color(srgb 0.914 0.9 0.886 / 0.12) dark — a 12%-alpha boundary on a translucent veil; see shots/tall-desktop-dark-open.png.
defects.mechanism: Six control species assembled from three different sources (producer atoms, a hand-rolled swatch button, a hand-rolled Search button) with no single focus owner. The Search button at :97 carries no `focus-ring` class and therefore falls back to the UA ring, a register that exists nowhere else in the system. WCAG 2.4.7 and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 ('focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes') both fail on the radio.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe6.mjs — walks Tab in Chromium and records outline/boxShadow per stop in both schemes. Manually: open the ⋮ menu in Chrome, press Tab once, and look at the Sort radio.
defects.proposedCure: One producer focus register for every seat: transpose the option rows onto DropdownMenu*Item, and replace the hand-rolled swatch and Search buttons with glass-ui `Button` so `focus-ring` is inherited rather than re-invented. The radio's missing register should be relayed to glass-ui BH as a producer defect.

defects.defect: Four horizontal dividing lines render inside the popover on the Browse route, whose binding boundary inventory is `none`.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:17 `class="flex flex-col divide-y divide-border"`. probe2.mjs, tallest state, all matrices: divide-y children borders = [{bt:0px,bb:1px,rgb(198,180,159)}, {bt:0,bb:1px}, {bt:0,bb:1px}, {bt:0,bb:1px}, {bt:0,bb:0}] -> renderedDividerCount 4. (Tailwind v4's divide-y writes border-BOTTOM on :not(:last-child), so a border-top-only read misses them.) docs/tranches/V/OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 binding table: Browse -> Retained non-P122 dividing line = `none`, and 'Any additional line … is a defect.' PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-05 concurs.
defects.mechanism: A boundary drawn where interval and material already express the grouping — demonstrated inside the same menu by the tag list, which has no divider and groups perfectly well.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe2.mjs, read `dividers` / `renderedDividerCount`; visible in shots/tall-desktop-light-open.png between SORT/TIER, TIER/TAGS, TAGS/FIND BY COLOR and above the Clear-all row.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `divide-y divide-border`. If the transposition to DropdownMenu is taken, boundaries become an explicit `DropdownMenuSeparator` decision, and the binding answer for Browse is zero.

defects.defect: All four section headings render in Fira Code uppercase — the rung the closed type matrix reserves for values, code and provenance — and the option rows declare `font-family: var(--font-serif)` for what must be the sans control voice.
defects.evidence: Computed .section-label across all four sections and all matrices: font-family "Fira Code", font-size 14.384px (--type-caption), text-transform uppercase, letter-spacing 1.4384px, weight 400. Traced to node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/utilities.css: `.section-label { @apply text-mono-caption; color: var(--muted-foreground) }` with `@utility text-mono-caption { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--type-caption); letter-spacing: var(--type-tracking-caps); text-transform: uppercase }`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 and OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 'Binding type matrix' both bind section headings -> text-heading + Plus Jakarta Sans, and reserve mono-caption for values/code/provenance. Separately SearchFilterBar.vue:243 sets `font-family: var(--font-serif)`, which only resolves to Jakarta because glass-ui aliases --font-serif -> --font-stack-text (documented as deliberate and fragile at demo/styles/foundation.css:95-102).
defects.mechanism: The demo mapped 'section heading' onto the producer's mono eyebrow recipe (demo/DESIGN.md:52 recommends `.section-label`), so the closed matrix is violated at four sites here and repo-wide as a family. The `--font-serif` line is a name that lies: it says serif and means sans, and is one producer change away from flipping every filter option to Fraunces.
defects.reproduction: Playwright evaluate on /#/browse with the popover open: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.section-label')) -> fontFamily "Fira Code", textTransform "uppercase". Visible in every open-popover frame as SORT / TIER / TAGS / FIND BY COLOR in monospaced caps.
defects.proposedCure: Locally: use `DropdownMenuLabel` with `text-small`/`text-heading` (Plus Jakarta Sans) for the four group labels, and write the type role directly rather than `var(--font-serif)`. Family-wide: the `.section-label` -> section-heading mapping needs a canon ruling, since the same substitution is repo-wide.

defects.defect: A god-menu: five unrelated jobs (sort, tier, tags, colour-distance search with a nested picker, clear-all) behind one unlabelled ellipsis, while the identical job is already implemented correctly in 58 lines by a sibling in the same directory — two chrome families for one job, on two routes.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue (249 lines) vs UserSortMenu.vue (58 lines) in the same folder. Measured differences: primitive Popover+RadioGroup+<label> vs DropdownMenu+DropdownMenuRadioGroup/RadioItem; announced semantics aria-haspopup="dialog" role="dialog" vs aria-haspopup="menu"; trigger geometry 32x40 stadium vs 28.4x28.4 circle; glyph NOT aria-hidden (glyphAriaHidden null) vs aria-hidden="true" (UserSortMenu.vue:13); option rows hand-rolled .filter-option at 57px pitch vs producer DropdownMenuRadioItem. The component's own activeFilterCount (:189-195) deliberately excludes `sort`, proving it knows sort is not a filter. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7: 'Search/filter chrome is one family.' Also: the mirror route /#/palettes has no filter affordance at all (shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png).
defects.mechanism: A hand-rolled clone of a producer family, hosting five jobs behind one anonymous entry point. Every geometry, rhythm, semantics and focus defect above is downstream of this one architectural choice, which is why they cannot be patched individually.
defects.reproduction: Read both files; compare the two triggers live at /#/browse and /#/admin/users (probe.mjs records the sibling's rect 28.4x28.4 and aria-haspopup="menu" against this one's 32x40 and "dialog").
defects.proposedCure: Transpose onto DropdownMenu + DropdownMenuLabel + DropdownMenuRadioGroup/RadioItem + DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, exactly as UserSortMenu.vue:1-37 does, and split sort out of the filter drawer into its own named control beside the field. The file should land near UserSortMenu's size.

defects.defect: Applying, changing or clearing a filter changes the wall with no announced result count and no status region — there is no aria-live anywhere in the document.
defects.evidence: probe3.mjs on /#/browse with the wall populated: resultDelta = { before: 5, after: 5, liveRegions: 0, statusRoles: 1 }. `liveRegions: 0` is a whole-document count; the single role="status" is not this component's and carries no count. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.1, row 'in-route filter, tab, selection, or pagination' -> Announcement rule: 'changed result count/state through the owning status region'.
defects.mechanism: The component emits filter changes upward and owns no status surface; the consumer (BrowsePane.vue) provides none either. Combined with the clipped badge (D2-B3) and the absence of applied-filter chips (D2-M8), the user's only route to learning what is filtering the wall is to reopen the drawer and read five separate controls.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe3.mjs; or on /#/browse run `document.querySelectorAll('[aria-live]').length` after applying a filter -> 0.

result.strongestDefect: L-1: drag-to-reorder in PalettesPane.vue:180-197 deterministically persists a CORRUPTED palette order. Seeding four palettes A,B,C,D and dragging index 0 onto index 2 yields stored order [C,B,D,A] instead of [B,C,A,D] — every position wrong — reproduced 3/3; dragging 3 onto 1 is a silent total no-op. Three compounding structural errors: (a) `useSortable` is handed `pm.filteredSaved.value`, a DEREFERENCED computed, so vueuse takes its `isRef(list)===false` no-copy branch and splices the caller's array in place with no write-back; (b) the options pass `onEnd`, which does not override vueuse's `defaultOptions.onUpdate` (different keys in the `{...defaultOptions, ...resetOptions}` spread), so BOTH fire and onUpdate's synchronous `array.splice(from,1)` runs before onEnd reads the indices; (c) `useFilteredList.ts:9` returns `items.value` by reference on an empty query, so the array being mutilated is `savedPalettes`'s own live computed cache. The corrupted order is written to localStorage and survives reload — data loss of user intent.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the overall verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded because the challenge's headline hypothesis was disproven: the demo → @mkbabb/value.js edge is SOUND by construction. (1) Exhaustive census of all 49 value.js import sites in demo/ shows every one is a bare published subpath specifier — 24 `@mkbabb/value.js/color`, 10 `/css`, 6 `/math`, 5 `/easing`, 4 `/quantize`; zero `../../src/…`, zero `@src/…`, zero `dist/…`, zero root-barrel imports. (2) The vite alias set cannot drift from the export map because it is GENERATED from it — vite.config.ts:37-50 reads this repo's own package.json#exports at config time and derives one anchored-regex alias per subpath. (3) tsconfig.demo.json carries no `@src/*` path, so a deep import would not typecheck from the demo tree. (4) PalettesPane's own 97-module closure reaches value.js only via `/color` and `/css`. A real consumer could write every import the demo writes. Two further soundnesses recorded so a later seat does not re-litigate: `demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue` is NOT an edict-3 contrivance (9 real consumers, owns `--pane-scroll`; and the `ScrollCardHeader` it books does not exist in glass-ui 7.0.0 — `grep -rl "ScrollCard" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` is empty, so that is a proposal to glass-ui, not a violation); and `../color-session/keys` is a correct cross-area edge (leaf module, 26 consumers, no cycle) — it is the exact pattern L-3 asks palettes to adopt.

defects.defect: Drag-to-reorder is structurally miswired and deterministically persists a corrupted palette order; backward drags are silently discarded entirely.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:180-197. Probe output (scratchpad/reorder-probe2.mjs, headless Chromium vs live dev server localhost:9000): `run1 drag 0->2 STORE=[C,B,D,A]` / `run2 drag 0->2 STORE=[C,B,D,A]` / `run3 drag 0->2 STORE=[C,B,D,A]` / `run4 drag 3->1 STORE=[A,B,C,D]`; `expected for 0->2 : BCAD`, `observed 0->2 set : ["CBDA"]`; `expected for 3->1 : ADBC`, `observed 3->1 : ABCD`. [...toValue(list)] : toValue(list); if (to >= 0 && to < array.length) { const element = array.splice(from, 1)[0]; nextTick(() => { array.splice(to, 0, element); if (_valueIsRef) list.value = array; }); }`. defects.defect: Two live export implementations. The app ships demo/palettes/export.ts; 78 test assertions certify demo/palettes/export/ — and the two disagree by construction in token prefix, index base, and colour spelling. The test suite is a false proof of the export surface.

defects.defect: Three homes for "name → identifier", with measured divergence; a downloaded file's name disagrees with the slug written inside the file's own body.
defects.evidence: Home 1: demo/palettes/utils.ts:3-13 `slugify` (NFKD normalize, strip combining marks, `[^a-z0-9 -]` drop). Home 2: demo/palettes/export.ts:9-11 `slugify` (naive `[^a-z0-9]+` → `-`). Home 3: demo/palettes/export/canonical.ts:50-59 `identifierPrefix` — comment states "no slugifier exists", uses the stored slug. Measured divergence over the two live regex chains: `"Café Noir"` → export.ts `"caf-noir"` vs utils.ts `"cafe-noir"`; `"Grüne Töne"` → `"gr-ne-t-ne"` vs `"grune-tone"`; `"Mötley 2.0"` → `"m-tley-2-0"` vs `"motley-20"`. The store mints palette.slug with home 1 (usePaletteStore.ts:87 → createSlug). export.ts:17 writes `slug: palette.slug` into the JSON payload while export.ts:21 names the file `${slugify(palette.name)}.json` using home 2.
defects.mechanism: Ownership duplication of a derivation. The identifier is minted once and stored, then independently re-derived at a second site by a different algorithm, so the stored identity and the derived identity drift on any non-ASCII input.
defects.reproduction: node -e with the two regex chains transcribed verbatim from export.ts:9-11 and utils.ts:3-12 over ["Café Noir","Grüne Töne","Sunset  Vibes","Mötley 2.0"] — output pasted in evidence. End-to-end: save a palette named "Café Noir", export as JSON; the file downloads as caf-noir.json and contains "slug": "cafe-noir-<uuid8>".
defects.proposedCure: Home 3 is correct — identifiers are minted once at creation and stored, never re-derived. Deleting export.ts (L-2) deletes home 2 and leaves exactly one slugifier, in utils.ts, invoked only by createPalette.

defects.defect: The imperative card-feedback registry is duplicated across the two panes with two different identity schemes, plus a third documented site; both copies leak instances for the session.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:177 `const cardRefs = reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({});`, :84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.id] = el)"` (keyed by id), :205 `const card = cardRefs[id]; card.showFeedback(…)`. demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:209 identical declaration, :94 `cardRefs[palette.slug] = el` (keyed by slug), :228/:237/:249/:264 four showFeedback call sites. defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a static structural duplication established by the grep census above, not a runtime failure. The unbounded `cardRefs` growth is a hypothesis I did not measure; the duplication and the divergent key schemes are confirmed by file:line.
defects.proposedCure: Feedback is a property of the palette, not of the component instance. PaletteCard takes `:feedback="feedbackFor(palette)"` and renders the already-existing browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue declaratively. A single usePaletteFeedback() composable holds Map<paletteKey, {message, variant, at}> keyed by the one identity the domain already has. defineExpose, both cardRefs registries, both `any` casts, and the leak all disappear.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 19 pure re-export shims onto glass-ui — aliases with no added surface — and PalettesPane refutes them inside its own 24-line import block by using both the shim and the direct subpath for the same design system.

defects.reproduction: NONE for a user-visible failure — sideEffects:["*.css"] means the root barrel is tree-shakeable in a production Rollup build, so this is a dev-graph and correctness-of-intent defect, not a measured shipped-bytes regression. defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ wholesale and rewrite the 31 importers to the granular glass-ui subpath (`@mkbabb/glass-ui/card`, `/button`, `/badge`, …). One codemod, no behaviour change, 19 files and one directory removed, and exactly one legal spelling for a design-system import.

defects.defect: `@click.prevent` on `<DropdownMenuSubTrigger>` makes the ENTIRE Export submenu (JSON / CSS Custom Properties / Tailwind Config / SVG Swatch / PNG Swatch) unreachable on every touch and pen device. The user taps "Export" and nothing happens; the menu stays open. Desktop mouse is rescued by reka's 100ms hover timer, which is why it shipped invisibly.
defects.mechanism: Event-handler merge-order inversion across an asChild primitive chain. node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Primitive/Slot.js does `mergeProps(attrs, firstNonCommentChildren.props)` — consumer fallthrough attrs FIRST, primitive's own props SECOND — so the DOM node gets `onClick: [consumerPrevent, rekaOpenHandler]`. reka-ui/dist/Menu/MenuSubTrigger.js guards `if (props.disabled || event.defaultPrevented) return;` and therefore always bails. reka-ui/dist/Menu/utils.js:63 `isMouseEvent(event) { return event.pointerType === "mouse"; }` means handlePointerMove (the hover-open path) returns immediately for touch/pen, so click is the ONLY pointer path on touch — and it is dead. Keyboard escapes because handleKeyDown calls menuContext.onOpenChange(true) directly, never through the click guard.
defects.reproduction: 1) node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-C1-touch.mjs (dev server live on :9000). It seeds one local palette into localStorage["color-palettes"], opens the card's "Palette menu", and taps the Export sub-trigger via page.touchscreen.tap. Observed: aria-expanded stays "false", no [data-slot=dropdown-menu-sub-content] in the DOM. 2) probe-C1-counterproof.mjs re-dispatches the same click with `defaultPrevented` forced false → submenu opens (aria-expanded "true"). 3) Manually: open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes on any phone/tablet with a saved palette, tap the ⋯ menu, tap Export.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the modifier: `<DropdownMenuSubTrigger class="gap-2 cursor-pointer">`. `preventDefault` on a div[role=menuitem] suppresses no browser default, and the 'don't close the menu' intent it appears to encode is already guaranteed by the primitive (a sub-trigger never emits ITEM_SELECT). It is pure cargo-cult; removal is a strict simplification with no trade. Architecturally: no consumer of a reka asChild primitive should ever attach a `.prevent` click — the merge order makes it an override of the primitive's own behaviour, not an addition to it.

defects.defect: The K-INV5 availability latch is read with a partial equality test — `apiOffline = availability.value === "unavailable"` against a FOUR-state union. In the `misconfigured` state (the state of the running dev server right now) the latch does not trip: Publish renders enabled, focusable and clickable, with no `offline` annotation, wired to an action that `assertApiAttemptAllowed()` throws `DevMisconfigError` on before any request is issued. The component's own header comment claims it 'disables the doomed action and NAMES the degraded state'.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:216-217 `const { availability } = useApiClient(); const apiOffline = computed(() => availability.value === "unavailable");` — governs `:disabled` at :30 and :51 and the annotation at :35-39 and :56-59. demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:40-44 declares `"unknown" | "available" | "unavailable" | "misconfigured"`; :189-190 `if (apiAvailability.value === "misconfigured") { throw new DevMisconfigError(); }`. Live measurement, same probe run: console shows the misconfig error emitted only at availability.ts:163, and ITEMS[0] = {"text":"Publish","ariaDisabled":null,"dataDisabled":null,"pointerEvents":"auto"}. Sibling consumer of the SAME injected seam handles both: demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:36-37 has `offline` AND `misconfigured` computeds and renders two registers (:12 role=alert, :20 role=status); demo/shell/dock/DockStatusLamp.vue:88-104 carries a third misconfigured face. PaletteCardMenu is the only latch consumer that collapses the union.
defects.mechanism: Ad-hoc re-derivation of a domain predicate at each consumer instead of once at the seam that owns it. Three consumers hand-roll booleans over the same `availability` ref; the newest one enumerated only one of the two failure members, so a new enum member silently degraded an affordance rather than breaking a build.
defects.reproduction: node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-C1-touch.mjs against the current `dev:web-only` server (no VITE_API_URL). Output shows the MISCONFIGURED console.error AND ITEMS[0] Publish with ariaDisabled:null / dataDisabled:null / pointerEvents:auto — i.e. enabled. Equivalent manual repro: open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a saved palette, open the ⋯ menu, observe Publish is enabled and un-annotated while the console shows the dev-misconfig error.
defects.proposedCure: Move the predicate to the seam, do not spread a fourth copy of the equality: `useApiClient()` exposes derived `degraded` / `misconfigured` / `reason` once and every affordance reads it — which kills the drift class instead of this instance. If deferred, the minimum correct local form is `availability.value === "unavailable" || availability.value === "misconfigured"`, with the small-caps annotation naming WHICH degradation, since naming the state is the entire point of the K-INV5 register.

defects.defect: `isPublic = palette.visibility !== "private"` collapses a documented 3-state enum into a binary. An owned `unlisted` remote palette renders the verb "Make private" with the small-caps state annotation `public` — the register lies about the current state — and taking the action emits `setVisibility(palette,"private")` → `unpublishPalette`, destroying the `unlisted` state with no UI path back, in direct contradiction of the API's explicit preservation guarantee.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:222 `const isPublic = computed(() => palette.visibility !== "private");` driving :52 (`isPublic ? 'makePrivate' : 'makePublic'`), :55 (label) and :59 (annotation). demo/palettes/types.ts:39-40 `/** I.W1 canonical visibility (3-state). */ visibility?: "public" | "unlisted" | "private";`. Canonical predicates that are NOT `!== "private"`: api/src/modules/palette/format.ts:86 `published: rest.visibility === "public"`; api/src/modules/palette/service/visibility.ts:28-37 `isActivePublic` = `visibility === "public" && !deletedAt`, doc'd "`unlisted`/`private` and trashed rows are NOT active-public". Preservation guarantee: demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:128-130 "The `unlisted` middle state is untouched"; api/src/modules/palette/service/visibility.ts:7-8 "The `unlisted` middle state is preserved and never destroyed". Reachability: api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:111-118 — an owner listing their OWN userSlug receives every visibility, unlisted included (non-owners are forced to `public`); api/src/platform/migrations/check.ts:53-60 asserts every doc carries one of the three. Truth table: visibility="unlisted" ⟹ isPublic=true ⟹ label "Make private", annotation "public", emit makePrivate — all three wrong.
defects.mechanism: Ternary domain modelled as a boolean by negating the least-common member instead of asserting the intended one. The canonical read already exists on the wire (`published`, computed server-side as `visibility === "public"`) and on the type, and was bypassed for a hand-rolled negation, so the middle enum member silently maps onto the wrong branch of a two-branch UI.
defects.reproduction: NOT EXECUTED — recipe (the current dev server is dev:web-only, so the latch short-circuits every request before it leaves the page; see C-2): 1) `npm run dev` (full local stack via scripts/dev.sh up), sign in. 2) create a palette, then PATCH /palettes/:slug with {"visibility":"unlisted"} (api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts accepts the enum). 3) open /#/browse filtered to your own userSlug and open that card's ⋯ menu. 4) observe the item reads "Make private" with annotation `public`. An isolated @vue/test-utils mount was attempted (scratchpad pcm-mount.test.ts + pcm.vitest.config.ts, run via npx vitest run --config …): the suite runs but reka's DropdownMenuPortal/Presence renders nothing under this repo's jsdom even with ResizeObserver/DOMRect/matchMedia polyfills — document.body.textContent is empty for every case. That negative is itself recorded (see C-4).
defects.proposedCure: Minimum: `const isPublic = computed(() => palette.visibility === "public");` — the canonical predicate, matching format.ts:86 and isActivePublic. Gestalt cure: stop modelling a ternary as a toggle. Annotate the ACTUAL value (public / unlisted / private) in the K-INV5 register and offer the transition that is missing, so the control is a state display plus transitions rather than a two-way flip that pretends the middle state does not exist — the API already treats all 9 (visibility, tier) tuples as legal resting states; the UI is the only layer that flattened it.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: this component has ZERO tests. No unit or component test anywhere mounts it, and the six e2e specs that open its trigger assert on only 2 of its 16 items (Remix, Versions). Three separate one-line mutations each break a distinct user-facing behaviour while every gate stays green.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "PaletteCardMenu" --include="*.ts" --include="*.vue" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git` returns only PaletteCard.vue:83,106,176 plus a doc comment in useApiClient.ts:9 and 25 docs-only hits — no test file. Trigger is opened at e2e/smoke/flows/{palette-fork,palette-delete,palette-edit,palette-flag}.spec.ts:47, e2e/smoke/admin/flows/palette-feature.spec.ts:47, e2e/smoke/oracles/o10d-display-voice-census.spec.ts:311. Only assertions on items: palette-fork.spec.ts:48 (/Remix/) and o10d:328 (/Versions/). `grep -rn "Export\|Make private" e2e` returns NOTHING. Vacuity mutations that keep all gates green: (a) delete PaletteCardMenu.vue lines 107-130 (the entire Export submenu); (b) `const isPublic = computed(() => true)`; (c) `const apiOffline = computed(() => false)`.
defects.mechanism: Coverage is anchored on the trigger button, not on the menu's item model. The gates assert that the menu OPENS, never what it contains or which branch each derived boolean selected — so every branch introduced after the specs were written (visibility flip, export family, offline latch) landed untested by construction. Compounded by a hard environmental blocker: reka menu content does not render under the repo's jsdom vitest environment (measured), so component-level tests for any menu are currently impossible and nobody wrote them.
defects.reproduction: Apply mutation (a): delete lines 107-130 of demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue, then run `npm test` and the e2e smoke suite. Both stay green with an entire user-facing feature removed. Environmental blocker reproduced at /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/pcm-mount.test.ts run via `npx vitest run --config .../pcm.vitest.config.ts`: 5 mounts succeed, document.body.textContent is '' in all 5.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition rather than more browser tests: extract the item model — a pure function (paletteKind, isOwned, isAdmin, availability, palette) → Item[] {label, annotation, disabled, action} — and let the template render it. That table is unit-testable without a DOM, and asserting it would have caught C-2 and C-3 the day they landed. Complement with ONE e2e spec in a touch-emulated project that taps Export, which would have caught C-1. Do not attempt to fix coverage inside jsdom: reka menu content demonstrably does not render there.

defects.defect: Stringly-typed action contract with a silent swallow. `defineEmits<{ action: [action: string] }>()` plus the parent's `const fn = actions[action]; if (!fn) return;` means any typo on either side is an unnamed masking fallback. The gap is already load-bearing: the parent carries a `copyAll` handler that NO menu item can ever emit — unreachable code the type system cannot see.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:224-227 `defineEmits<{ action: [action: string]; updateOpen: [value: boolean]; }>()`. PaletteCard.vue:315-316 `const fn = actions[action]; if (!fn) return;`. PaletteCard.vue:294 `copyAll: () => void writeClipboard(...)`. `grep -rn "copyAll" demo --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts"` → exactly ONE hit (PaletteCard.vue:294); no emitter exists. Downstream continuation: demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts switches on `format: string` with no `default:` case and wraps everything in `catch (e) { console.warn("Export failed:", e); }`, so an unknown format and a real failure are indistinguishable silence — even though the card owns an ActionFeedback channel and `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` that export never uses.
defects.mechanism: A cross-component command bus typed as `string`. The compiler cannot check either end, so the exhaustiveness that a discriminated union would enforce is replaced by a runtime `if (!fn) return` that converts every mismatch into a no-op instead of an error — the textbook masking fallback the owner edicts forbid.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "copyAll" demo --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts"` returns one line (the handler) and zero emitters — the dead branch is proof the contract is unchecked. To exhibit the swallow: change any `$emit('action', 'exportPNG')` to `'exportPng'` — typecheck passes, tests pass, the menu item silently does nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Declare `export type PaletteCardAction = "save" | "publish" | "delete" | ... | "exportPNG";` once beside the menu; type the emit `action: [action: PaletteCardAction]` and the parent map `Record<PaletteCardAction, () => void>`. That makes the map exhaustive, lets `if (!fn) return` be deleted, and turns `copyAll` into a compile error. Same treatment for the export format string (`"json" | "css" | "tailwind" | "svg" | "png"`), with the swallowed catch routed into the existing ActionFeedback channel.

defects.defect: The `rename` special case in the parent dispatcher is dead code that contradicts its own comment. The comment says rename keeps the menu open; the very next call closes it unconditionally.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:291-292 comment: "`rename` opens an inline input — keep the menu open visually until the input takes focus; all other actions close the menu immediately." PaletteCard.vue:317 `if (action !== "rename") menuOpen.value = false;`. PaletteCard.vue:298 `rename: () => startRenaming()`. PaletteCard.vue:280-283 `function startRenaming() { menuOpen.value = false; renaming.value = true; }`.
defects.mechanism: Two sites own the same piece of state; one was later given an unconditional write, orphaning the other's guard. The comment became the only surviving record of an intent the code no longer implements.
defects.reproduction: Read PaletteCard.vue:280-283 and :317 together: the guard skips the write at :317 only for `rename`, and `startRenaming()` performs the identical write at :281 on the next statement. The branch is provably unobservable.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the guard and the stale comment; close the menu unconditionally before dispatch. If the original intent (defer the close until the rename input has focus) is still wanted, it belongs in one place — PaletteRenameInput's mounted focus handler — not as a dispatcher special case.

defects.defect: Two parallel kind vocabularies inside one 228-line file: eight menu items branch on the `paletteKind` seam, one branches on raw `!palette.isLocal`.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue v-ifs on `paletteKind` at :16, :28, :49, :64, :74, :84, :134, :144, :153. PaletteCardMenu.vue:94 `v-if="!palette.isLocal && (palette.versionCount ?? 0) > 1"`. demo/palettes/utils.ts:23 `if (!palette.isLocal) return "remote";` — i.e. `!palette.isLocal` IS `paletteKind === "remote"`, spelled a second way.
defects.mechanism: Seam leak. The classifier `getPaletteKind` exists precisely so consumers stop reading raw shape fields; one row bypasses it, so a future change to the classifier (e.g. a fourth kind, or a remote palette that is also local-cached) desynchronises this row silently.
defects.reproduction: Static: compare PaletteCardMenu.vue:94 with demo/palettes/utils.ts:23. Behavioural divergence would appear the moment `getPaletteKind` gains a branch that returns non-"remote" for a non-local palette.
defects.proposedCure: `v-if="paletteKind === 'remote' && (palette.versionCount ?? 0) > 1"` — one vocabulary per concept per file. Broader: `palette.isLocal` should not be readable by presentational components at all; the kind seam is the interface.

defects.defect: Two activation idioms in one menu — 11 items use `@click`, 5 use `@select`. They are not equivalent: `@click` cannot use the primitive's cancelable ITEM_SELECT contract, and it fires from a listener merged AFTER reka's own handleSelect, so the parent's close and reka's onClose race to close the same menu.
defects.evidence: `@click` at PaletteCardMenu.vue:18, 31, 52, 66, 76, 86, 96, 136, 146, 158, 165; `@select` at :113, :116, :119, :123, :126. node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Menu/MenuItem.js: `emits("select", itemSelectEvent); await nextTick(); if (itemSelectEvent.defaultPrevented) isPointerDownRef.value = false; else rootContext.onClose();` — the cancelable affordance an @click item can never reach. Merge order (renderer fallthrough): onClick = [handleSelect, consumerOnClick], so the emit lands between handleSelect's sync half and its post-nextTick onClose.
defects.mechanism: The DOM event and the primitive's semantic event were treated as interchangeable. They differ in cancelability and in ordering relative to the menu's own close, so the file carries two different activation semantics for what reads as one uniform list — a KISS violation and a latent ordering hazard.
defects.reproduction: Static, in the reka source quoted above. The race is currently benign only because the parent's competing close-guard is itself dead (see C-6); it becomes observable the moment either close path grows a side effect.
defects.proposedCure: Use `@select` throughout — it is the primitive's contract, it is already what the export half uses, and it is the only one that composes with `preventDefault()` to keep the menu open. One menu, one activation contract.

defects.defect: The 8-matrix Safari visual audit contains ZERO captures of this component: both routes that host a PaletteCard were photographed with no cards on screen, so the REPORT's 60 smallTapTargets and 18 namelessButtons contain no contribution from this component and its silence must not be read as a pass.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json — /#/palettes (all 4 matrices): bodyTextLength 237 desktop / 169 mobile, button count 25, and every smallTapTargets entry is a PaletteSlugBar or ComponentSliders row ({"w":22,"h":22,"label":"Switch to slug"}, {"w":12,"h":24,"label":"L channel"}, …) — no "Palette menu" button in any capture. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/browse.png (read): the specimen-plate empty state "The commons is unreachable. / Failed to load palettes / Retry".
defects.mechanism: The visual matrix runs against a backend-less dev server, so every card-bearing surface renders its empty state. Component coverage is therefore conditional on seeded data that the capture harness does not provide.
defects.reproduction: node -e on REPORT.json filtering results to /palettes and /browse (done); and Read of shots/safari-mobile-light/browse.png (done). Both show zero cards.
defects.proposedCure: Seed the visual harness (localStorage store for /#/palettes; a route-intercepted browse fixture for /#/browse) so card-bearing routes are actually photographed. Until then the visual audit must record card surfaces as UNCOVERED rather than absent-of-defects. Corroborating detail: that same empty state reads "unreachable" while the latch was `misconfigured` — the same conflation as C-2, one surface over.

result.strongestDefect: C-1 — `@click.prevent` at PaletteCardMenu.vue:108 removes the entire Export submenu from every touch and pen device. Every other finding is a wrong label or an untested branch; this is a whole feature that does not exist on mobile. It is caused by a nine-character template modifier, it is invisible to every gate the repo owns (no test references the submenu at all — C-4 mutation (a)), and it is invisible to desktop manual QA because reka's mouse-hover timer masks it. Reproduced with a genuine CDP touchscreen tap (aria-expanded stays "false", no sub-content in the DOM, menu stays open) and isolated with a counter-proof that changes exactly one bit — forcing `event.defaultPrevented` to false makes the identical click open the submenu. Causality is closed: `props.disabled` is measurably false on that element, so `defaultPrevented` is the only branch reka's guard can bail on.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this is not a negative proof but the record of what WAS probed and found sound, so later passes do not re-litigate it. All measured live at http://localhost:9000 (probes archived beside the report as probe-C1-touch.mjs / probe-C1-counterproof.mjs / probe-C1-keyboard.mjs). Tap targets pass with margin: trigger 54x54, menu items 178x46, submenu items 326x44 — this component contributes ZERO of the REPORT's 60 smallTapTargets. Accessibility of the open menu is correct: content role="menu", aria-labelledby -> the aria-label="Palette menu" trigger, aria-orientation="vertical"; trigger carries aria-expanded / aria-haspopup="menu" / aria-controls; after Escape the menu closes and focus is restored to BUTTON[aria-label="Palette menu"]. Keyboard operability of the `@click` items is intact — reka synthesises a native .click() on Enter/Space (MenuItem.js onKeydown), and Enter on the Export sub-trigger opens it and enumerates all five items. Disabled items are genuinely inert on both paths: `.dropdown-menu__item[data-disabled]{pointer-events:none;cursor:not-allowed}` in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css plus the `_ctx.disabled` early return in reka's onKeydown. Edict compliance: verbatimModuleSyntax clean (`import type { Palette }` :177, `import type { PaletteKind }` :178 — every type-only import is `import type`); glass-ui-first clean (all nine menu primitives re-exported from @mkbabb/glass-ui via demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts, zero local forks, zero per-instance surface overrides); no god module (228 lines, one job). Leak sweep is clean: the script has no requestAnimationFrame, no addEventListener, no observers, no timers and no onUnmounted need — it contributes nothing to the PRM-RAF epidemic; the sub-trigger's open timer belongs to the primitive, which clears it on unmount. NONE of the six known local hazards are present: no defineModel (open state is prop + emit, so no stale-read round-trip), no oklch/HSV roundtrip, no ValueUnit wrapping, no reka slider pointer-capture, no WebGL, no parsing (so no parseCssColor crash surface). Zero console errors and zero page errors attributable to the component across every probe run — the two console errors observed are the dev-misconfig banner emitted once at client init. Menu content is portalled and presence-gated, so the 16 items do not mount per card while closed (measured: zero [data-slot=dropdown-menu-item] nodes until the trigger is clicked) — no per-card mount cost finding. Examined and deliberately NOT filed as defects: the partial props destructure at :206 (`const { palette } = defineProps<...>()` with four props read off the proxy) is legal Vue 3.5 with no stale-read hazard, only an unfinished-migration smell; and ActionFeedback.vue's missing role/aria-live (58 lines, no live region, so no menu action's outcome is announced) is a real a11y gap that belongs to that file's seat, not this one.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — 1M-context variant; served tier matches the explicit spawn declaration.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — a drag performed while the pane's own search filter is active silently and irreversibly reorders the user's ENTIRE persisted palette library: `onEnd` (PalettesPane.vue:187-196) hands the FILTERED id list to `reorderPalettes` (usePaletteStore.ts:153-167), which treats it as the complete new order and appends every non-matching palette to the tail. Measured live: `Alpha Beta Gamma Delta Zed-one Zed-two` → `Zed-two Zed-one Alpha Beta Gamma Delta` from one 2-card drag under q='zed', written through to localStorage. The damage is invisible until the user clears the search box.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negative results proved, so they are not re-run: no `defineModel` anywhere in the file so the stale-read hazard cannot apply; no ValueUnit wrapping; no rAF in PalettesPane.vue or PaletteCardGrid.vue; no WebGL; no reka-ui slider; `overflowX: 0` re-measured at 1440 with 6 cards; `verbatimModuleSyntax` satisfied at line 151; confirm-dialog focus restoration measured correct — Escape returns focus to the trigger; a zero-colour palette renders without incident.)

defects.defect: Drag-to-reorder inside a search-filtered view silently reorders the entire persisted library, not just the visible subset.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:187-196 (`const ids = pm.filteredSaved.value.map(p => p.id)` → `pm.reorderPalettes(ids)`) + demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:153-167 (`reorderPalettes` emits orderedIds first, then APPENDS every palette not in the list). Live headless-Chromium repro output: `C. store order BEFORE drag: Alpha Beta Gamma Delta Zed-one Zed-two` / `visible under q='zed': ["Zed-one3","Zed-two3"]` / `D. store order AFTER drag: Zed-two Zed-one Alpha Beta Gamma Delta` / `E. rendered order with q cleared: ["Zed-two3","Zed-one3","Alpha3","Beta3","Gamma3","Delta3"]`. Node harness transcribing both functions: `BEFORE: alpha beta gamma delta zed-one zed-two` → `AFTER (clear q): zed-two zed-one alpha beta gamma delta`.
defects.mechanism: A projection (the filtered list) is passed to an API whose contract is a total order; the store's append-the-rest branch then relocates every untouched palette.
defects.reproduction: Seed localStorage['color-palettes'] with 6 local palettes; open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; type `zed` in the pane SearchBar; mouse-drag the second visible card's `.drag-handle` above the first; clear the search box. The 4 non-matching palettes have moved from positions 1-4 to 3-6 and the new order is persisted.
defects.proposedCure: A drag is a gesture over a total order; a filtered list is a projection — stop conflating them. KISS answer: withdraw the drag affordance while a filter is active (`:draggable="!pm.searchQuery.value"` on PaletteCard plus `option('disabled', …)` on the sortable). Richer answer: translate the projection move into the base order — locate the dragged id and its target neighbour in `pm.savedPalettes.value`, splice there, and pass the FULL id list.

defects.defect: A single stored `oklch()` colour string destroys the whole pane on card expand, emitting zero pageErrors and zero console errors.
defects.evidence: Isolation table, one browser context per case, one click on the card: `CONTROL_valid "#ff0055" cardsAfter=1 CRASHED=false` / `oklch_empty "oklch()" cardsAfter=0 CRASHED=true` / `garbage "not-a-color" CRASHED=false` / `rgb_nan`, `hsl_inf`, `#`, `[]` all CRASHED=false. Post-crash: `document.querySelector('.palette-card-grid')` is null; boundary text `"This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')"`; pageerror count 0, console.error count 0 (ErrorBoundary.vue:69 `return false` halts propagation). Untrusted ingress: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:122-123 `onSaveRemote(palette) { addPublishedPalette(palette) }` spreads remote server rows into the local store; the store deserializer (usePaletteStore.ts:21-32) validates only `typeof parsed.version === "number"`.
defects.mechanism: No validation at the store→render boundary, plus no per-card error isolation, so the repo's known live parseCssColor('oklch()') crash class (R1) escalates from one bad swatch to a full pane teardown.
defects.reproduction: localStorage['color-palettes'] = {"version":1,"palettes":[{"id":"p1","name":"Probe","slug":"probe","colors":[{"css":"oklch()"}],"isLocal":true,"createdAt":"…","updatedAt":"…"}]}; load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; click the card once. The pane is replaced by the ErrorBoundary 'Try again' plate.
defects.proposedCure: Two structural layers: (1) validate ONCE at the store's own choke point — make `usePaletteStore`'s serializer `read()` a real validator (shape + per-colour `CSS.supports('color', css)`) instead of a `typeof version` rubber stamp, and route `addPublishedPalette` through it; (2) wrap the CARD in the repo's existing ErrorBoundary rather than the pane, so one bad palette costs one row. Library-side parseCssColor hardening stays the parser band's business (R1).

defects.defect: Malformed or partial `color-palettes` store shapes crash the app at boot or kill the pane on the first keystroke in its search box.
defects.evidence: Six shapes, six failures (measured, one context each): `{"version":1}` → PAGE ERROR "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')", grid never mounts; `{"version":1,"palettes":{}}` and `…"palettes":"oops"` → PAGE ERROR "getStore(...).value.palettes.filter is not a function"; palette with no `colors` key → ErrorBoundary "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')"; `colors: null` → ErrorBoundary "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')"; `name: null` → renders fine, then dies on the FIRST KEYSTROKE in the SearchBar with ErrorBoundary "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toLowerCase')" — the predicate at demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:112-114 `p.name.toLowerCase()`.
defects.mechanism: Same root as D-2: the deserializer at usePaletteStore.ts:25 checks only the `version` field, so every downstream consumer casts rather than knows. The first three are page errors, not boundary catches, because `savedPalettes` (usePaletteStore.ts:51) is a module-level computed evaluated outside any boundary's reach.
defects.reproduction: Set localStorage['color-palettes'] to any of the six strings above and load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes (for the `name: null` case, additionally type one character into 'Search your palettes...').
defects.proposedCure: Identical to D-2 §1 — make the serializer `read()` the single validating boundary that turns raw JSON into a genuinely-typed `PaletteStore`. Validate once there and every one of the nine downstream consumers reads a guaranteed shape with no defensive `?.` scattered across the tree.

defects.defect: `cardRefs` retains unmounted PaletteCard instances forever and grows without bound.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.id] = el)"` — the `el &&` guard discards Vue's unmount call. Vue calls function refs with null on unmount: node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:1763 `const value = isUnmount ? null : refValue;` then `if (shared.isFunction(ref)) callWithErrorHandling(ref, owner, 12, [value, refs])`. Measured (filter to nothing): `A. after mount, 6 seeded: {n:6, cards:6}` → `B. search 'zzzznomatch': {n:6, cards:0}`. Measured (unboundedness, 5 churn rounds of deleteAll+create-2-with-fresh-UUIDs, only 2 cards ever rendered): n = 2 → 4 → 6 → 8 → 10 → 12.
defects.mechanism: A short-circuit guard written for truthiness swallows the framework's own release signal; each retained value is a component public-instance proxy holding $el, setupState, the effect scope and the useLiquidPress/useHoverPopover closures.
defects.reproduction: Seed 2 palettes, open /#/palettes, then repeatedly call the port's `onDeleteAllSaved()` and `createPalette(...)` (fresh crypto.randomUUID ids). Read `Object.keys(cardRefs).length` off the PalettesPane instance between rounds: it rises 2,4,6,8,10,12 while `.palette-card-grid > [role=article]` stays at 2. Released only by page reload.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the map — it is contrivance. The pane needs at most one card's feedback at a time: move the feedback state into `usePaletteActions` as `feedbackFor: Ref<{id,message,variant}|null>` and have PaletteCard render ActionFeedback from a prop. Data down, no instance reaching. That one move also deletes D-5, the `defineExpose({showFeedback})` and two `any` casts. If a map must survive, the guard must be `(el) => { if (el) cardRefs[id] = el; else delete cardRefs[id]; }`.

defects.defect: A publish whose result lands after its card unmounts is silently lost — and the result is written into a retained dead instance, because the leak makes the `if (card)` guard always pass.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:199-209 — nothing revalidates mount state after `await pm.onPublish(palette)`. Measured with a control (port onPublish replaced by a 1200ms one modelling a real round trip, everything else shipped code): `CONTROL (card mounted, +1.6s): ["Published!"]` — chip renders; `RACE in-flight state: {"retained":true,"isUnmounted":true}`; `RACE chips after remount (+0.5s): []` — nothing, ever.
defects.mechanism: Unguarded post-await imperative reach into a child instance, compounded by D-4: the leak keeps `cardRefs[id]` truthy so the code takes the 'delivered' branch and writes to a corpse; the card that remounts is a fresh instance with feedbackVisible=false.
defects.reproduction: Seed 2 palettes; open /#/palettes; invoke the pane's onPublish on the first palette; while the request is in flight set `pm.searchQuery.value = 'zzzznomatch'` (unmounting the card); wait for resolution; clear the search. No feedback chip ever appears, for success or failure.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-4's cure — state that must survive an unmount belongs in the port, not in a child instance the parent pokes. If the imperative shape is kept at all, the guard must be `if (card && !card.$.isUnmounted)`, but that is a patch on a design that should not reach into instances.

defects.defect: The pane has no live region anywhere: publish success/failure and bulk-delete results are never announced.
defects.evidence: Measured with 5 palettes seeded at 1440×900: `live: []` — zero `[aria-live]`, `[role=status]` or `[role=alert]` inside the pane. demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue:4-15 renders the chip as a plain `<div>` with no role and no aria-live. Same file, lines 37-47: the 2500ms auto-dismiss setTimeout is never cleared on unmount (no onUnmounted/onScopeDispose; the watch only clears on the NEXT visibility change).
defects.mechanism: Async result feedback implemented as a purely visual chip; no status-message semantics, plus an uncancelled timer that outlives its component.
defects.reproduction: Seed palettes, open /#/palettes, publish a palette (backend unreachable is fine — the failure chip renders). Query the pane for `[aria-live],[role=status],[role=alert]`: empty. A screen-reader user is told nothing in either outcome.
defects.proposedCure: `role="status"` on the feedback chip (it is literally a status message — WCAG 2.2 4.1.3 AA), clear the timer in `onScopeDispose`, and once D-4's cure lands, promote it to ONE pane-level status region rather than one per card.

defects.defect: Drag-to-reorder is keyboard-inoperable and its handle is a 16×16 CSS-px target with no accessible name.
defects.evidence: Measured with 5 cards: `dragHandles: [{tag:"svg", tabindex:null, role:null, aria:null, w:16, h:16} ×5]`. Grid tabbables are only the five 'Palette menu' buttons. Card menu items measured: ["Publish","Rename","Export","Delete"] — no move-up/move-down alternative exists. Site: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:47-50 (bare `<GripVertical class="drag-handle …">`), consumed by PalettesPane.vue:184 `handle: ".drag-handle"`.
defects.mechanism: The reorder affordance is a decorative SVG driven exclusively by SortableJS pointer events; no focusable element, no role, no name, no single-pointer or keyboard alternative.
defects.reproduction: Seed 5 palettes, open /#/palettes, and Tab through the grid: focus visits only the five 'Palette menu' buttons; the drag handles are unreachable. Measure any handle's bounding box: 16×16 against the 24×24 floor. WCAG 2.2 failures: 2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA), 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum (AA).
defects.proposedCure: Make the handle a real `<button aria-label="Reorder {name}">` with arrow-key (or Space-to-lift) handling driving the same `pm.reorderPalettes`, and grow its hit area to >=24px via padding while the glyph stays 16px. If the pattern recurs, it belongs in glass-ui as a `DragHandle` primitive — not as a demo-local one-off (edict 4).

defects.defect: `role="list"` owns `role="article"` children — an invalid ARIA structure that reports zero list items.
defects.evidence: Measured with 5 cards: `gridRole: "list"`, `gridChildRoles: ["div[role=article]" ×5]`, `listitem count: 0`. Sites: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 (`role="list"`) and demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:22 (`role="article"`). In the empty state the list's only child is the EmptyState `div[role=status]` (measured) — a live region as an owned child of a list.
defects.mechanism: Two components each chose a defensible role in isolation; the composition PalettesPane assembles is invalid. WAI-ARIA 1.2, role `list`: Required Owned Elements: `listitem`.
defects.reproduction: Seed >=1 palette, open /#/palettes, and inspect `.palette-card-grid` and its children: role=list with N article children and 0 listitem. Assistive tech announces a list of 0 items and listitem navigation commands do not work.
defects.proposedCure: The CARD is the role to change: a saved palette is an item in a collection, not an independent syndicable composition. PaletteCard becomes `role="listitem"` (keeping its aria-label); PaletteCardGrid keeps `role="list"`; the EmptyState moves outside the list element. `article` survives only where a card renders standalone.

defects.defect: The list argument passed to `useSortable` is a detached, unobservable snapshot — a load-bearing-looking argument that does nothing.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:183 `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, {...})` passes `.value` of a ComputedRef (useFilteredList.ts:8). node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js (v14.3.0): `const defaultOptions = { onUpdate: (e) => moveArrayElement(list, e.oldIndex, e.newIndex, e) }` and inside moveArrayElement `const _valueIsRef = isRef(list); const array = _valueIsRef ? [...toValue(list)] : toValue(list);` — isRef is false, so it splices the computed's cached array in place. That array is a fresh `.filter()` result (usePaletteStore.ts:51, useFilteredList.ts:11) replaced on the next store write.
defects.mechanism: Unwrapping a ref at the call site converts a reactive binding into a one-shot snapshot; the mutation is untracked and detached, so it can never be observed. Reordering works only because the custom onEnd independently calls reorderPalettes and VueUse's default onUpdate reverts Sortable's DOM move first.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis-free but effect-free by construction: read the two cited sources. No user-visible symptom; the harm is that it reads as intentional to the next maintainer and camouflages D-1.
defects.proposedCure: Pass the ref itself (`pm.filteredSaved`) or nothing at all, and own the move explicitly in `onUpdate` — the hook the library actually reserves for it — instead of in `onEnd`.

defects.defect: Per-instance utility restyle of a design-system Button, contradicted 49 lines later in the same file by the correct API.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:63-72 `<Button variant="ghost" icon-only size="xs" class="cursor-pointer text-muted-foreground hover:text-destructive focus-visible:text-destructive hover:bg-destructive/10">` versus demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:116 `<Button tone="destructive">` in the same Dialog.
defects.mechanism: A quiet-destructive register hand-rolled in utilities on one trigger while the design system's own destructive tone is used on the other — violating owner edicts 4 (glass-ui is the design system) and 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance).
defects.reproduction: NONE — static, in-file: read lines 63-72 against line 116. `cursor-pointer` on a `<Button>` is further evidence the root recipe is being second-guessed per instance.
defects.proposedCure: Add a `tone="destructive" emphasis="quiet"` (or equivalent) variant to glass-ui's Button and carry ZERO utilities on this trigger. Relay to the active glass-ui BH inbox per the standing relay edict.

defects.defect: Non-idiomatic template refs plus three `any` escapes where Vue 3.5's `useTemplateRef` is the idiom — and is already used elsewhere in this repo.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:180-181 `const sortableGridRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid> | null>(null)` + `computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined)`; :84 `:ref="(el: any) => …"`. The 3.5 idiom is in the tree already: demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:39 `const alertRef = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>("alertRef")`.
defects.mechanism: `$el` is absent from the component's InstanceType surface, so the code casts through `any` instead of exposing what it needs — owner edict 7 (idiomatic Vue 3.5).
defects.reproduction: NONE — static: compare PalettesPane.vue:180-181 with ErrorBoundary.vue:39.
defects.proposedCure: `useTemplateRef` for the grid, and have PaletteCardGrid `defineExpose` its root element (or hold a plain element ref on a wrapper) so the `as any` disappears rather than being relocated.

defects.defect: Three dead imports that both configured gates are structurally unable to see — a vacuous-gate finding in its own right.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:128 imports `watch, onMounted, nextTick`; `grep -n "watch|onMounted|nextTick" demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue` returns line 128 and nothing else. `npx eslint demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue` → no output (clean), because eslint.config.js sets `"@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars": "off"` at :71 and :185 and `"no-unused-vars": "off"` at :81, :118, :186. `grep -n noUnusedLocals tsconfig.base.json` → no match.
defects.mechanism: Fossil of a removed lifecycle block; the repo's lint config deliberately disables unused-vars and tsconfig never enables noUnusedLocals, so dead code accretes undetected — exactly what owner edict 2 (no legacy) exists to prevent.
defects.reproduction: Run the two commands above from the repo root.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the three specifiers, and enable `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters` in tsconfig.base.json (type-only, zero churn on correct code) so the gate can see the next one. Type-only imports elsewhere in the file are correctly `import type` (:151), so verbatimModuleSyntax is already satisfied.

defects.defect: Test vacuity: the pane's entire gate is two visibility assertions; six feature-deleting mutations all keep the suite green.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "Search your palettes|filteredSaved|reorderPalettes|Delete all saved|showFeedback" test/ e2e/` returns exactly one hit: e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:63. walk.spec.ts:57-66 asserts only that the 'My Palettes' heading and the 'Search your palettes...' placeholder are visible. flows/palette-save.spec.ts exercises CurrentPaletteEditor only (asserts palettes.length >= 1); flows/palette-delete.spec.ts is a BROWSE-pane spec for a remote palette. 41 vitest files, 71 e2e specs, zero coverage of the saved-card grid, the sortable, the delete-all dialog or the publish feedback.
defects.mechanism: Existence assertions substituted for behaviour assertions.
defects.reproduction: Apply any of: M1 delete useSortable(...) lines 183-197; M2 `pm.reorderPalettes([])`; M3 v-for over `pm.savedPalettes.value` instead of `pm.filteredSaved.value` (the SearchBar becomes decorative — the spec asserts only that it is visible); M4 delete the `card.showFeedback(...)` call at line 207; M5 delete the whole delete-all `<Dialog>` block lines 102-122; M6 delete the `:ref` callback at line 84. Every one leaves the full suite GREEN.
defects.proposedCure: Behaviour gates that would have caught D-1, D-4 and D-5 outright: a spec that seeds a populated store, reorders under an active filter and asserts the untouched palettes' positions are invariant; a spec that asserts `Object.keys(cardRefs)` shrinks when cards unmount; a spec that asserts a publish chip appears after a routed, delayed API response.

defects.defect: The irreversible bulk-delete confirm is `role="dialog"` with no `aria-modal`, and is not an `alertdialog`.
defects.evidence: Measured: `H dialog open: {"active":"BUTTON:Cancel","dialogRole":"dialog","ariaModal":null}` / `I after Escape: {"active":"BUTTON:Delete all saved palettes","dialogOpen":false}`. Call site: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:102-122 `<DialogContent surface="glass" :show-close="false">`.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui `DialogContent` emits `role="dialog"` without `aria-modal="true"`, so AT is not told to constrain virtual-cursor review; and an alert-plus-confirm for an irreversible action is semantically `alertdialog`. Focus management itself measured CORRECT (initial focus on the safe Cancel; Escape restores focus to the trigger).
defects.reproduction: Seed >=1 palette, open /#/palettes, click 'Delete all saved palettes', then inspect the dialog element's `role` and `aria-modal`.
defects.proposedCure: Producer fix in glass-ui: `aria-modal="true"` on DialogContent, plus an `alertdialog` variant for destructive confirms. BH relay item under the standing glass-ui relay edict — not a demo-side override (edict 5).

defects.defect: The mega-tranche visual REPORT records ZERO contribution from this component because all four /#/palettes captures ran with an empty library, and the pane's crash class emits no console or page errors at all.
defects.evidence: REPORT.md:120/135/150/165 — /#/palettes bodyTextLength 237 (desktop) / 169 (mobile) = the empty-plate state; pageErr 0, consoleErr 0 on every row. Re-running the harness' own probe against a clean profile attributes all 8 smallTapTargets and the 1 namelessButton on that route: input 160×23 (dock slug form), 3× button 22×22 'Switch to slug'/'Generate new slug'/'Cancel' (dock), 4× span 12×24 'L/A/B/ALPHA channel' (picker sliders), nameless button 24×24 `.send-btn` (dock). NONE belong to PalettesPane. Its real contribution — 5 × 16×16 drag handles, one per card — never appears because no card rendered.
defects.mechanism: The capture matrix probes an unpopulated state, and its defect signals (pageErrors/consoleErrors) are exactly the ones ErrorBoundary.vue:69 `return false` suppresses — so a total pane teardown reads as a clean route.
defects.reproduction: Compare REPORT.json's /#/palettes a11y block (8 small targets, all dock/picker) with a re-probe at the same viewport with 5 seeded palettes (5 additional 16×16 drag handles, role=list/article mismatch, no live region — none of which the matrix saw).
defects.proposedCure: Harness fix, not component fix: seed a populated localStorage['color-palettes'] for the palettes and browse routes in capture.mjs, and add a `.vj-error-boundary` presence probe to every capture — the boundary element is the ONLY observable a swallowed crash leaves behind.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context), exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. The seat was spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration — declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — drag-to-reorder is doubly applied. `PalettesPane.vue:183-197` supplies only `onEnd` to `useSortable`, so vueuse's default `onUpdate` (`@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:14-16`, `moveArrayElement(list, …)`) still runs and splices the plain array `pm.filteredSaved.value` — which with an empty query IS the `savedPalettes` computed's cached array — and then `onEnd` re-reads that already-mutated array and applies the move a SECOND time before `reorderPalettes`. Measured, deterministic across 4 live WebKit runs: dragging row 0 onto row 1 of `[Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Zulu One, Zulu Two]` yields `[Charlie, Bravo, Zulu One, Zulu Two, Alpha]` — every row moves, the item lands nowhere near the drop target — and after reload the order reverts to the original, so the gesture is both wrong and non-persistent. With a search filter active the same handler builds `ids` from the SUBSET and `usePaletteStore.ts:153-167` appends the remainder, so swapping two visible rows silently demotes three untouched, invisible palettes (measured: `Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Zulu One, Zulu Two` → `Zulu Two, Zulu One, Alpha, Bravo, Charlie`).
result.negativeProof: Attacked and could NOT break, recorded to keep the report honest: (1) Reflow — measured at 720/360/320 CSS px with a seeded store, `document.scrollWidth - clientWidth = 0` at every width, the dual grid collapses to one column (gridTemplateColumns 688px → 328px → 288px), and every control stays 33–143px INSIDE the right edge; my first `document.documentElement.style.zoom = 2` result (delete-all at x=1544 in a 1440 viewport) was a CSS-`zoom` artefact and the honest narrow-viewport arm refutes it — no reflow defect. (2) RTL at 1440 — the pane mirrors cleanly (x 729 → 199), `justify-end` delete-all mirrors with it (x 1188 → 224), search reports `direction: rtl`, overflowX 0, no card clipped. (3) The EmptyPaletteMark matches VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 exactly: `EmptyState.vue:37-48` renders exactly three `WatercolorDot variant="ghost" tag="div"` inside `aria-hidden="true"`. (4) The count badge does not poison the heading name — `PalettesPane.vue:19-25` marks the Badge `aria-hidden="true"` with an `sr-only` companion; measured accessible name is "My Palettes (5 saved)", honouring P4-R3. (5) `verbatimModuleSyntax` is clean — the file's sole type-only import, `PalettesPane.vue:151 import type { Palette }`, is correctly annotated. (6) The tracked Safari matrix shows `/#/palettes` with overflowX 0, main 1, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0 in all four matrices (`visual/REPORT.md:120,135,150,165`) — the defects are design, not crashes. (7) `usePaletteActions.ts:65-77` is correctly local-first: `createPalette` runs unconditionally and the network act is deferred to publish, so a save with the backend down loses nothing.

defects.defect: Drag-to-reorder is doubly applied: one drag permutes the entire library, lands on a position the user never dropped on, and the result is lost on reload.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:183-197 supplies only `onEnd`; node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:14-16 `defaultOptions = { onUpdate: (e) => moveArrayElement(list, e.oldIndex, e.newIndex, e) }` therefore survives. Live WebKit 1440x1200, seeded 5 palettes, real mouse drag, 2 identical runs — drag row 0 -> row 1: DOM+localStorage become ['Charlie','Bravo','Zulu One','Zulu Two','Alpha']; after reload ['Alpha','Bravo','Charlie','Zulu One','Zulu Two']. Drag row 0 -> row 2: ['Charlie','Zulu One','Bravo','Zulu Two','Alpha'].
defects.mechanism: Two authorities apply one gesture to the same data. The vendor default splices `pm.filteredSaved.value` — a plain array captured once at setup which, for an empty query, IS the array `savedPalettes` (usePaletteStore.ts:51-55) cached (useFilteredList.ts:10 returns `items.value` unchanged) — then `onEnd` re-reads that already-mutated array and applies the move again before calling `reorderPalettes`. Neither writer is the store's transactional owner.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/pp-D-drag2.mjs (seeds localStorage `color-palettes` with 5 named palettes, loads http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, drags .drag-handle nth(0) onto card nth(1), reads localStorage, reloads, reads again).
defects.proposedCure: Reorder is a store transaction over identity, not a DOM side effect over a projection. Expose `movePalette(id, beforeId|null)` in usePaletteStore resolving against the FULL ordered list by id; make sortable a pure input by supplying `onUpdate` (displacing the vendor default) and deleting `onEnd`; disable reorder entirely while `searchQuery` is non-empty. Then implement the VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 keyboard grammar against the same `movePalette`, which is what makes pointer and keyboard resolve to one ordinal.

defects.defect: Reordering inside a search filter silently re-sorts palettes the user cannot see and never touched.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:190 `const ids = pm.filteredSaved.value.map((p) => p.id)` builds the id list from the SUBSET; usePaletteStore.ts:153-167 `reorderPalettes` places `orderedIds` first then appends the remainder. Measured live: store before ['Alpha','Bravo','Charlie','Zulu One','Zulu Two'], query 'Zulu' (2 of 5 visible), swap the two visible rows -> store after ['Zulu Two','Zulu One','Alpha','Bravo','Charlie'].
defects.mechanism: The filtered projection is mistaken for the collection. A partial ordering handed to a whole-list reorder promotes the matched set and demotes everything else.
defects.reproduction: pp-D-drag.mjs block B: fill the search input with 'Zulu', drag handle 0 onto card 1, read localStorage, then clear the search and re-read the DOM order.
defects.proposedCure: Same as D-1: `movePalette(id, beforeId)` over identity, and forbid the gesture while a filter is active — a projection has no ordinals to move. If ordering under filter is genuinely wanted, it must be expressed as a move relative to a neighbouring id in the FULL list.

defects.defect: The Library has no operation-state surface at all — no pending, no error, no storage-recovery arm — so publish failure can be silent and a corrupted store renders as a cheerful empty library.
defects.evidence: usePalettePorts.ts:136-153 `libraryPort` has 15 members, all data or commands, zero operation state; the sibling `browsePort` (usePalettePorts.ts:155-190) carries `browsing`, `browseError`, `loadingMore`, `sortLoading`. PalettesPane.vue:203-204 `const id = palette.id; if (id == null) return;` discards the awaited `{success:false, message:'Failed to publish: …'}`. usePaletteStore.ts:22-31 swallows a corrupt store and returns `defaultStore`. EmptyState.vue:17-29 ships an unused `variant="error"` with role=alert and a Retry slot; PaletteCardSkeleton.vue (124 lines, exported at browser/card/index.ts:6) is used by BrowsePane.vue:49,130 and ExtractWorkbench.vue:103 and never by PalettesPane.
defects.mechanism: Operation truth was never modelled. The only result channel is a transient in-card banner (`card.showFeedback`), which VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 forbids as the sole truth, and it is dropped on a null id. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 requires corrupt storage to REPLACE the Library body with a recovery article and says it is 'never rendered as an empty library'.
defects.reproduction: Publish path: usePaletteActions.ts:40-58 awaits ensureUser -> ensureSession -> createAndSavePalette with no pending render anywhere in PalettesPane.vue:199-209. Corrupt-store path: write invalid JSON to localStorage key `color-palettes`; usePaletteStore.ts:22-31 returns defaultStore and the pane renders 'No saved palettes yet.' with Delete-all still live beside it.
defects.proposedCure: Add `pending` (per entity), `lastError` and `storageState` to libraryPort. Render per-entity pending/failure persistently in the selected inspector (which D-2's cure creates), and render one storage-recovery article that REPLACES the field body — diagnosis, export, separately confirmed reset. Reuse EmptyState variant='error' and PaletteCardSkeleton; both already exist and are already used one file over.

defects.defect: The palette card is a clickable role="article" with no selection seat: not focusable, no aria-pressed/expanded, no keydown — expand is pointer-only and unreachable by keyboard or AT.
defects.evidence: Measured live (5 seeded palettes, 1440 and 390, light and dark): card root tabindex=null, tabIndex=-1, onkeydown=false, aria-pressed=null, aria-expanded=null, aria-selected=null, cursor='pointer', class='group rounded-card cartoon-surface border-card-edge bg-well cursor-pointer'. Tab order inside the pane: ['Search your palettes...','Delete all saved palettes','Palette menu' x5] — the card never appears. Wired at PalettesPane.vue:91 `@click="pm.toggleExpand(palette.id)"` onto PaletteCard.vue:22-26 (`role="article"` + `@click="$emit('click')"`). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 verbatim: 'A palette card is a bounded entity article, not a clickable role=article … The card body owns no expand, inline rename, action menu, transient result or hover-only swatch-action path.'
defects.mechanism: Because the route has no inspector lane (D-2), every entity action had to be crammed into the card body, and a div with cursor:pointer was used instead of the mandated native `<button type="button" aria-pressed>` seat. Zero such seats exist on the route.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a seeded store; Tab through the pane — focus goes search -> delete-all -> palette menus, never to a card; press Enter/Space anywhere and nothing expands. `document.querySelector('[role=article]').tabIndex` returns -1.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the omnibus. Card root becomes a non-interactive <article> carrying the exact §3.1 tuple (Card size='sm' material='content' tier='quiet' surface='opaque' :shadow='false' :grain='false' specular='off'); the specimen+identity region becomes one native <button type='button' :aria-pressed> that selects into the inspector lane; rename, menu, export, publish and their durable state move to that inspector; the reorder handle stays a separate named sibling control.

defects.defect: The /palettes desktop composition is an exact 50/50 split — neither sanctioned ratio, 14 percentage points below the Library field floor — and the companion lane is the Picker, not the mandated selected-inspector.
defects.evidence: Measured live, WebKit 1440x900: `.pane-container--dual` gridTemplateColumns = '512px 512px'; lane 0 (Picker) x=199 w=512, lane 1 (PalettesPane) x=729 w=512 — exactly 50.000%/50.000%. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 1 permits only golden (61.8033989/38.1966011) or preview-dominant (66.6666667/33.3333333); §3.1 Library row requires field 64%…66.6666667% and a 'complementary selected action/history inspector at 33.3333333%…36%'.
defects.mechanism: A default two-up layout was used where an earned composition is required, and the second lane was filled with an unrelated instrument instead of the Library's own inspector. The missing inspector is the direct cause of D-4 (all entity actions collapse into the card body) and D-7 (operation state has nowhere persistent to live).
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 1440x900 and evaluate getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.pane-container--dual')).gridTemplateColumns -> '512px 512px'.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the §3.1 Library composition literally: owner-state field at 64–66.7%, selected action/history inspector at 33.3–36%, inspector ABSENT (not empty) when nothing is selected. The Picker does not belong in the Library route's stage.

defects.defect: The empty invitation occupies 90.2% of the stage against a 15% ceiling and content-hugs nothing, and carries no action.
defects.evidence: Measured live, empty store, 1440x900: the [role=status] empty block is 462 x 218.1 px inside a 512px pane = 90.2% of the stage, 32.1% of the viewport width. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 2: 'Empty secondary content occupies at most a narrow invitation tray (≤15% of the stage) or disappears. It never receives half the viewport.' §7: 'A true empty invitation content-hugs its text/action.' PaletteCardGrid.vue:28-30 exposes an #emptyAction slot; PalettesPane.vue:75-81 never fills it.
defects.mechanism: The empty state is rendered inside a fixed half-viewport lane with col-span-full + justify-center + min-h-[120px], so it inherits the protagonist's geometry instead of shrinking to its own content.
defects.reproduction: Clear localStorage key `color-palettes`, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 1440x900, measure document.querySelector('[role=status]').getBoundingClientRect() against the enclosing .pane-scroll-fade rect. Also visible in the tracked capture docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png.
