defects.proposedCure: On empty, collapse the field to a content-hugging invitation tray (≤15% of stage) with a real action in #emptyAction ('Save current colors'), and let the route reclaim the remaining stage rather than reserving half the viewport for a sentence.

defects.defect: The pastel-rainbow identity — one of exactly two sanctioned coordinates in the product — is chromatically dead in dark mode; the three 'rainbow' stops are perceptually one near-white colour.
defects.evidence: Live computed tokens, WebKit 1440. Light --palettes-ramp-title-0/1/2 = oklch(47.093% 0.188343 329.834) / oklch(47.093% 0.188343 9.834) / oklch(47.093% 0.124795 49.834); dark = oklch(95.832% 0.033662 329.834) / oklch(95.832% 0.021053 9.834) / oklch(95.832% 0.023120 49.834). Mean chroma 0.1671 light vs 0.0260 dark = 6.4x collapse; OKLab ΔE between outer stops 0.207 light vs 0.0221 dark = 9.4x less separation (ΔE 0.022 at L 0.958 is at or below JND for text glyphs). Independently confirmed by per-column glyph-ink sampling of the tracked 2880x1800 Safari PNGs: light chroma mean 0.1502 (hue 336.7 -> 54.8 deg), dark chroma mean 0.0239. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2: 'Both coordinates render in light and dark.'
defects.mechanism: demo/color-session/palettes-ramp.ts:104-120 certifies each stop to a WCAG floor by walking LIGHTNESS along the hue's gamut cusp. Against a dark plate the reachable direction is up, so all three stops land at L 95.8%, where OKLCH chroma is arithmetically tiny for every hue. The certification succeeds by destroying the thing it certifies — the module's own header admits the open bracket.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with colorScheme dark and read getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--palettes-ramp-title-0/1/2'); or open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/palettes.png beside safari-desktop-light/palettes.png.
defects.proposedCure: Certify hue-preserving CHROMA, not lightness alone: hold the analogous fan's chroma at the dark-plate cusp and take the contrast from the plate (darken the resting tier locally behind the word) rather than from the ink. If the plate cannot move, take the large-text 3:1 floor at a mid lightness in dark (L ~0.72–0.78) where C ~0.10 is still reachable, so the word reads as pastel rainbow — the whole point of the coordinate.

defects.defect: The per-site ramp floor split — an entire resolver arm, a second token family and a per-instance alias — produces a difference below the just-noticeable threshold, and exactly zero difference in dark.
defects.evidence: Measured live: in dark, --palettes-ramp-0/1/2 and --palettes-ramp-title-0/1/2 are byte-identical. In light they are identical on stops 0 and 1; stop 2 differs by ΔL 1.34 percentage points and ΔC 0.0035, i.e. ΔE_ok ~0.014 — below JND. The machinery: palettes-ramp.ts:83-88 (two floors 4.5/3.0), useViewAccents.ts:146-165 (two mints), PalettesPane.vue:171-175 (the alias object).
defects.mechanism: An architecture was built to serve a distinction that the certification walk then flattens. Complexity with no measurable output delta.
defects.reproduction: Read both token triples off document.documentElement at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes in each scheme and diff them.
defects.proposedCure: One resolver, one token triple on :root, one .palettes-ramp-text recipe. Delete RAMP_LARGE_TEXT_CONTRAST_FLOOR, the second mint in useViewAccents, and the rampTitleVars alias in PalettesPane.

defects.defect: A search that matches nothing renders the empty-library invitation, so the pane asserts '5 saved' in its header and 'No saved palettes yet.' in its body at the same time, and offers the wrong remedy.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:77-80 keys `:empty` to `pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0` while the copy speaks about the unfiltered collection. Measured live (5 seeded palettes, query 'qqqzzz', both schemes, 1440 and 390): header badge '5', sr-only '(5 saved)', body [role=status] '· empty plate · No saved palettes yet. Add colors above, then save the set.', cards rendered 0, delete-all still present true. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1 requires the in-route filter to 'announce changed result count/state through the owning status region' — when results return (query 'Zulu' -> 2 cards, measured) the status region unmounts and nothing is announced.
defects.mechanism: One boolean is asked to carry three distinct states (empty library, no matches, populated). The role=status region also announces the wrong sentence to AT on every keystroke that empties the result set.
defects.reproduction: Seed 5 palettes into localStorage `color-palettes`, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, type 'qqqzzz' into the search field, and read the header badge and the [role=status] text in the same frame.
defects.proposedCure: Three named states: empty-library (0 saved), no-matches (saved>0 and filtered=0 — copy names the query and offers 'Clear search'), populated. Give the field one persistent role=status count line so both transitions announce, instead of a status element that only exists in one of the three states.

defects.defect: Export failure is console.warn-only — precisely what the palette contract forbids verbatim — so a failed export shows the user nothing.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts:21-23 `catch (e) { console.warn('Export failed:', e); }`, wired at PalettesPane.vue:96 `@export="(p, fmt) => onExport(p, fmt)"` and consumed at PalettesPane.vue:211. PALETTE-CONTRACT.md Appendix W51 opening: 'A serializer either yields the bytes below or a visible terminal/retryable operation state — never a partial download or console.warn-only result.' Appendix W51 §8 further requires a durable ExportOperation with states captured|ready|retryable-failure|terminal-failure|handoff-initiated and failure codes storage_quota|serialization_resource|handoff_unavailable|snapshot_corrupt|serializer_contract — PalettesPane renders none, and libraryPort exposes no field to render them from.
defects.mechanism: Failure was modelled as a log line rather than as operation state on an entity. The demo's toast layer was removed (vue-sonner) and the calls were replaced with console.warn, leaving no user-facing failure channel anywhere in the pane.
defects.reproduction: Trigger any export throw (e.g. quota, or a serializer contract failure in demo/palettes/export/png.ts) via the palette card menu on http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: the DOM is unchanged and only the console records it. Static: grep -n 'console.warn' demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Model export as an operation on an entity: put the ExportOperation record in the store keyed by (snapshotDigest, format), surface Prepare FORMAT -> Download FILENAME in the selected inspector's action region, and render retryable-failure / terminal-failure as visible persistent state with a real Retry. Delete the try/catch -> console.warn.

defects.defect: Material inversion: the field is wrapped in a Card the constitution forbids, that Card declares the structural-glass tier while rendering backdrop-filter: none, and three shadow species with two opposed light sources stack in one lane.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:2 `<Card tier="resting" …>`. Measured on that element in both schemes: class 'glass-resting card …', backdrop-filter 'none', -webkit-backdrop-filter 'none', filter 'none', background-color alpha 0.664 light / 0.7536 dark, box-shadow '8px 8px 0' (hard, zero blur, down-right). Palette card box-shadow '-3px 3px 0, -5px 5px 0, -7px 7px 0' (down-left); .dashed-well '-2px 2px 0, -3px 3px 0, -4px 4px 0' (down-left). Seven hard casts, two opposed light directions, ~30 CSS px apart — see the crop D-shadow-crop.png. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2: 'Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well.' §3.1: 'the field/lane/empty/inspector have none [no Card shell]'. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 1: 'A page region … does not become a Card by default.' §3 law 8: 'Supporting fixtures do not compete with it through equal size or equal shadow.'
defects.mechanism: The Card/no-Card assignment is exactly inverted — the container that must not be a Card is one, while the entities that must be Cards are hand-rolled divs (PaletteCard.vue:12-19 states it is deliberately NOT a glass-ui Card, wearing cartoon-surface + border-card-edge + bg-well). Two shadow vocabularies (the outer plate's and the cartoon register's) were never reconciled.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes and read getComputedStyle on the .pane-scroll-fade root (backdrop-filter 'none' on a glass-resting class) and on [role=article] (three hard casts). Visually: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png shows the ambient pink washing through the field.
defects.proposedCure: Pane root -> not a Card (a landmark-neutral region on the owner workspace chassis). Entities -> the exact §3.1 tuple with shadow=false. One shadow vocabulary, one light direction, owned in glass-ui — not two registers colliding in a consumer.

defects.defect: role="list" owning role="article" children is structurally invalid ARIA — the list semantics collapse and there is no substrate for the mandated 'position of total' announcement.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 `role="list"`; PaletteCard.vue:22 `role="article"`. Measured live: gridChildRoles = ['article','article','article','article','article']. ARIA requires `list` to own `listitem`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 vertical reorder requires 'every move announces item and `position of total`'.
defects.mechanism: Landmark semantics were chosen per-card (article, for a 'landmark per palette') without reconciling them with the container's list role.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a seeded store and evaluate [...document.querySelector('.palette-card-grid').children].map(c => c.getAttribute('role')).
defects.proposedCure: Use a real <ul>/<li>, or role=list with role=listitem wrappers, and drop role=article from the entity root (it becomes a plain <article> element or nothing). The listitem is then what carries position-of-total.

defects.defect: Empty-state typography breaks the closed type matrix: help prose is set in Fira Code at 16.4px and the empty message uses display-scale Fraunces, making 'nothing here' the loudest thing on the pane.
defects.evidence: Measured live on the strings PalettesPane.vue:78-80 supplies — 'Add colors above, then save the set.' renders Fira Code 16.4px (matrix: help prose -> text-prose, Plus Jakarta Sans); 'No saved palettes yet.' renders Fraunces 25.888px (no matrix row grants display type to an empty tray); '· empty plate ·' renders Fira Code 14.384px with 2.589px tracking, uppercase (no matrix row at all). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4: 'This matrix is closed across all eighteen compositions.' PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 5: an ornament carrying no information is removed.
defects.mechanism: The empty plate was designed as its own typographic set piece rather than against the closed role matrix, and PalettesPane supplies the strings that select it.
defects.reproduction:
Clear localStorage `color-palettes`, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, and read getComputedStyle font-family/font-size on the three

elements inside [role=status]. Visually obvious in shots/safari-mobile-light/palettes.png where the mono hint is the widest ink on screen.
defects.proposedCure: Map the three strings onto the closed matrix: hint -> text-prose (Plus Jakarta Sans), message -> text-heading, and delete the '· empty plate ·' eyebrow entirely (subtraction precedes explanation). Add the missing #emptyAction instead.

defects.defect: The route has zero H1 and the Library's identity is an <h3> rendered at 41.9px — a display-sized readout that is not a document heading, alongside a sibling <h3> that is the Picker's numeric value.
defects.evidence: Measured live on /#/palettes at 1440 light: mainCount 1, h1 [] (zero), headings ['H3:92.0%,88.8,20.0', 'H3:My Palettes5 (5 saved)']; the title element is <h3> at 41.888px Fraunces weight 400. PaneHeader.vue:21 emits the <h3>; PalettesPane.vue:10-26 is its Library consumer. Corroborated across the whole tracked matrix: the h1 column is 0 on all 60 captures (docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:119-178). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Each route has one H1'. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 11: 'A display-sized readout is not therefore a document heading or live status.'
defects.mechanism: The component that owns the route's identity string cannot reach the route's heading level, because PaneHeader hardcodes h3 and the shell emits no h1. That is a composition defect, not a typo.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes and evaluate document.querySelectorAll('h1').length -> 0, and [...document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3')].map(e => e.tagName + ':' + e.textContent).
defects.proposedCure: The shell owns one stable H1 per route (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1 makes it the focus target on in-app navigation); PaneHeader's title becomes that H1 for the route it identifies, or a non-heading identity element if the shell H1 lives elsewhere. The Picker's numeric readout must stop being a heading at all.

defects.defect: The reorder handle is an unnamed 16x16 <svg> with no role and no tab stop, and the mandated keyboard reorder grammar is entirely absent.
defects.evidence: Measured live: tag 'svg', tabindex null, role null, aria-label null, rect 16x16, cursor 'grab' (PaletteCard.vue:47-50). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1: 'An optional reorder handle remains a separate named control.' §5.2 vertical reorder requires Space grab, Down=next, Up=previous, Home/End, 'position of total' announcement, Space drop, Escape cancel — zero of six are implemented anywhere in PalettesPane.vue:183-197. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 target minimum is 24x24. Drag state is `ghostClass: 'opacity-30'` and nothing else. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 names this family: 'Hover-only/unlabeled controls and invisible drag state'.
defects.mechanism: Reorder was implemented as a pointer library binding rather than as a named control over a model, so there is nothing for a keyboard or AT user to grab and nothing to announce.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a seeded store and evaluate document.querySelector('.drag-handle') -> an <svg> with no tabindex/role/aria-label and a 16x16 rect; Tab through the pane and observe it is never reached.
defects.proposedCure: Make the handle a native <button type='button'> with an accessible name that includes the palette identity and its ordinal, a >=24x24 (preferably 44x44) invisible seat around a 16px glyph (PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 7 separates glyph size from target size), and bind the §5.2 grammar to the same movePalette authority D-1's cure creates.

defects.defect: The search field has no accessible name and is 22px tall on mobile, below the WCAG 2.2 target floor; it is also styled by a per-instance override class.
defects.evidence: Measured live: {aria-label: null, aria-labelledby: null, type: 'search', id: ''} — placeholder only, and it is the FIRST tab stop in the pane. Height 24.58px at 1440, 22.0px at 390 — the sole entry in the pane's smallTargets list at mobile (24x24 AA floor). PalettesPane.vue:33-37; PalettesPane.vue:35 applies class='search-seated', which the comment at :30-32 labels an interim register 'booked onto the P3 seated rung'.
defects.mechanism: The producer SearchBar was consumed without a label and then re-registered from the consumer side rather than at the producer root — owner edict 5 (style at the root, never per-instance overrides).
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844 and evaluate the input's aria-label/aria-labelledby (both null) and getBoundingClientRect().height (22).
defects.proposedCure: Give SearchBar a required label prop (visually hidden here) at the producer, raise its control height to the 24px floor at the producer root, and delete the .search-seated consumer override by landing the seated register in glass-ui.

defects.defect: Sortable motion is a bare untokenized 150ms literal and is not gated on prefers-reduced-motion.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:185 `animation: 150,`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: 'Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register' and 'Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry and stable chromatic state.' Measured under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the pane's CSS transitions do collapse (opacity 0.1s, color 0.1s, background-color 0.1s, border-color 0.1s, box-shadow 0.1s) but the sortable options object is constructed identically — there is no matchMedia guard anywhere in the file, so sortablejs animates transform on every sibling row for 150ms per drag regardless. The converse defect on the same surface is owner-marked at visual/owner-marked/OM-8-pane-transitions-unanimated.png.
defects.mechanism: JS-driven motion sits outside the CSS reduced-motion cascade the rest of the pane relies on, and the duration is a hand constant rather than --animation-slide-sm/md/lg.
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'animation: 150' demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue; then load the route in a reduced-motion context and drag — the FLIP animation still runs.
defects.proposedCure: Read the duration from a token and pass animation: 0 when prefers-reduced-motion matches — or, better, delete the vendor animation entirely once D-1's cure makes the store the single authority and the list re-renders from model order.

defects.defect: rampTitleVars is a per-instance style override carrying duplicated literal colour constants as a masking fallback, and it buys a perceptually null difference.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:171-175 injects three inline custom properties, each `var(--palettes-ramp-title-N, oklch(0.632 0.214 …))`. The three oklch literals are copies of demo/styles/utils.css:195-197 with no link between the files; the comment at :169-170 says they 'mirror utils.css' and exist because 'utils.css stays LANE-5-OWNED + untouched'. Measured benefit: ΔE_ok ~0.014 in light on one of three stops, exactly 0 in dark (see D-3b). Owner edict 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides) and edict 2 (no masking fallbacks).
defects.mechanism: Ownership friction encoded as a defect: the consumer aliased tokens inline to avoid editing a file owned by another lane, duplicating constants in the process.
defects.reproduction: Read demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:171-175 beside demo/styles/utils.css:195-197 — the same three oklch triples appear in both with no shared source.
defects.proposedCure: One token triple on :root, one .palettes-ramp-text recipe, no inline alias, no per-site split. Delete lines 171-175 and the RAMP_LARGE_TEXT_CONTRAST_FLOOR arm; land any needed change in utils.css itself.

defects.defect: Delete-all is a 28px unlabeled ghost glyph that owns an entire layout band, sits second in the tab order, and stays live when the filter shows zero cards.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:62-73. Measured: 28x28 px, variant='ghost', icon-only, size='xs', 14px Trash2, alone in a `flex items-center justify-end` row; second focusable in the pane (tab order: search -> delete-all -> palette menus); deleteAllStillPresent true while cardsRendered is 0. The comment at :56-61 records that the row's other content (a '{n} palettes' line that 'existed only to left-balance this button') was removed and the now-empty row kept. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 5 and PR-05 (a boundary retained for one glyph). 28px clears WCAG 2.2 AA (24) but not AAA (44) — the wrong side of the ladder for an irreversible bulk-destructive action.
defects.mechanism: A destructive verb was demoted visually (from an always-red beacon to a quiet ghost) without being relocated, so it kept its dedicated band and its high tab priority while losing its legibility.
defects.reproduction: Seed 5 palettes, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, type 'qqqzzz' — the body reads 'No saved palettes yet.' and the delete-all trigger is still present and operable; Tab once from the search field to reach it.
defects.proposedCure: Move the bulk-destructive verb into the library's overflow menu or the inspector's action region with a text label, gate it on savedPalettes.length > 0 AND an unfiltered view, and delete the empty band it currently owns.

defects.defect: Sibling asymmetry: BrowsePane, in the same card cluster and ports file, has skeletons, an error plate and a Retry; PalettesPane has none of them.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:49,130 render PaletteCardSkeleton for initial load and loadingMore; BrowsePane.vue:61-78 renders EmptyState variant='error' with a Retry; browsePort carries browsing/browseError/loadingMore/sortLoading (usePalettePorts.ts:155-190). PalettesPane imports none of these and libraryPort has no state members (usePalettePorts.ts:136-153).
defects.mechanism: Two panes a user reads as one product disagree about whether pending and failure exist, because only one of the two ports was given operation state.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'PaletteCardSkeleton\|variant="error"' demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue — hits only in BrowsePane.
defects.proposedCure: Resolve at the port layer (see D-7): give libraryPort the same operation-state shape browsePort already has, then reuse the identical EmptyState/skeleton composition so the two panes read as one system.

defects.defect: Pre-Vue-3.5 template-ref idioms, two `as any` escapes, and a reactive record of component instances that is never pruned.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:177 `const cardRefs = reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`; :180-181 `ref<InstanceType<...>>` + `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el`; :84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.id] = el)"`. Owner edict 7 names useTemplateRef as the Vue 3.5 idiom. cardRefs entries are written and never deleted, so deleting a palette leaves its component instance retained under a dead id.
defects.mechanism: The function-ref-into-reactive-record pattern predates useTemplateRef and has no teardown path; `any` was used to reach $el instead of typing the child's exposed surface.
defects.reproduction: Read demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:84 and :177-181 — there is no `delete cardRefs[id]` anywhere in the file. HYPOTHESIS on the retention magnitude: not measured.
defects.proposedCure: Use useTemplateRef for the grid, have PaletteCardGrid defineExpose a typed root element (retiring the `as any` $el reach), and either prune cardRefs on delete or — better — remove it entirely once showFeedback moves to the inspector under D-7's cure.

defects.defect: Three dead imports.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:128 `import { inject, reactive, ref, computed, watch, onMounted, nextTick } from "vue";` — `watch`, `onMounted` and `nextTick` each occur exactly once in the file, on that line (grep -c returns 1 for each).
defects.mechanism: Leftover surface from an earlier lifecycle the component no longer has.
defects.reproduction: for id in watch onMounted nextTick; do grep -c "\\b$id\\b" demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue; done -> 1 1 1.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the three identifiers from the import.

defects.defect: Evidence gap: /palettes appears in zero of the six state matrices, which is why the dark ramp collapse and the missing focus seat were never caught.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/{forced-colors-desktop,keyboard-focus-desktop,reduced-motion-desktop,rtl-desktop,rtl-mobile,zoom-200-desktop}/ each contain only adminusers.png, blob.png, browse.png, gradient.png, picker.png. The Library route — one of the eleven named VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 members and owner of one of the two pastel-identity coordinates — has no RTL, zoom, forced-colors, reduced-motion or keyboard-focus capture.
defects.mechanism: The state matrix sampled five routes rather than the eleven named members, and the Library was not among them.
defects.reproduction: ls docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/*/ | grep -c palettes -> 0 outside the four safari-* route matrices.
defects.proposedCure: Capture /palettes across all six state matrices as a precondition of any close on this component; the forced-colors arm additionally needs a real WHCM engine, since Playwright/WebKit forcedColors emulation rendered the page unchanged in my probe and is not decisive for the background-clip:text identity (.palettes-ramp-text is absent from the forced-colors tier-1 roster at demo/styles/foundation.css:678-695).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteCardMenu.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context arm), the tier explicitly declared at spawn. Seat declared, not inherited; no defect on this axis.
result.strongestDefect: D-3 — `@click.prevent` on the Export sub-trigger (PaletteCardMenu.vue:108) sets `event.defaultPrevented`, and reka-ui's `MenuSubTrigger.onClick` early-returns on exactly that flag (reka-ui/dist/Menu/MenuSubTrigger.js:132). A touch pointer emits no `pointermove`, so `onClick` is its ONLY submenu-open path — therefore the entire Export submenu (JSON / CSS Custom Properties / Tailwind Config / SVG Swatch / PNG Swatch) is unreachable on every touch device. Measured on an iPhone 14 context with real tap(): two taps leave `aria-expanded="false"`, `data-state="closed"`, no sub-content in the DOM; same-context control with a non-cancelable click (preventDefault a no-op) opens it (`subContentPresent: true`). Desktop masks the defect entirely because hover opens the submenu before the click lands.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict, but recorded as the seat's positive findings so the report is not one-sided: (1) MOTION is fully sound — the component declares none of its own (edict 6 satisfied), and the producer motion it inherits is PRM-honest: measured `transition-property` collapses from `scale, translate, opacity, filter, display, overlay` @ 0.35s to `opacity` @ 0.15s under `reducedMotion: "reduce"`, `animation-duration` 0s → 1e-05s, and no layout-forcing property (width/height/top/left) is animated. (2) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — both type-only imports are `import type` (:177, :178). (3) Vue 3.5 idiom clean — reactive props destructure (:206), `computed` for both derived flags, no `defineModel` stale-read hazard. (4) The DI seam is correct — `useApiClient()` (:216) reads the availability latch through the provided client, not a module singleton, exactly as `useApiClient.ts:9` intends; the bug is the predicate, not the seam. (5) a11y roles/attrs are producer-correct — measured `role="menuitem"`, `tabindex="-1"`, `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`; ArrowDown walks every row with `data-highlighted`; the trigger carries `aria-label="Palette menu"` and does not appear in REPORT.md's `namelessButtons` rows for /#/palettes. (6) Not a god module — 228 lines, one responsibility. (7) The degraded-state instinct (name the reason in-register on the disabled action rather than a toast) is canon-aligned even though its execution fails on three counts.

defects.defect: The component's existence is constitutionally abrogated: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 states the palette card body 'owns no expand, inline rename, action menu, transient result or hover-only swatch-action path' and that 'rename/lifecycle/export actions and durable operation state live in the selected inspector'. PaletteCardMenu.vue IS that forbidden action menu and hosts rename, lifecycle and export.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 (quoted verbatim); docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:77 §5 law 12 ('The Card/article root is a noninteractive container... Its one native named <button type="button" aria-pressed> child ... alone owns activation'); mounted at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:83-106; rename :73, lifecycle :15/:27/:48/:63/:133, export :107-130, admin :153-170. Card still carries role="article" + @click + cursor-pointer at PaletteCard.vue:19-26 instead of the mandated single <button aria-pressed>, requiring @click.stop at PaletteCard.vue:82 for the menu to survive.
defects.mechanism: Component predates the V constitution and was never reconciled with it; the seventeen actions were designed into a transient 192px overlay rather than the entity inspector.
defects.reproduction: Read docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 against demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue:1-173.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not patch: move all 17 actions into the selected inspector named by the constitution; delete PaletteCardMenu.vue; reduce the card to the single <button type="button" aria-pressed> seat of PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 12. This dissolves D-1, D-5, D-6, D-9, D-10, D-14, D-15, D-21 and D-25 rather than patching them.

defects.defect: `Delete` renders in EXACTLY the same ink as `Rename` in light, dark, mobile and forced-colors — `text-destructive focus:text-destructive` is inert. The menu's whole severity ladder (destructive / neutral / de-emphasised) collapses to one ink; `text-muted-foreground` on the Report row dies identically.
defects.evidence: probe-D-results.json (all 4 matrices): desktop-light Publish/Rename/Export/Delete all `color=rgb(28, 25, 23)`; desktop-dark all `rgb(233, 230, 226)`; forced-colors all `rgb(0, 0, 0)`; mobile-light all `rgb(28, 25, 23)`. In-page A/B (probe-D3-results.json): `colorWithProducerClass: "rgb(28, 25, 23)"` vs `colorWithoutProducerClass: "rgb(219, 36, 36)"` after removing the `dropdown-menu__item` class from the live node; `--destructive: light-dark(hsl(0 72% 50%), hsl(0 80% 60%))`. Source: PaletteCardMenu.vue:135, :164. Witness: evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png, evidence/forced-colors-menu-open.png.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui ships `.dropdown-menu__item{ ... color:inherit; ... }` in glass-ui.css. `.text-destructive` has identical (0,1,0) specificity and loses on source order. `focus:text-destructive` dies the same way (measured focused state color unchanged at rgb(28,25,23)).
defects.reproduction: Seed localStorage['color-palettes'] with a saved palette, open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, click [aria-label="Palette menu"], and read getComputedStyle(deleteItem).color vs getComputedStyle(renameItem).color — identical. Run docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D3-pcm.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Producer seam, not consumer patch: add `variant?: "default" | "destructive"` to glass-ui `DropdownMenuItem` (relay to the glass-ui BH inbox per the standing fond) so severity is expressible at the root; consumers stop writing colour utilities that `color:inherit` is guaranteed to eat. Severity must also carry a non-colour channel per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1.

defects.defect: The Export submenu cannot be opened by touch: `@click.prevent` on DropdownMenuSubTrigger defeats reka-ui's only touch open path, so all five export formats are unreachable on every touch device.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:108 `<DropdownMenuSubTrigger class="gap-2 cursor-pointer" @click.prevent>`; node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Menu/MenuSubTrigger.js:131-140 `onClick: async (event) => { if (props.disabled || event.defaultPrevented) return; ... menuContext.onOpenChange(true) }`. probe-D4-results.json touchTap (iPhone 14, hasTouch:true, real tap()): before/afterTap1/afterTap2 all `subContentPresent: false, ariaExpanded: "false"`, afterTap1 `dataState: "closed"`. Same-context control: `nonCancelableClick: { subContentPresent: true, ariaExpanded: "true" }`. probe-D5-results.json instrumented tail: both pointer modes end `click` with `defaultPrevented: true`; desktop has a preceding pointermove and opens, touch has none and stays closed. Witness: evidence/touch-tap-export-subtrigger.png.
defects.mechanism: Vue's `.prevent` modifier compiles to a no-op handler wrapped in withModifiers(['prevent']) that calls event.preventDefault() before reka's handler runs. Reka opens submenus from three paths — onPointermove (hover), onKeydown, onClick. A touch pointer produces no pointermove, so onClick is its only path, and it early-returns on defaultPrevented. Desktop hover opens the submenu first, entirely masking the defect from the desktop matrix.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D4-pcm.mjs (or probe-D5-pcm.mjs) against the live dev server at :9000. Open the card menu with tap(), then tap() the 'Export' row twice — aria-expanded stays "false".
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `@click.prevent` modifier at :108. It carries no handler, no comment, and buys nothing — the card's click is already stopped by the `@click.stop` wrapper at PaletteCard.vue:82. This is shipping breakage that should not wait for the D-1 transposition.

defects.defect: The `misconfigured` availability arm is unhandled: `apiOffline` tests only `=== "unavailable"` of a four-state enum, so the menu renders Publish enabled and undecorated while the app's own status lamp reads 'DEV MISCONFIGURED — RUN `NPM RUN DEV`'.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:217 `const apiOffline = computed(() => availability.value === "unavailable");` vs demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:40-45 `export type ApiAvailability = "unknown" | "available" | "unavailable" | "misconfigured";` and availability.ts:29-35 ('enter a DISTINCT, designed `misconfigured` state that fails LOUD (never the generic degraded affordance)'). evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png shows the DockStatusLamp rendering `● DEV MISCONFIGURED — RUN 'NPM RUN DEV'` in --destructive at top-right while probe-D-results.json records the adjacent Publish item as `disabled: false` with no annotation. Two consumers of one latch, one honest, one not.
defects.mechanism: A four-state enum was consumed by a boolean predicate; three of the four arms fall through to the fully-optimistic render, including the one arm the availability module explicitly designed to fail loud.
defects.reproduction: Run the dev server without VITE_API_URL on a loopback origin (the default `npm run dev:web-only` footgun described in availability.ts:22-35), open /#/palettes and the card menu. The lamp says misconfigured; the menu offers Publish enabled. Screenshot: evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the boolean with a four-arm match on the enum; `misconfigured` gets its own loud annotation, distinct from `offline` and from silence. Availability is a property of the action (disabled + named reason), not of the entity.

defects.defect: The Export seat is one-click fire-and-forget; PALETTE-CONTRACT Appendix W51 mandates a two-activation Prepare→Download seat with five durable operation states, none of which exist.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:113-128 — five identical rows `@select="() => $emit('action', 'exportJSON')"` etc., no prepare step, no state. docs/tranches/V/PALETTE-CONTRACT.md:325 ('Only after the verified bytes are resident in memory does the same action seat expose Download FILENAME; it is a fresh user activation, not an asynchronous continuation of Prepare'), :319 ('`state` is exactly `captured | ready | retryable-failure | terminal-failure | handoff-initiated`'), :174 ('never a partial download or console.warn-only result'). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-08 assigns 'Pending/failure/export/recovery truth only transient' → ADD-AFFORDANCE 'Persistent entity status/recovery' to W23. The menu closes on activation (PaletteCard.vue:317), leaving nowhere for operation state to live.
defects.mechanism: A five-state durable operation with an atomic capture transaction and storage-recovery arm was designed into a transient overlay that unmounts the instant the command is issued.
defects.reproduction: Read PALETTE-CONTRACT.md:319-325 against PaletteCardMenu.vue:107-130 and PaletteCard.vue:308-317.
defects.proposedCure: Export is not a menu row — it is a seat with two activations and five persistent states. It belongs in the inspector D-1 already sends everything else to.

defects.defect: One trailing slot carries two orthogonal facts, and availability destroys the visibility readout: when the backend goes down the annotation flips from `public`/`private` to `offline`, so the user loses the ability to read what state the palette is frozen in.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:56-59 `{{ apiOffline ? "offline" : isPublic ? "public" : "private" }}` — one span, mutually exclusive ternary. The adjacent row :35-39 uses the same pixel region to mean availability failure only. A palette that is `private` AND `offline` is a real state the design cannot express.
defects.mechanism: Entity state (visibility) and action availability are independent facts that were given one slot; availability wins the ternary.
defects.reproduction: Read PaletteCardMenu.vue:48-60; set availability to 'unavailable' and observe the visibility annotation replaced rather than supplemented.
defects.proposedCure: Separate the channels: availability is a property of the action (disabled + named reason on the action); visibility is persistent entity state that must remain readable regardless of connectivity.

defects.defect: glass-ui's `DropdownMenuShortcut` primitive is hand-rolled three times with three different recipes and consumed zero times repo-wide; the hand-roll diverges from the producer register on tracking (4x tighter), opacity, text-transform and rendered width.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:37, :57 (`ml-auto fira-code text-mono-caption opacity-55 tracking-wide` + inline small-caps) and :101 (`ml-auto text-caption text-muted-foreground`). Producer: glass-ui.css `.dropdown-menu__shortcut{font-size:var(--dropdown-text-secondary);letter-spacing:.1em;opacity:.6;margin-inline-start:auto}`. `grep -rn "DropdownMenuShortcut" demo/` returns only the re-export barrel line — zero consumers. Measured (probe-D6, same page/font): consumer letter-spacing 0.3596px vs producer 1.4384px; opacity 0.55 vs 0.6; rendered width of 'offline' 64.47px vs 50.09px.
defects.mechanism: `tracking-wide` (0.025em) is applied on top of `text-mono-caption`'s `--type-tracking-caps` (0.1em) and REDUCES tracking to a quarter of the caption register's own value — a class whose name says 'wider' makes it 4x tighter.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D6.mjs against the live dev server.
defects.proposedCure: Consume `DropdownMenuShortcut` (already exported by demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts). Owner edicts 4 and 5 both apply: the primitive exists, reuse it at the root rather than three per-instance re-derivations.

defects.defect: Three trailing annotations use the physical margin `ml-auto` instead of the producer's `margin-inline-start:auto`, so in RTL the annotation lands 17.5px short of the row's inline end and glued to the label.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:37, :57, :101 all `ml-auto`. Measured in a live dir="rtl" document with the exact markup (probe-D2-results.json `rtl`): consumer `{ marginLeft: "17.4688px", marginInlineStart: "0px", annX: 17.5, annRight: 81.9, lblX: 89.9, rowW: 178 }`; producer control `.dropdown-menu__shortcut` `{ marginInlineStart: "31.8438px", annX: 0 }` — flush at the inline end.
defects.mechanism: In an RTL flex row `margin-left:auto` places the free space on the physical left (= main-end in RTL), pushing the annotation toward the label rather than away from it; only the 8px flex gap then separates them, so the status reads as a suffix of the label.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D2-pcm.mjs — section `rtl` contains the A/B against the producer primitive.
defects.proposedCure: Use the producer primitive (D-7), which already writes `margin-inline-start:auto`. Never write a physical-direction margin in a component the app renders in RTL matrices (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2).

defects.defect: The Rename hand-off is broken on both activation paths: the menu closes (contradicting its own stated intent) and reka's closeAutoFocus returns focus to the trigger AFTER the rename input has mounted and self-focused, leaving the revealed field unfocused.
defects.evidence: Stated intent at PaletteCard.vue:290-292 ('keep the menu open visually until the input takes focus'). PaletteRenameInput.vue:53-56 does `onMounted(() => { inputRef.value?.focus(); inputRef.value?.select(); })`. Measured on the keyboard path (probe-D2-results.json enterOnItem) and the click path (probe-D3-results.json renameClick), both identical: `{ menuStillOpen: false, inputPresent: true, inputFocused: false, activeElement: "BUTTON/Palette menu" }`. reka-ui/dist/Menu/MenuItem.js:44-46 calls rootContext.onClose() regardless; PaletteCard.vue:281 also sets menuOpen=false inside startRenaming().
defects.mechanism: `@click` (not `@select`) was chosen, so the consumer cannot preventDefault reka's select→close. glass-ui's DropdownMenuContent exposes a cancellable `closeAutoFocus` emit precisely for this hand-off (DropdownMenuContent.vue.d.ts) and the component never listens to it. The comment at PaletteCard.vue:290-292 describes behaviour the chosen event cannot express.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D3-pcm.mjs — section renameClick. Or: open the menu, press ArrowDown to 'Rename', press Enter; the input appears and document.activeElement is the menu trigger.
defects.proposedCure: `@close-auto-focus.prevent` on the content when the pending command owns a focus target — or, per D-1, put rename in the inspector where no menu is closing over it.

defects.defect: Identity/action hierarchy is inverted: the palette name renders at 14.384px in --muted-foreground while every action beneath it renders at 16.4px in full-strength --foreground; the constitution mandates --type-subheading (20.352px) for palette identity. The name is also truncated to 56% of its length.
defects.evidence: probe-D2-results.json: `--type-subheading: "1.272rem"` = 20.352px (mandated by VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 type-jurisdiction table); measured label `{ font-size: "14.384px", font-family: Fraunces, font-weight: "600", color: "rgb(112, 89, 66)" }` = --muted-foreground; measured items `16.4px` at `rgb(28,25,23)`. Ratio 14.384/20.352 = 0.707. Truncation: `{ scrollW: 319, clientW: 178 }` = 56% shown. `max-w-[180px]` at :9 never binds (clientW 178 < 180) — a dead magic number. Witness: evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png shows 'Muted Terracotta an…' in the header while the card behind independently clips to 'Muted Terracot…'.
defects.mechanism: The producer's `.dropdown-menu__label{font-size:var(--dropdown-text-secondary);color:var(--muted-foreground);font-weight:600}` places the label in the secondary/muted role; the consumer's `font-display font-bold truncate max-w-[180px]` cannot lift it (font-bold is inert, see D-16) and the fixed w-48 content box leaves 178px.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D2-pcm.mjs — sections `tokens` and `menuVsSub.label`.
defects.proposedCure: Identity must not live in a 178px transient overlay at all (D-1). If a header survives the transposition it must render at --type-subheading in Fraunces at full ink, with a measure that does not clip the name it exists to state.

defects.defect: Four type-jurisdiction violations of the CLOSED VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 matrix; the sharpest renders all five export format names in italic because `text-caption` is the producer's italic caption voice and only its font-style survives.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 ('control or label, including dropdown options → text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'), matrix declared closed at §4. Measured: (a) :7 `text-small` on Content → items render Fira Code 16.4px (mono is a root decision at demo/styles/foundation.css:374 `--dropdown-menu-font: var(--font-mono)`); (b) :112 `text-caption` on SubContent → glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/semantic.css `@utility text-caption { ... font-style: italic; ... }`; probe-D2-results.json `subContent.fontStyle: "italic"`, `subItem.fontStyle: "italic"`, and subItem fontSize 16.4px identical to the parent — the size intent is overridden, only the italics inherit; (c) :9 `font-bold` → measured font-weight 600; (d) :155 `text-mono-caption uppercase tracking-wider` for the 'Admin' SECTION HEADING → mono, which §4 reserves for 'value, code, or provenance'. Witness: evidence/mobile-light-submenu-open.png shows JSON / CSS Custom Properties / Tailwind Config / SVG Swatch / PNG Swatch all in italic mono while the parent menu is upright.
defects.mechanism: `.dropdown-menu__item{font-size:var(--dropdown-text)}` overrides the SubContent's caption size but nothing overrides font-style, so a class chosen for size delivers only obliqueness. glass-ui already ships the correct utilities for this exact context — `.text-dropdown` and `.text-dropdown-secondary` — and they are unused.
defects.reproduction: Open the card menu on /#/palettes, hover 'Export', and read getComputedStyle on the sub-content and its items; or node probe-D2-pcm.mjs section menuVsSub.
defects.proposedCure: Consume `.text-dropdown` / `.text-dropdown-secondary` where a rung is genuinely needed and otherwise let the producer own the item type. Relay the mono-for-control-copy question (foundation.css:374 vs VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75) as a root-level ruling, not a per-component override.

defects.defect: Hover and keyboard focus are literally the same declaration — one background tint with no non-colour channel — so in a menu containing an irreversible Delete there is no visual answer to 'where will Enter land'.
defects.evidence: probe-D2-results.json `states`: rest `{ bg: "rgba(0,0,0,0)", outline: "none 3px", boxShadow: "none", textDecoration: "none" }`; focused `{ bg: "oklab(0.915626 0.00551148 0.0130686/0.52)", outline: "none 3px", boxShadow: "none", textDecoration: "none" }` — background-color is the only delta. The keyboard walk (probe-D2-results.json `keyboard`) shows the identical bg on every row with outline 3px but outline-style none. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'
defects.mechanism: reka's single `data-highlighted` attribute serves both pointer-hover and roving keyboard focus, and the producer expresses it with one background tint; the consumer adds no second channel. Compounded by D-2 (destructive ink already dead) and D-14 (Delete grouped with a disclosure).
defects.reproduction: Open the menu, ArrowDown through it, and diff getComputedStyle before/after — only backgroundColor changes. node probe-D2-pcm.mjs section `states`.
defects.proposedCure: Producer relay: focus needs an independent non-colour register (outline / inset ring) distinct from the hover tint, surviving forced-colors and reduced-transparency, per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1.

defects.defect: The availability latch guards 2 of 10 doomed remote actions; the other eight are offered and fail silently, which is worse than no latch because it teaches the user that an un-annotated row is safe.
defects.evidence: Gated: Publish (:27-40), visibility flip (:48-60). Ungated remote writes: Save-remote-arm (:15-22), Remix/fork (:63-70), Edit Tags (:83-90), Versions (:93-102), Delete-remote (:133-140), Report/flag (:143-150), Feature (:158-162), Delete-admin (:163-169). Source enumeration of PaletteCardMenu.vue.
defects.mechanism: The degraded-state affordance was added to the two actions the K-INV5 residual named and never generalised to the action set that shares the same failure mode.
defects.reproduction: Read PaletteCardMenu.vue:15-169 and cross-check each emitted action against PaletteCard.vue:293-313 for whether it reaches the backend.
defects.proposedCure: Availability gating belongs to the action-descriptor level (one predicate, applied uniformly), not to two hand-picked rows.

defects.defect: The irreversible destructive row is grouped with a disclosure sub-trigger, 44px below it, with no separator between them, no confirmation step, and (per D-2) identical ink.
defects.evidence: probe-D-results.json separators at y 653.1 and 750.1; items Publish 658.1, Rename 702.1, Export 755.1, Delete 799.1 — Export and Delete share a group with no divider. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 4: 'A divider is retained only when grouping would be ambiguous without it.' No confirmation anywhere in the menu: PaletteCardMenu.vue:136 → PaletteCard.vue:295 `delete: () => emit("delete", props.palette)`.
defects.mechanism: Dividers were placed by visual rhythm rather than by grouping ambiguity; the one boundary that matters (disclosure → destruction) is the one that is missing.
defects.reproduction: Open the menu on /#/palettes and read the separator/item y-coordinates, or see evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png.
defects.proposedCure: Destruction is not a menu row adjacent to a disclosure. In the inspector transposition (D-1) it becomes a guarded action with its own boundary and confirmation.

defects.defect: At 390px the Export submenu overlaps its own parent menu by 59.9px and clamps flush to viewport x=0, rendering overlapping double text through the translucent glass.
defects.evidence: probe-D-results.json: parent menu x 151.0–343.0 (w 192, fixed `w-48` at :7); sub-content x 0.0–210.9 (w 210.9, content-sized) → 59.9px overlap, left edge at exactly 0 with zero inset. Witness: evidence/mobile-light-submenu-open.png shows 'CSS Custom Properties' and 'Tailwind Config' rendered on top of the parent's palette name and 'Publish' row, both legible simultaneously. Note the two panels of one menu tree are also different widths (192 vs 210.9).
defects.mechanism: A fixed-width parent plus a content-width submenu plus default collision handling with no collisionPadding and no mobile disclosure alternative. REPORT.md reports `horizontalOverflow — 0` for /#/palettes because the menu was closed in every capture (see D-24).
defects.reproduction: node probe-D-pcm.mjs (mobile-light matrix) or open /#/palettes at 390x844, open the card menu, hover 'Export'.
defects.proposedCure: A nested flyout is the wrong form factor at 390px. Under the D-1 transposition Export becomes a seat, not a submenu; short of that, a mobile arm that discloses in place rather than flying out.

defects.defect: Fifteen declared styling tokens render nothing and a sixteenth renders the opposite of its name — more than half the file's declared visual intent is inert.
defects.evidence: Measured live: `cursor-pointer` x17 (grep -o count) → computed `cursor: default` on every item, producer sets it; `text-small` at :7 → `--dropdown-text: "calc(clamp( 0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem ) * 1)"` is the identical clamp to `--type-small: "clamp( 0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem )"`; `font-bold` at :9 → measured font-weight 600; `max-w-[180px]` at :9 → clientW 178 < 180, never binds; `text-destructive`/`focus:text-destructive` x4 → D-2; `text-muted-foreground` at :145 → same ink as neutral; `text-caption` at :112 → size overridden, only italics survive (D-11). Sources: probe-D-results.json, probe-D2-results.json tokens, probe-D3-results.json.
defects.mechanism: Uniform mechanism: single-class Tailwind utilities colliding with equal-specificity glass-ui component classes that load later in source order. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 8 ('Real rendered relation wins over token intent... token presence alone cannot close a row') is the governing rule and the file has never been measured against it.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D2-pcm.mjs and probe-D3-pcm.mjs; compare declared class lists at PaletteCardMenu.vue:7,9,17,29,50,64,75,84,95,108,112-126,135,145,158,164 against the computed values.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the inert tokens rather than raising their specificity; where a rung genuinely differs from the producer's, obtain it through a producer prop/variant (edicts 4 and 5), not a per-instance utility the cascade will eat.

defects.defect: The 'K-INV5 small-caps register' cited three times in the file's own comments does not render: `style="font-variant: small-caps"` is a measured no-op because `text-mono-caption` already applies `text-transform: uppercase`.
defects.evidence: probe-D6 A/B on the exact class bundle, same page, same font: withSmallCaps `{ textTransform: "uppercase", fontVariantCaps: "small-caps", renderedWidth: 64.47 }` vs withoutSmallCaps `{ textTransform: "uppercase", fontVariantCaps: "normal", renderedWidth: 64.47 }`, `identicalWidth: true`. Source of the uppercase: glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/utilities.css `@utility text-mono-caption { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--type-caption); letter-spacing: var(--type-tracking-caps); text-transform: uppercase; }`. Comments invoking the register: PaletteCardMenu.vue:24-26, :42-47; inline style at :39 and :59. `fira-code` at :37/:57 is also redundant — text-mono-caption already sets font-family: var(--font-mono).
defects.mechanism: font-variant: small-caps substitutes small capitals only for lowercase glyphs; text-transform: uppercase has already consumed them. Identical rendered width with and without the declaration proves it.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D6.mjs against the live dev server.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the duplicated inline styles (edict 5 — inline per-instance overrides) and the redundant `fira-code`; adopt `DropdownMenuShortcut` (D-7). If a small-caps register is genuinely wanted, it must be a producer utility that does not also uppercase.

defects.defect: Three shadow languages and two radii collide in one interaction: the card is a hard-offset pop-art caster at 16px radius, the menu it opens is soft frosted glass at 12px, and the project's own token declares a third recipe.
defects.evidence: probe-D3-results.json material: card `borderRadius: "16px"` (--radius-card 1rem), boxShadow 3-layer hard offset `-3px 3px 0`, `-5px 5px 0`, `-7px 7px 0`; menu `borderRadius: "12px"` (--radius-panel), boxShadow soft glass `0 8px 32px -4px`, `0 8px 24px 0` + 4 insets; declared token `--shadow-card: 8px 8px 0px 0px ...`. Item radius 8px against a concentric ideal of 12 − 6 = 6px. demo/styles/foundation.css:359-368 states the project law: 'so shadow-card consumers and explicit shadow-cartoon consumers render one cartoon language — no fourth ad-hoc shadow recipe.' Both surfaces are witnessed together in evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png.
defects.mechanism: The overlay band was never brought under the demo's cartoon material override; glass-ui's floating surface register ships unmodified and the two objects read as belonging to different design systems.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D3-pcm.mjs section `material`; or view evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png where the card's hard black caster sits beside the menu's blurred glass.
defects.proposedCure: Decide the overlay's material at the root (a `surface` choice on DropdownMenuContent, which the producer already exposes) rather than accepting a second language by default. The item-radius concentricity is producer-owned — relay, do not patch locally.

defects.defect: A stringly-typed command bus between two files in the same folder, with a silent unknown-key drop and one dead command that has zero producers.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:225 `action: [action: string]`; PaletteCard.vue:293-313 `const actions: Record<string, () => void>` with `if (!fn) return;` at :316. `grep -rn "copyAll" demo/` returns exactly one hit — PaletteCard.vue:294, the handler — and no emitter anywhere.
defects.mechanism: A union type was replaced by `string`, so the compiler cannot catch a typo in any of the 17 emitted literals, and the receiving lookup swallows the miss. Dead code accumulates unobserved inside it.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "copyAll" demo/ ; read PaletteCardMenu.vue:224-227 against PaletteCard.vue:290-319.
defects.proposedCure: One line: a union of the 17 literals on the emit. Delete `copyAll`. Edicts 2 (no legacy code) and 3 (KISS) both apply.

defects.defect: Two activation idioms in one menu — 11 `@click` rows and 5 `@select` rows — and the majority idiom is outside the producer's declared contract.
defects.evidence: `grep -o '@click=' PaletteCardMenu.vue | wc -l` = 11; `grep -o '@select=' ... | wc -l` = 5. glass-ui DropdownMenuItem.vue.d.ts declares `export interface DropdownMenuItemEmits { /** Cancel this event to keep the menu open. */ select: [event: Event]; }`. `@click` runs in parallel with reka's handleSelect and cannot cancel it — the direct cause of D-9's unachievable 'keep the menu open' intent.
defects.mechanism: `@click` lands as a fallthrough DOM listener alongside reka's own onClick; it has no access to the select-cancellation semantic the producer documents.
defects.proposedCure: One idiom: `@select` throughout, which is the producer's contract and the only one that can express 'keep the menu open'.

defects.defect: Two verbs mean the same thing and one word means two things: 'Publish' names both first-time remote creation and an existing palette's visibility flip (same Globe glyph), while a remote palette is offered both 'Save' and 'Remix' with no stated distinction.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:33 'Publish' emitting `publish` (saved arm) vs :55 'Publish' emitting `makePublic` (remote+owned arm), both with `<Globe class="h-4 w-4"/>` at :28 and :54. Remote arm renders Save (:15-22, emits `save`) and Remix (:63-70, emits `fork`). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-06 ('Three adjacent action species or duplicated selected fills' → REMOVE, 'One action/selection owner') is the governing row.
defects.mechanism: Label reuse across mutually-exclusive kind arms hides the fact that the two operations have different consequences (creating a remote resource vs mutating one).
defects.reproduction: Read PaletteCardMenu.vue:15-70 and enumerate the rows per paletteKind arm.
defects.proposedCure: One verb per operation. PR-06 assigns the family to W23.

defects.defect: The Versions row gates on `!palette.isLocal` while every sibling row gates on `paletteKind` — a second, redundant encoding of the same fact that will drift the moment getPaletteKind gains a case.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:94 `v-if="!palette.isLocal && (palette.versionCount ?? 0) > 1"` vs :16, :28, :49, :64, :74, :84, :134, :144, :153 which all test `paletteKind`. demo/palettes/utils.ts:22-31 derives `remote` from exactly `!palette.isLocal`.
defects.mechanism: Two predicates for one concept; equivalent today by coincidence of implementation, not by contract.

Normative assignment: demo/DESIGN.md:98 and demo/styles/utils.css:122 ("stamp — --shadow-cartoon-sm, the chip-scale elevation PaletteCard rides"). The unscoped rule lives in dist/styles/glass/glass-atom.css, one of two orphans in that directory that no stylesheet imports; a duplicate scoped to `.liquid-enter.is-cel >` lives in liquid-enter.css and IS loaded. defects.defect: The demo's map of the published `@mkbabb/value.js` surface is wrong in four of eight entries and the whole block is unnecessary. `package.json#exports` holds SEVEN keys and NO `"."` root; `src/subpaths/` matches it exactly. `tsconfig.demo.json#paths` declares eight value.js entries: three of them (`@mkbabb/value.js` → dist/index.d.ts, `/parsing`, `/units`) target files that exist in neither the checkout nor the published tarball, and two real exported subpaths (`/value`, `/css`) have no entry. Its header asserts "the bare '.' root + the 7 subpath barrels", "a CLOSED 8-key set", "the 8 public keys", and that glass-ui imports value.js by the bare specifier — all false.
defects.evidence: exports keys: ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize'] — has root ".": False. `node -e "import('@mkbabb/value.js')"` → BARE FAIL: ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED | No "exports" main defined in /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/package.json; control `import('@mkbabb/value.js/color')` → SUBPATH OK 23. ts.resolveModuleName with the demo program's parsed options (moduleResolution=Bundler, containing demo/color-session/ink.ts): bare UNRESOLVED, /parsing UNRESOLVED, /units UNRESOLVED, all seven exported keys → /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/*.d.ts. File existence: dist/index.d.ts MISSING, dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts MISSING, dist/subpaths/units.d.ts MISSING. glass-ui@7 specifiers, measured across its six value.js-importing chunks: only '@mkbabb/value.js/color', '/css', '/easing' — no bare import anywhere.
defects.mechanism: a hand-maintained mirror of a generated/derivable truth drifts from it; the authoritative map (package.json#exports) and its hand-copy disagree, and the hand-copy is the one an author reads
defects.reproduction: node -e "import('@mkbabb/value.js').then(m=>console.log('OK')).catch(e=>console.log(e.code))" → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. For the TS half: resolve '@mkbabb/value.js/parsing' with ts.resolveModuleName using tsconfig.demo.json's parsed options → UNRESOLVED, while the paths entry claims dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all eight `@mkbabb/value.js` entries from tsconfig.demo.json#paths. Node/TypeScript package SELF-REFERENCE already resolves every exported subpath to the checkout's own dist (measured: `/css` and `/value` resolve correctly with no paths entry at all, isExternalLibraryImport=false), so package.json#exports becomes the single source of truth for the type resolver exactly as it already is for the bundler (vite.config.ts:37-50 generates its alias set from the same map and therefore cannot drift). If a bare root is wanted, add `"."` to `exports` — never keep a paths entry granting a specifier the package refuses to serve. Correct or delete the three false header claims.

defects.defect: PaletteCard publishes 16 emits / 10 props (not the 18 emits pass-1 and pass-4 recorded), and the mean host wires 5.2 of 16. Two hosts consume the component for one event and inherit fifteen silently-dropped menu actions, because PaletteCardMenu renders from paletteKind/isOwned/isAdmin and never from what the host can service.
defects.evidence: Parsed defineEmits/defineProps: emits 16 ['click','delete','publish','save','vote','rename','editColor','addColor','feature','adminDelete','setVisibility','fork','versions','flag','editTags','export']; props 10. Wiring counted by kebab-cased listener presence — BrowsePane.vue 15/16 (missing publish), PalettesPane.vue 7/16, AdminUsersPanel.vue 3/16, ExtractWorkbench.vue 4/16, MixSourceSelector.vue 1/16, GenerateControls.vue 1/16. Silent drop: PaletteCard.vue:315-316 `const fn = actions[action]; if (!fn) return;` over an untyped Record<string, () => void>.
defects.mechanism: a stringly-typed action bus with an optional-listener surface — the compiler cannot see an unhandled member, so 67% of the published surface is a no-op at the average call site
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/mix, expose a palette card via MixSourceSelector, open its ⋯ menu and choose Delete → nothing happens, no diagnostic. MixSourceSelector.vue wires only @click of the 16 emits.
defects.proposedCure: Collapse the surface to two emits: `activate` and `action: PaletteAction`, where PaletteAction is a discriminated union rather than `string`. A host that does not handle a member becomes a compile error instead of a silent drop, which is the structural cure for every "host wires 3 of 16" row at once.

defects.defect: One shared `expandedId` ref serves two incompatible identity key spaces. usePaletteActions.ts:24 declares a single `ref<string|null>`, instantiated once (usePalettePorts.ts:92) and handed to all three ports; PalettesPane compares it against `palette.id`, BrowsePane and AdminUsersPanel against `palette.slug`. The composable's own writers use the id axis. The root cause is PaletteCard's surface: it takes `expanded?: boolean` and emits a payload-free `click`, so each host must invent a key.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePaletteActions.ts:24 `const expandedId = ref<string | null>(null)`; :28 toggleExpand(id: string); :76 `expandedId.value = palette.id`; :81 `expandedId.value = id`. Shared instance: usePalettePorts.ts:92 `const actions = usePaletteActions({` exposed at :144, :177, :226. Key spaces: PalettesPane.vue:87 `=== palette.id` / toggleExpand(palette.id); BrowsePane.vue:97 `=== palette.slug` / toggleExpand(palette.slug); AdminUsersPanel.vue:144 `=== palette.slug`. Axes disjoint by construction: usePaletteStore.ts:85 `id: crypto.randomUUID()`, utils.ts:14 `createSlug` = `${slugify(name)}-${uuid.slice(0,8)}`.
defects.mechanism: identity ownership pushed out of the component that holds the entity — one untyped string cell carrying two key spaces the type system cannot distinguish
defects.reproduction: NONE for the cross-talk half — this is a hypothesis; a UUID colliding with a slug is not reachable in practice. The structural half is not a hypothesis and is directly readable at the five cited lines: an expansion opened in Palettes is un-expandable in Browse because the surviving value can never match the other pane's key.
defects.proposedCure: Give the card ownership of row identity — `@activate: [palette: Palette]` — or, better, move expansion to the list owner (a PaletteGrid) keyed by a branded `PaletteRowKey` minted in demo/palettes/model/. Either way the untyped string cell and the two key spaces die together.

result.strongestDefect: L-43 — the rung-2 WELL "one shared shell" has three homes and has already drifted, and the card paints `--shadow-cartoon-md` (contact layer 7px) where its own normative material ladder (demo/DESIGN.md:98) and demo/styles/utils.css:122 both assign `--shadow-cartoon-sm` (4px). Measured live: cardShadowEqualsMd true, cardShadowEqualsSm false. This is the demo-side root cause of the owner's MT-F036 shadow mark, and it RE-DISPOSITIONS pass 4's ruling: pass 4 matched the slab to a producer token and routed the whole shadow half to glass-ui, but the majority of the visible defect is curable today in demo/styles/utils.css by writing the solid `.well-card` sibling of the existing `.dashed-well` — no producer dependency. Only the cartoon-rung parameterisation (`cartoon?: boolean` cannot express sm/md/lg) remains a BJ ask.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded negatives (hypotheses I attempted to convict and could not, §3 of the report): (1) "the hand-rolled root forfeits the producer's prefers-contrast compensation" — REFUTED by measurement; under WebKit emulateMedia({contrast:"more"}) the card's border alpha rises 0.12→0.55 and shadow alphas 0.32/0.26/0.18→0.42/0.34/0.24 even though isGlassAtom=false, because the compensation is token-level not .glass-atom-scoped. (2) "onPopoverAdd/Edit/Copy leave the 250ms leave-timer armed by poking openPopoverIndex instead of calling close()" — duplication only, no defect: both re-entry points (useHoverPopover.ts:26 onHover, :51 onSwatchClick) call cancelLeave() first. (3) ":style=\"press.pressStyle.value\"" double-unwraps — it does not; `press` is a SETUP_MAYBE_REF binding so .value is required. (4) "the demo typechecks against the npm-registry value.js while bundling the local dist" — REFUTED; ts.resolveModuleName returns the checkout's own dist for every resolvable specifier via package self-reference. (5) verbatimModuleSyntax clean across all six SFCs and four composables; (6) no deep src/ reach in the cone; (7) the card/ sub-barrel reach at MixSourceSelector.vue:8 is legal; (8) inv-K-1 (src/ may never import glass-ui) is live and correct — only the demo half of the lint config is dead.

defects.defect: The colours are neither controls nor content: `tag="button"` is silently ignored by glass-ui 7, the swatch ships aria-hidden + pointer-events:none, and an expanded card has exactly ONE tabbable element.
defects.evidence: probe-D5e output: `<span aria-hidden="true" class="w-9 h-9 … watercolor-swatch" style="…pointer-events:none…">`; probe-D5f-results.json → swatchTag "SPAN", swatchAriaHidden "true", swatchPointerEvents "none", tabOrder ["BUTTON:Palette menu"]; probe-D5d-results.json → axButtons [{name:"Palette menu"}]; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js offset 2548 `inheritAttrs: !1`; source SwatchHoverMenu.vue:29-35, PaletteColorStrip.vue:4
defects.mechanism: Three stacked: (1) the consumer's `tag="button"` prop is a no-op in glass-ui 7.0.0, which renders a `<span>` — a glass-6 API dropped in the glass-7 adoption with no compile-time or runtime signal (same class as the dead .cartoon-cast and --card-press-t); (2) `inheritAttrs:false` swallows the consumer's aria-label and the producer stamps aria-hidden; (3) inline pointer-events:none kills the swatch's own @click, so onSwatchClick and the touch-toggle path are dead code. The compact strip is aria-hidden by the consumer's own choice, so no colour is reachable in any state.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/probe-D5f.mjs; or /#/palettes → expand a card → Tab repeatedly (focus enters/leaves via the … menu only)
defects.proposedCure: Stop asking the producer's FACE to be a SEAT. Per constitution §5 the compact strip becomes noninteractive data carrying a real accessible description of the palette's colours; per-swatch add/edit/copy moves to the selected inspector where each colour is a named `<button>` wrapping a WatercolorDot face (the shape §7 Gradient already specifies verbatim). BJ ask: honour `tag`/forward ARIA, or remove `tag` from the typed surface.

defects.defect: MT-F036(a) root mechanism located: the hard-edged shadow slab is a PAINT-CONTAINMENT CLIP in PaletteCardGrid, not a shadow token in PaletteCard. Every card loses its left facet; the last card also loses its bottom facet.
defects.evidence: probe-D5b-results.json → clip: gridContain "content", gridPaddingLeft "0px", gridBox.x 754 == firstCardBox.x 754, gridBox.bottom 842.1 == lastCardBottom 842.1, shadowOffsets [-3/3, -5/5, -7/7 blur 0], leftOverflowPx -7, bottomOverflowPx -7; A/B witnesses evidence/p3-corner-clip-ON.png vs p3-corner-clip-OFF.png (same 34×34 CSS-px region, device-scale 6, only difference `contain:none`); source demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52
defects.mechanism: `contain: content` = `layout paint style`; paint containment clips descendants to the padding box. The grid has zero padding and the card is exactly grid-width, so the -7px left facet begins 7px outside the clip and the last card's +7px bottom facet ends 7px outside it. A component drew a decoration its own container is contractually forbidden from painting, and no gate noticed.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/probe-D5b.mjs, then compare evidence/p3-corner-clip-ON.png with p3-corner-clip-OFF.png
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT cure by deleting the containment (that inverts the priority: performance vs decoration). Land the canon-frozen tuple `{size:sm, material:content, tier:quiet, surface:opaque, shadow:false, grain:false, specular:off}` (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1; §7 'matte specimen slips … not cartoon casters'; PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 terminal verb REMOVE). defects.defect: ActionFeedback is a split-brain state machine: the parent owns the visibility state, the child owns the dismissal timer, and they synchronise through an event — which is why a second verdict inherits the first's deadline.

result.strongestDefect: C4-1 — under prefers-reduced-motion, PaletteCard's expand/collapse transition never completes, because useHeightTransition (useHeightTransition.ts:30-39,59-71) gates Vue's `done()` on a `transitionend` with propertyName==="height" while the app's own accessibility policy (glass-ui a11y-overrides.css, imported at demo/styles/foundation.css:56) rewrites transition-property to an allow-list that excludes height. Measured: only opacity transition events fire; the panel's inline height/opacity/transition are never cleared; the swatch subtree is never unmounted on collapse (panelPresent true vs false with motion); expanding and collapsing six cards retains 6 zero-height panels, 144 orphan swatch nodes and +1021 DOM nodes (607→1628) versus an exact 608→608 baseline with motion enabled. No suite in the repository runs under reduced motion, so no gate can see it. The cure is a transposition, not a patch: the card already uses the CSS-declared, PRM-safe `vj-morph` height morph twelve lines above for the rename row — the swatch panel is a hand-rolled fourth transition family in JavaScript, which the repo's own animation law (demo/styles/animations.css:60-80) declares a defect.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this records the hypotheses measurement KILLED, so pass 5 does not re-spend the probes. (1) Menu items wired with @click are NOT keyboard-dead — I expected the thirteen @click items (PaletteCardMenu.vue:18,31,52,66,76,86,96,136,146,158,165) to be keyboard-inert versus the five @select export items: measured, opening the menu with Enter, arrowing to Rename and pressing Enter gives {"focusedBefore":"Rename","renameInputAfterEnter":1}, identical to the mouse control {"renameInputAfterClick":1} — reka-ui synthesises the click. (2) The non-PRM expand/collapse is sound: with motion enabled the panel clears its inline style, unmounts on collapse, and a six-card expand/collapse walk returns the document to its exact baseline (totalDomNodes 608→608, swatchPanels 0) — pass 3's negative reconfirmed by a second method; the corruption is PRM-only. (3) verbatimModuleSyntax PASSES across all six components and three composables (PaletteCard.vue:168-169 is the only mixed-form import and uses the inline `type` specifier correctly). (4) Standing-hazard sweep is clean: no defineModel (stale-read hazard N/A), no oklch→HSV/stableHue path, no ValueUnit construction, no reka slider pointer-capture, no WebGL, no requestAnimationFrame in the nine files; useLiquidPress's spring registers onScopeDispose and respects PRM. (5) One claim is labelled HYPOTHESIS, not a finding: the per-render object spread at PaletteCard.vue:147 should fan renders out to all N swatch children on every hover — unmeasurable on this build (app.config.performance via the __vue_app__ handle produced zero measure entries, probe-C4c-pass4-results.json C5_hoverFanout.totalMeasures:0). (6) One apparatus correction: the store's real shape is {version:1,palettes:[…]} with PaletteColor.position required, and a bare array is silently discarded by usePaletteStore.ts:24-27 — probes in this folder seeded with a bare array (including probe-D5.mjs and my own first run) measured a page with zero cards.

defects.defect: `Button variant="…"` is a second dead producer contract. Glass 7 replaced Button's `variant` axis with orthogonal `emphasis` + `tone`; the demo still writes `variant` at 51 sites across 22 files (outline 28, ghost 19, destructive 1, default 1, `primary-audacious` 2 — the last belongs to no vocabulary the producer has ever shipped) against only 4 live `emphasis`/`tone` bindings. The prop falls through to the DOM as a literal invalid attribute and every authored plate collapses to the component default.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts declares exactly `emphasis?: ButtonEmphasis("primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text") · tone?: Tone · size · iconOnly · loading · type · disabled · class` — no `variant`. Runtime: `node -e "s=fs.readFileSync('node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button.js','utf8'); console.log(s.match(/variant:\{[^}]*\}/g))"` → NONE. Census (python parse of every <Button> tag in demo/**/*.vue): Button variant 51 across 22 files; Button emphasis 2; Button tone 2. Live probe (playwright, http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, 1440×900): {"domVariantAttrCount":3,"domVariantAttrTags":["BUTTON[variant=outline]","BUTTON[variant=ghost]","BUTTON[variant=outline]"],"buttonsWithVariantAttr":[{"label":"Login","attrVariant":"outline","dataEmphasis":"secondary","dataTone":"neutral"},{"label":"@mbabb","attrVariant":"ghost","dataEmphasis":"secondary","dataTone":"neutral"},{"label":"(nameless)","attrVariant":"outline","dataEmphasis":"secondary","dataTone":"neutral"}],"dataEmphasisNodes":3}. Sites: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:134,151,159. Producer documents the migration in Badge.vue.d.ts: "Replaces the former variant=\"destructive|success|warning|info\" (a tone is not a style)."
defects.mechanism: Structural-typing blindness at the design-system seam (same mechanism as prior L-2, now proven a law rather than one instance): Vue's fallthrough-attr rule makes an unknown prop legal TypeScript, so vue-tsc is green over all 51. The proximate structural cause is demo/ui/'s 19-module pure-alias layer (prior L-4): because every consumer imports `Button` from `../../../ui/button`, the Glass 6→7 upgrade changed NO import specifier anywhere in the demo. The alias layer is a signal absorber — a producer can rename an entire prop axis without any consumer's import changing one character.
defects.reproduction: 1) dev server at http://localhost:9000; 2) node scratchpad probe: chromium → /#/palettes → `document.querySelectorAll('button[variant]')` returns 3 nodes each carrying a literal `variant` attribute AND `data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral"`; `outline` and `ghost` render identically. Static: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts` (no `variant`), `grep -c 'variant=' ` census above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely (19 zero-logic barrels) so the specifier is `@mkbabb/glass-ui/button` at every call site, and codemod the axis IN THE SAME COMMIT: variant="outline"|"ghost" → emphasis="secondary"|"quiet"; variant="destructive" → tone="destructive"; variant="default" → omit; `primary-audacious` → emphasis="primary" plus a named plate shipped in glass-ui (edict 4), never a string the producer ignores. Then make the seam nominal (prior L-2's cure) — a `satisfies ButtonProps` object or excess-property-checked spread — so site 51 fails the build instead of the eye.
