result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this records the nine axes I attacked and could NOT break, with the evidence that proves each negative — so no downstream seat re-litigates them. (1) RENDERED text contrast is sound: pixel-measured at 4x DPR via screenshot->canvas readback, both schemes — section label 5.67/5.05, option text 13.69/7.85, Search pill 5.78/7.42, Clear-all 10.85/8.75, placeholder 5.60/6.02, field value 14.91/9.37. Every ink role clears AA at its size. (2) REDUCED MOTION is honoured — this OVERTURNS pass 1's D-16: under `reducedMotion:reduce` a 77-rule blanket rewrites the surface; the popover's `scale` and `translate` are REMOVED leaving `opacity 0.15s allow-discrete`, `.filter-option` -> 0.1s, `animation: 0.00001s`. No geometry animates. (3) The component's own motion IS tokenized: `var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard)` at :246, and bare Tailwind `transition-*` inherits house tokens via foundation.css `@theme` `--default-transition-duration/-timing-function`; nothing layout-forcing is animated; edict 6 met. (4) Radio options DO have accessible names via the wrapping <label> — the computed AT tree reads `radio "Newest"`, `"Most Popular"`, `"Most Forked"`, `"All"`, `"Featured"`; the defect is duplication and unnamed GROUPS, not nameless items. (5) MY OWN CLAIM WITHDRAWN: a WebKit tab walk suggested focus escapes the open popover after 3 stops; Chromium — authoritative per the repo's own rule at audit/visual/states.mjs:6-9 (macOS ships Full Keyboard Access OFF) — shows `stillOpenAfter8Tabs: true` and a cycling walk radio->swatch->input->Search->radio->radio->swatch->input. All species reachable. (6) `Escape` restores focus to the exact opener in WebKit and Chromium, both schemes (`focusIsTrigger: true`, `aria-expanded -> "false"`). (7) NO hit-target overlap — my own hypothesis falsified: the 44x44 radio boxes overflow their 30.94px rows but do not collide (`markerOverlap: -12.93px` desktop / `-9.59px` mobile) and a 1px-step elementFromPoint sweep returned `mismatchCount: 0` in every matrix; 44x44 around an 18x18 mark is exactly PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 7. (8) `.focus-ring` and `.scrollbar-thin` are NOT dead classes — a walk over every loaded stylesheet rule found 2 and 6 matching selectors respectively. (9) No horizontal overflow in any of 7 matrices (`docHorizontalOverflow: 0`) and no component-attributable console noise (the only error is the dev server's own VITE_API_URL misconfiguration warning).

defects.defect: The entire Tags filter section is inert: it calls a retired shadcn/radix-era Checkbox API against glass-ui 7, so ticking a tag paints checked and changes nothing.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts declares `modelValue?: CheckedState|null` and emits ONLY `update:modelValue`. demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55 passes `:checked` and `@update:checked`. Neither exists. `toggleTag` (:197) is never called and the `update:selectedTags` emit declared at :156 has no live caller.
defects.mechanism: Pre-glass-7 component API called against a glass-ui 7 contract. Vue fallthrough fails silently: the undeclared prop lands as a raw DOM attribute and the undeclared emit never fires; with `modelValue` absent the producer runs uncontrolled, so the box paints checked while the product holds no such state.
defects.reproduction: Static: read Checkbox.vue.d.ts against SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Live: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P3-3-truth.mjs (the section is absent in this environment, so the static proof is the load-bearing one).
defects.proposedCure: Transpose onto glass-ui `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` with `v-model` on one owned selectedTags model; the local toggleTag array-splice helper disappears with it. No shim, no dual path.

defects.defect: The menu has no scroll container anywhere in its chain, and at mobile and 200% zoom it overflows the TOP of the viewport, making the Sort section unreachable.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-2-states.json, tallest reachable state, 7 matrices: desktop 1440x900 dialog {y:381,h:521.06} bottomOverflow +2.06; mobile 390x664 {y:-154,h:530.41} topOverflow 154px (29%); zoom-200 720x450 {y:-227.5,h:501.64} topOverflow 227.5px (45.4%). `overflowY: "visible"` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` in all 7. The only `overflow-y:auto` in the component is the tag list at :49 (`max-h-28`).
defects.mechanism: An overlay whose height is data- and state-dependent was authored with no containment strategy; containment was applied to the one region that needed it least. Reka flips the menu upward when it will not fit below, and nothing constrains the flip or scrolls the content.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P3-2-states.mjs; frames shots-p3/P3-tall-mobile-open.png and shots-p3/P3-tall-zoom200-open.png. Manually: /#/browse on an iPhone-sized viewport, open the ⋮ menu — the top visible row is 'Most Forked'.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose onto `DropdownMenuContent`, which inherits the producer's collision/max-height/scroll behaviour, plus an explicit `max-h-[min(70svh,32rem)] overflow-y-auto`; delete the local `max-h-28` scroller. Separately split Sort out of the filter drawer — activeFilterCount (:189-195) already excludes it.

defects.defect: The active-filter count badge is clipped to an illegible olive crescent — 49.3% of its area painted away, digit entirely absent — and the count never reaches the accessible name either.
defects.evidence: Trigger measures 32.48 x 40.60 despite `icon-only` (documented in Button.vue.d.ts as 'Square geometry for an accessibly named icon command') because `class="relative h-8 w-8"` (:5) won on width and lost to `data-size=md` on height. `contain: paint` on the trigger in 7/7 matrices; badge overhang 4.1px top and 4.1px right (`-right-1 -top-1`, :9). Hit test 3 cardinal points, 7/7 matrices: centre true, top false, right false. Pixel census at DPR 4: surviving gold bbox 46x45 device px = 11.5 x 11.25 CSS px of a nominal 16.2 x 16.2 chip = 49.3% lost. AT tree of the trigger is exactly `- button "Filters" [expanded]: - img` — `aria-label` overrides the inner textContent "1".
defects.mechanism: A hand-positioned overhanging badge inside a producer root that declares paint containment; `contain: paint` clips to the padding box and the capsule radius bevels the remainder. The non-square icon-only geometry is what puts the overhang inside the bevel.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-4-pixels.mjs; see shots-p3/P3-px-light-badge.png and P3-px-dark-badge.png. Manually: /#/browse, open ⋮, select the Featured tier, press Escape and look at the trigger.
defects.proposedCure: Use the producer `Badge` atom as a sibling of the trigger, outside the contain:paint root, and put the count in the name (`aria-label="Filters, 2 active"`). Stop overriding `h-8 w-8` so `iconOnly` can keep its square. Never hand-position an overhang inside a producer root.

defects.defect: The field labelled 'Search by CSS color' with placeholder '#hex, hsl(...)' accepts exactly one syntax and silently searches a different colour for everything else, with no error state anywhere — and even a valid hex leaves the swatch wrong.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:218 `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;`. Six inputs driven live (evidence-p3/P3-3-truth.json -> substitution): `hsl(200 50% 50%)`, `rebeccapurple`, `oklch(0.7 0.15 30)`, `#abc`, `not-a-color` and `#FF0000` all left the swatch label at 'current color #4488cc', badge '1', zero `[role=alert]`, `aria-invalid: null`. `parseColorIn` — the library's own parser, which handles all six — is imported at :145 and used at :206.
defects.mechanism: A regex gate placed in front of the product's own competence, failing CLOSED to a silent substitution instead of OPEN to the parser. With no error state and no representation of the applied colour, the substitution is undetectable from the UI.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-3-truth.mjs. Manually: /#/browse, open ⋮, type `hsl(200 50% 50%)` in Find-by-Color, click Search — the badge increments and the wall filters, on #4488cc.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the regex gate at :218; pass the trimmed text to `parseColorIn` in a try/catch and render the two real states — parsed: the swatch and a removable applied-filter chip both take that colour; unparsed: a named error on the field with `aria-invalid`. This also makes the currently-unreachable `searching` register meaningful.

defects.defect: The menu is painted on TWO different grounds: 29.4% of its height hangs off the bottom of the card it was drawn over, so its own background steps by ΔRGB 71.6 partway down — with the seam falling across FIND BY COLOR, the one section whose job is to show a colour truthfully.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-5-rails.json: Browse card `bottom 747.84`; popover `y 380 -> bottom 901.06`; 153.22px (29.4%) hangs below the card. Popover material `background-color: oklab(0.936408 0.005529 0.013284 / 0.808)`, `backdrop-filter: blur(11px) saturate(1.6)`. Pixel readback of the menu's own body at 4x: top band rgb(241,224,220), mid rgb(241,223,220), bottom rgb(199,183,179) — ΔRGB(top,bottom)=71.6, luminance ratio 1.47:1; ΔRGB(top,mid)=1.0, so it is a STEP, not a gradient.
defects.mechanism: A translucent chrome material (glass-floating) was used as the page for a seven-control form, and the form is taller than the plate it was anchored over. The effective ground therefore changes where the plate ends — a defect no alpha value can fix. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 also gives the specimen tier an 'opaque/quiet neutral stage'; the colour swatch has none.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-5-rails.mjs; the seam is directly visible in shots-p3/P3-px-light-popover.png as a pink band behind FIND BY COLOR / Clear all filters against the cream behind SORT.
defects.proposedCure: Make the menu fit (P3-B2's cure) so it stops overhanging its plate; and give the colour specimen an opaque neutral well of its own — a colour cannot be read on a saturate(1.6) backdrop over a live chromatic aurora.

defects.defect: Seven distinct left rails share one 206px column — the section heading is 8px left of the marker column it heads and 56px left of the text it heads.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-5-rails.json, measured by range geometry to 0.01px: 449.75 (.filter-section box AND both ends of every divider) / 456.75 (radio 44x44 hit box, breaking 5px OUT of its own section) / 461.75 (.section-label ink, swatch, Clear button box) / 469.75 (radio visible ink) / 485.20 (Clear-all text ink) / 495.75 (colour input, and the text of 'All') / 517.75 (the text of Newest/Most Popular/Most Forked/Featured). Spread 68.0px = 33% of the content box. Option text begins 85.0px (35.4%) into a 240px menu; residual label measure 126.0px.
defects.mechanism: Two nested padding systems (producer 16px, which the inert `p-0` failed to remove, plus local `.filter-section` 12px at :238) and a per-row `padding: 0.25rem 0.5rem` at :241 that insets the option ink but not its hover chip. Nothing in the file establishes a shared rail because the producer menu that would have owned one was not used.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-5-rails.mjs; visible in shots-p3/P3-px-light-popover.png.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose onto DropdownMenuLabel + DropdownMenuRadioItem: the producer owns one marker lane and one text rail for label and items alike, and the local scoped CSS (`.filter-section`, `.filter-option`) is deleted entirely.

defects.defect: Proximity is inverted: sibling options sit 4.33x further from each other than from their own section heading, so five options read as five separate things.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-5-rails.json: row height 30.94px; gap between sibling options 26.00px; gap from section label to its first option 6.00px; ratio 4.33. Source measured: `getComputedStyle('[role=radiogroup]').gap === "26px"`, `className === "radio-group"` — glass-ui's FORM radio default, never overridden.
defects.mechanism: Category error: a form-field stack gap sized for labelled settings rows was imported into a 240px MENU. The producer's menu rhythm lives on DropdownMenuRadioItem, which the sibling UserSortMenu.vue:20-33 uses. This is also the direct cause of a large share of P3-B2's overflow.
defects.reproduction: Playwright evaluate on /#/browse with the popover open: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[role=radiogroup]')).gap -> '26px'; then read the .filter-option rects. Frame: shots-p3/P3-px-light-popover.png.
defects.proposedCure: Use DropdownMenuRadioItem/DropdownMenuCheckboxItem for both lists so the rhythm comes from the producer and neither list carries a local gap.

defects.defect: 'All' and 'Featured' — two options of the same radio group — do not share a left edge; the labels rag by exactly 22px.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-5-rails.json optionTextInk: 'All' 495.75, 'Featured' 517.75. 'All' (SearchFilterBar.vue:34-37) has no icon; 'Featured' (:38-42) carries <Award class="h-3.5 w-3.5">. The row is a bare flex with `gap: 0.5rem`, so omitting the glyph collapses its 14px lane plus the 8px gap.
defects.mechanism: A conditionally-present icon in an unreserved lane. Nothing holds the column when the optional element is absent.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-5-rails.mjs; visibly stair-stepped in shots-p3/P3-px-light-popover.png.
defects.proposedCure: DropdownMenuRadioItem owns the icon/marker lane, so an item without a glyph cannot rag. If any local layout survives, reserve the lane explicitly rather than letting flex collapse it.

defects.defect: Three horizontal dividers render (four when the Tags section is present) inside a popover on a route whose binding boundary inventory is `none` — and their rendered contrast is 1.57:1 light / 1.40:1 dark, so they are simultaneously forbidden and invisible.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:17 `class="flex flex-col divide-y divide-border"`. evidence-p3/P3-2-states.json: three children carry `border-bottom-width: 1px`, `paintedDividers: 3` in all 7 matrices (Tailwind v4 writes border-BOTTOM on :not(:last-child) — a border-top-only read misses them). docs/tranches/V/OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:69-90 binding table: `| Browse | n/a | n/a | none | ... |`, and line 90 'Any additional line ... is a defect.' Pixel contrast at 4x (evidence-p3/P3-4-pixels.json): light ink rgb(198,180,159) on ground rgb(241,223,220) = 1.57:1; dark ink rgb(101,87,73) on ground rgb(79,65,59) = 1.40:1. Geometry 449.75 -> 655.75: reaching neither the popover edge nor the content rail.
defects.mechanism: A boundary drawn where interval and material were meant to express the grouping — and drawn so faintly it cannot express it either. The grouping job is actually being (badly) done by the 26px gap of P3-M3.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-2-states.mjs (read `dividers`/`paintedDividers`) and node .../probe-P3-4-pixels.mjs (read `divider.contrast`); visible in shots-p3/P3-px-light-popover.png.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `divide-y divide-border`. Fix the rhythm (P3-M3) so interval carries the grouping; if the DropdownMenu transposition is taken, boundaries become an explicit DropdownMenuSeparator decision and the binding answer for Browse is zero.

defects.defect: The colour swatch casts a cartoon shadow down-and-LEFT while every card in the app casts down-and-RIGHT — two light sources in one frame — and it is the only shadowed object inside a glass popover.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-2-states.json -> light: live Browse Card `box-shadow: color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.8) 8px 8px 0px 0px`; `--shadow-cartoon`/`--shadow-card` = `8px 8px 0 0`. The swatch (`shadow-cartoon-sm`, :76) resolves to `-2px 2px`, `-3px 3px`, `-4px 4px`. Both are visible in one screenshot (shots-p3/P3-tall-mobile-open.png). In dark the stamp is a light tint at 26-46% alpha on a dark ground and is invisible (shots-p3/P3-desktop-dark-open.png).
defects.mechanism: A paper-grammar caster token stamped on a control seated on floating glass. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 gives the instrument-veil tier 'no drop shadow'; §3 law 8 forbids supporting fixtures competing through equal shadow. The token family itself is directionally inconsistent (`--shadow-cartoon` right-down vs `--shadow-cartoon-sm` left-down) — a producer row this consumer inherited by choosing the -sm token.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-2-states.mjs, read `light.swatchShadow` vs `light.cardShadow`; the crescent lower-LEFT of the blue circle and the slab lower-RIGHT of the Browse card are both in shots-p3/P3-tall-mobile-open.png.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the cartoon caster from the swatch — no shadow on a control seated on glass. Relay the `--shadow-cartoon` vs `--shadow-cartoon-sm` direction fork to the glass-ui BH inbox as a producer row.

defects.defect: Three producer parts are hand-rolled here, one of them by transcribing the producer's own class string, in a directory where a 58-line sibling already does the same job with the producer family.
defects.evidence: (a) Popover+RadioGroup+Checkbox as a menu = 125 template lines, vs glass-ui's DropdownMenu/RadioGroup/RadioItem/CheckboxItem/Label/Separator, all 14 already re-exported in demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts. (b) The count chip at :7-12 uses `bg-primary text-primary-foreground rounded-full text-micro font-bold`; glass-ui's Badge declares `VARIANT.default = "bg-primary text-primary-foreground"` in dist/components/badge/index.d.ts — the identical string. (c) The inline Search commit + Loader2 spinner + four `disabled:` classes at :97-104 re-implement Button's declared `loading?: boolean` ('Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles') and `disabled`. Counter-example: UserSortMenu.vue, same folder, 58 lines, DropdownMenu family.
defects.mechanism: A hand-rolled clone of a producer family, hosting five jobs behind one anonymous ⋮ entry point. Owner edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system) and edict 5 (style at the root, never per-instance) fail at the same coordinate; every geometry, rhythm and semantics defect in this ledger is downstream of it.
defects.reproduction: Read demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue against UserSortMenu.vue in the same directory, and against node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/badge/index.d.ts and .../button/Button.vue.d.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose onto DropdownMenu + DropdownMenuLabel + DropdownMenuRadioGroup/RadioItem + DropdownMenuCheckboxItem exactly as UserSortMenu.vue does; use producer Badge and Button :loading; the file lands near 90-110 lines with zero scoped CSS.

defects.defect: The accessibility tree announces every option TWICE, exposes four nameless images, and gives both radio groups no name at all — the visual grouping exists only in pixels.
defects.evidence: Computed AT tree (probe-P3-7-aria.mjs, WebKit): `- dialog "Filters": - text: Sort - radiogroup: - radio "Newest" [checked] - img - text: Newest - radio "Most Popular" - img - text: Most Popular ...`. Five options -> ten utterances. Four `img` nodes with no name (the lucide SVGs at :24 and :40 carry no aria-hidden). Both radiogroups unnamed (:21, :33 pass no aria-label; the .section-label divs at :20/:32/:48/:63 carry no id). probe-P3-6-close.json: `headings: 0`, `role=group: 0`, `sectionLabelTags: ["div#-","div#-","div#-"]`.
defects.mechanism: Wrapping a `[role=radio]` button in a <label> whose text is a SIBLING of the control: the label names the radio AND remains a separate text node. Section headings are unassociated <div>s, so no group can point at them.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-7-aria.mjs and read the snapshot.
defects.proposedCure: DropdownMenuLabel names the group and DropdownMenuRadioItem puts the text inside the item, producing the correct tree by construction; add `aria-hidden="true"` to the glyphs as UserSortMenu.vue:12 already does.

defects.defect: Closing the popover by clicking outside drops focus to <body> instead of the opener — cross-engine, both schemes.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-6-close.json (WebKit) and P3-8-chromium.json (Chromium light and dark): Escape -> `focusIsTrigger: true`, `aria-expanded -> "false"` in all three; click-outside -> `focusIsTrigger: false, focusTag: "body"` in all three. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.1, Dialog/Drawer/Popover row: 'exact connected opener on close, otherwise the nearest surviving owning action.'
defects.mechanism: Half the producer close contract is wired: the Escape path restores, the dismiss path does not. Choosing a bare Popover left the consumer owning a contract it did not implement.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-6-close.mjs and node .../probe-P3-8-chromium.mjs. Manually: open the ⋮ menu, click empty page, press Tab — focus restarts at the top of the document.
defects.proposedCure: DropdownMenu owns close/restore on both paths. If the Popover is kept for any reason, wire the dismiss path to return focus to the connected opener explicitly.

defects.defect: `variant="ghost"` is not a glass-ui 7 prop, so both Buttons paint at the producer default emphasis — making `Clear all filters`, a reset, the visually dominant object in the menu. Two more calls (`p-0`, `h-8 w-8`) are equally inert.
defects.evidence: Button.vue.d.ts declares `emphasis: "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"` — there is no `variant`. Live DOM (evidence-p3/P3-3-truth.json -> apiLeak): trigger `data-emphasis=secondary data-size=md data-icon-only=true ... variant=ghost`; Clear-all `data-emphasis=secondary data-size=sm ... variant=ghost`. `variant="ghost"` sits on both as an invalid HTML attribute — the fallthrough proof. PopoverContent authored `class="w-60 p-0"` (:16) computes `padding: 20.352px 16px`. Trigger authored `h-8 w-8` renders 32.48 x 40.60.
defects.mechanism: Pre-glass-7 idioms survived the 7.0.0 adoption as silent no-ops because Vue fallthrough never warns. The design defect and the legacy-code defect are one: the surface looks styled while nothing was applied. Because `p-0` lost, the local 12px section padding is ADDITIVE to the producer's 16px — 23.3% of the menu's width is padding.
defects.reproduction: Playwright: read `[...document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Filters"]').attributes]` and `getComputedStyle(popoverContent).padding` on /#/browse; or run vue-tsc with strict template checking, which would surface undeclared props as errors.
defects.proposedCure: Pass only declared axes — `emphasis="quiet" size="xs" iconOnly`. Delete `variant`, `p-0` and `h-8 w-8` outright, no shims. Enable strict template type-checking on demo/ so an undeclared prop is a compile error rather than a silent DOM attribute.

defects.defect: A failed tag catalogue and an empty one render identically — as nothing. There is no loading, empty, error or retry state for an entire filter dimension.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useTagEdit.ts:40-49 `try { allTags.value = await getTags(); loaded.value = true } catch { /* silent — tag catalog is best-effort */ }`; SearchFilterBar.vue:47 `v-if="availableTags.length > 0"`. Observed: the Tags section is absent in all ten matrices I captured, with nothing anywhere indicating a filter dimension failed to load. The `loading` ref is exposed by useTagEdit and consumed nowhere in this component. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only ... error/status are explicit.'
defects.mechanism: A best-effort fetch with an empty catch, consumed by a v-if on array length. The three distinct states (loading / empty / failed) collapse into one rendered outcome: absence.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-1-register.mjs against the dev server (whose VITE_API_URL points at the production API, so getTags() never resolves) — `tags: null`, no section, no message. Read useTagEdit.ts:46-48.
defects.proposedCure: Surface `loading` and an `error` from useTagEdit and render three explicit states in the section: a skeleton while loading, named empty copy when the catalogue is genuinely empty, and a named failure with a retry when it errored.

defects.defect: Applying, changing or clearing a filter changes the wall with no announced result count and no status region anywhere.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-1-register.json `dialog.liveRegions: 0`; P3-6-close.json `structure.liveRegions: 0`. No `aria-busy` on the trigger. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.1, row 'in-route filter, tab, selection, or pagination' -> 'changed result count/state through the owning status region'.
defects.mechanism: The component emits filter changes upward and owns no status surface; the consumer provides none either. Combined with the clipped badge (P3-B3), the user's only route to learning what is filtering the wall is to reopen the drawer and read five controls.
defects.reproduction: On /#/browse after applying a filter: `document.querySelectorAll('[aria-live],[role=status],[role=alert]').length` inside the popover -> 0.
defects.proposedCure: One polite status region owned by the Browse workspace announcing the changed result count and the active filter set on every filter mutation, paired with visible removable applied-filter chips beneath the SearchBar.

defects.defect: In forced colors the colour swatch loses the only thing it communicates: its author background is replaced with Canvas, so 'Find by Color' renders as a blank white circle.
defects.evidence: The swatch's entire content is `:style="{ backgroundColor: pickerHex }"` (SearchFilterBar.vue:77). Chromium (WebKit does not truly emulate forced-colors): `chromium-light` -> `getComputedStyle(swatch).backgroundColor === "rgb(68, 136, 204)"`; `chromium-forced-colors` -> `"rgb(255, 255, 255)"`, with `forced-color-adjust: auto`. evidence-p3/P3-3-truth.json.
defects.mechanism: A value conveyed by background-color alone. Forced colors substitutes author backgrounds by design, so the control's whole payload is erased; the hex survives only in the aria-label, which a sighted HCM user never hears.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-3-truth.mjs (the Chromium forced-colors arm), or open /#/browse in Chromium with forced-colors emulation active and open the ⋮ menu.
defects.proposedCure: Render the hex as text beside the colour face and seat the face in a named geometric button, per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2's WatercolorDot ruling — so the value survives forced colors, monochrome and reduced transparency.

defects.defect: Five of the seven controls in the menu — both radio groups — paint no visible focus state at all, in either scheme; and four different focus vocabularies share one 240px surface, including the browser's default outline on a hand-rolled button.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-8-chromium.json, Chromium (authoritative per audit/visual/states.mjs:6-9), light AND dark: `button[role=radio].radio-group__item` -> `outlineStyle: "none"`, `boxShadow: "none"`, `paintsAnyRing: false`. The hand-rolled Search pill (`button.absolute.right-1`, :97) -> `outline: auto 1px rgb(185,189,192)` — the user-agent default, a register that exists nowhere else in this app. The input -> producer ring `0 0 0 2px`. The hand-rolled swatch -> only its resting cartoon caster. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'
defects.mechanism: Six control species assembled from three sources (producer atoms, a hand-rolled swatch button at :75, a hand-rolled Search button at :97) with no single focus owner. The Search button carries no `focus-ring` class and falls back to the UA ring; the radio's missing register is a producer defect on glass-ui's form RadioGroup.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-8-chromium.mjs — walks Tab in Chromium in both schemes and records outline/boxShadow per stop. Manually: open the ⋮ menu in Chrome, press Tab once, look at the Sort radio.
defects.proposedCure: One producer focus register per seat: transpose the option rows onto DropdownMenu*Item and replace the two hand-rolled buttons with glass-ui Button so `focus-ring` is inherited. Relay the RadioGroup item's missing focus register to the glass-ui BH inbox as a producer row.

defects.defect: The designed loading state can never paint: the spinner, the disabled binding and four disabled: utility classes are dead code.
defects.evidence: `applyColorSearch` (SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225) is `async` but contains no `await`; `searching.value = true`, the body runs synchronously and `finally` sets it false inside one tick. Live: 30 requestAnimationFrame frames with a MutationObserver on the dialog -> `{"sawSpinner": 0, "sawDisabled": 0, "frames": 30, "buttonHTML": "Search"}` (evidence-p3/P3-3-truth.json -> spinnerWatch).
defects.mechanism: A local synchronous flag standing in for an asynchronous operation that lives in the parent. The work that actually is async — the wall refetch — has no affordance in this component at all.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-3-truth.mjs; read `spinnerWatch`.
defects.proposedCure: Bind glass-ui Button's declared `loading` prop to the parent's real in-flight flag, or delete the register honestly. Do not keep a state that cannot occur.

defects.defect: Type roles outside the closed matrix (text-micro at 11px, one of them bold) and a token consumed for the opposite of its name (`--font-serif` used to obtain the sans control voice).
defects.evidence: Measured: `.section-label` -> Fira Code 14.384px uppercase tracking 1.4384px (text-mono-caption); count badge (:9 `text-micro font-bold`) -> 11px bold; inline Search commit (:99 `text-micro`) -> 11px against neighbours at 16.4px. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 declares the matrix 'closed across all eighteen compositions' with no text-micro rung and control copy non-bold; mono-caption is reserved for value/code/provenance. SearchFilterBar.vue:243 `font-family: var(--font-serif)` measures Plus Jakarta Sans, working only through the alias that demo/styles/foundation.css:95-102 documents as deliberate and fragile.
defects.mechanism: Local type decisions written outside the closed matrix, plus a dependency on an alias whose name asserts the opposite family. `.section-label` is a producer utility, so that row is a repo-wide mechanism family with this component as one site; the badge and Search pill are authored here.
defects.reproduction: Playwright evaluate on /#/browse with the popover open: getComputedStyle('.section-label').fontFamily -> 'Fira Code'; getComputedStyle(searchPill).fontSize -> '11px'; getComputedStyle('.filter-option').fontFamily -> 'Plus Jakarta Sans'.
defects.proposedCure: Use DropdownMenuLabel with the matrix's section-heading role for group labels; give the badge and the commit action matrix rungs (Badge size + text-small); write the type role directly instead of `var(--font-serif)`. The `.section-label` -> section-heading mapping needs a canon ruling, since the substitution is repo-wide.

defects.defect: Three unrelated vertical spacings (6 / 8 / 12px) share one 240px surface with no ladder relation, and the last row breaks the section padding it sits in.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-2-states.json -> rhythm: three `.filter-section` children at `12px/12px/12px/12px` then the Clear-all row at `8px/12px/8px/12px`. Label->group gap 6.00px (SearchFilterBar.vue:239 `margin-bottom: 0.375rem`).
defects.mechanism: Hand-authored spacing per region with no shared scale; `py-2` on the Clear row (:110) versus `padding: 0.75rem` on the sections (:238).
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-2-states.mjs; read `rhythm`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the local spacing entirely with the DropdownMenu transposition — the producer menu owns item padding and label spacing on one ladder.

defects.defect: The colour row's control column has three heights, and the swatch is 1.93x shorter than the field beside it at mobile — a mismatch that widens as the screen narrows.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-5-rails.json and P3-1-register.json: desktop swatch 28 / input 36 / Clear 36; mobile swatch 28 / input 54. Optical centres 796.72 vs 797.72 (1.0px apart).
defects.mechanism: A fixed `h-7 w-7` swatch (:76) beside a producer field whose `size="sm"` scales with the viewport. Nothing ties the two.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-1-register.mjs; compare `colourRow.swatch.h` and `colourRow.input.h` across the desktop and mobile matrices. Visible in shots-p3/P3-tall-mobile-open.png.
defects.proposedCure: Seat the colour face inside a producer control of the same size axis as the field (Button size="sm" hosting the face), so both scale on one ladder.

defects.defect: The colour field cannot display the value its own placeholder advertises: 84px of usable measure, and the 64px reserve is 11.41px larger than the button it reserves for.
defects.evidence: evidence-p3/P3-1-register.json: input w 148px, `padding-right: 64px` (`pr-16`, SearchFilterBar.vue:94); the Search pill measures 52.59px wide -> `reservedMinusActual: 11.41`. The placeholder renders as `#hex, …`.
defects.mechanism: A magic-number reserve tied to the literal string 'Search', in a field narrowed by the popover's 240px width and 28px of nested padding. Any relabelling silently underlaps the text.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-1-register.mjs; read `colourRow.inputPadRight`, `colourRow.searchPill.w`, `colourRow.reservedMinusActual`. Visible in every open-popover frame as '#hex, …'.
defects.proposedCure: Put the commit action outside the field as a sibling Button rather than overlaying it, so the field gets its full measure and no magic reserve exists.

defects.defect: The trigger glyph is exposed to assistive technology as a nameless image, while the identical glyph in the sibling component in the same directory is aria-hidden.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:6 `<EllipsisVertical class="h-4 w-4 text-muted-foreground" />` — no aria-hidden; AT tree of the trigger is `- button "Filters" [expanded]: - img`. UserSortMenu.vue:12 `<EllipsisVertical class="w-4 h-4 text-muted-foreground" aria-hidden="true" />`.
defects.mechanism: No shared convention for decorative glyphs; two files in one directory disagree.
defects.reproduction: node .../probe-P3-7-aria.mjs and read the trigger snapshot; diff the two source lines.
defects.proposedCure: aria-hidden="true" on every decorative glyph, enforced by the transposition onto producer menu items which own their own icon slots.

defects.defect: The standing Safari visual matrix has never photographed this component's body — every open-state frame in this audit is new.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json: all four `/#/browse` rows report `probe.counts.dialog: 0`, and `probe.a11y.smallTapTargets` lists only PaletteSlugBar controls ('Switch to slug', 'Generate new slug', 'Cancel'). 107 of the component's 125 template lines are behind the closed popover.
defects.mechanism: The standing capture script does not open overlays, so any component living inside a popover, dropdown or dialog is structurally invisible to it.
defects.reproduction: node -e reading REPORT.json and filtering results for '/#/browse'; inspect `probe.counts.dialog`.
defects.proposedCure: Add an overlay-open pass to audit/visual/states.mjs so every popover/dropdown/dialog-hosted component is photographed in its open state in all four matrices; until then, treat 'the visual matrix is green for Browse' as 'green with this menu closed'.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Matches the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with; seat DECLARED, not inherited. No defect on the receipt axis.
result.strongestDefect: L-10 — item visibility and handler existence are DISJOINT authorities. PaletteCardMenu decides which items exist from paletteKind/isOwned/isAdmin; each of the five PaletteCard consumers independently binds an arbitrary subset of the 17 optional emits; the two are joined only by an untyped `action: [action: string]` (PaletteCardMenu.vue:225) and a `Record<string, () => void>` whose miss path is a silent `if (!fn) return;` (PaletteCard.vue:316). REPRODUCED LIVE: on /#/mix the Mix source card (MixSourceSelector.vue:264-267, zero listeners bound) renders four ENABLED menu items — Publish, Rename, Export, Delete — and clicking Delete leaves localStorage unchanged, the card present, with no error and no feedback. The same run measured the menu trigger nested inside another <button> (invalid HTML), a structural consequence of a 17-emit instrument component being consumed as a thumbnail.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negative results recorded in the report: exactly ONE value.js instance in the live page, all subpaths resolving to the checkout's dist/ — refuting a types-from-npm/runtime-from-local split-brain; zero deep-path forgery of the value.js public API across all 50 demo import sites; zero raw .vue reaches into palettes/browser from outside the feature; verbatimModuleSyntax clean; Vue 3.5 idioms clean; not a god module.)

defects.defect: Item visibility and handler existence are disjoint authorities: the menu renders enabled items whose handlers do not exist in 3 of 5 PaletteCard consumers. Four live, enabled, no-op items in the Mix source selector; nine in AdminUsersPanel; five in ExtractWorkbench. Menu trigger also renders as a <button> nested in a <button>.

defects.defect: The published package forces @mkbabb/glass-ui and @mkbabb/keyframes.js on every consumer as runtime dependencies, while src/ imports neither and the built dist/ has zero external imports.

defects.mechanism: manifest lying about the dependency graph
defects.reproduction: The three commands above. tsconfig.demo.json's own header states the broken invariant: 'the library program (tsconfig.lib.json) never [sees glass-ui] (inv-K-1 — structurally glass-ui-free)'.
defects.proposedCure: Move both to devDependencies alongside the other ~30 demo-only packages (@vueuse/*, clsx, tailwind-merge, sortablejs, reka-ui). Published `dependencies` becomes {}, which is the truth. `files: ["dist", "!dist/gh-pages"]` already excludes the demo build, so nothing published needs them.

defects.defect: glass-ui 7.0.0 already publishes SortableList/SortableItem/SortableHandle at ./sortable-list, yet the pane hand-rolls @vueuse/integrations/useSortable + sortablejs and reaches into a child component's $el via `as any`. Edict-4 violation — and pass 1's proposed cure for its own BLOCKER L-1 would have preserved it.
defects.evidence: $ cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/sortable-list/index.d.ts => exports SortableList, SortableItem, SortableHandle, type SortableId; sortable-list.js ships its own dropResolver with cross-group support. Against that: `grep -rn "useSortable" demo/` => exactly 2 hits, PalettesPane.vue:133 and :183 (plus one comment). PalettesPane.vue:181: `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el`. The victim documents its own damage at PaletteCardGrid.vue:8-12: 'a leading comment node would make this a multi-root component, and PalettesPane reads $el for useSortable — a fragment root resolves $el to the comment node, not the <div>.'
defects.mechanism: design-system primitive exists but was not adopted; parent reaches into child internals
defects.reproduction: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/sortable-list/index.d.ts` and `grep -rn "useSortable" demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'` — the primitive is published, the demo has one hand-rolled call site, and sortablejs@^1.15.7 + @types/sortablejs@^1.15.9 are in the tree for it.
defects.proposedCure: PaletteCardGrid renders <SortableList>/<SortableItem>/<SortableHandle> and emits @reorder(ids); the library port exposes movePalette(fromId,toId); usePaletteStore splices the store array. Deletes: the useSortable import, sortableGridRef, sortableEl, the `as any`, the $el read, the onEnd index arithmetic, PaletteCardGrid's comment-node constraint, sortablejs, @types/sortablejs — and, because no view holds the list, the entire vueuse branch L-1's corruption came from.

defects.defect: A palettes <-> shell dependency cycle created purely by co-locating the five InjectionKey symbols with the provider; five shell components reach into a feature module for one Symbol, and the identity they get is a pure pass-through of platform/auth. demo/palettes/ is the demo's god directory.
defects.evidence: palettes->shell: usePalettePorts.ts:19 `import type { ViewId } from "../shell/useViewManager"`. shell->palettes: Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, SlugEditLayer.vue:5, ProfileSection.vue:14, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13 all import SESSION_PORT_KEY. usePalettePorts.ts:5-7 imports useAdminAuth/useUserAuth/useSession from ../platform/auth/ and lines 127-135 forward seven members unchanged. Measured closure (pass-1 scratchpad/closure.mjs): PalettesPane.vue = 97 modules, 18 of them admin; usePaletteStore.ts = 3. demo/palettes/ also holds the app's whole HTTP client (api/ 8 modules incl. admin-audit/admin-users), all admin composables, browse, slug migration, mix.ts, export. 23 inbound edges from 7 non-palettes areas.
defects.mechanism: dependency-direction inversion: shell depends downward into a feature
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "SESSION_PORT_KEY" demo/shell/` -> 5 files. `grep -rn "palettes/" demo/shell demo/picker demo/workbenches demo/scenes demo/platform demo/color-session demo/color-picker --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'` -> 23 edges. Closure walk in scratchpad/closure.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Extract demo/palettes/keys.ts — the five InjectionKeys plus hand-written port INTERFACES (not `ReturnType<typeof providePalettePorts>`), type-only imports, a pure leaf. usePalettePorts.ts imports those keys and satisfies the interfaces, so the port contract becomes checked rather than inferred. The five shell files stop importing from palettes entirely and read platform/auth directly. PalettePortsDeps takes an opaque `currentView: Ref<string>` from the composition root (usePaletteWiring.ts:60 already is that root), so palettes stops naming the shell. Do this FIRST — mechanical, no behaviour change, unblocks verification of everything else.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 19 directories of pure re-export alias over glass-ui with zero implementation — the migration shim the no-legacy edict forbids — and PalettesPane refutes them inside its own 24-line import block by using both the shim and the direct subpath.
defects.evidence: Every demo/ui/*/index.ts is a single `export {...} from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` line (dumped all 19). demo/ui/alert/index.ts:1-9 states its local implementation was converted to a re-export at B.W2. PalettesPane.vue:129-131 imports Card/Button/Badge through the shims; :148-149 imports Dialog* and SearchBar from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog and /search — even though demo/ui/dialog exists and exports exactly that family. demo/ui/input alone uses a subpath (@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms) — a third convention. Measured: exports['.'] -> dist/glass-ui.js; `grep -oE 'from *"[^"]+"' glass-ui.js | sort -u | wc -l` = 46 (43 internal chunks + vue + reka-ui + @lucide/vue); `cat dist/card.js` = one import of a single 5299-byte chunk. glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes 70 export keys.
defects.mechanism: alias/shim layer + inconsistent module-path convention for one dependency
defects.reproduction: `for d in demo/ui/*/; do cat "$d/index.ts"; done` and the two glass-ui greps above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ wholesale; rewrite the 31 importers to the granular @mkbabb/glass-ui/<component> subpaths. One codemod, no behaviour change, 19 files and a directory removed, and one convention survives. Nothing has ever been swapped behind the seam, and edict 4 forbids anything ever being.

defects.defect: savedColorStrings reaches the palettes subtree by two independent transports simultaneously, from one origin: as a de-reffed prop through the pane router, and as a Ref through the ports deps.
defects.evidence: Route A: useColorPipeline.ts:166 -> App.vue:341 -> usePaneRouter.ts:155 -> PalettesPane.vue:154 (defineProps<{savedColorStrings: string[]}>) -> CurrentPaletteEditor prop. Route B: App.vue:356 -> usePaletteWiring.ts:31,63 -> usePalettePorts.ts:36,47,94 -> usePaletteActions.ts:13,101,103 (deps.savedColorStrings.value). PalettesPane already injects LIBRARY_PORT_KEY and COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY at :164-165.
defects.mechanism: duplicated ownership: one concept, two transports, two type spellings
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "savedColorStrings" demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'` -> 22 hits spanning both chains.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the prop. The owner is useColorPipeline; expose `currentColors` on the colour-session port and let PalettesPane and CurrentPaletteEditor read it there. usePaneRouter.rightProps('palettes') collapses to {} and the router stops knowing one pane's prop names (usePaneRouter.ts:150-158).

defects.defect: Commit/cancel-edit has two mechanisms — an emit routed into a component instance method, and an already-injected port member — and the instance route needs a 40x50ms mount poll that gives up with a console.warn.
defects.evidence: usePaneRouter.ts:156-157 `"onCommit-edit": () => deps.colorPickerRef()?.commitEdit()`. usePalettePorts.ts:239 `commitColorEdit: actions.commitColorEdit` — injected by this same component at PalettesPane.vue:165, unused. Third emitter at Dock.vue:143-144 handled by App.vue:41-42 the same way. Cost written down at usePaletteWiring.ts:31-58: `const PICKER_WAIT_ATTEMPTS = 40; // 40 x 50ms ~ 2s` ... `console.warn('[usePaletteWiring] gave up waiting for the color picker to mount')`.
defects.mechanism: instance-ref coupling instead of shared state, patched with a mount-order poll
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "commitEdit\|cancelEdit\|commitColorEdit" demo/` -> three emitters, one unused port member, one ref-call at usePaneRouter.ts:156, one bounded poll at usePaleteWiring.ts:41-52.
defects.proposedCure: Edit state is session state. Put editTarget + commit() + cancel() on the colour-session store; dock, pane and picker all call the store. colorPickerRef, PaneRouterDeps.colorPickerRef, whenColorPickerReady, the 2s poll and its console.warn all delete — and with them the mount-order race they exist to paper over.

defects.defect: The imperative card-feedback registry is duplicated across two panes with two different identity schemes (id here, slug in BrowsePane), an any-cast ref callback in each, a defineExpose escape hatch, and a leak (nothing deletes on unmount).
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:177 cardRefs reactive record; :84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.id] = el)"`; :205 `card.showFeedback(...)`. BrowsePane.vue:209 the same record; :94 keyed by palette.slug; :228/237/249/264 call sites. PaletteCard.vue:238-244 exists to defineExpose({showFeedback}) for these callers. Third site documented at browser/dialog/composables/useDialogBrowseActions.ts:41.
defects.mechanism: imperative cross-component method call instead of declarative state
defects.reproduction: `grep -n "defineExpose\|showFeedback" demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue` -> :238,:244; the two cardRefs registries at the line numbers above.
defects.proposedCure: Feedback is a property of the palette, not of a component instance. PaletteCard takes :feedback and renders ActionFeedback (already at browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue) declaratively. One usePaletteFeedback() holding Map<paletteKey, {message,variant,at}>. defineExpose, both registries, both any casts and the leak disappear.

defects.defect: Three homes for 'name -> identifier' with measured divergence: an exported file's name disagrees with the slug inside the file it names.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/utils.ts:3-13 slugify (NFKD-normalizing) vs demo/palettes/export.ts:9-11 slugify (naive [^a-z0-9]+) vs export/canonical.ts:50-59 identifierPrefix ('no slugifier exists' — uses the stored slug). result.strongestDefect: L-1 — drag-to-reorder deterministically persists a corrupted order (forward drag: all four positions wrong, 3/3 runs) and silently discards it (backward drag: total no-op), written through to localStorage and surviving reload. It is the one behaviour PalettesPane owns outright, and it is broken by three compounding library-structure errors: a dereferenced computed handed to useSortable (so vueuse takes its no-copy, no-write-back branch), a custom onEnd that does not override vueuse's default onUpdate (different keys in the same spread, so both fire and onUpdate's synchronous splice lands first), and the array being spliced is a live computed cache returned by reference from useFilteredList.ts:9. Pass 2 sharpens the cure: the fix is not to relocate the hand-rolled binding into PaletteCardGrid as pass 1 proposed, because glass-ui 7.0.0 already publishes SortableList/SortableItem/SortableHandle at ./sortable-list (L-13) — relocating would trade a correctness defect for an edict-4 defect and keep sortablejs in the tree. The deepest MECHANISM behind the whole finding set, however, is L-3: demo/palettes/ is the demo's god directory, holding the app's entire HTTP client, the admin console, browse, slug migration, mix math and export, with the shell depending downward into it for identity that actually lives in demo/platform/auth/ — a 97-module closure (18 admin) to render a list of saved palettes.
result.negativeProof: The challenge's headline hypothesis — that the demo reaches the library through paths a real consumer could not write — is FALSE at runtime, and I prove it positively rather than by failing to find fault. (1) Exhaustive census of all 49 value.js import sites in demo/: `grep -rhn 'from ".*value\.js.*"' --include=*.vue --include=*.ts demo/ | sed 's/.*from //' | sort | uniq -c` yields exactly 24 "@mkbabb/value.js/color", 10 "/css", 6 "/math", 5 "/easing", 4 "/quantize" — zero ../../src/, zero @src/, zero dist/, zero root-barrel. All five specifiers ARE in package.json#exports; a real consumer could write all 49. (2) tsconfig.demo.json carries no @src/* path, so a deep import would not typecheck from the demo tree; @src survives only for the exempt assets/docs/*.md source-embedding plugin. (3) PalettesPane's own transitive closure reaches value.js only through /color and /css (demo/palettes/mix.ts:14; demo/color-session/{picker-color,view-accent,ink,color-utils,generate-color}.ts) — all bare subpaths. (4) vite.config.ts:37-50 GENERATES its alias array from this repo's own package.json#exports at config time, one anchored regex per subpath, so the runtime alias set cannot drift from the map by construction. AMENDMENT (this is where pass 1 over-claimed and I correct it): property (4) belongs to the Vite half ONLY. The TypeScript half is hand-written and HAS drifted — tsconfig.demo.json declares '@mkbabb/value.js', '/parsing' and '/units', all three ABSENT from exports and MISSING on disk (L-11). So the sound statement is narrower than pass 1's: the demo does not reach into src/, and what it does import it imports legitimately; the defect is on the other side of the boundary — the published surface has no root, is over-declared in the demo's type config, over-specified in the manifest (L-12), and missing the one domain this component exists to demonstrate (L-16). Two further soundnesses, recorded so a later seat does not re-litigate: (a) demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue is NOT an edict-3 contrivance — demo/shared/ predates this work (3 files), PaneHeader has 9 real consumers and owns --pane-scroll and its only consumers, and `grep -rl "ScrollCard" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` returns EMPTY, so no glass-ui successor exists to adopt; it is a proposal to glass-ui, not a violation (contrast L-13, where the primitive DOES exist). (b) PalettesPane.vue:135's import of CSS_COLOR_KEY from ../color-session/keys is a CORRECT cross-area edge: colour state is genuinely owned by color-session, the keys module is a pure leaf with type-only imports and 26 consumers and no cycle — it is precisely the pattern L-3 asks palettes to adopt. Finally, the visual matrix is clean for this route: safari desktop+mobile x light+dark all show overflowX 0, main=1, 0 page errors, 0 console errors, no blank; the screenshot renders correctly; the one namelessButton on desktop tracks the left picker pane, not this component (PalettesPane's only icon-only button carries aria-label at :68). Every finding above is invisible to the eye and to the visual matrix both — which is what this seat is for.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (pass 2)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context arm). Tier explicitly declared at spawn; the seat is declared, not inherited. No defect on this axis.
result.strongestDefect: P2-1 — At 390px the palette card's identity renders at exactly 0px wide (nameRenderedWidth 0, nameVisibleFraction 0%) while this component's menu trigger holds an immovable 54px = 16.9% of the 320px metadata row and a "Featured" badge holds 148.4px = 46.4%. The card has no name on mobile. The only surviving spelling of the palette's identity is this menu's own header, which clips it to 56% (scrollW 319 / clientW 178) and carries title:null, so the remaining 44% is unreachable from anywhere in the card's UI. The protagonist mandated by VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 (`--type-subheading`, Fraunces) is the one element that yielded, because every competitor in the row is `shrink-0` and only the name sits in the `min-w-0` arm.
result.negativeProof: Verified sound, re-measured this pass: (1) the trigger's tap target is 54x54 at 390px and 36x36 at 1440 — meets the 44px touch floor, and appears in NONE of REPORT.json's `smallTapTargets` rows for /#/palettes or /#/browse across all four Safari matrices; (2) the trigger is named — `aria-label="Palette menu"` (PaletteCard.vue:100); the single `namelessButtons` hit on /#/palettes is also present on /#/ where this component does not render, so it is not this control; (3) producer menu semantics are correct and consumed correctly — measured role="menu"/"menuitem"/"separator", aria-haspopup, aria-expanded on the sub-trigger, data-highlighted roving walk; the component adds no ARIA of its own and breaks none; (4) motion is producer-owned, collapses to opacity/0.15s under prefers-reduced-motion, animates only composited properties, declares no local keyframes — edict 6 clean; (5) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — both type imports are `import type` (:177-178); (6) not a god module — 228 lines, one job, sub-components colocated; (7) the DI seam is right — `useApiClient()` reads the availability latch through the injected client, not a module singleton (the predicate is wrong, the seam is not); (8) the degraded-state instinct (name the reason in-register, not by toast) is exactly what VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 asks for — it is applied too narrowly and rendered unreadably, but the instinct is canon-aligned.

defects.defect: At 390px the palette identity renders at 0px while this component's trigger holds a fixed 54px (16.9%) of the 320px metadata row. The card has no name on mobile; the menu header is the sole surviving identity and truncates to 56% with no title recovery.
