defects.proposedCure: Delete PaletteSlugBar.vue, its `slug/` barrel and the re-export — but ONLY after replacing `slugBarRef` in useSlugMigration with a `Ref<string | null>` the composable owns and the live SlugEditLayer renders in a `role="alert"` region. Deleting the orphan first deletes the evidence and keeps the bug.

defects.defect: NEW — the `ADMIN_TOKEN=` disambiguator is stripped and then ignored: classification is purely shape-based, so an admin token in four-word form is routed to USER login and POSTed in cleartext to the unauthenticated `/sessions/login` endpoint as a `slug`, and admin login is unreachable for that whole token class.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:204-205 `const normalized = normalizeTokenInput(raw).toLowerCase(); const isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized);`. Measured emission table (probe P4-3): `ADMIN_TOKEN=correct-horse-battery-staple -> ["correct-horse-battery-staple", false]`; `ADMIN_TOKEN="correct-horse-battery-staple" -> ["correct-horse-battery-staple", false]`; contrast `ADMIN_TOKEN=change-me-to-a-secure-random-string -> [..., true]`. Wire shape: demo/platform/auth/sessions.ts:18-25 `POST /sessions/login body: JSON.stringify({ slug })`. Token format: api/.env.example:2 `ADMIN_TOKEN=change-me-to-a-secure-random-string`. Byte-identical logic live at demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:25-54.
defects.mechanism: A masking fallback (edict-2 violation) used as a security boundary — normalizeTokenInput cleans the input so a shape heuristic can classify it, then the explicit user-supplied label is discarded, so a legitimate credential is silently reclassified as a public identifier.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteSlugBar/probes/c4-vitest.config.ts — read the `RAW="ADMIN_TOKEN=correct-horse-battery-staple" -> [...]` line in P4-3.
defects.proposedCure: Move the decision into one exported predicate in demo/platform/auth/: an `ADMIN_TOKEN=`-prefixed input is an admin token BY DECLARATION; a bare input is a slug only if it matches the generator's alphabet; anything else is an explicit rejection with a message. Never a silent reclassification. Collapses C-5, C-23, C-24, C-30 and half of C-19 in one move.

defects.defect: NEW — the credential field is a bare `<input type="search">` with no name, autocomplete, autocapitalize, autocorrect, spellcheck, inputmode, aria-label or aria-describedby: an admin token is typed into a UA search field (retained in search/autofill history), iOS sentence-capitalization breaks the un-lowercased admin branch, and the field has no accessible name.
defects.evidence: Probe P4-1 rendered census: `INPUT ATTRS: {"type":"search","placeholder":"enter slug...","class":"input-bar-field","value":""}` with `HAS name/autocomplete/autocapitalize/autocorrect/spellcheck/inputmode/aria-label/aria-describedby: false` (all eight). Live twin, probes/c4-live.mjs on /#/palettes: `{"type":"text","placeholder":"enter slug or token...","name":null,"autocomplete":null,"autocapitalize":null,"spellcheck":null,"ariaLabel":null,"w":160,"h":23}`. Vendor render (dist/search.js) emits only ref/type/attrs/value/placeholder/class/onInput. Admin branch un-lowercased: PaletteSlugBar.vue:213 `emit("switchSlug", isAdmin ? normalizeTokenInput(raw) : normalized, isAdmin)`.
defects.mechanism: Same root as C-2 — a search primitive standing in for a credential field inherits search-field UA semantics (history retention, autocapitalize=sentences, spellcheck on) and none of the form-field ones (name, label, autocomplete control).
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config docs/.../probes/c4-vitest.config.ts (P4-1 stdout) and node docs/.../probes/c4-live.mjs (slugInputs block). NOTE: the iOS autocapitalize consequence is source/UA-spec proven, not device-reproduced — labelled a hypothesis in the report.
defects.proposedCure: Replace with the design system's form primitive carrying name, autocomplete="off", autocapitalize="off", autocorrect="off", spellcheck="false", a real label/aria-label and aria-describedby pointing at an announced error region; and lowercase-normalize both branches or neither.

defects.defect: The admin/user classifier is a negation, so any input that is not exactly four lowercase dash-separated words is treated as an admin token.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:184-186 + 205. Measured routing (P4-3): `"test-user" -> ["test-user", true]`, `"-a-b-c-" -> ["-a-b-c-", true]`, `"change-me-to-a-secure-random-string" -> [..., true]`. A typo in a slug therefore calls `adminLogin(value)` (demo/platform/auth/useAdminAuth.ts:36-39), which writes the bogus string to `localStorage["palette-admin-token"]` with no validation and flips `isAuthenticated` true.
defects.mechanism: Catch-all negation used where a positive, alphabet-checked predicate is required; the admin branch is the DEFAULT rather than an explicit, declared choice.
defects.reproduction: Same P4-3 table.
defects.proposedCure: Same as C-30 — one deciding predicate in demo/platform/auth/, with an explicit rejection branch.

defects.defect: `slugSwitching` is set true and false within one synchronous turn, so the spinner, the in-flight accessible name and the double-submit guard are all unrenderable.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:201-224 — `slugSwitching.value = true` … the emit at 213 is synchronous … `finally { slugSwitching.value = false }` runs before any render. The `:disabled="!slugInput.trim() || slugSwitching"` guard (line 23) and the `:aria-label="slugSwitching ? 'Signing in…' : ..."` (line 24) can never be observed; the `Loader2` at line 26 never paints.
defects.mechanism: An emit is not an await. The component models an async operation it does not actually own — the parent's handler is the async one, and its promise is discarded.
defects.reproduction: Read PaletteSlugBar.vue:198-225; pass 3 measured `spinner nodes while parent pending: 0`.
defects.proposedCure: Either the component owns the async call and awaits it, or it renders no in-flight state at all and the owning composable exposes a `pending` ref. Half-owning it is the defect.

defects.defect: The slug input has no accessible name — the placeholder is the only label, and it disappears on first keystroke.
defects.evidence: Probe P4-1: `HAS aria-label: false`, no `<label>` in the rendered markup dump; the live twin measures the same (`ariaLabel: null`). The visual REPORT independently books a nameless `{"w":160,"h":23,"tag":"input","label":""}` row on /#/palettes.
defects.mechanism: glass-ui `SearchBar` (unlike its sibling `FuzzySearch`) has no `ariaLabel` prop and the consumer supplies none via attrs.
defects.reproduction: P4-1 stdout; REPORT.json results[matrix=safari-desktop-light, route=/#/palettes].probe.a11y.smallTapTargets.
defects.proposedCure: Covered by C-31's cure — the form primitive carries the label seam.

defects.defect: The error paragraph is not announced: no role="alert", no aria-live, and the input has no aria-describedby/aria-invalid, so an async failure is invisible to assistive technology even when it renders.
defects.evidence:
PaletteSlugBar.vue:124-126 — `

` with no role and no aria-live. Live-region census after a failed login (probes/c4-live-login.mjs): `liveRegions` contains only unrelated readouts; no login message ever appears.
defects.mechanism: An error surface authored as a purely visual affordance.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../probes/c4-live-login.mjs — inspect the `liveRegions` array in the AFTER block.
defects.proposedCure: One `role="alert"` region owned by the composable (C-1 cure), referenced by the field's aria-describedby, with aria-invalid toggled on failure.

defects.defect: The identity pill is a bare `<span>` with tabIndex -1 behind a hover-only popover root — unreachable by keyboard, and its explanatory content unreachable by touch.
defects.evidence: Probe P4-6: `focusable: ["BUTTON:Account menu"]` — one focusable node in the entire default mode; `pill tag: SPAN tabIndex: -1 role: null`. Trigger config: PaletteSlugBar.vue:45 `<Popover trigger="hover" :close-delay="0" :open-delay="300">`.
defects.mechanism: A hover-only disclosure with a non-focusable trigger has no keyboard or touch equivalent.
defects.reproduction: P4-6 stdout.
defects.proposedCure: The pill either becomes a real button (focusable, click-toggled popover) or the copy moves somewhere reachable. `trigger="hover"` with `cursor-help` is a mouse-only affordance.

defects.defect: `variant="ghost"` is not a prop of glass-ui 7's `Button` (the axis is `emphasis`), so it falls through as a junk DOM attribute and the intended quiet styling never applies — and both gates pass.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts — `ButtonProps extends PrimitiveProps { emphasis?; tone?; size?; iconOnly?; loading?; type?; disabled?; class? }`; PrimitiveProps is `{asChild?, as?}` with no index signature. Rendered DOM (P4-1): `<button data-slot="button" data-emphasis="secondary" ... variant="ghost" aria-label="Sign in with slug">`. Sites: PaletteSlugBar.vue:19 and :31. Gates: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` EXIT=0, `npx eslint <file>` EXIT=0.
defects.mechanism: A retired API name kept alive by attribute fallthrough, which no gate in this repo inspects.
defects.reproduction: Run both gate commands above; read the P4-1 markup dump.
defects.proposedCure: `emphasis="quiet"` at the call sites, and a lint/type rule that rejects unknown attributes on design-system components so fallthrough stops masking retired names.

defects.defect: Vacuous gates — zero tests name either slug surface, the only login e2e seeds localStorage and pins /sessions/login to a permanent 200, and eight named mutations keep every gate green.
defects.evidence: grep -rn "PaletteSlugBar\|SlugEditLayer" test/ e2e/ → zero hits. e2e/smoke/fixtures/user-auth.ts:60 writes SLUG_STORAGE/TOKEN_STORAGE directly into localStorage; lines 84-89 `await page.route("**/sessions/login", route => route.fulfill({status: 200, ...}))` so the 404/409/429 branches are never exercised. Gates green at HEAD: vue-tsc EXIT=0, eslint EXIT=0. Mutations enumerated in §4 of the report (M-1..M-8), e.g. `function setError(_msg: string) {}` or `function looksLikeSlug() { return false }`.
defects.mechanism: The test suite was routed around the dead surface (documented in login-register.spec.ts:5-8) instead of the surface being fixed or deleted, so the login domain has coverage of its happy path only.
defects.reproduction: Run the two gate commands and the greps above.
defects.proposedCure: Land a born-RED test first: a failed /sessions/login must render an announced error. It is red today against BOTH the orphan and the shipped SlugEditLayer, and it closes the gate that let all eight mutations through.

defects.defect: The slug protocol is duplicated verbatim in the live `SlugEditLayer.vue`, and the copies have drifted (different error copy, different idioms, different field type).
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:25-37 carries byte-identical `looksLikeSlug` and `normalizeTokenInput`; :39-66 mirrors `onSlugSwitch`. Drift: error string "Already signed in." vs "Already signed in as this slug."; `useTemplateRef` (SlugEditLayer:14) vs `ref<InstanceType<...>>` (PaletteSlugBar:166); `<input>` type text vs type search.
defects.mechanism: Copy-then-orphan — the replacement was cloned from the original rather than extracted from it, so both the logic and its defects (C-5, C-30) were duplicated.
defects.reproduction: diff the two blocks: demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:184-225 vs demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:25-66.
defects.proposedCure: Extract the one predicate + one submit protocol into demo/platform/auth/ and delete both copies (C-30 cure).

defects.defect: Focus never reaches the slug input: `nextTick` inside a 50 ms `setTimeout` resolves in the same microtask as the mode flip, while the `mode="out-in"` leave holds insertion for a measured 200 ms.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:176-181 `setTimeout(() => { slugEditMode.value = true; nextTick(() => searchBarRef.value?.inputRef?.focus()) }, 50)`. Measured leave (probes/c4-live.mjs): `.vj-morph-leave-active` → `transitionProperty: "opacity, transform, max-height"`, `transitionDuration: "0.2s, 0.2s, 0.2s"`; token `--duration-fast: 0.2s`.
defects.mechanism: A microtask scheduled against a CSS transition — nextTick tracks the render queue, not the transition's completion, so the ref is still null when focus() is attempted.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../probes/c4-live.mjs — read the `morph` block.
defects.proposedCure: Focus on the Transition's `@after-enter` hook (or `@enter`), which is the event that actually means "the input exists". The arbitrary 50 ms delay then disappears, taking C-11 with it.

defects.defect: The account-menu trigger measures 22 x 22 px against the live cascade — below WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's 24 px minimum — and because it is hand-rolled it carries no `data-control-target`, so the design system's coarse-pointer 44 px rule never reaches it.
defects.evidence: probes/c4-tap.mjs, injecting PaletteSlugBar.vue:84's exact class string into the live page: `"menu": {"w": 22, "h": 22}`, `hasDataControlTarget: false`. Live stylesheet rule, enumerated from document.styleSheets: `@media (pointer: coarse) { [data-control-target] { min-block-size: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem); min-inline-size: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem); } }`. glass-ui stamps that attribute for iconOnly buttons (dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:54). The visual REPORT independently measures the live SlugEditLayer twins at 22x22.
defects.mechanism: Hand-rolling the button opted the control out of the design system's touch-target guarantee — an edict-4/edict-5 violation with a measurable a11y consequence, not a style preference.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteSlugBar/probes/c4-tap.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Use glass-ui `Button` with `iconOnly` for all six hand-rolled controls; the 44 px coarse-pointer floor and the press affordance (C-32) then arrive for free.

defects.defect: The 50 ms `setTimeout` in `onStartSlugEdit` is never cancelled and survives unmount, firing into a torn-down instance.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:176-181; no `onBeforeUnmount`/`clearTimeout` anywhere in the file. Probe P4-5: `pending timers after click: 1 · after unmount: 1 · after advance: 0` — it survives unmount and then fires.
defects.mechanism: An unowned timer handle; the component's only lifecycle resource has no cleanup.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config docs/.../probes/c4-vitest.config.ts — read the P4-5 block.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the timer entirely by moving focus onto the Transition's after-enter hook (C-3's cure); if a delay must remain, own the handle and clear it in onBeforeUnmount.

defects.defect: No path clears `slugError`, and no clearError is exposed, so an error raised in edit mode persists visibly into default mode after Cancel.
defects.evidence:
Probe P4-7 full replay (submit own slug -> click Cancel): `error after self-submit: "Already signed in as this slug."` then, in default mode, `paragraphs in default mode after cancel: ["Already signed in as this slug."]` and the markup dump shows the `

` still rendered beside the slug pill. Cancel handler is `@click="slugEditMode = false"` (line 36) — it touches nothing else. `resetEditMode()` (line 231-234) also leaves slugError set.
defects.mechanism: Error state scoped to the component but not to the mode it belongs to; two of the three state resets are incomplete.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config docs/.../probes/c4-vitest.config.ts — read the P4-7 block.
defects.proposedCure: Once the error moves to the composable (C-1's cure), clearing it becomes a single transition on the mode change rather than three call sites that must each remember.

defects.defect: NEW — the error line measures 989 px of `whitespace-nowrap` text hung 16 px below a 36 px bar, fed by an unbounded server string.
defects.evidence: probes/c4-tap.mjs, rendering PaletteSlugBar.vue:124's exact class string with a 105-char realistic message: `"err": {"w": 989, "h": 23}`; container `min-h-9` measured 36 px; `-bottom-4` measured `bottom: -16px`. Unbounded source: line 221 `else slugError.value = msg || "Login failed"`.
defects.mechanism: Absolute positioning + nowrap + an unbounded upstream string — three choices that are each fine alone and jointly guarantee overflow.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../probes/c4-tap.mjs — read the `err` block.
defects.proposedCure: The announced error region (C-7's cure) is in normal flow, wraps, and renders bounded, authored copy keyed off `ApiProblem.status` — never a raw server string.

defects.defect: NEW — every control pairs `active:scale-*` with `transition-colors`, so the press transform snaps instantly while the colour eases over 200 ms.
defects.evidence: probes/c4-tap.mjs: `"menu": {"transitionProperty": "color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, --tw-gradient-*", "transitionDuration": "0.2s"}` — `transform` is absent. Sites: PaletteSlugBar.vue:73, 84 (`active:scale-95`) and 91, 98, 106, 113 (`active:scale-[0.98]`).
defects.mechanism: A transition utility chosen for one property applied next to an animation on another; the press gesture's two halves run on different clocks.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../probes/c4-tap.mjs — compare `transitionProperty` against the class strings.
defects.proposedCure: Use glass-ui `Button`, which already ships the coherent press system (`tap-squish`, `data-press-armed`, `--glass-btn-press-t`) — visible in this same file's markup on its two real Buttons.

defects.defect: NEW (glass-ui/reka-ui relay) — the popover trigger renders `aria-controls=""` while closed, an invalid empty IDREF.
defects.evidence: Probe P4-6 markup dump: `<button id="reka-popover-trigger-v-0" type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="" data-state="closed" aria-label="Account menu">`.
defects.mechanism: reka-ui emits the attribute unconditionally through glass-ui's PopoverTrigger; ARIA has no 'controls nothing' value, so the attribute must be omitted when there is no target. Reproduced on every popover in the demo.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config docs/.../probes/c4-vitest.config.ts — read the P4-6 DEFAULT MARKUP dump.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox per the standing fond: omit aria-controls when closed.

defects.defect: NEW (glass-ui relay, HYPOTHESIS) — `SearchBar` hand-rolls a controlled input (`:value` + `@input`) with no compositionstart/compositionend guard, so IME composition should be clobbered.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/search.js — `b("input", w({ref_key:"inputRef", ref:s, type:"search"}, o.value, {value: e.modelValue, placeholder: e.placeholder, class:"input-bar-field", onInput: r[0] ||= e => i("update:modelValue", e.target.value)}), null, 16, Q)`. Vue's own v-model directive installs exactly the two composition guards this omits.
defects.mechanism: Re-assigning `value` during an active IME composition commits or clears the pre-edit buffer; Vue's v-model suppresses model writes between compositionstart and compositionend for precisely this reason.
defects.reproduction: NONE — mechanism proven from vendor source; no IME was driven in this pass. Labelled a hypothesis in the report.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui relay: add compositionstart/compositionend handling to SearchBar, or bind with v-model on the native input rather than hand-rolling the controlled pattern.

defects.defect: NEW (correction to the shared visual REPORT) — 4 of the 8 a11y rows booked on safari-desktop-light /#/palettes are measurement artifacts: the slug controls are on an inactive dock face with effective opacity 0, an `inert` ancestor and `aria-hidden="true"`, and focus does not land on them.
defects.evidence: REPORT.json a11y.smallTapTargets on that route lists `{"w":22,"h":22,"label":"Switch to slug"}`, `{..."Generate new slug"}`, `{..."Cancel"}` and `{"w":160,"h":23,"tag":"input","label":""}`. Measured ancestor walk (probes/c4-live-login.mjs): `{"opacityChain": 0, "anyAncestorInert": true, "anyAncestorAriaHidden": true, "focusLanded": false}`.
defects.mechanism: The visual probe's census is getBoundingClientRect-based, so it counts controls that are laid out but neither visible nor focusable. Dock layers are all rendered; only one face is active.
defects.reproduction: node docs/.../probes/c4-live-login.mjs — read the HIDDEN-FOCUSABLE block; compare against REPORT.json.
defects.proposedCure: Add an effective-opacity / `inert` / elementFromPoint filter to the visual probe's a11y census before its counts are used as a defect budget by other component seats. (The same measurement is a negative proof that the dock has NO hidden-focusable trap.)

defects.defect: NEW (meta) — pass 3's 'reproducible, committed' harness does not run: probes/c3-vitest.config.ts's `include` points at a session scratchpad path that no longer exists, so the committed probe file is never loaded.
defects.evidence: $ npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteSlugBar/probes/c3-vitest.config.ts → `FAIL .../scratchpad/slugbar.probe.test.ts` / `Error: Cannot find module '/private/tmp/claude-504/.../scratchpad/slugbar.probe.test.ts'` / `Test Files 1 failed (1) · Tests no tests`.
defects.mechanism: An absolute scratchpad path baked into a committed config — the artifact was copied but its pointer was not rehomed.
defects.reproduction: Run the command above.
defects.proposedCure: Fixed in probes/c4-vitest.config.ts, which resolves root and probe from its own import.meta.url and is verified green from the repo path (18 tests passed). Any audit finding about vacuous gates loses standing if the audit's own gate is vacuous.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue (area palettes), r4 pass
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared tier served throughout; no delegation, no inherited/ambient default.

defects.defect: MiniColorPicker (the subject's only child) latches its drag flags `canvasDragging`/`hueDragging` to true on pointerdown and clears them ONLY on pointerup. There is no `pointercancel` or `lostpointercapture` handler. After a cancelled touch gesture the drag never ends, and subsequent plain hover moves (buttons=0) keep driving the colour — which propagates through `update:hex` into SearchFilterBar's `pickerHex` AND `colorText`, so the colour that the next Search press actually searches changes because the pointer moved.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue:126-137 (and :143-149 for the hue strip). Measured, probes/probe-C-r4-6.mjs → evidence-r4/probeC-r4-6.json: "stuckDrag": { beforeTouch "#7e93a4", midTouch "#9badbb", afterCancel "#9badbb", afterHoverOnly "#000509", dragStuckAfterCancel true } with CONTROL "control": { base "#a7b7c4", after "#a7b7c4", changed false }. `grep -nE "pointercancel|lostpointercapture|releasePointerCapture" MiniColorPicker.vue` → no matches, while `grep -rn "pointercancel\|lostpointercapture" demo/` returns 5 other sites including demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue:18-19 — the same SV-canvas widget, with both handlers.
defects.mechanism: Pointer-session state cleared by one of its terminators instead of by the session; hand-rolled duplicate of an in-tree component that already solves it.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/probe-C-r4-6.mjs against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000 — no fixture. Sequence: open /#/browse → click ⋮ Filters → click the swatch → CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent touchStart(12,12) → touchMove(30,30) → touchCancel[] → then eleven page.mouse.move across the canvas with no button held. Colour moves #9badbb → #000509. Control: identical eleven hover moves after a clean pointerup → unchanged.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-rolled pointer machine rather than patching it: either consume demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue (already correct, already in-tree) or express the drag with @vueuse/core (already a dependency — glass-ui's own Input uses useVModel) so the flag is owned by the pointer session. If the hand-rolled form is kept, @pointerup, @pointercancel and @lostpointercapture must all clear it, with `e.buttons !== 0` in updateCanvas as the belt.

defects.defect: `onPickerHexUpdate` writes BOTH `pickerHex` and `colorText` unconditionally on every `update:hex`, and MiniColorPicker emits that from a `watch` on a `computed` — i.e. once per reactive tick of a drag, not once at commit. The user's typed query is silently destroyed by touching the picker. There is no history and the picker has no cancel.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178 (`colorText.value = hex`) bound at :70; MiniColorPicker.vue:105 `watch(currentHex, (hex) => emit("update:hex", hex))`. Measured, evidence-r4/probeC-r4-2.json: "clobber": { typed "rebeccapurple", beforeDrag "rebeccapurple", afterDrag "#081f33", clobbered true }. Rate measured at evidence-r4/probeC-r4-3.json "churn": 41 emissions for 41 pointermoves.
defects.mechanism: One ref serving two disagreeing roles (user query vs. swatch readout); a live writeback loop with no authored-text guard.
defects.reproduction: node .../probes/probe-C-r4-2.mjs — no fixture. Open /#/browse → ⋮ → fill the colour field with `rebeccapurple` → click the swatch → one SV-canvas drag. Field reads `#081f33`.
defects.proposedCure: Split the two roles. `pickerHex` is the picker's value (swatch + picker bind to it); `colorText` is the user's query, written by the user and by `applyColorSearchFromPicker` (:180-187) only — that is the explicit commit where overwriting is the user's own instruction. Delete the single line `colorText.value = hex;` from `onPickerHexUpdate`. This also deletes 41 of the 41 spurious writes behind C-30.

defects.defect: `applyColorSearch` guards the imported total CSS parser with `/^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i` and silently substitutes `pickerHex` for everything else, then sets `colorSearchActive = true` so the badge asserts a filter is applied. defects.defect: `colorSearch: [L, a, b]` emits three positional numbers with no radius and no verb, so nothing in the component's surface distinguishes 'ask the server' from 'filter what is already loaded'. The sole consumer implements it as an in-memory filter over the already-fetched page, hardcodes `radius = 0.15`, and drops any palette whose `oklabColors` is missing or empty — while the server route that does this properly exists and goes unused. Under a header reading 'Discover palettes from the community' and a field reading 'Search the commons…', the colour filter can only subtract from what is already on screen.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:159 (emit shape). demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:336-355 — `const radius = 0.15;` and `if (!oklabColors || oklabColors.length === 0) return false;` with the comment 'API also supports server-side via colorL/colorA/colorB params, but client-side is instant'. The unused route: api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:89-92 declares colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius; api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:155-167 implements the matcher with the same 0.15 default.
defects.mechanism: An emit contract too thin to carry the query's intent, letting the consumer silently downgrade a search into a page filter.
defects.reproduction: Source-level, verified by grep and read. NOT measurable end-to-end in this environment: the dev server has no VITE_API_URL and the production API's CORS allow-list excludes localhost, so the wall is empty (evidence-r4/probeC-r4-1.json wallBefore.cards 0 / wallAfter.cards 0; in-page fetch('/colors/palettes?limit=20') returned index.html). The oklabColors-drop blast radius is therefore labelled a HYPOTHESIS pending a reachable API.
defects.proposedCure: Emit the query rather than the coordinates: `colorSearch: [query: { L: number; a: number; b: number; radius: number }]`, and have the consumer pass it as server query params, which the API already accepts. The client-side filter then becomes an optimistic pre-filter while the round-trip lands, instead of the whole feature.

result.strongestDefect: C-23 — the stuck drag. It is the strongest not because it is the costliest (C-15 is: on a phone the whole Find-by-Color section is 92.7px off the device and the Search button cannot be clicked) nor the most embarrassing (C-2/§1.3 is: a component that imports a total CSS parser, guards it with a six-digit-hex regex, and returns the wrong answer for 11 of 13 inputs while reporting success for 13 of 13). It is the strongest on three grounds. (1) It breaks the causal contract of a pointer UI: every other defect here produces a wrong answer to something the user did; C-23 produces one from something the user did not do — after a cancelled gesture, hovering with no button held drove the colour #9badbb → #000509 and, via update:hex → onPickerHexUpdate, rewrote both the search field's text and the value the next Search press sends. (2) It has a clean control: dragStuckAfterCancel true against control.changed false, same eleven moves, same canvas, same session — no alternative explanation to argue about, unlike the geometry findings whose severity depends on a viewport. (3) The cure is already in this tree, in the same widget, and was dropped on the way past: demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue is an SV spectrum canvas that calls setPointerCapture at :148 and handles @pointercancel (:18) and @lostpointercapture (:19), written for exactly this failure on iOS Safari; four other demo/ sites handle pointercancel too. MiniColorPicker is a hand-rolled second implementation with the recovery absent. The three findings compound: C-23 lets a hover change the searched colour, C-24 lets that change eat the typed query, §1.3 and C-19 make it impossible to tell which colour was actually searched, and C-7 is why none of it was caught.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. The negative proof I do owe is §4 of the report, where nine hypotheses drawn from the brief's own hazard list were probed and KILLED rather than shipped: (1) defineModel stale-read hazard ABSENT — grep over both files returns no matches; all state is local refs. (2) PRM-RAF / leak surface ABSENT — grep for requestAnimationFrame|setTimeout|setInterval|addEventListener|*Observer|onUnmounted over both files returns NO MATCHES AT ALL; zero cleanup surface, which is the right amount. (3) "label rows are decorative" FALSE — CDP reports nameFrom "relatedElement" for all five radios, and clicking the word "Most Popular" at (568.7, 514.4) moved aria-checked; the 31px row is a correctly built control. (4) RadioGroupItem value="" never checks: FALSE — freshOpen.buttons[3] is { role radio, checked "true", state "checked" }, named "All". (5) nested Popover breaks the outer: FALSE — dialogCount 2 with outer surviving, Escape closes mini then outer, focus restored to the ⋮ trigger. (6) miniPickerOpen leaks across an outer close: FALSE — leakOnReopen { outer true, miniStillOpen false }. (7) the live parseCssColor crash class reaches this component: NO — thirteen inputs including #gggggg, NaN, #00000 and oklch(0.7 0.1 30) produced pageErrors [] in every probe; the unflattering reason is that §1.3's regex means the parser is never called, so curing §1.3 PUTS this component on the crash path and the cure must land with tryParse-shaped error handling. (8) "no .shadow-cartoon-md rule exists in any stylesheet" UNPROVEN BY MY OWN INSTRUMENT and RETRACTED — my CSSOM walk returned [] for rules that demonstrably apply (p0Rules [], pxOverlay [], h8 [] while measured padding is 20.352px 16px and measured width is 32px), so sheet.cssRules is silently failing on the Vite-served sheets; C-17 survives only on glass-ui source (.shadow-cartoon-md is @layer components, not @utility, three lines above @utility shadow-cartoon-hover) plus byte-identical rest/hover box-shadow. (9) overflow:clip breaks caret scrolling: FALSE — scrollLeft 234 at End, 0 at Home. Additionally, 3 of the 10 strictTemplates errors in this component pair are classified as FALSE POSITIVES (aria-label and onKeydown on Input, onClick on Button) because I measured all three working at runtime — they are glass-ui declaration gaps, not defects, and that ratio is itself the substance of relay item 5.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (the 1M-context arm), as declared at spawn. Seat declared, not inherited, not defaulted.
result.strongestDefect: P4-B4 — the component is a MENU BUILT OUT OF A FORM. glass-ui's `.radio-group` already solves PR-12 correctly (`--radio-face: 18px` optics, `--radio-seat: 44px` target, `margin: -13px` collapsing the seat, `gap: calc(44px - 18px)` so pitch == seat). SearchFilterBar interposes a `<label class="filter-option">` between the group and each item, so the producer's 26px gap now separates 30.94px TEXT ROWS instead of 18px circles. Measured: Sort/Tier pitch 56.93px for a 30.94px row (45.7% dead space, exactly 30.94 + 26.00), while the component's own hand-written Tags list is 32.94px — ONE 240px MENU, TWO RHYTHMS DIFFERING BY 1.73x. The same producer property (`align-items: flex-start`, right for bare circles) makes the rows shrink-to-fit: label widths 61.14 / 121.42 / 132.92 / 159.69 / 165.44px in a 182px column (2.71x max/min), so the hover fill AND the click target are a different width on every row, while every tag row is a constant 182px. This one structural decision produces most of the visible ugliness and is what forces the menu to 632.63px, which is what pushes `Find by Color` and `Clear all filters` below the fold.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Five sub-axes were attacked and could not be broken, and are recorded as negative proofs in §10 of the report so the next pass does not re-spend the budget: (1) the radios DO paint a focus register — the ring is on the `.radio-group__face` child (`box-shadow: color(srgb 0.665504 …/0.3) 0 0 0 2px, … 0 0 8px 0`, `faceHasRing: true`, Chromium, real Tab and ArrowDown), which OVERTURNS pass 3's P3-M14 and withdraws my own first reading; (2) Escape DOES restore focus to the trigger (`focusAfterEscape.isTrigger: true`, both engines); (3) `--leading-small` is NOT a dead `@theme inline` token — it resolves to `1.4` live, and `--font-serif` resolves to Plus Jakarta Sans, so the `.filter-option` recipe is correct; (4) the badge does NOT overflow at two digits (`scrollWidth 16 == clientWidth 16`); (5) opening MiniColorPicker does NOT clobber typed input (`clobberedOnOpen: false`). Motion is also clean: tokenised to `--duration-fast`/`--ease-standard`, no layout-forcing property animated, and `prefers-reduced-motion` reaches Tailwind's `animate-spin` (`animation-duration: 0.00001s`, `iteration-count: 1`).

defects.defect: The Tags filter is decorative — it speaks a producer API glass-ui 7 does not have, so the checkbox flips visually while the application model never moves and the wall is never filtered. A surface asserting a selection the product does not hold.

The rows are menu rows, not form controls: adopt the producer's `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` / `DropdownMenuRadioItem` (already re-exported in demo/ui/) and delete the `.filter-option` recipe, the interposed <label> and both RadioGroups. That single transposition also retires P4-B4, P4-M4, P4-M5, P4-M7, P4-m1, P4-m2, P4-m3.

SearchFilterBar.vue:22-26 inserts `<label class="filter-option">` between group and item. Measured (evidence-p4/p4-2.json): Sort/Tier row height 30.94, pitch 56.93 (= 30.94 + 26.00, 45.7% dead); Tags row height 30.94, pitch 32.94. 56.93/32.94 = 1.73x. Label widths (evidence-p4/p4-3.json): All 61.14, Newest 121.42, Featured 132.92, Most Forked 159.69, Most Popular 165.44 in a 182px column (2.71x); every tag row 182.00.

defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-2.mjs then probe-P4-3.mjs; frame evidence-p4/p4-popover-full-tall.png shows Newest/Most Popular/Most Forked floating apart while pastel/neon/earth are packed, and the hovered `All` pill stopping a third of the way across the menu.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a spacing patch: replace both RadioGroups with the producer's menu primitives, which own full-bleed rows, one indicator gutter, one focus register, roving focus, typeahead and an accessible name from the row's own text. Delete `.filter-option` and the <label> entirely.

defects.defect: "Search by CSS color" accepts exactly `#RRGGBB` out of the whole CSS colour grammar, advertises `hsl(...)` in its own placeholder, and silently searches the swatch colour for everything else — with byte-identical feedback for garbage and for the product's own `oklch()`. The library under audit is a CSS colour parser and its own parser is already imported into this file.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:218 `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;` against aria-label "Search by CSS color" (line 93) and placeholder "#hex, hsl(...)" (line 92), with `parseColorIn` imported at line 145 and used only at line 206 after the regex has discarded the input. evidence-p4/p4-5.json: six syntaxes (`rebeccapurple`, `hsl(200 80% 50%)`, `oklch(0.72 0.14 244)`, `#f00`, `not-a-color`, `#4488CC`) all → searched `#4488cc`, aria-invalid null, no error text, liveRegions [], no page error.
defects.mechanism: capability-narrower-than-the-affordance-advertises + no invalid state at all
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-5.mjs — the six-row truth table in evidence-p4/p4-5.json `colorInputTruth`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the regex. `parseColorIn(text, "oklab")` inside try/catch; on failure set aria-invalid and render the producer's field-error affordance; on success mirror the parsed colour back into the swatch so the instrument shows what it understood. Move the whole colour instrument out of the 240px popover into the search bar beside the query, where a colour string has room.

defects.defect: The active-filter count renders as a gold crescent with no digit — clipped by the producer button's own `contain: paint` — and it is the ONLY signal that filters are active: the count is absent from the accessible name, there is no live region, and the wall shows no filter chips.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:7-12 absolutely positions the badge at `-right-1 -top-1` inside the trigger. evidence-p4/p4-7.json: `triggerContain: "paint"`, `triggerOverflow: "visible"`, badge 16x16 at (661,382.36) vs trigger 32x40 at (641,386.36) — 4px clipped on the top and inline-end edges (>=43.75% of area) before the `border-radius: 9999px` ellipse is considered. Frame: evidence-p4/p4-adj-badge-chromium.png (DPR 3) shows a gold sliver, no digit. evidence-p4/p4-2.json `triggerAccNameIncludesCount: false`; evidence-p4/p4-5.json liveRegions [].
defects.mechanism: consumer-overhang-inside-a-producer-paint-containment-boundary
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-7-adjudicate.mjs — sets tier=Featured, closes the menu, measures and crops the trigger in WebKit and Chromium at DPR 3.
defects.proposedCure: The count does not belong inside the producer's contained button. Render applied filters as named removable chips beside the search field — one object that is simultaneously the count, the Clear-all affordance, the polite status announcement and the accessible name.

defects.defect: The menu overruns the viewport in every arm with `max-height: none` and `overflow: visible`, so the entire `Find by Color` section and the entire `Clear all filters` row are unreachable — and it is portalled/fixed, so document scroll cannot reach them either.
defects.evidence: `PopoverContent class="w-60 p-0"` (SearchFilterBar.vue:16) declares no height contract. evidence-p4/p4-2.json: desktop 1440x900 popover 240x632.63, bottom 1012.63 → 112.63px below the fold; with the Clear-all row 685.63 → 165.63px; mobile 390x844 → 123.32px; narrow 320x568 → 294.84px (47.6% of the menu); 200% zoom → 480x1265.5, bottom 1287.5 (387.5px below) AND right 1511 > 1440. `Find by Color` top 903.72, `Clear all filters` top 1000.28.
defects.mechanism: unbounded-overlay-height (no max-height, no scroller) compounded by a body that spends 337.82px / 53.4% of its height on five exclusive choices
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-2.mjs — arms A (desktop populated + active), B (mobile390 / narrow320), F (zoom200) in evidence-p4/p4-2.json.
defects.proposedCure: Give the popover a viewport-bounded `max-height` plus `overflow-y: auto` on the content with the producer's fading-scroll affordance — but first shrink the body: after P4-B4's transposition and P4-B5's removal of the colour instrument the menu is three short lists and the height contract becomes routine rather than a redesign.

defects.defect: The designed pending state is structurally unreachable — `applyColorSearch` is `async` but its body is fully synchronous, so Vue never flushes a render with `searching === true`. The spinner branch and every `disabled:` utility hanging off it are dead code.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 (no await between `searching.value = true` and the `finally` that clears it); line 102 `<Loader2 v-if="searching" class="animate-spin">`; line 99 `disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:pointer-events-none`. evidence-p4/p4-4.json: WebKit 68 frames / Chromium 84 frames sampled across 700ms after a real click — `mutationCount: 0`, `spinnerEverPresent: false`, `disabledEverTrue: false` in both. BrowsePane.vue:351-355 confirms no request is issued at all.
defects.mechanism: loading-state-for-an-operation-with-no-latency; the operation that DOES have scope (a client-side filter over the <=50 loaded rows) has no state at all
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-4.mjs — the `searchingPaint` block instruments the Search button with rAF sampling and a MutationObserver.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `searching` ref, the Loader2 branch and the disabled utilities. If the colour filter should query the commons (PALETTE-CONTRACT §1 puts colour-distance on the wire), make it a real request and give it a real pending + failure state that is not carried by motion alone.

defects.defect: Three per-instance overrides are declared and all three are defeated by the producer: `variant="ghost"` lands as an inert DOM attribute while the button paints `data-emphasis="secondary"` (the default), `h-8`/`h-7` lose to the producer's min-height, and `p-0` loses to the producer's padding. The residue is a 32x40 ellipse in a 36px field and a `Clear all filters` button that is the loudest object in the menu.
defects.evidence: evidence-p4/p4-7.json, identical in WebKit and Chromium: rendered attributes `data-slot=button data-emphasis=secondary data-tone=neutral data-size=md data-icon-only=true … variant=ghost`. Computed `height: 40px, min-height: 40px` against declared `h-8` (32px); `Clear all filters` declared `h-7` (28px) renders 36px (evidence-p4/p4-2.json); PopoverContent declared `p-0` computes `20.351999px 16px`. `w-8` succeeds where `h-8` fails, breaking `data-icon-only`'s square contract → 32x40 with `border-radius: 9999px` = an ellipse.
defects.mechanism: per-instance-override-vs-root-styling (owner edict 5) — the consumer reaches past the root, the root wins, and the leftover is a broken aspect
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-7-adjudicate.mjs (`trigger.attrs`); crops evidence-p4/trigger-safari-desktop-{light,dark}.png show the resulting lozenge breaking the field pill by 2.00px top and bottom (measured evidence-p4/p4-1.json).
defects.proposedCure: Consume the producer's size/emphasis API (`size`, `emphasis`) rather than Tailwind height/padding classes, and let `icon-only` keep its square. If a ghost emphasis is wanted, add or fix it in glass-ui — edict 4 — not by writing `variant` on a component that does not read it.

defects.defect: The colour field cannot render its own placeholder, let alone a colour value: 65px of usable text width for a placeholder needing 123.94px and a representative value needing 177.05px.
defects.evidence: evidence-p4/p4-2.json `placeholderFits`: clientWidth 145, paddingLeft 16, paddingRight 64 (`pr-16`) → 65px usable; `#hex, hsl(...)` needs 123.94px (truncated to 52.4%); `oklch(0.72 0.14 244)` needs 177.05px (2.72x). Renders as `#hex, …` in evidence-p4/p4-webkit-light-open-crop.png and p4-popover-full-tall.png. Budget: 240px popover − 2x16 producer padding − 2x12 section padding = 184px; 28px swatch + 6px gap = 34; pr-16 reserves 64px for a 52.59px overlay button.
defects.mechanism: an-instrument-sized-smaller-than-its-own-data (44% of the field reserved for the word "Search", 45% for the colour)
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-2.mjs — `placeholderFits` measures the placeholder and a canonical oklch value against the live computed font.
defects.proposedCure: Move the colour instrument out of the 240px popover into the search bar beside the query, and stop overlaying a word-labelled button inside the field — commit on Enter, with the swatch as the visible echo of what was parsed.

defects.defect: Three rendered `border-bottom` dividers where the binding register says the divider count is zero, duplicating a boundary already carried by a labelled section and 12px of padding — and they are the heaviest ink in the menu.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:17 `class="divide-y divide-border"`. evidence-p4/p4-2.json: `border-bottom: 1px rgb(198, 180, 159)` on the Sort, Tier and Tags sections (4 with the Clear-all row). Authorities: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:49 PR-05 REMOVE, "every other divider/ornament is zero"; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:92 "every other composition retains no divider"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:69 §5.4 "Spacing plus material already expressing the same boundary makes the line duplicative."
defects.mechanism: double-encoded-boundary (label + interval + rule)
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-2.mjs — the `sections` array in evidence-p4/p4-2.json; visible in evidence-p4/p4-popover-full-tall.png.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `divide-y divide-border`. Once the rows adopt the producer's menu primitives the section boundary is carried by the label plus the producer's own group interval, which is what the register intends.

defects.defect: The tag list is a fractional 3.4-of-12-row window with no fade, no count, no name, no role, and `tabIndex -1` on a scrollable region — so it is not keyboard-operable and slices a row through its x-height.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:49 `max-h-28 overflow-y-auto scrollbar-thin`. evidence-p4/p4-2.json `tagScroller`: maxHeight 112px, clientHeight 112, scrollHeight 400, scrollable true, tabIndex -1, role null, ariaLabel null, tagCount 12. 112 / 32.94 = 3.4 rows. Frame evidence-p4/p4-popover-full-tall.png shows `monochrome` cut through its x-height with a full-strength divider immediately below.
defects.mechanism: magic-height-window without the affordances the app already owns (`pane-scroll-fade`, glass-ui `fading-scroll`) and without WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard operability
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-2.mjs (stubbed 12-tag catalogue via the LAN origin) — the `tagScroller` block.
defects.proposedCure: Either show the whole list inside the menu's own bounded scroller (P4-B3's height contract) with a named, focusable region and a count, or — better — move tag selection out of a 112px keyhole into a named filter surface with search, since a growing tag catalogue is exactly what a 3.4-row window cannot serve.

defects.defect: In WebKit, Tab reaches 3 of 17 controls and then leaves the open role="dialog": the entire Tags section, the colour swatch and the Search button are unreachable by keyboard. Chromium traps focus and reaches all 17.
defects.evidence: evidence-p4/p4-4.json `tabSequence`, 22 consecutive Tab presses from a freshly-opened menu. WebKit: radio → radio → input[Search by CSS color] → OUT at press 4 (`tabLeftPopoverAtIndex: 3`). Chromium: radio → radio → 12x checkbox → swatch → input → Search → cycles at index 17, never leaves (`tabLeftPopoverAtIndex: -1`, `popoverStillOpenAfterEscapingTab: true`).
defects.mechanism: HYPOTHESIS for the WebKit cause — the radios ARE reached so it is not the plain "buttons are not tabbable" default, and I did not isolate it. The design consequence does not depend on the mechanism: a 17-control menu assembled from bare producer primitives declares no traversal contract of its own and behaves differently in the two engines the product ships to (the whole shipped visual matrix is Safari).
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-4.mjs — section 2, both engines.
defects.proposedCure: Adopting the producer's menu primitives replaces ad-hoc Tab traversal with a real roving-focus composite that owns its own contract in both engines; verify with a rendered cross-engine witness rather than a Chromium-only pass.

defects.defect: All 17 option controls and both groups are nameless to assistive technology — the menu announces "radio button, not checked" five times and "checkbox, not checked" twelve times inside two groups that announce no purpose.
defects.evidence: evidence-p4/p4-2.json / p4-1.json: 5x [role=radio] accessible name null, 12x [role=checkbox] accessible name null, 2x [role=radiogroup] aria-label null / aria-labelledby null. Mechanism: SearchFilterBar.vue:22-26,50-57 wrap a producer `<button role="radio">` in a `<label>` with no `for`; per HTML-AAM a button's name comes from its subtree contents (empty) then title — the wrapping label is not consulted, and the visible text is a sibling <span>. Authority: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 §4.1 — states are never colour-only; role, accessible name and state must be explicit.
defects.mechanism: label-wrapping-a-button does not name it (only input/select/textarea/meter/progress/output take a wrapping label's name)
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-1.mjs — the `focusables` array; and probe-P4-2.mjs `rows[].controlAccName` / `radiogroupNames` / `checkboxNames`.
defects.proposedCure: Producer menu items take their name from their own row text. Until then the four decorative lucide glyphs on nameless rows also fail PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 §5.5 and should go with the label.

defects.defect: In RTL the count chip flips into the search field's text area instead of the button's outer corner, because the offsets are physical rather than logical.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:9 `absolute -right-1 -top-1`. evidence-p4/p4-3.json under dir=rtl: trigger 767.5→799.5, badge 787.5→803.5, field 754→1216; `badgeOutsideTriggerInlineEnd: false`, `badgeOverlapsFieldInterior: true`. Authority: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:150 §6.1 — "chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document." The same run records `triggerOverflowsFieldBlock: {top: 2, bottom: 2}` — the lozenge is direction-independent.
defects.mechanism: physical-inset-in-direction-following-chrome
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-3.mjs — section B sets dir=rtl, applies a tier, closes the menu and measures; crop evidence-p4/p4-rtl-badge-crop.png.
defects.proposedCure: Logical insets throughout. The deeper point is that no state in this component was authored against a direction — the RTL arm belongs in the state matrix, not in a follow-up.

defects.defect: Under forced colors every producer-owned part adapts and every hand-rolled part does not: the dividers keep their author tan, the row hover (the menu's only hover cue) resolves to an author colour, the inline Search keeps author beige/brown, and the one data-bearing colour — the swatch — has no `forced-color-adjust` declaration so its survival is engine-dependent.
defects.evidence: evidence-p4/p4-2.json (`forcedColors: "active"`, WebKit): popover → rgb(255,255,255) / border rgb(0,0,0) [producer, adapts]; radio face/checked/focus → ButtonText / Highlight / 2px Highlight outline [producer @media (forced-colors: active) block in radio-group/styles.css, adapts]; `sectionBorderBottom: "1px rgb(198, 180, 159)"` [consumer, does not]; `hoverMixResolves: "color(srgb 0.874 0.8254 0.766 / 0.5)"` [consumer, does not]; swatch bg stays rgb(68,136,204) in WebKit while pass 3 measured Chromium forcing it to rgb(255,255,255). Frame: evidence-p4/p4-forced-open-crop.png.
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled-surfaces-outside-the-producer's-forced-colors-contract
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-2.mjs — arm D; and probe-P4-6.mjs for the swatch pixel crop.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-rolled surfaces (dividers, hover recipe, inline Search) so the producer's forced-colors handling applies by construction, and declare `forced-color-adjust: none` on the swatch alone, since it is the one element whose colour IS the datum.

defects.defect: Three type roles sit outside the constitution's closed matrix: mono-caption used as a section heading, `text-micro` (11px) on the badge and the inline Search label, and `text-caption` on the mini-picker readout.
defects.evidence: evidence-p4/p4-1.json `labels`: SORT/TIER/FIND BY COLOR render Fira Code 14.384px uppercase, letter-spacing 1.4384px (glass-ui `.section-label` = `@apply text-mono-caption`). evidence-p4/p4-1.json `searchBtn.fontSize: "11px"`, badge `fontSize: "11px"`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:68-78 §4 closes the matrix at display / --type-title / --type-subheading / text-heading / text-prose / text-small / text-mono-small|mono-caption, and reserves mono for "value, code, or provenance".
defects.mechanism: out-of-register-type-role — `.section-label` is a 12-site repo idiom, so this is a family row and this component is one of its sites
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P4-1.mjs — the `labels` and `searchBtn` blocks.
defects.proposedCure: Section headings take `text-heading` (Plus Jakarta Sans). The `text-micro` uses disappear with the badge and the inline Search button under the §12 cure. The `.section-label` family belongs in a separate register row, not a local patch.

defects.defect: One filter model, two owners: `colorSearchActive` is component-local while `colorSearchParams` lives in the parent, so `activeFilterCount` mixes parent-owned truth with a child-local shadow and any parent-side clear leaves the badge lit. Plus a single-child flex wrapper and an inline `<button>` with no `type`.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:171 `const colorSearchActive = ref(false)` and :189-195 `activeFilterCount` reads it alongside the `tier`/`selectedTags` props, while BrowsePane.vue:336 owns `colorSearchParams`. SearchFilterBar.vue:2 `<div class="flex items-center gap-1.5">` wraps exactly one child. SearchFilterBar.vue:97 the inline Search button declares no `type` (defaults to submit) twenty lines below a swatch that correctly declares `type="button"`.
defects.mechanism: split-state-ownership + KISS residue
defects.reproduction: NONE for the badge-latch path (source read; the parent currently has no independent clear path, so it is a latent inconsistency rather than a live one). The wrapper and the missing `type` are direct source facts at the cited lines.
defects.proposedCure: Lift `colorSearchActive` to the parent so one component owns the whole filter model and the count is derivable from it; delete the single-child wrapper; and let §12's chip summary own the count so the question of who holds it stops arising.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context Opus 5). Matches the explicit spawn declaration; the seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-17 — a drag-to-reorder performed while the search box is non-empty silently rewrites the order of palettes the user cannot see and did not touch. `PalettesPane.vue:190-194` derives `ids` from `pm.filteredSaved.value` (a projection) and hands it to `usePaletteStore.reorderPalettes`, whose contract requires a TOTAL ordering and which completes any partial one by appending the remainder to the tail. Reproduced live at http://localhost:9000 this session: seeded A,B,C,D,E; filtered to "e" (beta/delta/epsilon visible); dragged one slot; localStorage persisted D,B,E,A,C — alpha and gamma flung from positions 1 and 3 to the tail. Correct result is A,D,B,C,E. This is a second, independent mechanism from L-1 and it survives every cure proposed for L-1 (including swapping in glass-ui's SortableList), because the defect is in WHICH list is reordered, not in how the drag is bound.

defects.defect: Drag-to-reorder under an active search filter silently rewrites the stored order of palettes the user cannot see. The pane hands a filtered projection to `reorderPalettes`, a TOTAL reordering primitive that completes any partial ordering by appending the remainder to the tail.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:190-194 (`const ids = pm.filteredSaved.value.map(p => p.id); … pm.reorderPalettes(ids)`) vs demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:153-166 (`// Append any palettes not in the ordered list` loop). Live probe output, HEAD 9268f054: {"seedOrder":["A(alpha)","B(beta)","C(gamma)","D(delta)","E(epsilon)"],"filter":"e","visibleNames":["beta","delta","epsilon"],"afterDragWithinFilter":["D","B","E","A","C"],"intended":["A","D","B","C","E"]}
defects.mechanism: Ownership of list ORDER is split: the store owns the array but exposes only a total-permutation API, while the view owns the gesture and can only see a projection. No type expresses the totality precondition, so a filtered view silently violates it.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/live3.mjs — headless Chromium against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000; page.addInitScript seeds localStorage["color-palettes"] with five local palettes A..E; navigate /#/palettes; fill input[placeholder="Search your palettes..."] with "e"; retrieve the app's own Sortable instance off .palette-card-grid via Object.keys(grid).find(k=>k.startsWith("Sortable")) and invoke options.onUpdate then options.onEnd with {oldIndex:0,newIndex:1}; read localStorage back. Persisted D,B,E,A,C.
defects.proposedCure: Retire `reorderPalettes(orderedIds: string[])` entirely — it is the wrong primitive because it makes every caller responsible for a totality the type system never states. Replace with a RELATIVE move the store can always satisfy against its own source array: `movePalette(id: string, before: string | null)`. The view supplies two identities from the gesture; the store performs one splice on `store.value.palettes`. A projection can correctly express "put A before C" even when B is filtered out, which a permutation structurally cannot. This transposition also subsumes L-1's cure.

defects.defect: Drag-to-reorder with no filter persists a corrupted order. A dereferenced computed is passed as useSortable's list argument, so vueuse's default `onUpdate` (which the custom `onEnd` does not override — different keys in the options spread) splices the computed's live cached array in place before `onEnd` reads it.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:183 `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, {…})`. node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js: `const defaultOptions = { onUpdate: e => moveArrayElement(list, e.oldIndex, e.newIndex, e) }; sortable = new Sortable(target, {...defaultOptions, ...resetOptions})` and `const _valueIsRef = isRef(list); const array = _valueIsRef ? [...toValue(list)] : toValue(list)` — no copy, no write-back when not a ref. Live probe at HEAD 9268f054: {"hasDefaultOnUpdate":true,"hasOnEnd":true,"handle":".drag-handle","cards":3,"before":["A","B","C"],"afterDrag_0_to_2":["C","B","A"],"expected":["B","C","A"]}. Isolated repro against the real moveArrayElement: onEnd sees [B,C] (A already spliced out); ids handed to reorderPalettes = ["C","B"].
defects.mechanism: Same root as L-17 — the view owns reorder state against a derived projection instead of the store owning it against the source. Compounded by mutating a Vue `computed`'s cache from outside (useFilteredList.ts:9 returns `items.value` by reference when the query is empty).
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/live.mjs — seed A,B,C in localStorage["color-palettes"], load /#/palettes, invoke the live Sortable instance's options.onUpdate then options.onEnd with {oldIndex:0,newIndex:2}, read localStorage: C,B,A. Expected B,C,A. Also reproduced in isolation with node scratchpad/probe.mjs importing the real `moveArrayElement` from @vueuse/integrations against exact copies of usePaletteStore/useFilteredList.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-rolled binding rather than repair it. glass-ui 7.0.0 already publishes ./sortable-list (SortableList/SortableItem/SortableHandle, verified present at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/sortable-list.js), so PaletteCardGrid renders <SortableList> and emits @reorder; the pane stops importing @vueuse/integrations/useSortable, and sortablejs + @types/sortablejs leave the tree. Pair with L-17's `movePalette(id, before)` — SortableList alone does not close L-17.

defects.defect: The owner-RULED (Q5, T-43 owner-CONFIRMS) 'Palettes' letterform ramp is measurably dead in dark scheme: the three stops collapse to a near-white monochrome. The invariant has no owner because the concept is split across three modules — the producer writes one token namespace, the CSS recipe reads another, and a FEATURE PANE is the inline-style adapter between them.
defects.evidence: Measured on :root at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, two contexts differing only in colorScheme. LIGHT: oklch(47.119% 0.188448 329.834), oklch(47.119% 0.188448 9.834), oklch(47.119% 0.124865 49.834) → rgb(144,32,140) (170,0,67) (144,65,0). DARK: oklch(95.832% 0.033662 329.834), oklch(95.832% 0.021053 9.834), oklch(95.832% 0.023120 49.834) → rgb(255,234,252) (255,236,238) (255,237,228) — spread ΔR=0, ΔG=3, ΔB=24 of 255; chroma collapse 5.6×/8.9×/5.4×. result.negativeProof:
The challenge's headline hypothesis — that the demo imports the library through paths a real consumer could not write — is DISPROVEN at runtime, and I verified it independently at HEAD 9268f054 rather than inheriting the prior passes' claim.

(1) Exhaustive census: `grep -rho '@mkbabb/value\.js[a-z/]*' demo/ | sort | uniq -c` → 25 /color, 10 /css, 6 /math, 5 /easing, 4 /quantize = 50 sites, and every one of those five specifiers is a key in package.json#exports. `grep -rn '@src/|from "\.\./\.\./src/|value\.js/src' demo/` → no matches. `grep -rn '@mkbabb/value\.js"' demo/` → one hit, demo/shared/utils.ts:16, which is prose in a comment, not an import. Zero deep imports, zero dist/ imports, zero root-barrel imports. A real consumer could write all 50.

(2) The Vite alias set cannot drift from the export map because it is GENERATED from it — vite.config.ts:37-50 reads this repo's own package.json#exports at config time and derives one anchored-regex alias per subpath. The anchoring is load-bearing (the comment at :30-36 records the R-era boot break caused by the prefix-matching string form).

(3) PalettesPane.vue itself imports nothing from @mkbabb/value.js at all; the library enters its closure only through ../color-session/* and ./mix.ts, both via bare subpaths.

(4) demo/palettes/api/index.ts:1-19 documents a genuinely clean layering: generic HTTP transport, session lifecycle and colour-naming were split OUT of the palettes api capsule into platform/transport, platform/auth and color-session, with no forwarding re-exports surviving. I confirmed demo/platform/transport/ holds exactly api-problem.ts, availability.ts, client.ts, useApiClient.ts.

(5) ../color-session/keys (PalettesPane.vue:135) is a correct cross-area edge: colour state is genuinely owned by color-session, the key module is a type-only leaf, 26 consumers, no cycle. This is the pattern the palettes area should adopt for its own keys.

(6) I re-verified the prior pass's three load-bearing claims rather than trusting them: glass-ui 7.0.0 does publish ./sortable-list (dist/sortable-list.js present); dist/subpaths/*.js has zero external imports (only ../anchors-*, ../operations-*, ../result-*); and dist/index.d.ts, dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts and dist/subpaths/units.d.ts are all absent. All three CONFIRMED.

So the demo does not reach into src/, and what it does import it imports legitimately. The defects are all on the other side of the boundary — the published surface is incomplete (no "." export), the demo's type config is both over- and under-declared (L-21), the manifest over-specifies runtime deps, and the one domain this component exists to demonstrate (Palette) is the one the library does not own.

defects.defect: CORRECTION to pass 2: its Part III explains its own measured `{"t":"Publish","disabled":false}` as 'the latch is applied only on the saved-Publish item (:30)' — but MixSourceSelector renders `saved`-kind palettes, so the item measured IS the :28-32 saved-Publish item, and that item DOES carry `:disabled="apiOffline"`. defects.defect: Dual export implementation, and the SHIPPED path is the legacy one. 914 lines of contract-authoritative, byte-exact serializers in `demo/palettes/export/` have zero runtime consumers; the five Export items this component renders route to the 132-line legacy `demo/palettes/export.ts`.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "export/serializers|export/json|export/css|export/png|export/svg|export/tailwind|export/reload|export/canonical|export/digest" demo src e2e` → ONE hit: `demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23`. Live route: PaletteCardMenu.vue:113-128 → PaletteCard @export → BrowsePane.vue:198/PalettesPane.vue:152 `usePaletteExport` → `usePaletteExport.ts:9` `from "./export"` = export.ts. Collateral: three homes for the filename-slug concept — `utils.ts:3` (NFKD, diacritic-stripping), `export.ts:9` (naive `[^a-z0-9]+`), `export/canonical.ts:52-59` `identifierPrefix`.
