defects.reproduction: grep -n "h-4 w-4\|w-3.5 h-3.5" demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue demo/palettes/browser/search/UserSortMenu.vue
defects.proposedCure: One producer-owned row-glyph rung for DropdownMenuItem; consumers pass no size class at all.

defects.defect: In the admin arm two irreversible actions at different authority scopes — `Delete` and `Delete (admin)` — share the same first letter, the same Trash2 glyph and the same measured ink, separated only by a label with no programmatic scope.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:133-140 and :163-169 (both `<Trash2 class="h-4 w-4"/>`, both `text-destructive focus:text-destructive`); the destructive class is inert with ΔRGB 0–1 in all five arms (probe-D11-pass3-results.json deleteVsRenameDelta: 1/0/1/1/0); the intervening DropdownMenuLabel at :155 has no role="group"/aria-labelledby (pass 2 P2-7, corroborated by probe-D10 parentOrder being flat).
defects.mechanism: Two commands differing in blast radius and authority agree in every rendered channel except a parenthetical, inside a group that is declared by comment and separator but never expressed structurally.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the typeahead consequence — the admin arm requires a signed-in admin against a live backend, which this seat did not have. The label/glyph/ink collision is source- and pixel-evidenced; the claim that reka's typeahead resolves `d` ambiguously between them is a labelled HYPOTHESIS.
defects.proposedCure: Elevated authority is communicated by labeling and scope (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7), so the admin arm needs a real DropdownMenuGroup with aria-labelledby and a distinct verb ("Remove as moderator" vs "Delete") — or, per D-1, admin actions belong in the Admin review suite rather than on a browse card.

defects.defect: Pass 2's dark-arm pixel measurement is instrument-invalid (light-mode polarity hard-coded), and correcting it shows D-2 is worse in dark than pass 2 reported: the destructive-vs-neutral ink delta is 0, not 11.
defects.evidence: probe-D8-pass2.mjs:96-104 — "darkest pixel inside a box = the ink". probe-D8-pass2-results.json .dark reported surface rgb(195,185,172), Rename ink rgb(74,63,55)/5.28, Delete rgb(81,69,61)/4.79, Δ=11, annotation 5.19. probe-D11-pass3-results.json .dark, polarity-agnostic: surface rgb(81,69,61), Rename ink rgb(233,230,226)/7.44, Delete rgb(233,230,226)/7.44, Δ=0, annotation 1.94. Pass 1 measured Delete color=rgb(233,230,226) in dark by computed style — agreeing with pass 3, not pass 2.
defects.mechanism: A contrast sampler that assumes ink is the darkest pixel inverts in dark mode, returning the surface as ink and vice versa. Pass 2's light arm is unaffected; its dark conclusions understated both the destructive-ink collapse and the annotation failure.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D11-pass3.mjs and compare to probe-D8-pass2-results.json .dark
defects.proposedCure: Evidence law for this formation: any rendered-pixel probe must derive polarity from the sampled region (surface = modal pixel, ink = the pixel furthest from it in luminance) rather than assuming it, and must assert the arm it claims to be in before sampling (probe-D11 records a mediaCheck block per arm).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (PalettesPane.vue), pass 3
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared seat, served tier matches the spawn declaration; not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-23/D-24/D-5 as one family: the component has ONE empty state where the domain has THREE. "No saved palettes yet. / Add colors above, then save the set." renders identically for (a) a genuinely empty library, (b) a filter that matched nothing while the header badge simultaneously reads 6, and (c) corrupt/unreadable localStorage — the arm VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 forbids by name ("It is never rendered as an empty library, silent reset..."). The two truths it cannot express are exactly the two where the user stands to lose data. Measured live: storedCount 6 / cardsRendered 0 / emptyStatus "No saved palettes yet."; and rawStillCorrupt "{{{not json" with the same empty invitation painted.
result.negativeProof: Ten attacks that did NOT break it, recorded so the next seat does not re-spend the probes: (1) zero horizontal overflow at 1440/720/RTL, at 6 and 40 palettes, with an 88-char name — matches REPORT.md overflowX 0 in all four matrices; (2) the count-badge a11y construction is correct — aria-hidden Badge + sr-only companion yields the heading name "My Palettes (6 saved)", not "My Palettes6"; (3) long names truncate with ellipsis, no layout break; (4) the delete-all row's `justify-end` is logical and mirrors correctly (x 1188 LTR → 224 RTL); (5) producer PRM IS honoured where the producer owns it — card and cast both compute `transition: … 0.1s` under reducedMotion:"reduce", isolating D-15 to this file's hand-passed Sortable options; (6) the EmptyState mark is §7-compliant (exactly three WatercolorDots + dashes, aria-hidden, static); (7) demo/ui/{card,button,badge} are clean one-line glass-ui re-exports — no local fork; (8) reorder DOES persist across reload once the probe stops re-seeding on navigation (pass 2's retraction of "lost on reload" is correct and I could not reproduce the loss either); (9) zero page errors and zero component console errors on /#/palettes in every run — the only console error is the dev VITE_API_URL banner; (10) corrupt bytes are not destroyed on read — localStorage still holds the original string after reload, so D-24 is a presentation + overwrite-risk defect, not immediate data loss.

defects.defect: The first drag-to-reorder of every session permutes the entire library. Two competing reorder authorities run on one gesture: vueuse's surviving defaultOptions.onUpdate (which splices a detached array snapshot AND physically re-parents a DOM node Vue's v-for owns) plus the component's own onEnd (which writes the store).
defects.evidence: probe4.mjs, 3 fresh WebKit contexts: `TEST1 run1/2/3: before=P1,P2,P3,P4,P5 after=P3,P4,P2,P5,P1 intended=P2,P3,P1,P4,P5 *** WRONG ***`; `TEST2 drag#2 -> P4,P2,P3,P5,P1 (correct)`. Mechanism pasted from node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:11-26 — `const defaultOptions = { onUpdate: (e) => moveArrayElement(list, ...) }` then `new Sortable(target, {...defaultOptions, ...resetOptions})`; PalettesPane.vue:183-197 passes onEnd, never onUpdate.
defects.mechanism: dual reorder path — a captured non-reactive computed snapshot plus a surviving library default that mutates DOM Vue owns
defects.reproduction: Seed 5 palettes in localStorage['color-palettes']; load /#/palettes; drag row 1's .drag-handle onto row 3; read localStorage. 3/3 deterministic. Independently replicated byte-for-byte against the pass-2 seat.
defects.proposedCure: Delete SortableJS from this component. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 already specifies reorder as a model verb (Space grabs, Up/Down move ordinal, Space drops, Escape cancels, every move announces `position of total`). A named <button> emitting move(id, delta) against the STORE's order — never a filtered projection, never a captured array — kills D-1, D-1b, D-9 and D-25 together and removes a dependency.

defects.defect: Reordering while a filter is active silently rewrites the global order of palettes the user cannot see: onEnd maps only filteredSaved ids and reorderPalettes hoists them to the front, appending everything else.
defects.evidence: 40 seeded palettes, filter `palette 1` (11 visible), one drag: store head `probe-0…probe-7` → `probe-9, probe-0, probe-10, probe-11, probe-12, probe-13, probe-14, probe-15`. usePaletteStore.ts:163-165 is the append arm.
defects.mechanism: a local gesture bound to a filtered projection is applied as a total reordering of the whole store
defects.reproduction: Seed 40 palettes; type `palette 1` into 'Search your palettes...'; drag the top visible handle down one row; read localStorage order. 29 unseen palettes move.
defects.proposedCure: Same as D-1: reorder is an operation on the store's ordinal, not on a filtered view. Disable reorder while a filter is active, or map the visible move back onto absolute store indices.

defects.defect: One searchQuery ref sits behind two search fields whose placeholders declare different scopes ('Search your palettes...' vs 'Search the commons...'), plus Admin and the color-name queue. A commons query silently hides the user's entire private library and the pane then reports the library as empty.
defects.evidence: usePalettePorts.ts:54 `const searchQuery = ref("")` feeds :65 browse, :68 admin, :69 colorQueue and :112 filteredSaved. Both PalettesPane.vue:34 and BrowsePane.vue:11 bind `v-model="pm.searchQuery.value"`. Live: after typing in Browse then navigating to /#/palettes → `{ myPalettesFieldValue: "commons-query-xyz", cardsRendered: 0, emptyStatus: "No saved palettes yet." }`.
defects.mechanism: two scope contracts (placeholders) over one model value — the design declares per-surface scope and implements global scope
defects.reproduction: Seed 6 palettes; go to /#/browse; type `commons-query-xyz` into 'Search the commons...'; navigate to /#/palettes. The library field is pre-filled with the commons query and the library renders empty.
defects.proposedCure: Scope belongs to the surface that declares it. useFilteredList already takes its query as a parameter — give the Library its own `libraryQuery` in the Library port and leave Browse `commonsQuery`. No screen shows both fields at once, so the shared ref buys nothing.

defects.defect: Corrupt or wrong-schema palette storage is rendered as an empty library. usePaletteStore's serializer catches JSON.parse failure and returns defaultStore, so an unreadable library is presented as a library the user never filled — and the empty invitation encourages them to save over it.
defects.evidence: usePaletteStore.ts:23-33 — `catch { return defaultStore; }` plus a shape guard returning the same. Live: `localStorage['color-palettes'] = '{{{not json'` + reload → `{ rawStillCorrupt: "{{{not json", emptyStatus: "· EMPTY PLATE · | No saved palettes yet. | Add colors above, then save the set." }`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 verbatim: "It is never rendered as an empty library, silent reset, migration choice, overlay, or companion pane."
defects.mechanism: masking fallback (owner edict 2) collapsing an error arm onto the empty arm; the §7 recovery composition does not exist in the component
defects.reproduction: In devtools: `localStorage.setItem('color-palettes','{{{not json')`; reload /#/palettes. The pane paints the ordinary empty invitation; no recovery article, no diagnosis, no export offer.
defects.proposedCure: read() returns a discriminated `{ok:true,store} | {ok:false,reason:'unparseable'|'schema'}` and preserves the raw bytes. PalettesPane renders the §7 recovery article — diagnosis, download-raw-backup, then separately-confirmed reset — in place of the field. EmptyState already carries the variant="error" register that this arm needs; it is simply never reached from this pane.

defects.defect: A search that matches nothing renders the empty-LIBRARY invitation, contradicting the pane's own header badge within the same viewport, and giving advice that is factually wrong.
defects.evidence: Live with 6 stored palettes and query `zzzzz-no-match`: `{ emptyStatus: "· EMPTY PLATE · | No saved palettes yet. | Add colors above, then save the set.", cardsRendered: 0, storedCount: 6 }` while the header renders `My Palettes ⟨6⟩`. PalettesPane.vue:75-81 passes fixed empty copy keyed only on `filteredSaved.length === 0`.
defects.mechanism: one empty predicate serving two distinct domain states (nothing exists vs nothing matched)
defects.reproduction: Seed 6 palettes; type `zzzzz-no-match` into 'Search your palettes...'. Screenshot at scratchpad/palpane-D/light-nomatch.png.
defects.proposedCure: Split the predicate. `filteredSaved.length === 0 && savedPalettes.length > 0` is a no-matches composition that echoes the query and offers 'Clear filter'; `savedPalettes.length === 0` is the invitation. Third arm is D-24's recovery.

defects.defect: An empty Library receives exactly 50.00% of the desktop stage, against a law that caps empty secondary content at 15% and forbids half the viewport by name; a quarter of the pane's height is unpainted tail below the last ink.
defects.evidence: Live 1440×900, empty store, both schemes identical: `.pane-container--dual w=1042.0`; `.pane-wrapper--left w=512.0 x=199`; `.pane-wrapper--right w=512.0 x=729` → shares [50.00, 50.00]. Pane 512.0×684.7, ink ends y=662.3 → dead tail 169.9px = 24.8%. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 2: "at most a narrow invitation tray (≤15% of the stage) or disappears. It never receives half the viewport." §3 law 1 permits only 61.8033989/38.1966011 or 66.6666667/33.3333333.
defects.mechanism: the route is composed as an equal companion Card (PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-04, terminal verb REMOVE) rather than as the Library chassis §3.1 specifies
defects.reproduction: Clear localStorage['color-palettes']; load /#/palettes at 1440×900; measure .pane-wrapper rects.
defects.proposedCure: Content-hug the empty invitation (§7: "A true empty invitation content-hugs its text/action") and let the protagonist expand. Inseparable from D-3: a Library that owns its route cannot be 50% of a Picker's scene.

defects.defect: PalettesPane is a route composed as a Card. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 gives Library an owner workspace chassis with a field at 64–66.7% and a selected inspector at 33.3–36%, and says verbatim that the field/lane/empty/inspector have NO Card. What ships is <Card tier="resting"> wrapping the whole route in a 50/50 split with the Picker in the inspector's slot.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:2 `<Card tier="resting" class="pane-scroll-fade w-full mx-auto ...">`. Measured shares [50.00, 50.00]; 512/1440 = 35.56% where the golden inspector would be 550.0px. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1: "Card remains semantic housing for a bounded object or specimen and is never the default page primitive."
defects.mechanism: page-as-Card — the composition primitive is one tier above where the canon puts it, which pushes every inspector job down into the card body
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes at 1440; read .pane-container--dual and its two .pane-wrapper children.
defects.proposedCure: Compose the owner workspace chassis: owner-state selector (Draft/Workspace/Published/Trash) across the top, field at 64–66.7%, selected inspector at 33.3–36%. The inspector then absorbs rename/export/publish/delete/expand/operation-state by construction.

defects.defect: The pastel-rainbow identity — one of exactly two sanctioned coordinates — is perceptually achromatic in dark. The contrast certifier's only lever is L, but the ramp's identity is hue; on a dark plate the feasible walk direction is lighter, so all three stops land at L≈0.958 where cusp chroma is ~0.02 for every hue.
defects.evidence: Live computed root tokens: light `--palettes-ramp-title-0/1/2` C = 0.188343 / 0.188343 / 0.124795 (C̄ 0.1673) at L 47.093%; dark C = 0.033662 / 0.021053 / 0.023120 (C̄ 0.0260) at L 95.832% — a 6.44× collapse, all three dark stops sharing L to 11 decimals. Shipped Safari PNG pixels agree: dark glyph cores OKLCH C 0.0257 / 0.0206 / 0.0205. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2: "Both coordinates render in light and dark."
defects.mechanism: contrast-first certification applied to a hue-carrying identity — the guard cannot fail to destroy what it guards
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with prefers-color-scheme: dark; read getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--palettes-ramp-title-0..2'). Or crop 'Palettes' from shots/safari-desktop-dark/palettes.png and convert glyph-core pixels to OKLCH.
defects.proposedCure: Certify on an axis the identity does not live on: hold hue and chroma, satisfy the floor by compositing the letterforms against a local plate the ramp owns. Failing that, choose the walk direction by chroma preservation with L free only inside a chroma floor — dark-scheme identity ink is normally more chromatic, not less.

defects.defect: The palette entity is a cursor:pointer role="article" div with no focusable seat — precisely the "clickable role=article ... seven-mode omnibus" the constitution forbids by name. Zero aria-pressed seats exist; selection, activation and every lifecycle verb hang off a root @click.
defects.evidence: Measured with 6 palettes: `cardArticles: 6`, `cardAriaPressed: 0`, `cardCursor: "pointer"`. PalettesPane.vue:82-97 wires @click/@delete/@publish/@rename/@edit-color/@export plus :expanded and :editable-name onto one card. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5: "A palette card is a bounded entity article, not a clickable role=article, listbox/option composite, or seven-mode omnibus ... One native named <button type=\"button\"> spans its specimen/identity region and expresses inspector selection only through aria-pressed."
defects.mechanism: with no inspector (D-3) there is no seat that owns selection, so selection collapsed onto the container
defects.reproduction: Seed palettes; load /#/palettes; querySelectorAll('.palette-card-grid [aria-pressed]').length === 0 while [role=article].length === 6. Tab through the pane: no card is reachable.
defects.proposedCure: One native <button type="button" aria-pressed> spanning the specimen/identity region, inside one Card shell; every other verb moves to the selected inspector.

defects.defect: The delete-all control's scope is the whole store while its visible context is the filtered list. With a filter matching nothing it remains on screen, above the words "No saved palettes yet.", and deletes six palettes the user cannot see.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:62 gates on `pm.savedPalettes.value.length > 0` (unfiltered) while :83 renders `pm.filteredSaved`. Measured: `{ deleteAllStillPresent: true, cardsRendered: 0, storedCount: 6 }`. The button is 28×28px with `visibleText: ""`.
defects.mechanism: the destructive verb is bound to a different collection than the one the user is looking at
defects.reproduction: Seed 6 palettes; filter to zero matches; the trash chip is still rendered and its confirm dialog reads "permanently delete 6 palettes" over a body that says none exist.
defects.proposedCure: Bind the verb to the visible set or name the divergence in the label ('Delete all 6' / 'Delete 2 matching' / disabled when the visible set is empty). Deeper cure: lifecycle verbs belong to the selected inspector, not a floating chip.

defects.defect: Card polarity is exactly inverted against §3.1: the field has a Card and the entity does not. The palette entity is a hand-rolled utility-class div carrying the cartoon decoration atom, so the ratified quiet tuple (shadow=false, specular=off, surface=opaque) is not merely unset but contradicted — casters within casters, which §7 forbids verbatim.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:2 wraps the field in <Card tier="resting">. PaletteCard.vue:14-27 root is `<div class="group rounded-card cartoon-surface border-card-edge bg-well cursor-pointer" role="article">`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1: "every rendered bounded palette entity slip has exactly one Card shell, and the field/lane/empty/inspector have none"; §7: "not cartoon casters stacked within casters." demo/ui/{card,button,badge}/index.ts are one-line glass-ui re-exports, so this is a bypass at the consumption site, not a local fork.
defects.mechanism: design-system bypass — a producer primitive with a ratified tuple replaced in place by a utility-class recipe that cannot express the tuple
defects.reproduction: Read PaletteCard.vue:14-27 against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1's tuple; inspect a rendered card's computed box-shadow (three stacked casts) inside the pane Card's own cast.
defects.proposedCure: Give the entity the mandated <Card size="sm" material="content" tier="quiet" surface="opaque" :shadow="false" :grain="false" specular="off"> shell and drop cartoon-surface; remove the Card from the field.

defects.defect: The field has no design at scale: 40 palettes render as a 4468px single column inside a 774px viewport, with no density option, no grouping, no pagination and no virtualization; the shared grid hardcodes grid-cols-1 and its only escape is a per-instance override prop.
defects.evidence: Measured at 40 seeded palettes: `{ cards: 40, gridCols: "462px", gridH: 4468, paneScrollH: 4805 }` — 5.8× overflow. PaletteCardGrid.vue:4 `class="palette-card-grid grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 min-h-[120px]"` with `:class="gridClass"` (:5, :43) as the only variation point, which PalettesPane never passes.
defects.mechanism: the layout was derived from the 0-item and 6-item cases and never re-decided for the n-item case; the producer's answer to more-than-one-column is a consumer root override (edict 5 inverted into an API)
defects.reproduction: Seed 40 palettes; load /#/palettes at 1440; measure .palette-card-grid height and the pane's scrollHeight.
defects.proposedCure: Decide the field's density and grouping as a design question: owner-state partition (§3.1's four states) supplies the grouping, a compact row rung supplies the density, and column count responds to the field's own width once D-3 gives the field 64–66.7% instead of a fixed 512px slab.

defects.defect: The component's only motion is three raw literals passed into a third-party library: a bare `animation: 150` millisecond integer, a Tailwind utility name as the drag ghost state, and no reduced-motion branch anywhere.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:185-186 `animation: 150, ghostClass: "opacity-30"`. `grep -rn 'prefers-reduced-motion|motion-reduce' demo/palettes/` returns only ShadowPalette.vue:25 and ApiOfflineChip.vue:81. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: "Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register" and "Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry." I measured that the card's own CSS DOES honour PRM (transition ... 0.1s under reducedMotion:reduce), isolating the defect to this file's hand-passed options.
defects.mechanism: motion authored as library options rather than as design-system tokens, so it sits outside every register and every media query the design system honours
defects.reproduction: Read PalettesPane.vue:183-197; grep demo/palettes for a PRM guard. (Whether the SortableJS FLIP itself animates under PRM is recorded in the report as a HYPOTHESIS — I could not catch the inline transition inside my sampling window.)
defects.proposedCure: Consume the producer spring register for the FLIP duration/easing and give the drag state a real register (lift, drop target, ordinal announcement) per PR-07. Under the D-1 cure the whole option bag disappears with SortableJS.

defects.defect: The empty plate's type hierarchy is inverted as well as off-matrix: the lowest-priority line (the how-to hint) is set 2.0px LARGER than the eyebrow above it, and in the machine voice, where §4 assigns prose/help to Plus Jakarta Sans text-prose.
defects.evidence: Measured computed styles on the empty plate: eyebrow '· empty plate ·' Fira Code 14.384px; display line 'No saved palettes yet.' Fraunces 25.888px; hint 'Add colors above, then save the set.' Fira Code 16.400px. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 type jurisdictions table: prose/help → text-prose → Plus Jakarta Sans; the matrix "is closed across all eighteen compositions."
defects.mechanism: copy authored at the consumer (PalettesPane.vue:78-80) against a producer that offers only mono/display registers for the empty plate
defects.reproduction:
Load /#/palettes with an empty store; getComputedStyle each

under [role=status].
defects.proposedCure: Map the hint to text-prose (Plus Jakarta Sans) and keep it below the eyebrow rung. The eyebrow's mono-caption is defensible under §4's caption carve-out; the hint's is not.

defects.defect: The single asymmetric spacing decision in the header is authored as a physical margin, so the designed 8px gap between the title and its count badge becomes 0px under RTL and the 8px lands in dead space on the far side. This refutes pass 2's negative proof that RTL mirrors cleanly.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:22 `class="text-mono-small ml-2"`; computed `marginLeft: 8px, marginRight: 0px`. Measured rendered geometry — LTR: title-block 754.0…967.2, badge 975.2…1004.6, gap 8.0px. RTL: title-block 472.8…686.0, badge 443.3…472.8, gap 0.0px. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: "chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document."
defects.mechanism: physical margin utility (ml-) where a logical one (ms-) is required
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with palettes seeded; set document.documentElement.dir='rtl'; measure the badge rect against the title span's rect.
defects.proposedCure: ml-2 → ms-2. The design point beyond the fix: the header's rhythm was authored in one direction only, and no captured matrix would have caught it because /#/palettes has no RTL capture.

defects.defect: The pane carries a centring utility that is inert on its own root while the ratio the constitution assigns it is decided two levels up in a file it does not own — so no cure for the proportion laws can be written inside this component.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:2 `class="... w-full mx-auto ..."` — mx-auto cannot distribute free inline space on a w-full child. Measured: the real cap is the shell wrapper `pane-wrapper ... max-w-md sm:max-w-lg`, pinning the pane to exactly 512px at both 1440 (35.56% of viewport) and 720 (71.11%).
defects.mechanism: contrivance (owner edict 3) — a utility that reads as intent and expresses none, over a width authority that lives elsewhere
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes at 1440 and at 720; measure .pane-scroll-fade width — 512.0px in both.
defects.proposedCure: Delete mx-auto. Move the width/ratio authority to the Library chassis as part of the D-3 cure, so the composition's proportion is expressed where the composition is declared.

defects.defect: Three imported symbols are never used, and two escape hatches from the type system sit in the reorder wiring.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:128 imports watch, onMounted, nextTick — measured 0 uses each after line 128 (`sed -n '129,212p' | grep -c`). PalettesPane.vue:181 `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el`; :84 `(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.id] = el)`.
defects.mechanism: dead imports plus `any` used to reach through a child component's DOM
defects.reproduction: grep the script block of PalettesPane.vue for each symbol after its import line.
defects.proposedCure: Remove the three imports. Replace the string template ref with Vue 3.5 useTemplateRef (owner edict 7), and expose the grid element from PaletteCardGrid via defineExpose rather than reading its $el — PaletteCardGrid.vue:8-12 already carries a comment explaining that its markup is shaped by the parent's private $el read, which is the encapsulation inversion made explicit in a code comment.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context arm), the tier explicitly declared at spawn. Seat declared, not inherited; no defect on the model-receipt axis.

defects.defect: Choosing `Delete` from this menu destroys a palette immediately — no confirmation dialog, no undo, no announcement — while the SAME pane's bulk "Delete all" opens a role="dialog" saying "This cannot be undone. Cancel / Delete all". The confirmation grammar exists, is glass-ui-native, is mounted in this component's own parent pane, and the per-card destructive path is the one path in the feature that skips it.

defects.defect: Pressing this component's 36x36 trigger runs the whole palette entity's activation press choreography — the card squashes 4.85% vertically and stretches 0.94% horizontally, indistinguishable to three decimals from pressing the card body itself — while `@click.stop` guarantees the card is NOT being activated. The motion says "you pressed the card"; the code says "you did not". All three prior passes certified motion as the one clean axis.
defects.evidence: probe-D17-pass4-results.json A_pressLeak: rest {pressT "0.0000", scale none, 462x100} -> +590ms holding the trigger {pressT "1.0000", scale "1.0094 0.9515", 466.34x95.15}. Control (pressing the card body) {pressT "1.0125", scale "1.0091 0.9512"}. menuOpenDuringHold: 0 — the trigger opens on click, so for the whole hold there is no menu, only a deformed palette. Mechanism sites: PaletteCard.vue:82 `<div class="flex items-center gap-1" @click.stop>` stops click only; PaletteCard.vue:24 `v-bind="press.handlers"`, and glass-ui useLiquidPress handlers are onPointerdown/onPointerup/onPointercancel/onPointerleave.
defects.mechanism: event-name mismatch between the guard and the drive — the wrapper cancels `click` while the press register listens on `pointerdown`, which is never stopped; the Card root is therefore carrying activation choreography VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 12 forbid it to own
defects.reproduction: `node docs/…/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D17-pass4.mjs`; read A_pressLeak (mouse.down on the trigger, sample --card-press-t and the inline scale at +90ms and +590ms).
defects.proposedCure: Under D-1's transposition there is no trigger inside the card and the question disappears. Short of that: the wrapper that already carries `@click.stop` must also carry `@pointerdown.stop`. Note the local patch re-affirms the wrong composition — the card should not own an activation animation at all.

defects.defect: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the P4-4 deformation becomes an instantaneous 4.85% geometry snap of the palette entity: at the same +120ms sample the press value is 1.0000 (fully deformed) versus 0.1034 with motion enabled. The arm that exists to remove motion delivers the most abrupt version of a motion this component should not be firing.
defects.evidence: probe-D17-pass4-results.json E_reducedMotion_no-preference {motionWeight "0.618", card at +120ms pressT "0.1034", scale "1.001 0.9948"} vs E_reducedMotion_reduce {motionWeight "0", card at +120ms pressT "1.0000", scale "1.0094 0.9515"}. defects.mechanism: glass-ui's PRM fence collapses the spring so it resolves directly to final geometry (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6's literal requirement) — but a press has no final geometry, it is the transient the spring exists to smooth; removing the spring exposes rather than removes the defect
defects.reproduction: `node docs/…/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D17-pass4.mjs`; compare E_reducedMotion_reduce.cardWhilePressingTrigger against E_reducedMotion_no-preference at the identical +120ms sample.
defects.proposedCure: Same as P4-4 — the press must not fire from a control that cancels activation. This finding is not a separate repair; it is the reason the P4-4 repair cannot be deferred as cosmetic.

defects.defect: After the destructive action, focus lands on `<body>`: the action destroys its own opener, so the producer's return-focus-to-trigger contract has no target. A keyboard user who deletes the fourth of eleven palettes is returned to the top of the document with no announcement and must re-traverse the field.
defects.evidence: probe-D18-pass4-results.json F_irreversible.afterSingleDelete.focused = "BODY.relative". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.1, Dialog/Drawer/Popover row, states the fallback exactly: "exact connected opener on close, otherwise the nearest surviving owning action" — <body> is not the nearest surviving owning action; the adjacent card's seat is.
defects.mechanism: a per-entity overlay whose opener is a child of the entity it destroys cannot satisfy any opener-restoration contract; the component has no knowledge of the field it sits in and therefore no candidate for the canon's named fallback
defects.reproduction: `node docs/…/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D18-pass4.mjs`; read F_irreversible.afterSingleDelete.focused.
defects.proposedCure: An inspector region survives the deletion of any row, so focus returns to a stable heading/action that still exists. This is the canon's own fallback, obtainable only once the actions leave the card.

result.strongestDefect: P4-2 — the per-card `Delete` destroys a palette with no confirmation, no undo, no announcement and focus dumped on <body>, measured 11 cards/11 stored -> 10/10 with `[role="dialog"]` count 0 throughout, while the same pane's bulk "Delete all" opens a role="dialog" reading "This cannot be undone. Cancel / Delete all". It is the only finding across four passes whose failure mode is irreversible user data loss, and P4-1 makes it probable: on cards in the lower half of the list the panel flips and `Delete` becomes the row NEAREST the pointer (51.5px vs 233.5px, 4.5x closer), in identical ink to `Rename` and with no separator above it.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this is the bounded sound-set rather than a negative proof of the whole. Six things were checked this pass and found to have no defect, each measured: (1) the disabled row's pointer semantics are producer-correct — with data-disabled set, cursor `not-allowed`, pointer-events `none`, opacity 0.5, hitTestIsTheRow false; the consumer's inert `cursor-pointer` produces no affordance lie because the producer wins the cascade in both states (probe-D17 D_disabledAffordance). (2) The stuck-press hypothesis is FALSE — upEarly 0.0275, upSettled 0.0000, scale none; the modal layer taking pointer-events from the card does not strand the spring at 1. (3) `align="end"` is direction-aware — in RTL the panel's aligned edge is physical-left (C_rtl.menuRtl.alignedEdge "physical-left"); the RTL defect is the pinned `dir` attribute on the portal, not the alignment prop. (4) The producer honours prefers-reduced-motion on the panel — "scale, translate, opacity, filter, display, overlay" @0.35s collapses to "opacity" @0.15s and animation-duration to 1e-05s; every reduced-motion defect here is consumer-side wiring. (5) The card row itself mirrors correctly in RTL — trigger x 1166 -> 238, card 754…1216 -> 224…686. (6) No layout-forcing property is animated on either side — the card press writes `scale` plus custom properties (--card-press-t, --flex-vel) with transform `none`; the panel transitions scale/translate/opacity/filter. Compositor-only; the motion defect (P4-4/P4-5) is semantic, not performance. One method correction is recorded under evidence law as P4-C1: this pass's first RTL arm used addInitScript and silently measured an LTR document because demo/color-picker/index.html:11 pins `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">`; that arm was discarded, re-run post-boot, and none of its numbers are cited.

defects.defect: The T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone proves a library surface that does not exist on npm: `dist/` is gitignored and locally regenerated, and it is NOT byte-equal to the published @mkbabb/value.js 4.0.0 that npm installed to satisfy glass-ui's peer dep. The local `dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` (12,490 B) carries 1,580 bytes of `_2`-suffixed duplicate colour types (Alpha_2/Channel_2/ChannelsBySpace_2/Color_2/SpaceId_2) and wires CssColorMap to Color_2<S>; the published copy (10,910 B) has the clean Color<S>. Both claim version 4.0.0.
defects.evidence: `git check-ignore -v dist` -> `.gitignore:17:dist/`; `git ls-files dist | wc -l` -> 0. `diff -rq dist node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist` -> `Files dist/subpaths/css.d.ts and node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts differ` + `css.js differ`. `wc -c` -> 12490 vs 10910. probe-L4-resolve-results.json: repoPackageVersion 4.0.0, installedPackageVersion 4.0.0, css js sha 'DIFFERENT (ca87007bf75062e8 vs 8b5381305ea26236)', dts 'DIFFERENT (ded101dc54ef70f6 vs c81d095213d112c6)'. tsconfig.demo.json:5-9 declares dist/*.d.ts the 'trust boundary'.
defects.mechanism: The trust boundary was drawn around a PATH (dist/) rather than an ARTIFACT (a published tarball). A path can be silently regenerated; with dist/ untracked there is no pin, no checksum, and no CI step that could observe the divergence. All the drift-prevention machinery (vite.config.ts:24-50 generated self-alias, tsconfig.demo.json:41-49 paths mirror) exists only to compensate for that choice.
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && git check-ignore -v dist && diff -rq dist node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist && wc -c dist/subpaths/css.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts && node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-L4-resolve.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Dogfood the package, not the directory. (1) `npm pack` in CI and install the tarball into the demo typecheck/build job (or self-link so node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js IS the thing under test); then DELETE the entire valueJsSelfAlias generator (vite.config.ts:24-50, ~27 lines + 14 of comment) — a package that resolves itself needs no alias. (2) Fix the rollup-dts collision that emits the `_2` family in the css subpath build, and add a test/dist/ hygiene gate asserting no `_2`-suffixed declaration survives in dist/subpaths/*.d.ts (that gate convention already exists per vitest.config.ts:24-28).

defects.defect: @mkbabb/value.js publishes NO root export — package.json#exports has 7 subpath keys and no "." — yet tsconfig.demo.json:42 declares `"@mkbabb/value.js": ["./dist/index.d.ts"]`. The config comment justifying that entry is false in two independent claims: it asserts glass-ui's dist imports value.js by the bare specifier (it imports only /color x5, /css x3, /easing x1) and names an alias target `dist/value.js` that is not an exports key.
defects.evidence: `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports))"` -> ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize']. probe-L4-resolve-results.json: {"specifier":"@mkbabb/value.js","error":"ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: No \"exports\" main defined in /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/package.json"}. `grep -ho '"@mkbabb/value\.js[^"]*"' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.js | sort | uniq -c` -> 5 /color, 3 /css, 1 /easing (zero bare). tsconfig.demo.json:22-25 asserts the opposite.
defects.mechanism: A derived artefact (the TS paths mirror of the exports map) was hand-copied instead of generated, drifted when the exports map changed, and its 23-line justifying comment was never re-read against the map. This upgrades pass-1 L-5's labelled HYPOTHESIS to a reproduction, and the false comment is why L-19 stayed invisible across four passes.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-L4-resolve.mjs  # row 4 of `resolution` raises ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED for the bare specifier
defects.proposedCure: Delete the whole `@mkbabb/value.js*` paths block (8 lines) and its 23 lines of comment from tsconfig.demo.json. Node/TS self-reference resolution already resolves every subpath correctly (probe row 1-3) and, unlike a hand-copied mirror, cannot drift. One authority — the exports map — then governs compile and runtime.

defects.defect: Two different slugify algorithms own one concept: utils.ts:3 (NFKD-folding) mints the slug a palette is STORED under; export.ts:9 (no normalisation) mints the filename and the CSS custom-property namespace the Export sub-menu produces. Non-ASCII names diverge: 'Café Noir' stores as cafe-noir but exports as caf-noir.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/utils.ts:3-12 vs demo/palettes/export.ts:9-11. Live run, probe-L4-results.json: {"seededSlugs":["cafe-noir-aabbccdd","underscoremix-aabbccdd"], "downloadFilenames":["caf-noir.json"]}. Computed table: 'Ünderscore_Mix' -> underscoremix vs nderscore-mix; '中文 palette' -> -palette vs palette. A third, correct home exists and never ships: export/canonical.ts:52-58 identifierPrefix ('no slugifier exists').
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated — 'name -> identifier' has two implementations with different Unicode semantics, one per module that happened to need it, and no canonical home. The CSS export propagates the broken stem into the custom-property namespace (export.ts:27 -> --palette-caf-noir-0), so it is not merely a filename.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-L4-slug-and-open.mjs  # seeds two saved local palettes on /#/palettes, opens the card menu, Export > JSON, intercepts the anchor download attribute
defects.proposedCure: One exported `slug()` in the palette domain module consumed by both minters — or, under pass-1 L-1's cure (delete export.ts + usePaletteExport.ts, promote export/serializers.ts to index.ts), no second slugifier at all, because the byte-exact serializers take the identifier from the snapshot's server slug. The bug then disappears without being separately fixed.

defects.defect: `paletteKind` is a derived prop: a total pure function of the `palette` prop passed alongside it, from the single call site, with the invariant `paletteKind === getPaletteKind(palette)` unstated and unchecked — and the receiving component does not trust it, re-deriving the same discriminator at :94 as `!palette.isLocal`.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:206-212 (props: palette + paletteKind). utils.ts:22-31 getPaletteKind is total and depends only on palette.isLocal + three id prefixes. `grep -rn "palette-kind|:paletteKind" demo --include="*.vue"` -> exactly one site, PaletteCard.vue:85 `:palette-kind="kind"` where PaletteCard.vue:225 `const kind = computed(() => getPaletteKind(props.palette))`. Eight template branches use paletteKind (:16,:28,:49,:64,:74,:84,:134,:144) while :94 uses `!palette.isLocal`, which utils.ts:23 defines as the same predicate.
defects.mechanism: The kind has no home at the seam, so the seam carries both the value and a function of it. That is what produces the two spellings pass 2 recorded as L-13 — the spellings are the symptom, the redundant prop is the mechanism.
defects.reproduction: The grep above is a fact (redundancy). A DESYNC is a HYPOTHESIS — reproduction: NONE. With one call site it cannot fire today; it becomes reachable at the second consumer, which is exactly the shape of the already-firing isOwned bug (pass 2 L-11) and the already-firing unwired-emits bug (pass 2 L-10).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the prop. `const kind = computed(() => getPaletteKind(palette))` inside the menu (one line, one home), and :94 becomes `kind === 'remote' && (palette.versionCount ?? 0) > 1`. The seam narrows 5 props -> 4 and the invariant becomes unstateable because unnecessary.

defects.defect: The open-state model is hand-rolled over a primitive that already ships the correct one, it is not v-model-compatible, and the guard it exists to serve is provably dead. glass-ui's DropdownMenu publishes `open` + `update:open`; PaletteCardMenu republishes that as `menuOpen` + `updateOpen`, which Vue cannot bind as v-model (it requires `update:menuOpen`), forcing the consumer to hand-wire both halves.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.vue.d.ts — `open?: boolean; defaultOpen?: boolean;` and `export interface DropdownMenuEmits { "update:open": [value: boolean]; }`. PaletteCardMenu.vue:209 `menuOpen: boolean;` and :224-227 `defineEmits<{ action:[string]; updateOpen:[boolean] }>()`. PaletteCard.vue:87 `:menu-open="menuOpen"`, :89 `@update-open="menuOpen = $event"`. Dead guard: PaletteCard.vue:317 `if (action !== "rename") menuOpen.value = false;` then :318 `fn()` — for rename, fn is startRenaming whose first statement is :281 `menuOpen.value = false`. Live: probe-L4-results.json `"menuStateBeforeRename":["open"], "openMenusAfterRename": 0`.
defects.mechanism: A wrapper published a weaker model than the primitive it wraps. Four moving parts (prop, emit, parent ref, guard) re-implement behaviour reka's MenuItem already provides (close-on-select), and the comment at PaletteCard.vue:291-292 describes behaviour the code two lines below contradicts. Edict 7 (defineModel is the 3.5 idiom), edict 2 (dead branch), edict 3 (contrivance).
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-L4-slug-and-open.mjs  # opens the second card's menu, clicks Rename, counts visible [role=menu] -> 0
defects.proposedCure: Delete `menuOpen`, `updateOpen`, the parent ref and the :317 guard. Let the menu own its open state via the primitive's `defaultOpen`; if a consumer ever needs control, `const open = defineModel<boolean>('open')` gives real `v-model:open` with the primitive's own vocabulary. Net: -1 prop, -1 emit, -1 ref, -1 dead branch, -2 lines of false comment. Generalised as Amendment 5: a wrapper may never publish a weaker model than what it wraps.

defects.defect: The palette area root is a 21-file flat drawer (14 `use*` composables at the root, plus utils.ts/constants.ts/mix.ts and an `export.ts` that collides by name with the `export/` directory beside it), and `types.ts` — the module this leaf imports `Palette` from — declares 12 types spanning four domains including generic HTTP pagination envelopes.
defects.evidence: `find demo/palettes -maxdepth 1 -type f | wc -l` -> 21; `find demo/palettes -maxdepth 1 -name 'use*.ts' | wc -l` -> 14; `grep -cE '^export (interface|type)' demo/palettes/types.ts` -> 12. types.ts:1-141 spans palette (Palette, PaletteColor, PaletteVersion, ProvenanceNode, PaletteStore), identity (User), moderation/admin (Flag, FlaggedPalette, Tag, AuditEntry) and transport (PaginatedResponse<T>, CursorPaginatedResponse<T>). export/serializers.ts:5-9 documents the name collision as deliberate: 'This module is intentionally NOT named index.ts: the sibling legacy ../export.ts (the pre-contract routed seat that W50 will replace) still resolves ./export'.
defects.mechanism: No sub-feature lattice at the area root, so every new concept lands flat next to every other; 'utils' and a single cross-domain 'types' are where unique ownership goes to die. The documented-deliberate file/directory name collision is edict 2 (dual path with a deferred-migration promise) in written form.
defects.reproduction: The three counts above, run at HEAD 9268f054.
defects.proposedCure: Split types.ts along its four seams (palette domain -> palettes/index.ts; PaginatedResponse/CursorPaginatedResponse -> platform/transport/; User/Flag/FlaggedPalette/AuditEntry/Tag -> their own feature homes); move the 14 composables under the sub-feature each serves; dissolve utils.ts into the domain module (getPaletteKind, slug). Delete export.ts and rename export/serializers.ts -> export/index.ts, which retires the collision along with the dual path.

defects.defect: Two writers own palette order on every drop. The pane supplies `onEnd`, which does not override vueuse's default `onUpdate`, so vueuse's `moveArrayElement` also runs — performing raw removeChild/insertBefore DOM surgery on a Vue-managed subtree — while the pane's onEnd writes the store. The `list` argument is a dereferenced computed (`pm.filteredSaved.value`), i.e. a setup-time snapshot where a ref/getter is required.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:183-197. node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:11-16 — `const defaultOptions = { onUpdate: (e) => { moveArrayElement(list, e.oldIndex, e.newIndex, e); } }` then `new Sortable(target, { ...defaultOptions, ...resetOptions })`; `moveArrayElement` at :77-91 opens with `removeNode(e.item); insertNodeAt(e.from, e.item, from)` and its splice is a no-op for a non-ref list (`isRef(list)` false). useFilteredList.ts:8 returns a ComputedRef; usePaletteStore.ts:51-55 makes savedPalettes a computed that mints a new array each recompute. usePaletteStore.ts:161-165 completes a partial id list by appending, so a filtered reorder hoists the visible subset (pass-3 L-17, mechanism re-confirmed by reading).
defects.mechanism: Ordering has no single home: sortable holds one truth, the store another, and the store patches the difference. The same hazard class as the documented Teleport insertBefore NotFoundError at vite.config.ts:83-90 — Vue-managed DOM mutated outside Vue.
defects.reproduction: Code path confirmed by reading vueuse + store, pasted. The live drag was NOT re-run this pass — the shared Playwright browser was held by another seat (`Error: Browser is already in use for … mcp-chrome-83447af`). Pass 3's live reproduction (seeded A,B,C → persisted C,B,A; filtered A..E → persisted D,B,E,A,C) stands as the executed evidence.
defects.proposedCure: Order is store state. Move the sortable binding into PaletteCardGrid.vue, which owns the element it operates on, and pass a getter not a snapshot: `useSortable(rootEl, () => library.savedPalettes.value, { handle, animation, ghostClass, onUpdate })` — supply onUpdate so the default is genuinely replaced and no unowned DOM mutation runs; disable dragging while searchQuery is non-empty. The pane then never mentions sortable, and PalettesPane.vue:180-181's `(… as any)?.$el` reach into the child's DOM disappears with it.

defects.mechanism: Geometric congruence between a repeated-row list and the menu it spawns, compounded by a modal layer. The card list pitch (112 px) is a near-multiple of the menu item pitch (44 px) with the menu top 22.4 px below the trigger centre, so offsets 112 and 224 land 19.5 px and 9.5 px from item centres; the last item is the destructive one. reka's `modal: true` default puts `pointer-events: none` on `<body>`, so the covered triggers cannot absorb their own clicks (`triggerComputedPE "none"`, `triggerIsTopMost false`) and the topmost hit target is the menu item. Neither number that produces the collision appears in the source file — it exists only when the component is rendered beside copies of itself, which is the only way it is ever rendered.
defects.reproduction: 1. `pnpm dev` (server live at http://localhost:9000). 2. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/evidence/pass-4/pcm-p4-c.mjs`. Manually: seed localStorage `color-palettes` with >=3 local palettes, open /#/palettes at 1440x900, click the first card's `⋯`, then click the THIRD card's `⋯` at its own centre. The first palette is deleted with no confirmation.
defects.proposedCure: Do not fix by geometry — any bottom-anchored menu in a repeated-row list covers the rows beneath it; changing the offset only relocates which item lands on the trigger. Two architectural changes, which together also discharge P4-2, P4-4, P4-5, C2-14 and C2-15: (a) destructive actions in a per-row menu are CONFIRMED — route `delete`/`adminDelete` through the glass-ui `AlertDialog` naming the palette (the admin path already is; the owner path is the outlier), so a stray activation costs a dismissal rather than a palette; and treat `publish` (a real remote write, PaletteCard.vue:295) the same way. (b) `:modal="false"` on PaletteCardMenu.vue:2, so neighbouring triggers stay hit-testable and reka's `onPointerDownOutside` turns the cross-row gesture into "close this menu, open that one" instead of "activate an item".

defects.defect: `<DropdownMenu>` (:2) never passes `:modal="false"`, so reka's `modal: true` default makes the entire document inert while a per-row card menu is open. One omitted prop produces five measured symptoms — including the mechanism of P4-1 — and the scroll lock it applies does not lock the actual scroll container.
defects.evidence: reka default: node_modules/reka-ui/dist/DropdownMenu/DropdownMenuRoot.js:26-30 `modal: { type: Boolean, required: false, default: true }`. Prop exists and is forwarded: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.vue.d.ts `modal?: boolean` in `DropdownMenuBaseProps`, doc-comment "Whether opening the menu makes outside content inert", runtime default `modal: boolean`. `$ grep -rn ":modal" demo --include="*.vue"` → no output. Consumers: `$ grep -rn "DropdownMenu" demo --include="*.vue" -l` → PaletteCardMenu.vue, UserSortMenu.vue, MobileMenuDropdown.vue, ProfileSection.vue (the other three are dock/filter singletons). Symptoms — probe pcm-p4-a.mjs `::A1_afterOpenCard0 {bodyPointerEvents "none", bodyOverflow "hidden"}`; probe pcm-p4-b.mjs `::B0_hitTestUnderLock {topMost "div", triggerIsTopMost false, triggerComputedPE "none", bodyPE "none"}`; `::B4_scrollUnderLock {window {before 0, after 0, moved false}, inner {before 0, after 200, moved true, cls "glass-resting card rounded-card text-card-foreground scrollb…"}, bodyOverflowInline "hidden"}`; `::B2_crossCardSequence` click1 lastClickTarget path ["div{menuitem}","div{menu}","div"] menuCount 0, click2 menuCount 1 owner "Probe Palette 1", click3 menuCount 0 target ["html"], `::B3_clicksToMoveMenu {opened true, clicksNeeded 3}`.
defects.mechanism: A library default chosen for singleton menus applied unexamined to the only menu rendered once per list row. The modal barrier's stated job (make outside content inert, lock scroll) is simultaneously over-applied (it disables every sibling control on the page, which is what stops the covered triggers absorbing their own clicks) and under-delivered (it writes `overflow: hidden` to `<body>` while the real scroller is an inner div that still scrolls 200 px).
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/evidence/pass-4/pcm-p4-b.mjs` — see `::B0_hitTestUnderLock`, `::B4_scrollUnderLock`, `::B2_crossCardSequence`. Manually: open any card's menu, then click a different card's `⋯` — it takes three clicks to move the menu, and the first one activates an item on the card you are leaving.
defects.proposedCure: `:modal="false"` on PaletteCardMenu.vue:2. If a modal barrier is genuinely wanted for the dock singletons, make it a glass-ui `DropdownMenu` default that per-row consumers override — the shipped truth is that no consumer has made the choice deliberately, because none of the four names the prop. This one edit also gives the APG `Tab` behaviour for free (P4-5), removes the ineffective body scroll lock (C2-15), and converts P4-1's cross-row gesture into the ordinary dismiss-then-open.

defects.defect: Two menu items render the identical visible label `Publish` and the identical `Globe` icon while emitting different actions into different host emits: `:33` emits `'publish'` (mint a new remote palette from a local one) and `:52-55` emits `'makePublic'` (flip an existing remote's visibility). Same word, same glyph, different API call.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:27-40 (`v-if="paletteKind === 'saved'"`, `<Globe/>`, text `Publish`, `@click="$emit('action','publish')"`) vs :48-60 (`v-if="paletteKind === 'remote' && isOwned"`, `<component :is="isPublic ? EyeOff : Globe"/>`, text `{{ isPublic ? "Make private" : "Publish" }}`, `@click="$emit('action', isPublic ? 'makePrivate' : 'makePublic')"`). Host divergence: PaletteCard.vue:295 `publish: () => emit("publish", props.palette)` vs PaletteCard.vue:302 `makePublic: () => emit("setVisibility", props.palette, "public")`. Name is the only AT discriminator because the menu inherits the trigger's name (pass-3 C3-2: `"Palette menu"` x6, `ariaLabelledby: "reka-dropdown-menu-trigger-…"`). Test-locator exposure: the repo's idiom is `getByRole("menuitem", { name: … })` — e2e/smoke/flows/palette-delete.spec.ts:48 uses the anchored `/^Delete$/` precisely because this menu's names are ambiguous; neither Publish branch is covered by any spec.
defects.mechanism: One English verb reused for two different state transitions across two `v-if` branches four lines apart, with no discriminating icon and no discriminating accessible name — the same untyped `action: [action: string]` channel (`:225`) that C2-1 showed the `if (!fn) return` dispatcher (PaletteCard.vue:316) will silently swallow.
defects.reproduction: NONE — source-level, verified by reading both branches at HEAD e39da983 and both host handlers. Reachable at runtime whenever a remote+owned palette has `visibility === "private"`; the /#/browse route needs a configured API, so I did not drive it live.
defects.proposedCure: Name the operations for what they do. The saved item becomes `Publish to the commons…`; the remote flip becomes `Make public` / `Make private`, which is what `isPublic ? EyeOff : Globe` already implies. The label then carries the transition and the K-INV5 annotation (:56-59) carries the current state — the same `state display + transition` shape C2-5 and C3-5 independently converge on. Replace `action: [action: string]` with a string-literal union so the two verbs cannot be confused at the emit either.

defects.defect: Escalation of C2-14: the owner `Delete` path has no confirmation dialog and no undo, and P4-1 supplies a routine cross-row gesture that reaches it without the user ever opening that palette's menu. "Unconfirmed delete" is no longer a matter of intent — it is a data-loss primitive.
defects.evidence: probe pcm-p4-d.mjs `::D2_determinism` — three runs, `dialogs: 0` each, `undoAffordance {hasUndoText: false, hasRestore: false}` each, store 8→7→6→5. The admin branch IS confirmed (PaletteCardMenu.vue:163-169 → PaletteCard.vue:301 `adminDelete`), so the owner branch (PaletteCardMenu.vue:133-140 → PaletteCard.vue:296 `delete`) is inconsistent with its own sibling, not with a missing convention. Pass-2 recorded the same `confirmDialogs: 0` on the deliberate path and scored it MINOR on an intent reading that P4-1 invalidates.
defects.mechanism: The severity of a missing confirmation is a function of how easily the action is reached by accident. Pass 2 measured the dialog count; pass 4 measured the accident. The two facts were filed in different passes and neither is dangerous alone.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/evidence/pass-4/pcm-p4-d.mjs` — `::D2_determinism` shows three deletions with `dialogs: 0` from a single repeated coordinate.
defects.proposedCure: Route `delete` (and `adminDelete`, already so routed) through the glass-ui `AlertDialog` naming the palette, and schedule it as ONE work item with P4-1 rather than as an independent MINOR. Confirmation is the cure that holds regardless of how the geometry is later changed.

defects.defect: `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` inside the open menu are dead keys: focus stays on the menu CONTAINER, never reaches a `menuitem`, and the menu never closes — contrary to the WAI-ARIA APG Menu Button contract ("Tab: moves focus to the next element in the tab sequence, and if the menu is open, closes the menu").
defects.evidence: probe pcm-p4-a.mjs `::A9_tabWalkWithMenuOpen` → four consecutive Tab presses, all four `{el "DIV:menu", inMenu true, menus 1}`. probe pcm-p4-e.mjs `::E3_keyboardWhileOpen` → `{key "Tab", menus 1, active "DIV{menu}", insideMenu true}`, `{key "Shift+Tab", menus 1, active "DIV{menu}", insideMenu true}`, `{key "ArrowDown", menus 1, active "DIV{menuitem}", activeText "Publish"}`, `{key "Escape", menus 0, active "BUTTON", activeText "Palette menu", insideMenu false}`.
defects.mechanism: reka's modal `FocusScope` traps focus when `modal` is true (P4-2). Escape works and restores focus correctly, so this is escapable and not a WCAG 2.1.2 trap — but a keyboard user who reaches for Tab gets no response and no indication that Escape is the exit.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/evidence/pass-4/pcm-p4-e.mjs` — `::E3_keyboardWhileOpen`. Manually: open a card menu, press Tab repeatedly, observe nothing changes.
defects.proposedCure: `:modal="false"` on PaletteCardMenu.vue:2 — the same single edit as P4-2; reka's non-modal content gives the APG Tab behaviour without any bespoke key handling.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate, sharpened: the repo already owns the `elementFromPoint` occlusion-oracle idiom and has pointed it at the WebGL bead and the dock band — never at the one surface where an occluded control destroys user data. Eight distinct mutations to this file keep every existing gate green, three of them new this pass.
defects.evidence: `$ grep -rn "elementFromPoint" e2e` → e2e/smoke/oracles/t31-dock-band.spec.ts:33 and e2e/smoke/oracles/o12-blob-seat.spec.ts:124 only. e2e/smoke/flows/palette-delete.spec.ts:46-48 uses `getByRole("button", {name: "Palette menu"}).first().click()` then `getByRole("menuitem", {name: /^Delete$/}).click()` — a Playwright locator click auto-scrolls and clicks the ITEM's centre, so it is structurally incapable of clicking at another card's trigger coordinates. Pass-2/3 infrastructure claim re-confirmed: no `@vue/test-utils` usage, zero `mount(` in test/ or demo/test/.
defects.mechanism: The suite asserts that named roles exist and that clicking them by name works. It never asserts anything about where controls are in space relative to each other, except for two decorative surfaces. Every geometry-changing mutation is therefore invisible.
defects.reproduction: NONE (gate analysis). Green-keeping mutations, verified against the suite's selectors: (1) delete :107-130 entirely; (2) `isPublic = computed(() => true)`; (3) `apiOffline = computed(() => false)`; (4) delete both `style="font-variant: small-caps"`; (5) make :9's DropdownMenuLabel render nothing; (6) change `align="end"` to `align="start"` on :7; (7) add `:side-offset="200"`; (8) change :33 to emit `'makePublic'`.
defects.proposedCure: Add the born-RED oracle the repo has already written twice: with any card's menu open, no OTHER card's interactive control may resolve to a `[role=menuitem]` under `document.elementFromPoint` at its own centre. Four lines; it fails on 8 of 8 openings today. Pair it with a component-level harness (`@vue/test-utils` is an unused devDependency) so the two `v-if` branches of P4-3 and the `misconfigured` latch of C2-4 become assertable at all.

defects.defect: Scope correction (not itself a defect, filed so the cure is not over-scoped): P4-1 is reachable by mouse and by touch only. Keyboard users are immune — the modal focus scope gives them no path to another card's trigger without first pressing Escape, which restores focus to the owning trigger.
defects.evidence: probe pcm-p4-e.mjs `::E3_keyboardWhileOpen` — Tab/Shift+Tab inert inside the menu, ArrowDown moves within the menu only, Escape closes and lands on `BUTTON` "Palette menu". probe pcm-p4-a.mjs `::A9_tabWalkWithMenuOpen` — 4/4 presses `inMenu: true`.
defects.mechanism: Same modal FocusScope as P4-5. The trap that makes Tab a dead key also makes the destructive cross-row gesture unreachable from the keyboard.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/evidence/pass-4/pcm-p4-e.mjs` — `::E3_keyboardWhileOpen`.
defects.proposedCure: None required. Record it: this component's defects cluster on the pointer path (P4-1, P4-2, C2-2, C2-13), which is exactly the path no gate in this repo exercises at coordinates. Note that `:modal="false"` (P4-2's cure) removes this immunity, so it MUST land together with the confirmation dialog (P4-4's cure) rather than alone.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion + seat law) for demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared seat, matching the explicit Opus 5 spawn declaration; not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: N-1 — in forced-colors a palette card shows no colours at all, and because the strip is simultaneously `aria-hidden="true" role="presentation"` there is no accessible-name channel either: the entire content of the artifact reaches neither a high-contrast user nor a screen-reader user. This closes the exact question pass 3 recorded as an untested hypothesis, and the answer is a defect in a child component (`PaletteColorStrip`) that no prior pass names.
result.negativeProof: Four things I attacked and could not break, each a state pass 3 declared unphotographed or a claim I tried to extend. (1) 200% zoom is SOUND: at 720x450@2x the pane reflows to single-column, `scrollWidthOverflow: 0`, all 12 cards present, title fluid clamp resolves at 30.72px — `probe/webkit-zoom200-desktop-populated.png`. (2) The ramp identity SURVIVES forced-colors: `color:transparent` + `background-clip:text` renders as system ink and "My Palettes" is fully legible in Chromium `forcedColors:"active"` — pass 3's open hypothesis resolves in the component's favour. (3) Reduced motion IS honoured including SortableJS's JS-injected inline transition, because `demo/styles/animations.css:184-192` uses `transition-duration: 0.01ms !important`, which outranks a normal inline declaration in the cascade — this NARROWS pass 3's D-15, which is right that `animation: 150` is untokenized but wrong that PRM is defeated. (4) Zero page errors, zero component console errors and zero horizontal overflow across all 8 probed matrices (1440/720/iPhone14 x light/dark x LTR/RTL x empty/12-palettes, forced-colors included). Also sound and not to be disturbed by any cure: the `aria-hidden` badge + `sr-only` companion at `:16-25` (independently PRESERVE-marked at om-15-text/TEXT-CONTRIVANCE-AUDIT.md:129); identity keying at `:85`; local-first save at usePaletteActions.ts:65-77; `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean (`import type { Palette }` at `:151`); no layout-animating property anywhere in the tree.

defects.defect: In forced-colors the entire palette specimen disappears from a palette card, and the same element is aria-hidden, so there is no accessible-name fallback either. A palette in My Palettes conveys only its name and a bare numeral to high-contrast users and to screen-reader users.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PalettesPane/probe/chromium-forced-colors-populated.png — 12 cards render as empty rounded rectangles with a blank ~48px band where the colours were. Mechanism at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue:3-4 (`aria-hidden="true" role="presentation"`) and :18-19 (`:style="{ backgroundColor: color.css }"`). `grep -c PaletteColorStrip challenge-D-design.pass-3-prior.md` -> 0. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83.
defects.mechanism: colour-only data with no second channel: background-color is in the forced-colors override set, and the same node is removed from the a11y tree, so one design decision blinds two independent user populations at once
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/challengeD-palettespane-probe.mjs with ENGINE=chromium; matrix `forced-colors-populated` (playwright context `forcedColors: "active"`, 1440x900, 12 seeded palettes at localStorage key `color-palettes`), route http://localhost:9000/#/palettes. Screenshot committed at probe/chromium-forced-colors-populated.png.
defects.proposedCure: The strip is data, not decoration. Drop aria-hidden/role=presentation and give each segment an accessible name (the colour's `name`, else its CSS string); add a `@media (forced-colors: active)` treatment that renders segments as bordered labelled cells. Architecturally the palette specimen must have a non-visual representation before the host is allowed to ship a card whose only content is colour.

defects.defect: The delete-all button is configured with `variant="ghost"`, which is not a prop in glass-ui 7's Button API — a dead Glass-5/shadcn survivor. It falls through as an inert DOM attribute, so the button ships as a FILLED translucent chip, not the quiet ghost its own comment documents, and four hand-rolled utility classes stand in for producer axes that already exist.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:64,67. glass-ui 7 API at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:4-19 declares only `emphasis: "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"`, `tone`, `size`, `iconOnly`, `loading` — no `variant`. Measured computed style: `background-color: oklab(0.915631 0.00547 0.013051 / 0.52)` (filled, not transparent). Same file uses the correct axes at :113 (`emphasis="text"`) and :116 (`tone="destructive"`). Zero occurrences of `variant="ghost"` in any prior pass.
defects.mechanism: a design-system prop rename across a major was applied at two of three call sites in one file; the third site compensated with per-instance utility classes, so intent and shipped pixels diverge silently
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with >=1 saved palette; inspect the `Delete all saved palettes` button. `variant="ghost"` appears as a literal DOM attribute and computed background-color is a filled 52%-alpha surface. Also visible as a light disc in probe/webkit-desktop-light-populated.png.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the dead prop and the four classes with the producer axes: `emphasis="quiet" tone="destructive"`. Owner edicts 2 (no legacy code) and 5 (root-level styling). Sweep the repo for other surviving `variant=` on glass-ui 7 Buttons in the same cut.

defects.defect: The safety gradient is inverted: deleting one palette is instant, unconfirmed and irreversible from a 36px menu, while deleting all palettes gets a full modal. The ruled `Trash` owner state does not exist even though the data model carries `deletedAt`.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:92 wires `@delete` straight to usePaletteActions.ts:31-38, which calls `deps.deletePalette(id)` with no confirmation. Contrast PalettesPane.vue:102-122, the guarded delete-all Dialog. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 names Trash as one of four explicit non-interchangeable owner states; demo/palettes/types.ts:49 declares `deletedAt` and nothing renders it.
defects.mechanism: guard placed by rarity rather than by consequence; the domain has a reversible-delete concept the UI never exposes, so every delete is annihilation
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with saved palettes -> any card's `...` menu -> Delete. The palette is gone from localStorage immediately with no dialog, no toast, no undo. Compare the trash-icon button, which opens a counted confirmation dialog.
defects.proposedCure: Delete moves the entity to the Trash owner state (`deletedAt`) rather than removing it; the Trash lane in the workspace chassis owns restore and permanent-purge. The confirmation modal then belongs on purge, not on the everyday act.

defects.defect: With a populated library, 41.6% of the desktop pane and 60.0% of the mobile pane is chrome before the first palette pixel; the mobile Library opens showing 1.7 of 12 palettes.
defects.evidence: probe/TELEMETRY-webkit.json. desktop-light-populated: paneRects y 102.9->876.9 (774px), gridRect y=424.9 -> 321.9px band = 41.6%, 4.0 of 12 cards visible at 112px pitch. mobile-light-populated: pane y 104->656 (552px), grid y=435.3 -> 331.3px = 60.0%, 1.7 cards visible. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:34 (law 8).
defects.mechanism: four support fixtures (title block, SearchBar, CurrentPaletteEditor plate, orphan trash row) stack above the protagonist inside the same scroll box, so the protagonist's first-paint share is whatever is left
defects.reproduction: Seed 12 palettes at localStorage `color-palettes`, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 1440x900 and at iPhone 14; measure `.palette-card-grid` getBoundingClientRect().y against `.pane-wrapper` .y. Screenshots probe/webkit-desktop-light-populated.png and probe/webkit-mobile-light-populated.png.
defects.proposedCure: Move the CurrentPaletteEditor and the destructive action out of the field and into the selected-inspector / action region of the owner workspace chassis (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:45). The field then starts immediately under the identity line and the band collapses to title + search.

defects.defect: The delete-all control has an inverted-gravity silhouette in both directions: 28x28 on desktop (smaller than the 36x36 per-card menu beside it) and a 44x44 isolated circular chip on mobile occupying the exact position and shape of a primary floating action button.
defects.evidence: probe/TELEMETRY-webkit.json: desktop trashRect {w:28,h:28} vs 12 `Palette menu` targets at 36x36; mobile trashRect {x:313,y:379,w:44,h:44} alone in a 56px band 56px above the first card (gridRect y=435.3). Visible in probe/webkit-mobile-light-populated.png. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 (law 5), :72 (law 7).
defects.mechanism: one untyped per-instance override (N-2) plus a producer coarse-pointer adaptation produce two different and both-wrong readings of the same destructive command
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with saved palettes at 1440x900 and at iPhone 14 and compare the trash control's box to the per-card menu's box.
defects.proposedCure: Same cure as N-4: the library-scope destructive command belongs in the workspace action region with a visible name, not floating unlabelled above the field at whatever size the viewport happens to give it.

defects.defect: The count badge nearly doubles its weight relative to the title on mobile, so a subordinate count reads almost as loud as the identity it annotates.
defects.evidence: probe/TELEMETRY-webkit.json computed font-size: desktop title 41.888px / badge 16.4px = 0.39; mobile title 25.888px / badge 21.0px = 0.81. Cause: the display-1 title floor-pins on phones (PaneHeader.vue:100-112) while the badge rung does not. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:34 (law 8).
defects.mechanism: two type rungs with different clamp behaviour paired by adjacency rather than by a locked ratio
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with >=1 palette at 1440x900 and at iPhone 14; read getComputedStyle on `.pane-header-title` and on the Badge.
defects.proposedCure: Pair the badge to the title through one clamp (the P019 paired-scale precedent) so the ratio is invariant across bands, rather than letting two independently-clamped rungs converge on phones.

defects.defect: In RTL the count badge renders before the noun it counts and flush against it: the heading reads `12 My Palettes` left-to-right with zero separation, because `ml-2` is a physical margin.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:22 `class="text-mono-small ml-2"`. Measured RTL: `margin-left: 8px`, `margin-inline-start: 0px`; badge box x=433.9 while the title block runs 224->686 (leftmost). LTR: both 8px. Photographed at probe/webkit-rtl-desktop-populated.png. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:151. Extends pass 3's D-28, which measured the gap but not the badge coordinate.
defects.mechanism: the one asymmetric spacing decision in the header was authored physically, and the badge's source position was chosen for LTR inline flow only
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with >=1 palette, then `document.documentElement.setAttribute('dir','rtl')`; the badge sits left of `My` touching the M. Two shared-atom bidi defects are visible in the same frame: the description renders `.Save, organize, and share your colors` and the placeholder `...Search your palettes`.
defects.proposedCure: `ms-2` fixes the gap; the ordering needs the badge to be a logically-later inline sibling of the ramped span. The two bidi defects belong to PaneHeader/SearchBar and need LTR isolation per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:154.

defects.defect: REPLICATED (pass 3). Dragging one card while a search filter is active silently rewrites the global order of the whole library: every matched palette is promoted to the head and every unmatched palette demoted, invisibly, persisted immediately, with no undo and no announcement.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:183-197 hands `useSortable` the filtered list and calls the global writer `pm.reorderPalettes(ids)`; usePaletteStore.ts:153-167 rebuilds the store as [given ids in order, ...everything else appended]. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:132 requires `position of total` announcement.
defects.mechanism: a view projection is used as the authority for a store-wide ordinal rewrite
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/challengeD-reorder-probe.mjs (Chromium, live :9000). Pasted output: BEFORE : Alpha,Bravo,Charlie,Delta,Echo,Foxtrot,Golf,Hotel / FILTERED: ["Foxtrot","Hotel"] (typed `ot`) / AFTER : Hotel,Foxtrot,Alpha,Bravo,Charlie,Delta,Echo,Golf / VISIBLE AFTER CLEAR: same. One local swap between items 6 and 8 produced a global re-shuffle of all eight.
defects.proposedCure: The reorder command must express a relative insertion (`move(id, before: id)`) that the store resolves against the full list, never a full-order array derived from a projection. Drag should additionally be disabled while a filter is active, since the ordinal the user manipulates and the ordinal the store writes are different quantities.

defects.defect: REPLICATED (pass 3). The empty state lies: with 12 palettes saved and a non-matching query the pane renders `My Palettes 12` in the header over `No saved palettes yet. / Add colors above, then save the set.`, and still offers the delete-all-twelve control. The advice is not merely unhelpful, it is wrong.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:77 keys on `filteredSaved.length === 0` while :79-80 supply copy true only when `savedPalettes.length === 0`; :20/:24 count `savedPalettes`. defects.mechanism: palettes-ramp.ts:117 certifies each stop with `certifyAccentInk(guarded, surfaceL, floor)`, an objective function that optimises WCAG contrast only; in dark the feasible band is near-white where chroma is arithmetically unavailable, so the walk destroys the exact quantity the ruling is about — inter-stop chromatic distance is not in the objective at all

defects.proposedCure: Add a chroma floor and a minimum inter-stop deltaE as hard constraints and solve lightness/contrast within them. In dark that means dropping off the near-white ceiling to roughly L 0.80-0.85, where the 3:1 large-text floor is still met with C >= 0.10. Identity is inter-stop distance; it must be an explicit term in the certification, not a hoped-for side effect.
