result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation (pass 4)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Seat spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; served tier matches. Not inherited, not downgraded.
result.strongestDefect: P-1 — a `localStorage` payload the deserializer's own validation ACCEPTS (`{"version":1}`) whiteouts the entire application on every route, permanently. Carried from pass 3 and independently re-confirmed this pass with my own contexts: bodyText 0, appHTML 167, canvas 0, 2 pageErrors on /#/, /#/palettes and /#/blob. The app cannot boot to repair the storage it poisoned, so the only user recovery is DevTools. Strongest NEW defect this pass is N-2 (dead `variant="ghost"` prop under Glass 7, which the HARD `vue-tsc` gate exits 0 on — a class of defect the toolchain structurally cannot detect, with 16 instances already shipped).
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — but these were checked first-hand this pass and found sound, so DEFECTIVE is not read wider than it is: the delete-all confirm dialog is well-behaved (trigger 28x28 ≥24px floor; focus moves to Cancel on open; role=dialog with aria-labelledby AND aria-describedby; Escape closes; focus RESTORED to the trigger — only aria-modal is absent, a glass-ui matter); the single nameless button on /#/palettes belongs to the DOCK (`.send-btn`), not this pane (seeded, the pane subtree has 0 nameless buttons out of 7); the header count badge is correct a11y (aria-hidden badge + sr-only companion, so AT never announces "My Palettes2"); zero `requestAnimationFrame` in demo/palettes (no PRM-RAF contribution); no `defineModel` (the stale-read hazard does not apply — both v-models write straight to injected refs); no ValueUnit, no WebGL, no `parseCssColor` call; `verbatimModuleSyntax` honoured (`import type { Palette }`); Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure used correctly on vue 3.5.35; `Badge variant=` IS legitimate (glass-ui Badge declares `variant`, unlike Button — do not sweep those with N-2); console/page errors clean on all four /#/palettes matrices; the store singleton lifecycle is sound (lazy, module-level, one binding, try/catch serializer); no god module (usePalettePorts is a genuine 5-port decomposition); `onCurrentPaletteSaved` is correctly local-first so a save with the backend down loses nothing.

defects.defect: A store payload that passes the deserializer's only validation check whiteouts the ENTIRE application on every route, permanently. `read()` casts instead of parsing: it checks only `typeof parsed.version === "number"` and never checks `palettes`. `savedPalettes` is a module-level computed doing `.filter()` on it, read in App's OWN template, so the error is above ErrorBoundary and the tree never mounts.
defects.evidence: usePaletteStore.ts:19-37 (read), :51-55 (computed), demo/color-picker/App.vue:154. My run of repro-C9-adjudicate.mjs: `P-1 version-only /#/ bodyText=0 appHTML=167 canvas=0 pageErrors=2 Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')` — identical on /#/palettes and /#/blob; control rows show bodyText 2060/274/750, canvas 2.
defects.mechanism: unvalidated-deserialization — a boundary that casts `unknown` into a typed shape instead of parsing it
defects.reproduction: localStorage['color-palettes'] = '{"version":1}' then load any route. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PalettesPane/repro-C9-adjudicate.mjs`
defects.proposedCure: `read()` is the single choke point for every store ingress — make it PARSE, not cast: validate array-ness and per-entry required fields, drop malformed entries, return defaultStore on total failure. Then `PaletteStore` becomes a type rather than an assertion, `savedPalettes` cannot throw, and the P-3 orphan class disappears with it. Second layer: nothing downstream of a localStorage read belongs unguarded on the root component's render path.

defects.defect: The FIRST drag-reorder of every page load scrambles the saved-palette order and persists it to localStorage. The pane hands `useSortable` a plain array snapshot (`pm.filteredSaved.value`) that IS the Vue computed's live cached array; vueuse's default `onUpdate` splices it in place with no copy; SortableJS fires `update` before `end`, so the pane's own `onEnd` re-reads an n-1 list and splices by the original indices.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:183 (`useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, …)`), :187-196 (onEnd), useFilteredList.ts:10 (returns items.value by identity), usePaletteStore.ts:51 + :163-165. Vendored proof: node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js defaultOptions.onUpdate spread BEFORE resetOptions, and `const array = _valueIsRef ? [...toValue(list)] : toValue(list)`; sortablejs/modular/sortable.esm.js:2002 ('update') then :2023 ('end'). Live: `EXPECTED Bravo Charlie Alpha Delta / ACTUAL store order Charlie Delta Bravo Alpha`. Offline harness prints `identity(list === filteredSaved.value): true`.
defects.mechanism: stale-snapshot binding — a value passed where a reactive binding was required, letting a third-party library mutate a computed's cache
defects.reproduction: `node .../repro-C1-live.mjs` (live dev server, real SortableJS mouse drag) and `npx vite-node .../repro-C1-sortable.ts` (offline, real modules). Drag #2 is clean (repro-C2-live.mjs), confirming the arm-once-per-mount shape; PaneSlot.vue:120 KeepAlive means it re-arms per page load and per cache eviction.
defects.proposedCure: The list argument is a binding, not a value. Hand useSortable the FULL saved order as a ref/getter and delete the hand-rolled onEnd entirely — moveArrayElement's isRef branch already copies-then-assigns correctly (requires a writable `savedPalettes` computed setter, or a `reorderPalettes(from, to)` port method). If onEnd is kept it must DISPLACE the default by also passing `onUpdate() {}`. Invariant to restore: nothing outside the store mutates a computed's cache.

defects.defect: Reordering while a search filter is active silently relocates every palette the filter excluded. `onEnd` builds its id list from the FILTERED projection, and `reorderPalettes` rebuilds the store from `orderedIds` first and appends everything else at the tail — so the matches are hoisted to the head of the library and the non-matches are banished to the end.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:190 (`pm.filteredSaved.value.map(p => p.id)`), usePaletteStore.ts:153-167 (the two-loop rebuild with the append-the-rest tail). Live: `filtered DOM ('l') : Alpha Charlie Delta (Bravo is filtered OUT)` → `full store order : Charlie Alpha Delta Bravo` — Bravo moved from index 1 to index 3 without being touched. Offline harness gives the identical result.
defects.mechanism: projection-as-total-order — a partial view used to express a complete ordering
defects.reproduction: `node .../repro-C2-live.mjs` section (b), and `npx vite-node .../repro-C1-sortable.ts` section C-2. Pass 3 declined to re-run this; measured live for the first time this pass.
defects.proposedCure: A projection cannot express a total order. Either map filtered indices back onto the full order before writing (reorderPalettes should take a complete order, or a (fromId, beforeId) pair), or — the KISS reading, and what every list app does — disable the sortable while a query is active.

defects.defect: `commitEdit` / `cancelEdit` never reach a handler. usePaneRouter supplies the listeners under kebab keys (`"onCommit-edit"`) in an untyped `Record<string, unknown>` prop bag, but Vue's emit resolves only `onCommitEdit`; its kebab-case fallback is gated on `isModelListener` (events starting with `update:`).

Vue source node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:4388 (`const isModelListener = event.startsWith("update:")`) and :4417-4418 (`if (!handler && isModelListener) handler = props[toHandlerKey(hyphenate(event))]`). defects.defect: NEW — the owner-RULED 'Palettes is rainbow' title (Q5 RULED 2026-07-09, T-43 owner-CONFIRMS) is NOT rainbow in dark scheme. The resolved ramp collapses to three near-identical near-whites and the title paints as flat white ink on both desktop and mobile dark.

Mechanism labelled a hypothesis; the chroma collapse and the flat render are measured.

defects.defect: NEW — `<Button variant="ghost">` on the delete-all trigger is a DEAD PROP under Glass 7. The Glass 7 Button API is {emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class} with no `variant`, so the attribute falls through inert and the button renders at the default `emphasis="secondary"` — a filled glass capsule, the exact opposite of the in-file ruled intent ('DEMOTED … to a quiet ghost'). The HARD demo typecheck cannot see it.

defects.defect: `cardRefs` never releases: the `:ref` callback's `el && (…)` guard swallows Vue's null-on-unmount call, so unmounted PaletteCard instances are retained forever. Upgraded this pass from pass-3's retention COUNTS to proof that the retained objects are DEAD — which makes `onPublish`'s `if (card)` guard vacuous and lets the publish result be written into a disposed instance and silently swallowed.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:84 (`:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.id] = el)"`), :177 (`reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`), :199-208 (await then `cardRefs[id].showFeedback`). Measured: with 6 seeded and the search narrowed to 1 card — `DOM cards while filtered: 1` but `{"keys":6}`; and the retained entries are `{"id":"id-Bravo","isUnmounted":true,"stillInDom":false}`.
defects.mechanism: imperative ref map as a feedback channel — state routed through component handles instead of through the port, with a guard that discards the release signal
defects.reproduction: `node .../repro-C3-a11y-refs.mjs` (retention across filter churn) and `node .../repro-C4-refs-dialog.mjs` (isUnmounted/stillInDom on the retained entries).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the ref map. The feedback message is STATE: put `{ id, message, variant }` on the library port and bind it as a prop to the card. The imperative `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` handle is the only reason the map exists, and it is what makes the leak load-bearing. If a map must survive, use a plain `Map` with an honest null-delete (`el => el ? map.set(id, el) : map.delete(id)`) — never `reactive()` over component instances.

defects.defect: Expand is keyboard-unreachable, and it gates every per-colour control in the pane. The expand gesture sits on a `role="article"` div with no tabindex and no keydown; the card menu offers no expand and no reorder. defects.defect: An `isLocal: true` palette with no `id` satisfies neither the saved nor the published projection: it is stored, invisible, uncounted, and it SURVIVES 'Delete all saved palettes' — whose dialog promises to permanently delete everything. Because the copy is private, no test, type, or build gate binds it to the definition, so it drifted. defects.defect: The hue-stability domain law is re-invented locally with a strictly weaker threshold. The colour session's law is `s·v > 0.01` (near-achromatic); the component substitutes `d === 0` (exact achromatic only).
defects.evidence: Canonical law, stated twice: demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:92 `if (s * v > 0.01) stableHue.value = channelNumber(hsv, "h")` and demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:43 `if (saturation * value > 0.01) stableHue.value = ...`, documented at useColorPipeline.ts:73-76 ('oklch→HSV loses hue at low chroma (atan2(0,0)=0)'). Local substitute: MiniColorPicker.vue:119 `if (d === 0) return; // keep existing hue`. Exhaustive measurement over all 16,777,216 sRGB hexes (scratchpad/huelaw.mjs): `divergence band: 4578 / 16777216 (0.027%)` — e.g. #000001 (s=1, v=0.0039, s·v=0.00392) where the component slams hue to 240 from a 1/255 channel difference while the canonical law holds it steady. Corroborating: the library itself returns hue "none" for #000000 (CSS Color 4 powerless channel) — the exact case the canonical law is built around and which `d === 0` handles only by accident, at a single point.
defects.mechanism: Copied-and-weakened domain law. A documented invariant of the colour model was re-derived from scratch by a component that cannot see the model.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/huelaw.mjs → 4,578/16,777,216 hexes in the divergence band. The band is small but is exactly the region users hit dragging into the black corner of the plate.
defects.proposedCure: Do not hold hue locally at all. Read HSVCurrentColor (useColorPipeline.ts:106-109), which already applies stableHue. Separately — and this is the real root cause — the law is written TWICE inside the session itself before this component wrote it a third time differently; export the 0.01 constant with a docstring exactly as spectrumLuma.ts:21 does for its 0.5 threshold.

IMPORTANT HONESTY QUALIFIER recorded in the report: the STRUCTURAL defect is CONFIRMED, but the contrast failure it would normally imply is a HYPOTHESIS, not observed — I captured the live plate and looked at it, and the white ring stays legible at the default position because shadow-cartoon-sm supplies an offset dark shadow the canonical instrument does not rely on. defects.defect: The component's public contract is a hex `string`, which caps the entire colour-search feature at 6-digit hex and produces a masking fallback in the parent that silently discards input the UI explicitly invites.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:65-74 types props/emits as bare `string`. Decode gate at :111 `if (!incomingHex || !incomingHex.startsWith("#") || incomingHex.length < 7) return;` silently rejects #48c, named colours, and every functional CSS colour — all of which the library accepts (scratchpad/cure.mjs section B). The cap propagates: SearchFilterBar.vue:92 advertises `placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)"` but :218 reads `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;` — a user who types the hsl(...) the placeholder invites gets the picker's current colour searched instead, with no error. The parent already imports the library-backed parseColorIn (SearchFilterBar.vue:137) that would parse it correctly.
defects.mechanism: A stringly-typed boundary between two components that both sit above a typed colour model, plus a masking fallback (edict 2: no masking fallbacks). Invalid states are representable because the contract is `string`.
defects.reproduction: Read SearchFilterBar.vue:92 against :218 — the regex is unambiguous. Typing `hsl(210 60% 50%)` into the colour field searches pickerHex instead. defects.proposedCure: Type the boundary as AnyColor / PickerColorIn<"hsv"> (both already exported from demo/color-session/picker-color.ts), making invalid states unrepresentable. SearchFilterBar then feeds parseColorIn(text, "oklab") directly and the advertised hsl(...) finally works. Delete the :218 fallback rather than fixing it.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/palettes/browser/dialog/VersionHistoryDrawer.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Seat declared explicitly at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — VersionHistoryDrawer never loads its version list on its FIRST open. `watch(() => open, …)` at VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:158 has no `immediate`, but BrowsePane.vue:275-278 flips `versionPalette` (the `v-if`) and `versionDrawerOpen` (the `:open`) in one synchronous handler, so the component's first render already has `open === true` and the watcher never fires. The mechanism is the library defect, not a watch typo: "when does the list load" has no owner — the host owns opening, the drawer owns loading, and the composable built to own both (`useVersionHistory`) is bypassed.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the overall verdict (DEFECTIVE), but the published-surface sub-axis is genuinely SOUND and proven positively: the drawer imports `@mkbabb/value.js` zero times and `@src` zero times (`grep -n "value.js\|@src" VersionHistoryDrawer.vue` → no output), so it makes no false claim about the public API. defects.defect: The drawer's version list never loads on first open: the sole load trigger is a non-immediate `watch(() => open)` while the host mounts the component already open.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/dialog/VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:158-167 (watch, no `immediate`); demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:157-165 (`v-if="versionPalette"` + `:open="versionDrawerOpen"`) and :275-278 (both flipped in one synchronous handler). defects.mechanism: Ownership split across a prop boundary: the host owns *when the drawer opens*, the drawer owns *when the list loads*, and the only coupling is a prop edge whose mount-time value a non-immediate watcher is structurally blind to. In-app path (currently blocked by §Reachability): open Browse, click a card with versionCount>1 → menu → Versions; the drawer renders empty; Escape and reopen → rows appear.

BrowsePane.onVersions calls `pm.versions.open(palette.slug)`. The failure class becomes unconstructible.

defects.defect: Two live implementations of the same version-paging state machine; 7 of useVersionHistory's 10 exported members are dead code, kept alive by a `fetchVersions` escape hatch that exists solely to license the duplicate.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useVersionHistory.ts:46-48 (versions/total/loading refs) and :65-86 (loadVersions/loadMore) vs demo/palettes/browser/dialog/VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:133-135 and :137-155 — the accumulate-or-replace body is verbatim identical. The hatch is self-documented at useVersionHistory.ts:27: `/** Fetch a single page of versions (raw; drawers manage their own list). */`. Grep census of every consumer: `grep -rn "\.versions\b|useVersionHistory|loadVersions|fetchVersions|listVersions" demo test e2e` → only BrowsePane.vue:279 (revert), useDialogBrowseActions.ts:55 (fork), VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:140 (fetchVersions). versions/total/loading/paletteSlug/loadVersions/loadMore/reset have ZERO consumers.
defects.mechanism: Dual path plus dead code (edict 2). The composable was authored to own the concern; the component refused it; instead of deleting the composable's stateful half, a raw accessor was added so both could coexist. Revert and list then acquired opposite ownership conventions inside one 168-line file.

defects.defect: A leaf presentational drawer imports the application composition root to obtain one injection Symbol, dragging 36 runtime modules — the whole admin console, both auth composables, slug migration, the palette store and the transport client — into its graph.
defects.evidence: VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:115 imports BROWSE_PORT_KEY from demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts (the module that constructs and provide()s all five ports, usePalettePorts.ts:242-246). Measured transitive crawl (type-only edges pruned): 36 demo modules, including demo/palettes/api/{admin-audit,admin-colors,admin-palettes,admin-users}.ts and demo/palettes/use{AdminAudit,AdminFlagged,AdminTags,AdminUsers,ColorNameQueue,SlugMigration}.ts. Counterfactual on the same crawler: demo/palettes/api/versions.ts = 4 modules; drawer + dateFormat + 2 UI barrels on top = 8. 36 → 8 is a 4.5x reduction with no behaviour change. BrowsePort itself is 32 members spanning browse+actions+admin+auth+versions+tagEdit+flagged (usePalettePorts.ts:157-192), despite the :21-31 comment claiming 'FIVE narrow, feature-owned ports'.
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of dependency (feature leaf → shell/composition root), disguised by a port abstraction that is itself a god module (edict 1). Any leaf injecting BrowsePort depends structurally on all 32 of its members.
defects.reproduction: python3 <scratchpad>/vhd-L/crawl.py demo/palettes/browser/dialog/VersionHistoryDrawer.vue — prints 'modules in graph: 36' for the runtime (type-pruned) crawl and the full file list; the same script on demo/palettes/api/versions.ts prints 4.
defects.proposedCure: With L-1/L-2 cured the drawer needs no port at all — it becomes props-in/events-out and its import of usePalettePorts disappears. If any leaf must still reach data directly, it should import the narrow transport module (api/versions.ts), never the module that provides the ports.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is 19 barrel files containing nothing but bare re-exports of @mkbabb/glass-ui — an alias layer with zero content and 48 consumers, including this component.
defects.evidence: `ls demo/ui/*/index.ts | wc -l` → 19; `find demo/ui -type f ! -name index.ts | wc -l` → 0; `cat demo/ui/*/index.ts | wc -l` → 29. demo/ui/dialog/index.ts is one line re-exporting eight Dialog symbols from '@mkbabb/glass-ui'; demo/ui/button/index.ts is `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. 48 demo files import through them. The drawer's own reach is VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:105-112 `from "../../../ui/dialog"` / `"../../../ui/button"` — a three-level climb out of browser/dialog/ into a demo-root directory. demo/ui/alert/index.ts's comment records that the directory once held real re-implementations and was converted to re-exports.
defects.mechanism: Legacy alias / wrapper directory (edicts 2 and 3). The migration to glass-ui was completed at the implementation level but the barrels were never deleted, so a boundary with no semantics is still encoded in 48 import paths.
defects.reproduction: for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do echo "=== $f ==="; cat "$f"; done — every file is a single re-export line.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ (19 files, 29 lines) and rewrite the 48 consumers to import '@mkbabb/glass-ui' / '@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms' directly. Mechanical, behaviour-preserving, and removes 2 modules from this component's graph.

defects.defect: The drawer never refetches when the host swaps paletteSlug/currentHash while it is open; the stale list then offers a Revert button whose hash belongs to a different palette, and the API's revert never scopes the hash lookup to the palette.
defects.evidence: VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:158 watches only `open`. Probe output: `[probe] props swapped while open → fetches before = 1 after = 1 | body text = "Version HistorySunset — 1 version v1 Jun 30, 08:00 PMSunset Revert"` — after paletteSlug became 'other' the row is still sunset's and the Revert control has appeared (the `(current)` suppression at :76 no longer matches). Host reassigns the prop at BrowsePane.vue:283 (`versionPalette.value = updated`). API side: api/src/modules/palette/repository/paletteVersion.ts:13-15 `findByHash` is `findOne({_id: hash})`, unscoped; api/src/modules/palette/service/versions.ts:103 + the following `$set` copies `version.name`/`version.colors` onto the target palette with no `version.paletteSlug === slug` assertion.
defects.mechanism: Identity (the slug prop, host-owned) and data (the list, drawer-owned) live on opposite sides of a boundary that should not exist, so they can disagree with no mechanism to notice.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED for the no-refetch half: npx vitest run --config <scratchpad>/vhd-L/probe.config.ts, third test ('open drawer, host swaps paletteSlug + currentHash'), fetch count unchanged at 1. HYPOTHESIS for the cross-palette write: today's single host closes the drawer between palettes (versionDrawerOpen false→true re-fires the watcher), so the slug never changes mid-open in practice — the trap is loaded, not sprung.
defects.proposedCure: Same transposition as L-1: identity and data in one cell inside useVersionHistory, so a slug change IS the reload. Independently, harden the API: scope revertToVersion's lookup to the palette (assert version.paletteSlug === slug).

defects.defect: 'How many versions a palette has' has two homes that provably diverge: the palette document's `versionCount` (card badge) and `listVersions().total` (drawer header and v-numbering).
defects.evidence: Card badge reads palette.versionCount at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue:101; drawer reads page.total at VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:11, :37 (`v{{ total - i }}`) and :89 (load-more gate). Divergence source: api/src/modules/palette/service/versions.ts (revertToVersion) runs `$inc: { versionCount: 1 }` unconditionally, while createVersionRecord (versions.ts:40-44) early-returns when a record with that content hash already exists — and a revert restores prior content, so its hash always exists. Deeper: version identity IS the content hash globally (`_id: hash`, versions.ts:60) while listVersions filters `{paletteSlug}` (repository/paletteVersion.ts:22). Live corroboration: `curl https://api.color.babb.dev/palettes?limit=50` shows hey-v2-cd3e1e3b-remix-fecce815 and hey-v2-cd3e1e3b-remix-2a95820d sharing the SAME currentHash 6691aae4.
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated across the API/demo seam: one concept, two independently-written numbers, plus a version-identity model that is global-by-content while the read path is scoped-by-palette.
defects.reproduction: Code-path proof pasted above (unconditional $inc vs early-return on existing hash). Live end-to-end reproduction NOT run: no public palette has versionCount > 1 (measured — all 10, hasMore:false), so no revert can be performed against the live commons.
defects.proposedCure: Derive versionCount from the palette_versions count rather than $inc-ing the document, so both surfaces read one number; and make version identity per-palette (composite {paletteSlug, hash}) rather than a global content hash, so a shared-content row cannot be invisible to one of its owners.

defects.defect: `demo/palettes/export.ts` and `demo/palettes/export/` are two live implementations of palette export; the app ships one and the byte-exactness test suite certifies the other.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn 'from "./export"|palettes/export/' demo test e2e` → demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts:9 imports './export' (the APP) and demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23 imports '../../palettes/export/serializers' (the TESTS). `ls demo/palettes/export/index.ts` → No such file or directory, so './export' resolves to export.ts (132 lines, 5 serializers + downloadExport). The 12-file export/ directory totals 914 lines (serializers 47, canonical 98, digest 77, rfc8785 46, bytes 45, png 213, svg 23, css 17, json 29, tailwind 22, reload 235, types 62) and has zero runtime consumers.
defects.mechanism: Dual path with the test gate pointed at the unused branch — the shipped serializers are untested and the tested serializers are unshipped. Same mechanism as L-2 at a larger radius.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'from "./export"\|palettes/export/' demo test e2e | grep -v node_modules; ls demo/palettes/export/index.ts
defects.proposedCure: Delete one implementation. Keep the decomposed export/ tree (it is the one with canonical/digest/rfc8785 rigor), give it an index.ts, repoint usePaletteExport at it, delete export.ts. One home, one gate.

defects.defect: The destructive Revert control is hover-only (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`) with no focus state, and it is a drifted second copy of an idiom that has no shared home.
defects.evidence: VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:79 `class="mt-2 h-7 text-caption opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100"`. The only other instance in the demo carries an extra state: `grep -rn "opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100" demo --include=*.vue` → demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:58 (`… group-hover:opacity-100 group-focus-visible:opacity-100`) vs VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:79 (hover only).
defects.mechanism: No unique home for 'reveal on interaction', so two hand-rolled copies drifted apart — one keyboard-aware, one not. `opacity-0` removes neither tab-order membership nor hit-testing, so the invisible destructive button remains focusable and tappable.
defects.reproduction: NONE — mechanism-proven from source. Live reproduction blocked: the drawer is unreachable in every running environment (see the reachability finding), so the touch-tap-on-invisible-Revert path could not be exercised.
defects.proposedCure: Move the idiom into glass-ui as one row-action / reveal-on-interaction primitive that pairs group-hover with group-focus-visible and drops to always-visible under `(hover: none)`; delete both inline recipes. Design-system concept, design-system home (edict 4).

defects.defect: Five DialogContent call sites carry four different per-instance sizing recipes; glass-ui owns drawer placement but not drawer size, so every consumer invents one.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "DialogContent" demo --include=*.vue`: PalettesPane.vue:103 and AdminUsersPanel.vue:159 (`surface="glass" :show-close="false"`), FlagReportDialog.vue:3 (`class="sm:max-w-md"`), VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:3 (`placement="right" class="w-[380px] sm:max-w-[420px] flex flex-col"`), MigratePalettesDialog.vue:3 (`class="rounded-dialog max-w-sm"`). The drawer's is the only one that also carries layout (flex flex-col) and a raw arbitrary pixel value.
defects.mechanism: Per-instance override of a design-system root component (edict 5). The placement concept was correctly lifted into glass-ui (the Glass 7 Sheet-onto-Dialog fold, noted at VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:5-8); the size concept was not, so it fragmented across consumers.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "DialogContent" demo --include=*.vue | grep -v node_modules
defects.proposedCure: Add a `size` variant to glass-ui's DialogContent covering the drawer width alongside the existing `placement`; collapse the four class-string dialects to one prop.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json's value.js `paths` block is 3/8 phantom, omits 2 real exports keys, and its load-bearing comment asserts a glass-ui import shape that does not exist.
defects.evidence: tsconfig.demo.json:31-46 declares 8 keys; package.json#exports and src/subpaths/ hold exactly 7 (color value css easing math transform quantize). `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts` → all three 'No such file or directory'; `/value` and `/css` are absent from paths entirely. Resolution still lands correctly via package self-reference — `npx tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --traceResolution | grep 'value.js/css'` → "successfully resolved to '/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts' with Package ID '@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts@4.0.0'". The comment at tsconfig.demo.json:18-22 claims glass-ui imports the core by the bare specifier; it does not: `grep -rho 'from "@mkbabb/value.js[^"]*"' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.js | sort | uniq -c` → 5 /color, 3 /css, 1 /easing, zero bare. vite.config.ts:37 calls the map a 'CLOSED 8-key set' while generating 7 aliases from it. Separately, node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js is a physically installed 4.0.0 copy (not a symlink) whose dist/subpaths/css.js hash differs from the repo's (8b53813… vs ca87007…) — currently shadowed by self-reference in both tsc and Vite, so inert.
defects.mechanism: Configuration documenting a shape the tree no longer has: dead map entries plus false prose (edict 2). Harmless today only because self-reference resolution masks it; a live footgun if either alias set is loosened.

defects.defect: A failed version fetch renders identically to 'this palette has no versions' — the feature's existing degraded-state affordance is not routed into the drawer.
defects.evidence: useVersionHistory.ts:59-62 catches, console.warns and returns undefined; VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:141 `if (!page) return;` inside a try/finally that clears `loading`. defects.reproduction: NONE — mechanism-proven from source; live reproduction blocked because the drawer is unreachable (no palette with versionCount>1; dev stack in the `misconfigured` latch).

defects.defect: The component is unreachable in every running environment: no public palette satisfies its entry gate, and the local dev stack cannot reach any API.
defects.evidence: Entry gate is demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue:94 `v-if="!palette.isLocal && (palette.versionCount ?? 0) > 1"`. Measured: `curl -s "https://api.color.babb.dev/palettes?limit=50"` returns 10 palettes with `hasMore: false`, every one at versionCount === 1 (hey-v2-cd3e1e3b-remix-fecce815, …-2a95820d, hey-v2-cd3e1e3b, hey-7600d315, audit-test-palette-51f63f52, lavender-dreams, forest-canopy, neon-cyberpunk, ocean-depths, sunset-blaze). Live Playwright drive of http://localhost:9000/#/browse shows the `misconfigured` latch banner ('dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`') and the wall in its 'The commons is unreachable. / Failed to load palettes / Retry' state, matching audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png. The only render site is the e2e fixture that hand-sets versionCount: 3 (e2e/smoke/oracles/o10d-display-voice-census.spec.ts:125), and that spec asserts only the title's typeface, never a row.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue (route /#/browse, two popovers deep)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — declared seat, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the picker drags on hover. Press-and-hold on the SV field, press Escape (which unmounts PopoverContent mid-press), release, reopen: canvasDragging is never cleared, so every subsequent bare pointermove with NO button pressed rewrites the color and stamps the parent's filter field. Reproduced 3x in independent runs (#406080 -> #17181a -> #174fe5 on hover alone; #993d3d -> #eb0c0c; #804080 -> #1a181a) and screenshotted. The cure exists one directory away in SpectrumCanvas.vue:18-19 (@pointercancel/@lostpointercapture + releaseCapture + onUnmounted).
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE

defects.defect: Stuck drag: pointer-capture taken on e.target and never released; canvasDragging/hueDragging are plain `let` flags cleared ONLY by pointerup on the element. No @pointercancel, no @lostpointercapture, no onUnmounted. When PopoverContent unmounts mid-press (Escape, outside click, the component's own `search` emit, route change, or an iOS scroll takeover firing pointercancel) the capture element dies before pointerup, so the flag stays true for the life of the MiniColorPicker instance — which outlives the popover content because the instance root is <Popover>, not <PopoverContent>. Thereafter every bare pointermove rewrites the color and emits update:hex into the parent's filter field.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue:79-80,127-133,142-148 (flags + setPointerCapture, no cancel/lost/unmount handlers). Live: `S2.1 pressed mid-canvas, hex: #406080 / S2.2 mini popover unmounted: true / S2.3 hover-only sweep: #406080 -> #17181a -> #174fe5  STUCK-DRAG: true` (playwright issued no mousedown after S2.2). Independent runs: `P7 hex before hover: #804080  after hover-only: #1a181a => STUCK DRAG: YES`; `T4 hover-only after Escape-mid-press: #993d3d -> #eb0c0c (pointer never pressed)`. Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/MiniColorPicker/evidence/mini-picker-stuck-drag.png. House cure present at demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue:18-19,81-91,168-175,217-224 and demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts:91-92.
defects.mechanism: drag-state flag never reset on interrupted pointer sequence; no pointer-capture recovery; state outlives the DOM that owned it
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/browse -> click the `⋮ Filters` button -> click the swatch (aria-label starts 'Open color picker') -> press-and-hold anywhere on the SV field -> press Escape -> release the button -> click the swatch again -> move the mouse across the SV field WITHOUT pressing. The color follows the cursor. Script: /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/mcp-live4.mjs (block S2).
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition: delete the hand-rolled pointer plumbing and consume the repo's already-hardened demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue (plus a glass-ui Slider for the hue rail). If a compact form is genuinely required it is a `size` prop on SpectrumCanvas, not a second implementation. Patch-level equivalent (inferior): bind @pointercancel/@lostpointercapture to a stopDragging() that also releasePointerCapture() in a try/catch, and clear both flags in onUnmounted.

defects.defect: The hex round-trip through the parent destroys hue AND saturation, and the thumb deserts the pointer. watch(currentHex) -> emit update:hex -> parent pickerHex -> :hex prop -> watch re-parse forms a closed loop through an 8-bit-per-channel hex, which is not injective for HSV. The `if (d === 0) return; // keep existing hue` guard catches only exact greys; near-black quantization garbage passes it and rewrites hue, and `sat.value = max === 0 ? 0 : d / max` has no guard at all.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:107,110-125 (esp. :118 sat, :119 the half-guard) + SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178. Live, pointer held at x=60% and dragged straight down: `P6 after pointerdown at x=60% y=15%: thumbStyle "left: 59.9078%" hex #5798d9 hueVar "--hue: 210;"` then `P6 after drag to BOTTOM (still x=60%): thumbStyle "left: 50%" hex #010202 hueVar "--hue: 180;"` — thumb renders at 50% while the pointer is at 60%, and hue flips 210->180 with no hue interaction. Algebraic (verbatim transcription of :85-125): `worst |Δsat| over 4000 random states: 0.7916 = thumb x-jump of 79.16% of canvas width`; `val=0.005 hex=#000101 -> sat becomes 1.0000 (was 0.7500)`; `updateCanvas(val=0) -> emit #000000 -> after prop round-trip {hue:210,sat:0,val:0} SATURATION CLOBBERED: YES`. House cure named in comment at SpectrumCanvas.vue:58-63 ('Raw spectrum coords to avoid HSV roundtrip jitter').
defects.mechanism: non-injective lossy round-trip used as the render source of truth; no pointer-space raw coordinate cache (the stableHue/rawS-rawV family of cure)
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/browse -> ⋮ Filters -> swatch -> press at 60% width / 15% height of the SV field and drag straight down to the bottom edge; observe the thumb's computed `left` (50%) versus the pointer (60%) and `--hue` flipping 210 -> 180. Scripts: scratchpad/mcp-live.mjs (block P6) and scratchpad/mcp-math.mjs (blocks C-1, C-7, C-8).
defects.proposedCure: Adopt SpectrumCanvas's rawS/rawV discipline: hold pointer-space coordinates as the render source of truth and clear them only when the color changes from a non-canvas source. Falls out for free by consuming SpectrumCanvas rather than re-implementing it.

defects.defect: The picker is 100% keyboard-inoperable and unnamed: both interactive surfaces are bare <div>s with role=null, tabindex=null, aria-label=null. The only focusable in the popover is the Search button, so Tab stop 1 and Tab stop 2 are the same element; arrow keys change nothing. The hex readout is a plain <span> with no aria-live. Focus is not restored to the trigger swatch on close.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:8-15 (SV div), :24-31 (hue div), :44-46 (readout span). Measured live: `R2 svAttrs: {"role":null,"tabindex":null,"aria":null}`, `R2 stripAttrs: {"role":null,"tabindex":null,"aria":null}`, `R2 hexReadout: {"tag":"SPAN","ariaLive":null}`, `P4 focusables inside mini popover: [{"tag":"BUTTON","text":"Search"}]`, `P5 tab stop 1: BUTTON|…|Search / P5 tab stop 2: BUTTON|…|Search`, `P5 hex before arrows: #4488cc after arrows: #4488cc => keyboard changes color: NO`. Focus: `S3.2 focus after the mini's Search closed it: {"cls":"absolute right-1 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/…"}` (the parent's inline Search button) and `S3.3 trigger swatch is: {"aria":"Open color picker, current color #4488cc","focused":false}`. WCAG 2.1.1 (A) and 2.4.3. House idiom + its ruling at SpectrumCanvas.vue:4-9 and ComponentSliders.vue:227-228.
defects.mechanism: interactive semantics implemented purely as pointer handlers on presentational divs; no role, no tab stop, no keyboard handler, no live region, no focus return
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/browse -> ⋮ Filters -> swatch -> press Tab repeatedly (only the Search button is ever focused) -> press ArrowRight/ArrowUp (the hex readout never changes). Then click the picker's Search button and inspect document.activeElement (it is the parent's inline Search button, not the trigger swatch). Script: scratchpad/mcp-live.mjs (P4/P5), mcp-live3.mjs (R2), mcp-live4.mjs (S3).
defects.proposedCure: SV field -> role="img" with a reactive descriptive aria-label (SpectrumCanvas's exact, already-ruled idiom). Hue rail -> the glass-ui Slider primitive (edict 4), which supplies role="slider", Arrow/Home/End operation, and an accessible name. Readout -> aria-live="polite". Close path -> dismiss through reka's own path so FocusScope restores the trigger, rather than flipping the `open` prop from the parent.

defects.defect: The hue rail is a 12px-tall drag target — half the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) 24px minimum — and both thumbs are sliced by overflow-hidden at every domain extreme, because the containers clip while the thumbs are -translate-x-1/2 / -translate-y-1/2.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:26 (`h-3` = 12px, `overflow-hidden`), :10 (`overflow-hidden`), :18 and :33 (translate). Measured on both matrices: `P10 {"cls":"relative w-full h-3 mt-2 rounded-f","w":174,"h":12}` and `R4 mobile geometry: {"hueStrip":[174,12],"hueThumb":[16,16],"searchBtn":[53,24]}`. Clipping: `T1 CLIPPED left px: 7  clipped top px: 7 (overflow: hidden)` on a 16px thumb, `T2 thumb overhang past right edge: 6 px => visible half-width: 6 of 12`. Screenshot: evidence/mini-picker-edges.png. Counter-example in house: SpectrumCanvas.vue:234 sets `overflow: visible` explicitly. Coverage note: the visual matrix never sees this component (two popovers deep) — REPORT.md's `/#/browse` row of 4 small tap targets counts four other elements, and shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png shows the trigger closed on an error-state pane.
defects.mechanism: target sized by a bare Tailwind height utility with no minimum-target floor; clipping container inherited from a decorative rounded-full treatment while the thumb is centre-translated
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/browse -> ⋮ Filters -> swatch; measure getBoundingClientRect() on the hue rail (174x12 desktop and mobile). Drag the SV thumb past the top-left corner and the hue thumb past the right end, then compare thumb rect to container rect. Script: scratchpad/mcp-live5.mjs (T1/T2) and mcp-live3.mjs (R4).
defects.proposedCure: Replace the rail with the glass-ui Slider (which ships a >=24px hit area with a visually thinner track) and set overflow: visible on the SV plate as SpectrumCanvas does — i.e. the same transposition that cures C-1/C-2/C-3. Separately: extend the visual-audit STATES matrix to open the ⋮ Filters popover and the swatch, so this component enters the tap-target budget at all.

defects.defect: The `hex?: string` prop contract is a lie and the divergence is never reported outward. The :111 guard silently discards anything that is not a >=7-char '#'-prefixed string, and parseInt's leniency accepts and mangles partial garbage; 8-digit alpha hex is truncated and the alpha destroyed on the echo; 3/4-digit hex and named/oklch colors are silently no-ops. Meanwhile the mount-time update:hex emission is measured NOT to reach the parent inside the reka popover, so the component can display one color while the parent believes another and never says so.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:65-68 (prop type), :110-125 (guard + parse), :107 (outward watch). Algebraic, verbatim transcription: `in="#12345g" -> emit #123405` (parseInt("5g",16)===5), `in="#zzzzzz" -> state {hue:null,…} -> emit #000000`, `in=#3b82f680 (50% alpha) -> emit #3b82f6 (alpha gone)`, `in=#f00 -> state UNCHANGED -> emit #528fcc (parent asked for #f00)`, `in=rebeccapurple / oklch(0.7 0.15 210) -> state UNCHANGED`. Missing mount emission: `Q1 t=1200ms after outer open: {"colorText":"","swatchLabel":"Open color picker, current color #4488cc"}`, `Q2 mini open: {"hexLabel":"#4488cc","colorText":""}`, `S1.2 after flipping Tier=Featured (forced parent re-render), field shows: ""` — yet hexLabel #4488cc proves sat moved 0.6->0.6667 (currentHex(210,0.6,0.8)==="#528fcc"), so currentHex did change. The identical logic DOES emit at mount outside the popover on the app's own Vue: `R1 vue version: 3.5.35 / R1 after MOUNT — emissions: [["emit","#4488cc","#4488cc"]]`. The parent already imports the real parser at SearchFilterBar.vue:145 (parseColorIn) and advertises `placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)"` at :92.
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled narrow parser + hand-rolled serializer standing in for the repo's own color pipeline, combined with an outward binding whose mount-time half is context-dependent on the Vue scheduler / reka Presence mount ordering
defects.reproduction: Contract half is PROVEN algebraically against a verbatim transcription of :85-125 (scratchpad/mcp-math.mjs, blocks C-2..C-5) but is currently LATENT through SearchFilterBar, which only ever feeds the component its own 6-digit output (SearchFilterBar.vue:170,176,181). Missing-mount-emit half is PROVEN live: http://localhost:9000/#/browse -> ⋮ Filters -> read the 'Search by CSS color' field (empty) while the swatch reads #4488cc, then flip Tier=Featured to force a parent re-render — still empty (scratchpad/mcp-live2.mjs Q1/Q2, mcp-live4.mjs S1). Isolated control: scratchpad/mcp-live3.mjs block R1.
defects.proposedCure: Stop hand-rolling both directions. Parse with the repo's own parseColorIn (already imported by the parent at SearchFilterBar.vue:145, fronting parsePickerColor/convertPickerColor), hold the value as a PickerColor, and serialize to hex only at the readout. That deletes the 20-line inline HSV->hex switch (:85-105) and the 15-line inline hex->HSV block (:110-125), both duplicating src/units/color, and makes the prop accept what its type and the sibling field's placeholder already promise.

defects.defect: Neither drag surface sets touch-action, and there is no touch gate — so a vertical drag inside a scrollable popover is eligible to be claimed by the scroller, and the claim arrives as pointercancel, which this component does not handle (C-1). This is the iOS Safari detonation path for the stuck-drag flag.
defects.evidence: Measured: `R2 svTouchAction: "auto"  stripTouchAction: "auto"`, `R4 mobile stripTouchAction: "auto"`. On the emulated mobile matrix the drag currently does follow (`S4.1 touch drag down the SV canvas: #4488cc -> mid: #185da3 … followed: true`, `S4.3 page scrollY: 0`). House cure at SpectrumCanvas.vue:11-21 (touch-gate-target + useTouchGate() + @touchmove.passive + @touchend.passive, tap-to-activate).
defects.mechanism: missing touch-action declaration + missing tap-to-activate gate on a pointer-drag surface inside a scroll container
defects.reproduction: Measured facts (touch-action: auto on both surfaces; no pointercancel handler) are PROVEN — scratchpad/mcp-live3.mjs (R2/R4). The scroll-steal-on-real-iOS-Safari half is a HYPOTHESIS: Chromium mobile emulation did not steal the gesture, and no real-device probe was run.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt useTouchGate + the touch-gate-target class from SpectrumCanvas (which also sets the tap-to-activate contract the rest of the picker already uses), which subsumes touch-action handling — again, free upon consuming SpectrumCanvas rather than duplicating it.

defects.defect: The hue rail's gradient is seven raw hex literals in a per-instance inline style attribute, contradicting the file's own scoped-style comment eight lines below and the repo's token-routing precedent.

defects.reproduction: Read demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue:27 and :158 — the file states the rule and breaks it on the adjacent element. No runtime repro needed.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the rail with its gradient when the glass-ui Slider lands (C-3); until then move it into the scoped block as a class beside .sv-canvas, expressed in tokens.

Weaker mutations that also stay green: swap sat.value and val.value in updateCanvas (:138-139); make currentHex return "#000000" unconditionally; delete both @pointerup bindings.
defects.proposedCure: Add a component test with three assertions, each of which fails today: (a) press, unmount mid-press, remount, then move — the value must NOT change (C-1); (b) hsv -> hex -> hsv must be a fixed point for the rendered thumb position (C-2); (c) arrow keys must move the value (C-3). Pair with a visual-audit STATES entry that opens ⋮ Filters and the swatch so the component enters the 60-capture defect budget.

result.axis: D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Seat declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the component should not exist. `MiniColorPicker.vue:85-125` hand-rolls HSV↔RGB↔hex inside the demo of a colour-conversion library, one line from a parent that already imports `parseColorIn` (`SearchFilterBar.vue:145`), duplicating both the product's own spectrum instrument (`SpectrumCanvas.vue`) and the producer's `Slider variant="spectrum"` that this same repo already consumes at `ComponentSliders.vue:64-82`. Every other finding — no keyboard path, unreachable on mobile, stuck drag, wide-gamut clobber, 2.46× non-uniform rail, 40.5% parent eclipse — is a symptom of that one architectural error. Its sharpest single proof is D-5: typing `oklch(0.72 0.31 145)` and tapping the field once yields `#567695` (probe5.json) — the "Find by Color" instrument silently destroys the colour the field next to it accepted.

defects.defect: A second, private, inferior colour instrument hand-rolled inside a colour library's own demo — 40 lines of HSV↔RGB↔hex maths plus a bespoke SV plane and hue rail, duplicating both the product's route-`/` spectrum instrument and a producer Slider variant the repo already consumes.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:85-125 (hand-rolled HSV maths); SearchFilterBar.vue:145 already imports `parseColorIn`; SpectrumCanvas.vue:7-9,18-19,54,78-91,97-108,217-224 is the real instrument with aria, touch gate, capture release, pointercancel/lostpointercapture, rAF throttle and unmount teardown; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/slider/types.d.ts:4,18 declares `variant: "standard" | "spectrum"`; demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:64-72 already consumes `<Slider variant="spectrum">`
defects.mechanism: design-system boundary breach: reimplementing a producer primitive and a sibling feature component instead of consuming them (owner edicts 3 and 4)
defects.reproduction: Static read of MiniColorPicker.vue:85-125 against SpectrumCanvas.vue and glass-ui/dist/components/slider/types.d.ts:4,18; `grep -n variant demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue` → line 67 `variant="spectrum"`
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue. `Find by Color` becomes one row: the existing Input (which already parses full CSS via parseColorIn) plus a non-interactive specimen dot; if a chromatic affordance is still wanted it is one `<Slider variant="spectrum">` bound to the OKLCH hue of the typed colour, per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:104's single domain-neutral axis composition.

defects.defect: The component cannot be opened on mobile or at 200% zoom: its trigger sits below the fold inside a non-scrolling overlay with zero scroll containers on the path.

Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:32 §3.6; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:16 (400%-zoom arm).
defects.mechanism: no mobile composition — a fixed-height 459px overlay on a 664px viewport with no max-height, no internal scroller and a non-scrolling document
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/MiniColorPicker/probe2.mjs — the mobile-light and mobile-dark and zoom-200 blocks; the click on `button[aria-label^="Open color picker"]` is refused as outside the viewport
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1: with the picker deleted, `Find by Color` is one row inside the menu rather than a second overlay. The mobile law is the acceptance test — the whole group must be reachable and operable at 390×664 and at actual 200%/400% in-app zoom, in the document-scrolling sequence VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:32 names.

defects.defect: Neither spatial axis has any keyboard path. Of the three controls in the surface, exactly one is focusable; the SV field and hue rail carry no role, no accessible name, no tabindex, no Home/End and no numeric equivalent.
defects.evidence: probe.json desktop-light.census.focusables = [{"tag":"button","name":"Search"}] (the complete inventory); desktop-light.keyboard = {"canvasFocusable":false,"railFocusable":false}; census canvasRole null, canvasAriaLabel null, canvasTabIndex null, railRole null, railTabIndex null. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:99 §5 ("every spatial action has a keyboard/numeric equivalent"), :125 §5.2 Spectrum-coordinates row ("pointer canvas is not the sole keyboard control"), PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 §5.5 ("operable ornaments without names are forbidden").
defects.mechanism: raw <div> + pointer handlers used where a named, roled control is required; no producer control consumed
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/MiniColorPicker/probe.mjs → desktop-light.keyboard and desktop-light.census.focusables
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1. `<Slider variant="spectrum">` supplies role=slider, accessible name, arrow keys, Home/End, aria-valuetext, RTL and the producer focus ring with no local code; the 2D coordinate, if retained at all, must expose two named numeric axes per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:125.

defects.defect: An interrupted drag leaves the drag flag set forever; after it, hovering the field with no button pressed rewrites the colour and the parent's text input.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:79-80 `let canvasDragging = false; let hueDragging = false;`; :133 `onCanvasUp` is the only clear; no pointercancel, no lostpointercapture, no onUnmounted; the `<Popover>` root never unmounts so the flag survives close/open. Measured probe2.json desktop-deep.stuckDrag = {"beforeHover":"#406080","afterHover":"#18a2e7","mutatedByHoverAlone":true}. Cure precedent: SpectrumCanvas.vue:18-19,168-175,217-224.
defects.mechanism: drag state held in un-torn-down setup-scope mutable flags with no pointer-cancellation contract
defects.reproduction: node .../probe2.mjs desktop-deep block: mouse.down at the SV field centre → press Escape (PopoverContent unmounts mid-press) → mouse.up over nothing → reopen the picker → move the mouse across the field with NO button pressed → hex changes #406080 → #18a2e7
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1 (the producer Slider owns its own press lifecycle). If any pointer canvas survives anywhere, it must adopt SpectrumCanvas's contract wholesale: capture tracking with explicit release, pointercancel + lostpointercapture handlers, and onUnmounted teardown.

defects.defect: One tap on the SV field silently destroys an authored wide-gamut CSS colour, replacing it with an unrelated sRGB hex.
defects.evidence: probe5.json = {"typed":"oklch(0.72 0.31 145)","afterOpen":"oklch(0.72 0.31 145)","afterOneTap":"#567695","clobbered":true}. Path: MiniColorPicker.vue:103-104 (hex is the only emittable form) → :107 watch(currentHex) → SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178 writes both pickerHex and colorText. The replacement is not even the sRGB projection of the typed colour — the picker never parsed it and is still on its private hue of 210°.
defects.mechanism: two disconnected colour models sharing one output slot, with the narrower (sRGB-HSV, 8-bit) one holding the write
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/MiniColorPicker/probe5.mjs — type `oklch(0.72 0.31 145)` into the `Search by CSS color` input, open the picker, one pointer press at (0.42, 0.42) of the field; the input reads `#567695`
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1: one colour model, the product's own, owned by the Input + parseColorIn. No instrument may write a lossy projection over an authored value; if a chromatic control edits the value it must edit the parsed model, not replace it with a hex.

defects.defect: The 8-bit hex round-trip is a closed feedback loop: one tap near the bottom of the field moves the thumb 16.7% (29 px) away from the pointer and jumps the untouched hue rail from 210° to 240°, permanently.
defects.evidence: Loop: MiniColorPicker.vue:107 emit → SearchFilterBar.vue:176 pickerHex → prop → MiniColorPicker.vue:110-125 re-derives sat/val/hue from the quantised hex. Measured probe.json desktop-light.drive: center (0.5,0.5) → hex #406080, thumbLeft 50%, hueLeft 58.333333%; bottomCenter (0.5,0.995) → hex #020203, thumbLeft 33.333333%, hueLeft 66.666667%. #020203 has max=3/255, d=1/255 → sat=0.333 and max===b forces h=240°. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:135 ("Pointer drag, arrow movement, and numeric entry must resolve to the same model value").
defects.mechanism: lossy round-trip through an 8-bit sRGB hex used as the interchange between parent and child, with error amplified by sat = d/max as max → 0
defects.reproduction: node .../probe.mjs → desktop-light.drive.center vs desktop-light.drive.bottomCenter
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1. Structurally: the continuous model must be the source of truth and never be reconstructed from its quantised serialisation — exactly the rawS/rawV + spectrumIsSource guard SpectrumCanvas.vue:58-75 already implements.

defects.defect: The position marker is invisible and half-clipped in exactly the corner it must indicate most precisely: white ring on white field, and 50.9% of the thumb cut away by overflow-hidden.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:10 `overflow-hidden`, :18-19 `border-2 border-white` with `background: currentHex` at `left: sat%` / `top: (1-val)%` and -translate-*-1/2. At sat→0,val→1 the measured gradient stack (probe.json canvasStyle.backgroundImage) composites to exactly #ffffff and currentHex is #ffffff → contrast 1.00:1. Pixel-sampled from shots/desktop-light-mini-topleft.png: thumb fill (247,247,251), ring (255,255,255), adjacent field (231,233,249) → WCAG 1.069:1 and 1.205:1; the row scan at y=32 shows popover chrome (229,218,208) immediately left of the thumb, i.e. no left/top arc at all. probe.json desktop-light.drive.topLeft.thumbHiddenPct = 50.9; bottomCenter 35.6; rightEdge 35.4; hueRail.handleHiddenPct 32.9. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 §5.8.
defects.mechanism: scheme- and content-invariant #fff marker inside an overflow-clipped box whose own gradient reaches #fff, with the cartoon shadow offset away from the clipped edge
defects.reproduction: node .../probe.mjs (drive.topLeft), then `python3` PIL sample of shots/desktop-light-mini-topleft.png at row y=32, x=26..47
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1. Structurally: a position marker must not be clipped by its own field (allow overflow or inset the travel), and must carry a contrast-independent ring — the WatercolorDot + `--dot-border` treatment SpectrumCanvas.vue:259-270 already uses.

defects.defect: Three of the component's six local style overrides are inert: the surface it specifies is not the surface that ships, and the typecheck is green about it.
defects.evidence: probe2.json desktop-deep.type — dialogClassList includes both `px-(--overlay-pad-inline) py-(--overlay-pad-block)` and `p-2.5` with dialogPadding `20.351999px 16px` (not 10px); miniSearchStyle height `36px` / minHeight `36px` against `h-6`; searchBtnAttrs contains a raw `variant=outline` DOM attribute alongside `data-emphasis=secondary`. glass-ui 7.0.0 Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 declares no `variant` (the axis is `emphasis`). `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` returns clean. Applied: w-52 → 208px, size=sm → data-size=sm, text-micro → 11px. Law: owner edict 5 (root-level styling).
defects.mechanism: per-instance utility overrides racing a producer root's own utilities of equal specificity, plus a non-existent prop falling through as a DOM attribute
defects.reproduction: node .../probe2.mjs → desktop-deep.type; `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` (clean); `sed -n '1,20p' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts`
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three dead overrides on sight. If the producer's padding rung, size rung or emphasis axis is wrong for a surface, that is a glass-ui BH/BI relay (a producer variant), never a local class or an invented prop.

defects.defect: Two buttons named `Search`, 64 px apart in one frame, 36 px vs 24 px tall, built two different ways, one with a pending state and one without.

Child: MiniColorPicker.vue:47-54 (glass-ui Button). Parent: SearchFilterBar.vue:97-104 (raw <button> with Loader2 + disabled arm). `searching` (SearchFilterBar.vue:173) is never passed down. defects.defect: The hue rail is a hand-rolled six-stop sRGB rainbow div where the producer ships `Slider variant="spectrum"`, and it is perceptually non-uniform by 2.461× in the product's own OKLCH ground.
defects.evidence: MiniColorPicker.vue:24-36 (div + inline gradient + three raw pointer handlers + absolute handle). Producer: glass-ui/dist/components/slider/types.d.ts:4,18; already consumed at ComponentSliders.vue:64-72. Measured with the repo's OWN library (dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js, convertColor(parseCssColor(stop),"oklch")): OKLCH hue at the seven stops 29.23, 109.77, 142.50, 194.77, 264.05, 328.36, 29.23; arc per equal sixth 80.54, 32.73, 52.27, 69.28, 64.31, 60.87 (sum 360.00); over the measured 174px rail that is 2.777 … 1.128 deg/px; max/min gain ratio 2.461. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:5,7 (chromatic laboratory / liquid-colour rail), :158 (OKLCH seed ground).
defects.mechanism: a linear sRGB primary/secondary interpolation used as a perceptual hue axis, in place of the producer's spectrum track

defects.defect: The child dialog eclipses 40.5% of its own parent's area, as a portalled DOM sibling rather than a contained disclosure, through two translucent surfaces that stack three legible text layers.
defects.evidence: probe.json desktop-light.census: miniRect 208×218.7 @ (462,560), outerRect 240×468.1 @ (433,381), eclipsePct 40.5, nested false, dialogCount 2, both surfaces backgroundColor alpha 0.808 with backdrop-filter blur(11px). defects.reproduction: node .../probe.mjs → desktop-light.census.eclipsePct / nested / dialogCount; read shots/desktop-light-mini.png and shots/mobile-light-mini-forced.png

defects.defect: Both drag surfaces declare `touch-action: auto` with no touch gate, and the hue rail's operable height is 12 px against a 24 px WCAG 2.2 floor.
defects.evidence: probe2.json mobile-light.forced = {"touchActionCanvas":"auto","touchActionRail":"auto","railH":12}; probe.json desktop-light.census.canvasStyle.touchAction / railStyle.touchAction both "auto"; railRect 174×12 and railHandleRect 12×12. Cure precedent in-repo: SpectrumCanvas.vue:11-21,54,138-146 (`useTouchGate`, touch-gate-target/active). Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72 §5.7 and :56 PR-12 ("Invisible/seat geometry preserves target floor while optics follow rung").
defects.mechanism: a pointer-drag surface with no touch-action contract and no invisible operable seat under an intentionally thin optic
defects.reproduction: node .../probe2.mjs → mobile-light.forced.touchActionCanvas / touchActionRail / railH
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1 — the producer Slider owns touch-action and the seat. Structurally: the 12px optic is legitimate; the missing ≥24px invisible seat and `touch-action: none` are not optional.

defects.defect: The hex readout ships in ITALIC because the component composed glass-ui's serif-italic figure-caption role and cancelled only its font-family, and `text-caption`/`text-micro` are outside the constitution's closed type matrix.
defects.evidence: probe2.json desktop-deep.type.readout = {"fontSize":"14.384px","fontStyle":"italic","fontWeight":"400","fontFamily":"\"Fira Code\""}; probe4.mjs inheritance chain shows the parent div is font-style normal, so italic is set on the span itself. Source: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/semantic.css — `@utility text-caption { font-family: var(--font-text); font-size: var(--type-caption); line-height: var(--type-leading-caption); font-style: italic; font-weight: 400; }`. Component: MiniColorPicker.vue:44 `class="fira-code text-caption …"`, :50 `text-micro`. The wanted role already exists: `@utility text-mono-small` in typography/utilities.css. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:68-78 §4 is a closed matrix.
defects.mechanism: role-splicing — adopting a producer semantic role and overriding half of it, keeping the half that was never wanted

defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1. If a 2D field survives anywhere, its aspect is a deliberate proportion decision with a register row, not a leftover of the container width.

defects.defect: Five states were never designed: no empty, loading, error, disabled or pending arm; dragging is broken; focus exists on 1 of 3 controls; forced-colors is untreated; and `truncate` guards a state that cannot occur.
defects.evidence: `searching` (SearchFilterBar.vue:173) is never passed to the child, and glass-ui `ButtonProps.loading` (Button.vue.d.ts:14) is unused; MiniColorPicker.vue:111 returns silently on any malformed incoming hex with no aria-invalid, message or live region; no `disabled` prop or styling on any control; probe.json focusables = 1 of 3; both instruments are pure background-image so a forced-colors backplate flattens them (HYPOTHESIS — WebKit does not truly emulate forced-colors); :44 `truncate` on a span that can only hold 7 characters. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:52 PR-08.
defects.mechanism: a single happy-path state design — every other state renders as the populated state or as absence
defects.reproduction: State-by-state enumeration in the report §D-17; measured rows from probe.json/probe2.json, with the forced-colors row explicitly labelled a hypothesis
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1: the surviving Input row inherits the producer's disabled/invalid/loading arms and gains the real error arm the colour parse needs. No new state machinery — consume the producer's.

defects.defect: A non-role radius token, and a producer utility shadowed locally with its font-feature-settings dropped.
