result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue, area palettes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — claude-opus-5[1m] (1M context), the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with; declared, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: F-3 — the Delete button does not clear the flag queue: the server soft-deletes the palette and never cascades its flags (api/src/modules/admin/service/palettes.ts:53-79, whose own docstring L6 falsely claims "cascade votes/flags"), while the panel optimistically splices the row out locally (useAdminFlagged.ts:93-103). The flagged $lookup has no deletedAt filter (flag.ts:88-95), so on the next refresh the row returns FULLY POPULATED and indistinguishable from a live palette. A moderator deletes an abusive palette, watches it vanish, and it is back — permanently untriageable except by pressing Dismiss, which records the opposite verdict.
result.negativeProof: Cleared by measurement, not by assumption: (1) tap targets — h-7 px-2 = 28x28 CSS px, above the 24x24 AA floor; REPORT.json for /#/admin/flagged lists 4 small targets and all four (Switch to slug / Generate new slug / Cancel / a 160x23 input) belong to the slug bar, with namelessButtons: 0 on all four matrices; (2) Badge tone="destructive" IS a valid glass-ui 7 prop (dist/components/badge/index.d.ts TONE map) — correctly used; (3) EmptyState's error variant carries role="alert" (EmptyState.vue:17) and every prop the panel passes exists; (4) verbatimModuleSyntax clean — all SFC imports are value imports; (5) none of the repo's known local hazards apply here — no defineModel, no oklch->HSV roundtrip, no ValueUnit wrapping, no reka-ui slider, ZERO requestAnimationFrame (not a PRM-RAF site), no WebGL, no parseCssColor (c.css goes straight to backgroundColor where CSS drops malformed values); (6) the component registers no listeners, timers or observers, so there is nothing to leak — onMounted(loadFlagged) is the entire lifecycle and the port is a composition-root singleton; (7) my deletePaletteAdmin 204-crash hypothesis DIED against the real route, which returns 200 {deleted:true} (admin/routes/palettes.ts:40) — only the e2e fixture models the dangerous shape.

defects.defect: With no admin token, loadFlagged returns before issuing any request and sets no state, so the panel renders the TRUE-EMPTY plate and asserts an empty moderation queue: '0 flagged' / '· nothing flagged ·' / 'No flagged palettes.' The panel is not auth-gated (AdminPane.vue:64 mounts on route alone), so this is the default state for every non-admin who reaches /#/admin/flagged. It is the exact P0 the file's own comment at L20-21 forbids ('error != empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear moderation queue'), arriving through the auth door the comment did not watch.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:59-62 (`const token = getToken(); if (!token) return;`); AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:5-7, :37-41; live capture docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-flagged.png shows '0 flagged / · NOTHING FLAGGED · / No flagged palettes.' with REPORT.json results[/#/admin/flagged].consoleErrors=[] and failedRequests=[]; family: useAdminAudit.ts:49-50, useAdminUsers.ts:56,73,84,107,118,133
defects.mechanism: M-A: the state machine is not a machine — 'unauthenticated' is unmodelled, so it collapses into the same shape as 'confirmed empty'
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-composable.test.ts, C5): mock getToken -> null, await loadFlagged() → `C5 requests = 0 | loading = false | loadError = null | items = 0 → template branch = "No flagged palettes."`. Also visible in the shipped Safari capture named above.
defects.proposedCure: Model it as a state, not an early return: a single discriminated FlaggedState = {unauthenticated}|{loading}|{error}|{empty}|{rows} computed in useAdminFlagged, with the template total over state.kind. The unauthenticated arm renders a sign-in prompt; no arm can ever claim 'empty' without a completed 200.

defects.defect: The 'palette deleted' annotation (the W5-5/F-11 cure) is unreachable dead code. The server never sends `palette: null`; the aggregation's computed $project sub-document emits an EMPTY OBJECT `{}` when the $lookup misses, which is truthy, so `v-if="!item.palette"` never fires. What renders instead is a bare slug with an empty swatch strip and no annotation — verbatim the thing the comment at L68-70 says must never happen. The client type declares the fiction (`palette: Palette | null`).
defects.evidence: api/src/modules/palette/repository/flag.ts:99-113 ($project palette:{name:"$palette.name",…}); demo/palettes/types.ts:110-115; AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:66, :68-75
defects.mechanism: M-D: contract fiction — the cure was written against the intended shape and never checked against the wire
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/probe-flagged.mjs, real MongoDB via the repo's own mongodb-memory-server, pipeline copied verbatim): `slug=p3  'palette' in row = true  palette={}  Boolean(palette)=true  name=undefined → template v-if="!item.palette" fires: false | header renders: p3`. Then EXECUTED against the real SFC (repro/flagged-repro.test.ts R3/R3b): `R3 text = "1 flagged sunset-riot-9a3f2 Dismiss spamjunkJul 4"`, `R3 swatch count = 0`, no 'palette deleted'; fed the DECLARED palette:null the annotation does appear.
defects.proposedCure: Stop branching on object truthiness. Fix the projection to emit a real null ($cond/$ifNull), correct demo/palettes/types.ts:112 to the wire (`palette?: Partial<Palette>`), and branch on a field only a live palette has (item.palette?.slug). Ship both halves together or the annotation stays dead.

defects.defect: Delete does not clear the flag queue. The admin delete soft-deletes the palette and never cascades its flags, and the flagged aggregation's $lookup has no deletedAt filter, so the row survives server-side AND rejoins fully populated. The panel meanwhile splices the row out locally and decrements total, so the moderator is told the opposite of the truth. Server-side `total` (countDistinctPalettes over flags) is unchanged by a delete, so the client counter also drifts permanently.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:93-103; api/src/modules/admin/service/palettes.ts:53-79 (no flags touched; module docstring L6 claims 'delete palette + cascade votes/flags'); api/src/modules/palette/repository/flag.ts:88-95 ($lookup on slug, no deletedAt filter); api/src/modules/palette/repository/flag.ts:117-129 (countDistinctPalettes)
defects.mechanism: M-B: optimistic local mutation without server truth, compounded by a missing backend cascade
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-composable.test.ts, C6): `C6 after delete → items = 0 | total = 0` then `C6 after refresh → items = 1 | total = 1`. The 'looks alive' half is EXECUTED in repro/probe-flagged.mjs: the soft-deleted p2 joins with `palette={"name":"SoftDeleted","colors":[{"css":"#000"}],…}`.
defects.proposedCure: Client: await the mutation then reload from the server (never splice-and-decrement). Backend (relay to the API owner): call flags.deleteByPaletteSlug(slug) inside deletePalette's existing withTransaction — the repository method already exists — and filter deletedAt in the flagged $lookup so the queue means what it says.

defects.defect: The row v-for is NOT part of the v-if/v-else-if chain, and loadFlagged's catch never clears items. Result: the 'The flag queue is unreachable.' role=alert plate renders ON TOP OF a full, clickable moderation list (whose Dismiss/Delete will now fail silently against the dead backend the alert just named), and a refresh paints two loading skeletons above the still-present rows.
defects.evidence: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18 (v-if), :22-33 (v-else-if error), :37-41 (v-else-if empty), :44 (v-for — an independent element); demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:72-78 (catch leaves items intact)
defects.mechanism: M-A: the render arms are neither mutually exclusive nor exhaustive, so impossible states are reachable
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-repro.test.ts): `R1 skeletons = 2 | stale row rendered = true`; `R2 text = "1 flagged The flag queue is unreachable.Backend unreachable Retry Sunset Riotcrimson-owl-772 Dismiss spamjunkJul 4"`.
defects.proposedCure: One chain, one arm each: put the row list inside the {kind:'rows'} arm of the single discriminated state (see F-1's cure). The count, the pager and the rows then exist only where data exists.

defects.defect: Emptying the last page strands the panel with no way back. pageCount is derived from the locally-decremented total, and PaginationBar renders only when pageCount > 1 — so dismissing the last row of the last page leaves 0 rows on page 2, total 20, pageCount 1, hasPrev true, and the pager UNMOUNTED. The panel then displays 'No flagged palettes.' while 20 remain, and Refresh re-requests offset=20 forever. Only unmounting the panel escapes.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:55 (pageCount), :87 and :99 (total decrements), :105-117 (nextPage/prevPage); demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:3 (`v-if="pageCount > 1"`)
defects.mechanism: M-B: local counter arithmetic drives a control's existence, so a mutation can delete the user's own escape hatch
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-composable.test.ts, C3): total 21, page 2, dismiss the one row → `C3 page = 2 | items = 0 | total = 20 | pageCount = 1 | hasPrev = true | PaginationBar rendered = false`.
defects.proposedCure: Reload from the server after every mutation with page clamping (page = min(page, pageCount)); never derive control visibility from an optimistically mutated counter.

defects.defect: loadFlagged has no request identity — no sequence token, no AbortController — and nextPage/prevPage fire it without awaiting. An out-of-order response paints the WRONG page's rows under the new pager, and a double-click on Next skips a page entirely while leaving the loser in flight to overwrite the winner. The boolean `loading` flag is cleared by whichever finally runs first, so the skeleton disappears while a request is still open and the un-disabled Refresh stays armed for spamming.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:59-79 (no sequencing; `loading` is a plain boolean), :105-117 (nextPage/prevPage fire-and-forget); AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10 (Refresh has no :disabled/:loading — glass-ui 7 Button ships a `loading` prop)
defects.mechanism: M-C: fire-and-forget async with last-write-wins by arrival order
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-composable.test.ts): C1 → `C1 page = 2 | rendered slug = [ 'page1-row' ] | loading = false` (the stale page won); C2 → `C2 page = 3 | offsets requested = [ 20, 40 ]` (page 2 never displayed, two flights airborne).
defects.proposedCure: A monotonic request token in the composable; drop any response that is not the newest. Disable the affordances while a flight is open using the glass Button's existing :loading/:disabled props.

defects.defect: A failed Dismiss or Delete is completely invisible: both catches are console.warn only. There is no mutation error state (loadError is load-scoped), no toast (vue-sonner was removed repo-wide) and no live region. A 403 from an expired admin token and a 500 from the server produce EXACTLY the same UI as a no-op click.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:88-90 and :100-102 (`console.warn` and nothing else); AdminFlaggedPanel.vue has no aria-live node (measured: 0)
defects.mechanism: M-B: mutations resolve outside the state machine that drives the render, so failure has nowhere to land
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-composable.test.ts, C4): dismissFlags rejects 403, deletePaletteAdmin rejects 500 → `C4 after two FAILED moderation actions → loadError = null | items = 2 | total = 2`.
defects.proposedCure: Resolve every mutation into the same discriminated state as the load ({kind:'error'} with the caught message) and announce the result in the panel's single polite live region.

defects.defect: The panel still speaks the shadcn `variant` vocabulary at a glass-ui@7 Button that has no such prop, so variant="outline" (x3) and variant="ghost" land as inert DOM attributes. All three rendered buttons carry data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral" — the L86-89 design claim ('the pair weighted asymmetrically — the labeled neutral Dismiss is the primary affordance; the delete is a QUIET icon, never its equal-weight red twin') describes a DOM that does not exist. glass 7 ships exactly these axes (emphasis="quiet", tone="destructive", size="xs", iconOnly) and the file uses none of them, hand-rolling geometry with h-7 px-2 per instance (edicts 4 and 5).
defects.evidence: demo/ui/button/index.ts (one line: re-export from @mkbabb/glass-ui); node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 (ButtonProps = emphasis|tone|size|iconOnly|loading|type|disabled|class — no `variant`); AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10, :29, :90, :93; the correct usage sits in the same directory at AdminUsersPanel.vue:174-176 (`emphasis="text"`, `:tone="…'destructive'…"`)
defects.mechanism: M-E: design-system vocabulary drift left by the W44 glass 7.0.0 adoption
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-dom.test.ts) — the actual rendered DOM: `<button data-slot="button" data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral" data-size="sm" … class="… h-7 px-2 text-caption font-display" … variant="outline"> Dismiss </button>` and `D1 emphases as RENDERED = [ 'secondary', 'secondary', 'secondary' ]`. Blast radius measured: `grep -rno 'variant="[a-z]*"' demo --include=*.vue | grep -v demo/ui/` → 29 outline + 28 ghost across 36 files, 21 of them in demo/palettes/browser/admin/.
defects.proposedCure: Speak glass 7: size="xs", emphasis="quiet", tone="destructive", iconOnly, :loading — deleting the per-instance geometry utilities. Then the asymmetric weighting the comment promises becomes true for the first time. Sweep the 57-occurrence family as a carry-ledger row, not a one-file fix.

defects.defect: The destructive delete has no confirmation: one click soft-deletes another user's palette, with no dialog, no undo, and (per F-7) no visible failure. The sibling panel in the same directory gates the same class of operation behind a Dialog confirm — and the comment above that guard is from the SAME W5-12/F-8 wave that wrote this panel's 'asymmetric weighting' comment, having just excised a shift-click bypass as 'an invisible, undocumented, un-undoable fast path on the two most destructive actions in the app'.
defects.evidence: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:93-101; demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:157-178 (Dialog), :263-333 (showConfirm), :310-313 (the W5-12 F-8 excision comment)
defects.mechanism: M-G: a hardening wave hardened one panel and left its neighbour unguarded — the gate never noticed because nothing tests the click
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-a11y.test.ts, A4): click the 'Delete palette …' button → `A4 deletePalette called with = [ 'a' ] | dialogs in DOM = 0`.
defects.proposedCure: Route the delete through the Dialog + showConfirm the sibling already owns (reuse, per KISS — do not invent a new confirm wrapper).

defects.defect: The gate is vacuous. Zero unit tests name the component or the composable; the whole gate is three e2e presence assertions (heading visible, the text 'Sunset Riot' visible, some /Dismiss/i button visible, a 'Refresh flagged palettes' button exists, and the name's font-family). Nothing anywhere clicks Dismiss or Delete. Six named mutations keep every test green, including wiring the Dismiss button to deletePalette. The populated fixture is itself rotten: it answers DELETE /admin/palettes with 204 empty (the real route returns 200 {deleted:true}) which adminRequest's unconditional res.json() cannot consume, and it imports its types from a path that no longer exists, so its shapes are unchecked.
defects.evidence: `grep -rl "AdminFlaggedPanel|useAdminFlagged" test demo/test | wc -l` → 0; e2e/smoke/admin/admin-populated.spec.ts:91-108; e2e/smoke/admin/admin-walk.spec.ts:42-44; e2e/smoke/admin/fixtures/admin-populated.ts:153 (`json("", 204)`) vs api/src/modules/admin/routes/palettes.ts:38-41 (200 {deleted:true}); demo/platform/transport/client.ts:155 (unconditional res.json()); e2e/smoke/admin/fixtures/admin-populated.ts:28 imports "../../../../demo/@/lib/palette/types" → `ls` returns No such file or directory
defects.mechanism: M-G: the suite asserts presence, never behaviour, and its fixture was authored from imagination rather than from the wire
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED — coverage census pasted above; the fixture's 204 shape proven unconsumable by `node -e 'new Response("",{status:200}).json()'` → `THREW: SyntaxError Unexpected end of JSON input`. Mutations that survive: (1) point L90's Dismiss handler at flagged.deletePalette — the Dismiss button now DELETES; (2) delete the flag-details block L106-122; (3) make dismiss()/deletePalette() return immediately; (4) drop the v-else-if on L37; (5) remove the delete button's :aria-label; (6) delete the PaginationBar.
defects.proposedCure: A component spec over the five states plus a click-through of Dismiss and Delete that the six mutations must fail; repair the fixture (200 {deleted:true}, a live type path, and one palette:{} row so F-2 is covered).

defects.defect: formatDate renders the literal string 'Invalid Date' for a malformed or missing flag timestamp, and its try/catch is dead code — toLocaleDateString does not throw on an invalid date, it returns that string. A guard that guards nothing (edict 2: masking fallback).
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/dateFormat.ts:16-25; AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:119
defects.mechanism: M-D: a defensive shape assumed rather than verified
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED: `node -e '…new Date("garbage").toLocaleDateString(…)'` → "Invalid Date" and the same for new Date(undefined). Against the real SFC (repro/flagged-repro.test.ts, R4): `R4 text = "1 flagged Sunset Riotcrimson-owl-772 Dismiss spamInvalid Date"`.
defects.proposedCure: Validate with Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) and render an explicit em-dash (or the raw value); delete the unreachable try/catch.

defects.defect: The loading state emits TWO identical role="status" 'Loading' regions (one per skeleton) while the useful sentence — aria-label="Loading flagged palettes" — sits on a bare div, where ARIA does not expose it (role=generic). Screen readers hear 'Loading' twice and never what is loading.
defects.evidence: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18; demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListSkeleton.vue:8-12 (role="status" aria-label="Loading")
defects.mechanism: M-F: a11y added element-by-element with no owner for the panel's live-region story
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-a11y.test.ts, A1): `A1 role=status count = 2 | labels = [ 'Loading', 'Loading' ]` and `A1 wrapper role = undefined | aria-label = "Loading flagged palettes"`.
defects.proposedCure: One role="status" on the wrapper carrying the real sentence; aria-hidden the shadow rows.

defects.defect: Removing a row destroys the control the keyboard user is standing on and strands focus on <body>, so the next Tab restarts from the top of the document. The repo already knows the pattern — ErrorBoundary.vue explicitly focus-manages on catch citing WCAG 2.4.3 — but this panel does not.
defects.evidence: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:90-101 (the removed row's buttons); demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:86, :98 (the splice); contrast demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:62-64
defects.mechanism: M-F: no focus continuity across list mutation
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-a11y.test.ts, A2): focus the Dismiss button, click it → `A2 focus before = Dismiss`, `A2 focus after = BODY | rows left = 1`.
defects.proposedCure: After a removal move focus to the next row's Dismiss, or to the toolbar Refresh when the list empties, and announce the outcome in the panel's live region.

defects.defect: The flag-count Badge is a bare unlabelled number (a screen reader hears '2' beside the palette name), and the toolbar count publishes '{{ total }} flagged' unconditionally — so it asserts '0 flagged' while loading and while the queue is unreachable. The host pane already enforces the opposite law: AdminPane suppresses its count badge while loading because 'a 0 over the loading skeletons lies' (A-3), and S.W5-7/F-12 re-aimed the names badge for the same reason.
defects.evidence: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:81-83 (bare Badge), :5-7 (unconditional count); demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:117-131 (the A-3 precedent, in the very component that mounts this panel)
defects.mechanism: M-A / M-F: the count is not bound to the state that produced it, and the badge has no accessible name
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (repro/flagged-repro.test.ts, R5): `R5 text = "0 flagged The flag queue is unreachable.Backend unreachable Retry"`. And (repro/flagged-a11y.test.ts, A3) the badge renders as `<div data-slot="badge" data-tone="destructive" …>` with no aria-label.
defects.proposedCure: Move the count inside the {kind:'rows'} arm so it cannot exist without data, and give the badge an accessible name ('2 flags').

defects.defect: Per-instance styling where the design system or a token exists: an inline style="font-variant: small-caps" for what the file itself calls a 'register' (a register is a class); cursor-pointer on one of four buttons only; h-7 px-2 geometry repeated per button instead of size="xs"; and inconsistent handler binding (@click="flagged.loadFlagged" passes the MouseEvent as arg 1 on L10 while L29 calls loadFlagged(); same split on @prev/@next).
defects.evidence: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:75 (inline style), :96 (cursor-pointer), :10/:29/:90/:93 (h-7 px-2 + the binding split), :131-132; the same ad-hoc h-7 px-2 rung recurs at AdminAuditPanel.vue:30
defects.mechanism: M-E: styling and binding decided per instance rather than at the root/system level (edicts 5 and 3)
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a static-source finding read directly off the cited lines (the rendered class strings are visible in the F-8 DOM dump, which shows `class="… h-7 px-2 text-caption font-display"` and `… cursor-pointer text-muted-foreground hover:text-destructive …`).
defects.proposedCure: Tokenize the small-caps annotation as a class in demo/styles; take geometry from glass-ui's size rungs; bind handlers uniformly as explicit arrow calls so no DOM event ever rides into a composable.

result.strongestDefect: C-1 — Approve/Reject/Delete are ungated during their own await, so one impatient double-click fires two POSTs AND appends two entries under the same `id` into the list the Approved tab keys on; a later single Delete then removes both phantom rows for one server DELETE. Reproduced twice (composable + real SFC mount): `approveCalls = ["c1","c1"]`, `approvedColors ids = ["c1","c1"]`, `rows rendered for ONE unique id = 2`.

The hazards I DID clear, with evidence: no `defineModel` (tab is a plain local `ref`, :151); no color math, so no oklch→HSV/`stableHue` exposure; no `ValueUnit` construction; no slider/pointer-capture; `grep -c requestAnimationFrame` → 0 (no PRM-RAF site); no canvas/WebGL; no listeners or observers registered by the panel; tap targets are 28×30px and `REPORT.json results[].probe.a11y` for `/#/admin/names` shows `namelessButtons: 0` and its 4 smallTapTargets resolve to the slug bar (`22×22 "Switch to slug" / "Generate new slug" / "Cancel"` + a 160×23 unnamed input) — this component contributes ZERO to both counts; `REPORT.md:129` overflowX 0, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0 on the route; edict 8 satisfied (`:127` is the only type import and it is `import type`); edict 1 satisfied (152 lines, one responsibility).

defects.defect: Approve/Reject/Delete emit on every click with no in-flight guard; the approve handler then unconditionally appends the optimistic row, so a double-click double-POSTs and puts two entries with the SAME id into the array the Approved tab keys on (`:key="item.id"`). A subsequent Delete on either phantom row filters by id and removes both for one server DELETE.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue:55,66,94,111 + demo/palettes/useColorNameQueue.ts:68-79,92-102. Reproduced: `npx vitest run --config <scratch>/vitest.dup.config.ts` → `approveCalls = ["c1","c1"]` / `approvedColors ids = ["c1","c1"]` (1 passed). defects.mechanism: unguarded concurrent mutation — no in-flight set, no idempotent append
defects.reproduction: Mount AdminNamesPanel with one pending item and click Approve twice inside the network RTT (equivalently: `await Promise.all([q.onApproveColor(item), q.onApproveColor(item)])` in probe-C-queue.test.ts). Two POSTs fire; approvedColors holds ["c1","c1"]; the Approved tab renders 2 rows for 1 proposal.
defects.proposedCure: Move the guard into the port, not the template: `useColorNameQueue` holds a `busyIds` set, the three mutation handlers early-return on a busy id, and the row binds glass-ui Button's existing `loading?: boolean` prop — the library documents it as 'Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles' (components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:15). Make the optimistic append replace-by-id rather than push.

defects.defect: All five `variant=` props on this panel are inert. glass-ui 7.0.0's Button has no `variant` prop (its axes are `emphasis` + `tone`), so `variant="outline"`/`"ghost"` fall through to the DOM as dead attributes while `data-emphasis`/`data-tone` stay at defaults — Approve and Reject render as the SAME button. The destructive register is instead hand-rolled as a 5-utility per-instance class string, duplicated at :64 and :109.
defects.evidence: Rendered from a real mount: `<button data-slot="button" data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral" data-size="sm" ... variant="outline"> Retry <` (note `size` WAS consumed, `variant` was not). API: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 (no `variant`); axes.d.ts:16-17 — TONES includes "destructive" with the docstring 'the semantic status register …; NEVER a `variant` member'. Sites: AdminNamesPanel.vue:37,55,61,87,106 and class strings :64,:109. Repo-wide `grep -rn 'variant="\(outline\|ghost\|default\|destructive\|secondary\|link\)"' demo/ | wc -l` → 66. Gate is blind: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0.
defects.mechanism: un-migrated pre-Glass-7 API kept alive as a no-op, with per-instance utility classes substituting for the library's own semantic axis
defects.reproduction: Mount the panel and read any Button's outerHTML (probe-C-mount.test.ts case E, green): `getAttribute('variant') === 'outline'` while `data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral"`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all 5 `variant=` props and both hand-rolled class strings; express the intent in the library's axes — `emphasis="quiet" tone="destructive" size="sm" icon-only` for reject/delete, `emphasis="secondary"` for approve/retry. `h-7 px-2` dies with them (glass-ui ships `iconOnly` + the size ladder). Repo-wide this is a 66-site migration; make it a wave, and add a lint or codegen guard so an unknown prop on a glass primitive fails the typecheck.

defects.defect: The SegmentedTabs labels are built from raw list length with no reference to load or error state, so the strip asserts counts that contradict the body directly beneath it: 'Pending · 0' over three loading skeletons, and 'Pending · 2' over an error plate rendering zero rows.
defects.evidence: AdminNamesPanel.vue:18-21. Measured from real mounts: `LOADING tab labels = ["Pending · 0","Approved · 0"]` and `pendingItems=2 + error → rendered rows = 0 | tab label = "Pending · 2"`. The feature already codified the opposite rule one file up: AdminPane.vue:120-122 — 'A-3: suppress the badge while the roster/queue loads — a "0" over the loading skeletons lies'.
defects.mechanism: a derived display value computed from data alone, ignoring the load/error state machine that governs the data
defects.reproduction: probe-C-mount.test.ts cases A and F (both green): mount with loadingPending/loadingApproved true → labels read '· 0'; mount with 2 pendingItems + pendingError → label reads '· 2' while the body renders 0 rows.
defects.proposedCure: One `computed` tabOptions (which is also the C-12 cure): count is `null` whenever `loadingX || xError`, and a null count renders the bare word — 'Pending', not 'Pending · 0'. Extend the same rule to AdminPane's header badge, which today guards on loading only and shows '0' in the error state.

defects.defect: All three moderation mutations swallow their failures into `console.warn` and set no state — the panel maintains a full error idiom for READS and none for WRITES. A failed reject leaves the row in place with no message; the operator cannot distinguish 'rejected' from 'silently failed'.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useColorNameQueue.ts:76-78, 87-89, 99-101 — each catch is exactly `console.warn(...)`. Contrast the read path :44,:61 which sets queueLoadError/approvedLoadError, rendered prominently at AdminNamesPanel.vue:30-41 and :80-91. Aggravated by availability.ts:188-195, which throws BEFORE issuing a request during the latch cooldown, making the failed click indistinguishable from a no-op.
defects.mechanism: asymmetric error surfacing — the write path has no channel to the view at all
defects.reproduction: NONE (hypothesis for the exact user-visible sequence; the code path is certain). To exhibit: route `POST **/admin/colors/*/reject` to a 500 and click Reject — the row remains, nothing is shown, one console.warn is emitted.
defects.proposedCure: Add `mutationError: Ref<string|null>` to the port, set in each catch and cleared on the next success; the panel renders it once as a `role="alert"` line above the list. Optimistic removal already happens after the await, so only the failure needs a voice.

defects.defect: False-empty: with no admin token the loaders early-return without setting loading, error, or any flag, so the panel falls through to the empty plate and asserts '· QUEUE CLEAR · No pending proposals.' when no request was ever issued. The admin route is reachable in that state because the loader watcher is `immediate` while the sign-out guard is not.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useColorNameQueue.ts:36-37 and :52-53 (`const token = getAdminToken(); if (!token) return;`). Rendered proof already in the mega-tranche's own capture: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-names.png shows an UNAUTHENTICATED page (dock shows 'Login') at /#/admin/names displaying 'Pending · 0 / Approved · 0' and '· QUEUE CLEAR · / No pending proposals.'. Route reachability: demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:148-155 fires the loaders with `{immediate:true}`; the anonymous-eviction watcher at :169-173 is not immediate.
defects.mechanism: a designed state (true-empty) used to mask an un-attempted one — a masking fallback, edict 2
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/names with no `palette-admin-token` in localStorage. Panel renders the moderation surface and claims the queue is clear; zero network requests are made. (Confirmed live: my first probe recorded `calls: []` with the panel rendered.)
defects.proposedCure: `if (!token) { queueLoadError.value = 'Not signed in as an administrator.'; return; }`, or better: do not mount the moderation panels without a token and make the eviction watcher `immediate`. 'Empty' must mean the server said zero.

defects.defect: Raw transport `e.message` is forwarded verbatim into user-facing copy. On the live route this renders a 484-character developer paragraph — shell commands and env-var instructions — as the body of the moderation panel.
defects.evidence: useColorNameQueue.ts:44,:61 (`e?.message ?? 'Backend unreachable'`) → AdminNamesPanel.vue:34,:84 (`:detail="pendingError"`) → EmptyState.vue:23-25 prints it unedited. Live measurement at http://localhost:9000/#/admin/names: `alertLens: [37, 484]`, body = 'The proposal queue is unreachable. value.js dev is MISCONFIGURED: … Run `npm run dev` (the full local stack via scripts/dev.sh up) …'. Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminNamesPanel/probe-C-error-state.png.
defects.mechanism: no error-to-copy mapping layer — the view renders whatever string the transport threw
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/admin/names with an admin token seeded and no VITE_API_URL (the dev-misconfig latch, availability.ts:118-131). The 12-line paragraph fills the Names card. In production the same slot carries ApiProblem detail and raw `TypeError: Failed to fetch`.
defects.proposedCure: Map, do not forward. The transport already throws typed errors (`DevMisconfigError`, `ApiUnavailableError`, `ApiProblem`); the port selects one human sentence per class and keeps the machine text for the console. `detail` should carry an actionable token (status code / correlation id), never prose.

defects.defect: Retry is a no-op with zero feedback whenever the transport latch is closed: the request is refused before it is issued, the constant error message re-renders identically, the loading flag flips within one microtask so no skeleton ever paints, and there is no live region. Production-reachable via the 30s `unavailable` cooldown after any single network failure.
defects.evidence: AdminNamesPanel.vue:37,:87 → AdminPane.vue:56-57 → availability.ts:188-195 (`assertApiAttemptAllowed` throws before fetch) with `RETRY_COOLDOWN_MS = 30_000` at availability.ts:59. Live, three consecutive Retry clicks: alert `outerHTML` length 1548 / 1548 / 1548 / 1548 (byte-identical), `skeletons: 0` at every sample, `networkToApi: []`, `liveRegions: 0`.
defects.mechanism: a control whose only effect is a state transition the view cannot distinguish from no transition
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/admin/names in the error state, click Retry three times and sample the alert element: identical outerHTML each time, zero requests to the API host, no skeletons, no announcement.
defects.proposedCure: Read the reactive `apiAvailability` cell (availability.ts:47) and make the latch visible: disable Retry with a 'retry in Ns' label during the cooldown, or guarantee the click always produces an observable transition (skeleton → result) plus a polite live-region announcement of the outcome.

defects.defect: The tab strip is an UNNAMED role=group of aria-pressed toggle buttons controlling zero tabpanels — no `aria-controls`, no `role=tabpanel`, no accessible group name — even though glass-ui's SegmentedTabs ships `semantics="tabs"`, per-option `controls`, and `ariaLabel` for exactly this case.
defects.evidence: AdminNamesPanel.vue:14-22 (only `variant="pill"` passed; pill defaults to `toggle` semantics per SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts). Live at /#/admin/names: `tabs: [{role:null, ariaPressed:"true", ariaControls:null}, {role:null, ariaPressed:"false", ariaControls:null}]`, `groupAriaLabel: null`, `groupLabelledby: null`, `tabpanels: 0`. Mount confirms: `aria-live = 0 | role=tabpanel = 0 | aria-controls = 0`. Library API quotes: `controls` — 'completing the APG tablist↔tabpanel linkage for consumers that own a panel'; `ariaLabel` — 'Accessible name shared by the desktop strip and responsive Select'.
defects.mechanism: the consumer owns two panels but declares none of the three relationship affordances the primitive provides
defects.reproduction: probe-C-mount.test.ts case D (green) and the live snapshot above; the panel bodies at :24 and :75 are bare `<div class="min-w-0">` with no id or role.
defects.proposedCure: Four lines: `semantics="tabs"`, `aria-label="Color name queue"`, `controls: 'names-pending' | 'names-approved'` on the options, and `id` + `role="tabpanel"` + `tabindex="0"` on the two bodies.

defects.defect: The loading state is simultaneously unannounced and triple-announced: `aria-label` sits on a role-less `<div>` (prohibited on ARIA `generic`, so ignored by AT), while the three skeleton children each carry their own `role="status" aria-label="Loading"`. Nothing at all is announced when the load resolves or when a row is approved away.
defects.evidence: AdminNamesPanel.vue:26 and :76. Measured from a mount: `loading wrapper: tag = DIV | role = NONE | nested role=status count = 3`, and `aria-live = 0` for the whole panel. Spec: WAI-ARIA 1.2 lists `generic` among the roles for which `aria-label` is prohibited; HTML-AAM maps `<div>` → `generic`. The sibling panel does it correctly — AdminTagsPanel.vue:51-56 puts `role="status"` on the equivalent wrapper. Skeleton source: AdminListSkeleton.vue:10-13.
defects.mechanism: naming an element that cannot be named, plus live-region multiplication in a v-for
defects.reproduction: probe-C-mount.test.ts case B (green): `w.find('[aria-label="Loading pending proposals"]').attributes('role')` is undefined and the element is a DIV; three nested `[role=status]` are present.
defects.proposedCure: One `role="status" aria-live="polite"` wrapper per list region that owns both the loading text and the settled result text ('3 pending proposals'); AdminListSkeleton drops its per-instance `role="status"` (decorative once the container speaks). Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox if the Skeleton primitive itself is touched.

defects.defect: The gates around this component are vacuous, and the repository has no component tests at all: `@vue/test-utils` is a declared, installed, entirely unused devDependency and no `mount(` call exists in test/ or demo/test/. Seven named mutations to this file keep every existing gate green — including the hard CI typecheck.
defects.evidence: `grep -rln "AdminNames" test/ e2e/` → no matches. `grep -rn "@vue/test-utils" --exclude-dir=node_modules .` → only package.json:96 + lockfile (+ historical docs). `grep -rn "Pending|Approved|proposal queue|Retry" e2e/ test/` → nothing. Coverage is 3 e2e specs asserting only: POST fired (color-approve.spec.ts, color-reject.spec.ts), one row removed at 390px (admin-populated.spec.ts:83-85), and no nameless/sub-24px visible control (a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts:44-55). Gate blindness proven: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0 with 66 inert `variant=` attributes in demo/.
defects.mechanism: assertions on the request, never on the resulting state — plus a whole component tier with no test harness in use
defects.reproduction: Apply any of these and re-run the suite green: (1) delete useColorNameQueue.ts:75 so the Approved list never updates; (2) hardcode both tab labels to '· 0'; (3) delete the entire `v-else` Approved block :75-118; (4) delete both error EmptyState blocks :30-41,:80-91; (5) change `:key="item.id"` to `:key="item.name"`; (6) delete the `cssColorOpaque` prop; (7) change `variant="ghost"` to `variant="banana"` (typecheck still EXIT=0, measured).
defects.proposedCure: This component is pure props/emits — the cheapest mount target in the tree. Six component tests (loading counts, error-vs-empty precedence, approve emits exactly once, approved-branch render, tab semantics, retry emits) catch C-1, C-3, C-8, C-9 and C-10. The harness is already installed and paid for; the probes in this report directory are runnable starting points.

defects.defect: A failed refresh hides rows that are still held in memory: the error branch precedes the list in the template, so a transient reload failure replaces a working queue with a full-plate error while the tab strip keeps counting the hidden rows.
defects.evidence: AdminNamesPanel.vue:26/:30/:42/:43 precedence; useColorNameQueue.ts:43-45 never clears the array on failure. Measured: `pendingItems=2 + error → rendered rows = 0 | tab label = "Pending · 2"`.
defects.mechanism: error treated as a replacement for data rather than an annotation over it
defects.reproduction: probe-C-mount.test.ts case F (green): mount with two pendingItems and a non-null pendingError; zero Approve buttons render.
defects.proposedCure: Full-plate error only on cold fail (`items.length === 0`); otherwise render the list with a single error line above it and a Retry.

defects.defect: `cssColorOpaque` is declared as a REQUIRED prop and never read anywhere in the component; the parent injects CSS_COLOR_KEY partly to feed it.
defects.evidence: `grep -n cssColorOpaque demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue` → a single hit, :140 (the declaration). Bound at AdminPane.vue:52.
defects.mechanism: dead public surface left behind by an earlier shape — edict 2
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — the grep is total: one occurrence, and it is the declaration.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the prop and the `:css-color-opaque` binding at AdminPane.vue:52.

defects.defect: The `:options` array is an inline template literal, so a new array identity is produced on every render; Vue's shallow props compare therefore forces a SegmentedTabs re-render on every parent tick — including every keystroke in the admin search box, which drives both filtered lists. Both sibling SegmentedTabs consumers hoist their options into a `computed`; this file is the sole deviation.
defects.evidence: AdminNamesPanel.vue:18-21 vs demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue:29-32 (`const tabOptions = computed(...)`) and demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue (`:options="tabOptions"`). Search coupling: AdminPane.vue:11-16 binds `pm.searchQuery`, consumed by useColorNameQueue.ts:27-33. The strip's indicator is ResizeObserver-driven (glass-ui/dist/useTabRovingFocus-*.js — it threw `ReferenceError: ResizeObserver is not defined` under jsdom, which is how I identified it).
defects.mechanism: per-render allocation of a prop value that has no per-render reason to change
defects.reproduction: NONE measured for the frame cost (labelled a hypothesis on impact); the allocation and the identity-compare re-render are certain from the code and the two sibling counter-examples.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist to `const tabOptions = computed(...)` — the same computed that should carry the C-3 count-suppression logic.

defects.defect: `namesTab` is `ref<string>` with a catch-all `v-else`, so any value that is not exactly 'pending' silently renders the Approved panel; and only 2 of 8 props are destructured, with `= null` defaults that can never fire because the parent always passes both.
defects.evidence: AdminNamesPanel.vue:151 (`ref<string>("pending")`), :24 (`v-if="namesTab === 'pending'"`), :75 (`v-else`), :132 (partial destructure with defaults) vs AdminPane.vue:50-51 (both always bound).
defects.mechanism: stringly-typed state plus a fallback branch standing in for an explicit one
defects.reproduction: NONE (no current caller can produce a third value); it is a latent-correctness and idiom finding under edict 7.
defects.proposedCure: `ref<"pending" | "approved">("pending")` and `v-else-if="namesTab === 'approved'"`; make the props destructure all-or-nothing and drop the dead defaults.

defects.defect: An unparseable or browser-unsupported css literal renders as a blank bordered circle — indistinguishable from transparent — and the row stays approvable, so an admin can approve a name for a color they are not seeing.
defects.evidence: AdminNamesPanel.vue:46 and :96 (`:style="{ backgroundColor: item.css }"`). Measured from a mount with `css: "not-a-color"`: `swatch style = "" | row still approvable = 1` — the inline style is dropped entirely. The repo's own populated fixture seeds `color(display-p3 …)` (e2e/smoke/admin/fixtures/admin-populated.ts:87-94), which is exactly the class of literal an older reviewing browser drops.
defects.mechanism: the browser's silent invalid-declaration drop used as the only validation
defects.reproduction: probe-C-mount.test.ts case G (green): mount with an item whose `css` is 'not-a-color'; the swatch element carries no style attribute at all and the Approve button is still present and enabled.
defects.proposedCure: Gate the swatch on `CSS.supports('color', item.css)`: mark unsupported literals visibly (a hatched swatch + a caption) and suppress approval for them. Do NOT call `parseCssColor` unguarded here — the repo carries a live crash class in it.

defects.defect: No `<Transition>` on the pending↔approved panel swap — the content change is a one-frame cut.
defects.evidence: `grep -c "<Transition" demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue` → 0; the swap is the bare `v-if`/`v-else` at :24/:75. Already booked by the design lane as F034-b at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/excavation/DESIGN-CANON-BRIEF.md:97.
defects.mechanism: un-animated conditional swap under a segmented control
defects.reproduction: NONE (design-lane finding, recorded here only to prevent re-derivation as new).
defects.proposedCure: Adopt whatever the design lane rules for F034-b; do not solve it locally and do not delete any existing animation (edict 6).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) beneath demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — claude-opus-5[1m] (1M context). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — one `searchQuery` ref (usePalettePorts.ts:54) is handed to three ports and v-model-bound by three panes (AdminPane.vue:13, BrowsePane.vue:11, PalettesPane.vue:34). Typing in the admin roster search verbatim rewrites the user's private saved-palette filter and the public-wall filter. Reproduced live at localhost:9000: admin field set to "zzq-leak-probe" → browse field "zzq-leak-probe" → palettes field "zzq-leak-probe". `useFilteredList(savedPalettes, searchQuery, …)` (usePalettePorts.ts:112) then renders "My Palettes" empty after an admin visit.

defects.defect: One shared `searchQuery` ref serves three semantically disjoint search scopes (admin roster / public wall / private library); all three panes v-model the same ref object.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:54 `const searchQuery = ref("")` → exported on libraryPort (:141), browsePort (:183), adminPort (:224). Bound at demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:13, demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:11, demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:34. Live Playwright measurement against http://localhost:9000: {"adminUsersSearchValue":"zzq-leak-probe","browseSearchValue":"zzq-leak-probe","palettesSearchValue":"zzq-leak-probe"}
defects.mechanism: shared-mutable-state-without-owner (no unique semantic home for the search term)
defects.reproduction: Live, run and pasted: location.hash='#/admin/users'; set input[placeholder="Search users..."] to 'zzq-leak-probe' via native setter + input event; location.hash='#/browse'; read input[placeholder="Search the commons..."].value → 'zzq-leak-probe'; location.hash='#/palettes'; read input[placeholder="Search your palettes..."].value → 'zzq-leak-probe'.
defects.proposedCure: A search term is a property of a list, not of the palette domain. Each list-owning composable (useAdminUsers, useColorNameQueue, useBrowsePalettes, usePaletteStore) declares its own searchQuery; useFilteredList already accepts the ref as a parameter, so this is a construction-site change. Zero shared refs survive, and the `currentView === "browse"` guard inside usePaletteWiring.ts:157 — a runtime check compensating for the aliasing — deletes with it.

defects.defect: AdminPane forwards 5 props + 7 events to AdminUsersPanel from the very port that AdminUsersPanel already injects itself; and 3 of the 5 panels it renders inject the port and take no props at all, so the file encodes two contradictory wiring idioms fifteen lines apart.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:234 `const pm = inject(ADMIN_PORT_KEY)!`; AdminPane.vue:95 injects the same key and forwards at :28-40. All 12 forwarded targets are members of adminPort (usePalettePorts.ts:195-231). Prop-less injecting siblings: AdminAuditPanel.vue:107, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:149, AdminTagsPanel.vue:122 (each with its own onMounted at :119/:152/:125). Template contrast: AdminPane.vue:25-41 (prop-driven) vs :61-67 (self-injecting).
defects.mechanism: redundant-plumbing / no single answer to where the port boundary sits
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural, verified by reading both the injection and the forwarding in shipped source.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the majority idiom the three self-sufficient panels already prove: every panel injects its own slice, AdminPane's forwarding deletes, and AdminNamesPanel (the only genuinely prop-driven panel) joins them.

defects.defect: AdminPane re-declares the five admin view ids inline and re-derives the five pane titles that VIEW_MAP already owns — in a schema file that opens by declaring itself the single source of truth and by claiming it retired a 4-copy ViewId enumeration.
defects.evidence: viewSchema.ts:1-15 (the claim); ids at viewSchema.ts:45-49 vs AdminPane.vue:91; labels at viewSchema.ts:191/200/209/218/226 vs AdminPane.vue:99-103. Screenshot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png shows the dock select "Users" (VIEW_MAP.label) and the pane header "Users" (AdminPane.headerTitle) on one screen from two independent sources.
defects.mechanism: ownership-duplication (two homes for one table; a derived subset type re-typed by hand)
defects.reproduction: NONE for divergence (hypothesis: renaming VIEW_MAP["admin-audit"].label leaves the pane header saying "Audit Log" — no type, test or lint prevents it); the duplication itself is certain from the cited lines.
defects.proposedCure: PaneConfig gains `description`; PaneHeader reads title+description from viewManager.currentConfig. All nine panes stop hardcoding header strings. Where an admin subset type is genuinely needed it is `Extract<ViewId, `admin-${string}`>` — derived, never re-typed.

defects.defect: AdminPane is a second router: usePaneRouter maps every left pane 1:1 to a component except admin, which it prefix-dispatches into one multiplexer whose declared 5-member prop union is never checked at the only call site.
defects.evidence: usePaneRouter.ts:80-92 (nine exact 1:1 matches) vs :93 `if (name.startsWith("admin-")) return AdminPane;` and :140 `return { subView: name }`; leftProps returns Record<string, unknown> (usePaneRouter.ts:64), so the union at AdminPane.vue:91 is unenforced. Re-dispatch at AdminPane.vue:26/45/61/64/67 plus two default-less switches at :97-115.
defects.mechanism: duplicate-registry / string-prefix dispatch shadowing a typed table one layer up
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS — add a sixth admin view (e.g. "admin-reports") to ViewId + VIEW_MAP: componentFor prefix-matches it to AdminPane, leftProps passes the unchecked string, every v-if misses and both computeds fall off the end returning undefined → a Card with a blank header and empty body, with no type error, console error or test failure.
defects.proposedCure: Register the five panels directly in componentFor — the same shape the other nine panes already have — and delete AdminPane entirely (135 lines → 0). Three of the five panels already own their data lifecycle; the other two gain it.

defects.defect: Two live import routes to one design system, both used inside AdminPane: 19 one-line `demo/ui/*` re-export shims onto the glass-ui ROOT barrel, alongside bare published subpath imports.
defects.evidence: AdminPane.vue:74 `from "../../ui/card"`, :75 `from "../../ui/badge"`, :87 `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/search"`. demo/ui/card/index.ts is one line re-exporting from "@mkbabb/glass-ui". 48 demo files use the shim route (`grep -rl 'from "[^"]*\.\./ui/' demo/ | wc -l` → 48). Measured: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js = 25,239 bytes importing 43 distinct chunks (`grep -oE '"\./[^"]+\.js"' glass-ui.js | sort -u | wc -l` → 43); dist/card.js = 217 B → 1 chunk; dist/badge.js = 92 B → 1 chunk. glass-ui 7.0.0 exports ./card, ./badge, ./button, ./dialog, ./input, ./select, ./popover, ./tooltip, ./separator, ./label, ./switch, ./slider, ./collapsible, ./dropdown-menu — every shimmed symbol has a real subpath.
defects.mechanism: alias-layer / dual-path to the design system (edict 2 + edict 4)
defects.reproduction: NONE for a break. Cost is dev-only and honest: glass-ui declares "sideEffects": ["*.css"], so production tree-shakes; in dev the shim route fetches 43 modules instead of 1, paid on first admin navigation (AdminPane is defineAsyncComponent-loaded, usePaneRouter.ts:76).
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely and repoint all 48 files at the glass-ui subpath that already exists for each symbol. One route to the design system, no demo-side barrel that can drift.

defects.defect: adminPort is a 34-member injected object spanning four unrelated data domains; the RF-15 'god facade dissolution' redistributed the facade rather than dissolving it.
defects.evidence: usePalettePorts.ts:22-30 states the file dissolves a '153 L, ONE cross-everything injected blob' into five narrow ports. Measured members: adminPort 34 (usePalettePorts.ts:195-231), browsePort 32 (:157-192). defects.reproduction: NONE — measurement, not failure.
defects.proposedCure: The sub-composables are already separate and already correct. Provide them under four keys (ADMIN_USERS_KEY, COLOR_QUEUE_KEY, ADMIN_AUDIT_KEY, ADMIN_MODERATION_KEY), each injected by exactly the panel that renders it. Only the aggregation step is deleted; nothing is written.

defects.defect: A composable owns a component instance and calls methods on it; AdminPane exists partly to bind that inverted ref, and the null case is silently masked.
defects.evidence: useAdminUsers.ts:27 `const adminUsersPanelRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof AdminUsersPanel> | null>(null)`, called into at :99, :121, :136, :150; usePalettePorts.ts:121-124 `onPrune()` awaits admin.onPruneEmpty() then calls `admin.adminUsersPanelRef.value?.onPruneDone(pruned)`. AdminUsersPanel.vue:389 defineExpose({removeUserPalette, updatePaletteTier, clearUserPalettes, onPruneDone, userPalettes}); AdminPane.vue:134 binds the ref, AdminPane.vue:39 forwards the emit.
defects.mechanism: wrong-direction dependency (data layer → component instance) + masking fallback (`?.` at usePalettePorts.ts:123 discards the prune count whenever subView !== 'admin-users')
defects.reproduction: NONE for a runtime break; the inversion is read from the five call sites. Note the structural consequence: useTemplateRef (edict 7) cannot be used at AdminPane.vue:134 because the ref must be the composable's object — the structure forbids the idiom.
defects.proposedCure: Invert it back: onPruneEmpty() already returns the count, so the panel awaits its own action and updates its own state. defineExpose drops to empty, adminUsersPanelRef and the InstanceType import delete from useAdminUsers.ts, and the last reason for AdminPane to hold a template ref disappears.

defects.reproduction: `grep -c cssColorOpaque demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue` → 1

defects.defect: The feature's declared 'TOP-LEVEL SEAM' barrel has zero importers, and the eslint rule documented as enforcing it targets a deleted directory tree and a deleted path alias, so it cannot fire.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:1-8 declares the seam and cites G-DEMO-3b. `grep -rn 'from "\./browser"\|from "\.\./browser"' demo/` → no output. eslint.config.js:232-255 scopes to demo/color-picker/**, demo/@/components/**, demo/@/lib/** and bans '@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue'; `ls demo/@` → No such file or directory; vite.config.ts:69-72 records that W43 killed the demo @… aliases. demo/palettes/** is not in the glob. `npx eslint demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue` → clean.
defects.mechanism: unenforced boundary (an enforcement claim that cannot match)

defects.proposedCure: Either delete the unused seam and the stale rule (sub-barrels are the real API), or re-aim the rule at demo/** banning demo/palettes/browser/*/*.vue. Do not keep a barrel nobody imports guarded by a lint that cannot fire.

defects.defect: The 'pane shell' concept has no home: nine panes hand-copy the same six-utility class string onto the glass-ui Card root, and PaneHeader defines an UNSCOPED style for a class it never applies, to reach its own siblings' root elements.

defects.mechanism: per-instance styling of a design-system root (edict 5) + producer/consumer inversion stated in a comment instead of fixed
defects.reproduction: NONE — read from the ten cited sites.
defects.proposedCure: Ask glass-ui for a `Pane` primitive (Card root + header slot + named scroll-timeline host) — every ingredient already ships in 7.0.0 (./card, ./surface, ./fading-scroll, ./scroll-progress-rim, SURFACE_TIERS). defects.defect: demo/palettes/export.ts and demo/palettes/export/ are two independent implementations of palette export; the shipped one is untested and the tested one is unshipped, and the specifier './export' resolves between them by file-before-directory precedence.

defects.defect: The published exports map has no "." root, yet tsconfig.demo.json declares TS paths for three specifiers that cannot resolve at runtime and omits two that can — a false-green typecheck surface for the library's public API.

Measured against the installed 4.0.0 artifact: `node --input-type=module -e 'import("@mkbabb/value.js")'` → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED 'No "exports" main defined'; '/parsing' → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED; '/units' → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. tsconfig.demo.json declares paths for all three and omits ./value and ./css (the latter used 10x in demo, resolving only via the Vite alias generated from exports at vite.config.ts:44-51). demo/shared/utils.ts:8-20 re-implements debounce locally with the comment 'the library's root-barrel export stands for external consumers' — that barrel is exported to no one.

defects.defect: Every Admin route ships at exactly 50/50 beside an empty 'My Palettes' companion — the composition three binding canon documents ruled out with an explicit 50%→0 disposition. AdminPane is a left-slot half-pane, not a route body.
defects.evidence: Live probe (Chromium 1440x900 @2x, http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users): cards:2, adminRect {x:199,y:232.5,w:512,h:514.7}, companionRect {x:729,y:232.5,w:512,h:514.7}, splitPct: [50, 50], companionHeadingText: "My Palettes". Screenshots: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-{light,dark}/admin-{users,names,audit,flagged,tags}.png (8 captures). Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 "Each Admin route uses the full main width: the current Palettes companion, right label and resulting mobile pane selector are removed rather than restyled"; §3 law 1 (two-part scene must be exactly 61.8033989/38.1966011 or 66.6666667/33.3333333 — 50/50 is neither); §3 law 2 "Empty secondary content … never receives half the viewport" (companion renders "No saved palettes yet."); OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:51 and rows :57-:61 (`Companion rect 50%→0` for all five); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-04. Mechanism site: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:93 + :140 (admin registered as a LEFT slot, so desktopRight at :169 unconditionally mounts PalettesPane).
defects.mechanism: F1 — AdminPane is registered as a half-pane (left slot) rather than a full-width route body, so the view config's non-null `right` forces a companion; the Card's `h-full` then takes its height from the grid row the companion sizes.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users (or /names /audit /flagged /tags) at viewport width >=1024. Measured splitPct [50,50]. Also visible in 8 committed Safari screenshots at shots/safari-desktop-{light,dark}/admin-*.png.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not restyle: the five Admin view configs declare `right: null` and AdminPane stops being a left-slot Card. Each route body becomes a full-width structural review field. This one move also dissolves D-02 (the mobile selector exists only to reach the right pane), D-11 (the Card/caster housing), and the 158.78px empty-state void (30.85% of card height) that the companion-sized grid row donates.

defects.defect: The 'Users | Palettes' mobile pane selector that VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 and §3 law 6 explicitly retire is still rendered at 390px, 320px and at 200% zoom.
defects.evidence: Live probe: at 390x844 → controls labelled "Users" 57.50x26.25 @y35.88 and "Palettes" 57.50x26.25 @y35.88; at 320x720 → 56.98x26.05 @y35.97. At 1440 both measure 0x0 (not rendered). Screenshots: shots/safari-mobile-{light,dark}/admin-users.png (visible in the dock), shots/zoom-200-desktop/adminusers.png. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 (names "the resulting mobile pane selector" as removed); §3 law 6 "no global pane selector, left/right split state, or simultaneous two-stage miniature survives"; OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:107 "The global narrow PaneSegmentedControl and left/right view state are retired because all mobile compositions are single sequences."
defects.mechanism: F1 — same root as D-01: usePaneRouter.ts:180-186 `mobile` returns `desktopRight` at pane-index 1, so a right pane requires a selector to reach it.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users at 390x844 or 320x720; or open shots/safari-mobile-light/admin-users.png and shots/zoom-200-desktop/adminusers.png.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of D-01's cure: with `right: null` there is no second pane to select, so the selector and the left/right view state both die rather than being restyled.

defects.defect: The header count badge asserts "0" during the load-error state while the body renders the error branch. The identical lie was already cured one register down and the fix was never carried up.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:54-68 — on catch, `usersLoadError` is set, `adminUsers` is LEFT UNTOUCHED ([] on first load), `loadingUsers` returns false in the finally. The composable's own comment at :62 reads "W5-5 (F-2): a dead backend must never read as 'No users found.'". demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:120-122 then evaluates `return pm.loadingUsers.value ? null : pm.adminUsers.value.length;` → 0. The A-3 comment at AdminPane.vue:120-121 covers only the LOADING arm ("a '0' over the loading skeletons lies"); the error arm was never covered. Same shape on admin-names via queueLoadError (AdminPane.vue:126-128).
defects.mechanism: F2 — the identity band carries data whose trustworthiness it does not check; `adminCount` asks "am I loading?" instead of "do I have a trustworthy number?".
defects.reproduction: /#/admin/users with a valid admin token and the API unreachable (stop the api container or block GET /admin/users): header renders "Users 0", body renders the usersLoadError branch.
defects.proposedCure: `adminCount` returns null unless the sub-view's port is in a settled-success state. The null arm already exists; it is being asked the wrong question. Better still (see D-06): delete the header badge — the count belongs in the review field's status row where the error, filter and truncation truths already live.

defects.defect: The two header badges that exist mean different things: the Users badge is the UNFILTERED total while the Names badge is the FILTERED visible queue. Same slot, same chip, two semantics.
defects.evidence: AdminPane.vue:122 `return pm.loadingUsers.value ? null : pm.adminUsers.value.length;` (unfiltered) vs AdminPane.vue:126-128 `return pm.loadingColorQueue.value ? null : pm.filteredColorQueue.value.length;` (filtered). The rendered Users list is `pm.filteredAdminUsers` (AdminPane.vue:28), computed by slug substring at useAdminUsers.ts:29-34. AdminPane.vue:125-126 records the exact reasoning that was applied to Names and not to Users: "S.W5-7 (F-12): the header badge is the ACTIONABLE queue — the old pending+approved sum matched neither visible list."
defects.mechanism: F2 — identity band carrying data, with no single rule for what the number counts.
defects.reproduction: /#/admin/users with N users loaded → type a slug fragment into "Search users…". The list shrinks (useAdminUsers.ts:32-34); the badge does not move (AdminPane.vue:122). Requires a backend seeded with users; the divergence between the two code paths is unambiguous on read.
defects.proposedCure: One rule for what a header count counts, applied across all five sub-views — or, preferred, no header count at all (D-06) and one status row in the review field that states filtered/total/truncated honestly.

defects.defect: The same number is rendered twice inside one Card in two type registers ~137px apart, plus a third time in words — AdminPane feeds the panel the very value it also renders itself.
defects.evidence: Live probe, leaf text nodes inside the admin Card containing a bare 0: zeroMentions: ["0", "0 users"]; badge rect {x:345, y:268.5, w:29.47, h:26.05}. AdminPane.vue:5 renders `<Badge …>{{ adminCount }}` = pm.adminUsers.value.length; AdminPane.vue:33 passes `:total-users="pm.adminUsers.value.length"` to the same panel, which renders it again at AdminUsersPanel.vue:9 `{{ totalUsers }} user{{ totalUsers !== 1 ? 's' : '' }}`; the empty state then says it a third time ("No users found."). Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 5 (a small mark is data, status, labeled action, drag affordance, focus register, or REMOVED) and law 6 ("Subtraction precedes explanation").
defects.mechanism: F2 — one fact, three renderings, no owner.
defects.reproduction: Any /#/admin/users capture: shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png — badge "0" at the title, "0 users" 137px below, "No users found." below that.
defects.proposedCure: One owner. The review field's status row already renders the count with room for filter/error/truncation qualifiers; the badge and the empty-state restatement go.

defects.defect: A live counter is welded into the document heading, so the heading's accessible name mutates with network state and the display line mixes two type jurisdictions.
defects.evidence: Live probe: h3.text = "Users 0", tag = "H3"; badge computed fontFamily "Fira Code" at 16.4px inside a Fraunces --type-display-1 line box; h1Count = 0, mainCount = 1. demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:22 puts `<slot/>` inside `<h3 class="pane-header-title font-display">`; AdminPane.vue:4-5 puts BOTH the title text and the Badge into that slot, so the name goes "Users" (loading) → "Users 0" → "Users 42". Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5 / PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 11 "A display-sized readout is not therefore a document heading or live status"; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 type matrix (identity = Fraunces, value/provenance = Fira text-mono-small — the h3 line is now both); §4.1 "Each route has one H1" measured 0 on all 20 admin captures (REPORT.md h1 column).
defects.mechanism: F2 — the identity band is being used as a status surface.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users — evaluate `document.querySelector('h3.pane-header-title').textContent` → "Users 0". REPORT.md rows /#/admin/* all show h1 = 0.
defects.proposedCure: The count is status, not identity. Move it into the review field's status region (where "0 users" already is) and announce it through that region. The h3 slot carries identity only. (The absent route H1 is shell-owned and not AdminPane's to fix, but it is why a mutating h3 is the route's only heading.)

defects.defect: The count badge is styled with a per-instance physical-direction override (`ml-2`), so under dir=rtl the title↔badge gap collapses from 8px to exactly 0.00px and the 8px is spent on the badge's outboard side.
defects.evidence: Live probe, computed badge margins IDENTICAL in both directions: dir=ltr → marginLeft "8px", marginRight "0px"; dir=rtl → marginLeft "8px", marginRight "0px". Measured rects at 1440: LTR admin card x199→right711, header paddingInlineStart 24px ⇒ title left 223; badge x=345 minus 8px margin ⇒ title right 337 ⇒ glyph run 114px. RTL admin card x729→right1241 ⇒ title inline-start 1217, extends left 114px ⇒ title left edge 1103; badge measured right edge = 1103.00. Gap: 8.00px LTR vs 0.00px RTL. Corroborated visually in shots/rtl-desktop/adminusers.png ("⓪Users" with the chip touching the title and clear air to its left). Badge class list measured: "badge-atom … bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground … text-mono-small ml-2" (AdminPane.vue:5). Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1 "chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document"; owner edict 5 (style at the root, never per-instance).
defects.mechanism: F2/F4 — a glass-ui root spaced by a consumer physical-margin utility instead of a producer-owned logical gap.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users → `document.documentElement.dir = "rtl"` → measure badge.right vs the title glyph left edge: 1103.00 vs 1103. Or open shots/rtl-desktop/adminusers.png.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the badge from the heading (D-06). If a count chip survives anywhere it sits in the review field's status tray with a producer-owned gap token — never a consumer `ml-*`. Any surviving spacing uses logical `ms-*`.

defects.defect: One component serves five separately-ratified compositions, and the union prop buys nothing at runtime because the router keys each sub-view separately — five KeepAlive entries of one component, no instance reuse, full fork cost.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:93 returns the same AdminPane for all `admin-*`, but usePaneRouter.ts:165 sets `key: left` (the sub-view name) and demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:123 binds `:key="liveKey"` inside `<KeepAlive :max="6">`. demo/color-picker/App.vue:97-100 concedes the cost in its own comment: ":max = the 6 distinct non-admin LEFT panes … admin left panes fall off the LRU rather than bloating the cache" — 11 distinct left keys against a 6-slot LRU. Cost paid: a five-way v-if fan (AdminPane.vue:12,26,45,61,64,67), three parallel switch blocks over the same union (:97, :107, :117), four unrendered branches per instance. Laws demanding the opposite: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 "one Admin frame cannot stand in for its four siblings"; OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:9 "a family frame cannot stand in for a member", with five separately-specified rows at :57-:61.
defects.mechanism: F3 — one component forked five ways where the canon specifies five compositions over one shared review-field anatomy.
defects.reproduction: Navigate /#/admin/users → /#/admin/names and observe a full unmount/remount (liveKey changes, PaneSlot Transition fires) rather than an in-place content change; read usePaneRouter.ts:165 + PaneSlot.vue:123.
defects.proposedCure: Five route bodies. The genuinely shared parts — identity band, query tray, review-row rhythm, dangerous-confirmation grammar — become ONE review-field composition consumed five times (which is what "one review-row anatomy" means), not one component branched five ways. D-09 and D-10 are downstream of this fork.

defects.defect: The ratified ADMIN5 major-section interval is --spacing(6) = 24px; the shipped query-tray→review-field interval measures 12px, inverting the grouping the composition asks for.

defects.defect: Admin's outer housing is a glass Card with an 8px cartoon caster shadow; the ratified register says structural review field / quiet data field / structural list — no Card, no caster — and Card is never the default page primitive.

Live probe computed: boxShadow "color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.8) 8px 8px 0px 0px", contain "content", overflowY "auto", display "block". defects.defect: Two dead classes on the root: `mx-auto` on a `w-full` element and `min-h-0` on a block-in-block child. Both are inert cargo.

AdminPane.vue:7 `min-h-0` — measured parent (Card root) display "block", body minHeight "0px" with no flex/grid parent to relax. Owner edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance).

defects.defect: AdminPane is a DI shim: it plants a child component instance into a composable's ref so two other modules can call five imperative methods across the tree.
defects.evidence: AdminPane.vue:134 `const adminUsersPanelRef = pm.adminUsersPanelRef;` re-exposes a ref owned by useAdminUsers (useAdminUsers.ts:27) purely so the string template ref at AdminPane.vue:27 fills it — so that usePalettePorts.ts:123 can call `admin.adminUsersPanelRef.value?.onPruneDone(pruned)` and useAdminUsers.ts:99,121,136,150 can call .updatePaletteTier(), .removeUserPalette(), .clearUserPalettes(). Five imperative calls on a child instance from two other modules, routed through a view whose only role is happening to render that child. Also not the Vue 3.5 idiom the edicts name (useTemplateRef), though that is the smaller half.
defects.mechanism: F4 — a view used as a wiring harness; state flows sideways as method calls instead of down as props.
defects.reproduction: Read AdminPane.vue:27 + :134 against useAdminUsers.ts:27,99,121,136,150 and usePalettePorts.ts:123. AdminPane cannot be moved, split, or lazily mounted without breaking prune.
defects.proposedCure: Prune/feature/delete results are state, not method calls: they flow down from the port as props and AdminUsersPanel renders them. The ref, the string binding and the alias all die together.

defects.defect: `.search-seated` is a consumer-side recipe filling a producer gap, applied as a per-instance override on a glass-ui SearchBar root at three sites, with a descendant selector reaching into producer internals.

result.strongestDefect: D-01 — every Admin route ships at exactly 50/50 beside an empty "My Palettes" companion (measured splitPct [50,50]; adminRect w:512 / companionRect w:512 at 1440), a composition ruled out by three separate binding canon documents with an explicit `50%→0` disposition (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3 laws 1-2 and §7, OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:51 and :57-61, PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-04). It is measured rather than argued, visible in eight committed screenshots, and it is the parent of D-02 (the mobile pane selector exists only to reach the right pane), D-11 (the Card/caster housing) and the 158.78px empty-state void. Nothing else in this report changes what the route IS; this one does.

Card and Badge are pure glass-ui re-exports (demo/ui/{card,badge}/index.ts), so owner edict 4 is satisfied at the import boundary. The inline gutter rung is also correct (measured paddingInlineStart 24px at 1440, 16px below the sm breakpoint, matching PR-35) — only the section interval is wrong (D-10).

result.axis: L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant), matching the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with. Not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — `demo/palettes/useAdminTags.ts:49-51` returns silently when there is no admin token, mutating no state, so `AdminTagsPanel.vue:82` falls through to the TRUE-empty branch and renders "· no tags minted · / No tags yet." to an unauthenticated viewer. The component carries a comment three lines above (`AdminTagsPanel.vue:67`: "W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty") asserting exactly the law it breaks. The mega-tranche's own visual audit captured this 60 times across 4 Safari matrices — dock rendering "Login" beside a panel reading "0 tags / No tags yet." — without recognising it, because the panel reports the lie as a designed empty state. Family: 21 identical silent `if (!token) return` sites across 5 admin composables, two of which fabricate values (`return []`, `return 0`).

(N-2) `verbatimModuleSyntax` satisfied — `AdminTagsPanel.vue:113-119` imports only values; no mis-declared type-only import. (N-4) The 4 small tap targets `REPORT.json` flags on `/#/admin/tags` are NOT this component's — live DOM probe identifies the 160×23 nameless input as the slug/token login form (`placeholder: "enter slug or token..."`, inside a `<FORM>`) and the three 22×22 buttons as the migrate dialog ("Switch to slug"/"Generate new slug"/"Cancel"), present on every route.
