(N-6) Route hygiene clean in all 4 matrices: `pageErrors: []`, `consoleErrors: []`, `failedRequests: []`, `overflowX: 0`, `counts.main: 1`, `namelessButtons: 0`.

defects.defect: The unauthenticated state renders as a TRUE empty — the panel's own "error ≠ empty" (F-2) law is broken by its own data source.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminTags.ts:49-51 — `const token = getToken(); if (!token) return;` mutates nothing (loading stays false, loadError stays null, tags stays []), so AdminTagsPanel.vue:52/:69 are both false and :82 renders `eyebrow="· no tags minted ·" message="No tags yet."`. Captured in all four matrices: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-tags.png shows the dock rendering a "Login" button (isAdminAuthenticated === false) beside "0 tags / · NO TAGS MINTED · / No tags yet."; same in safari-desktop-dark, safari-mobile-light, safari-mobile-dark. Live: browser_network_requests(filter "admin|tags|colors") on /#/admin/tags returned EMPTY — no request is issued at all. Contradicted by the component's own comment at AdminTagsPanel.vue:67. Family measured: `grep -rn "if (!token) return" demo | wc -l` → 21, across useAdminTags.ts:51,:89 · useColorNameQueue.ts:37,:53,:70,:83,:94 · useAdminAudit.ts:50 · useAdminFlagged.ts:61,:83,:95 · useAdminUsers.ts:56,:73,:84,:107,:118,:133,:146,:159(`return []`),:171,:181(`return 0`).
defects.mechanism: An auth precondition expressed as a silent early return inside the data composable instead of as a state of the resource — a masking fallback (standing edict 2). The resource has four real states (unauthenticated / loading / error / ready) but only three are representable, so two collapse onto one render.
defects.reproduction: Fresh browser profile (no `palette-admin-token` in localStorage) → http://localhost:9000/#/admin/tags → panel renders "0 tags" + "· no tags minted ·" + "No tags yet." with zero network requests. The 60-capture visual-audit matrix IS this render (dock shows "Login"). Full live re-confirmation of the no-token path was impeded by a polluted Playwright profile that restores a stale FAKE-AUDIT-TOKEN, so the finding rests on the captured matrix plus the source, not on inference.
defects.proposedCure: One `useAdminResource<T>(fetcher)` primitive in demo/palettes/admin/ returning a discriminated status — `{status:"unauthenticated"} | {status:"loading"} | {status:"error",problem} | {status:"ready",data}` — and hoist the auth gate to AdminPane.vue so no panel mounts without a token. 21 silent returns collapse to one, and "error ≠ empty ≠ unauthenticated" becomes structural instead of per-panel prose.

defects.defect: The tag chip is a hand-rolled second implementation of glass-ui `Chip`, a primitive glass-ui 7 ships and this repo already adopts elsewhere.
defects.evidence: AdminTagsPanel.vue:91-105 builds a removable pill from utility classes: `class="group flex items-center gap-1 rounded-full border border-card-edge bg-muted/30 px-2.5 py-1 text-mono-small ..."` plus a raw `<button>` with 8 more classes (opacity-0/group-hover, hover:bg-accent/50, active:scale-95, focus-visible:ring-2 ...). glass-ui already exports "./chip" (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json#exports) and node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/chip/types.d.ts declares `RemovableChipProps { mode: "removable"; removeLabel: string }` — the exact affordance, with its accessible name. chipVariants.d.ts: `SIZE.sm = "gap-1 px-2.5 py-1 text-caption"` — character-for-character the geometry retyped by hand. Already adopted at demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:14 (`import { Chip } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/chip"`), so this is a live second implementation, not an adoption gap.
defects.mechanism: Design-system primitive re-authored in a leaf, including its focus/hover/press ink — edicts 4 and 5 violated together. The `demo/ui/` barrel layer (L-6) hides which glass-ui capsules exist, so `Chip` was never discoverable from this file's import list.
defects.reproduction: Diff AdminTagsPanel.vue:94 against node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/chip/chipVariants.d.ts SIZE.sm; render both — identical box, divergent hover/focus ink and no shared remove semantics.
defects.proposedCure: `<Chip mode="removable" size="sm" :remove-label="`Delete tag ${tag.name}`" @remove="tagsApi.deleteTag(tag.name)">{{ tag.name }}</Chip>`; delete lines 91-105 wholesale. Any affordance Chip lacks is authored in glass-ui, never here.

defects.defect: The "tag" concept has four client homes against one server module; two unreconciled catalog caches fed by two different endpoints.
defects.evidence: Homes: (1) demo/palettes/api/colors.ts:15 — `getTags()`, a 17-line module named *colors* that contains only tags; (2) demo/palettes/api/admin-colors.ts:58-82 — getAdminTags/createTag/deleteTag, whose own header admits it holds "Two cohering admin concerns"; (3) demo/palettes/useAdminTags.ts — admin state + groupedTags; (4) demo/palettes/useTagEdit.ts — public catalog + per-palette patch with its own `loaded` cache. The server already has the right lattice: api/src/modules/admin/routes/tags.ts, api/src/modules/admin/service/tags.ts, api/src/modules/color/repository/tag.ts, api/src/modules/admin/__tests__/admin-tags.test.ts. Four presentations too: AdminTagsPanel.vue:94 (pill), PaletteCardMeta.vue:39 (`rounded-full bg-muted/60 px-1.5 py-0.5 text-micro`), TagEditPopover.vue:23-33 (checkbox row), SearchFilterBar.vue:50 (checkbox `filter-option`).
defects.mechanism: The client's module boundaries do not mirror the API's, even though the client transport is a 1:1 wrapper of those routes. Unique semantic ownership fails: two caches of the same catalog exist and neither invalidates the other (useTagEdit.ts:35 short-circuits on `loaded.value`).
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS (not executed — requires an admin token against a live API): open TagEditPopover (populates allTags, sets loaded=true) → go to /#/admin/tags → create a tag → reopen the popover → the new tag is absent because loadAllTags() returns at useTagEdit.ts:35 without refetching. The four-home/four-rendering enumeration itself is measured, not hypothetical.
defects.proposedCure: One `demo/palettes/tags/` capsule: transport.ts (the only file that knows the URLs, public + admin), useTags.ts (ONE catalog, ONE cache, admin writes invalidate it), TagChip.vue / TagsPanel.vue / TagEditPopover.vue. api/colors.ts disappears; admin-colors.ts keeps only the proposal queue and is renamed to what it is.

defects.defect: `ADMIN_PORT_KEY` is a 34-member god port; the panel injects the whole surface to read one member. The "dissolved" god facade grew.
defects.evidence: Measured: `awk 'NR>=195 && NR<=231' demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts | grep -cE "^\s+[a-zA-Z]+[,:]"` → 34 (adminPort); the same over 157-192 → 32 (browsePort). AdminTagsPanel.vue:122-123 does `const pm = inject(ADMIN_PORT_KEY)!; const tagsApi = pm.tags;` — 1 of 34 consumed. usePalettePorts.ts:21-31 states the intent: dissolving "the old `usePaletteManager` god facade (153 L, ONE cross-everything injected blob) into FIVE narrow, feature-owned ports"; the resulting assembler is 276 lines with a 34-member and a 32-member port.
defects.mechanism: Aggregation-by-key. Because the key is the only injection handle, every new admin capability must be appended to adminPort — edict 1 (never add to a god module) is structurally unenforceable.
defects.reproduction: Read usePalettePorts.ts:195-231 (34 members) against AdminTagsPanel.vue:122-123 (1 consumed). Re-run the two awk counts above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the port aggregation. The repo already proves the right idiom at demo/platform/auth/useAdminAuth.ts:17-24 — a lazily-initialised module-level singleton. Make useAdminTags() a singleton the same way and let the panel write `const tags = useAdminTags();`: one import, one concept, no key, no composition-root coupling, 33 fewer coupled members. The provide/inject ceremony buys testability only if the seam is substituted, and nothing in the tree substitutes it.

defects.defect: Injection keys are colocated with the provider, so every leaf statically imports the composition root — and the state layer imports and imperatively drives the view layer, closing a type-level cycle.
defects.evidence: (a) ADMIN_PORT_KEY is declared at usePalettePorts.ts:274, in the same module as providePalettePorts, which imports 14 composables plus ../platform/auth/* (:5-7) and ../shell/useViewManager (:19). So AdminTagsPanel.vue:119 pulls slug migration, palette actions, browse sorting and the shell view manager into a tag panel's static graph. The correct idiom exists and is unused here: `find demo -name "keys.ts"` returns exactly one file, demo/color-session/keys.ts, used correctly by AdminUsersPanel.vue:187. (b) demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14 — `import type { AdminUsersPanel } from "./browser/admin"` — then drives the component from the state layer at :99 (`adminUsersPanelRef.value?.updatePaletteTier(...)`), :121, :136, :150. Cycle, every edge verified: usePalettePorts.ts:9 → useAdminUsers.ts → useAdminUsers.ts:14 → browser/admin/index.ts → browser/admin/index.ts:7 → AdminTagsPanel.vue → AdminTagsPanel.vue:119 → usePalettePorts.ts.
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of dependency. The composable owns a handle to a component instance and mutates the view, instead of the view reading state. The `import type` is erased under verbatimModuleSyntax so there is no runtime cycle, but the type graph is cyclic and the architecture is inverted.
defects.reproduction: Follow the four import edges above (all file:line). Confirm the cycle closes at AdminTagsPanel.vue:119.
defects.proposedCure: (i) demo/palettes/admin/keys.ts, or no keys at all per L-4. (ii) Delete adminUsersPanelRef and its four imperative calls: updatePaletteTier / removeUserPalette / clearUserPalettes are mutations of state useAdminUsers already owns (plus a per-user palette map it should own), so the panel re-renders because state changed — which is the only reason the composable exists.

defects.defect: Two live import paths to the same design system; `demo/ui/` is 20 pure alias barrels and 24 files use both paths at once.
defects.evidence: All 20 files under demo/ui/*/index.ts are pass-through re-exports, e.g. `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`, `export { Input } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms";`, `export { Skeleton } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. Measured: `grep -rl "@mkbabb/glass-ui" demo | wc -l` → 82 (direct); barrel importers → 48; files doing BOTH → 24. The subject's own siblings are among them: AdminNamesPanel.vue:124 takes SegmentedTabs from @mkbabb/glass-ui/tabs while :125 takes Button from ../../../ui/button; AdminUsersPanel.vue:197 takes the dialog cluster from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog while :188-189 take Button/Badge from barrels. demo/ui/alert/index.ts documents its own history as a converted shim.
defects.mechanism: A pass-through re-export barrel is an alias — standing edict 2 verbatim ("no aliases, migration shims, dual paths"). Converting the barrels from local re-implementations to re-exports removed the duplication but left the alias. Second order: the barrels flatten glass-ui's subpath map (Input is really at /forms, Chip at /chip, Skeleton at the root), so a reader cannot see which glass-ui capsules a component depends on — which is why Chip was never found (L-2).
defects.reproduction: Run the three greps above; open any of the 24 dual-path files (AdminNamesPanel.vue and AdminUsersPanel.vue are the nearest).

defects.defect: AdminPane hands AdminUsersPanel a SEARCH-FILTERED user list (`:users`) while the panel derives the prune scope from that same filtered list and prints it into the confirm copy for a server-side op that is global and unfiltered. The confirm dialog for an irreversible cross-collection delete states a number smaller than the number of records the click destroys.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:28 `:users="pm.filteredAdminUsers.value"` vs :33 `:total-users="pm.adminUsers.value.length"` · demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.filter(u => !(u.paletteCount ?? 0)).length)` · :290-291 `title: \`Prune ${emptyCount.value} empty users?\`` · api/src/modules/admin/service/users.ts:228-250 `const slugs = await users.findEmptyUserSlugs()` (no filter argument; deletes users + sessions in one transaction). MEASURED (probe-C-populated.mjs, 4 seeded users / 2 empty): unfiltered dialog = 'Prune 2 empty users? This will permanently delete 2 users… This cannot be undone.'; with query 'verdant' = 'Prune 1 empty users? This will permanently delete 1 user…' while the server prunes 2. Same probe measured pruneDisabled flipping false→true under the query 'azure' while two empty users exist.
defects.mechanism: denominator drift — a filtered and an unfiltered collection cross the same prop boundary and the filtering semantics are not part of the contract; the destructive-scope count is computed from the wrong one. AdminPane is the only site that sees both.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminPane/probe-C-populated.mjs (drives the live dev server from its LAN origin 192.168.1.166:9000 with the admin-populated route mocks; sections 4 and 5 print the two dialogs).
defects.proposedCure: The panel must not compute destructive scope at all. Promote it to a filter-independent port cell (`pm.emptyUserCount`, derived from `adminUsers`, never `filteredAdminUsers`), or better, have the server return the prune preview (`GET /admin/users/prune-empty/preview → { count }`) so the confirm quotes the number the transaction will actually use. Then the filtered/unfiltered pair stops crossing the boundary: the panel gets one list to render and one count to confirm against.

defects.defect: The admin console's search field is not its own state. MEASURED live: typing only in 'Search users...' set 'Search your palettes...' to the same string, and it survived the sub-view switch into 'Search color names...'. MEASURED leak: after typing 'azure' in Browse and navigating to /#/admin/users the admin console read `Search users...="azure"` with left pane `Users 4 … 4 users Prune empty Refresh azure-fox-01 4 Palettes` — one of four rows, admin typed nothing. Isolated confirmation probe-C-mount.test.ts C-6: `port.searchQuery after typing in AdminPane = "verdant"`. The shipped capture shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png shows both fields in one frame; PalettesPane.vue:25-27 records that the team scoped the twin PLACEHOLDER and not the state.

defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminPane/probe-C-search-leak.mjs (section A: type in Browse, walk to admin/users, read the admin field and roster) and probe-C-unauthed.mjs (types only in the admin field, reads the palettes field).

The Browse pane's debounced server reload then watches its own cell, and the `currentView === "browse"` guard in usePaletteWiring.ts:159-166 (which exists solely to stop OTHER panes' typing from firing network requests) disappears with it — that guard is the tell that the shared cell was already being worked around.

The `admin-names` arm two lines below uses the filtered list — one computed, two opposite rules, and the users arm violates the rule its own sibling comment states.

defects.defect: A never-attempted load renders as an authoritative zero. `loadAdminUsers()` returns before touching `loadingUsers` or `usersLoadError` when there is no admin token, and AdminPane's badge guard covers `loadingUsers` only — so an unauthenticated visitor is shown a full, credible admin console asserting `Users 0` / `0 users` / `· ROSTER CLEAR · No users found.`, plus live Prune-empty and Refresh buttons. The size prop already resolves height and inline padding at the producer; the consumer overrides both — and the override does not even win (measured 28x36, so the producer min-height reasserts), it only obscures which rung is in force. The same three tokens are a copied idiom across the suite.
defects.evidence: AdminTagsPanel.vue:10 and :40 · measured live rects: button[aria-label="Refresh tags"] and button[aria-label="Create tag"] both 28x36 CSS px at 1440/390/320 · same idiom at AdminAuditPanel.vue:30, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10, AdminNamesPanel.vue:55,63,107 · canon: owner edict 5 'style at the shadcn/glass root component level, never per-instance overrides'; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-12

defects.proposedCure: If the admin toolbar genuinely needs a tighter rung than sm, that rung belongs in glass-ui as a size value; the six consumer sites then carry a prop, not a class.

defects.defect: The error surface pours a 400-character developer diagnostic into the user plate, centred, in monospace, at ~10 lines occupying roughly 46% of the panel body. The defect is not the message's existence but that the error composition has no length budget and no disclosure: any exception string of any length is rendered verbatim, centred, at full weight — the least readable form available.

defects.mechanism: F-C · state truth incomplete — the failure composition has no bounded shape, so severity of message length becomes severity of layout damage
defects.reproduction: Load /#/admin/tags on a dev:web-only server with an admin token present; the error arm renders exactly as captured — 10 centred mono lines beneath 'The tag ledger is unreachable.'
defects.proposedCure: The error composition owns a two-tier shape — a bounded human statement (already present) plus a COLLAPSED technical detail behind a named disclosure, left-aligned once it exceeds one line. One change in EmptyState, not in every caller.

defects.defect: `ml-0.5` is a physical margin and does not flip in RTL. In RTL the flex row reverses, so the 2px meant to separate the label from the remove glyph lands on the button's outer side against the pill's inner edge, and the intended separation drops to 0.

defects.defect: The delete control's motion is `transition-all` at 0.2s, untokenized, and animates transform (`active:scale-95`), so any property added later is animated by accident. No --animation-* token and no producer spring is involved. Reduced motion IS honoured, so this is a tokenizing and property-scope defect, not a PRM defect.
defects.evidence: AdminTagsPanel.vue:99 (`transition-all` + `active:scale-95`) · measured: transition-property 'all', duration 0.2s, timing cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) (the Tailwind default) · under prefers-reduced-motion:reduce the computed value becomes '0.1s / opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow' and settled focus is unchanged · canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6 'Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register'; owner edict 6
defects.mechanism: F-A · producer bypass — interaction motion authored ad hoc in the consumer instead of consumed from the producer register
defects.reproduction: Load /#/admin/tags, inject the replica, read getComputedStyle(btn).transitionProperty → 'all', transitionDuration → '0.2s'; then page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}) and re-read → '0.1s / opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow'.
defects.proposedCure: Name the properties (transition-opacity / transition-colors), or let the producer Chip own the interaction motion entirely.

defects.mechanism: Absence is not modelled as a state — four independent booleans (loading, loadError, tags.length, token-presence) are asked to encode five situations, so `!loading && !loadError && tags==[]` is representable for two different realities.

defects.defect: Any shape drift in GET /admin/tags crashes the entire application main region — the response is assigned to reactive state with no runtime validation.

Measured (WebKit 1440×900, authenticated, route-fulfilled): `{"items":[],"total":0}` → "This panel hit an unexpected error. / {} is not iterable"; `null` → "null is not an object (evaluating '$setup.tagsApi.tags.value.length')"; 204 empty → error plate reads "The string did not match the expected pattern."; `[{"category":"c"},{"category":"c"}]` → "2 tags", header "C", two blank pills keyed undefined. The {items:…} envelope is this same API module's own PaginatedResponse shape (api/admin-colors.ts:21-27,41-50).

defects.defect: Unguarded concurrency in loadTags: N clicks issue N requests and the LAST-TO-RESOLVE wins, so the panel deterministically settles on stale data with no loading indication.
defects.evidence: useAdminTags.ts:49-63 — no in-flight guard, no sequence number, no AbortController; the `finally` at :60-62 clears `loading` on the first resolution. Measured: three Refresh clicks → {"rapidRefresh":{"requests":["GET …/admin/tags","GET …/admin/tags","GET …/admin/tags"]}}. Forced inversion (req#2 delayed 2500ms → STALE-OLD, req#3 immediate → FRESH-NEW): {"raceMidflight":{"pills":["FRESH-NEW"],"skeletonVisible":false},"raceFinal":{"pills":["STALE-OLD"],"countLine":"1 tag","skeletonVisible":false},"raceRequestCount":3}.
defects.mechanism: Unsequenced async writes to shared reactive state — last-to-resolve rather than last-issued wins.
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/tags-probe3.mjs section R: authenticated, route /admin/tags so the 2nd call sleeps 2500ms and returns [{name:'STALE-OLD'}] while the 3rd returns [{name:'FRESH-NEW'}]; click "Refresh tags" twice 150ms apart. The list shows FRESH-NEW, then reverts to STALE-OLD 2.5s later.
defects.proposedCure: Capture a monotonic reqId before the await and bail after it if superseded; hold one AbortController on the composable and abort on re-entry; make `loading` an in-flight count, not a boolean. Same fix retires C-7's reconcile problem when paired with reconcile-by-identity.

defects.defect: The tag delete control is a 16×16 px, opacity:0, hover-revealed, hit-testable destructive button with no confirmation, no undo and no error surface — while the sibling admin console gates every destructive action behind a ConfirmDialog.

One glass-ui variant retires C-4/C-11/C-12/C-13.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardSkeleton.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. Matches the explicit Opus 5 declaration this seat was spawned with; seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1: the component's entire two-register design is addressed at a @mkbabb/glass-ui API surface that does not exist in the pinned ^7.0.0. glass-ui 7.0.0's Skeleton declares exactly one prop (`class`); `surface` and `variant` fall through to the DOM as literal HTML attributes, and all four custom properties the component writes (--skeleton-shimmer-delay, --skeleton-glass-bg, --pulse-aura-opacity-max, --animate-ambient-pulse-easing) have ZERO readers anywhere in the producer. Live-measured consequence: variant="shadow" and variant="developing" render pixel-identical (identicalRender: true), and the segment background is var(--muted) rgb(246,243,239) rather than the --skeleton-ink recipe the component and demo/styles/utils.css both claim to enforce. ~22 of the 66 non-comment lines (33%) are inert. The consumer authored the producer's public surface — dependency direction inverted.

defects.defect: The component addresses a glass-ui API surface that does not exist in the pinned ^7.0.0: props `surface`/`variant` and custom properties `--skeleton-shimmer-delay`, `--skeleton-glass-bg`, `--skeleton-shimmer-tint`, `--pulse-aura-opacity-max`, `--animate-ambient-pulse-easing` all have zero readers in the producer. Both advertised registers render identically; the ink recipe never reaches the pixels.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/skeleton/Skeleton.vue.d.ts declares only `{ class?: HTMLAttributes["class"] }`. Compiled impl at dist/data-table-BygKg6ZA.js:135-149 — `props: { class: {...} }`, useAttrs filter strips only `role` and `aria-*`, so unknown attrs reflect to the DOM. `grep -ro "skeleton-shimmer-delay" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ | wc -l` → 0; same for skeleton-shimmer-tint → 0; `grep -rl skeleton-glass-bg` and `grep -rl pulse-aura-opacity-max` over dist → no output. Producer CSS (dist/glass-ui.css): `.skeleton{...background:var(--muted)...}` and `.skeleton:after{animation:skeleton-scan-cd03d0b0 var(--duration-shimmer,2.4s) ease-in-out infinite}` — only --duration-shimmer is a real seam. LIVE PROBE (localhost:9000, Playwright, both registers mounted, count=5): rendered segment = `<div ... surface="glass" variant="breath" data-slot="skeleton" aria-hidden="true" class="skeleton h-full rounded-none" style="width: 20%; --i: 0; --skeleton-shimmer-delay: 0s;">`; backgroundColor rgb(246,243,239) [= --muted, NOT --skeleton-ink] in BOTH; element animation-name `none` in BOTH; ::after animation-name skeleton-scan-cd03d0b0, animation-delay 0s, duration 5s in BOTH; identicalRender: true. Dead sites in file: PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:43,57,63,74 (surface), :45,58,64,75 (:variant), :46, :50,60,66,77 (delay writes), :93, :99, :110-112, :120-123. Repo-wide blast radius: 12 <Skeleton> call sites across PaletteCardSkeleton.vue, AdminListSkeleton.vue:13,15,16,18, AdminTagsPanel.vue:57, Markdown.vue:4,6,7.
defects.mechanism: Inverted dependency direction — the consumer authored the producer's public surface. Component comments defer correctness to a future producer release ('the choreography goes live the day glass-ui's shimmer reads them', PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:20-21), converting a broken render into a documented waiting posture.
defects.reproduction: npm run dev; navigate http://localhost:9000; in the console mount the SFC: `const vue=await import('/@id/vue'); const m=await import('/@fs/<repo>/demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardSkeleton.vue'); const h=document.createElement('div'); document.body.append(h); vue.createApp(m.default,{count:5,variant:'shadow'}).mount(h);` then read `getComputedStyle(h.querySelector('[data-slot="skeleton"]')).backgroundColor` → rgb(246,243,239) and inspect outerHTML → literal `surface="glass" variant="breath"`. Repeat with variant:'developing' — byte-identical computed styles.
defects.proposedCure: Two legal moves, never both (edict 2 forbids the dual path). (1) PRODUCER-SIDE, preferred per edict 4: the register belongs in the design system — glass-ui's Skeleton gains `variant: "shimmer"|"breath"` and reads --skeleton-glass-bg/--skeleton-shimmer-delay; relay on the standing BH/BI inbox before any demo line moves. (2) CONSUMER-SIDE if the producer declines: delete every dead prop and property write and adopt the mechanism that already works in-tree — ShadowPalette.vue:103-114 paints `background: var(--skeleton-ink)` on its own elements and staggers with real inline animationDelay. Until one lands, `variant` must be deleted from this component's props: a prop selecting between two indistinguishable renders is a lie in the component's public shape.

defects.defect: Three independent implementations of the 'palette card lattice' exist and have already drifted: PaletteCard (+PaletteColorStrip/PaletteCardSwatches), PaletteCardSkeleton, and ShadowPalette. The card's geometry has no owner.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSkeleton.vue and ShadowPalette.vue share seven geometry constants and four stagger expressions verbatim: meta row `px-3 py-2.5 flex items-center gap-2` (PCS:55 == SP:60); name block `h-5 w-32 rounded-md` (PCS:58 == SP:62); count block `h-5 w-6 rounded-md` (PCS:64 == SP:66); swatch row `px-3 pb-3 flex flex-wrap gap-2` (PCS:70 == SP:71); swatch `w-12 h-12 sm:w-14 sm:h-14 shrink-0 rounded-badge` (PCS:76 == SP:75); delays (i-1)*0.12 / count*0.12+0.1 / +0.22 / +0.34+(i-1)*0.1 (PCS:50,60,66,77 == SP:56,63,67,77); same `count = 5` default. Two divergences from the REAL card are semantic regressions: (a) both ghosts set `overflow-hidden` on the root (PCS:34, SP:43) which PaletteCard.vue:16-18 deliberately removed — 'NO overflow-hidden (S.W5-10 / S-15-A): a card-level radius clip rasterizes 1-bit at compositing-layer bounds'; live-measured real card `overflow: visible` vs skeleton `overflow: hidden`. (b) ghosts hand-roll `shadow-cartoon-sm` where the card uses the producer atom `cartoon-surface` (PaletteCard.vue:19); live-measured box-shadow `-3px 3px 0px` (card) vs `-2px 2px 0px` (skeleton).
defects.mechanism: Ownership duplication — one concept, three homes, no tool relating them. Under-abstraction across files rather than over-accumulation in one.
defects.reproduction: diff <(sed -n '32,81p' demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardSkeleton.vue) <(sed -n '41,81p' demo/palettes/browser/card/ShadowPalette.vue) — row structure, padding, block sizes and delay arithmetic align line-for-line. Live overflow/box-shadow delta measured via the Playwright probe on /#/palettes.
defects.proposedCure: Mint the shell once and slot it. NEW demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardShell.vue (~40 lines): geometry ONLY — three rows as named slots, `swatchClass`+`count`+`showSwatches` props, zero color, zero motion, zero aria. It becomes the sole owner of h-10 / px-3 py-2.5 / px-3 pb-3 gap-2 / border-t / the no-overflow-hidden rule / cartoon-surface. PaletteCard.vue = Shell + live content. PaletteCardSkeleton.vue = Shell + <Skeleton> fills. DELETE ShadowPalette.vue (115 lines) — it is PaletteCardSkeleton at Extract's seat with count=k. Net −115 −22 −28 +40 lines and the drift table becomes unrepresentable.

defects.defect: Measured layout pop: on the browse wall the ghost is 25% taller than the card it stands in for, because the skeleton hardcodes ONE seat's swatch geometry while serving two seats, and renders a swatch row the collapsed browse card never shows.
defects.evidence: LIVE MEASUREMENT (localhost:9000/#/palettes, viewport 1440, both plates constrained to the same 462px column): realCard { h: 120, w: 462, overflow: 'visible', boxShadow: '… -3px 3px 0px …' }; skeleton { h: 150, w: 462, overflow: 'hidden', boxShadow: '… -2px 2px 0px …' }; heightDeltaPx: 30; heightDeltaPct: 25; skeletonSwatchBox { w: 56, h: 56 }. ExtractWorkbench.vue:150 passes swatch-class="w-12 h-12 sm:w-14 sm:h-14" — a verbatim duplicate of the skeleton's hardcoded PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:76 string with nothing binding them. BrowsePane.vue:90-93 passes NO swatch-class, so the wall uses the default `w-9 h-9 sm:w-10 sm:h-10` (PaletteCard.vue:197) = 40px vs the skeleton's 56px (+40%). PaletteCardSwatches renders `v-if="expanded"` (PaletteCard.vue:140), false for every card at mount, so the swatch row does not exist at rest on the wall at all. SKELETON_COUNT = 4 (BrowsePane.vue:207) → 4 × 30 = 120px of phantom vertical space collapsing at swap, under a <Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in"> whose own comment claims 'ONE surface, NEW content … instead of a hard v-if POP' (BrowsePane.vue:30-39).
defects.mechanism: L-2's duplicated lattice cashed out: a layout constant with no shared owner is correct at the seat it was copied from and wrong at every other.
defects.reproduction: Playwright on http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: mount PaletteCardSkeleton with {count:5} into the card column at the sibling card's width, then compare getBoundingClientRect().height against document.querySelector('[role="article"][aria-label^="Palette:"]') → 150 vs 120.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of L-2's PaletteCardShell: the skeleton takes the SAME swatchClass prop the card takes, threaded from the same call site, and renders the swatch row only when the card beside it would. One home for 'how big is a swatch here'.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 19 alias-only barrel directories that re-export glass-ui and contain no components — an aliasing indirection layer standing exactly where edict 4 says nothing should stand, and a false proof of the public API.
defects.evidence: `cat demo/ui/skeleton/index.ts` → the whole file is `export { Skeleton } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. Directory census: 19 dirs (alert avatar badge button card checkbox collapsible dialog dropdown-menu input label popover radio-group select separator skeleton slider switch tooltip), 0 .vue files anywhere, 18 of them exactly 1 line (alert is 11). Four files import Skeleton and ALL four go through the barrel: Markdown.vue:36, PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:85, AdminTagsPanel.vue:116, AdminListSkeleton.vue:23 — `grep -rn "Skeleton" demo/ | grep glass-ui` → 0 hits. No demo file writes the specifier a real consumer would write.
defects.mechanism: Alias / dual path (edict 2) plus design-system leakage into demo/ui (edict 4). The three-dot relative traversal makes a published package component read like a demo-local file — the proximate cause of L-1, since the author then wrote demo-side CSS against it as if it were demo-owned.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "ui/skeleton" demo/ → 4 relative hits; grep -rn "Skeleton" demo/ | grep glass-ui → 0 hits. Note the relative form itself is correct-by-ruling: vite.config.ts:68-70 records W43/RF-15 killing the demo @… path aliases. The defect is the barrel, not the dots.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all 19 directories. Write `import { Skeleton } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` at each of the four sites. The specifier then states the truth — this is a design-system component, its surface is the package's, and you may not extend it from here. demo/ui/alert/index.ts (11 lines) needs reading before deletion; the other 18 are mechanical.

defects.defect: A global utility block in demo/styles/utils.css exists only to feed producer seams that have no readers: --skeleton-glass-bg and --skeleton-shimmer-tint are written and never consumed, and the entire .specimen-seg ink-walk (plus its @supports block) feeds only the dead .skeleton-seg rule in the subject file.
defects.evidence: demo/styles/utils.css:56-83 defines `.skeleton-ink-register { --skeleton-ink: …; --skeleton-glass-bg: var(--skeleton-ink); --skeleton-shimmer-tint: …; }` and `.specimen-seg { --specimen-ink: … }` + an @supports oklch relative-color block. Reader census for --skeleton-shimmer-tint across demo/ src/ test/ e2e/: exactly 3 hits, two of them prose (utils.css:40 comment, PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:18 comment) and one the definition itself (utils.css:59) — ZERO readers. --skeleton-glass-bg: 0 readers in glass-ui dist (grep -rl → no output) and its only demo write-sites are utils.css:58 and the dead PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:111. --skeleton-ink IS live but only for ShadowPalette.vue:104-113, which reads it directly as `background`. Live probe: --skeleton-glass-bg resolves to the full color-mix chain on the segment while backgroundColor is rgb(246,243,239) = --muted.

defects.reproduction: grep -rn "skeleton-shimmer-tint" demo/ src/ test/ e2e/ → 3 hits, 2 prose + 1 definition. Live: getComputedStyle(seg).getPropertyValue('--skeleton-glass-bg') returns the recipe while getComputedStyle(seg).backgroundColor returns rgb(246,243,239).
defects.proposedCure: Delete --skeleton-glass-bg and --skeleton-shimmer-tint from .skeleton-ink-register; delete .specimen-seg and its @supports block outright (only consumer is the dead .skeleton-seg). Keep --skeleton-ink — it has one real reader. If L-1's producer-side cure lands, re-add the two seams AT THAT TIME, not before: a token minted for a future reader is speculative generality (edict 3).

defects.defect: Per-instance override of design-system motion tokens at the component root — and the tokens do not exist in the producer, so the block is a no-op that reads as a calibration.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:120-123 — `[data-slot="palette-card-skeleton"] { --pulse-aura-opacity-max: 0.75; --animate-ambient-pulse-easing: var(--ease-standard); }`, framed by the comment at :114-119 as 'tuned ONLY through the published seams … never a demo re-declaration of the producer keyframes'. Live probe: element animation-name `none` on both registers; the producer's ::after uses a hard-coded `ease-in-out`, not a token.

defects.defect: The 'loading' announcement has two homes: every ghost carries its own role="status", and the wall container carries one too — five overlapping live regions for one event on the browse wall. The sibling ShadowPalette documents the opposite rule.

PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:28-31 argues the opposite. Two components in the same directory, two contradictory rulings on one concept.

Labelled: structurally certain from source, not browser-confirmed.

defects.defect: The hard CI type gate is structurally blind to this entire defect class: Vue templates treat undeclared attributes on a component as fallthrough attrs, which are always type-legal, and no linter checks that a written CSS custom property has a reader.
defects.evidence: package.json: `"typecheck": "vue-tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json --noEmit && vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit"`, hard in CI and green per the tranche record (run 29626722378). `surface="glass"` on a component whose props are `{ class }` is a well-typed program. This is why 12 dead call sites in 4 files survived the glass-ui 7.0.0 adoption (W44) with every gate green.
defects.mechanism: Gate blindness — the verification apparatus cannot represent the invariant being violated, so the defect is invisible to it by construction.
defects.reproduction: npm run typecheck passes with the 12 dead surface/variant attrs in place (CI green per tranche record); adding a further nonsense attr to any <Skeleton> would likewise pass.
defects.proposedCure: Not a demo change. Either glass-ui's components set inheritAttrs:false + an explicit attr allowlist so a stray `variant` is visible rather than silently reflected to the DOM, or the mega-tranche adds a mechanical gate: for every custom property written in demo/, assert >=1 reader across demo/** union node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/**. The second is ~20 lines and would have caught all of L-1, L-5 and L-6.

defects.defect: Unauthenticated, the panel renders the TRUE-EMPTY plate: "0 entries / · LEDGER CLEAR · / No audit entries found." useAdminAudit.ts:50 `if (!token) return;` discards the state before the try/catch that implements the error!=empty cure, and the composable's surface (loading | loadError | entries) has no "never attempted" arm, so the view's v-if chain falls through to the honest-empty plate. Present identically in useAdminFlagged.ts:62, useAdminTags.ts:52 and useAdminUsers.ts — four panels, one hole.
defects.evidence: useAdminAudit.ts:49-50 and the UseAdminAudit interface at :15-33; AdminAuditPanel.vue:35,42,56 (the three-arm v-if chain). Measured live at http://localhost:9000/#/admin/audit: localStorage['palette-admin-token'] === null and document.body.innerText contains "0 entries · LEDGER CLEAR · No audit entries found." Corroborated by docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-audit.png (dock shows the logged-out "Login" pill beside the clear-ledger plate) and by REPORT.json, which records bodyTextLength 259 and zero page/console errors for all four matrices — the app reports perfect health while asserting a falsehood. Defeats the contract quoted at AdminAuditPanel.vue:41-42 and useAdminAudit.ts:64.
defects.mechanism: state machine split across a module boundary with one state lost at the seam — the auth precondition is swallowed by the data layer, and the view owns a trichotomy over a machine that has four states
defects.reproduction: Clear localStorage['palette-admin-token'] (or use a fresh profile) and load http://localhost:9000/#/admin/audit. Executed via Playwright; adminToken null and the quoted body text returned.
defects.proposedCure: Make the state total rather than patching the view: replace the three loose refs with one discriminated `status: "idle" | "unauthenticated" | "loading" | "error" | "ready"` on UseAdminAudit and switch the template on it exhaustively. That fixes all four panels at once and makes the missing arm a TypeScript error instead of a rendered lie. (Alternative: lift the precondition — pm.session.isAdminAuthenticated already exists at usePalettePorts.ts:139 — and have the panel render an authenticate plate and never mount the fetch.)

defects.defect: The filter policy — debounce 300ms, reset to page 1, refetch — lives in the view (AdminAuditPanel.vue:109-118) over refs the composable owns (useAdminAudit.ts:41-42 actionFilter/targetFilter, :38 page, :48 loadAuditLog, which already folds the filters into the request at :56-57). A second consumer of pm.audit reimplements it or silently gets un-debounced, page-preserving behaviour. The raw setTimeout also has no onUnmounted teardown.
defects.evidence: AdminAuditPanel.vue:110-118 (`let filterTimeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>; watch([audit.actionFilter, audit.targetFilter], () => { clearTimeout(filterTimeout); filterTimeout = setTimeout(() => { audit.page.value = 1; audit.loadAuditLog(); }, 300); });`) against useAdminAudit.ts:38,41-42,48,56-57. @vueuse/core@^14.3.0 is a declared dependency used in six demo files (useStorage, useMediaQuery, useEventListener, useMagicKeys) and ships watchDebounced; `grep -rn "useDebounceFn|watchDebounced|refDebounced" demo/palettes/` -> 0.
defects.mechanism: ownership split — an invariant over composable-owned state parked in a view, plus a hand-rolled version of an installed primitive
defects.reproduction: The absent onUnmounted teardown is fact (read AdminAuditPanel.vue:109-119 — the file ends at 120 with only onMounted). HYPOTHESIS, labelled, on the observable consequence: AdminPane.vue:61 mounts this panel under v-if, so switching sub-view within 300ms of a keystroke leaves a live timer that mutates app-root port state (audit.page.value = 1) for an unmounted panel; the network call does not fire unauthenticated because loadAuditLog early-returns at useAdminAudit.ts:50, so I did not observe it.
defects.proposedCure: Move the debounce into useAdminAudit as watchDebounced([actionFilter, targetFilter], …, { debounce: 300 }) inside the composable's own effect scope, and delete AdminAuditPanel.vue:109-118. The view then contains no policy at all, and the scope handles teardown.

defects.defect: AdminAuditPanel injects ADMIN_PORT_KEY — a 34-member object — to read exactly one member (pm.audit). Its declared type AdminPort = ReturnType<typeof providePalettePorts>["admin"] forces TypeScript to instantiate the return type of the entire five-port composition root. Worse, the parent uses two wiring idioms simultaneously: AdminPane.vue passes 8 and 12 props into two panels and mounts the other three bare to self-inject.
defects.evidence: Parsed count of the adminPort object literal in demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts -> 34 members spanning three unrelated sub-domains (users, colour-name queue, audit/flagged/tags) plus searchQuery, searchPlaceholder, expandedId, toggleExpand and a component ref. AdminAuditPanel.vue:107-108. Type alias at usePalettePorts.ts:255-259. usePalettePorts.ts:23-31 calls itself the dissolution of the usePaletteManager god facade into "FIVE narrow, feature-owned ports." AdminPane.vue:20-60 (props idiom) vs :61,:64,:67 (bare-mount inject idiom) — same parent, adjacent template lines, opposite contracts. AdminAuditPanel.vue:107 `inject(ADMIN_PORT_KEY)!` also discards the failure mode (bare TypeError outside the provider, no diagnostic); consistent tree-wide, so INFO within this finding.
defects.mechanism: god-port — an aggregate wider than any consumer's real dependency, so every panel over-declares and the type instantiation pulls the whole composition root
defects.reproduction: python3 parse of the adminPort literal (34 keys, pasted in the report); read of AdminPane.vue:20-67.
defects.proposedCure: Split port 4 into the five keys the composition root already builds as five separate objects at usePalettePorts.ts:68-76 — AUDIT_PORT_KEY: InjectionKey<UseAdminAudit>, FLAGGED_PORT_KEY, TAGS_PORT_KEY, ADMIN_USERS_PORT_KEY, COLOR_QUEUE_PORT_KEY. Each panel injects its own and nothing else; the type instantiation collapses to the sub-composable's own interface. Then pick one wiring idiom for all five panels.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue (+ its composable useAdminAudit.ts, transport, styles, and tests)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared at spawn, observed and named in the report's Model receipt; not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-2 — AdminAuditPanel.vue:59: the entries `v-for` is a SIBLING of the loading/error/empty `v-if` chain rather than its terminal branch, so `loadError` and `loading` decorate a fully populated ledger instead of replacing it. Measured: `[C-2] loadError set -> errorBanner=true rows=2 toolbarCount="2"`, rendered text `"2 entriesThe ledger is unreachable.user.deleteJul 4, 08:00 PMspammer-42palette.featureJul 4, 09:00 PMsunset-riot"`. The component's own comment at :40-41 declares the invariant it breaks ("error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger"), and the markup inverts F-2 into something worse: on the product's record-of-truth surface a dead backend costumes as a COMPLETE, timestamped, authoritative ledger. One `v-else` cures it. AdminTagsPanel.vue:85 and AdminNamesPanel.vue:43/93 already do it right; AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:44 shares the defect.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Two honest negatives recorded for completeness: the panel contributes ZERO nameless buttons and ZERO small tap targets — all three of its controls measured live at 128x36, 109.1x36, 28x36, and REPORT.json's four `/#/admin/audit` smallTapTargets belong to the dock/palettes pane, not this component; and `verbatimModuleSyntax` (edict 8) is clean in both files.)

defects.defect: The entries `v-for` sits OUTSIDE the loading/error/empty `v-if` chain, so the shadow plate and the error plate render ON TOP OF a fully populated ledger instead of replacing it. Inverts the panel's own stated F-2 invariant into a worse failure mode.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-56 (chain) vs :59-80 (unconditional sibling). Compiler proof: `compileTemplate` output ends the chain with `: _createCommentVNode("v-if", true),` then emits `_renderList(_ctx.audit.entries.value, …)` as a sibling fragment. Mount proof: `[C-1] loading=true -> skeletons=3 rows=2`; `[C-2] loadError set -> errorBanner=true rows=2 toolbarCount="2"`; rendered text `"2 entriesThe ledger is unreachable.user.deleteJul 4, 08:00 PMspammer-42palette.featureJul 4, 09:00 PMsunset-riot"`. Correct siblings: AdminTagsPanel.vue:85, AdminNamesPanel.vue:43/93. Same defect: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:44.
defects.mechanism: Missing `v-else` terminal branch — the state machine's exhaustive chain does not own the success rendering, so states are additive rather than exclusive.

Also reproducible by inspection of the compiled render function.
defects.proposedCure: Make the list the chain's terminal branch: `<div v-else class="grid gap-2">` wrapping the `v-for`, matching AdminTagsPanel/AdminNamesPanel. Relay the identical fix to AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:44 — it is a two-member family, not a one-off.

defects.defect: `loadAuditLog` returns silently when there is no admin token, leaving loading=false / loadError=null / entries=[] — which drives the template past the error branch into the TRUE-EMPTY specimen plate `· ledger clear · No audit entries found.` The F-2 costume, re-entered through the auth gate instead of the network gate.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:49-50 `const token = getToken(); if (!token) return;` -> AdminAuditPanel.vue:56 renders `eyebrow="· ledger clear ·"`. Mount: `[C-6] no token -> loading=false loadError=null entries=0 total=0` / `[C-6] panel text with no token: "0 entriesNo audit entries found."`. ALREADY SHIPPING IN CAPTURED EVIDENCE: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-audit.png shows the dock reading "Login" (unauthenticated) beside the panel declaring "0 entries · LEDGER CLEAR · No audit entries found." — all four matrices, REPORT.json bodyTextLength 259, zero rows.
defects.mechanism: A precondition failure is encoded as a no-op instead of as a state, so the view's default (empty) is used as the answer for an unknown condition.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config …/pi/vitest.probe.config.ts (case C-6) with an empty localStorage shim; or open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/audit with no `palette-admin-token` in localStorage.
defects.proposedCure: The token guard must produce a state, not a silence: add a `notAuthenticated` branch to the composable and a sign-in plate to the chain. Not a `loadError` string — this is a precondition, not a failure, and it wants its own register.

defects.defect: `adminRequest` returns `res.json()` with zero shape validation and `useAdminAudit` assigns straight through, so any 200 with the wrong envelope sets `entries.value = undefined` AND clears `loadError` — the render then throws and the designed error plate never fires.
defects.evidence: demo/platform/transport/client.ts:155 `return res.json();` (no validation). demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:60-63 `entries.value = res.data; total.value = res.total; loadError.value = null;`. Mount: `[C-8] after 200-with-{} -> entries=undefined total=undefined loadError=null` and `[C-8] render threw: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` (thrown at AdminAuditPanel.vue:56).
defects.mechanism: Unvalidated trust of a network boundary combined with an optimistic success-path write — the composable cannot distinguish 'succeeded' from 'returned garbage', so the failure is invisible to the error apparatus.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config …/pi/vitest.probe.config.ts (case C-8) — `vi.doMock` `getAuditLog` to resolve `{}`, call `loadAuditLog()`, then mount the panel: render throws.
defects.proposedCure: Validate the envelope once at the transport boundary for the whole admin surface — a `PaginatedResponse<T>` shape assertion in `adminRequest` (or `parsePaginated` in api/admin-audit.ts) that throws an `ApiProblem`, so the existing error plate does its job. NOT a `?? []` at the callsite: that masks a real backend break (edict 2).

defects.defect: `loadAuditLog` has no request sequencing — no in-flight token, no sequence id, no AbortController — so a slow stale response overwrites a newer one, and `loading` is cleared by whichever request settles first. Refresh is never disabled while loading; nextPage/prevPage gate on hasNext/hasPrev but not on loading.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:48-71 (no guard), :68-70 `finally { loading.value = false }`, :73-85 (nextPage/prevPage ungated on loading); AdminAuditPanel.vue:30 (Refresh Button, no `:disabled`), :115 (debounced load), :119 (mount load). Mount: `[C-7] after fresh(page3) lands: entries=[{"id":"off-40"}] loading=false` then `[C-7] after stale(page2) lands: entries=[{"id":"off-20"}] page=3` — the pager reads page 3 while the rows are page 2's, and `loading` went false with a request still pending.
defects.mechanism: Last-writer-wins over a shared mutable cell; `loading` modelled as a boolean where a concurrent-request count is required.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config …/pi/vitest.probe.config.ts (case C-7) — mock getAuditLog with manually-held resolvers, fire page 2 then page 3, resolve page 3 first then page 2. By hand: hold the Next button, or type in the target filter while a refresh is in flight.
defects.proposedCure: A monotonic request id captured at call time; apply the response only if it is still the newest (`if (seq !== latest) return`), and clear `loading` on the same condition. Disable Refresh and the pager while a request is outstanding. Lives in the composable, not the SFC.

defects.defect: The 300ms filter-debounce `setTimeout` is never cleared on unmount. There is no `onUnmounted`/`onScopeDispose` in the file, and the callback closes over the module-singleton admin port — so it fires after destruction, resets `page` to 1 and issues an orphan fetch into state the user is no longer looking at.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:110-117 (`let filterTimeout`, `setTimeout(…, 300)`, no cleanup hook anywhere in the 120-line file). The port is a singleton: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:72 + :245; the panel is a plain `v-if` with no KeepAlive at that level: demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:61. Mount with fake timers: `[C-3] after unmount + 400ms -> loadAuditLog calls=2 page=1` (mounted with page=4).
defects.mechanism: A timer whose lifetime exceeds its owner's, writing into state whose lifetime exceeds them both — the classic missing-cleanup leak, amplified because the target is a shared singleton rather than component-local state.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config …/pi/vitest.probe.config.ts (case C-3). By hand: type one character in the "Action…" filter, then click the Users tab within 300ms.
defects.proposedCure: Move the debounce into the composable that owns the state — expose `setFilters(action, target)` from `useAdminAudit` and let its own `effectScope` own the timer. Minimum viable: `onUnmounted(() => clearTimeout(filterTimeout))`.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate. Zero unit tests touch AdminAuditPanel or useAdminAudit. The only e2e coverage asserts a heading rendered by a DIFFERENT component, one button's accessible name, and an empty console — under the EMPTY-envelope fixture. The populated fixture routes /admin/audit with 3 seeded entries but no spec that uses it ever navigates there, so the component has never rendered a single row in any test, the visual matrix, or the live capture. This is the mechanism behind D-1 and D-2.
defects.evidence: `grep -rln "useAdminAudit|AdminAuditPanel" test/ demo/test/` -> empty. e2e/smoke/admin/admin-walk.spec.ts:37-40 (the WALK row), :74-84 (heading + control assertions), :88 (`expect(consoleErrors).toEqual([])`) — the heading "Audit Log" is rendered by AdminPane.vue:3-6, not this component. e2e/smoke/admin/fixtures/admin-populated.ts:170 routes /admin/audit with AUDIT (:79-83), but `grep -n goto` over admin-populated.spec.ts / a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts / o10d-admin-title-voice.spec.ts shows only users/names/flagged. e2e is not typechecked (package.json:65 runs vue-tsc on tsconfig.lib.json + tsconfig.demo.json only), which is why admin-populated.ts:22 still imports from `demo/@/lib/palette/types` — `ls demo/@` -> No such file or directory.
defects.mechanism: Assertions aimed at chrome (a heading owned by the parent, a button name) rather than at behaviour, on a fixture that guarantees the behaviour can never occur.
defects.reproduction: Mutations that keep the suite green: delete the whole entries v-for (:59-80); delete `onMounted(() => audit.loadAuditLog())` (:119); delete the debounced filter watch (:110-117); make formatTime return ""; swap the error EmptyState (:42) for the empty one (:56); delete <PaginationBar> (:83-90); hardcode total to 0. Each removes load-bearing behaviour and is undetected.
defects.proposedCure: Point the existing populated fixture at the route it already serves: add /#/admin/audit to a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts:28-30 and one populated spec asserting 3 rows, action/target text, a filter round-trip, and the error plate under a routed 500. Add the unit suite that does not exist: useAdminAudit sequencing (D-5), the no-token branch (D-3), the malformed-body branch (D-4). Also bring e2e into a typecheck program so the dead `demo/@` import surfaces.

defects.defect: The loading plate's accessible name is silently dropped by the browser: `aria-label` on a role-less <div> maps to role=generic, for which WAI-ARIA 1.2 specifies "Name from: prohibited". What AT actually receives instead is three identical `role=status "Loading"` announcements from the three skeletons. No `aria-busy`; no live region for the count; no list semantics on the 20 sibling row divs.
defects.evidence:
AdminAuditPanel.vue:36 `
`, :37 `v-for="i in 3"` of AdminListSkeleton which each carry `role="status" aria-label="Loading"` (AdminListSkeleton.vue:11-12). PROVEN LIVE via ariaSnapshot (pi/probe-aria.mjs), input `
inner
` + `
`, output: `- text: inner` / `- status "Loading audit log"` — the generic div contributes nothing. Mount: `[C-5] tag=DIV role=(none) aria-live=(none) aria-busy=(none)`, and C-5 asserts no `[role=list]` in the panel. Correct in the neighbourhood: PaginationBar.vue:17, EmptyState.vue:17/:29.
defects.mechanism: Naming an element whose implicit role prohibits accessible names; the a11y intent is present in the markup but discarded by the AX mapping, so the surface reads as remediated while being unremediated.
defects.reproduction: Run docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminAuditPanel/pi/probe-aria.mjs against http://localhost:9000 — the injected role-less div's name is absent from the ARIA snapshot; the role=status sibling's is present.
defects.proposedCure: One `role="status"` + `aria-busy` region around the list; `aria-hidden="true"` on the three skeletons (decoration once the region is named); `role="list"`/`listitem` on the rows (free if D-1's AdminListItem transposition lands); move the `{{ total }} entries` count inside the live region so filter results announce.

defects.defect: `formatTime`'s try/catch fallback is unreachable — `Date.prototype.toLocaleString` does not throw on an Invalid Date, it returns the string "Invalid Date" — so a malformed or missing timestamp renders "Invalid Date" into the audit row instead of falling back to the raw ISO string.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/dateFormat.ts:2-13. `node -e 'try{new Date("x").toLocaleString(undefined,{month:"short",day:"numeric",hour:"2-digit",minute:"2-digit"})}catch(e){…}'` -> "Invalid Date", NO THROW. Probe: `[C-4] formatTime("not-an-iso-timestamp") = "Invalid Date"`, `[C-4] formatTime(undefined as any) = "Invalid Date"`, `[C-4] formatTime("") = "Invalid Date"`, and rendered into the row: `[C-4b] row text: "1 entryx.yInvalid Datet"`.
defects.mechanism: A masking fallback guarding the wrong failure signal — RangeError comes from toISOString and from invalid options, never from an invalid date value.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config …/pi/vitest.probe.config.ts (case C-4 / C-4b); or the one-line node command above.
defects.proposedCure: `const d = new Date(iso); return Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) ? iso : d.toLocaleString(…)`. Drop the try/catch entirely — it never did anything.

defects.defect: A hover affordance on a row that is not interactive: `hover:bg-accent/50 transition-colors` on a div with no @click, no role, no tabindex, no cursor-pointer, no focus-visible treatment. The row lights up under the pointer and does nothing, and keyboard users cannot reach it at all. Every other hover:bg-accent/50 in the tree is paired with real interactivity.
defects.evidence: AdminAuditPanel.vue:62. Paired instances elsewhere: AdminUsersPanel.vue:82-86 (`cursor-pointer hover:bg-accent/50 focus-visible:bg-accent/50 focus-visible:ring-2` + `:tabindex`), AdminTagsPanel.vue:94 and :99 (on <button>, with focus-visible:ring-2), PaletteSlugBar.vue:73/84/91 (same pairing). AdminAuditPanel.vue:62 is the sole unpaired instance.
defects.mechanism: Decoration borrowed from an interactive grammar without the semantics that grammar implies — a false affordance, and a mouse-only one.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis-free proof by inspection: grep for `hover:bg-accent` across demo/ shows the audit row is the only occurrence with no cursor-pointer, no focus-visible, no role/tabindex and no click handler in its element.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the hover class — an audit ledger row is a readout, and that is the honest register. Folding into AdminListItem per D-1 removes it for free. If a disclosure is genuinely wanted, do it the way AdminUsersPanel.vue:82-86 did (role + tabindex + focus ring).

defects.defect: A raw internal `Error.message` is piped verbatim into the error plate's user-facing detail slot. Live, that is 443 characters of developer prose occupying 444x252px inside the panel, exposing the build tooling, the internal API hostname and shell commands to a moderator-facing surface.
defects.evidence: AdminAuditPanel.vue:46 `:detail="audit.loadError.value"` fed by demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:64-66 `catch (e: any) { loadError.value = e?.message ?? "Backend unreachable" }`. Live measurement: {"detailLen":443,"detailBox":{"w":444.1,"h":252.5},"detailTag":"P.text-mono-small plate-ink max-w-[44ch] break-words"}. Screenshot: pi/live-error-detail-dump.png — the Audit Log card is dominated by "value.js dev is MISCONFIGURED: http://localhost:9000 has no VITE_API_URL and is targeting the cross-origin production API (https://api.color.babb.dev) … Run `npm run dev` (the full local stack via scripts/dev.sh up)…". EmptyState.vue:79 documents `detail` as "the caught message" — correct for ApiProblem.detail, not a licence for an unbounded arbitrary Error.message.
defects.mechanism: No narrowing between the throw surface and the presentation surface: every throwable in the transport graph (DevMisconfigError, ApiUnavailableError, ApiProblem, TypeError) reaches the DOM with the same fidelity.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/audit with any value in localStorage['palette-admin-token'] — the dev-misconfig latch (demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:151-164, 188-195) throws before fetch and its 443-char message renders. Measured via pi/probe-live.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Narrow the catch: surface `ApiProblem.detail` when the throw is an ApiProblem, a fixed short string otherwise, and keep the raw error on `console.warn` (which useAdminAudit.ts:67 already does). ApiProblem already carries a bounded user-facing detail — use it.

defects.defect: `class="h-7 px-2"` is a per-instance override of a glass-ui root component (edict 5 violation) AND it is dead: glass-ui's root `min-height: 36px` wins, so `h-7` (28px) changes the rendered height by zero pixels. `px-2` does apply, leaving an unrequested 28x36 aspect.
defects.evidence: AdminAuditPanel.vue:30 `<Button variant="outline" size="sm" class="h-7 px-2" aria-label="Refresh audit log" …>`. Live computed style: {"refreshBtn":{"h":"36px","minH":"36px","cls":"button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover h-7 px-2"}} and bounding box 28x36. Copy-pasted identically at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10.
defects.mechanism: Callsite styling fighting a design-system root and losing — the override survives in the markup implying an effect it does not have.
defects.reproduction: page.evaluate on http://localhost:9000/#/admin/audit: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Refresh audit log"]')).height -> "36px", minHeight -> "36px", while the element carries class h-7.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `h-7 px-2` and let `size="sm"` speak. If a tighter icon-only rung is genuinely wanted it is a glass-ui Button variant (edict 4), not a demo-side class list — and it should be relayed to the glass-ui BH inbox per the standing fond.

defects.defect: `duration-fast` at the callsite is a measured no-op against a rule the repo wrote down: foundation.css already aliases the bare-utility transition default to the house token expressly so no callsite needs the modifier.
defects.evidence: AdminAuditPanel.vue:62 `transition-colors duration-fast`. demo/styles/foundation.css:122-129: "Alias it at the @theme ROOT to the house motion tokens so every un-tuned `transition` utility speaks the app's fast duration + standard ease by construction — no per-callsite modifier." Live measurement: {"dur":"0.2s","baseDur":"0.2s","tokenFast":"0.2s","tokenTdFast":"0.2s"} — `transition-colors duration-fast` and bare `transition-colors` are both 0.2s.
defects.mechanism: Redundant per-callsite modifier duplicating a root token alias — noise, not behaviour.
defects.reproduction: page.evaluate on the live page: append a div with class 'transition-colors duration-fast' and one with 'transition-colors', read getComputedStyle().transitionDuration on both -> 0.2s and 0.2s.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the modifier. Nothing changes visually (edict 6 satisfied — no animation is removed, only a redundant restatement of the default).

defects.defect: `total` is trusted raw from the wire at the domain boundary: pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize)) guards the low side and nothing guards the high side or NaN.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:44, fed by the unvalidated assignment at :62 (see D-4). Measured (case C-9): total=NaN -> pageCount=NaN hasNext=false toolbar="NaN" (and PaginationBar's `v-if="pageCount > 1"` is false, so the pager silently disappears); total=Infinity -> pageCount=Infinity hasNext=true toolbar="Infinity" (always-enabled Next, pages forever past the end); total=-5 -> toolbar="-5"; total=null -> blank count; total="40" (string) -> works by coercion but the strict `total.value === 1` pluralisation at AdminAuditPanel.vue:27 renders "1 entries" for the string "1".
defects.mechanism: Arithmetic on an unvalidated wire value; a one-sided clamp treated as validation.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config …/pi/vitest.probe.config.ts (case C-9) — mount the panel with total set to each of NaN / Infinity / -5 / null / "40" and read pageCount, hasNext and the toolbar text.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-4's envelope validation at the transport boundary — a validated `total: number` makes the clamp unnecessary. Separately, make the pluralisation coercion-safe (`Number(total) === 1`) or derive it from the validated number.

defects.defect: House idioms missed in the composable: `entries` is a deep-reactive `ref` over a collection that is only ever replaced wholesale (shallowRef is the edict-7 idiom), and the catch is typed `any` in a repo that tracks `as any = 0` as a gate.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:35 `const entries = ref<AuditEntry[]>([]);` — up to 20 objects deep-proxied, never mutated in place (only `entries.value = res.data` at :61). :64 `catch (e: any)`. (Negative recorded: verbatimModuleSyntax / edict 8 is CLEAN — :9 `import { ref, computed, type Ref }`, :11 `import type { AuditEntry }`, and the SFC has no type-only imports.)
defects.mechanism: Default reactivity depth applied to a replace-only collection; untyped catch binding.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis-free proof by inspection of demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:35 and :61 (the only write site) and :64.
defects.proposedCure: `shallowRef<AuditEntry[]>([])` for entries. `catch (e: unknown)` with an `instanceof ApiProblem` narrowing — which is the same narrowing D-11's cure needs, so the two land together.

defects.defect: The shared admin row atom exists and is bypassed, so the skeleton the panel shows shadows a row shape the panel does not render; and the AuditEntry.ipHash field is fetched on every request and never displayed.
defects.evidence: AdminListItem.vue is the admin row atom, used by AdminNamesPanel.vue:44 and :94; AdminListSkeleton.vue:2-6 states it is "shaped as the AdminListItem row grammar (leading swatch + primary/secondary lines + trailing action lozenge)". AdminAuditPanel.vue:59-80 duplicates the markup instead (root cause of D-1 and D-10) and renders neither a swatch nor an action, so AdminAuditPanel.vue:37's three skeletons shadow a shape that never arrives. demo/palettes/types.ts:122 declares `ipHash: string` on AuditEntry; it appears nowhere in the panel.

defects.defect: The documented 'same bones, ONE recipe' contract between PaletteCardSkeleton and ShadowPalette is false in every measurable dimension — the two ghosts swap in the same Extract seat with opposite ink polarity, different corner geometry and flat vs graded ink.

defects.defect: The loading register has no terminal arm: no slow state, no stalled state, no route to failure. A 200ms wait and an infinite wait are the same picture.
defects.evidence: No duration, escalation or failure branch exists in the 124-line source. `useImageQuantize.ts:87` sets `isProcessing` true and only :65/:71 clear it; DEFECT-LEDGER.md:7499 reproduces the plate still ghosted 4s after a successful decode. DEFECT-LEDGER.md:10440: a 4000x3000 upload blocks the main thread 517ms and the skeleton 'never renders'. Error is handed to a different component with no visual continuity (BrowsePane.vue:59 `EmptyState variant="error"`; ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85 bare div). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 binds: 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit.'
defects.mechanism: Pending is modelled as a shape, not as a state with value/duration/outcome, so there is nowhere to express escalation or failure.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the stall itself in this session — cited from DEFECT-LEDGER.md:7499 and :10440, which carry their own reproductions. The absence of any slow/failed branch is verified by reading the full 124-line source.
defects.proposedCure: Give the pending arm a state object (elapsed, escalation threshold, outcome) and one route to the error register inside the same plate, so the surface never swaps components to report failure. Pairs with the D-13 single-live-region cure.

defects.defect: In reduced-motion and forced-colors the loading register carries no perceptible signal at all: it degrades to twelve static boxes, which is exactly the resting appearance of the empty-state ghost. The source claims a PRM 'trough' that does not exist.

defects.proposedCure: Design a static differentiator that survives both environments — a non-motion register (border/dash/label) that distinguishes pending from empty — and drop the false PRM claim from the source.

defects.defect: Canon violations on the plate itself: a cartoon cast shadow on a palette slip (tuple says shadow=false), a card-level `overflow-hidden` that the loaded card documents as a rendering defect, and an elevation step at handoff.

defects.defect: No gate in the repository can observe any of the above: the demo typecheck is clean and the one e2e oracle asserts DOM presence only.
defects.evidence: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0, 0 lines of output (Vue template typing permits arbitrary fallthrough attributes on components, so `surface="glass" variant="breath"` on a one-prop component is legal). `e2e/smoke/views/browse-loading.spec.ts` asserts only `expect(skeletons.first()).toBeVisible()`, `toHaveCount(0)` for `svg.animate-spin`, and card count after load — no ink, radius, phase or silhouette assertion. The 60-capture Safari matrix settles at ~3.5s (visual/REPORT.md:121,137) and contains zero frames of this component.

A presence assertion cannot close a visual row (PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.8).

defects.proposedCure: Key any revived sweep/stagger on the inline axis, not on physical left→right. Currently moot because both mechanisms are dead (D-1, D-5).

defects.defect: 43% of the file (53 of 124 lines) is prose asserting, in the present indicative, behaviour that has never executed — the habitat that let a fully inert design survive four tranches.

result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded for balance (report §4): motion property choice is correct (transform-only on a ::after, `will-change: transform`, no layout-forcing property animated); reduced motion IS honoured at the producer level (the scan sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`); forced-colors has a producer arm; zoom to 200% is clean because every dimension is rem-derived (`h-10`, `w-32`, `w-12/14`); glass-ui's Skeleton emits `aria-hidden=\"true\"` per leaf so only the plate root announces; Vue 3.5 idiom is correct (reactive props destructure with defaults at :87, no withDefaults boilerplate, no defineModel stale-read hazard); `verbatimModuleSyntax` is satisfied (no type-only imports needed); `role=\"status\"` is the correct role choice for this component (the defect is cardinality, D-13, not the choice); and both host routes are clean on the overflow and landmark axes — `visual/REPORT.md:22,28` report `horizontalOverflow 0` and `mainCountNotOne 0` across all 60 captures.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)

result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the audit ledger has no actor. The server puts `actorSlug` and `payload` on the wire for every event (api/src/modules/admin/service/audit.ts:17-25), the client type deletes both (demo/palettes/types.ts:117-123), and the row anatomy has no third slot for them (AdminAuditPanel.vue:64-79). Three binding canon instruments require the opposite — OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:59 ("actor/scope/effect", "detail disclosure"), VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 ("Actor, scope, provenance and effect remain visible"), PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-11. `impersonate` — the most sensitive event in the product — renders as "IMPERSONATE · Jul 27, 04:29 PM · slug=mbabb": it names the victim and never the perpetrator. A record of what happened with no record of who made it happen does not do the one job the route exists for.

(For completeness, the edicts the component DOES satisfy, each verified: #1 no god module — 120 lines, state delegated to useAdminAudit; #2 no legacy code — no shim/alias/dual path/back-compat fallback anywhere; #3 KISS — no invented shared/ dir or wrapper; #6 animations never deleted — the component adds no keyframes and removes none, its transition register is globally inherited; #8 verbatimModuleSyntax — AdminAuditPanel.vue:95-104 imports only values and the sole type usage `ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>` at line 110 needs no import. Also NOT filed after re-measurement: "the Badge renders with no chrome" (my first replica omitted the real badgeVariants class string; re-run with glass-ui's own cn(badgeVariants({variant:'secondary'}),…) the badge measures 16.4px/600/bg rgb(237,230,222)/padding 4px 10px/radius 9999px) and "reduced motion is not honoured" (matchMedia matched true; the row resolves to a 0.1s colour transition with zero geometry movement, which VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6 permits).

defects.defect: The audit ledger cannot answer *who*: the server sends `actorSlug` and `payload` on every event, the client `AuditEntry` type drops both, `ipHash` is typed but never rendered, and the row anatomy has no slot for actor, scope-effect or the canon-mandated detail disclosure.

defects.defect: Signed out, the panel reports the administrative audit trail as clear — the exact P0 its own comment (line 40-41 'a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger') claims to have cured. All four shipped Safari captures are this false-empty.

defects.defect: The loading grammar is broken twice: the `v-else-if` chain terminates before the list so skeletons render stacked ABOVE the stale rows (and the error plate renders above the rows it contradicts), and the shared skeleton is the shadow of a different component's shape.

defects.defect: A hover state that promises an action the design never built: the row repaints on pointer-over while the cursor stays `auto`, tabIndex is -1, there is no role, no click handler, no keyboard path, and no detail disclosure for a click to open.

defects.reproduction: node AAP-probe2.mjs → hover.pre 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' vs hover.post.bg 'oklab(0.871139 0.007229 0.023625 / 0.5)' with hover.post.cursor 'auto'; d1440.rowTabIndex -1, d1440.rowRole null.

The canon already names the destination (OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:59 'contextual event detail' / 'detail disclosure'): one native named `<button type="button" aria-expanded>` spanning the row, a focus register distinct from hover, and `payload` behind it.

defects.defect: In the error state the toolbar still asserts `0 entries` beside 'The ledger is unreachable.' — the count falls back to its initial zero (or a stale previous page count) rather than going to an unknown state.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never colour-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit.' defects.proposedCure: A count is a measured value; when the measurement fails the readout goes to its unknown state (`—`) or leaves the toolbar. Never fall back to 0.

defects.defect: Offset pagination over a `timestamp:-1` feed where the binding composition requires a stable cursor — concurrent inserts shift the window, so a page turn can silently skip an event; the cursor response type already exists in the codebase and was not adopted.

OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:59 result column: 'Companion 0; stable cursor, actor/scope/effect and readable event density.' demo/palettes/types.ts:132 already declares `CursorPaginatedResponse<T>`, in use elsewhere in the same module.
defects.mechanism: offset window over a mutating descending-time feed
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis at runtime (needs a live backend with concurrent writes). The source-level mechanism is confirmed by the three coordinates above.
defects.proposedCure: Cursor on `(timestamp, _id)`; the response type is already in the tree.

defects.defect: The timestamp drops the year and the timezone, repeats the full date on all 20 rows of a page, and its variable-width AM/PM defeats the `tabular-nums` it is given.

defects.defect: The loading region's accessible name is discarded (aria-label on a role-less div), so the loading state announces 'Loading' three times without ever saying what; and the filter's result count — the thing that changes — has no live region, contrary to the navigation/announcement law.
defects.evidence: AdminAuditPanel.vue:36 `<div v-if=… class="grid gap-2" aria-label="Loading audit log">` — no role, so the name is not exposed; AdminListSkeleton.vue:11-12 each carry their own `role="status" aria-label="Loading"`. The sibling does it right: AdminTagsPanel.vue:51-56 puts role=status + a specific label on the wrapper. Count span at line 26 has no aria-live. Measured live: the only live regions on the route are the error plate's role=alert and the COMPANION card's role=status. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.1: 'in-route filter, tab, selection, or pagination → … announce changed result count/state through the owning status region'. PaginationBar.vue:17 does announce its page, so the grammar exists and the count was left out of it.
defects.mechanism: ARIA applied to a generic element that cannot carry it; the owning status region never designated
defects.reproduction: node AAP-probe5.mjs → errD1440light.liveRegions lists exactly two regions, neither of which is the entries count.
defects.proposedCure: role="status" on the loading wrapper with the children mute; aria-live="polite" on the count, which is the natural owning status region for the filter.

defects.defect: Machine strings — slugs, ids, `k=v` targets — are rendered without bidi isolation, so they reorder inside RTL flow.

Measured in the RTL arm: the row mirrors (badge x=997.2, timestamp x=860.0, target starting x=708.5) with no isolation attribute anywhere in the subtree. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1: 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance → render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose'; §5.2 last row repeats it.
defects.mechanism: domain strings treated as prose
defects.reproduction: node AAP-probe2.mjs (the rtl1440 arm sets dir="rtl" on documentElement) → rtl1440 rects mirror; grep the component for `dir`/`bdi` → zero hits.
defects.proposedCure: Wrap target, action and timestamp in `<bdi>` (or dir="ltr") — one change covers all three.

defects.defect: 209 px of unowned card sits beneath the empty plate at desktop — 40.5% of the card's height reserved for nothing.
