At 390 the same interval is 61px; at 320 the message wraps and it closes — so it is a desktop-only artifact of the equal-card matrix. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 1 ('A Card houses one bounded object/specimen … not … mere padding group') and law 3 ('may reserve collision space only on the axis where collision exists'). Visible in the shipped safari-desktop-light/admin-audit.png.
defects.mechanism: registered-but-unshipped composition row (PR-04) — the card neither hugs nor fills
defects.reproduction: node AAP-probe2.mjs → d1440.before.card {y:232, h:515.8}; AAP-probe1 → emptyMsg {y:503.2, h:35.6}.

defects.defect: No request lifecycle: the 300ms debounce is never cancelled on unmount, responses are unsequenced so an older reply can overwrite a newer one, and no control is ever disabled while a request is in flight.
defects.evidence: AdminAuditPanel.vue:110-119 — `let filterTimeout` with a 300ms setTimeout and no `onUnmounted` to clear it, so a route change within the debounce window still fires an admin fetch from a destroyed component. demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:60-62 assigns `entries.value = res.data` unconditionally with no AbortController and no sequence token. AdminAuditPanel.vue:30 Refresh has no `:disabled="audit.loading.value"`, and the filters stay live during load and during error — while the sibling does gate its action (AdminTagsPanel.vue:42 `:disabled="… || tagsApi.creating.value"`).
defects.mechanism: no owner for the async lifecycle — pending/abort/disabled state never modelled
defects.reproduction: Source-level: the three guards (onUnmounted, AbortController/sequence token, :disabled) are absent at the coordinates above.
defects.proposedCure: One async-task owner inside useAdminAudit carrying `pending`, aborting the previous request, and exposing the disabled state the toolbar binds to.

defects.defect: Under forced colors the action badge should lose its only differentiator: its entire visual identity is a background fill, with no border utility in its class list and no `.badge-atom` rule in glass-ui's stylesheet, while the declared tier-2 policy hands chrome to the UA palette.
defects.evidence: demo/styles/foundation.css:665-678 — two-tier WHCM policy; tier 1 keeps author colors only on a named roster of colour-display surfaces (canvas, spectrum-picker, gradient-rail, watercolor-swatch, …), tier 2 chrome adopts Canvas/CanvasText/ButtonFace. The audit row is chrome and is not on the roster. Structural fact measured: badge background rgb(237,230,222) light / rgb(47,40,35) dark, border-radius 9999px, and `grep -o "\.badge-atom[^{]*{[^}]*}" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css` returns nothing — badge-atom is a marker class with no CSS rule and the merged class list contains no `border` utility.
defects.mechanism: state expressed by fill alone, with no shape or border to survive colour substitution
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a HYPOTHESIS. WebKit reported matchMedia('(forced-colors: active)').matches === true while returning byte-identical computed colours to the normal arm (AAP-probe2.mjs fc1440 vs d1440), so the emulation matched the query without repainting and proves nothing about UA behaviour. Confirming needs a real Windows High Contrast session or a Chromium forced-colors run.
defects.proposedCure: Give the badge a border (which also survives print), or select it into the tier-1 roster in foundation.css.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/palettes/browser/dialog/FlagReportDialog.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]) — seat explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited. No receipt-axis defect.
result.strongestDefect: L-2 — `variant="outline"` / `variant="destructive"` are DEAD props. Glass 7's ButtonProps (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19) has no `variant`; the axis was split into emphasis × tone. Both land as inert fallthrough DOM attributes and both buttons fall back to identical defaults. Measured on the live render: Cancel and Report BOTH carry data-emphasis=secondary data-tone=neutral with byte-identical computed background oklab(0.721321 0.00495294 0.0108792 / 0.6) and color rgb(0,0,0) — the destructive moderation action is pixel-indistinguishable from its own escape hatch (screenshot corroborates on the app's production instance). vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit exits 0 with the file confirmed in the program, so the design-system API removal produced ZERO signal. The mechanism is L-1: demo/ui/button/index.ts re-exports the value without restating the contract, laundering the shadcn-era vocabulary past the gate. Blast radius is 51 sites across 22 files (DEFECT-LEDGER.md:22422).
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded negative proofs (checked clean, so their absence is evidence rather than omission): no feature→shell or component→boot edge; no @src/* or deep-src/ import; the component imports NOTHING from @mkbabb/value.js, so there is no deep-path false proof of the public API in this file; edict #8 (verbatimModuleSyntax) has nothing to violate — zero type-only imports; not a god module (101-line SFC, 5 lines of host wiring); no second implementation of this dialog anywhere (`grep -rn FlagReportDialog demo src test e2e` → one component, one barrel, one host, two e2e specs).

defects.defect: `variant="outline"` (:38) and `variant="destructive"` (:41) are dead props on Glass 7 Button; the destructive moderation action renders identical to Cancel
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 declares ButtonProps { emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class } — no `variant`. Live DOM (SFC mounted off the Vite module graph at localhost:9000): [{"text":"Cancel","attrs":["data-slot=button","data-emphasis=secondary","data-tone=neutral","variant=outline"],"bg":"oklab(0.721321 0.00495294 0.0108792 / 0.6)","color":"rgb(0, 0, 0)"},{"text":"Report","attrs":["data-slot=button","data-emphasis=secondary","data-tone=neutral","variant=destructive"],"bg":"oklab(0.721321 0.00495294 0.0108792 / 0.6)","color":"rgb(0, 0, 0)"}] — identical bg/color, variant present as a RAW attribute. Screenshot evidence/flagreport-probe.png shows two identical neutral glass capsules (captured on the app's own instance, not the probe mount). Gate blind: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0; `--listFiles | grep -c FlagReportDialog` → 1. Fleet scale: DEFECT-LEDGER.md:22422 — 51 `<Button variant=…>` sites in 22 files; `grep -o "outline|ghost" button-Bu9F4uU6.js` → 0 matches.
defects.mechanism: Type-erasing alias hop plus Vue attribute fallthrough. demo/ui/button/index.ts re-exports the value binding without restating the contract, so the shadcn-era `variant` vocabulary survives at call sites after the vendor deleted it; Vue lets unknown attributes fall through to the root element, so neither the template compiler nor vue-tsc can distinguish an intended prop from a set attribute. A design-system API removal therefore emits no type error, no runtime warning, no console message — only a silent semantic regression on the most dangerous control in the component.
defects.reproduction: Mount the SFC (import('http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/dialog/FlagReportDialog.vue')) with open:true, or open /#/browse → non-owned palette menu → Report. Read getComputedStyle on both footer buttons: backgrounds match exactly and both expose data-emphasis=secondary data-tone=neutral.
defects.proposedCure: variant="outline" → emphasis="secondary"; variant="destructive" → emphasis="primary" tone="destructive". Then execute L-1 so the class cannot recur: with demo/ui/ deleted and imports pointing at @mkbabb/glass-ui/button, vue-tsc types the props directly and all 51 sites become compile errors instead of silent visual defects.

defects.defect: demo/ui/* is a 19-barrel pure alias layer over glass-ui with zero implementation; the same Dialog concept is reached two ways inside one directory family
defects.evidence: `for d in demo/ui/*/; do cat "$d/index.ts"; done` → every barrel is a one-line re-export (demo/ui/button: `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`, demo/ui/dialog: 8 symbols, demo/ui/radio-group: 2 symbols). Zero local .vue files under demo/ui/. The alert barrel's own comment records its conversion from implementation to re-export at B.W2. Dual path: `grep -rn '"\.\./.*ui/dialog"' demo` → VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:111, MigratePalettesDialog.vue:52, FlagReportDialog.vue:63; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog" demo` → PalettesPane.vue:148, AdminUsersPanel.vue:197. Repo-wide: 29 barrel imports, 37 bare-root glass-ui imports, 17 distinct direct subpaths, 51 `../../../ui/*` hops.
defects.mechanism: A rename table is a legacy shim by definition — it exists so call sites written against the old vendor need not be migrated, which owner edict #2 forbids (no aliases, migration shims, dual paths). Because the barrel re-exports values without restating contracts, it is also the type-erasing hop that makes L-2 possible and invisible.
defects.reproduction: `cat demo/ui/button/index.ts` → one line, no implementation. Then the two greps above, verbatim.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely and rewrite the 29 call sites to published glass-ui subpaths (@mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog, /button, root for RadioGroup which glass-ui exports at dist/index.d.ts:17 with no dedicated subpath). Mechanical codemod that removes a directory rather than adding one (KISS-positive), converts L-2 into a compile error, and deletes 51 relative-path hops.

defects.defect: FLAG_REASONS has two homes — the API-owned enum is hand-copied into the component template and re-widened to `string` at every demo layer
defects.evidence: Authoritative home api/src/modules/palette/model.ts:25-26: `export const FLAG_REASONS = ["inappropriate", "spam", "copyright", "other"] as const; export type FlagReason = (typeof FLAG_REASONS)[number];` Enforced at the wire api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:70-73: `reason: z.enum(FLAG_REASONS), detail: z.string().max(500).optional()`. Hand-copy at FlagReportDialog.vue:79-84 — same four values, same order, zero type relationship. Widened twice: demo/palettes/types.ts:103-108 types Flag.reason as `string`; FlagReportDialog.vue:76 emits `submit: [reason: string, …]`; demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:153-156 keeps `reason: string` to fetch. The maxlength="500" at :33 is a third hand-copy of the same schema line.
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated: one concept, two homes, no link. Because both demo-side types are `string`, a typo in the template array — or a fifth reason added server-side — typechecks green and fails at runtime as a 400 from z.enum.
defects.reproduction: Change "copyright" to "copywrite" at FlagReportDialog.vue:82. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0. Selecting that radio then Report POSTs an invalid body; the API rejects 400; the user sees nothing (see L-6).
defects.proposedCure: Export FLAG_REASONS / FlagReason / FLAG_DETAIL_MAX from a demo-visible contract module derived from the API model; derive the radio list from it so the four labels are the only demo-side data (`const REASON_LABELS: Record<FlagReason, string>`), and type the emit `submit: [reason: FlagReason, detail?: string]`. Adding a server-side reason then fails the demo build until a label is supplied — the correct failure direction.

defects.defect: raw <textarea> hand-cut where glass-ui ships a Textarea primitive; the control has no accessible name at all
defects.evidence: Census: `grep -rn "<textarea" demo` → FlagReportDialog.vue:29 is the ONLY hit in the entire demo; `grep -rn "Textarea" demo` → no output (glass primitive used zero times). The primitive exists and is reachable: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/forms.d.ts exports `./components/textarea` alongside `./components/input`, and demo/ui/input/index.ts ALREADY consumes that exact subpath (`export { Input } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms";`, 4 consumers: CurrentPaletteEditor, AdminAuditPanel, AdminTagsPanel, SearchFilterBar). Live computed style on the rendered textarea: {"radius":"4px","bg":"rgb(251, 250, 248)","border":"rgb(198, 180, 159)","ariaLabel":null,"labelledby":null,"id":""} — no accessible name; only a placeholder, which AT does not treat as a name and which vanishes on first keystroke.
defects.mechanism: Edict #4 violated: field anatomy — ground, radius, border token, invalid state, focus ring, accessible name — is exactly what a design system owns once. Hand-cutting it re-derives six decisions per site and, as measured, silently drops one of them. The sibling primitive (Input) was adopted from the same subpath while this one was hand-rolled beside it.
defects.reproduction: Mount the dialog; `document.querySelector('[role=dialog] textarea').getAttribute('aria-label')` → null, `.id` → "", and none of the four <label for> elements target it (all four point at radios).
defects.proposedCure: `import { Textarea } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms"` and delete the class string; pair with glass-ui's LabeledField (published subpath ./labeled-field) so the "Additional details" name is structural rather than placeholder-only. The radius drift (L-8) and the missing name then disappear as consequences, not as separate fixes.

defects.defect: `submitting` is owned by the wrong module — the dialog holds a loading flag for a promise the parent owns, so the Loader2 spinner is unreachable code
defects.evidence: FlagReportDialog.vue:90-100 — no `await` inside the try: submitting=true; emit("submit", …); finally { submitting=false; reason=""; detail="" }. Vue invokes emit listeners synchronously and discards the promise returned by the parent's async onFlagSubmit (BrowsePane.vue:296-300). Measured across a real submit with four sampling phases: {"emitted":[["submit","spam",null]],"spinnerTimeline":[{"phase":"sync-after-click","spin":false,"dt":0.2},{"phase":"microtask","spin":false},{"phase":"raf","spin":false},{"phase":"+300ms","spin":false}]} — .animate-spin absent at every phase. glass-ui already owns the affordance: Button.vue.d.ts:16 `loading?: boolean` — "Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles."
defects.mechanism: State placed in the module that does not own the operation. The in-flight condition belongs to whoever holds the promise (BrowsePane). The component re-implemented, with a manual icon and manual :disabled, a primitive the design system ships — and the re-implementation does not work. Second-order: the same finally clears reason/detail BEFORE the parent's request resolves, so on failure the user is left with an emptied form and a Report button disabled by !reason at :43.
defects.reproduction: Mount, select Spam, click Report, poll `.animate-spin` at sync / microtask / requestAnimationFrame / +300 ms — false at all four (output pasted above).
defects.proposedCure: Delete `submitting`, the Loader2 import (:66), the try/finally and the `async`; make the emit contract awaitable (`submit: [reason: FlagReason, detail?: string]`). In BrowsePane hold a reportPending ref, bind `<Button :loading="reportPending">`, and clear the form only on success. Net −10 lines, one dead import gone, and the affordance actually works because glass-ui implements it.

defects.defect: the failure path has no owner — a failed moderation report closes the dialog exactly like a success, violating a precept the codebase has already ruled
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:119-131 — `try { return await flagPalette(...) } catch (e) { console.warn("Failed to flag palette:", e); return undefined; }`. BrowsePane.vue:296-300 never inspects the result: `await pm.flagged.report(...); flagDialogOpen.value = false;` — because report() swallows, the await never rejects, so the close always runs. The precept already exists in the SAME barrel: useDialogBrowseActions.ts:39-46 — "F2: host-supplied surface for a failed fork. … never a silent swallow on the pane path" — and is implemented at :71-75 via onForkError.
defects.mechanism: The error surface is a concept with no home: the lowest layer decided unilaterally to discard information the upper layer needs, so the host cannot observe failure even if it wanted to. The flag path is the identical shape to fork — a user-triggered remote mutation on the pane — and simply did not receive the ruled treatment.
defects.reproduction: Stop the API, or `page.route('**/flag', r => r.abort())`; open the dialog, select a reason, click Report. The dialog closes; the only trace is a console.warn; the palette is not flagged.
defects.proposedCure: Stop swallowing in report() — let it reject. Give onFlagSubmit the same onForkError-shaped feedback surface F2 already established, routing onto the palette card's showFeedback exactly as onSave / onDeleteOwned / onFork do, and close the dialog only on success. Applies an existing ruled pattern to the one path that missed it rather than inventing a mechanism.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json#paths and package.json#exports have drifted — three declared subpaths point at files that do not exist, two real exports are unmapped
defects.evidence: Programmatic diff: exports = ['./color','./css','./easing','./math','./quantize','./transform','./value']; tsconfig = ['.','./color','./easing','./math','./parsing','./quantize','./transform','./units']. PHANTOM (typecheck-only, no runtime export) = ['.', './parsing', './units']; UNTYPED (runtime export, no path) = ['./css', './value']. `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts` → 3× "No such file or directory". `ls src/subpaths/` → color.ts css.ts easing.ts math.ts quantize.ts transform.ts value.ts (no parsing.ts, no units.ts). package.json#exports has NO "." key at all, so the bare specifier is not importable by any real consumer, yet tsconfig maps it.
defects.mechanism: vite.config.ts:37-47 GENERATES its alias set from package.json#exports with an explicit comment ("GENERATED (not hand-rolled) so the alias set can never drift from the exports map"); tsconfig.demo.json#paths is hand-rolled and received no such treatment. The runtime map is derived, the type map is copied, and the copy rotted — one-way dangerous, because a stale path grants a green typecheck while proving nothing about the published surface.
defects.reproduction: LATENT, not live — labelled as such. Current usage is clean: `grep -rhn '@mkbabb/value.js[^"]*' demo -o | sort | uniq -c` yields only /color, /css, /math, /easing, /quantize, all genuine exports; the subject imports no value.js at all. The trap fires for the first file that writes `@mkbabb/value.js/units` or `/parsing`: green typecheck, broken build.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-rolled paths block and generate it from package.json#exports by the same mechanism vite.config.ts already uses — one source of truth for both maps. The three phantom entries cease to exist by construction and ./css / ./value gain the coverage they lack.

defects.defect: useDialogBrowseActions is homed under browser/dialog/ and re-exported from the dialog barrel, but its only consumer is BrowsePane — a pane, not a dialog
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "useDialogBrowseActions" demo` → BrowsePane.vue:199 `import { useDialogBrowseActions } from "./browser/dialog";`, BrowsePane.vue:261 (call site), browser/index.ts:41, browser/dialog/index.ts:9, and the definition at browser/dialog/composables/useDialogBrowseActions.ts:48. Its own docstring at :2 says "host-agnostic fork + revert + browse-filter wiring", and :48-56 confirms it takes pm plus an OPTIONAL modalStack precisely so it needs no dialog context. demo/palettes/useVersionHistory.ts:10 still cites the deleted original home `palette-browser/PaletteDialog/composables/…`, a path that no longer exists.
defects.mechanism: The module lattice encodes history rather than dependency. dialog/index.ts is documented as "palette-browser · dialog cluster — hardened public surface"; shipping a browse-filter composable through it makes the cluster's name a lie and forces a pane→dialog edge the graph does not require. It also widens the eager-chunk surface — DEFECT-LEDGER.md:13805 records App.vue:176 → ../palettes/browser/dialog pulling all four barrel members while only MigratePalettesDialog is used.
defects.reproduction: BrowsePane.vue:199 imports from ./browser/dialog; BrowsePane renders no PaletteDialog. The grep above shows no other consumer.
defects.proposedCure: Move the file to demo/palettes/useBrowseActions.ts — sibling of usePaletteActions.ts and useBrowsePalettes.ts, where pane-level composables already live — rename off the dead host, drop the re-export from dialog/index.ts, and fix the stale citation at useVersionHistory.ts:10. The dialog barrel then exports only dialogs.

defects.defect: demo/DESIGN.md:195 asserts --radius-input = 8 px; the token actually holds 0.25rem = 4 px, and the demo never defines it
defects.evidence: demo/DESIGN.md:195 — "`rounded-input` (= `--radius-input` = 8 px) — text inputs." Measured on document.documentElement: {"radiusInputVar":"0.25rem","radiusVar":"0.25rem","taRadius":"4px"} — 0.25rem = 4px, confirmed by the rendered textarea's computed border-radius. `grep -rn radius-input demo/styles/` returns nothing, so the demo has no independent input radius; it inherits glass-ui's --radius.
defects.mechanism: A doc transcribing a numeric token value, with no test binding the two, drifts the moment the producer changes its default. The bad number has already propagated: DEFECT-LEDGER.md:72804 reasons about this surface using the stale 8 px figure.
defects.reproduction: `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--radius-input')` → "0.25rem", against DESIGN.md:195's "8 px".
defects.proposedCure: DESIGN.md should name tokens, not transcribe their values — write `rounded-input` (= `--radius-input`) with no number, so there is nothing to drift. If 8 px was the intent, define `--radius-input: 0.5rem` in demo/styles/ and the doc becomes true again.

defects.defect: paletteSlug is a declared required prop the component never reads — the public surface overstates its coupling
defects.evidence: `grep -n "paletteSlug" demo/palettes/browser/dialog/FlagReportDialog.vue` → exactly 2 hits: :68 (the destructure) and :71 (the type declaration). Zero reads in template or script. The template uses only paletteName (:11); onSubmit (:90-100) emits reason/detail only. The host already holds and uses its own copy — BrowsePane.vue:298 `await pm.flagged.report(flagPalette.value.slug, …)` — while still passing it in at :171.
defects.mechanism: A prop is a contract term. An unread required prop obliges every future host to supply data that changes nothing, and misrepresents the component's dependency surface.
defects.reproduction: The grep above: 2 occurrences, both declarations, none a read.
defects.proposedCure: Delete paletteSlug from the props type and the destructure, and drop :palette-slug at BrowsePane.vue:171. Under the L-5 cure the emit is already the slug-free channel, so nothing regresses.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/browser/card/ShadowPalette.vue` (the Extract instrument-face ghost plate)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context Opus 5 seat), spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; not inherited, not undeclared
result.strongestDefect: C-1/C-2/C-3 are ONE mechanism and it is the component's entire reason to exist: the staggered pulse choreography is expressed as a per-element declared `animation-delay` computed from `count`, so the "one wave travels the plate" contract is destroyed by the exact interaction the plate is built for. Turning the live k slider (1..16) splits the plate into EIGHT animation time origins (measured `startTime` set at k=12: 646935, 699543, 699585, 699626, 699668, 699710, 699751, 699793), injects +1272/+638/+1292 ms phase discontinuities into a chain that admits only negative steps, teleports the phase of every already-running meta/swatch block by the delay delta (measured: one ArrowRight, 14 ms wall, `animationRestarted:false`, delay 700→820 ms, phase ran BACKWARD 434→330, opacity popped 0.805→0.883 in one frame), and — because maxDelay(count)=0.22*count+0.24 s overruns the 2 s `animate-pulse` period at count>=9, i.e. 8 of the slider's 16 positions — folds the wave back on itself (measured at k=12 within ONE time origin: `.shadow-seg` #1 phase 716 ms vs `.shadow-swatch` #3 phase 736 ms — the "last exposure pass" fires WITH the strip's leading edge). The gate cannot see any of it: O-9 reads `getComputedStyle().animationDelay`, the DECLARED value, which stays perfectly correct while the rendered animation is shattered.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded anyway, since the brief demands honest negatives: the following hazards were TESTED and found SOUND. PRM — `demo/styles/animations.css:184-192` really does collapse the pulse app-wide via `*{animation-duration:.01ms!important;animation-iteration-count:1!important}` and the inline delays do not conflict, so both the component claim and the O-9 PRM leg are real. Accessibility — the component's contribution to the visual REPORT is exactly ZERO: `/#/extract` `namelessButtons:3` + `smallTapTargets:6` in REPORT.json resolve entirely to neighbours (two 12x24 reka slider thumbs, three 22x22 PaletteSlugBar buttons, one 160x23 input); the plate is `aria-hidden`, has no focusable descendant, and its AT text is a real seated caption at ExtractWorkbench.vue:161-165. Leak classes — no defineModel, no rAF, no listeners/observers/timers, no WebGL, no async, no network, no parsing, no ValueUnit, no reka pointer capture: nothing to clean up and nothing left uncleaned. Idioms — reactive props destructure is correct 3.5; zero imports so verbatimModuleSyntax is vacuously satisfied; 115 lines, far under the 400-LoC cap. Route health — `/#/extract` shows overflowX 0, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0 in all four Safari matrices (REPORT.md:122,137,152,167). Probe artifact disclosed and NOT reported as a defect: my synthetic KeyboardEvent bubbled to an app-level arrow handler and drifted the route once; the C-2 measurement was re-run with propagation stopped at the slider root.)

defects.defect: The staggered pulse cascade shatters on every live-k change: `v-for="i in count" :key="i"` appends nodes whose CSS animations start at their own INSERTION time, while their declared delay `(i-1)*0.12s` is written as if all nodes shared the plate's mount origin. The 'LIVING cascading shimmer that travels the plate ... one wave' (ShadowPalette.vue:11-13) is destroyed by the exact interaction the component exists to serve.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/ShadowPalette.vue:52-57 (`v-for="i in count" :key="i"` + `:style="{animationDelay: ...}"`); count threaded live at demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:159 from useExtractSession.ts:44,171 with slider domain min=1 max=16 step=1 (ExtractControls.vue:27-30). MEASURED at k=12 via getAnimations(): distinctStartTimes = [646935, 699543, 699585, 699626, 699668, 699710, 699751, 699793] (EIGHT origins); chainPhases (segs→meta→swatches, ms in the 2000 ms period) = [716,596,476,356,236, 1508,1346,1185,1023,861,700,538, 1176,1056, 936,836,736,636,536, 1828,1686,1545,1403,1261,1120,978]; consecutive deltas = [-120,-120,-120,-120, +1272, -162,-161,-162,-162,-161,-162, +638, -120,-120, -100,-100,-100,-100, +1292, -142,-141,-142,-142,-141,-142]. Neighbour opacity seam measured at the same instant: seg#5 0.940 vs seg#6 0.757. Newly inserted cells honour the full positive delay from insertion — at k=12 the last swatch sits bright and static for 2.88 s.
defects.mechanism: time-origin-dependent choreography expressed as origin-independent geometry (declared animation-delay as if all nodes shared one start time)
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/extract (ghost is the true-empty branch, no image needed). Raise k from 5 to 12 on the 'Number of colors' slider (7x ArrowRight). Then evaluate: `const g=document.querySelector('[data-slot=\"shadow-palette\"]'); Array.from(g.querySelectorAll('.shadow-seg,.shadow-block-name,.shadow-block-count,.shadow-swatch')).map(el=>{const a=el.getAnimations()[0],ct=a.currentTime,d=a.effect.getComputedTiming().delay,dur=a.effect.getComputedTiming().duration; return {start:Math.round(a.startTime), phase:Math.round((((ct-d)%dur)+dur)%dur)};})`. Observe >1 distinct startTime and non-monotone phase chain.
defects.proposedCure: Give the `data-slot="shadow-palette"` root a `:key="count"` so a k change re-mounts the instrument face as ONE animation cohort — one attribute, kills C-1 and C-2 together, at a cost of <=19 trivial nodes per k tick (strictly cheaper than the 2+count forced opacity discontinuities it removes). Pair with the period-normalized negative-delay ladder of C-3.

defects.defect: Every k tick teleports the phase of the already-running meta and swatch blocks: their `animation-delay` is a function of `count`, so it is rewritten mid-flight on animations that are never restarted. Phase = (currentTime - delay) mod duration, so the delay mutation re-seats the phase instantaneously — an opacity pop on `2 + count` elements per tick, 15 pops across a full slider drag.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/ShadowPalette.vue:63 (`count*0.12+0.1`), :67 (`count*0.12+0.22`), :77 (`count*0.12+0.34+(i-1)*0.1`). MEASURED, one ArrowRight (k 5→6), two rAFs apart, on `.shadow-block-name`: before {startTime:21249, currentTime:1134, delayMs:700, phase:434, opacity:0.805} / after {startTime:21249, currentTime:1150, delayMs:820, phase:330, opacity:0.883}; wallElapsedMs:14, animationRestarted:false, opacityJump:+0.078, discontinuityMs:1882 (phase ran BACKWARD 120 ms in 14 ms of wall time). Identical startTime is the proof it is a live-animation discontinuity, not a re-mount.
defects.mechanism: mutating a timing input of a running CSS animation as if it were a static layout value
defects.reproduction: On http://localhost:9000/#/extract evaluate: read `.shadow-block-name`'s `getAnimations()[0]` startTime/currentTime/effect.getComputedTiming().delay and computed opacity; dispatch one ArrowRight keydown on the 'Number of colors' thumb (stop propagation at `[data-slot="slider"]` so the app-level arrow handler does not drift the route); wait two rAFs; re-read. startTime identical, delay +120 ms, phase shifted backward by exactly the delta, opacity discontinuous.
defects.proposedCure: Same `:key="count"` single-origin cure as C-1 — a re-mount restarts the whole cohort together instead of re-seating live phases — plus expressing the stagger as a NEGATIVE delay (a phase offset consumed at start), which is immune to being read as a pending wait.

defects.defect: The delay ladder is unbounded but the animation period is fixed at 2 s, so past count>=9 the delays wrap modulo the period and the stated 'strip → meta → swatches, one wave' ordering inverts: the last exposure pass fires with (or before) the strip's leading edge.
defects.evidence: Period: node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css:440 `--animate-pulse: pulse 2s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.6,1) infinite` (keyframe at :457). Ladder: maxDelay(count) = count*0.12 + 0.34 + (count-1)*0.1 = 0.22*count + 0.24 s (ShadowPalette.vue:77) → exceeds 2 s at count>=9, i.e. 8 of the slider's 16 positions (ExtractControls.vue:28-29 min=1 max=16). MEASURED at k=12, restricted to the ONE original time origin startTime=646935 so C-1 cannot be the cause: `.shadow-seg` #1 declared 0s → phase 716 ms; `.shadow-swatch` #3 declared 1.98s → phase 736 ms (20 ms apart — they pulse together); `.shadow-swatch` #5 declared 2.18s → phase 536 ms, which fires BEFORE `.shadow-seg` #4 (declared 0.36s → phase 356 ms is later in the cycle... measured ordering inverted relative to the declared cascade).
defects.mechanism: an unbounded delay ladder driven into a bounded (2 s) periodic animation — declared delays wrap modulo the period
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract, set k>=9 (ArrowRight from the default 5), then read declared `animationDelay` and measured phase for `.shadow-seg` and `.shadow-swatch` restricted to elements sharing one `startTime`. Declared delays exceed 2000 ms; measured phases interleave the strip and swatch groups.
defects.proposedCure: Emit the stagger as a period-normalized NEGATIVE delay: `animation-delay: calc(-1 * mod(var(--i) * var(--skeleton-wave-step), var(--skeleton-wave-period)))` (fold the modulo into the `--i` ladder where CSS `mod()` is unavailable). A negative delay starts the animation already advanced, so the cascade is a phase offset that can never overrun the period and never parks a cell bright-and-static.

defects.defect: The ink ladder below the strip was never certified against its ground: the E1-R2 remediation note in the file certifies `--skeleton-ink` at full strength (i.e. `.shadow-seg` only) and declares the 1.02:1 dark collapse 'dead', but the 60/40/30 % rungs sit at 1.237 / 1.144 / 1.116 : 1 at rest and 1.111 / 1.069 / 1.056 : 1 at the pulse trough. The swatch group — `count` elements, the largest visual mass on the plate — is effectively invisible. Same file, internal contradiction: the comment forbids element opacity for the ladder ('never element opacity — D6') while `animate-pulse` applies exactly that on top, MULTIPLYING each rung (0.30 → 0.15 alpha at the trough).
defects.evidence: ShadowPalette.vue:92-114 (the E1-R2 claim + the 60/40/30 % color-mix ladder); the D6 claim at :100-102. MEASURED live, canvas-composited over the plate's own `bg-well`, WCAG relative luminance: .shadow-seg alpha 1.00 → 1.427:1 rest / 1.193:1 trough; .shadow-block-name 0.60 → 1.237 / 1.111; .shadow-block-count 0.40 → 1.144 / 1.069; .shadow-swatch 0.30 → 1.116 / 1.056. Scheme-symmetric by construction (the ink is a fixed fraction of --foreground mixed into --well-bg; the dark read gave wellBg oklab(0.345295 0.0103877 0.0175526) and the same ratios). WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor is 3:1 (not binding — the plate is aria-hidden — but the component's OWN contract at utils.css:53 and ShadowPalette.vue:101 is 'reads as BLOCKS whether the plate is light or dark').
defects.mechanism: a certified base ink with uncertified derived rungs, then a blanket element-opacity animation multiplying them away
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/extract; for each of `.shadow-seg`, `.shadow-block-name`, `.shadow-block-count`, `.shadow-swatch` read `getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor`, resolve via a 1x1 canvas fillStyle, composite over `getComputedStyle(plate).backgroundColor` at alpha and at alpha*0.5 (the animate-pulse 50 % keyframe), and compute the WCAG contrast ratio against the plate ground.
defects.proposedCure: Extend the E1-R2 tone-step guarantee DOWN the ladder so every rung clears a stated floor against `--well-bg` (certify the rungs, not just the base ink), and replace Tailwind's blanket `animate-pulse` with a bounded opacity-floor token so the pulse is motion on top of the ink — as the comment already promises — instead of a multiplier that erases the ladder.

defects.defect: The component's only gate is vacuous over two of the plate's three wave stages. `assertPulsesLive` queries `.shadow-seg` alone; `.shadow-swatch` and `.shadow-block-*` are referenced NOWHERE outside the component itself. The live-k leg asserts element COUNT only and never re-checks phase — which is exactly why C-1/C-2/C-3 have shipped green since T.W6.5 (`0ad772f`).
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:81-102 (assertPulsesLive → `root.querySelectorAll('.shadow-seg')` only) and :148-159 (live-k leg → `toHaveCount(6)`/`toHaveCount(5)` only). `grep -rn "shadow-swatch\|shadow-block" --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' demo e2e test` → 6 hits, ALL inside ShadowPalette.vue (:62,:66,:75,:106,:109,:112); zero test references. No vitest component test exists (`find test/demo -type f` → the single file test/demo/palettes/api/admin-palettes.test.ts). The oracle reads `getComputedStyle().animationDelay` — the DECLARED value — which stays correct while the rendered animation is shattered.
defects.mechanism: gate asserts declared style on one of three element groups, never rendered animation state, never post-interaction
defects.reproduction: Named green-keeping mutations: (1) delete ShadowPalette.vue lines 59-80 entirely — the whole meta row and every swatch — O-9 still passes (ghost exists, aria-hidden, no role=status, caption visible, 5 segs, re-segments 5→6→5, delays i*0.12, PRM collapses); (2) set every non-seg animationDelay to '0s'; (3) set .shadow-block-name/-count/.shadow-swatch background to `transparent`; (4) replace the swatch delay expression with `Math.random()` seconds. All four keep the gate GREEN.
defects.proposedCure: Re-aim O-9 onto what it claims to protect: (a) cover `.shadow-block-*` and `.shadow-swatch`, not only `.shadow-seg`; (b) assert ONE shared `startTime` across the plate; (c) assert a monotone phase chain strip → meta → swatches; (d) re-run all three AFTER a k change, at a k in the folding range (>=9). Every mutation above then fails, as it should.

defects.defect: The instrument face shows a shape the instrument never produces. The plate's stated job is 'showing its output shape before any image exists', but its swatch placeholders are perfect circles while the real output swatch is a WatercolorDot organic silhouette.
defects.evidence: ShadowPalette.vue:19-22 (the 'output shape' claim) and :75 (`rounded-badge` circles). defects.defect: One wave, two implementations: the identical stagger arithmetic is duplicated verbatim across ShadowPalette.vue and PaletteCardSkeleton.vue — two components that morph into one another in the same seat — so any fix to C-1/C-2/C-3 applied to one silently diverges the other.
defects.evidence: Line-for-line duplication: strip ShadowPalette.vue:56 `((i-1)*0.12)` vs PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:50 `(i-1)*0.12`; meta name :63 vs :60 `count*0.12+0.1`; meta count :67 vs :66 `count*0.12+0.22`; swatches :77 vs :77 `count*0.12+0.34+(i-1)*0.1`. They occupy the same seat under `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:101-160). The sibling already expresses the ladder as CSS custom properties (`'--i': i-1`, `--skeleton-shimmer-delay`, PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:49-51) while ShadowPalette re-implements it as template string arithmetic. The house already performed exactly this lift for the INK — demo/styles/utils.css:42 names both components as the two consumers of the one `.skeleton-ink-register` recipe — and never performed it for the WAVE.
defects.mechanism: shared choreography copy-pasted instead of lifted to the one recipe root, in violation of the same rule the ink already obeys
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a static duplication finding, confirmed by the paired line citations above.
defects.proposedCure: Lift the wave to demo/styles/utils.css beside `.skeleton-ink-register` as a `--i`-driven stagger recipe (both plates already have, or trivially gain, `--i`). Template arithmetic disappears from both files; the duplication collapses; C-8's geometry disagreement gets one place to be fixed; and the C-3 period normalization lands once for both consumers.

defects.mechanism: three independent expressions of one strip geometry

defects.defect: `count` is unvalidated and the component is exported from the public barrel: a non-integer, negative or NaN count renders a silently EMPTY, still, aria-hidden plate with only a dev-mode console warning — no error, no fallback, no visible failure.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface) · subject `demo/palettes/browser/card/ShadowPalette.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, matching the explicit Opus 5 declaration this seat was spawned with. Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the design-system bypass erases the component under `forced-colors: active`. ShadowPalette hand-rolls its skeleton blocks (`animate-pulse` + four scoped `background` rules) instead of rendering glass-ui's `Skeleton`, and thereby drops the three environment carve-outs the producer ships with that primitive. Measured live on http://localhost:9000/#/extract with `page.emulateMedia({forcedColors:'active'})`: plate `rgb(255,255,255)` and `.shadow-seg` `rgb(255,255,255)` — contrast 1.00:1, the 40px live-k strip the component calls its own primary readout is gone. glass-ui ships the exact cure (`@media (forced-colors:active){.skeleton{opacity:.18;background:canvastext}}`), which the sibling ghost in the SAME `<Transition>` slot inherits. ShadowPalette is the only `animate-pulse` consumer in the entire demo (1 of 4 `skeleton-ink-register` consumers bypasses the primitive; the other 3 do not).
result.negativeProof: Two limbs of this axis came back clean and are recorded as positive evidence rather than silence. (1) LIBRARY PUBLIC-SURFACE REACH: `ShadowPalette.vue`'s entire `<script setup>` (`:84-90`) contains ZERO import statements, so it cannot false-proof the value.js public API — no deep `src/` path, no bare-root reach, nothing to trace. The repo-wide posture on that limb is structurally sound: `vite.config.ts:37-50` machine-derives the seven self-aliases from `package.json#exports` so they cannot drift, `vite.config.ts:63-66` records T.W1 retiring every `@src/*` demo import, and `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/` returns 0 bare-root hits while the only five subpaths the demo speaks (`/color` 25, `/css` 10, `/math` 6, `/easing` 5, `/quantize` 4) are all real keys in the exports map — verified resolvable from Node (`import('@mkbabb/value.js/css')` → OK, 19 exports). (2) `verbatimModuleSyntax`: vacuously satisfied, zero imports. (3) The automated visual corpus is genuinely green on this route: `audit/visual/REPORT.md:122,137,152,167` shows `/#/extract` at pageErrors 0, consoleErrors 0, horizontalOverflow 0, blankOrNearBlank 0 across all four Safari matrices — the L-1 defect is invisible to it precisely because `shots/forced-colors-desktop/` contains no extract capture.

The component hand-rolls its skeleton blocks instead of rendering glass-ui's `Skeleton`, dropping all three environment carve-outs the producer ships (forced-colors, reduced-transparency, reduced-motion-as-opt-in).

defects.defect: The swatch silhouette has two owners and the ghost's owner disagrees with the truth, falsifying the component's own stated contract ('the instrument showing its output shape').
defects.evidence: TRUTH: a palette swatch is glass-ui's `WatercolorDot` (demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-20,29-34, rendered per colour by PaletteCardSwatches.vue:26-33, owned by PaletteCard.vue:148), whose silhouette is computed by node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/useWatercolorBlob.d.ts — 'Border-radius range [lo, hi] as percentages (default [20, 80])', 'the seeded border-radius silhouette is set ONCE (the dot's identity)'. defects.mechanism: duplicate ownership of one concept ('what a palette swatch looks like'): a primitive computes it, a consumer re-declares a competing answer inline, and the two compute different functions so drift is structural not accidental
defects.reproduction: On http://localhost:9000/#/extract: `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.shadow-swatch')).borderRadius` → '9999px'; `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-variant="ghost"]')).borderRadius` → the seeded percentage octuple above.

One home, one silhouette function; the ghost trio and the ghost plate finally speak one shape language.

defects.defect: The 'tone-stepped, staggered skeleton block' concept has no home in the design system, so it has two homes in the demo and one of them is dead. glass-ui 7.0.0's `Skeleton` publishes ONE prop, hardcodes its fill, ships one animation register and no stagger seam — so both consumers invented, in opposite directions.
defects.evidence: PRODUCER SURFACE, entire: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/skeleton/Skeleton.vue.d.ts → `type __VLS_Props = { class?: HTMLAttributes["class"]; };`. RECIPE (glass-ui.css): `background: var(--muted)` hardcoded, `border-radius: var(--radius-input)` baked, one `skeleton-scan` sheen whose only seam is `--duration-shimmer`. `grep -o skeleton node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/components.css | wc -l` → 0 (the recipe exists only in the compiled scoped sheet keyed [data-v-cd03d0b0] — not an overridable house recipe). INVENTION A (dead): PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:41-45,58-66,71-77 passes `surface="glass"`, `variant="shimmer"/"breath"` and writes `--skeleton-glass-bg`, `--skeleton-shimmer-delay`, `--skeleton-shimmer-tint`, `--pulse-aura-opacity-max` — none exist. INVENTION B (works, at the cost of L-1): ShadowPalette.vue:55,103-114. DEMO-SIDE EVIDENCE OF THE MISSING SEAM: demo/styles/utils.css:56-60 mints three custom properties for a producer contract that does not exist; its own docblock (:37-43) admits the future tense — 'the sheen joins the same ink family once glass-ui's ::after reads it'.
defects.mechanism: missing producer surface: a variant that belongs to the design system has no home there, so every consumer that needs it forks — edict 4 violated in both directions at once
defects.reproduction: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/skeleton/Skeleton.vue.d.ts` (one prop) and the extracted `.skeleton[data-v-cd03d0b0]` rule block from glass-ui.css (hardcoded `var(--muted)`, single scan register, no delay seam). Then `grep -n 'surface=\|variant=' demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardSkeleton.vue` — four props that do not exist.
defects.proposedCure: A glass-ui ask, relayed per the standing BH/BI edict — three seams, each one line from the producer's existing recipe: `--skeleton-bg` (tone; `background: var(--skeleton-bg, var(--muted))`), `--skeleton-delay` (stagger; `animation-delay` on the element and the ::after), and a `register` prop (`scan` | `breath` | `none`). With those, `.skeleton-ink-register` collapses to one property, both demo ghosts become `<Skeleton>` compositions, and the three carve-outs are inherited rather than re-invented.

defects.defect: The four scoped classes squat Tailwind v4's `shadow-*` generated-utility namespace — a producer-owned namespace the same element consumes on the same line.
defects.evidence: ShadowPalette.vue:43 mixes the author class `shadow-palette` and the generated utility `shadow-cartoon-sm` in one class list; :103-114 defines `.shadow-seg`, `.shadow-block-name`, `.shadow-block-count`, `.shadow-swatch`. In Tailwind v4 a `--shadow-<name>` theme entry generates `.shadow-<name>{box-shadow:…}`; glass-ui mints exactly such tokens (`--shadow-cartoon-sm/md/lg`, consumed at demo/styles/utils.css:106,136,144 and documented at demo/DESIGN.md:147,188).
defects.mechanism: namespace squat: author classes sharing a prefix with a design-system-owned generated-utility namespace; a future producer token silently emits a competing rule for the identical selector with no tool relating them
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS about a future `--shadow-seg`-shaped token. The present facts are measured: the element mixes author classes and generated utilities from one prefix namespace (:43), and `--shadow-*` is a live producer-owned Tailwind theme namespace.
defects.proposedCure: Rename out of the producer's namespace (`ghost-seg`, `ghost-swatch`, `ghost-block-name`, `ghost-block-count`) — or, under the L-5 cure, delete them entirely as the blocks become `<Skeleton>` instances carrying `--skeleton-bg`.

defects.mechanism: bundle utility addressed at a different consumer: the component adopts a three-property block written for the <Skeleton> route while taking the hand-rolled route

defects.defect: `count` has no domain, and the domain it implicitly has is restated in four unrelated places. The prop type admits values the producer can never emit and the component has no guard.

Defaults, four times: useExtractSession.ts:44 `const colorCount = ref(5)`; useExtractSession.ts:181 `colorCount.value = 5` (reset); ShadowPalette.vue:85 `const { count = 5 }`; PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:87 `const { count = 5, … }`. Upper end measured by the OM-15 audit (§3.2): k=16 → 3-row wrap, ≈276px vs ≈148px at k=5.
defects.mechanism: no single home for a value domain: range, default and meaning each re-declared by an unrelated file; the type is wider than the producer's image
defects.reproduction: NONE for the degenerate render — HYPOTHESIS that `count <= 0`/NaN renders zero children and silently degenerates the plate to a 40px empty band plus two meta blocks. The four-way default duplication, the 1..16 range and the unguarded `count?: number` type are the file:line facts above.
defects.proposedCure: One home in the session that owns k: `export const K_RANGE = { min: 1, max: 16, default: 5 } as const` in useExtractSession.ts, clamped at the single mutation point (:171). ExtractControls binds K_RANGE; the ghost takes `count: number` as a REQUIRED prop (there is no sensible ghost without a k) and both `= 5` defaults die.

defects.reproduction: evidence/probe-console.js → `probeD3()`. Open Report on palette A, choose Copyright violation, type a note, press Cancel; open Report on palette B — the note about A is still present, the reason is still selected, Report is armed, one Enter files it.

defects.defect: A raw `<textarea>` with ten utility classes where glass-ui 7 ships a `Textarea` primitive — producing a 4px-radius opaque plate in a 16px-radius glass overlay, and a near-black hole in dark mode.
defects.evidence: FlagReportDialog.vue:29-34. Producer primitive exists: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/forms.d.ts:2 → components/textarea, with `size,rows,resize,invalid,maxlength,minlength,required,readonly,disabled,name`. defects.reproduction: evidence/probe-console.js → `probeGeometry()`; see evidence/dark-focus-first-radio.png and evidence/desktop-light-checked-report-enabled.png.

defects.defect: The four 44px radio hit targets overlap each other by 13.05px; the bottom band of every option belongs to the option below it.
defects.evidence: Measured: `seatH 44`, `pitch 30.95`, `faceDiameter 18`. `overlaps: [{pair:[reason-inappropriate,reason-spam],overlapPx:13.05,probePoint:[530,376],hitId:"reason-spam"}, {…,hitId:"reason-copyright"}, {…,hitId:"reason-other"}]` — `document.elementFromPoint` at each overlap midpoint returns the LOWER radio. Cause: producer 44px coarse-pointer floor vs consumer `class="flex flex-col gap-2"` (FlagReportDialog.vue:16), an 8px gap on an 18px glyph.
defects.mechanism: M-3 / PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 7 verbatim: "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities." The component sized the gap from the glyph and let the invisible seat spill. This is a measured instance of PR-12.

defects.proposedCure: The row, not the gap, is the unit: each option becomes one seat whose block size is the target floor with the glyph centred inside; `gap` goes to 0 and the rhythm comes from the seat. `LabeledField` + `RadioGroup` composition supplies this.

defects.defect: The radio group has no accessible name; the question exists only as the dialog's subtitle.

defects.reproduction: evidence/probe-console.js → `probeGeometry()` field `radiogroupName`.

defects.defect: Proximity is inverted: the question sits 24px from its own options while the options sit 12px from an unrelated optional field, so Gestalt groups [radios + textarea] and orphans the question.

defects.defect: The detail field truncates silently with no counter and no resize, and its fixed 80px height is not a multiple of the line box — so a fourth line is permanently sliced through its x-height.

defects.defect: Mobile is a different, worse design that was never drawn: the header alignment axis flips, the action ordinal flips (Report above Cancel), and the housing goes full-bleed while keeping a 16px radius.

defects.proposedCure: One composition for both breakpoints: pick the mobile housing deliberately (inset card or bottom sheet — the producer supports both via `DialogContent placement`), keep one text alignment, and fix the action order so the destructive commit never changes ordinal position across breakpoints.

defects.defect: Per-instance overrides of roots the author knew should own the decision, plus two sibling dialogs in one folder running two different type laws — and help text rendered smaller than the controls it introduces.

defects.defect: There is no failure state and no state that survives failure; an API rejection closes the dialog exactly like a success, having already destroyed the user's input.
defects.evidence: The component's entire state vocabulary is `reason`, `detail`, `submitting` (FlagReportDialog.vue:86-88). No `error`, no `invalid`, no retry, no `aria-invalid`, no error region. Both `RadioGroup` (RadioGroup.vue.d.ts:13) and the producer `Textarea` (textarea/types.d.ts:10) expose `invalid`; neither is used. BrowsePane.vue:297-299 awaits and closes unconditionally.

defects.reproduction: NONE — this is an absence, established by exhaustive read of the 101-line file plus the producer prop surfaces. Not a hypothesis: the absence is complete and verifiable by inspection.
defects.proposedCure: One committed/failed/pending model owned by the dialog, expressed through the producer's `invalid` + `errorLive` seams, with the user's input preserved across a failure.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (FlagReportDialog.vue, area palettes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared by the spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the form's state is not bound to the palette it edits. `reason`/`detail` are reset ONLY inside onSubmit's `finally` (FlagReportDialog.vue:97-98); nothing resets on close, and BrowsePane never clears `flagPalette` so the instance never unmounts. Measured (probe P3): select "Copyright violation" + type "LEAKED DETAIL TEXT" on palette A → Cancel → open Report on palette B → the dialog re-opens with `checked:["reason-copyright"]`, `textarea:"LEAKED DETAIL TEXT"`, `reportDisabled:false`. One stray click writes an immutable, unique-indexed moderation record (api/src/modules/palette/service/flags.ts:38-47 — the reporter can never correct it, only 409) against the WRONG palette, carrying free text written about a different one. Tied for weight with C-2 (a server-legal 100-char palette name blows the dialog's own layout apart: title off-screen, both button labels off-screen) and C-3 (all four API rejections render as success).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but one candidate finding was FALSIFIED and is reported as a negative so no seat re-spends it: under headless Chromium+SwiftShader the dialog's enter transition measured `filter:blur(6px)`, `opacity:0`, three CSSTransitions at `playState:"running", currentTime:0` at t=100/400/1000ms (screenshots show an illegible smear) — but the identical trace re-run under WebKit gives `currentTime:115` at t≈100 and fully settled (`blur(0px)`, `opacity:1`) by t≈400. It is a headless frame-starvation artifact, NOT a product defect. Methodological warning: Chromium+SwiftShader captures of any `glass-reveal` overlay in this repo can be transparent/blurred; the visual audit's real-Safari choice is what makes its overlay captures trustworthy. Other proven negatives: Escape + outside-click dismissal work (data-state trace: closed at t=0/200/400, unmounted by t=600); `<label for>` → radio activation works (label click yields `{"id":"reason-copyright","checked":"true"}`) and radios carry real aria-labels at 43.8x39.1px; the focus trap cycles strictly inside the dialog; `maxlength="500"` matches the server's `z.string().max(500)` exactly (typed 600 → typedLen=500, sentDetailLen=500) and whitespace-only detail is correctly dropped (`body={"reason":"other"}`); POSTS=1 under a 2.5s in-flight window; the component registers NO lifecycle hook, listener, observer, timer or rAF — immune to the PRM-RAF class, with no WebGL, no parsing, no ValueUnit contact; no page-level horizontal overflow (docScrollW 390 === innerW 390); `verbatimModuleSyntax` satisfied (all 8 imports are value imports); Vue 3.5 idiom satisfied (reactive props destructure, no defineModel so no stale-read hazard); edicts 1 and 6 satisfied.

defects.defect: Form state is not bound to the palette it edits: a cancelled report re-arms on the NEXT palette, pre-selected and pre-filled with the previous palette's free text, with the Report button already enabled.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/dialog/FlagReportDialog.vue:86-87,97-98 (reset lives only in onSubmit's finally); demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:167-174,288-294 (v-if="flagPalette", never cleared). Probe P3 output: `=== REOPEN STATE === {"title":"Report Palette Why are you reporting \"Other Palette\"? ...","checked":["reason-copyright"],"textarea":"LEAKED DETAIL TEXT","reportDisabled":false}`
defects.mechanism: M2 identity-unbound state — the child instance outlives the palette it edits; state lifetime is tied to nothing.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/browse with two remote palettes seeded: open Palette menu on "Shady Spam" → Report → select "Copyright violation" → type "LEAKED DETAIL TEXT" → click Cancel → open Palette menu on "Other Palette" → Report. Dialog shows copyright still checked, the leaked text still present, Report enabled. Spec: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/FlagReportDialog/evidence/challenge-C/flag-probe.spec.ts:184
defects.proposedCure: Bind lifetime to identity, two lines, no new abstraction: `:key="flagPalette.slug"` on <FlagReportDialog> in BrowsePane.vue:167 so the instance IS the palette, plus `watch(() => open, v => { if (!v) { reason.value=''; detail.value=''; } })` inside the component — and delete the reset from `finally`, where it never belonged (it is a close concern, not a submit concern).

defects.defect: Unbounded `paletteName` interpolation destroys the dialog's own layout at the API's legal 100-character maximum: the title is pushed entirely off-screen and both footer buttons render as unlabelled capsules.
defects.evidence: FlagReportDialog.vue:10-12 interpolates with no clamp; api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:25 `paletteNameSchema = z.string().trim().min(1).max(100)`. Probe P12 at 390x844 with name="A".repeat(100): `"dialog":{"w":390}` but `"desc":{"w":998.4,"scrollW":998,"clientW":998,"overflowWrap":"normal","wordBreak":"normal"}` — 2.56x the viewport. Screenshot: evidence/challenge-C/flag-longname100-mobile.png (no title, no button labels).
defects.mechanism: M6 unbounded interpolation — untrusted remote display text printed with no clamp inside a fixed-width overlay; the centred flex header then centres the <h2> inside the 998px box, putting it off-screen.
defects.reproduction: Seed a remote palette whose `name` is 100 unbroken characters (server-valid), open its Palette menu → Report at any viewport. Desktop is not spared: sm:max-w-md caps the dialog at 448px and 998 > 448. Spec: evidence/challenge-C/flag-probe7.spec.ts
defects.proposedCure: Clamp at the point of use — `class="break-words line-clamp-2"` on the DialogDescription; or, since four surfaces print remote palette names, a `truncateName()` in the already-existing demo/palettes/utils.ts (no new shared/ dir — edict 3). Note the repo's horizontalOverflow oracle cannot see this (documentElement.scrollWidth stays 390): the overflow is inside a clipped overlay the route-capture never opens.

defects.defect: Every API failure renders as success. 401 / 404 / 409 / 5xx / offline all close the dialog with no alert, no live region, no on-page text — only a console.warn.
defects.evidence: FlagReportDialog.vue:76 `submit: [reason, detail]` returns void; BrowsePane.vue:296-300 drops the async handler's promise and closes unconditionally; demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:120-131 catches everything and returns undefined. Probe P4 (live 409): `=== AFTER 409 === {"dialogPresent":false,"anyAlert":0,"bodyHasError":false,"activeElement":"BODY"}` with only `warning: Failed to flag palette: ApiProblem: Conflict`. Probe P5 (live 401): `sawPost=true {"dialogPresent":false,"bodyHasError":false}`. Server rejections: api/src/modules/palette/routes/flags.ts:17 (401), service/flags.ts:31 (404), :44-46 (409 Already flagged), :33 (400).
defects.mechanism: M1 no acknowledgement channel — the emit contract has no completion path, so the component cannot know, show, or survive an outcome; the port then swallows the error below it.
defects.reproduction: Route **/palettes/<slug>/flag to 409 (or 401), open Report, pick a reason, click Report. Dialog closes exactly as on success. Reachable without any mock: report a palette, then report it again — the Report menu item survives a successful report (probe P6: `REPORT MENUITEM COUNT AFTER SUCCESSFUL REPORT === 1`) and the second attempt 409s silently. Spec: evidence/challenge-C/flag-probe.spec.ts:215,254
defects.proposedCure: The house already built the rail and wrote the precept. useDialogBrowseActions.ts:69 states `// F2: a user-triggered remote mutation must surface its failure.` — the flag path is the one that never got wired. Three moves: (1) useAdminFlagged.report rethrows instead of swallowing; (2) BrowsePane.onFlagSubmit try/catches, closes ONLY on success, and calls `cardRefs[slug]?.showFeedback(message,'error')` — the identical shape onSave/onDeleteOwned/onSetVisibility/onForkError already use; (3) the dialog stops closing itself blind (see C-4).

defects.defect: `submitting` and the Loader2 spinner are unreachable dead code — provably never observable — so a 2.5s in-flight report shows the user nothing but the form erasing itself.
defects.evidence: FlagReportDialog.vue:90-100 — `async function onSubmit()` sets submitting=true, calls a SYNCHRONOUS emit, and clears it in `finally`; there is no await, so no reactive flush observes true. Probe P2 sampled the DOM every 100ms across a 2500ms held POST: `spinner:false` at ALL 24 samples; `liveRegions:0` throughout; at t=600 `checkedRadios` 1→0 and `textareaValue` "some detail text"→"" while the dialog stays open and the request is still in flight; `POSTS=1`.
defects.mechanism: M1 no acknowledgement channel — the shape of an async submit with none of the substance (C-11: `async`/`try`/`finally` around a synchronous emit). The button-disable at t=600 is accidental, coming from `!reason` after the reset, not from `submitting`.
defects.reproduction: Route **/palettes/shady-spam/flag with a 2500ms delay, open Report, pick Spam, type detail, click Report; poll the dialog for `.animate-spin` and for the radio/textarea values. Spec: evidence/challenge-C/flag-probe.spec.ts:127
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui 7's Button already ships the primitive this hand-rolls — `loading?: boolean` ("Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles", dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts). Delete Loader2, the @lucide/vue import and the animate-spin classes; bind `:loading="submitting"`. Then make `submitting` real by giving the emit a completion channel (C-3) — cleanest: a colocated `useFlagReport(slug)` in the already-existing dialog/composables/ that the dialog awaits.

defects.defect: `variant="destructive"` is not a glass-ui 7 prop: the destructive Report button renders pixel-identical to Cancel and leaks a stray `variant` attribute into the DOM.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/palettes/browser/dialog/MigratePalettesDialog.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — model id claude-opus-5[1m]. Explicitly declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — useSlugMigration.ts:55/69/76 call setActiveTab("saved"), but "saved" is not a member of ViewId (demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:35-41). The compiler cannot see it because useSlugMigration widens the brand away at its own boundary (`activeTab: Ref<string>`, `setActiveTab?: (tab: string) => void`) and usePalettePorts.ts:88 launders the widened value back with `depsSwitchView(tab as ViewId)`. vue-router 5 throws on the unknown route name. Live-reproduced on the dev server with a full stack trace ending at useSlugMigration.ts:36 (dev-transformed) = source line 55; the throw is unhandled because SlugEditLayer.vue:54 calls the async onSlugSwitch without await, so its own try/catch cannot observe the rejection. This is precisely the library-structure defect this seat exists to find: a type boundary that erases a branded union, plus a cast on the far side that re-admits an invalid literal — producing a live page error on the primary slug-switch path that gates this dialog.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the overall verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as tested-and-refuted hypotheses so absences count as evidence: (1) Deep-import / false-public-API axis is CLEAN — `grep -rn 'from "@src|from "../../src/|from "../../../src/' demo/` returns 0, and every demo value.js specifier is a real key in package.json#exports (`./color` x25, `./css` x10, `./easing` x5, `./math` x6, `./quantize` x4); this component imports nothing from @mkbabb/value.js at all, so its published-surface conformance is vacuous rather than violated. (2) Duplicate glass-ui component identity REFUTED — node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js:12 and dist/dialog.js:1 both import the same chunk ./dialog-TNRDkcE4.js, so the root-barrel vs subpath dual path yields one module instance and one reka-ui context. (3) CSS side-effect retention REFUTED — a static-closure walk of the published dist finds 0 .css imports reachable from either glass-ui.js or dialog.js; with sideEffects:["*.css"] rollup tree-shakes the root barrel, so L-4's cost is dev-time (measured +39 modules / +712,892 bytes) plus the standing-edict violation, not a prod-bundle regression. (4) eslint on the subject file is clean (0 findings). (5) The named historical suspects (ActionBarLayer/useLayerTransition, palettes/export.ts vs usePaletteExport.ts vs export/serializers, the three useDark stores) do not touch this component's import graph. (6) The "Migrate = back-compat shim" premise is REFUTED: this is a legitimate one-shot user-facing data-disposition prompt at an identity boundary (slug switch / slug regenerate), not a schema or version shim; it stays, though the name is a misnomer.

defects.defect: setActiveTab("saved") throws at runtime: "saved" is not a ViewId, and the branded union is erased to `string` at the useSlugMigration boundary then laundered back with `as ViewId`.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:55,69,76 call setActiveTab("saved"). demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:35-41 declares ViewId = "picker"|"palettes"|"browse"|"extract"|"atmosphere"|"blob"|...; `grep -n '"saved"|saved:' demo/shell/viewSchema.ts` → no output. The erasure: useSlugMigration.ts:8-17 `activeTab: Ref<string>` + `setActiveTab?: ((tab: string) => void)`. The launder: usePalettePorts.ts:87-88 `activeTab: currentView as Ref<string>, setActiveTab: (tab: string) => depsSwitchView(tab as ViewId)`. LIVE STACK: `Error: No match for {"name":"saved","query":{},"params":{}} at createRouterError (vue-router.js:90:16) at switchView (demo/shell/useViewManager.ts:46:10) at setActiveTab (demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:50:26) at setActiveTab (demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:9:11) at Object.onSlugSwitch (demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:36:4) at onSlugSubmit (demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:57:8)`. Dev-transformed line 36 maps to source line 55, verified by `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/.../demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts" | sed -n '33,40p'` → `if (isAdmin) { deps.clearUserSlug(); deps.adminLogin(value); setActiveTab("saved"); return; }`. The rejection is unhandled because SlugEditLayer.vue:54 calls `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` with NO await inside its try (catch at :55-63).
defects.mechanism: Type-erasing composable boundary + rescuing cast on the far side. viewSchema.ts:4 documents itself as "the single source of truth for ViewId" that collapsed "the 4-copy ViewId enumeration"; this edge re-opens the hole. Unique semantic ownership broken at the exact seam the schema was built to seal.
defects.reproduction: Dev server http://localhost:9000. (1) localStorage.setItem("color-palettes", JSON.stringify({palettes:[<2 entries>]})); reload. (2) const inp=document.querySelector('input[placeholder="enter slug or token..."]'); Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype,'value').set.call(inp,'audit-probe-slug'); inp.dispatchEvent(new Event('input',{bubbles:true})); inp.closest('form').dispatchEvent(new Event('submit',{bubbles:true,cancelable:true})). The 3-segment slug fails looksLikeSlug (/^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+$/) → isAdmin branch → setActiveTab("saved") → the stack above appears in the console.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the widening. useSlugMigration takes `setActiveTab: (id: ViewId) => void`, importing ViewId from demo/shell/viewSchema.ts (the shell already owns it; palettes already depends on the shell). Delete the `as ViewId` at usePalettePorts.ts:88. All three "saved" sites then become compile errors and the author must name the real destination ("palettes"). One type, one home, one direction — no cast anywhere on the path.

defects.defect: PaletteSlugBar.vue is a dead 243-line fork of the live SlugEditLayer.vue; the error surface this whole flow routes to is never mounted, and the documented S.W2 typed-ApiProblem repair landed in the unmounted twin while the bug it fixed is still running in the live copy.

All four remaining references are barrels/type-imports: demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:44, demo/palettes/browser/slug/index.ts:3, demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:6 and :30. Live surface is demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue (119 lines), mounted at demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:149. Byte-identical fork: looksLikeSlug regex /^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+$/ at PaletteSlugBar.vue:184-186 AND SlugEditLayer.vue:25-27; normalizeTokenInput at :188 and :29-37; onSlugSwitch/onSlugSubmit at :198-224 and :39-66. useSlugMigration.ts:79-82 comment states the S.W2 W2-6 fix: "branch on the typed ApiProblem.status, not .message substrings — the server titles ... never contain '409'/'404'/'429', so those branches matched nothing". That exact broken idiom is LIVE at SlugEditLayer.vue:59-61: `if (msg.includes("409")) ... else if (msg.includes("404"))`. useSlugMigration.ts:84-87 routes errors via `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)` where slugBarRef (line 30) points at the unmounted PaletteSlugBar → permanently null → optional-chain silently no-ops.
defects.mechanism: Component replacement without retiring the predecessor. A second implementation of the same concept stayed alive behind a barrel; the subsequent repair was applied to the dead copy because the barrel made it look load-bearing. Three homes for "slug-switch failure feedback", zero working ones.
defects.reproduction: Static: `grep -rn "<PaletteSlugBar" demo/ e2e/ test/` → 0 matches while demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:44 still exports it. Dynamic: with the L-3 probe, a 404 login failure produces no inline error anywhere in the DOM — slugBarRef.value is null so useSlugMigration.ts:84-87 no-ops, and SlugEditLayer's own catch never runs (L-1's missing await).

Then delete slugBarRef from useSlugMigration and have the composable surface a plain `slugError: Ref<string>` that SlugEditLayer binds — data down, no component-instance handle crossing a layer boundary. defects.defect: Every failure of a dialog response is masked by a console.warn; the dialog closes before the action runs, so the user is shown nothing and has no path to retry.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:106-116: `try { await action(choice); } catch (e: any) { console.warn("Migration action failed:", e?.message); }`. MigratePalettesDialog.vue:68-71 sets `open.value = false` BEFORE `emit("respond", choice)`, so the surface is already unmounted when the action rejects. LIVE MEASUREMENT after clicking "Just switch" with console instrumented: {"logs":[["warn","Migration action failed: User not found"]],"dialogStillOpen":false,"route":"#/palettes","savedCount":2}. The login 404'd; the dialog vanished; zero user-visible feedback; the user silently remains on the previous identity.
defects.mechanism: Ownership gap. The dialog owns the DECISION, the composable owns the ACTION, and nobody owns the OUTCOME. The no-masking-fallbacks edict is violated at the seam between the two homes.
defects.reproduction: Dev server http://localhost:9000 with 2 seeded local palettes. Submit the 4-segment slug 'alpha-beta-gamma-delta' via the dock slug form (looksLikeSlug true → switch path → dialog opens with 3 buttons). Instrument console.warn, then click the button labelled "Just switch". Observe the single warn line and the closed dialog with no other UI change.
defects.proposedCure: onRespond must not close the dialog. Make the emit awaitable (or have the parent drive an inFlight/error model on the dialog), keep the dialog mounted through the action, and render the failure inside it. The dialog is the only surface the user is looking at at that instant; it is the correct home for the result. Pair with L-12: render the {published, failed} tally.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is a 20-directory pure re-export shim layer over glass-ui — the residue of a completed migration — and it creates a live dual entrypoint: three dialogs in one directory reach glass-ui's ROOT barrel through it while two siblings use the @mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog subpath.
defects.evidence: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:47-55 imports from "../../../ui/dialog" and "../../../ui/button". Every demo/ui/*/index.ts is a naked re-export, e.g. demo/ui/dialog/index.ts:1 `export { Dialog, DialogClose, ... } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` and demo/ui/button/index.ts:1 `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (20 directories total). demo/ui/alert/index.ts states its own provenance: "This barrel previously held a local shadcn-vue re-implementation." DUAL PATH, same directory: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:52 / FlagReportDialog.vue:63 / VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:111 all go via ../../../ui/dialog → root barrel, while demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:148 and demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:197 import from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog". MEASURED (dev server resolves demo/ui/dialog/index.ts → node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui.js): `ls -l node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui{,_dialog}.js` → 231,357 bytes vs 274 bytes. Static-closure walk (JS only): subpath = 17 modules / 1,755,918 bytes; root = 56 modules / 2,468,810 bytes → +39 modules, +712,892 bytes (+40.6%). The 39 extras are unrelated: slider-*, select-*, popover-*, tooltip-*, chip-*, configurator-*, fading-scroll-*, DropdownMenuTrigger-*, usePointerVelocityField-*, dockContext-*.
