defects.reproduction: `for d in demo/ui/*/; do echo "=== $(basename $d)"; head -1 $d/index.ts; done` → 20 naked re-exports. `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/.../demo/ui/dialog/index.ts"` → resolves to node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui.js (the 231KB root barrel). `ls -l node_modules/.vite/deps/@mkbabb_glass-ui{,_dialog}.js` → 231357 vs 274.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ wholesale. Import glass-ui by subpath at every site (@mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog, @mkbabb/glass-ui/button) — the shape two files in this very directory already use. For the dialog cluster this is a ~5-line mechanical rewrite and removes 20 directories. Note: I tested and REFUTED both the duplicate-component-identity hypothesis (glass-ui.js:12 and dialog.js:1 share chunk ./dialog-TNRDkcE4.js) and the CSS-side-effect-retention hypothesis (0 .css imports reachable from either published entry) — the prod bundle tree-shakes, so this finding rests on the edict violation plus the measured dev cost, not on a prod regression.

defects.defect: The G-DEMO-3b barrel-seam lint boundary is dead code: it is scoped to file globs that no longer exist and bans a specifier built on the @components alias that W43/RF-15 deleted. The raw .vue reach it exists to forbid passes lint clean.
defects.mechanism: A tree restructure (W43/RF-15 killed the @ path aliases and moved demo/@/components → demo/palettes etc.) moved the code out from under its own guard rail without updating the guard rail. Both dialog/index.ts:1-4 and browser/index.ts:1-17 carry long comments asserting the boundary is "enforced standing" — the comments are now false, and the three-tier barrel apparatus they justify is ceremony with no enforcement (KISS/no-contrivance inverted).
defects.reproduction: printf 'import X from "../palettes/browser/dialog/MigratePalettesDialog.vue";\n' | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename demo/color-picker/__probe.ts  →  clean, 0 problems.
defects.proposedCure: Either re-point globs and patterns at the real tree (files: ["demo/**/*.{ts,vue}"], group: ["**/palettes/browser/*/*.vue"]) and keep the seam, or delete the seam. Do not keep both a dead rule and the barrels it was supposed to justify. Given L-7 I recommend re-pointing AFTER the component moves to demo/color-session/identity/.

defects.defect: MigrateChoice — the domain vocabulary — is declared inside the .vue SFC and re-exported by neither barrel, so the only legal way to obtain it is the raw .vue reach the seam law forbids; the composable therefore hand-copies the union twice.
defects.evidence: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:56 `export type MigrateChoice = "publish" | "transfer" | "discard";`. demo/palettes/browser/dialog/index.ts:8 exports only `{ default as MigratePalettesDialog }`; demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:38-43 re-exports the same names — neither exports the type. Consequence, verbatim: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:29 `ref<((choice: "publish" | "transfer" | "discard") => Promise<void>) | null>(null)` and demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:106 `async function onMigrateRespond(choice: "publish" | "transfer" | "discard")`. Three copies of one vocabulary across two files with no compiler edge between them.
defects.mechanism: A domain type homed inside a presentation file, behind a seam that can only export component values. Unique semantic ownership violated: add a fourth choice and only the dialog knows.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn 'publish" | "transfer" | "discard"' demo/` → 3 hits: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:56 (the declaration) plus useSlugMigration.ts:29 and :106 (the hand copies). `cat demo/palettes/browser/dialog/index.ts demo/palettes/browser/index.ts` → no `export type` line for MigrateChoice in either.
defects.proposedCure: Move the vocabulary to demo/palettes/types.ts (beside Palette / PaletteColor, which both files already import freely) — or, after L-7, to demo/color-session/identity/types.ts. Rename per L-11 to PaletteDisposition. Both the dialog and the composable then import one type from one home, and the seam no longer has to export types at all.

defects.defect: Wrong home / wrong dependency direction: the dialog lives three levels deep inside the palette-browser sub-feature, but nothing in browser/ uses it — it is mounted by the shell and driven by the feature root, and it belongs to the session/identity flow.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "MigratePalettesDialog" demo/palettes/browser/` returns only barrel lines and comments: browser/index.ts:13 (comment), browser/index.ts:40 (re-export), dialog/index.ts:3 (comment), dialog/index.ts:8 (re-export). No component, pane, or composable under demo/palettes/browser/ renders or reads it. Its real relations all live outside: mounted at demo/color-picker/App.vue:152 under `<!-- Global modals -->` (shell reaching down three levels into a sub-feature of a feature); driven by demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts via demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:79; triggered from demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:54, demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue:87, demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:61. Additionally useSlugMigration.ts:6 does `import type { PaletteSlugBar } from "./browser/slug"` — a feature-root composable reaching DOWN into a sub-feature for a component handle.
defects.mechanism: Misplaced ownership. The dialog is not part of the palette BROWSER; it is part of the identity flow. Its location forces the shell→feature-internal edge, forces the two-barrel apparatus of L-5 to make that edge respectable, and forces the downward type edge into browser/slug.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "MigratePalettesDialog" demo/palettes/browser/  →  4 hits, all barrel lines or comments; contrast grep -rn "MigratePalettesDialog" demo/color-picker/  →  App.vue:152 (mount) and App.vue:176 (import).
defects.proposedCure: Re-home to demo/color-session/identity/ as { types.ts, useIdentityChange.ts, PaletteDispositionDialog.vue }. demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts dissolves into useIdentityChange; usePalettePorts consumes it. This kills the shell→palettes/browser/dialog edge, kills the two-barrel apparatus around this component, and gives PaletteDisposition a real type home (L-6).

defects.defect: The per-instance class restates a glass-ui default: rounded-dialog is rendered twice on the live DialogContent element.
defects.evidence: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:3 `<DialogContent class="rounded-dialog max-w-sm">`. glass-ui already applies it — node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dialog-TNRDkcE4.js: `let Y = P(h, m), X = a(() => e(t("floating"), "rounded-dialog")), ...`. LIVE DOM className of the rendered [role="dialog"]: "fixed left-1/2 top-1/2 z-modal grid w-full gap-4 ... glass-reveal glass-floating rounded-dialog rounded-dialog max-w-sm" — the token appears twice. It is the only occurrence in the demo (`grep -rn "rounded-dialog" demo/ | wc -l` → 1) and neither sibling does it (FlagReportDialog.vue:3 = class="sm:max-w-md"; VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:3 uses placement="right").
defects.mechanism: Per-instance override of a root-component default — the root-level-styling edict. Dead markup that also signals to the next reader that the default is absent.
defects.reproduction: Open the dialog live (see L-3 repro), then `document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]').className` → the string contains "rounded-dialog rounded-dialog".
defects.proposedCure: Delete `rounded-dialog` from the class attribute. The correct idiom is already in the tree at demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:103 — `<DialogContent surface="glass" :show-close="false">` configures by prop, not by class.

defects.defect: All three buttons use Tailwind-core rounded-full instead of the glass-ui rounded-pill / --radius-pill design token, hard-pinning the radius outside the design system.
defects.evidence: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:16, :25, :34 all carry class "... rounded-full". `grep -c "rounded-full" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/components.css node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css` → 0 and 0. glass-ui ships `.rounded-pill{border-radius:var(--radius-pill)}` (alongside rounded-button, rounded-card, rounded-dialog, rounded-tooltip). LIVE computed style of the three dialog buttons: borderRadius "1.67772e+07px" each (Tailwind's calc(infinity*1px)), vs "4px" for the glass-ui close button.
defects.mechanism: Design-system bypass. Every other capsule in the app rides --radius-pill; if that token moves, this dialog does not.
defects.reproduction: Open the dialog live, then `[...document.querySelectorAll('[role="dialog"] button')].map(b => getComputedStyle(b).borderRadius)` → ["1.67772e+07px","1.67772e+07px","1.67772e+07px","4px"].
defects.proposedCure: Replace rounded-full with rounded-pill at MigratePalettesDialog.vue:16, :25, :34. Better still, after L-7/L-11 the three buttons come from one `choices` table and the class is authored once.

defects.defect: Dead computed: the `title` ternary returns the identical string in both arms.
defects.evidence: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:73-77 — `const title = computed(() => mode === "switch" ? "What about your palettes?" : "What about your palettes?");`. Both arms byte-identical. Confirmed live: the regenerate-mode probe and the switch-mode probe both rendered innerText beginning "What about your palettes?".
defects.mechanism: False parameterisation — a reactive computed over a constant, with a branch that cannot differ. Signals a copy variation that was planned and never written, or one that was collapsed without collapsing the machinery.
defects.reproduction: Read MigratePalettesDialog.vue:73-77. Live: open the dialog in each mode (3-segment slug → regenerate copy, 4-segment slug → switch copy) and compare `document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]').innerText.split('\n')[0]` — identical.
defects.proposedCure: `const title = "What about your palettes?"` — or, under the § 3 lattice, the title becomes a prop supplied by the flow's choice table and the computed disappears entirely along with the other three copy-switches at :79-96.

defects.defect: The choice set is degenerate and one literal is a lie: `transfer` and `publish` invoke the identical operation differing only in ordering, and `discard` discards nothing.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:62-71 — `if (choice === "publish") { await publishAllLocal(); } await deps.userLogin(value); if (choice === "transfer") { await publishAllLocal(); } setActiveTab("saved");`. Both branches call the same publishAllLocal(); the only difference is whether it runs before or after userLogin (i.e. under the old or the new identity) — which is precisely what the UI labels do NOT say ("Publish, then switch" vs "Transfer to new account"). `discard` runs neither branch and clears nothing: verified live, after clicking "Just switch" localStorage["color-palettes"].palettes.length was still 2. MigrateChoice (MigratePalettesDialog.vue:56) names that branch "discard".
defects.mechanism: Vocabulary drift between the presentation home (labels, icons) and the behaviour home (the composable closure). No single home owns the concept, so the type literal and the button label describe different things.
defects.reproduction: Read useSlugMigration.ts:62-71. Live: open the switch-mode dialog with 2 seeded palettes, click "Just switch", then `(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("color-palettes")).palettes||[]).length` → 2 (unchanged).
defects.proposedCure: Rename to what it means: `type PaletteDisposition = "publish-as-current" | "publish-as-new" | "keep-local"`. Under the § 3 lattice the two publish rows sit adjacent in one `choices` literal, which makes the degeneracy visible at the point of authorship — the author must state the difference in the label or delete one row.

defects.defect: publishAllLocal swallows every per-palette failure with a bare catch, so the dialog's "Publish, then switch" contract is not one the implementation keeps.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:35-51 — `for (const palette of deps.savedPalettes.value) { try { await createAndSavePalette({...}); } catch { /* Skip failures (e.g. duplicate slugs) */ } }`, wrapped in an outer `catch (e) { console.warn("Publish all failed:", e); }`.
defects.mechanism: Masking fallback (no-legacy edict). Combined with L-3 the user gets no signal at all: a user with 12 palettes and 11 duplicate-slug failures sees a dialog close and nothing else.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis at the observation level (I did not construct a duplicate-slug corpus). The code path is unambiguous at useSlugMigration.ts:44 and the outer swallow at :49-51; the user-invisibility half is proven by the L-3 live measurement.
defects.proposedCure: Have publishAllLocal return `{ published: number; failed: Array<{slug: string; reason: string}> }` and have the dialog render the tally while it is still mounted (per L-3's cure). The dialog is the surface the user is looking at; it is the correct home for the outcome.

defects.defect: The component has zero coverage in the visual audit matrix and cannot appear in it by construction — it is a modal gated on non-empty local storage plus an interaction.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md has no row involving this component across 4 matrices x 15 routes. The gate is `deps.savedPalettes.value.length > 0` at demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:60 and :92. I read docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png: it renders the empty state — "· EMPTY PLATE ·" / "No saved palettes yet." / "Add colors above, then save the set." — the exact state in which the dialog can never open.
defects.mechanism: The visual harness captures cold routes only, so every storage-gated or interaction-gated modal is structurally invisible to it. All rendering evidence in this report came from my own live probes, not from the matrix.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "MigratePalettes|migrate" docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md → no hits. Read shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png → empty-state plate.
defects.proposedCure: Add a seeded-storage variant to the visual harness (pre-populate localStorage["color-palettes"] before capture) plus a small interaction script per gated modal. Otherwise this dialog — and every other gated modal in the app — stays permanently unaudited.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (MigratePalettesDialog.vue, area palettes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — matches the explicit spawn declaration; no inherited or undeclared seat.
result.strongestDefect: C-2 — "Publish, then switch/regenerate" publishes every local palette under a throwaway server identity: useSlugMigration.publishAllLocal calls only session.ensureSession() (useSession.ts:36-38 mints a session via POST /sessions, which api/src/modules/session/routes.ts:32 implements as registerSession — a real new user — and persists only the token, discarding the returned userSlug), while the canonical usePaletteActions.onPublish:42 calls ensureUser() which persists the slug. The `ensureUser` dependency is declared at useSlugMigration.ts:15 and never appears in the body (grep of `deps.` proves it). In regenerate mode the very next step deletes that session and registers a different user, so the palettes are public, ownerless to the user, and unrecoverable — silently. I MEASURED the reachable precondition live: dialog open, primary button focused, localStorage["palette-user-slug"] === null, two local palettes present.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Cleared hazards, recorded as negative evidence in the report: defineModel stale-read is not exploitable here since nothing reads `open` after writing it and onMigrateRespond nulls the latch before awaiting; no ValueUnit wrapping, no oklch/HSV roundtrip, no colour parsing, no WebGL, no rAF owned by the component — glass-ui's two rAFs are cancelled in W() and reset via onScopeDispose; no listeners/observers/timers; count is bound to Array.length so NaN/Infinity/negative are unconstructible and pluralisation is correct at 0/1/2 (MEASURED "2 local palettes"); verbatimModuleSyntax compliant (no type-only imports present); Vue 3.5 reactive-props-destructure used correctly; aria-labelledby and aria-describedby both present and resolving (MEASURED); zero console errors on /#/palettes across all four visual matrices and zero during the live open/close cycle; the /#/palettes namelessButtons row is not attributable to this component.)

defects.defect: Escape, the glass-ui close X, and outside-click all close the dialog without emitting `respond`, so the user's already-committed slug switch/regenerate is silently abandoned — no network call, no error, no feedback, and the pendingMigrateAction latch is left armed.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/dialog/MigratePalettesDialog.vue:2,58,69-72 (respond emitted only from the three buttons); demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:91-104 (the whole operation is parked in pendingMigrateAction before the dialog opens); node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dialog-TNRDkcE4.js `showClose: { type: Boolean, default: !0 }`. MEASURED live after page.keyboard.press('Escape'): {"dialogOpen": false, "slugAfter": null, "fetches": [], "activeEl": "BODY", "errorText": [], "storeCount": 2}.
defects.mechanism: The response domain omits dismissal: MigrateChoice has no `cancel` member and the `open` v-model has no false-handler, so three of the six close paths fall through a hole in the component's contract.
defects.reproduction: Seed localStorage['color-palettes'] with 2 local palettes, reload http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, invoke the production handler `document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Generate new slug"]').click()` (SlugEditLayer.vue:107 → pm.onRegenerateSlug()), then press Escape. Dialog closes; zero fetches; palette-user-slug unchanged (null); no error text in the DOM.
defects.proposedCure: Make dismissal a first-class answer rather than patching each close path: extend MigrateChoice with `cancel`, wire `@update:open="v => { if (!v) onRespond('cancel') }"` so every exit funnels through one emit, and have onMigrateRespond clear the latch and restore the slug bar on cancel.

defects.defect: The primary action publishes all local palettes under a throwaway identity: publishAllLocal skips the injected `ensureUser` dep and calls only session.ensureSession(), which registers a brand-new server user and discards its slug; in regenerate mode the next line then destroys that session and registers a different user.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:15 declares `ensureUser` and `grep -n "deps\." demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts` returns 11 lines, none of them deps.ensureUser or deps.userLogout; publishAllLocal at :32-49 calls only session.ensureSession(). demo/platform/auth/useSession.ts:36-38 — `const res = await createSession(); persistToken(res.token, false);` (slug discarded). api/src/modules/session/routes.ts:32 — `POST /sessions` → registerSession (mints a user). Canonical contrast: demo/palettes/usePaletteActions.ts:42 `await ensureUser()`. api/src/modules/palette/routes/crud.ts:85 `userSlug: c.var.userSlug ?? null` and service/crud.ts:118 `if (userSlug)` (no version record without one). MEASURED precondition live: {"before": {"slug": null, "dialogOpen": true, "active": "Publish, then regenerate"}}.
defects.mechanism: Two identity primitives with different persistence semantics (ensureUser persists the slug; ensureSession persists only a token) are treated as interchangeable inside a data-publishing path, so ownership is minted and thrown away in one gesture.
defects.reproduction: Precondition MEASURED live (no slug + 2 local palettes + dialog armed on 'Publish, then regenerate'). The consequence chain is CONFIRMED-BY-CODE, not executed: clicking would write real rows to the live API, outside a read-only audit seat.
defects.proposedCure: Delete publishAllLocal and pass the canonical publish verb in as a dependency (see C-4) — it establishes identity by construction. Minimum viable: `await deps.ensureUser()` at the head of publishAllLocal, using the dependency already injected and already unused.

defects.defect: The publish is non-idempotent, transitions no state, and reports neither success nor failure: the local store is never mutated, so the dialog re-fires forever with the same count, and repeat publishes 409 into an empty catch.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:32-49 — no updatePalette/deletePalette; :42 `} catch { // Skip failures (e.g. duplicate slugs) }`; :47 outer `console.warn`. demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:51-55 — savedPalettes filters on `p.isLocal && p.id != null`. api/src/platform/db/db.ts:41 — `createIndex({ slug: 1 }, { unique: true })` (global). api/src/modules/palette/service/crud.ts:133-137 — code 11000 → ConflictError. demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:106-116 — onMigrateRespond returns void, only console.warn on throw.
defects.mechanism: An operation whose completion condition is `savedPalettes.length === 0` never writes the flag that condition reads, so it can neither terminate nor detect its own repetition; every failure class is collapsed into a swallowed catch.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED-BY-CODE. Compound path: choose 'Publish, then switch' with a slug that 404s — palettes are POSTed to the OLD account, userLogin throws, the throw is caught at useSlugMigration.ts:112 and console.warn'd, the user stays signed in as before and is told nothing. First-publish collision also reachable: createSlug('Sunset') = 'sunset', globally unique index, silently skipped.
defects.proposedCure: One publish verb returning a typed result; the caller flips isLocal (or adopts the server row) on success and surfaces published/skipped/failed counts; the dialog is satisfied only when the local set is empty.

defects.defect: Dual publish path — publishAllLocal is a second, weaker implementation of usePaletteActions.onPublish that drops identity, collapses two failure classes into `catch {}`, and returns void. This is the edict-2 (no dual paths) violation in this flow.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:32-49 vs demo/palettes/usePaletteActions.ts:40-58 — both call createAndSavePalette({name, slug, colors}); only onPublish calls ensureUser() (:42), distinguishes session failure (:44-46) from publish failure (:54-57), and returns {success, message}.
defects.mechanism: A divergent copy of an existing verb, made at the call site instead of by reuse, quietly loses the invariants the original holds.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED-BY-CODE — read both functions side by side; the divergence is total (identity, error typing, return value).
defects.proposedCure: useSlugMigration takes `publish: (p: Palette) => Promise<Result>` — the same function usePaletteActions already exposes — and maps it over the local set. publishAllLocal is deleted; the now-orphaned ensureUser/userLogout deps go with it.

defects.defect: Vacuous gate: the only test naming this component reads a file path deleted at commit a61094e3, so it throws ENOENT if ever run — and CI runs no playwright step at all. Unit coverage is zero.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/oracles/o10d-display-voice-census.spec.ts:453-461 reads '../../../demo/@/components/custom/palette-browser/dialog/MigratePalettesDialog.vue'. `node --input-type=module` resolving that exact URL: `resolves to: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/@/components/custom/palette-browser/dialog/MigratePalettesDialog.vue` / `THROWS: ENOENT`. `ls demo/@` → 'No such file or directory'. `git log --oneline --diff-filter=D -1 -- <that path>` → `a61094e3 feat(v-w43b3)!: home the feature UI trees; demo/@ dies (D-c)`. `grep -n "run:" -A2 .github/workflows/ci.yml` → lint, two vue-tsc, build, npm test, verify-packed-surface, api tsc+test — no playwright. `find demo/test -type f` → 3 files, none related (demo/test/palettes/api/ is empty; vite.config.ts:21 includes demo/test/**/*.ts).
defects.mechanism: A byte-grep oracle pinned to a path rather than to behaviour, in a suite that CI does not execute — so a whole-tree restructure broke it invisibly and it still reads as coverage.
defects.reproduction: Run the node URL-resolution snippet above: deterministic ENOENT. (I did not execute playwright: playwright.config.ts's second webServer builds dist/gh-pages when absent, a multi-minute cost, and the throw is already proven.)
defects.proposedCure: Add demo/test/palettes/useSlugMigration.test.ts driving the composable against a fake transport — dismissal cancels and clears the latch, publish flips isLocal, a 409 is reported not swallowed, regenerate never publishes to an unpersisted identity. Then repair or delete o10d; a census oracle pointing at a deleted tree is worse than none. Mutations that keep the current suite green: delete the transfer button; swap the publish/discard emit args; delete the emit entirely; hard-code count to 1; invert every mode ternary.

defects.defect: The dialog's premise is false and its third choice is misnamed: 'discard' discards nothing, and local palettes are device-scoped, never at risk from an identity change. The title computed also has two byte-identical ternary branches.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:61-70,94-99 — the discard branch merely skips the publish. `grep -rn "color-palettes|store.value.palettes = " demo/` returns only usePaletteStore.ts:6 (the key) and :166 (reorder). demo/platform/auth/useUserAuth.ts:44-48 clearAuth touches the slug and token, not the palettes. MEASURED: storeCount 2 before and after the full open→Escape cycle. MigratePalettesDialog.vue:74-78 — both ternary branches are 'What about your palettes?'.
defects.mechanism: Copy written for a data model (account-scoped palettes) that the storage layer does not implement (device-scoped), plus a computed whose dependency cannot change its output.
defects.reproduction: MEASURED — the live cycle left localStorage['color-palettes'] with 2 palettes; the grep proves no code path clears it on login/logout/regenerate.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the three-way modal with the honest question — an opt-in 'also publish these before you change identity?' — and make `title` a constant, or write the second string the ternary was reaching for.

defects.defect: `transfer` is unimplemented in regenerate mode and would silently behave as `discard`; the only guard is a template v-if, because the emitted type is mode-independent. It is also the one mode where transfer is the semantically correct option.
defects.evidence: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:56 `export type MigrateChoice = "publish" | "transfer" | "discard"` and :22-30 `v-if="mode === 'switch'"`; demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:94-99 — the regenerate closure handles only 'publish', everything else falls through to userRegenerate(). Contrast :66-68 where switch mode implements transfer as publish-AFTER-login.
defects.mechanism: A type admitting states its handler cannot serve, policed by a render condition instead of by the type system.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis for the silent no-op, since the v-if currently prevents emission. The type/handler mismatch itself is CONFIRMED-BY-CODE.
defects.proposedCure: Split the choice per mode (SwitchChoice / RegenChoice) so the handler must be total, or implement transfer for regenerate — it is exactly the publish-after-identity-change the flow needs.

defects.defect: Accessibility: the close target measures 16x16 CSS px with zero padding (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 requires 24x24); a multi-second async operation runs after the dialog closes with no aria-live, no aria-busy, no pending state and no spinner; and focus restoration cannot succeed because the trigger hides itself in the same handler that opens the dialog.
defects.evidence: MEASURED live: btns [{"t":"Publish, then regenerate","w":334,"h":40},{"t":"Just regenerate","w":334,"h":40},{"t":"Close","w":16,"h":16}], close computed padding "0px 0px 0px 0px". glass-ui root: dialog-TNRDkcE4.js DialogClose carries only `absolute right-… top-… rounded-sm opacity-70` around a `w-4 h-4` icon. MigratePalettesDialog.vue:70 closes before emitting; useSlugMigration.ts:35-45 then runs N sequential awaited POSTs. demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:107 `@click="slugEditMode = false; pm.onRegenerateSlug()"`. Visual REPORT.md:31 records 60 smallTapTargets across the matrix.
defects.mechanism: Interactive affordances sized by their icon rather than by their hit area, plus an async operation with no result channel of any kind (visual or assistive).
defects.reproduction: MEASURED via getBoundingClientRect on the live dialog. CAVEAT recorded in the report: the activeElement===BODY reading after close is contaminated because I invoked the trigger programmatically, so it is NOT claimed as proof; the structural focus-restoration defect is proven by reading SlugEditLayer.vue:107 instead.
defects.proposedCure: Fix the close target at the glass-ui root per edict 4 (pad the DialogClose to a 24px minimum hit area, not per-instance). Give the flow a result channel: an aria-live status region plus a pending state on the buttons, driven by the typed result C-3/C-4 introduce.

defects.defect: Measured contrast failure on the dialog description: 3.63:1 against the 4.5:1 required for normal-size text, and the failure is structural because the glass surface is 70% opaque over arbitrary live app content.
defects.evidence: PNG-decode of the live capture (evidence-migrate-dialog-regenerate-light.png, 768x480 device px = 384x240 CSS at DPR2): `DESCRIPTION darkest [112, 89, 66]  lightest [210, 188, 183]  CR 3.63` — taking the LIGHTEST background pixel, which biases in the component's favour. Authoritative computed colour: getComputedStyle(description).color === 'rgb(112, 89, 66)'; --muted-foreground = light-dark(hsl(30 22% 40%), hsl(34 14% 62%)). Surface: background oklab(0.903549 0.0153586 0.0142464 / 0.705088), backdrop-filter blur(11px) saturate(1.6). Class is text-small (normal size, so 4.5:1 applies).
defects.mechanism: A fixed foreground token over an unbounded composited background: the dialog is translucent over whatever the app renders behind it, so no static colour pair can guarantee AA.
defects.reproduction: Open the dialog on /#/palettes in light theme with the pink accent plate behind it; screenshot the [role=dialog] element at device scale; decode and sample the description band (device y 110-200). Reproduced and pasted in the report.
defects.proposedCure: Raise the surface opacity (or add a solid content-layer behind text) so the composited background is bounded, and verify the token pair against that bound at the glass-ui root rather than per dialog.

defects.defect: The per-instance `text-muted-foreground` on the tertiary button is inert — it loses to the glass-ui Button root, so the dismissive action renders with exactly the same label colour as the primary action and the intended hierarchy does not exist.
defects.evidence: MEASURED live in the same dialog: ghost button className includes `text-muted-foreground`, computed color 'rgb(0, 0, 0)'; a bare <span class="text-muted-foreground"> injected into the same dialog computes 'rgb(112, 89, 66)'; the primary button also computes 'rgb(0, 0, 0)'. Visible in evidence-migrate-dialog-regenerate-light.png — two identically weighted black serif labels. Source: MigratePalettesDialog.vue:33.
defects.mechanism: Leaf-level utility override defeated by a higher-specificity root rule, failing silently — the exact failure mode the owner's root-level-styling edict exists to prevent.
defects.reproduction: MEASURED — inject a probe span with the identical class into the open dialog and compare getComputedStyle(...).color against the button carrying the same class.
defects.proposedCure: Express the tertiary/dismissive emphasis as a glass-ui Button variant at the root, and delete the per-instance class. If no such variant exists, add it to glass-ui per edict 4.

defects.defect: publishAllLocal serialises its POSTs behind a dialog that has already closed and shows no progress.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardSwatches.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — declared explicitly at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-2 — SwatchHoverMenu passes `tag="button"` + `:aria-label` to glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which has NO `tag` prop; the swatch renders as `<span aria-hidden="true">` with `pointer-events: none`, so every click/tap action PaletteCardSwatches wires (swatchClick, popoverAdd/Edit/Copy, and the whole touch Popover branch) is unreachable and the swatch has no accessible name — while `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded negatives, each positively verified: no deep `src/` import — the component imports zero value.js and the whole demo/palettes tree reaches the library only via published subpaths, `grep -rn "@mkbabb/value.js" demo/palettes/` → 2 hits, both `@mkbabb/value.js/color`; no feature→shell or component→boot edge — its only imports are `@lucide/vue`, `@mkbabb/glass-ui`, `../../../types`, `../SwatchHoverMenu.vue`; barrel seam intact in practice — `PaletteCardSwatches` is correctly absent from `browser/card/index.ts` and `grep -rn "browser/card/" demo/ | grep -v "^demo/palettes/browser/card/"` returns nothing; `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean at line 72; not a god module at 96 lines; and the suspected `useHoverPopover` async-`currentTarget` bug is NOT real — a real trusted pointerenter measured `{syncCurrentTarget:"DIV", microtaskCurrentTarget:"DIV"}` and the live inline style came out numerically exact at `left: 824.445px` for a swatch centre of 804.445+20.)

defects.defect: `SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-20,29-36` passes `tag="button"` and `:aria-label` to glass-ui 7.0.0 `WatercolorDot`, whose prop set is `{color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed}` — no `tag`. The dot renders `<span aria-hidden="true" … pointer-events: none>`, killing every swatch action PaletteCardSwatches declares and erasing the accessible name.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts (__VLS_Props has no `tag`). Live DOM of the expanded card, `[role="article"] [data-testid="watercolor-swatch"]` ×2: {"tag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"tagAttr":null,"pe":"none","w":40,"h":40,"role":null,"tabindex":null}. Gate blindness: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` → `EXIT=0`, zero diagnostics.
defects.mechanism: Dependency on a design-system component through the untyped fallthrough-attribute channel. Vue's template type checker accepts undeclared attrs as fallthrough, so a prop rename/removal in glass-ui is invisible to the `dist/*.d.ts` trust boundary. `git log --oneline -L '/glass-ui/,+1:package.json'` → `f2c8f565 feat(v-w44)!: adopt @mkbabb/glass-ui 7.0.0` touched PaletteCardSwatches.vue but its entire edit was `copyToClipboard` → `writeClipboard`; it never touched SwatchHoverMenu.vue (last touched `a61094e3`), so the untyped half of the glass-ui contract was never audited.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → click `[aria-label="Palette: Audit Alpha"]` to expand → evaluate `getComputedStyle` + attributes on `[role="article"] [data-testid="watercolor-swatch"]`. Observed SPAN / aria-hidden=true / aria-label=null / pointer-events:none / 40×40. Clicking the dot never emits `swatchClick`; on `(hover: none)` the `<PopoverTrigger as-child>` wrapping the same inert span never opens.
defects.proposedCure: Move the contract into the prop channel where it can be enforced: glass-ui `WatercolorDot` gains `interactive?: boolean` (or `as?: "span"|"button"`) that renders a real `<button>`, drops `aria-hidden`, restores hit-testing, forwards `aria-label`, and carries `tap-squish focus-ring` — plus a `size?: "sm"|"md"|"lg"` token so consumers stop passing Tailwind rungs. BH/BI relay item under the standing glass-ui coordination edict.

defects.defect: `SwatchHoverMenu.vue:42` styles the Teleported hover action panel with `class="floating-panel"` — a class that is defined nowhere in the repo or in glass-ui 7.0.0. The panel is therefore `position: static`, its inline `top`/`left` are inert, and it renders full-viewport-width at the bottom of `<body>`, 756px off the left edge, transparent and shadowless.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "floating-panel" demo/ src/` → 1 template use, 2 prose mentions, 1 comment, 0 declarations. Node scan of `dist/glass-ui.css` + all 20 `dist/styles/*.css` for the string → no output. Live computed-style probe: `.floating-panel` == bare div (position static / rgba(0,0,0,0) / none / auto), while `.glass-floating` is live (position relative + 8-layer glass shadow + backdrop-filter). Real-hover readback: {"parentTag":"BODY","position":"static","inline":"top: 491.547px; left: 824.445px; transform: translateX(-50%);","bg":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","shadow":"none","zIndex":"auto","rect":{"x":-756,"y":806,"w":1512,"h":40},"visibleInViewport":false}. Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardSwatches/evidence-hover-panel-offscreen.png
defects.mechanism: The component depends on glass-ui through the CSS class-name channel, which is not in `package.json#exports`, not in any `.d.ts`, and not linted. glass-ui 7.0.0 dropped the class at the W44 adoption and nothing in the repo could notice. `positionPanel` computes correctly (824.445 = swatch x 804.445 + w/2; 491.547 = y 533.5 − 42) — the coordinates are right and inert.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes → click `[aria-label="Palette: Audit Alpha"]` → Playwright `.hover()` on `[aria-label="Palette: Audit Alpha"] .px-3.pb-3 > div:nth-child(1)` → evaluate rect+computed style of `.floating-panel`. Panel exists with correct aria-labelled buttons but sits at x=-756, y=806 in a 1512×806 viewport.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-positioned Teleport branch entirely. glass-ui 7 ships `<Popover trigger="hover">` (the W44 commit records `HoverCard -> <Popover trigger="hover">`), so `SwatchHoverMenu` collapses to one `<Popover :trigger="canHover ? 'hover' : 'click'">` + `<PopoverContent>` + the actions slot — killing ~120 lines, `useHoverPopover`, `useLeaveTimer`, the `translateX(-50%)` split (L-8) and the self-confessed keyboard-inaccessible `aria-hidden` panel.

defects.defect: `btn-interactive` — the producer atom the T.W5-R5 ruling migrated press/hover choreography onto — does not exist in glass-ui 7.0.0. The ruled cure is a no-op, and PaletteCardSwatches (never migrated) carries the un-cured original: `active:scale-95` paired with `transition-colors`, so the scale leg is instantaneous and untimed at all four of its buttons.
defects.evidence: `grep -rl "btn-interactive" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui` → no matches (only `data-table-row-interactive` / `fourier-field--interactive` contain the substring). Live computed-style probe: `.btn-interactive` == bare div. Applied at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:75,78,100 and demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:69,78; documented as the cure at demo/DESIGN.md:237,247. Un-migrated original at PaletteCardSwatches.vue:14,44,51,58.
defects.mechanism: Same class-name channel as L-1. A design ruling was recorded as 'landed' in DESIGN.md against a class that the design system later removed; the ruling's own audit trail cannot detect its target's disappearance.
defects.reproduction: Live page → create a div with class `btn-interactive`, read getComputedStyle: identical to a bare div in every property (position/background/box-shadow/z-index/transition/border/padding). Then read PaletteCardSwatches.vue:44 — `active:scale-95 … transition-colors` with no transform transition.
defects.proposedCure: Stop naming classes. Press/hover choreography is component behaviour: glass-ui `Button` already carries it (measured live on the card's own menu trigger: `class="button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule …"`). Adopt the component and delete the recipe — this and L-4 are one edit.

defects.defect: The icon-only action-button recipe is duplicated verbatim six times across four files (plus two near-copies at other padding rungs), while glass-ui's `Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm"` atom is used 10 lines away in the same component's parent, with a comment saying exactly this migration was performed.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "p-1.5 rounded-sm hover:bg-accent active:scale-95" demo/ | wc -l` → 6 (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:44,51,58; CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:46,49,52). Near-copies: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:14 (p-0.5), PaletteSlugBar.vue:84 (p-1). Precedent: PaletteCard.vue:93-104 — 'S.W5-4: 3rd copy of the hand-rolled icon-trigger recipe dies onto the glass-ui atom; the sm square also cures the ~24px touch target.' Live measurement of the surviving copies: 28×28 px.
defects.mechanism: A partial migration. S.W5-4 cured the three copies its census found and stopped; the six in the swatch family were out of that census's scope and inherited the same sub-44px touch target the ruling names as the defect it cured. Violates edict 1 (no god modules / focused modules), edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system), edict 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides).
defects.reproduction: grep as above (6 exact hits, 4 files). Live: the panel's buttons measure `{"al":"Edit color #e11d48","w":28,"h":28}` and `{"al":"Copy color #e11d48","w":28,"h":28}` — below the 44px floor the visual audit flags 8× per matrix on /#/palettes.
defects.proposedCure: `<Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm">` at all eight sites. Zero new abstractions, zero new files — the atom is already imported by the parent. Combined with M-3 (leaf takes an action list) the three buttons become one `v-for`.

defects.defect: The three 'STANDING' eslint import-boundary gates (G-DEMO-1 / G-DEMO-3a / G-DEMO-3b) that exist specifically to protect the palette-browser barrel seam match zero files: their globs key on `demo/@/**`, deleted at W43b3, and their banned pattern is `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue`, an alias retired at W43.
defects.evidence: eslint.config.js:229-296. `ls -d demo/@` → 'No such file or directory'. Glob census: demo/color-picker→28 files, demo/@/components→0, demo/@/lib→0, demo/@/composables→0. `git show --stat a61094e3 | grep -c "eslint.config.js"` → 0 (the commit that deleted demo/@ never updated the config). `git log --oneline -3 -- eslint.config.js` → last touched at 616e84f2, the tranche before the move. Only surviving `@components/custom` string in demo/ is a comment (demo/palettes/browser/status/index.ts:5). tsconfig.demo.json header confirms: 'W43 (RF-15): the demo `@…` path aliases were killed'.
defects.mechanism: Boundary law encoded as path globs against a tree that moved twice. Globs rot silently: eslint does not warn that a rule matched nothing, so a deleted directory converts a hard gate into a no-op with no signal. The seam currently holds by accident, not by construction.
defects.reproduction: Run the four `find` commands above; three of four boundary file-globs resolve to 0 files. Honest negative: no live violation exists today — `grep -rn 'from "[^"]*palettes/browser/[^"]*\.vue"' demo/ | grep -v '^demo/palettes/browser/'` and `grep -rn "browser/card/" demo/ | grep -v "^demo/palettes/browser/card/"` both return nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Express the seam in the resolver, not in lint strings: `package.json#imports` subpath declarations (`#palettes` → demo/palettes/index.ts) or workspace sub-packages with their own `exports`, so a raw cross-feature `.vue` reach fails to resolve — rename-proof and build-state-independent. Minimum viable: re-key the globs onto the live tree AND add a CI assertion that every `no-restricted-imports` glob matches at least one file, so a boundary rule that matches nothing fails loudly.

defects.defect: `writeClipboard` is imported from the glass-ui ROOT barrel (`@mkbabb/glass-ui`) rather than the `./dom` subpath where it is declared — a 66-file / 218.9 KB transitive module closure instead of 8 files / 12.3 KB, for the identical symbol. All 12 demo sites make the same choice, while a sibling composable three files away already uses `/dom`.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:71. Declaration home: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:37, re-exported by dist/dom.d.ts (`export * from "./composables/dom"`); verified `dom.js` contains the symbol. Measured closures — root @mkbabb/glass-ui → {"files":66,"kb":"218.9"}; sub @mkbabb/glass-ui/dom → {"files":8,"kb":"12.3"} (17.8× by weight, 8.3× by module count). `grep -rn "writeClipboard" demo/ | grep import | wc -l` → 12, all root. Counter-example: useHoverPopover.ts:3 `import { useBreakpoint } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom";`
defects.mechanism: glass-ui publishes 68 subpaths precisely so consumers can reach narrow surfaces, but nothing prevents the bare root specifier, so the wide reach became the majority idiom by copy-paste. The card cluster now consumes one package at two granularities within three files.
defects.reproduction: node closure script over node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist (resolve `from "./…"` transitively from glass-ui.js vs dom.js): 66/218.9KB vs 8/12.3KB. In Vite dev that is 58 extra module requests per consumer.
defects.proposedCure: `import { writeClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom";` at all 12 sites, plus a `no-restricted-imports` rule banning the bare `@mkbabb/glass-ui` root specifier for any symbol a published subpath owns.

defects.defect: glass-ui's `writeClipboard` returns a discriminated `CopyResult` (`{ok:true} | {ok:false, reason}`) explicitly documented as 'rather than a lossy boolean'. All six palettes call sites discard it — and PaletteCardSwatches.vue:16 does not even `void` it, leaving a floating promise in a template handler — while `ActionFeedback.vue` and `PaletteCard.defineExpose({showFeedback})` sit in the same directory as the designed feedback channel, wired to nothing.
defects.evidence: Contract: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:17-22,32-37. Call sites: `grep -rn "writeClipboard(" demo/palettes/ | grep -v import` → usePaletteActions.ts:134, PaletteSlugBar.vue:169, useSwatchActions.ts:87, PaletteCardSwatches.vue:16, PaletteCard.vue:294, PaletteCard.vue:333 — six `void`/bare calls, zero result reads. Unused sibling: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue; PaletteCard.vue:238-244. glass-ui also ships an unused `useClipboard` ('reactive clipboard copy with scope-owned confirmation state').
defects.mechanism: A library failure channel discarded at the consumer boundary. Especially sharp here because package.json:4 describes value.js itself as 'Immutable, failure-explicit', and because the feedback component the result should drive already exists two files away.
defects.reproduction: Read the six call sites; none destructures `{ ok }`. PaletteCardSwatches.vue:16 `@click="writeClipboard(displaySlug)"` returns Promise<CopyResult> from a template handler — a rejection is unhandled. A clipboard-permission denial produces silent no-op UI at every site.
defects.proposedCure: One `useSwatchClipboard()` in the card cluster: wraps `writeClipboard` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom` (L-6), consumes `{ ok }`, drives `showFeedback(ok ? "Copied" : "Copy failed", ok ? "success" : "error")`. Four call sites collapse to one and ActionFeedback becomes load-bearing.

defects.defect: `useHoverPopover.positionPanel` deliberately emits the swatch CENTRE as `left` but never owns the centre→left-edge conversion. PaletteCardSwatches adds `transform: translateX(-50%)`; CurrentPaletteEditor does not. Two consumers of one composable hold contradictory contracts, so the current-palette editor's panel is offset by +½ panel width.
defects.evidence: useHoverPopover.ts:20-24 (`style.left = `${rect.left + rect.width / 2}px``). PaletteCardSwatches.vue:31 `:floating-style="{ ...floatingStyle, transform: 'translateX(-50%)' }"`. CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:35 `:floating-style="currentFloatingStyle"` — no transform. Live confirmation that positionPanel itself is correct: inline style read back as `top: 491.547px; left: 824.445px` for a swatch at x=804.445 w=40 y=533.5 (exact centre, exact −42 offset).
defects.mechanism: Split ownership of one concept. The composable owns the hard half (measuring) and leaves the trivial half (centring) to each consumer, so the trivial half drifted. Currently masked by L-1 (position:static makes all offsets inert) — it is a latent regression that surfaces the moment L-1 is fixed.
defects.reproduction: NONE as a user-visible failure today (L-1 masks it). Static reproduction: compare PaletteCardSwatches.vue:31 with CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:35 against useHoverPopover.ts:23. Hypothesis for the post-L-1 world, labelled as such.
defects.proposedCure: `positionPanel` returns a complete style object `{ position: "fixed", top, left, transform: "translateX(-50%)" }`; consumers spread it and add nothing. (Moot under M-2, which deletes manual positioning entirely.)

defects.defect: One value carries three different type declarations across the three files that touch it: the composable's `reactive({top:string,left:string})`, PaletteCardSwatches' `Record<string, string | number>`, and SwatchHoverMenu's `CSSProperties | undefined`.
defects.evidence: useHoverPopover.ts:17 `const style = reactive({ top: "0px", left: "0px" });` · PaletteCardSwatches.vue:82 `floatingStyle: Record<string, string | number>;` · SwatchHoverMenu.vue:73 `floatingStyle?: CSSProperties | undefined;`
defects.mechanism: Structural typing lets all three pass, so nothing catches the drift. The middle hop widens to `Record<string, string|number>`, erasing CSSProperties' safety for any property a future author adds.
defects.reproduction: NONE (type-level only; `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0). Static: read the three declarations.
defects.proposedCure: The composable owns the type — `export type FloatingPanelStyle = CSSProperties` from useHoverPopover.ts; both components import it. One declaration, one home.

defects.defect: The swatch-size Tailwind literal `"w-9 h-9 sm:w-10 sm:h-10"` has two live defaults plus a doc-comment copy plus a fourth hand-rolled instance in another feature; PaletteCardSwatches declares `swatchClass: string` REQUIRED with no default, forcing the parent's copy to win and making SwatchHoverMenu's default permanently dead on this path.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "w-9 h-9 sm:w-10 sm:h-10" demo/` → SwatchHoverMenu.vue:82 (withDefaults), PaletteCard.vue:194 (doc comment), PaletteCard.vue:197 (withDefaults), demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:205. PaletteCardSwatches.vue:83 `swatchClass: string;` (non-optional).
defects.mechanism: A design token expressed as a class string travelling through props. Because it is a string, no type prevents divergence, and because the leaf makes it required, the sibling's default is unreachable dead code.
defects.reproduction: NONE (no runtime failure). Static: change SwatchHoverMenu.vue:82's default and observe no effect on the card path, because PaletteCard.vue:197 always supplies a value.
defects.proposedCure: A swatch has sizes, not class strings: `WatercolorDot` carries `size?: "sm"|"md"|"lg"` in glass-ui (same edit as L-2) and the demo passes a token. Interim: one exported constant with one home.

defects.defect: A domain rule — 'you may only pull colours out of a non-local palette' — is expressed as `v-if="!isLocal"` in a presentational leaf, using a raw `boolean | undefined`, while the concept already has a named home (`PaletteKind`) that the same parent already computes and passes to a sibling child.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:42 `v-if="!isLocal"` and :77 `isLocal: boolean | undefined;`. The concept's home: demo/palettes/utils.ts `getPaletteKind` / `PaletteKind`. The parent already computes it: PaletteCard.vue:225 `const kind = computed<PaletteKind>(() => getPaletteKind(props.palette));` and passes `:palette-kind="kind"` to PaletteCardMenu (PaletteCard.vue:85) while passing raw `:is-local="palette.isLocal"` to PaletteCardSwatches (PaletteCard.vue:141).
defects.mechanism: Two representations of one concept cross two child boundaries from the same template — one is the domain concept, the other is its wire form. The leaf becomes a place business rules can accumulate.
defects.reproduction: NONE (behaviour is currently correct). Static: PaletteCard.vue:85 vs :141 in one template.
defects.proposedCure: Pass `kind`; better, invert it — the parent computes which actions exist and hands the leaf a list (`swatch.actions`), so the leaf renders a `v-for` and holds no predicate at all (see M-3).

defects.defect: Clipboard ownership is split inside a single parent/child pair: the slug copy is executed locally in the leaf, while the colour copy is emitted upward and executed by the parent — one operation, two ownership answers, eleven lines apart. Two further homes exist in the same feature.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:16 `@click="writeClipboard(displaySlug)"` (local, imported at :71) vs PaletteCardSwatches.vue:59 `@click="$emit('popoverCopy', color.css)"` → PaletteCard.vue:331-334 `void writeClipboard(css)`. Third home: useSwatchActions.ts:85-88. Fourth: usePaletteActions.ts:134.
defects.mechanism: No stated rule for 'leaves emit, containers act' vs 'leaves act', so each site chose independently. Unique semantic ownership is violated for the copy concept across four files.
defects.reproduction: NONE (both paths work). Static: read PaletteCardSwatches.vue:16 against :59 + PaletteCard.vue:333.
defects.proposedCure: One seam (M-6 / L-7's `useSwatchClipboard()`); every copy in the feature goes through it and reports through ActionFeedback.

defects.defect: Half the component's prop/emit surface is pure conduit: 4 of 8 props and 5 of 8 emits exist only to relay SwatchHoverMenu's own contract through a level that never reads them, because the popover state is owned two levels above its only consumer.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:75-95. Conduit props: `openPopoverIndex`, `canHover`, `floatingStyle`, `swatchClass` (forwarded verbatim at :29-32). Conduit emits: `hover`, `leave`, `cancelLeave`, `swatchClick`, `popoverTouch`. State owner: PaletteCard.vue:246-255 `useHoverPopover()`; the only reason it is hoisted is PaletteCard.vue:277 `onBeforeCollapse: () => { openPopoverIndex.value = null; }`.
defects.mechanism: State hoisted for one incidental need (closing at the START of the collapse rather than at unmount) drags nine members of API surface through an intermediate component. The component is v-if-mounted at PaletteCard.vue:139, so unmount already closes the popover.
defects.reproduction: NONE (no failure). Static: count the props/emits that appear only inside the `<SwatchHoverMenu>` binding block.
defects.proposedCure: Fold `useHoverPopover` into SwatchHoverMenu (or, under M-2, delete it with the Popover adoption) and expose `close()` via defineExpose for the collapse hook; the leaf then takes one model prop and one action emit (M-3), dropping to ~40 lines.

defects.defect: Sibling components in the same cluster consuming the same data disagree on both array variance and the Vue 3.5 props idiom.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:76 `colors: readonly PaletteColor[]` vs PaletteColorStrip.vue `colors: PaletteColor[]` — both receive `palette.colors` from PaletteCard.vue:34 and :141. Idiom: PaletteColorStrip.vue and CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:196 use reactive props destructure; PaletteCardSwatches.vue:75 uses bare `defineProps<…>()`.
defects.mechanism: No cluster-level convention; each file was authored under a different wave's idiom. Harmless in a template-only component, but edict 7 names the idiom and the cluster is inconsistent.
defects.reproduction: NONE. Static: compare the two prop declarations.
defects.proposedCure: One convention per cluster: `readonly` on all display inputs, reactive destructure everywhere (it is the house idiom in two of three siblings already).

defects.defect: This component was never rendered in any of the 60 visual-audit captures: the matrix ran against an unreachable API and an empty local store, so no PaletteCard was ever expanded. The green rows for /#/palettes and /#/browse say nothing about PaletteCardSwatches.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png shows 'The commons is unreachable. / Failed to load palettes' and 'No saved palettes yet.' REPORT.md:120-121,135-136,150-151,165-166 record 0 pageErrors / 0 consoleErrors / 0 horizontalOverflow for these routes. The `smallTapTargets: 8` on /#/palettes therefore comes from collapsed chrome only; this component's 28px and 40px targets are additive.
defects.mechanism: A capture matrix run without seeded fixture data produces green rows for components that never mounted — a false negative that reads as coverage.
defects.reproduction: Open the four browse.png / palettes.png captures: no expanded card, no swatch row, no slug chip in any of them. (A sibling seat's shot-browse-desktop-light-expanded.png in this directory does show the component, with the slug chip and five inert dots.)
defects.proposedCure: Seed the API + localStorage fixture and drive one expand before capture, so every route's interactive sub-state is photographed; otherwise mark such rows NOT-COVERED rather than green.

defects.defect: The demo's core palette colour datum is an unvalidated `string` that never passes through value.js. The card path — API → PaletteCard → PaletteCardSwatches → WatercolorDot → `background-color` — consults the published library zero times, so the demo is not a proof of the public API for its own central concept.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/types.ts:1-12 `PaletteColor { css: string; … }`. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/value.js" demo/palettes/ | wc -l` → 2 (mix.ts:14 `@mkbabb/value.js/color`, export/png.ts:11 `@mkbabb/value.js/color`). PaletteCardSwatches imports nothing from value.js; the string reaches glass-ui's WatercolorDot (`color: string` — 'painted straight onto the swatch background', per its d.ts) unparsed.
defects.mechanism: Under-consumption of the published surface rather than a boundary violation. An invalid `css` from the wire is indistinguishable from a valid one until a browser paints nothing; the library's `Result` failure discipline is bypassed for the datum the whole application is about.
defects.reproduction: NONE as a user-visible failure today (this is the structural observation the challenge asked for, labelled a hypothesis about future breakage).
defects.proposedCure: `PaletteColor` becomes `{ color: Color<"oklch">; css: string; position: number; weight?: number }`, parsed once at the API boundary with `parseCssColor` + the library's Result discipline. `useSafeAccentFn` then receives a real colour instead of re-parsing, the strip's weight maths and export/png.ts stop being the only two consultations, and the demo becomes an actual dogfood proof of the published surface.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardSwatches.vue (area: palettes)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — declared, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: C-2 — the hover action panel names a CSS class (`.floating-panel`) that does not exist in @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 or anywhere in the repo, so it renders with `position: static` as the last child of <body>: measured rect {x:-720, y:900, w:1440, h:40} in a 1440x900 viewport, background rgba(0,0,0,0), boxShadow none, borderWidth 0px, zIndex auto — entirely off-screen and invisible — while silently adding 40px of scroll height (docScrollH 940 vs winH 900). Combined with C-1 (the swatch itself is an inert aria-hidden span with pointer-events:none, so the touch Popover path is dead too), the component's entire reason to exist — the swatch action menu — is non-functional on every interaction path in the shipping demo.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Negatively confirmed sub-claims, for the record: no defineModel anywhere in the component or its composables, so no stale-read hazard; no oklch→HSV/stableHue involvement; no ValueUnit wrapping; no reka-ui slider pointer capture; no requestAnimationFrame in the component or in useHoverPopover/useLeaveTimer — the only rAF in the subtree is glass-ui WatercolorDot's, which is `pauseWhenHidden:!0, respectReducedMotion:!0` and `animate` defaults false, so not a PRM-RAF site; no WebGL; `e.currentTarget` read inside nextTick does NOT null out under real Chromium pointer input — measured inline style `top:537.625px; left:884px` is exactly rect.top-42 / rect.left+w/2 for wrapper {x:864,y:579.625,w:40}, pageErrors 0; verbatimModuleSyntax is satisfied — `import type { PaletteColor }` at line 72.)

defects.defect: Every swatch is an inert, nameless, AT-hidden <span>: SwatchHoverMenu passes `tag="button"`, `:aria-label`, `@click.stop` and a reka-ui `PopoverTrigger as-child` binding to glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which declares no `tag` prop, sets `inheritAttrs:false`, consumes only attrs.class/attrs.style, and hardcodes `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`. All handlers and labels are silently dropped; the dot is removed from hit-testing.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:13-20 and :29-36 (the two WatercolorDot call sites). Producer: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js — `c({inheritAttrs:!1, __name:"WatercolorDot", props:{color:{},variant:{...},animate:{...},cycleDuration:{...},range:{...},seed:{...}}, setup(e){let n=h(),c=i(()=>n.class),f=i(()=>n.style); ... return o("span",{"aria-hidden":"true",class:l([c.value,"watercolor-swatch",...]),style:u([f.value,{...,pointerEvents:"none",...}])})})`. Measured (chalC-swatches-5.mjs): DOTS [{"tag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"pointerEvents":"none","w":40,"h":40,"parentCls":"relative"} x5]. Hit test (chalC-swatches-9.mjs): HIT_TEST_AT_SWATCH_CENTER {"tag":"DIV","cls":"relative"}. Touch (chalC-swatches-6.mjs, 390x844 hasTouch): HOVER_MQ false; AFTER_TAP {"popoverContent":0,"floatingPanel":false,"cardH":185}. Registered as P051 at docs/tranches/V/coordination/CONSTELLATION.md:26 and :50 (palette consumer migration scheduled W19-W22/W25-W27, producer cut ALREADY shipped in glass-ui 7.0.0).
defects.mechanism: producer contract abrogated (P051 `tag`/button-host branch removed) while the consumer still passes the abrogated props; inheritAttrs:false makes the breakage silent — no warning, no type error, no runtime throw
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/chalC-swatches-6.mjs — seeds localStorage["color-palettes"], loads http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844 hasTouch, expands the card, taps a swatch: no popover, no panel, card height unchanged. Desktop equivalent: chalC-swatches-5.mjs.
defects.proposedCure: Give the operable face a NAMED GEOMETRIC SEAT, exactly as P051 requires: wrap WatercolorDot inside a real <button> (or the glass-ui `Button` atom, icon-only variant="ghost") that carries the aria-label and the PopoverTrigger as-child binding; the dot becomes the noninteractive face it now is. Do not re-add a `tag` prop to the producer.

defects.defect: The desktop hover action panel depends on a `.floating-panel` CSS class that has no rule in @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 nor anywhere in this repo. Without `position: fixed` the inline top/left are inert, so the panel renders unpositioned and unstyled as the last child of <body>, off-screen, and grows the document by 40px while open.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37-51 (Teleport to body + class="floating-panel" + :style=floatingStyle). CSSOM walk over every loaded sheet (chalC-swatches-1.mjs): CSS_PROBE {"sheetCount":40,"hits":[]}. Live element while hovering swatch #2 (chalC-swatches-5.mjs): PANEL {"parentTag":"BODY","isLastChildOfBody":true,"inlineStyle":"top: 537.625px; left: 884px; transform: translateX(-50%);","position":"static","zIndex":"auto","background":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","backdrop":"none","borderWidth":"0px","boxShadow":"none","rect":{"x":-720,"y":900,"w":1440,"h":40},"docScrollH":940,"winH":900,"buttons":[{"label":"Edit color rgb(0 128 255 / 0.5)","x":-714},{"label":"Copy color rgb(0 128 255 / 0.5)","x":-682}]}. Producer absence: `grep -rn "floating-panel" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui` -> zero selector hits (only --glass-*-floating tokens). Repo absence: `grep -rn "floating-panel" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .` -> SwatchHoverMenu.vue:42 (sole consumer) + stale prose in demo/styles/animations.css:2 and tranche A/S docs. Historical proof the class once existed: docs/tranches/A/research/Ad-interactive-states.md:135-136 cites `glass-ui/src/styles/floating-panel.css`. Screenshots taken WHILE the panel is open show nothing: <scratchpad>/chalC-hover.png, chalC-hover-full.png.
defects.mechanism: positioning + surface outsourced to a producer utility class with no compile-time or runtime binding; the Glass 7 adoption (W44) dropped the class and nothing verified it — unbooked debt, unlike C-1 this loss is registered nowhere in docs/tranches/V/
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/chalC-swatches-5.mjs — seeds a local palette, loads http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, expands the card, moves the real mouse over swatch #2, then reads getComputedStyle + getBoundingClientRect of `.floating-panel`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-rolled hover branch entirely (SwatchHoverMenu.vue:27-52 + useHoverPopover.ts + useLeaveTimer.ts + the floatingStyle/canHover/openPopoverIndex prop-emit chain through PaletteCardSwatches.vue:29-37 and PaletteCard.vue:246-255) and keep ONE reka-ui Popover for both pointer classes — reka-ui/floating-ui owns positioning, collision flip, scroll tracking, focus management, Escape and dismissal. Do NOT cure by re-adding a local `.floating-panel` block: that re-forks a producer utility into the consumer (edict 4) and leaves C-1/C-3/C-5/C-7 standing.

defects.defect: The swatch actions are keyboard- and AT-unreachable, and the hover panel declares aria-hidden="true" while containing two focusable buttons (axe `aria-hidden-focus`), teleported to the end of <body> so focus order is broken.
defects.evidence: Tabbable census of the expanded card (chalC-swatches-4.mjs, selector a[href],button:not([disabled]),input,select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex='-1'])): the only tabbable descendant of [role="article"] is {"tag":"BUTTON","label":"Palette menu"} — zero swatch seats. PANEL measurement: {"ariaHidden":"true","buttons":[{"label":"Edit color …"},{"label":"Copy color …"}]}. Source comment SwatchHoverMenu.vue:38-39 names the reka-ui Popover as "the accessible route", but useHoverPopover.ts:11-14 makes canHover true on every desktop, so `v-if="!canHover"` (line 9) never renders it. No Escape handler, no focus trap, no focus restoration in SwatchHoverMenu.vue or useHoverPopover.ts.
defects.mechanism: an aria-hidden decorative layer used as the primary interactive surface; the declared accessible fallback is v-if'd off for exactly the population that needs it
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/chalC-swatches-4.mjs (tabbable census) and chalC-swatches-5.mjs (panel aria-hidden + focusable children).
defects.proposedCure: Same single transposition as C-2: one reka-ui Popover with a real focusable named seat as trigger. reka-ui supplies aria-expanded, focus management, Escape and dismissal; the aria-hidden hand-rolled layer ceases to exist.

defects.defect: The copy-slug icon button is a 16x16 CSS-px tap target — below the WCAG 2.5.8 AA 24x24 minimum — and it is invisible to the megatranche visual audit because no palette card ever rendered in any capture.

Measured on /#/browse with the palette API stubbed (chalC-swatches-7.mjs, page.route("**/palettes**")): OFFSITE_REQS ["GET http://localhost:3000/palettes?limit=50&sort=newest", …]; BROWSE_CARD_COUNT 1; SLUG_COPY_BTN {"present":true,"label":"Copy slug aVeryLongUserSlugName","w":16,"h":16}. The ratified cure already exists one file up: PaletteCard.vue:93-104 uses <Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm"> with the comment "the sm square also cures the ~24px touch target" — measured 36x36 in the same probe.

defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/chalC-swatches-7.mjs — intercepts **/palettes** with a stub payload, loads http://localhost:9000/#/browse, expands the card, measures the button whose aria-label starts with "Copy slug".
defects.proposedCure: Replace all four hand-rolled icon buttons (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:13, :41, :49, :56) with the glass-ui `Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm"` atom already used at PaletteCard.vue:96-104 — the p-0.5/p-1.5 fork disappears with them.

defects.defect: False press affordance: pressing a swatch drives the card's liquid-press spring to 97% completion and squashes the card 8px, then releases with no effect at all — the interface teaches the user the click registered when nothing happened.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:2 stops CLICK only (`<div @click.stop class="overflow-hidden">`) while PaletteCard.vue:24 binds `v-bind="press.handlers"` (useLiquidPress, pointer-level). Measured (chalC-swatches-9.mjs, pointer down/up over swatch #1): IDLE {"pressT":"0.0000","h":172} -> PRESS_ON_SWATCH {"pressT":"0.9741","h":164} -> AFTER_CLICK_ON_SWATCH {"pressT":"0.0000","h":172}.

defects.proposedCure: A real focusable seat (C-1 cure) consumes the pointer, so the card press no longer fires beneath it; no additional event plumbing needed.

defects.defect: Four hand-rolled icon-button recipes in a 96-line file instead of the glass-ui Button atom — violating owner edicts 4 (glass-ui is the design system) and 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides) — and the per-instance fork is the direct cause of C-4's 16px target.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardSwatches.vue:14, :44, :51, :58 all carry the identical string `p-1.5 rounded-sm hover:bg-accent active:scale-95 active:bg-accent/70 transition-colors cursor-pointer focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40` (line 14 differs only by p-0.5 + shrink-0). The repo's own precedent retired exactly this recipe one directory up: PaletteCard.vue:93-104, "S.W5-4: 3rd copy of the hand-rolled icon-trigger recipe dies onto the glass-ui atom".
defects.mechanism: design-system bypass; a copied class string cannot carry the atom's invariants (touch-target floor, focus ring, tone), so each copy drifts independently
defects.reproduction: grep -n "p-1.5 rounded-sm hover:bg-accent" demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardSwatches.vue -> lines 44, 51, 58; line 14 is the p-0.5 variant.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt <Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm"> from glass-ui at all four sites (the S.W5-4 pattern), deleting every local class-string copy.

defects.defect: A dual path (owner edict 2 forbids dual paths): a reka-ui Popover branch and a hand-rolled Teleport branch implement the same affordance, selected by v-if="!canHover"/v-else. One is accessible and collision-aware, the other is aria-hidden and hand-positioned — and the branch that ships to every desktop is the broken one, which is exactly why C-2 went unnoticed.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:8-25 (Popover branch) vs :28-52 (Teleport branch); the file admits the hazard at :64-66 — `/** Shared panel layout — applied to both PopoverContent and the hover Teleport panel so the two paths cannot drift. */ const PANEL_LAYOUT = "p-1.5 flex items-center gap-1";`. A shared layout constant cannot prevent SEMANTIC drift, and semantic drift is what happened. Measured consequence: the accessible branch never renders on desktop (HOVER_MQ true), so no a11y gate, e2e spec, or visual capture ever exercised it.
defects.mechanism: branch-per-input-modality instead of one modality-agnostic primitive; the untested branch rots silently
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/chalC-swatches-5.mjs (desktop -> Teleport branch, aria-hidden, static) vs chalC-swatches-6.mjs (touch -> Popover branch, HOVER_MQ false, popoverContent 0).
defects.proposedCure: One reka-ui Popover for both pointer classes; delete the v-else Teleport branch, useHoverPopover.ts, useLeaveTimer.ts and the canHover plumbing. reka-ui already handles hover-vs-touch activation on a single trigger.

defects.defect: Clipboard actions are silent on both success and failure: the `{ok, reason}` result of glass-ui's writeClipboard is discarded, so a denied permission, an insecure context, or a missing Clipboard API produces zero user feedback — and there is no aria-live/role=status announcement even on success.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardSwatches.vue:16 — `@click="writeClipboard(displaySlug)"` (result discarded); demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:333 — `void writeClipboard(css)`. Producer contract (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js): `async function r(e){ if(typeof navigator>"u"||!navigator.clipboard?.writeText) return {ok:!1,reason:"no-api"}; try{ return await navigator.clipboard.writeText(e), {ok:!0}; } catch(e){ console.warn("[useClipboard] clipboard writeText rejected:",e); return {ok:!1,reason:"clipboard-api"}; } }` — it never throws, so ignoring the return value is the ONLY way to lose the failure. The machinery already exists unused: ActionFeedback is mounted at PaletteCard.vue:123-128 and showFeedback is exposed at :244 (consumed by BrowsePane.vue:230,239,249,264 and PalettesPane.vue:207 for save/publish).
defects.mechanism: a Result-returning (non-throwing) producer API consumed as if it were fire-and-forget; the error channel is discarded at the call site
defects.reproduction: Source + producer-API read (both quoted above). Runtime demonstration is blocked upstream by C-1/C-2 — the copy buttons cannot currently be activated by any user.
defects.proposedCure: `const r = await writeClipboard(css); showFeedback(r.ok ? "Copied" : "Copy failed", r.ok ? "success" : "error")` through the existing ActionFeedback, and give that chip role="status" (WCAG 4.1.3).

defects.defect: useLeaveTimer leaks its pending timeout across component unmount — no onScopeDispose/onUnmounted, so a scheduled 250ms callback fires against a disposed scope.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useLeaveTimer.ts:1-17 — the whole module is `let timer; function schedule(cb){cancel(); timer=setTimeout(cb, delay);} function cancel(){...} return {schedule, cancel}` with no lifecycle hook. Scheduled at useHoverPopover.ts:33-36 (`leaveTimer.schedule(() => { openIndex.value = null; })`).
defects.mechanism: composable owns a timer resource but not its disposal; the owning scope's teardown does not reach it
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis. The callback body is a benign ref write today, so the leak is latent rather than a live crash; unmount inside the 250ms window (route change, filter keystroke, delete, filteredSaved re-render) is the triggering path.
defects.proposedCure: Add `onScopeDispose(cancel)` in useLeaveTimer — or delete the composable entirely, which the C-2/C-7 cure does anyway (reka-ui owns the open/close timing).

defects.defect: The floating panel's position is computed once at hover time and never corrected: no scroll listener, no resize listener, no ResizeObserver, no viewport clamp, no collision flip, and a hardcoded `offsetY = -42` guess at the panel's own height (measured 40px).
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:20-31 — `function positionPanel(swatchEl, offsetY = -42){ const rect = swatchEl.getBoundingClientRect(); style.top = `${rect.top + offsetY}px`; style.left = `${rect.left + rect.width/2}px`; }` called only from onHover via nextTick. A swatch within 42px of the viewport top yields a negative `top`; swatches near either edge overflow horizontally with no flip.
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled positioning without a positioning engine; a one-shot measurement in a scrollable, resizable world
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis; currently MASKED by C-2 (position:static makes the offsets inert). I attempted to demonstrate scroll detachment by injecting `.floating-panel{position:fixed}` and scrolling: the attempt was invalid because the app scrolls an inner container, not the window (chalC-swatches-7.mjs -> SCROLL_DETACH afterScroll.scrollY 0 after window.scrollBy(0,120)).

defects.defect: One swatch hover re-renders every swatch: the template spreads the SHARED reactive position cell inside the v-for, coupling all N SwatchHoverMenu children to one child's position, and it re-allocates the constant `transform: translateX(-50%)` into a fresh object per swatch per render.

result.strongestDefect: D-3 — the commit has no state and the measured outcome contradicts the promise. `onRespond` (MigratePalettesDialog.vue:69-72) sets `open.value = false` BEFORE emitting, demolishing the surface before the operation begins, so there is nowhere to render pending, partial or failed. Driven live against an UP backend with 12 seeded palettes, clicking the primary "Publish, then regenerate" produced: 0 of 12 palettes published (`"network": []`), `palette-user-slug` wiped to `null` by 101 ms and still null at 8 s, `aria-busy` 0 / spinners 0 / no operation status at any sample, and one console warning — `Migration action failed: Backend unreachable — working locally.` — as the sole report. The user picked the option whose entire purpose is "don't lose my work" and lost their account handle in silence. Compounding it, the journey has no error surface at all: the only authored one, `slugBarRef.setError`, is permanently null because `PaletteSlugBar` is never mounted anywhere in the app. This is the direct target of VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-08. It is strongest because it is the one defect that damages the user rather than merely misrepresenting the design — and because D-1 (no visual hierarchy) and D-2 (false premise) mean the user was steered into it by a button that looked exactly like the two alternatives.
result.negativeProof: N/A — the verdict is DEFECTIVE (3 BLOCKER, 6 MAJOR, 4 MINOR, 2 INFO). For completeness, the axes I probed and found genuinely clean, so the formation does not re-open them: (1) Vue 3.5 idioms (edict 7) — reactive props destructure at :60, defineModel at :58, no stale-read hazard, no useTemplateRef needed; (2) verbatimModuleSyntax (edict 8) — no type-only value imports in the file; (3) motion (edict 6) — nothing deleted, nothing hand-rolled, geometry resolves directly under prefers-reduced-motion (measured animationName "none", transform/scale/translate "none"); (4) no god module — the file is 97 lines with one job; (5) no code back-compat shim — despite the "Migrate*" name there is no version bridge, alias, dual serializer path or masking fallback, so `feedback_no_backwards_compat` is not violated in the literal sense; (6) count boundaries — 1 / 3 / 12 / 137 all render correct copy with no overflow or truncation, and horizontal overflow is 0 at every viewport probed (320, 390, 720@2x, 1440). The seat's framed question resolves as: NEITHER a legacy shim NOR a legitimate data operation — it is a fabricated data-safety ceremony around one real verb (bulk publish) misfiled into the identity flow, and the disposition is RETIRE + re-home, not repair.

defects.defect: prefers-reduced-motion is unhandled for this component's expand/collapse: the 350ms height+opacity transition runs at full duration under PRM, the animated property is layout-forcing `height`, and an un-gated smooth `scrollIntoView` fires on completion.
