Separately the four action buttons carry `active:scale-95` under `transition-colors` (`PaletteCardSwatches.vue:14,44,51,58`), which excludes `transform` — the press is an un-eased jump-cut while the parent card runs a real spring (`useLiquidPress`, `PaletteCard.vue:263-267`).

Radius drift: ApiOfflineChip.vue:50,:60,:77 use bare `var(--radius-pill)` while DockStatusLamp.vue:57,:83 use `var(--radius-pill, 9999px)`; --radius-pill measured present ("9999px").
defects.mechanism: Masking fallback (owner edict 2) — a second, drifting, hardcoded definition of a token that exists, hidden inside a var() default.
defects.reproduction: Playwright page.evaluate: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--destructive') → "light-dark(hsl(0 72% 50%), hsl(0 80% 60%))"; and .getPropertyValue('--radius-pill') → "9999px". Both tokens resolve, so every fallback in the cited lines is unreachable code.
defects.proposedCure: These lines die with L-1 (all sit inside .api-misconfig-chip / .misconfig-dot). For the surviving `unavailable` face, use bare var() with no fallback throughout, and settle one spelling across the codebase. Enforce structurally if desired: a stylelint rule banning var() fallbacks on tokens the theme defines.

defects.defect: The design system already ships the exact primitives both twins hand-roll: glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes ./status-dot, ./chip, ./badge and ./pulse, and StatusDot's state union is a near-isomorphism of ApiAvailability. The demo re-derives them twice in scoped CSS.
defects.evidence: `node -e "...require('@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json')..."` → glass-ui 7.0.0, exports include `./badge ./chip ./status-dot ./pulse`. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/feedback.d.ts: `export declare const STATUS_DOT_STATES: readonly ["online", "warning", "error", "unknown"];`. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/status-dot/StatusDot.vue.d.ts props: `{ state?: StatusDotState; size?: FeedbackSize; label?: string; class?: HTMLAttributes["class"] }`. Hand-rolled equivalents: ApiOfflineChip.vue:57-64 and :74-79 (the dot), :41-55 (the pill), :81-89 (the pulse); DockStatusLamp.vue:79-86, :104-107, :43-62, :109-122. ApiAvailability union at availability.ts:40-44 ("unknown"|"available"|"unavailable"|"misconfigured") vs STATUS_DOT_STATES ("online"|"warning"|"error"|"unknown").
defects.mechanism: Design-system bypass (owner edict 4): a variant/primitive re-implemented in demo scoped CSS when the producer already exports it under the exact existing component-type name.
defects.reproduction: NONE required — the published subpaths and the .d.ts prop surfaces are pasted above from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/.
defects.proposedCure: Consume `StatusDot` from @mkbabb/glass-ui/status-dot inside a glass-ui `Chip`; delete the scoped pill/dot CSS from both twins. Animations are NOT deleted (edict 6): `offline-dot-pulse` moves into the glass-ui StatusDot primitive, or is tokenized into demo/styles/animations.css if it stays demo-side. The keyframe is census-tracked (docs/tranches/T/audit/w1-pr7-keyframes-census.md:58 row 17) and ApiOfflineChip.vue:81 is one of the 6 conforming prefers-reduced-motion blocks (excavation/DESIGN-CANON-BRIEF.md:88) — the PRM idiom must survive the move intact.

defects.defect: `initApiEnvironment(BASE_URL)` runs as a top-level module side effect, so importing the transport for any reason mutates global app state and emits a console error; the "guaranteed visible at first paint" justification for the T-9 re-home rests on chunk-eval order, not on shell structure.
defects.evidence: demo/platform/transport/client.ts:38-45 — `export const BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL ?? DEFAULT_REMOTE_API_URL;` followed immediately by a bare top-level `initApiEnvironment(BASE_URL);`. That function writes `apiAvailability.value = "misconfigured"` (availability.ts:161) and calls `console.error` (availability.ts:163). The first-paint claim it is supposed to underwrite: DockStatusLamp.vue:2-6 ("guaranteed visible the moment the shell paints") and status-lamp.ts:20-25. The app-root provider that would be the honest seat already exists and is already called: demo/color-picker/App.vue:189 `import { provideApiClient } from "../platform/transport/useApiClient";`.
defects.mechanism: Import-for-effect: initialization performed at module evaluation rather than by an explicit call from the composition root, making the effect ordering-dependent and untestable without module-registry surgery.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is labelled a HYPOTHESIS on its timing consequence. The structural fact (side effect at client.ts:45) is read directly from source and is not in doubt; the first-paint hole is NOT proven — my successful :9137 probe included a 3000ms settle, so I have no clean first-paint timing measurement and do not assert one. Measure before asserting.
defects.proposedCure: Make initialization explicit: `provideApiClient()` at demo/color-picker/App.vue:189 calls `initApiEnvironment(BASE_URL)` as its first act; delete the top-level invocation at client.ts:45. Imports stop having effects, the effect becomes trivially testable, and the paint-order question becomes answerable by construction.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, component ApiOfflineChip.vue (demo/palettes/browser/status/)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — model id claude-opus-5[1m]; the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with, declared not inherited.

defects.defect: The owner-ordered-dead `dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`` surface has a SECOND live seat in this component, byte-identical to the dock lamp's. OM-5/MT-F031 is not discharged by killing DockStatusLamp alone. The component's own barrel comment documents the death that never happened.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:11-18 (v-if="misconfigured" → the literal string) vs demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:50-55 (label: "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`", role: "alert"). demo/palettes/browser/status/index.ts:3-6 verbatim: "DevMisconfigBanner DIED at T.W6 · W6-6 (T-9, owner order): the misconfigured-state affordance re-homed as the dock status lamp". Live probe at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with the latch forced to "misconfigured": lamps=[{cls:"dock-status-lamp fira-code", role:"alert", variant:"misconfigured", text:"dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`", rect:{x:1177,y:33,w:247,h:23}}] — that geometry/ink is the OM-5 witness crop. Isolated mount of ApiOfflineChip against the app's own module graph, state="misconfigured": {rendered:true, role:"alert", cls:"api-offline-chip api-misconfig-chip fira-code", text:"dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`", w:252, h:23}.
defects.mechanism: Duplicated surface / dead-code resurrection: the T.W6 re-home cloned the affordance into a dock seat and deleted the banner, but never deleted the per-surface copy. Two components, two areas, one latch, one string.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED. Playwright against the live dev server: (1) navigate http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; (2) `const m = await import('/@fs/.../demo/platform/transport/availability.ts'); m.apiAvailability.value='misconfigured'` → `.dock-status-lamp` renders the string (OM-5 witness identified). (3) Mount ApiOfflineChip in isolation with provideApiClient() and drive apiAvailability through all four states → the chip renders the identical string at state "misconfigured". Both halves measured; the two v-ifs read the same Ref and neither excludes the other, so with a staged colour the string appears twice on screen.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the misconfigured register from this SFC entirely — template lines 11-18, the `misconfigured` computed (:37), `.api-misconfig-chip` (:68-72), `.misconfig-dot` (:74-79), and the :8-10 comment. Under MT-F031 the dock seat dies too. The dev diagnosis already lives where the owner ruled it belongs: availability.ts:163 `console.error("[value.js] …")`. What survives here is one honest state: `unavailable`.

defects.defect: The chip's dev-only message is NOT dev-gated, while its sibling implementing the same state IS. A production bundle served from a loopback host renders "run `npm run dev`" at the user; the dock lamp correctly goes dark in the same build.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:48 `if (!isDev) return null; // dev-gated — the lamp ships dark in production` and DockStatusLamp.vue:31 `const isDev = import.meta.env.DEV;`. ApiOfflineChip.vue:37 has no gate; its only imports are `computed` and `useApiClient`. Live measurement of the predicate that decides the state: {availability:"available", BASE_URL:"http://localhost:3000", origin:"http://localhost:9000", detect:true} where detect = detectDevMisconfig({viteApiUrlSet:false, baseUrl:BASE_URL, pageOrigin, pageHostname}). test/status-lamp.test.ts:106 independently asserts true for pageOrigin http://localhost:9000 + baseUrl https://api.color.babb.dev, which is exactly what client.ts:36-37 resolves to when VITE_API_URL is unset. `sed 's/=.*//' .env` → only CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, no VITE_API_URL; scripts/dev/dev.sh:287 `export VITE_API_URL="http://localhost:${BACKEND_PORT}"` is the only thing setting it, so `npm run dev:web-only` (package.json → `vite --port 9000`), a bare `npx vite`, or a CI build all leave it unset.
defects.mechanism: detectDevMisconfig (availability.ts:112-116) keys on loopback PAGE HOSTNAME, not on DEV BUILD. The two seats therefore diverge in any production artefact served from localhost: import.meta.env.DEV is false (lamp → null) while apiAvailability is "misconfigured" (chip → renders).
defects.reproduction: PARTIAL — the predicate half is EXECUTED and measured (detect:true, above; plus the closed-form assertion at test/status-lamp.test.ts:106). The build half is DERIVED, deliberately not run because a build writes dist/ outside my write scope: `VITE_API_URL= npm run build && npx vite preview --port 4173` from a checkout with no VITE_API_URL, open http://localhost:4173 → DEV false ⇒ lamp null; misconfigured computed true ⇒ chip renders the dev instruction in a production bundle.
defects.proposedCure: Moot once C-1 lands. If the branch were kept, the dev gate would have to be duplicated into a second component — which is the argument for deleting the branch, not for copying `import.meta.env.DEV` around.

defects.defect: The honest degraded-backend affordance is gated on unrelated application state: it only exists when the staging palette is non-empty, so it is invisible in exactly the state preceding a first save.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:116 `<ApiOfflineChip v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0" class="self-start" />`. Measured live at #/palettes with localStorage["color-picker"] = {"inputColor":"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)","savedColors":[]} and the latch forced to "misconfigured": chips: [] (component absent from the DOM) while lamps: [ …one lamp… ]. The repo names this exact failure as the reason for the re-home: DockStatusLamp.vue:4-7 "never inside a collapsible layer, never gated on a palette save, so the `misconfigured` state is guaranteed visible the moment the shell paints"; e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:55-57 asserts it — for the lamp only.
defects.mechanism: Parent v-if ANDs with the component's own self-gating v-if. A status region that is only sometimes mounted cannot carry a visibility guarantee.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED. Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/palettes (persisted savedColors []), force apiAvailability='misconfigured', evaluate document.querySelectorAll('.api-offline-chip').length → 0, while document.querySelectorAll('.dock-status-lamp').length → 1.
defects.proposedCure: Transport state is a property of the transport, not of the palette well. Either drop the v-if at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:116 (the chip's own v-if already self-gates — its :5-6 comment says so) or accept the dock seat as the single truth and delete the chip. Do not keep a sometimes-mounted status region.

defects.defect: `white-space: nowrap` with no label-fold breaks WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text 200%) and 1.4.10 (Reflow at 320 CSS px). The sibling lamp has explicit relief for the same string; this component has none.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:54 `white-space: nowrap;`. DockStatusLamp.vue:67-74 `.lamp-label { display: none; } @media (min-width:1024px){ .lamp-label { display: inline; } }`. Measured with the chip mounted inside a `width:320px; overflow:hidden` container: at root font-size 16px → scrollWidth 210px both states, no overflow; at root font-size 32px (the 200% text-resize case) → unavailable 427px, misconfigured 508px, BOTH overflow 320px (overflowsAt320: true).
defects.mechanism: Every dimension is rem/em-derived (font-size var(--type-mono-caption, 0.6875rem), padding 0.3rem 0.7rem, letter-spacing 0.06em) so the box scales 1:1 with user text size, while nowrap forbids the only escape — forcing two-dimensional scrolling.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED. Playwright: mount ApiOfflineChip inside a fixed 320px overflow:hidden div, set document.documentElement.style.fontSize='32px', read chip.scrollWidth per state → 427 (unavailable) / 508 (misconfigured) vs a 320px container.
defects.proposedCure: Drop `white-space: nowrap` (:54). The label is a sentence, not a token; a wrapped two-line chip in a flex-wrap well is correct. If one line is a hard requirement it belongs to a container query on the well, never to an unconditional nowrap.

defects.defect: VACUOUS GATE: the component has zero test coverage, and the one e2e assertion that claims to prevent this surface's resurrection watches a CSS class that exists nowhere in the product.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "ApiOfflineChip\|api-offline-chip\|api-misconfig-chip\|offline-dot\|misconfig-dot" test/ e2e/` → NO OUTPUT. `grep -rln "backend offline — saved locally" demo/ test/ e2e/ src/` → demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts, demo/platform/transport/availability.ts, demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue, test/status-lamp.test.ts (the last matches only because it asserts the resolver's label at :68, over resolveLampState from demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts — a different module). `grep -rn "dev-misconfig-banner" demo/ src/ e2e/ test/` → only e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:13 and :37 `await expect(page.locator(".dev-misconfig-banner")).toHaveCount(0);` — the selector exists in NO source file; it was deleted with the banner component it belonged to.
defects.mechanism: No test imports the SFC, so no mutation of it can fail a gate. The lone negative watch asserts the absence of a corpse while the live resurrection wears a different class (.api-misconfig-chip, ApiOfflineChip.vue:14) and walks past it — an assertion whose subject cannot exist is 0===0.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (the greps above). The exact green-keeping mutation: delete ApiOfflineChip.vue:11-18 and :37 (the whole misconfigured branch), OR change :36 to `availability.value === "available"` (inverting the semantic so the chip claims "backend offline" while the backend is up). Then `vitest run` green (nothing imports the file), `vue-tsc` green (no type changes), `eslint` green, `playwright test` green (o22 asserts .dock-status-lamp and .dev-misconfig-banner, never .api-offline-chip).
defects.proposedCure: One component test over the measured four-state matrix (mount with a stubbed API_CLIENT_KEY provider; assert rendered/not, role, and text per ApiAvailability member) — the same closed-form discipline test/status-lamp.test.ts:51-86 already applies to the lamp. Retarget the e2e negative watch from the dead `.dev-misconfig-banner` to the live `.api-misconfig-chip`, and post-MT-F031 to `.dock-status-lamp[data-variant="misconfigured"]`.

defects.defect: `--type-mono-caption` is a phantom token — referenced three times, defined zero times — so `font-size: var(--type-mono-caption, 0.6875rem)` is a hardcoded 11px wearing a token's clothes (a masking fallback, owner edict 2).
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "type-mono-caption" demo/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → three USE sites only (ComponentSliders.vue:310, DockStatusLamp.vue:54, ApiOfflineChip.vue:47); `grep -rno "--type-mono-caption\s*:" demo/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no output (no definition anywhere, including glass-ui's @theme blocks). Measured computed value on the live chip in both rendering states: fontSize: "11px" = 0.6875rem, i.e. the fallback, always. Independently observed by the design seat at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-componentsliders/challenge-D-design.md:382 (`ApiOfflineChip.vue:47 → 0.6875rem`).
defects.mechanism: A var() whose fallback is always taken: the literal is dressed as a token so it reads system-compliant, and because the token never resolves the CSS never fails loudly. Two files, three sites, one silent hardcode.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED. The two greps above, plus getComputedStyle(chip).fontSize === "11px" measured on the live isolated mount.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the real token (`var(--type-caption)`, defined in glass-ui's bridges.css) with no fallback, or mint `--type-mono-caption` once in glass-ui's typography theme and consume it bare.

defects.defect: The entire visual register — chip recipe, dot geometry, destructive face, and the pulse keyframes — is copy-pasted between this component and DockStatusLamp, including two identically-bodied keyframes under different names.
defects.evidence: ApiOfflineChip.vue:41-90 vs DockStatusLamp.vue:43-122: identical display/align-items/gap:.4rem/font-variant:small-caps/letter-spacing:.06em/font-size:var(--type-mono-caption,0.6875rem)/line-height:1/border-radius:var(--radius-pill)/border:1px solid var(--card-edge)/color:color-mix(in oklab,var(--foreground) 72%,transparent)/background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--background) 55%,transparent)/white-space:nowrap; identical dot geometry (.4rem, 1.5px solid currentColor); identical destructive recipe (55% border, 12% fill). Keyframes: `offline-dot-pulse` (ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-85) and `lamp-dot-pulse` (DockStatusLamp.vue:110-118), both `2.4s var(--ease-standard) infinite`, both `0%,100%{opacity:1} 50%{opacity:.35}`. Measured on the chip: animationName "offline-dot-pulse-cb533f05", 2.4s, cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1). DockStatusLamp.vue:41-42 even names the copy: "in the ApiOfflineChip's exact register … one status language, two seats".
defects.mechanism: The re-home cloned the register instead of extracting it. Every future ink change must be made twice or the two seats drift.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (side-by-side read at the cited line ranges + the measured computed animation on the live mount).
defects.proposedCure: One `.status-annotation` recipe in demo/styles/ — or, per edict 4, a glass-ui Badge/Chip variant, which is where a design-system register belongs — consumed by whichever seat survives MT-F031. Per edict 6 the keyframe is MOVED, never deleted: relocate `offline-dot-pulse` into demo/styles/animations.css under the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) idiom and retire the duplicate name.

defects.defect: `font-variant: small-caps` renders the literal shell command in small capitals — the user is shown `RUN `NPM RUN DEV`` , a case they must not type.
defects.evidence: ApiOfflineChip.vue:41-42 (`font-variant: small-caps; letter-spacing: 0.06em`) applied to a string containing a verbatim command at :17. The owner-marked witness renders the result: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-5-dev-misconfigured-banner.png reads "DEV MISCONFIGURED — RUN `NPM RUN DEV`".
defects.mechanism: A typographic register applied to a copy class it does not fit; a code literal inside prose needs a <code>-register escape from the parent's font-variant.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED (read the owner-marked witness image; confirmed the same register on the live isolated mount, text "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`" with font-variant small-caps in effect).
defects.proposedCure: Moot for the misconfigured branch, which dies under C-1. For the surviving `unavailable` string no literal is present and small-caps is correct — which is itself the argument that the misconfigured copy never belonged in this register.

defects.defect: `detectDevMisconfig`'s documented third conjunct ("a cross-origin resolved BASE_URL") is a tautology at its only call site, and it tests "different origin", not "production" — the tests exercise a matrix the app cannot produce.
defects.evidence: availability.ts:29-31 and :107-111 document the triad. Measured live: detectDevMisconfig({viteApiUrlSet:false, baseUrl:"http://localhost:3000", pageOrigin:"http://localhost:9000", pageHostname:"localhost"}) → true — and http://localhost:3000 is this repo's own local backend (scripts/dev/dev.sh:287), not "the production API". At the sole call site the inputs are not independent: availability.ts:151-158 builds viteApiUrlSet from import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL while client.ts:37 sets baseUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL ?? DEFAULT_REMOTE_API_URL, so viteApiUrlSet===false ⟹ baseUrl==="https://api.color.babb.dev" (client.ts:36), whose origin can never equal a loopback page origin ⟹ isCrossOrigin is always true whenever legs 1 and 2 pass. test/status-lamp.test.ts:98-119 varies each leg independently and passes.
defects.mechanism: A pure function written to be closed-form testable over inputs the production wiring cannot generate; the effective predicate is `!viteApiUrlSet && isLoopbackHost(hostname)`.
defects.reproduction: EXECUTED. Playwright evaluate importing the app's own availability.ts and client.ts via /@fs specifiers: {availability:"available", BASE_URL:"http://localhost:3000", origin:"http://localhost:9000", detect:true}.
defects.proposedCure: Out of scope for this file but it governs when this file renders: reduce the predicate to what it actually decides, or feed it the real independent input (the raw VITE_API_URL string) so the third leg can ever be false.

defects.defect: The `misconfigured` invariant is defended on only one side of the latch: markApiUnreachable() guards it, markApiReachable() does not.
defects.evidence: availability.ts:167-172 `markApiUnreachable()` opens with `if (apiAvailability.value === "misconfigured") return;` and the comment "A designed misconfig is NOT an unreachable backend — never mislabel it". availability.ts:175-179 `markApiReachable()` has no such guard: `if (apiAvailability.value !== "available") { apiAvailability.value = "available"; }`. `grep -rn "markApiReachable" demo/ test/` → the only product call site is client.ts:86, downstream of the assertApiAttemptAllowed() throw at client.ts:74, so the hole is unreachable today; test/status-lamp.test.ts:46 reaches it deliberately as an afterEach reset — exactly the shape a future caller would take.
defects.mechanism: Asymmetric invariant: the rule is stated in one transition's comment and never learned by its mirror. This component's misconfigured branch would silently vanish on any future direct markApiReachable() call.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis. Unreachable through the current product call graph; reachable only via a direct call, as the test's afterEach demonstrates.
defects.proposedCure: Guard both transitions, or make `misconfigured` terminal by construction — it is a boot-time configuration fact, not a runtime observation.

result.strongestDefect: C-1 (BLOCKER) — the owner-ordered-dead "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`" surface has a second, live seat at ApiOfflineChip.vue:11-18, byte-identical to the dock lamp's (status-lamp.ts:50-55). The component's own barrel (status/index.ts:3-6) records that this affordance "DIED at T.W6 · W6-6 (T-9, owner order)" and was re-homed — it is not dead, it is duplicated. I proved by live probe that the OM-5 witness is DockStatusLamp (measured lamp at x=1177,y=33,w=247,h=23 rendering the string; chip absent only because the audit's persisted savedColors is []), and that the chip renders the identical string the moment a colour is staged. MT-F031 is therefore NOT discharged by killing the dock lamp alone. Worse, the single gate that claims to prevent this resurrection — e2e o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:37, `expect(page.locator(".dev-misconfig-banner")).toHaveCount(0)` — watches a class name that exists in no source file, while the live resurrection wears `.api-misconfig-chip`.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded so they are not re-raised, each checked and killed as a live hypothesis from the brief's hazard list: (1) PRM idiom is CORRECT here — @keyframes offline-dot-pulse is declared inside the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) block (:81-89) together with the animation declaration, and var(--ease-standard) resolves (glass-ui scheme-spring.css → --motion-ease-standard), measured animationName "offline-dot-pulse-cb533f05" 2.4s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) — the declaration is not invalid-at-computed-value-time, the pulse does not silently die. (2) ZERO PRM-RAF exposure: no requestAnimationFrame, setInterval/setTimeout, addEventListener, observers, or WebGL anywhere in the file; the pulse is a composited CSS opacity animation; no cleanup surface therefore no leak class and no unmount race. (3) NONE of the six named local hazards apply: no defineModel (no props at all, so no stale WritableComputedRef read and no shallowRef cure owed), no oklch→HSV/stableHue, no ValueUnit wrapping, no reka-ui slider pointer-capture, no rAF, no WebGL — and no parser, so the live parseCssColor crash class cannot reach it. (4) Error paths are total: the only input is a four-member string union, all four exercised in the measured matrix, none throws; there is no network call, no user input, no collection and no numeric domain, so no 0/NaN/Infinity/-0/huge boundary exists. The one throw in its dependency chain (useApiClient.ts:55-61 missing-provider guard) is a correct fail-fast. (5) verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied — both imports (computed, useApiClient) are value imports. (6) Not a god module (38 lines of logic, one responsibility) and idiomatic Vue 3.5 <script setup>. (7) The 23px box is NOT a tap-target defect: a non-interactive <span> with no handler, tabindex or operable role — WCAG 2.5.8's 24px floor binds pointer targets, not annotations. (8) The component contributes ZERO rows to audit/visual/REPORT.md's nameless-button and small-tap-target counts — grep -rn -i "misconfig" over REPORT.md/REPORT.json returns no hits, and it rendered in none of the captured matrices because the persisted savedColors is [] — but that absence is C-3's evidence, not a clean bill. One item is explicitly labelled HYPOTHESIS rather than a finding: both branches mount a live region together with its content (v-if on the region element itself) rather than mounting an empty region ahead of the announcement; ARIA's live-region model is defined over changes to a region already in the accessibility tree and AT behaviour for a region inserted with content is inconsistent (most reliable for role="alert", least for role="status"), so the unavailable announcement may never reach a screen-reader user — I have NO AT reproduction, so it is banked as a hypothesis only.

Focus probe: `{swatchTabIndex:-1, wrapperTabIndex:-1, elFocused:false, parFocused:false, tag:"SPAN", role:null}`. Playwright a11y snapshot of the expanded card exposes zero swatch nodes. `@click.stop="$emit('click')"` at :35 is discarded by the same mechanism, so `useHoverPopover.ts:51 onSwatchClick` is unreachable from this component. `cursor-pointer` at :19,:34 is applied to a `pointer-events:none` element and can never take effect.
defects.mechanism: Same `inheritAttrs:false` + class/style-only forwarding as D-2. Typecheck does not catch it because unknown attrs on a component are legal `$attrs`. The design assumed a polymorphic `tag` prop that the installed producer does not have — a stale contract carried across the Glass 7 adoption.
defects.reproduction: Expand a palette card at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes and run `[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="watercolor-swatch"]')].filter(d=>d.parentElement.className==='relative')[0]` — inspect `.attributes`, `.tabIndex` and attempt `.focus()`. No `tag`, no `aria-label`, tabIndex -1, focus is a no-op.
defects.proposedCure: Introduce the native seat named in AUDIT-HANDOFF-2026-07-28.md §8.3 — one `ColorSwatchButton` (`<button type="button">`, accessible name, producer focus register, `aria-pressed` where selection applies) whose visual child is the WatercolorDot/WatercolorSwatch face. The dot stays what its own docstring says it is: aria-hidden, pointer-events:none paint. This retires all six `tag="button"` impostors in one consumer cut.

defects.defect: The hover panel is `aria-hidden="true"` yet contains three `tabindex=0` buttons and carries no `inert` — focusable controls inside an ARIA-hidden subtree.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:40-50 (`aria-hidden="true"` on the panel). Live probe while open: `{ariaHidden:"true", focusableCount:3, inertAttr:false, tabIndexes:[0,0,0]}`. The source comment at :38-39 asserts "hover-only panel is keyboard-inaccessible — hidden from AT. The reka-ui Popover (touch path) is the accessible route" — D-2 proves that route is dead.
defects.mechanism: `aria-hidden` removes a node from the accessibility tree but not from the tab order. The comment documents a trade the mechanism never made: the component has no accessible route at all, and the "hidden" panel is still reachable by Tab — landing focus on three invisible, off-viewport buttons with no visible ring and no announced name (axe `aria-hidden-focus`, WCAG 4.1.2).
defects.reproduction: Hover a swatch at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes (card expanded), then evaluate `const p=document.querySelector('.floating-panel'); [p.getAttribute('aria-hidden'), p.querySelectorAll('button').length, p.hasAttribute('inert')]` -> `["true", 3, false]`.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1's cure: the producer `PopoverContent` renders `role="group"` with `aria-label`, is genuinely dismissable, and manages focus — so there is no aria-hidden subtree to leak focus into. No local `inert` patch.

defects.defect: `PANEL_LAYOUT` is presented as an anti-drift device but shares only three layout utilities; the two paths have already drifted on positioning, offset, material, elevation, radius, entrance motion, dismissal and a11y — and the two consumers position the same panel differently.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:64-66 declares PANEL_LAYOUT as "applied to both PopoverContent and the hover Teleport panel so the two paths cannot drift". Touch path receives `popover-content z-popover w-72 glass-floating ... glass-reveal` + `avoidCollisions:!0` (compiled popover-BQGYXZyO.js); hover path receives `position:static, zIndex:auto, radius 0px, animation none` (D-1 measurement). Offsets: `:side-offset="8"` at :22 vs `offsetY = -42` at demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:20. Consumer drift: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:31 `:floating-style="{ ...floatingStyle, transform: 'translateX(-50%)' }"` (centre-anchored) vs CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:35 `:floating-style="currentFloatingStyle"` (no transform), both fed the identical `left = rect.left + rect.width/2` from useHoverPopover.ts:23.
defects.mechanism: The anti-drift device was scoped to the one axis that was never going to drift (three Tailwind layout utilities) and left the seven that did — because geometry travels through a sibling `floatingStyle` prop the device does not cover, and material travels through the class the device does not define.
defects.reproduction: Read SwatchHoverMenu.vue:22 vs :41-44; read PaletteCardSwatches.vue:31 vs CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:35 — one consumer applies `translateX(-50%)`, the other does not, against the same centre-derived `left`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete PANEL_LAYOUT along with the fork. One `<Popover trigger="hover"><PopoverContent>` means there is exactly one panel implementation and one placement engine; drift becomes structurally impossible instead of conventionally discouraged. Delete `offsetY = -42` and `:side-offset="8"`; take the producer defaults (`side: "bottom"`, `sideOffset: 4`).

defects.defect: `PANEL_LAYOUT`'s `p-1.5` plus `w-auto` are per-instance overrides of a root-owned, anisotropic, sqrt(phi)-derived overlay padding ladder and width.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:22 sends `class="w-auto"` + PANEL_LAYOUT (`p-1.5 flex items-center gap-1`, :66). Installed PopoverContent root classes (compiled node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js): `popover-content z-popover w-72 glass-floating [--overlay-pad-inline:1rem] [--overlay-pad-block:calc(var(--overlay-pad-inline)*1.272)] px-(--overlay-pad-inline) py-(--overlay-pad-block) glass-reveal`. 1.272 ≈ sqrt(phi) = 1.2720196. `p-1.5` = 0.375rem isotropic, flattening 1rem x 1.272rem and deleting `w-72`.
defects.mechanism: Consumer-level utility classes layered onto a producer root whose padding is expressed as a named token ladder. Violates owner edict 5 and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 §5.8 ("Real rendered relation wins over token intent. Adjacent rungs, measured rects and ink gaps appear in DELTA; token presence alone cannot close a row") — the resulting inline/block relation is not an adjacent rung of anything.
defects.reproduction: Read SwatchHoverMenu.vue:22,66; then `node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js','utf8'); const i=s.indexOf('glass-floating'); console.log(s.slice(i-1800,i+900))"` and read the `O = i(() => e("popover-content z-popover w-72 glass-floating [--overlay-pad-inline:1rem] ...", l.class))` line.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `p-1.5` and `w-auto`; let PopoverContent own overlay padding and width at its root. If the action row genuinely needs a denser rung than the default overlay pad, that is a producer `surface`/size variant relayed to the glass-ui BH inbox — not a consumer override.

defects.defect: glass-ui 7.0.0 already ships this entire component behind one prop; the demo hand-rolls a strictly worse floating engine across three files.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/popover/Popover.vue.d.ts: `trigger?: "click" | "hover"` documented as "Click command or pointer-adaptive hover preview", plus `openDelay` (default 250) and `closeDelay` (default 150). PopoverContent.vue.d.ts: `{portal, side, sideOffset, align, alignOffset, surface, ariaLabel}`; compiled render sets `avoidCollisions: !0`. Against that: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:8-52 (canHover fork + Teleport), useHoverPopover.ts (67 lines: `useBreakpoint("(hover: hover)")`, openIndex, manual `positionPanel`, leave scheduling), useLeaveTimer.ts (20 lines reimplementing `closeDelay`), and a `floatingStyle` prop threaded through two consumers. `Popover` is already imported at SwatchHoverMenu.vue:61.
defects.mechanism: The fork predates the Glass 7 adoption and was never re-derived against the producer's grown surface. Owner edict 4 violation with a named, installed, already-imported replacement.
defects.reproduction: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/popover/Popover.vue.d.ts` — the `trigger`/`openDelay`/`closeDelay` props are the fork's entire feature set, and `trigger="hover"` is documented as pointer-adaptive, i.e. it already handles the coarse-pointer case the `canHover` branch exists to serve.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the fork with `<Popover trigger="hover" :open="open" @update:open="..."><PopoverTrigger><WatercolorDot/></PopoverTrigger><PopoverContent><slot name="actions"/></PopoverContent></Popover>`. Delete useHoverPopover.ts and useLeaveTimer.ts. SwatchHoverMenu.vue 93 -> ~25 lines; two consumer prop-chains (floatingStyle, canHover, cancelLeave, hover, leave) collapse.

defects.defect: The panel's entrance animation was deleted rather than moved or tokenized, and the false attribution that glass-ui supplies it is still asserted in two places — masking the regression for four months.
defects.evidence: `git show c84504d3^:demo/@/styles/floating-panel.css` contains `animation: floating-panel-in var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-decelerate);`; the same commit removed `@keyframes floating-panel-in { from { opacity:0; filter: blur(4px); scale: 0.96; } ... }` from demo/@/styles/animations.css. Today `grep -c "floating-panel" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/animations.css` -> `0`. Live computed on the open panel: `animationName: "none"`. Stale claims: demo/styles/animations.css:2 and demo/DESIGN.md:273 both state "Shared keyframes (dialog, floating-panel, card-menu, shimmer, etc.) are provided by @mkbabb/glass-ui/styles/animations.css" — measured against the installed producer: dialog 1, shimmer 1, card-menu 0, floating-panel 0.
defects.mechanism: A bulk style migration deleted a local stylesheet on an unverified producer-coverage assumption, and left a comment asserting the assumption as fact. The comment then served as the answer to anyone who looked. Owner edict 6 violation; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:139 ("Spatial continuity uses one producer-owned glass-ui spring register") unmet.
defects.reproduction: `for k in dialog card-menu shimmer floating-panel; do printf "%-16s %s\n" "$k" "$(grep -rc "$k" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/animations.css)"; done` -> `dialog 1 / card-menu 0 / shimmer 1 / floating-panel 0`, against the claim at demo/styles/animations.css:2.
defects.proposedCure: Do not re-add a local keyframe. The producer's `glass-reveal` on PopoverContent restores an entrance that already honours `prefers-reduced-motion` upstream; a re-added local keyframe would have to re-implement that guard, which is the wrong direction. Separately, correct or delete the false attributions at demo/styles/animations.css:2 and demo/DESIGN.md:273 (`card-menu` is equally absent).

defects.defect: Every swatch reserves a 6px phantom vertical band it never paints: the component root is a block box wrapping the producer's inline-block span, so an inline line box adds a baseline descender gap.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:2-6 (`<div class="relative">`). Measured at the CurrentPaletteEditor site (`size-class="w-11 h-11 sm:w-12 sm:h-12"`): `{swatch:{w:48,h:48}, wrapper:{w:48,h:54}, wrapperDisplay:"block", swatchDisplay:"inline-block", lineHeight:"27.912px", fontSize:"18.608px"}`. Expanded-card site (`w-9 h-9 sm:w-10 sm:h-10`): swatch 40x40, wrapper 40x46. 12.5%–15% dead vertical reservation per swatch, inherited by the row's `items-start` (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:22) and by the `#overlay` slot's absolute anchor box.
defects.mechanism: Un-designed inline/block seam. The root has no display discipline (`flex`/`inline-flex`/`leading-none`), so layout reservation silently exceeds the glyph — PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72 §5.7 failing in the direction nobody audits.
defects.reproduction: Expand a palette card at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, then evaluate `const d=[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=\"watercolor-swatch\"]')].filter(x=>x.parentElement.className==='relative')[0]; [d.getBoundingClientRect().height, d.parentElement.getBoundingClientRect().height]` -> `[48, 54]` (or `[40, 46]`).
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-3's cure: the native `ColorSwatchButton` seat is an `inline-flex` box sized by the seat, not by a line box, so reservation equals the seat rect by construction. No `leading-none` patch on the current div.

defects.defect: Dead API surface: a prop no consumer passes, an emit whose only source is discarded, and one swatch scale declared in three places with no token.
defects.evidence: `swatchExtraClass` declared at demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:75 and used at :19,:34 — `grep -rn swatchExtraClass demo/` returns only those three lines in that one file (zero consumers). `click` emit declared at :90; its only source `@click.stop="$emit('click')"` at :35 is discarded by D-3's mechanism. `sizeClass` default `"w-9 h-9 sm:w-10 sm:h-10"` at :82, restated verbatim at PaletteCard.vue:197, contradicted by CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:36's `"w-11 h-11 sm:w-12 sm:h-12"`.
defects.mechanism: Speculative generality plus per-site scale authoring. Owner edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance): the two live values (40px / 48px) are a hand-chosen 1.2x ratio, not adjacent rungs of any ladder, and there is no single declaration site to change.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "swatchExtraClass" demo/` -> 3 hits, all inside SwatchHoverMenu.vue. `grep -n "size-class\|sizeClass" demo/palettes/browser/card/**` -> defaults at SwatchHoverMenu.vue:82 and PaletteCard.vue:197, override at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:36.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `swatchExtraClass` and the `click` emit outright. Move the swatch scale to one named token (a producer size rung on the ColorSwatchButton seat, e.g. `size="sm"|"md"`), so the two live sizes become two rungs of one ladder with a single authoring site.

defects.defect: Tap targets sit below the coarse-pointer floor, and opening the panel adds three more per swatch, with no hit-area hook for the producer floor to reach.
defects.evidence: Measured: swatch 40x40 CSS px at >=640px (`sm:w-10 sm:h-10`, demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:82); each action button 28x28 (`{label:"Edit color rgb(255 0 0)", w:28, h:28}` x3 from the live panel dump). docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:34,64 records `smallTapTargets` for `/#/palettes` = 8 desktop / 4 mobile with the panel closed. No `data-icon-only` / touch-hit-area attribute anywhere in the component.
defects.mechanism: Visual glyph size and operable target size are conflated into one box — PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:79 §5.12 ("Invisible/seat geometry preserves target floor while optics follow rung") and §5.7. The seat geometry here IS the optic geometry, so glass-ui's coarse-pointer floor has nothing to expand.
defects.reproduction: Expand a palette card and hover a swatch at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; measure `document.querySelector('.floating-panel').querySelectorAll('button')` rects -> 28x28 each; measure the swatch rect -> 40x40.
defects.proposedCure: Give the ColorSwatchButton seat a separate invisible hit box (producer `touch-hit-area` / `data-icon-only`) so the 40px optic keeps its rung while the operable target reaches the 44px floor, and let PopoverContent's producer-sized action buttons replace the 28px hand-rolled ones.

defects.defect: `positionPanel` reads `e.currentTarget` from inside a deferred `nextTick` callback, where the DOM spec has already reset it to null; an `as Element` cast suppresses the type error that would have caught it.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:30 `nextTick(() => positionPanel(e.currentTarget as Element));` and :21 `const rect = swatchEl.getBoundingClientRect();`. Reproduced with a programmatic dispatch — live console: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect') at positionPanel (http://localhost:9000/@fs/.../useHoverPopover.ts:18:25) at .../useHoverPopover.ts:26:18`.
defects.mechanism: `Event.currentTarget` is only non-null during dispatch (DOM §2.9). Under a real mouse move the microtask checkpoint fires while dispatch is still live, so the read happens to succeed; under any deferred flush (a programmatic dispatch from a non-empty JS stack, an awaiting parent, a Suspense boundary, a synthetic-event test harness) it is null and throws.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS for the real-user path — NOT reproduced under `page.mouse.move`. Reproduced only via `page.evaluate(() => target.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerenter', {bubbles:true, pointerType:'mouse'})))` on the SwatchHoverMenu root, which throws the TypeError above.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-7's cure — the producer floating engine anchors to the trigger element it owns a ref to, so no event-object read survives. If any interim code must resolve the element, capture `const el = e.currentTarget as Element` synchronously before `nextTick`, and delete the `as Element` cast so the null case is a type error.

defects.defect: The component's concept is forbidden by name in the ratified tranche canon: the palette card body may own no hover-only swatch-action path, and its swatch strip must be noninteractive data.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 — "The card body owns no expand, inline rename, action menu, transient result or hover-only swatch-action path. ... the card's compact swatch strip remains noninteractive data with zero activation/focus/drag semantics". docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 row PR-07 — terminal disposition "ADD-AFFORDANCE / REMOVE", Primary W23: "palette hover paths retire into selected inspector; every surviving action/drag seat has a name/state". Also PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 §5.5 ("Decorative controls and operable ornaments without names are forbidden"), :74 §5.9 ("A renderer specimen is not an unlabeled button"), :77 §5.12 (the card's ONE native named button "alone owns activation").
defects.mechanism: The component predates the constitution and was never re-adjudicated against it. It introduces a second activation species inside a card body the canon defines as a bounded noninteractive article, and it makes the specimen the control — the exact two prohibitions.
defects.reproduction: Read VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51 against demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:29-51 (hover-only action panel) and PaletteCardSwatches.vue:25-64 (that panel mounted inside the card body).
defects.proposedCure: After D-1..D-11 are cured, re-decide whether the component should exist. The transposition that satisfies the canon: the card's swatch strip becomes inert data with zero activation/focus/drag semantics, and Edit/Copy/Remove move to the selected inspector — where they acquire names, keyboard reach, durable operation state and a place to report failure (which also closes the missing loading/error states in the state matrix).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 + C-2 + C-3 together: the component is INOPERATIVE on every input modality. On desktop the hover action panel renders as an unstyled, `position: static`, 1440px-wide block at the very bottom of `<body>` (measured `panelRect [0,900,1440,40]` vs `anchorRect [768,349,48,54]`) because `.floating-panel` matches ZERO rules across all 32 live stylesheets — it was deleted in c84504d3 on a false claim that glass-ui supplies it (`grep -rl floating-panel node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` → no output). On touch the reka-ui Popover can never open, because `PopoverTrigger as-child` forwards `onClick`/`id`/`aria-*`/`data-state`/`ref` through `$attrs` into a glass-ui 7 `WatercolorDot` that declares `inheritAttrs:!1` and forwards only `class`/`style`, and hard-codes `pointerEvents:"none"` + `aria-hidden:"true"` on a `<span>`. `tag="button"` is not a prop of that component at all. Live: 0 elements named "Color swatch …", 0 of the dots are `<button>`, 100% are `aria-hidden` + `pointer-events:none` + `tabIndex -1`.
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded negatives, proved rather than assumed: no `defineModel` stale-read hazard — the component correctly uses `:open` + `@update:open`; no oklch/HSV maths; no `ValueUnit`; no slider pointer-capture; no ungated rAF — `WatercolorDot`'s loop is gated behind `animate` default false, which no call site sets, and the producer's `useRAFLoop` is `pauseWhenHidden` + `respectReducedMotion`; no WebGL; `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — `import type { CSSProperties }` at line 60; tap targets pass at 36–48px swatch and 28px action buttons.)

defects.defect: The `.floating-panel` class carries ZERO CSS anywhere in the shipped app, so the teleported hover action panel renders `position: static` at the end of `<body>`: full-viewport-width, below the fold, transparent, unelevated, unanimated, with its correctly-computed inline `top`/`left` inert. It also grows the document, so scrolling toward it fires `pointerleave` and closes it — the panel is unreachable by construction.

defects.proposedCure: Do NOT restore the orphaned demo CSS. The Teleport panel is a second, worse implementation of `PopoverContent`, which glass-ui already ships and which already solves anchoring, collision, layering and dismissal. defects.defect: `tag="button"` and `:aria-label` are passed to glass-ui 7 `WatercolorDot`, which has neither prop, declares `inheritAttrs: false`, forwards ONLY `attrs.class`/`attrs.style`, and hard-codes `<span>` + `aria-hidden="true"` + `pointer-events: none`. The swatch is therefore not a button, has no accessible name, is not focusable, is removed from the a11y tree, and cannot receive any pointer event.

Producer contract `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts` declares exactly `{color, variant?, animate?, cycleDuration?, range?, seed?}` — no `tag`. LIVE on /#/palettes: {"totalWatercolorDots":2,"dotsThatAreButtons":0,"dotsAriaHidden":2,"dotsPointerEventsNone":2,"elementsLabelledColorSwatch":0}; rendered element `<span aria-hidden="true" class="… watercolor-swatch" data-testid="watercolor-swatch" style="… pointer-events: none; …">` with tabIndex -1; `document.elementFromPoint(cx,cy)` at the swatch centre returns the wrapping DIV, not the swatch. defects.mechanism: dead-prop across a producer contract change — an `inheritAttrs:false` component silently swallows every unknown attribute, and neither `vue-tsc` nor any runtime warning surfaces it
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, expand a saved palette card, then in the console: `Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="watercolor-swatch"]')).map(d=>[d.tagName, d.getAttribute('aria-label'), d.getAttribute('aria-hidden'), getComputedStyle(d).pointerEvents, d.tabIndex])` → every row is `['SPAN', null, 'true', 'none', -1]`

The seat must be a real native `<button>` carrying the accessible name and the activation contract, with the dot placed INSIDE it as decoration. defects.defect: The touch branch's `PopoverTrigger as-child` can never open the popover: reka-ui passes the whole trigger contract (`onClick: onOpenToggle`, `id`, `type`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `data-state`, `ref`) as vnode props that land in `WatercolorDot`'s `$attrs` and are discarded. Every per-colour action (Add / Edit / Copy / Remove) is unreachable on every touch device, with no alternate route.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:13-21. `node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Popover/PopoverTrigger.js` renders `createVNode(Primitive, {id, ref: forwardRef, type:"button", "aria-haspopup":"dialog", "aria-expanded":…, "aria-controls":…, "data-state":…, "as-child": props.asChild, onClick: rootContext.onOpenToggle})`. `Primitive.js`: `inheritAttrs:false; if (asTag !== 'template') … return () => h(Slot, attrs, {default: slots.default})`. `Slot.js`: `cloneVNode({...firstNonCommentChildren, props:{}}, mergeProps(attrs, childProps))` → the contract is merged onto the WatercolorDot component vnode → `$attrs` → dropped per C-2. Compounded by the measured `pointer-events: none` on the rendered span. Consumers whose actions become unreachable: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:46,49,52 (Edit/Copy/Remove) and PaletteCardSwatches.vue:41,49,56 (Add/Edit/Copy).
defects.mechanism: as-child prop-forwarding into an `inheritAttrs:false` leaf — the same dead-prop mechanism as C-2, but it destroys a whole control contract rather than one attribute
defects.reproduction: NONE for a direct touch-device tap — the desktop matrix renders the `v-else` hover branch, so the touch branch was not mounted. CONFIRMED BY CONSTRUCTION from three independently verified premises: (a) the compiled reka-ui PopoverTrigger/Primitive/Slot chain quoted above, (b) the compiled WatercolorDot `inheritAttrs:!1` + class/style-only forwarding, (c) the live-measured `pointer-events:none` on the identical element. Labelled as such in the report.
defects.proposedCure: Same as C-2/C-1: one native `<button>` seat wrapping the dot, and ONE glass-ui Popover/DropdownMenu opened by click and by hover-intent. Deleting the `canHover` fork removes the modality split entirely.

defects.defect: `aria-hidden="true"` is set on a container holding three tabbable native `<button>` elements — the axe-core `aria-hidden-focus` violation (impact: serious) — and the code comment justifying it ("The reka-ui Popover (touch path) is the accessible route") is falsified by C-3. A documented tranche-A remediation (`role="toolbar"` + `aria-label`) was reverted to produce this state.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:38-48. Live-measured on the mounted panel: `"ariaHidden": "true"`, containing buttons named ["Edit color rgb(255 0 0)", "Copy color rgb(255 0 0)", "Remove color rgb(255 0 0) from palette"]. Those buttons are declared at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:46,49,52 with no `tabindex` and no `disabled`, so they are in the sequential focus order by HTML spec while removed from the a11y tree. Provenance: docs/tranches/A/audit/W5-a11y.md:51-56 and :180 record `role="toolbar"` + `:aria-label="Actions for color ${color}"` as ADDED and the item as "Done"; commit bda38b6c (B.W1) replaced both with `aria-hidden="true"` on exactly the now-false reasoning (diff quoted in the report).
defects.mechanism: a11y remediation reverted on a premise that later became false — the ledger still records the fix as landed, so no gate re-checks it
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a non-empty current palette, hover a swatch, then `const p=document.querySelector('.floating-panel'); [p.getAttribute('aria-hidden'), Array.from(p.querySelectorAll('button')).map(b=>[b.getAttribute('aria-label'), b.tabIndex])]` → ['true', [[…,0],[…,0],[…,0]]]
defects.proposedCure: Deleted along with the hover branch. The single glass-ui Popover gives the actions a real dialog/menu role, a real accessible name, keyboard operability, Escape dismissal and focus restoration for free — none of which this hand-rolled div has ever had.

defects.defect: `useSwatchActions.swatchKeys` derives TransitionGroup identity from `${color}::${index}`, so removing or reordering any swatch changes EVERY key and remounts the whole row — destroying every live `SwatchHoverMenu` instance instead of animating one leave. The `// --- Stable keys for TransitionGroup ---` comment is false precisely in the cases the map exists for.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useSwatchActions.ts:42-59; consumed at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:31 `:key="swatchKeys[i] ?? i"`. Worked trace: ['red','green','blue'] → map {red::0→0, green::1→1, blue::2→2}, keys [0,1,2]. Remove 'red' → ['green','blue'] → mapKeys 'green::0','blue::1' are absent → fresh counter values → keys [3,4]. The two UNCHANGED swatches are torn down and recreated. `addCurrentColor`'s reorder branch (useSwatchActions.ts:63-69, moves an existing colour to the end) triggers the identical full remount. Secondary: the `computed` at :45 mutates `swatchKeyMap`/`swatchKeyCounter` — a side-effecting computed, not a pure derivation.
defects.mechanism: index-coupled identity in a keyed list — the key incorporates the very quantity that the mutation changes
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with ≥3 colours in the current palette, remove the FIRST swatch, and observe every remaining swatch replay the `vj-enter` insert transition rather than the survivors staying put
defects.proposedCure: Key by a stable per-entry identity minted once at insert (a monotonic id stored alongside the colour in the palette buffer), never by `(value, position)`. The `swatchKeyMap`/prune-watch machinery then disappears entirely.

defects.defect: Vacuous gates across the board: ZERO tests target this component; the hard CI `vue-tsc` demo gate exits 0 over the dead `tag="button"` prop; and the single e2e that touches this cluster queries a locator that resolves to zero live elements, so it cannot be passing against the current tree.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "SwatchHoverMenu" test/ e2e/` → no output. `grep -rn "floating-panel|Color swatch" e2e/ test/` → no output. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo exit=$?` → `exit=0`. e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts:33-36 does `main.getByRole("button", { name: /Add current color .* to palette/ }).filter({visible:true}).click()`; live count of candidates on /#/palettes: {"anyElementWithAddCurrentColorLabel":0,"buttonsWithAddCurrentColorLabel":0} — the target (CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:95-105) renders as an aria-hidden `<span>` with no name and no role per C-2.
defects.mechanism: no behavioural gate exists, and the two structural gates that do exist are blind to `inheritAttrs:false` prop-swallowing
defects.reproduction: MUTATION THAT KEEPS THE SUITE GREEN: replace the entire `<template>` of SwatchHoverMenu.vue with `<div/>`. `npm run test` and `npm run typecheck` both stay green — nothing in test/ or e2e/ names, renders, or asserts anything about this component.
defects.proposedCure: One component test that asserts (a) the swatch exposes `role=button` with an accessible name containing the colour, (b) activating it by click AND by Enter opens a panel, (c) the panel's actions are focus-reachable and not inside `aria-hidden`. That single test catches C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5 and C-16 at once.

defects.defect: The `floating-panel-in` entrance keyframe was deleted rather than moved or tokenized, in direct violation of the standing owner edict that animations are never deleted.
defects.evidence: Deleted in commit c84504d3 from demo/@/styles/animations.css (diff shows `-@keyframes floating-panel-in { from { opacity: 0; filter: blur(4px); scale: 0.96; } to {…} }`) on the claim it now comes from the producer. `grep -o "floating-panel" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/animations.css | wc -l` → 0. Live measurement on the mounted panel: `"animationName": "none"`. demo/styles/animations.css:2 still asserts the producer supplies it.
defects.mechanism: same orphaning event as C-1 — the keyframe and its consuming rule were deleted together on one unverified migration claim
defects.reproduction: hover a swatch at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, then `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.floating-panel')).animationName` → 'none'
defects.proposedCure: Do not re-add the keyframe to demo/. The producer's Popover already ships its own entrance choreography (`@keyframes scale-in`/`tooltip-in` + the `glass-top-layer` @starting-style transitions in glass-ui/dist/styles/animations.css); adopting `PopoverContent` restores an entrance animation that is tokenized and producer-owned.

defects.defect: The two consumers disagree about the centering transform the shared positioning math requires: `PaletteCardSwatches` supplies `translateX(-50%)`, `CurrentPaletteEditor` does not, although both feed the identical `left = rect.left + rect.width/2` centre-anchor.
defects.evidence: Math at demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:20-24. PaletteCardSwatches.vue:31 `:floating-style="{ ...floatingStyle, transform: 'translateX(-50%)' }"` vs CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:35 `:floating-style="currentFloatingStyle"`. Live-measured on the CurrentPaletteEditor path: `"inlineStyle": "top: 307.18px; left: 791.5px;"`, `"computed": {"transform": "none"}`.
defects.mechanism: a positioning invariant left to call sites instead of being owned by the component — exactly the drift the file's own PANEL_LAYOUT comment claims to prevent
defects.reproduction: grep the two lines above; then hover a Current-Palette swatch and read the inline style — no transform is present on that path, while the card path emits one
defects.proposedCure: The centering belongs inside the surface, not at the call site. `PopoverContent`'s `side`/`align`/`side-offset` own it, and the `floatingStyle` prop disappears with the hover branch.

defects.defect: The `click` emit is unreachable dead code, and both consumers wire handlers to it that can never run.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:35 `@click.stop="$emit('click')"` and :90 `click: []`. The listener is an `$attr` on WatercolorDot and is dropped per C-2; the element is additionally `pointer-events: none`. Dead consumers: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:41 → `onCurrentSwatchClick(i)`; PaletteCardSwatches.vue:36 → `$emit('swatchClick', i)` → PaletteCard.vue:154 → `onSwatchClick`. The composable implementation useHoverPopover.ts:51-54 is therefore unreachable.
defects.mechanism: dead listener — the same `inheritAttrs:false` swallow as C-2, applied to an event binding rather than an attribute
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, click (not hover) any Current-Palette swatch — the panel does not toggle; `document.elementFromPoint` at the swatch centre returns the wrapping DIV, which has no click handler
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of C-2: once the seat is a real `<button>`, click/Enter/Space all bind natively and the toggle emit becomes reachable — or is deleted outright if the glass-ui Popover owns open state.

defects.defect: glass-ui 7 `WatercolorDot` renders no default slot, so the `<Plus>` glyph in the current-palette add-slot is discarded — the primary "add a colour" affordance of the palettes route ships as an empty, nameless, aria-hidden, untappable dashed blob.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:95-105 places `<Plus class="w-5 h-5 …"/>` in WatercolorDot's default slot. The compiled render function (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js) builds children as `[svg.watercolor-filter-host, (variant==='ghost' ? span.watercolor-ghost-stroke : createCommentVNode())]` — there is no `renderSlot` call anywhere in it. Live: the rendered span is `<span aria-hidden="true" class="add-slot-ghost … watercolor-swatch" style="…pointer-events:none…">` with tabIndex -1 and no aria-label. Shipped visual confirmation: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/palettes.png shows the "Start a new palette" affordance as an empty dashed blob with no `+`.
defects.mechanism: same dead-prop / dropped-content mechanism as C-2, applied to slot content — collateral in the sibling file that owns half of SwatchHoverMenu's instances, and the clearest visual proof of the mechanism
defects.reproduction: open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes and look at the 'Start a new palette' well — the ghost slot has no plus glyph; `document.querySelector('.add-slot-ghost').children` contains only the SVG filter host and the ghost-stroke span; `getComputedStyle(el).pointerEvents === 'none'`
defects.proposedCure: Same transposition: a native `<button aria-label="Add current color …">` containing the WatercolorDot face AND the Plus glyph as siblings, so the glyph is rendered by the demo, not smuggled into a producer slot that does not exist.

defects.defect: The component maintains two parallel implementations of one affordance — a reka-ui Popover for touch and a hand-rolled `<Teleport to="body">` panel for hover — duplicating `PopoverContent`. This violates the no-dual-paths, KISS, and glass-ui-is-the-design-system edicts, and was already logged in tranche A as Ad-9 and never resolved.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:8-25 (Popover) vs :28-52 (Teleport). The `PANEL_LAYOUT` constant at :66 with its comment "so the two paths cannot drift" dedupes only the padding; the WatercolorDot markup is duplicated verbatim at :14-20 and :29-36, and the centering transform HAS already drifted (C-7). Prior record: docs/tranches/A/research/Ad-interactive-states.md:158-159 ("SwatchHoverMenu hand-rolls a teleported panel parallel to PopoverContent"), docs/tranches/A/audit/W4-states-b.md:78, and the standing recommendation "collapse to one HoverCard" at Ad-interactive-states.md:377.
defects.mechanism: modality fork — branching an affordance on `(hover: hover)` instead of building one control that responds to click, hover-intent and keyboard alike
defects.reproduction: read the file; the `v-if="!canHover"` / `<template v-else>` pair at lines 9 and 28 is the fork
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hover branch. One glass-ui Popover, opened by click (all modalities) and by hover-intent (pointer devices only, as a convenience). This single deletion is simultaneously the cure for C-1, C-5, C-6, C-7, C-10, C-11, C-12, C-13 and C-15.

defects.defect: `useLeaveTimer` never disposes its pending 250 ms timeout — no `onScopeDispose`/`onUnmounted` anywhere in the card composables directory.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useLeaveTimer.ts:1-17 returns only `{schedule, cancel}`; `grep -rn "onScopeDispose|onUnmounted" demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/` → no output. Used by useHoverPopover.ts:18 for every PaletteCard in the grid and for CurrentPaletteEditor.
defects.mechanism: missing cleanup — a composable that owns a timer but not its scope's disposal
defects.reproduction: NONE observed (the stale callback writes a ref nobody reads after unmount, so it is currently silent). Hypothesis-grade as a user-visible bug; CONFIRMED as an uncleaned resource by the grep above.
defects.proposedCure: `onScopeDispose(cancel)` — one line. Or moot entirely once the hover branch and its leave-intent timer are deleted with C-14.

defects.defect: The panel's position is captured once at hover and never updated: no scroll/resize listener, no ResizeObserver, no collision handling, and `offsetY = -42` is a magic constant independent of the panel's real height.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:20-31 — `positionPanel` reads `getBoundingClientRect()` once inside `nextTick` and writes `style.top/left`; no listener is registered anywhere in the file. The panel is `flex items-center gap-1` with 1–3 children (SwatchHoverMenu.vue:66), measured 40px tall today, so `-42` happens to clear it — a two-row wrap would overlap the swatch.
defects.mechanism: one-shot positioning of a viewport-anchored overlay, with no autoUpdate loop
defects.reproduction: NONE currently observable, because C-1 makes `top`/`left` inert. Becomes live the moment `.floating-panel` is restored: hover a swatch, scroll one line, and the panel detaches from its anchor. Labelled as a hypothesis conditional on C-1's naive cure.
defects.proposedCure: Never restore hand-rolled positioning. `PopoverContent` uses Floating-UI `autoUpdate` with flip/shift middleware — scroll tracking, resize tracking and collision avoidance all come with the primitive.

defects.defect: `e.currentTarget` is read inside a `nextTick` callback, i.e. potentially after event dispatch has completed, and cast with `as Element` so the compiler cannot force the null branch.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:26-31 — `nextTick(() => positionPanel(e.currentTarget as Element))`. Reproduced live as an uncaught page error: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect') at positionPanel (…/useHoverPopover.ts:18:25) at (…/useHoverPopover.ts:26:18)`.
defects.mechanism: reading a dispatch-scoped property outside dispatch; the `as Element` assertion suppresses the `EventTarget | null` the type system would otherwise surface
defects.reproduction: In the console at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a non-empty current palette: `const w = document.querySelector('[data-testid="watercolor-swatch"]').parentElement; const b = w.getBoundingClientRect(); w.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerenter',{pointerType:'mouse',clientX:b.x+b.width/2,clientY:b.y+b.height/2}))` → the TypeError above. CAVEAT, stated honestly: with a TRUSTED Chromium hover the microtask checkpoint still runs inside `dispatch`, so `currentTarget` survives and the inline style is written correctly (verified: `top: 307.18px; left: 791.5px`). The crash is therefore NOT shipping on the mouse path in Chromium today — it hard-crashes under any programmatic dispatch, which is exactly what a component test would do.
defects.proposedCure: Capture the element synchronously before deferring — `const el = e.currentTarget as Element;` outside the `nextTick` — or, properly, hand the panel a `useTemplateRef` anchor so no event property is retained at all.

defects.defect: `swatchExtraClass` is a declared, template-consumed prop that no consumer ever passes — a per-instance styling escape hatch with zero users.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "swatch-extra-class|swatchExtraClass" demo/` returns exactly three hits, all inside demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue (:19, :34, :75). Neither CurrentPaletteEditor.vue nor PaletteCardSwatches.vue binds it.
defects.mechanism: speculative extension point — dead API surface kept alive by nothing
defects.reproduction: the grep above; the prop has no binder anywhere in the tree
defects.proposedCure: Delete it. Edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance) and edict 5 (style at the root component level, never per-instance) both point the same way.

defects.defect: `PopoverContent` receives per-instance layout overrides rather than consuming a producer variant.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:22 — `<PopoverContent class="w-auto" :class="PANEL_LAYOUT" :side-offset="8">` where `PANEL_LAYOUT = "p-1.5 flex items-center gap-1"` (:66).
defects.mechanism: call-site restyling of a design-system root component
defects.reproduction: read line 22 and line 66
defects.proposedCure: A compact/toolbar `PopoverContent` variant in glass-ui, per the standing edict that variants and primitives belong to the producer.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M context). Matches the explicit Opus 5 declaration this seat was spawned with; not an inherited or undeclared seat.
result.strongestDefect: D-2: the component's "loud, attention-owning" misconfigured register renders text at a MEASURED 2.08:1 contrast in light (sampled from the owner's own OM-5 witness) and 2.38:1 in dark (sampled live) against a 4.5:1 AA floor for 11px text — a ~2.16x shortfall. Mechanism is hue-on-hue: `color: var(--destructive)` painted over `background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 12%, transparent)` (ApiOfflineChip.vue:69,71). A tint of the ink can never be a ground for that ink. In dark mode the chip fill sampled pixel-identical to the card behind it (CR 1.00:1) — the surface does not exist at all. The single message on screen about work not reaching the server is, by measurement, the least legible text in its container.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (What IS sound, recorded in report §6 so this is not read as indiscriminate: self-gating is correct and measured — chipCount 0 at availability==="available", no empty shell or skeleton; prefers-reduced-motion is gated correctly with BOTH the @keyframes and the animation declaration inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` at :81–90, which is better than the common `animation:none` counter-patch; the animated property is `opacity`, compositor-only, zero layout-forcing properties in the file; the DI seam uses `useApiClient()` rather than a module singleton per useApiClient.ts:9; verbatimModuleSyntax is clean — both imports are genuine value imports; 91 lines, one job, not a god module; and the `misconfigured ≠ unavailable` distinction at the LATCH level (availability.ts:169,189–191) is real engineering — the objection is only that it was given two visible surfaces where it needed zero.)

defects.defect: The `misconfigured` visual surface is owner-ordered DEAD (OM-5 / MT-F031) and this file is its second live copy. The repo's own barrel declares the affordance already died and was 're-homed' to the dock lamp — it was copied, not moved, so one sentence is hard-coded in two components and both render simultaneously.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/status/index.ts:2-6 ("DevMisconfigBanner DIED at T.W6 · W6-6 (T-9, owner order): the misconfigured-state affordance re-homed as the dock status lamp") vs ApiOfflineChip.vue:11-18 which still carries the branch, and demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:54 which holds the identical label string. Live measurement with latch=misconfigured: `.api-offline-chip` count 1 AND `.dock-status-lamp` count 1, both reading "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`", both role="alert". Owner mark MT-F031 2026-07-27, witness docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-5-dev-misconfigured-banner.png: 'this nonsense needs to be removed'.
defects.mechanism: duplicated-affordance / dead-surface-not-actually-removed (a 're-home' executed as a copy, leaving two authorities for one fact)
defects.reproduction: Live dev server http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; `const m = await import('/@fs/.../demo/platform/transport/availability.ts'); m.apiAvailability.value='misconfigured'` → document.querySelectorAll('.api-offline-chip').length === 1 and document.querySelectorAll('.dock-status-lamp').length === 1, identical text.
defects.proposedCure: Delete ApiOfflineChip.vue:11-18 and .api-misconfig-chip/.misconfig-dot (:66-79); delete the `misconfigured` arm of status-lamp.ts:50-55 and DockStatusLamp.vue:91-107. The LATCH stays (it is load-bearing: assertApiAttemptAllowed:189-191 throws DevMisconfigError synchronously; markApiUnreachable:169 refuses to relabel). The diagnosis already exists at full fidelity in the console (availability.ts:163 console.error naming page origin, resolved base URL and the exact fix) — which is where a dev-environment diagnosis belongs.

defects.defect: The alert register fails WCAG AA contrast in BOTH schemes by roughly 2x. Ink and fill share the same hue, so only lightness can separate them, and 12% of the destructive supplies almost none.
defects.evidence: PIL sampling of the owner's witness OM-5-dev-misconfigured-banner.png: pill fill (225,144,140), glyph ink (201,57,48) → CR 2.08:1; pill fill vs page field (230,158,153) → 1.13:1. Live dark (evidence/desktop-1440-dark-misconfigured.png): chip fill (86,57,50) == card well (86,57,50) → CR 1.00:1; ink brightest-2.5% (215,69,68) → 2.38:1, peak pixel (235,71,71) → 2.73:1. Threshold is 4.5:1 for 11px text (WCAG 1.4.3). Source: ApiOfflineChip.vue:69 `color: var(--destructive...)`, :71 `background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive...) 12%, transparent)`.
defects.mechanism: hue-on-hue wash — a tint of the ink used as the ground for that ink; no neutral surface tier beneath
defects.reproduction: python3 + PIL sampling of docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-5-dev-misconfigured-banner.png and of the live capture at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ApiOfflineChip/evidence/desktop-1440-dark-misconfigured.png; sRGB relative luminance, WCAG 2.x contrast formula. Numbers pasted in report §1.1-1.2.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1 — the surface dies. If any destructive chip is ever reinstated, the ground must come from the neutral surface ladder (--surface-tint-*), never the ink's own hue, and the pairing must be --destructive-foreground on --destructive or the inverse — i.e. consume glass-ui `Chip`'s `tone`/`surface` axes rather than hand-mixing.

defects.defect: `--type-mono-caption` does not exist anywhere in the repo or in glass-ui. The font-size is therefore always the hard-coded fallback 0.6875rem = 11px — below the 12px floor of the design system's caption rung, frozen outside the fluid arm, and forked: the same phantom token has two different fallbacks across three files.
defects.evidence: Live: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--type-mono-caption') === "" ; getComputedStyle(chip).fontSize === "11px". `grep -rn -- "--type-mono-caption:" demo/ src/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → 0 declaration sites, 3 consumption sites (ApiOfflineChip.vue:47, DockStatusLamp.vue:54, ComponentSliders.vue:310). glass-ui's actual rung: `--type-caption: clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem)` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/scale.css) = 12→16px. ComponentSliders.vue:310 falls back to `var(--type-caption)`; the other two fall back to `0.6875rem` — same phantom token, up to 5px of silent divergence.
defects.mechanism: masking fallback / phantom token — token appearance with no token behind it, which also defeats PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.8 ('token presence alone cannot close a row')
defects.reproduction: mcp playwright browser_evaluate on http://localhost:9000/#/palettes reading the custom property off :root (empty string) and the chip's computed fontSize (11px); plus the grep above showing zero declaration sites.
defects.proposedCure: Consume the role, not a number: the `text-mono-small` utility (registered at demo/styles/foundation.css:88,586) or glass-ui `Chip size="sm"` whose own size map is `gap-1 px-2.5 py-1 text-caption`. Delete `--type-mono-caption` from all three consumption sites in the same cut — a token with zero declarations and two divergent fallbacks is worse than no token.

defects.defect: glass-ui@7 already ships this exact component three times over — `./chip`, `./badge`, `./status-dot` — and the demo already consumes the producer Chip on another route. This leaf forked the design system in scoped CSS.

defects.reproduction: The package-exports probe and the d.ts reads above; plus grep showing EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:14 consuming the producer chip correctly on a sibling route.
defects.proposedCure: Compose from the producer: `<Chip mode="static" size="sm" shape="pill" :tone surface="quiet"><StatusDot :state /> {{ message }}</Chip>`. Chip supplies pill geometry + caption rung + spacing ladder (kills D-3, D-8 and the off-ladder numbers); StatusDot supplies the mark and its accessible identity (kills D-9's bug class and D-13).

defects.defect: The entire CSS recipe is copy-pasted into DockStatusLamp.vue — 17 (property,value) pairs byte-identical, ~21 of 28 identical modulo whitespace — and the pulse keyframe body is duplicated under two names in two scoped blocks.
