defects.reproduction: python3 regex extraction of (property,value) pairs from both scoped style blocks, set intersection — output pasted in report §D-5.
defects.proposedCure: One seat, from the producer (see D-4). If any pulse survives, move it to demo/styles/animations.css — which already hosts exactly this class of shared motion (edit-drawer-in, stagger-child-in, vj-settle) — per owner edict 6: a keyframe consumed by two components is global by definition.

defects.defect: The transport truth is gated on the swatch count. The backend's reachability is conditioned on how many colours the user has picked, so an offline warning appears and disappears as a side effect of adding/removing a swatch.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:116 `<ApiOfflineChip v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0" class="self-start" />`. Measured live at 390px with latch=unavailable and an empty draft palette: `.api-offline-chip` count = 0 while the backend is down (evidence/mobile-390-misconfigured-lamp-only.png). Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §4 PR-08 'Pending/failure/export/recovery truth only transient → ADD-AFFORDANCE ... Persistent entity status/recovery'; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5 'Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace.'
defects.mechanism: status coupled to unrelated local state — a workspace-level fact rendered as a per-card annotation inside an unrelated v-if
defects.reproduction: Live http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844 with m.apiAvailability.value='unavailable' and an empty current-palette draft → chipPresent false, wellPresent false; the only indication is the dock lamp. Add one swatch → chip appears; delete the last swatch → chip vanishes with the backend still down.
defects.proposedCure: Hoist the status out of CurrentPaletteEditor's v-if and out of the card entirely into a persistent workspace-level status region (Move 3 of the report's cure). The region is always mounted; only its text changes.

defects.defect: No recovery arm, and the live region flaps. When the latch returns to `available` the chip is v-if'd out with no 'reconnected / N synced' statement; and because the node mounts/unmounts on every latch transition, an offline session re-announces the same sentence roughly every 30s — twice (chip + lamp).
defects.evidence: availability.ts:175-179 markApiReachable sets 'available' with no UI counterpart; availability.ts:59 `RETRY_COOLDOWN_MS = 30_000`; assertApiAttemptAllowed:188-195 admits one probe past the cooldown, so a genuinely-offline session oscillates unavailable→probe→unavailable. ApiOfflineChip.vue:19-26 is a `v-if` on a `role="status"` node; measured live there are TWO such nodes (chip + DockStatusLamp) carrying identical text: statusTexts: ['backend offline — saved locally','backend offline — saved locally']. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5: 'A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth.'
defects.mechanism: transient-only truth with no recovery state; v-if on a live region turns state changes into repeated announcements
defects.reproduction: NONE end-to-end for the 30s flap (I did not sit through a cooldown cycle) — HYPOTHESIS on the timing, mechanism quoted from availability.ts:59,188-195. CONFIRMED on the duplication: two role="status" nodes measured live after a clean reload with prior-session probe debris removed.
defects.proposedCure: One persistent live region whose TEXT changes rather than a node that mounts/unmounts, with three arms: unavailable → 'backend offline — N palettes held locally'; available-after-unavailable → 'reconnected — N synced' then settles to empty; otherwise present-and-empty. Closes PR-08 properly (persistent status AND recovery) and stops the re-announcement.

defects.defect: The chip has no material tier — its own surface is optically null. It pays the geometric cost of a chip (fill + hairline + pill radius) for zero optical return, and in dark mode the fill is pixel-identical to the container behind it.
defects.evidence: Measured: light, chip fill (243,239,235) vs its well (233,225,217) → CR 1.13:1. Dark, chip fill (86,57,50) vs card well sample (86,57,50) → CR 1.00:1. Source: ApiOfflineChip.vue:53 `background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--background) 55%, transparent)` — 55% of the page background painted over a well already derived from the page background. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §2: 'One surface has one tier... Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well.'
defects.mechanism: null material — a translucent tint of the ground composited onto that same ground
defects.reproduction: PIL sampling of evidence/desktop-1440-light-unavailable.png (box x755-930, y372-390 vs well mode) and evidence/desktop-1440-dark-misconfigured.png (box x755-975, y416-432 vs px[1000,420]).
defects.proposedCure: Pick one: either a bare annotation (drop fill and border, keep dot + text at full ink) or a real chip on a real producer tier (glass-ui Chip `surface`/`tone`). Currently it is neither.

defects.defect: Below 1024px the sibling DockStatusLamp's role="alert" region has an EMPTY accessible name — `display:none` on the label removes it from the a11y tree, contradicting the source comment two lines above which claims it stays. It is the only surviving affordance on mobile once D-6 suppresses the chip: a 26x18px unnamed red mote.
defects.evidence: Live @390px: lamp.getAttribute('role') === 'alert'; getComputedStyle('.lamp-label').display === 'none'; lamp.innerText === "" (innerText respects display:none — the a11y-visible text) while lamp.textContent === 'dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`'; .lamp-dot aria-hidden === 'true'; lamp rect 26x18. Source DockStatusLamp.vue:67-69 `.lamp-label { display: none; }` and the false claim at :66-68 'The role + label stay in the accessibility tree (visually-hidden, not v-if'd)'. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.5: 'A small icon/mark is either data, status, labeled action, drag affordance, focus/selection register or removed.' VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: states are never colour-only; role, accessible name, state/value explicit.
defects.mechanism: display:none mistaken for visually-hidden — an assertive live region left with no accessible name
defects.reproduction: Live http://localhost:9000/#/palettes resized to 390x844, latch=misconfigured, browser_evaluate reading lamp.innerText (empty) vs lamp.textContent (full sentence) plus the label's computed display. Witness: evidence/mobile-390-misconfigured-lamp-only.png.
defects.proposedCure: Replace display:none with the producer's visually-hidden utility, or name the compacted lamp with aria-label. Structurally: use glass-ui StatusDot, whose `label` prop exists precisely to carry accessible identity when the adjacent text is hidden.

defects.defect: No narrow-viewport behaviour at all: white-space:nowrap with max-width computed `none`, no truncation, no wrap, no compaction, no media arm — while its byte-identical sibling compacts to a 26px dot below 1024px.
defects.evidence: ApiOfflineChip.vue:54 `white-space: nowrap`; live computed maxWidth 'none', overflow 'visible'. Measured intrinsic widths at 11px: 212px (offline face), 252px (misconfigured face). Sibling: DockStatusLamp.vue:67-74 folds the label below 1024px — measured w:26 at 390px. ApiOfflineChip has no equivalent rule anywhere in its 50 lines of CSS.
defects.mechanism: unbounded nowrap inline-flex with no responsive arm — geometry that cannot degrade
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS on the exact clip point: I could not photograph the overflow because at 390px the draft palette was empty and D-6's v-if suppressed the chip. CONFIRMED on the missing responsive arm (grep of the scoped block shows zero @media width queries) and on the measured 252px intrinsic width vs a 320px-viewport card content box.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui Chip carries the producer's size ladder and wrap behaviour; adopt it (D-4). A hand-rolled nowrap with no max-width ceiling is the anti-pattern.

defects.defect: Motion is untokenized, mis-eased, and unpausable: a raw `2.4s` literal duplicated in two files, a one-shot transition curve applied to a symmetric loop, and `infinite` with no pause mechanism.
defects.evidence: ApiOfflineChip.vue:88 `animation: offline-dot-pulse 2.4s var(--ease-standard) infinite`, duplicated verbatim at DockStatusLamp.vue:120. glass-ui exposes a full duration ladder (--duration-instant/fast/normal/slow/panel/xl/xxl, --spring-*-duration in dist/styles/theme/bridges.css) — none consumed. `--ease-standard` resolves live to `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` — an accelerate-then-decelerate one-shot curve, which between two stops of a symmetric loop renders an asymmetric tick, not a breath. `infinite` with no control: WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide) for auto-starting motion past 5s; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6 holds the same line ('terminates within five seconds or exposes one persistent keyboard-operable still/pause control').
defects.mechanism: ad-hoc motion — magic-number duration, wrong-token curve, unbounded iteration count
defects.reproduction: Source read plus live getComputedStyle: animationName 'lamp-dot-pulse-45530b34', animationDuration '2.4s', animationIterationCount 'infinite'; --ease-standard measured 'cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)'.
defects.proposedCure: Move any surviving pulse to demo/styles/animations.css with a --duration-* token and a symmetric ease-in-out, and cap it at <=5s or drop it. A status that must pulse forever to be noticed is styled too quietly — which is D-15 restated. (Credit: the prefers-reduced-motion gating at :81 is correct, and opacity is compositor-only — those parts are right.)

defects.defect: The shell command in the misconfig message is emitted as a bare text node with no LTR isolation, so under dir="rtl" the backtick pair and the em-dash reorder around the Latin run.
defects.evidence: ApiOfflineChip.vue:17 — the literal ``dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev` `` with no <bdi> and no dir="ltr". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1: 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose.' A shell command is provenance.
defects.mechanism: missing bidi isolation on an embedded LTR technical string
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/ and rtl-mobile/ contain no capture with this component rendered (it renders in zero of the 60 Safari captures). Mechanism is the absent <bdi>/dir="ltr".
defects.proposedCure: Moot if D-1's ruling kills the misconfig surface. Otherwise wrap technical strings in <bdi> / dir="ltr" per §6.1 — and note the same law applies to any hex/slug/CSS string this status language ever carries.

defects.defect: Under forced-colors the designed register split collapses: the open ring and the filled lamp resolve to the same glyph, and the destructive-vs-muted ink difference is forced away at the same time. The 'distinct by construction' claim in the source holds only while author colours are honoured.

Under forced-colors: active the UA overrides background-color and border-color with system colours. Source comments asserting the distinction: ApiOfflineChip.vue:66-67 and DockStatusLamp.vue:88-90. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never colour-only.'

defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/forced-colors-desktop/ has no capture with this component rendered. Mechanism is the CSS above plus the forced-colors override rules.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui StatusDot's `state` axis is the producer's answer; it owns whatever forced-colors treatment the design system decides once. Failing that, carry the register in shape/glyph as well as colour, and keep the label text distinct (it already is).

defects.defect: Role register error plus an asymmetric dev gate: role="alert" (assertive, interrupting) is used for a developer-facing instruction shown to whoever loads the page, fired twice on one view; and unlike the dock lamp the chip has NO dev gate, so a loopback production build would show an end user a `npm run dev` instruction with the lamp dark.
defects.evidence: ApiOfflineChip.vue:13 `role="alert"` on a message reading 'run `npm run dev`'; two such regions render simultaneously (D-1). Gate asymmetry: status-lamp.ts:48 `if (!isDev) return null;  // dev-gated — the lamp ships dark in production` vs ApiOfflineChip.vue:12 which has no equivalent. detectDevMisconfig (availability.ts:112-116) requires a loopback host but NOT import.meta.env.DEV; client.ts:36 DEFAULT_REMOTE_API_URL = 'https://api.color.babb.dev'.
defects.mechanism: assertive live-region register misused for a developer diagnostic; dev-gating applied to one of two copies of the same affordance
defects.reproduction: NONE — HYPOTHESIS BY CONSTRUCTION. The two code paths are quoted verbatim; I did not build and serve a `vite preview` on loopback with VITE_API_URL unset to observe it. (The running dev server has VITE_API_URL set — measured BASE_URL http://localhost:3000 — so misconfigured never latches naturally here.)
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by D-1: the surface dies and the diagnosis lives in the console, which is dev-gated by definition. For the surviving `unavailable` face, role="status" (polite) is the correct register and needs no dev gate.

defects.defect: Hierarchy inversion: the one message about work not reaching the server is the smallest, faintest, lowest-contrast element in its container — quieter than the decorative '3 colors' count beside it and the name placeholder below it.
defects.evidence: Collected measurements: 11px (below the 12px floor of --type-caption, D-3); ink at 72% of --foreground (ApiOfflineChip.vue:52); surface 1.13:1 light / 1.00:1 dark (D-8); text 3.58:1 offline stroke body / 2.08:1 alert (D-2). Visual: evidence/desktop-1440-light-unavailable.png, the chip inside the Current Palette well. The source comment at :2-6 states the intent as 'a DESIGNED state in the instrument's own register ... never an apologetic toast' — the intent is right and the canon supports it; the execution inverted it.
defects.mechanism: restraint executed as inaudibility — every subordination lever pulled at once on the one element that carries risk information
defects.reproduction: The composite of the measurements above, read against evidence/desktop-1440-light-unavailable.png at 1440x900.
defects.proposedCure: A persistent workspace-level status region (D-6/D-7 cure) can afford full-strength ink at the caption rung on a real surface without shouting. Restraint = small and calm at full contrast; not small, translucent, off-scale and on a null surface.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model ID claude-opus-5[1m] (1M context). Seat declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-3 — the @mkbabb/value.js public surface is declared twice and the two declarations have measurably drifted: tsconfig.demo.json:42-49 (hand-written) omits `/value` and `/css`, invents `/parsing` and `/units` (neither exists in package.json#exports, src/subpaths/, or dist/subpaths/), and maps the bare root to a nonexistent ./dist/index.d.ts. The missing `/css` entry falls through to node resolution, which finds @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 installed transitively via glass-ui 7.0.0 + keyframes.js 6.0.0 (npm ls) — and `diff dist/subpaths/css.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` is NON-EMPTY. So the demo's 10 `@mkbabb/value.js/css` import sites typecheck against the published July-17 snapshot while Vite (vite.config.ts:41-50, generated from exports) serves the working tree's build. Every green demo typecheck is, for those sites, a proof about a different library.
result.negativeProof: Coverage of the soundness checks, recorded so the verdict's scope is auditable: (1) verbatimModuleSyntax — PaletteColorStrip.vue:29 is `import type { PaletteColor }`; the only other import is a value import of `computed`; clean. (2) Vue 3.5 idiom — :31-45 uses reactive props destructure with defaults, not withDefaults(defineProps()), and is more idiomatic than its own parent PaletteCard.vue:182-196. (3) No god module — 72 lines, one computed, one constant, zero side effects, adds to nothing. (4) No deep reach into src/ — the component imports nothing from src/, and the demo tree carries no `@src/*` import outside the exempt assets/docs/*.md reference pages; the T.W1 dogfood keystone holds at the specifier level (L-3 is a defect in type RESOLUTION of those specifiers, not in the specifiers themselves). (5) glass-ui boundary — imports nothing from demo/ui/, defines no design-system primitive locally, smuggles nothing into demo/ui/. (6) Animations — no <style> block, no keyframes, nothing deleted. (7) Barrel hygiene — card/index.ts and browser/index.ts are named re-exports only per the PI-6 rule they cite; no star re-export; the stated tree-shaking rationale holds. (8) Route health — /#/palettes and /#/browse show pageErr 0, consoleErr 0, overflowX 0 in all four Safari matrices (REPORT.md:120-121,135-136,150-151,165-166); the strip renders correctly where it appears (shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png cropped at 4x, top-left corner rounded and correct). No visual defect attributable to this component.

defects.defect: The demo module-graph boundary is not enforced — all three G-DEMO eslint rules are inert, so `browser/index.ts`'s claim that the seam is "enforced standing (eslint.config.js)" is a false proof of encapsulation.
defects.evidence: $ npx eslint --print-config demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue → no-restricted-imports: undefined ; $ npx eslint --print-config demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue → no-restricted-imports: undefined. Cause A: eslint.config.js:232-239 scopes G-DEMO-3b to demo/@/components/**, demo/@/lib/**; eslint.config.js:274-277 scopes G-DEMO-1/3a to demo/@/composables/** — `$ ls demo/@` → "No such file or directory". Cause B: all three ban groups key on the `@components` alias, which tsconfig.demo.json:32-34 and vite.config.ts:68-74 record as deleted at W43/RF-15 ("No @styles/@components/@utils/@lib/@composables/@assets project alias survives"). Claim being falsified: demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:9-12.
defects.mechanism: guard-rail decoupled from the tree it guards — globs and ban patterns left pointing at a dissolved directory layout and a deleted path alias
defects.reproduction: Run the two `npx eslint --print-config` commands above and read `rules["no-restricted-imports"]`; then `ls demo/@`.
defects.proposedCure: Re-point the boundary at the tree that exists: one `no-restricted-imports` object per demo area, banning `**/<other-area>/**` except that area's own index.ts, plus a ban on any relative import climbing more than one `../` out of an area. Delete the three dead objects rather than patching their globs — the rule set should be regenerated from the area list, not hand-maintained.

defects.defect: The `palettes` area has no seam. `browser/index.ts` calls itself "the mega-feature's TOP-LEVEL SEAM" but is only the barrel for `palettes/browser/**`; everything above it is reached raw and cross-area, including the shell reaching up into a feature.
defects.evidence: $ ls demo/palettes/index.ts → "No such file or directory". Raw cross-area reaches into palettes internals: demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue:10,13; MixSourceSelector.vue:6; MixConfigBar.vue:14; demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:21; GeneratePane.vue:6,8; demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractPane.vue:27; demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:18; demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:8; demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:24. Label being contradicted: demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:1.
defects.mechanism: a barrel drawn one level below the boundary it is named for, so the area's types/ports/composables have no public face at all
defects.reproduction: `ls demo/palettes/index.ts`; then `grep -rn 'from "\.\./\.\./palettes/' demo/`.
defects.proposedCure: Introduce `demo/palettes/index.ts` as the real area seam (types, port injection keys, the browser components) and make it the only legal reach; `shell/dock` stops importing `palettes/usePalettePorts` entirely — ports are provided at the app root and INJECTED into the dock, restoring shell-below-feature direction.

defects.defect: The @mkbabb/value.js public surface is declared twice — a generated runtime alias set and a hand-written TS `paths` block — and the two have drifted, so the demo typechecks against a different copy of the library than it runs.
defects.evidence: package.json exports keys = ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize (7, no `.` root). tsconfig.demo.json:42-49 declares 8: `.`, /color, /parsing, /math, /easing, /units, /transform, /quantize. `ls src/subpaths` = color css easing math quantize transform value — no parsing.ts, no units.ts; same for dist/subpaths. `ls dist/index.d.ts` → "No such file or directory". /value and /css have NO paths entry. `npm ls @mkbabb/value.js` → installed transitively under @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 and @mkbabb/keyframes.js@6.0.0. `diff dist/subpaths/css.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` is NON-EMPTY (Alpha_2/Channel_2/SpaceId_2/ChannelsBySpace_2 present locally, absent in the installed copy; line 136 `[S in CssColorSpace]: Color_2<S>` vs `Color<S>`), while value.d.ts and color.d.ts are identical. Demo import tally: 24×/color, 10×/css, 6×/math, 5×/easing, 4×/quantize. Intent being violated: vite.config.ts:28-29 "GENERATED (not hand-rolled) so the alias set can never drift from the exports map".
defects.mechanism: one public surface, three declarations, only one of them generated — the hand-written type half drifted and then silently resolved to a transitively-installed published snapshot
defects.reproduction: `node -e 'console.log(Object.keys(require("./package.json").exports))'`; `ls src/subpaths dist/subpaths`; `ls dist/index.d.ts`; `npm ls @mkbabb/value.js`; `diff dist/subpaths/css.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts`.
defects.proposedCure: Generate the tsconfig.demo.json `paths` block from package.json#exports with the same code path vite.config.ts:41-50 already uses (one generator, one truth), so /parsing, /units and the phantom bare root cannot survive and /value + /css cannot go missing. Structurally the recurrence is impossible once the type map and the runtime map come from the same generator.

defects.defect: The `weights` prop is dead code and is a second input channel for data the component already receives on `colors[].weight`.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:34,38-44 declares and documents `weights?: number[]`. `$ grep -rn ':weights\|weights=' demo/ --include="*.vue"` → no output (zero of three call sites: PaletteCard.vue:33-37, GenerateControls.vue:135, MixSourceSelector.vue:203). Its own JSDoc concedes the duplication: "absent → the colors' own `weight` fields". The single weight producer in the tree is demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:88 (`weight: entry.source.population / total`), which writes the FIRST channel; demo/palettes/types.ts:5-11 declares the same single-channel law.
defects.mechanism: an escape hatch kept alive past the day the through-line was drawn — a dual path preserved as an unused prop
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn ':weights\|weights=' demo/ --include="*.vue"` returns nothing.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the prop and the branch at :54-59. There is one channel: `colors[].weight`. (Edict 2 — no dual paths.)

defects.defect: The strip's geometry is copy-pasted as a literal into two sibling components, so three (really four) files must be kept in agreement by hand with no token and no test.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:10 `'flex h-10 w-full'` and :9 `'flex flex-col w-10 h-full'`; PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:39 `<div class="flex h-10 w-full">` (comment: "Shadow color strip"); ShadowPalette.vue:51 `<div class="flex h-10 w-full gap-px">`. defects.defect: The documented "8% legibility floor" for weighted segments is not a floor — segments are clamped to WEIGHT_FLOOR and then divided by the clamped total, which pushes every floored segment back below 8%.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-48 (WEIGHT_FLOOR=0.08, doc "8% legibility floor"), :63-67 (clamp then `x / flooredTotal * 100`). LIVE MEASURED at http://localhost:9000/#/extract after uploading a synthesised 200x200 PNG with populations 0.96/0.01/0.01/0.01/0.01: {"stripW":458,"n":5,"pcts":["75%","6.25%","6.25%","6.25%","6.25%"],"px":[343.5,28.625,28.625,28.625,28.625]} — 28.625px where 8% of 458px is 36.64px. Pure-function simulation of :50-71 verbatim: n=5 one-dominant -> 75.000, 6.250 x4; n=8 -> 5.369 x7; n=16 -> 3.902 x15; n=20 -> 3.433 x19. k reaches 16 per demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:29 (:max="16").
defects.mechanism: Normalisation applied AFTER a clamp, undoing the clamp (broken-floor idiom).
defects.reproduction: node the segmentPcts body over [0.96,0.01,0.01,0.01,0.01]; or live: generate the fixture PNG (scratchpad/mkpng.mjs), drop it on /#/extract at localhost:9000, then read document.querySelector('div[aria-hidden="true"][role="presentation"]').children[i].style.width -> "6.25%".
defects.proposedCure: Water-fill instead of clamp-then-renormalise: sort ascending; while the smallest share is below floor, pin it to floor, remove it from the pool, and re-proportion the remainder over the residual mass (1 - pinned*floor). Exact, idempotent, terminates in <=n passes, and makes the arithmetically-impossible n>=13 case fail loudly instead of silently. If no real floor is wanted, delete WEIGHT_FLOOR and the prose — a documented invariant the code does not hold is worse than none.

defects.mechanism: The guard is placed in the computed rather than on the render, so the container renders regardless.

defects.defect: role="presentation" alongside aria-hidden="true" is redundant, and the sibling skeleton carries neither — so the family does not agree on whether a colour strip is decorative.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:4-5 carries both; a bare <div> has no implicit role so role="presentation" is a no-op, and aria-hidden already removes the subtree. PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:39 renders the same strip with neither attribute.
defects.mechanism: Two attributes for one intent, one of them inert — evidence neither was chosen deliberately.
defects.reproduction: Read PaletteColorStrip.vue:4-5 against PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:39.
defects.proposedCure: Keep aria-hidden="true", drop role="presentation", and apply the same decision to the skeleton under C-7's single-strip cure.

defects.defect: Index keys on a list that is user-reorderable.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:14-15 `v-for="(color, i) in colors" :key="i"`, while the host card supports dragging (PaletteCard.vue:44 GripVertical, draggable prop).
defects.mechanism: Index keys make a reorder patch every segment's inline style in place rather than moving nodes; forecloses any future TransitionGroup and repaints all n segments on any reorder.
defects.reproduction: NONE — functionally benign today, the segments hold no state. Labelled a hypothesis as to consequence.
defects.proposedCure: Key on color.css + i if the strip ever animates; moot under C-2's flex-share cure, which removes the per-segment inline style entirely.

defects.defect: The population story has no non-visual equivalent — the strip is the app's only rendering of the weight dimension and it is aria-hidden, so dominance is unavailable to assistive tech.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:4 aria-hidden="true" on the sole surface that expresses weight anywhere in the app; the host card's accessible name is `Palette: ${palette.name}` (PaletteCard.vue:23) plus a colour count (:73) — no share information. Hiding a decorative strip is right; hiding the app's only rendering of a data dimension is a data-loss decision that was never stated.
defects.mechanism: aria-hidden applied to a surface that is simultaneously decorative (colour swatches) and informational (population shares).
defects.reproduction: Read PaletteCard.vue:23,73 and PaletteColorStrip.vue:4 — there is no other consumer of PaletteColor.weight in demo/ (grep -rn "weight" demo/palettes/ returns only mix.ts, types.ts and the strip itself).
defects.proposedCure: When weights are present, append the dominant share to the card's aria-label (e.g. "..., 5 colors, dominant 75%"). The strip stays aria-hidden; the information does not disappear.

defects.defect: The strip is absent from the demo's own forced-colors color-display roster, so under Windows High Contrast a COLLAPSED palette card shows no color at all — while its sibling WatercolorDot specimen on the same plate survives. Combined with aria-hidden="true", the palette's content is simultaneously invisible and unreachable.
defects.evidence: Live selector match against the roster at demo/styles/foundation.css:679-696 → {stripMatchesForcedColorsRoster:false, segMatchesForcedColorsRoster:false, stripHasDataColorSurface:false, strip forcedColorAdjust:"auto"}. Sibling `.generate-swatch .watercolor-swatch` DOES match. foundation.css:655-657 states the policy intent verbatim: "the surfaces whose whole PURPOSE is to show a color — the actual content of a color tool — must survive WHCM's system-color substitution." PaletteColorStrip.vue:4 aria-hidden; PaletteCard.vue:139-140 shows PaletteCardSwatches is v-if="expanded", so the strip is the ONLY color surface on a collapsed card.
defects.mechanism: Unowned state — a named, authored policy register (the two-tier forced-colors roster) that the component never joined; the raw <div> falls through to forced-color-adjust:auto.
defects.reproduction: Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/browse with any palette; evaluate strip.matches('canvas,.spectrum-picker,.gamut-overlay,.atmosphere-canvas,[data-glass-field-canvas],.gradient-rail,.rail-handle,.readout-rail,.swatch-row > *,.generate-swatch,.shadow-swatch,.goo-blob-canvas,.watercolor-swatch,.glass-slider[data-variant="spectrum"] .slider-range,[data-color-surface]') → false. Note the tracked forced-colors-desktop matrix has only 5 routes and browse.png was captured in the commons-unreachable state, so this arm has NEVER been captured.
defects.proposedCure: Stamp `data-color-surface` on the strip root — the roster already ships that hook precisely for this case, so the component becomes a member of the existing register rather than a new selector appended to it. Do not grow the roster per component.

defects.defect: The 8% weight floor has no n-guard: it destroys the dominance story it exists to tell. At Extract's own max k=16 a 41%-dominant color draws 25.5%, and a 100%-dominant color can never draw wider than 45.45%. The weighted render is visually INDISTINGUISHABLE from the unweighted fallback. The `weights` prop that documents the mechanism has zero consumers — a dual path with a permanently dead arm.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-68 (WEIGHT_FLOOR=0.08, Math.max(w/total, 0.08) then renormalize). node re-run of that exact formula: floor binds for uniform palettes at n=13; n=16 dominant 0.41 → drawn 25.47%; max representable dominance for a 100% color: n=13 51.02%, n=16 45.45%, n=20 39.68%, n=50 20.33%. ExtractControls.vue:29 `:max="16"`; PALETTE-CONTRACT.md §3 allows 1–50 colors. Render probe rows 3 vs 4 (probe-states-4up.png) are indistinguishable. `grep -rn ':weights|weights=' demo/` (excluding mix.ts) → NO OUTPUT; only 3 call sites exist and none pass it. Sole weight producer: useExtractSession.ts:88.
defects.mechanism: Truth — a per-segment floor F costs F·(n−1) of a budget of 1, so past n≈13 the floor consumes the strip and every share renormalizes toward equal; no adaptation, no cap, no truncation arm.
defects.reproduction: Extract with k=16 from an image with one dominant region: the strip's dominant segment measures 25.5% of strip width while the pane's dominance stat reads 41%. Formula verification is deterministic: node -e with the code from :61-67 reproduces every number above without an image.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `weights` prop and its dead ternary (:38-44, :54-59) — the population story already travels on PaletteColor.weight per types.ts:3-10. Replace the constant floor with a budgeted one (F = min(0.08, β/n) with β named), or adopt the honest law the sibling PreviewStrip already reached — cap and truncate with a mask-faded tail that reads as "continues" (PreviewStrip.vue:15-22, STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP=7). A silently-flattened bar is worse than an admittedly-truncated one.

defects.defect: A zero-color palette renders a 40px void. The host declares this state reachable and even mints EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH for it, but routes that constant away from the one surface that shows swatches.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:50-51 returns [] for n===0; v-for emits no children; the root keeps `flex h-10 w-full overflow-hidden`. Live render probe row 1: {h:40, w:460, children:0} — see probe-states-4up.png. PaletteCard.vue:220-223: "a palette with zero colors is a real, reachable state (a freshly-created palette before any swatch). This neutral mid-gray is the designed empty-state swatch" — but EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH feeds only firstColor at :226 → safeFirstColor for ink contrast, never the strip. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 specifies the empty register (EmptyPaletteMark: three WatercolorDots plus dashes) which the empty LIBRARY renders (visible in safari-desktop-light/palettes.png as EMPTY PLATE) — the empty PALETTE got nothing.
defects.mechanism: Unowned state — the empty arm was never designed, so it falls through to a bare box that is indistinguishable from a rendering failure.
defects.reproduction: Any palette with colors: []. Measured live by rendering the component's own template semantics at its real 458px width: root box 40px tall, zero children, transparent.
defects.proposedCure: Give the empty arm the established dashed empty register at strip scale — the same dashed-outline vocabulary the "Start a new palette" row and EmptyPaletteMark already use — so an empty palette reads as an invitation, not a bug. Zero new primitives.

defects.defect: No segment boundary: n colors render as fewer than n visible bands, contradicting the count badge rendered inches away. The far smaller sibling PreviewStrip already carries the inset hairline this one lacks; the defect was filed in the N tranche and never closed.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:13-23 emits adjacent background-color fills with no border/gap/ring; measured live boxShadow:"none". Render probe row 2 (probe-states-4up.png): 5 colors (#3b6ea5/#3d70a7/#3f72a9/#c94f3d/#cb5140) render as TWO visible bands, while PaletteCard.vue:72-74 renders `<Badge>{{ palette.colors.length }}</Badge>` = 5. PreviewStrip.vue `.preview-chip` has `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 12%, transparent)`. Prior filing: docs/tranches/N/audit/lanes/C5.md:246 "[P1/F-4] Add a swatch-boundary hairline to PaletteColorStrip". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: "states are never color-only".
defects.mechanism: Truth/register non-membership — the strip encodes cardinality purely in color difference, and never joined the material register (inset hairline ring) its own sibling strip belongs to.
defects.reproduction: Render probe row 2, live at the strip's real 458px width with the component's real class string. Reproducible with any k-means-extracted palette whose adjacent clusters are within a few ΔE.
defects.proposedCure: Not per-segment borders (they would eat 1px×n of the proportional budget and re-break D2's arithmetic): one producer-owned inset hairline ring on the container plus an optical inset-shadow seam on segments, so geometry stays exactly proportional. Better: lift PreviewStrip's `.preview-chip` material into a shared glass-ui `Strip` primitive and make both strips postures of it (edict 4).

defects.defect: The corner/radius law lives in three different consumers instead of the component, and one of them (Mix) re-introduces the exact ancestor-clip rasterization artifact PaletteCard was rewritten to cure. The aside arm additionally uses a physical `rounded-l-card`, which lands on the wrong edge in RTL.
defects.evidence: Component root emits no radius (:6-11). Measured live class strings: PaletteCard/Generate → `overflow-hidden flex h-10 w-full rounded-t-card` with host overflow:visible; MixSourceSelector.vue:199-203 → strip has NO radius and the ancestor is `rounded-card border border-border/30 overflow-hidden`. PaletteCard.vue:16-18 states the law as a comment on the CONSUMER: "NO overflow-hidden (S.W5-10 / S-15-A): a card-level radius clip rasterizes 1-bit at compositing-layer bounds; the strip clips its OWN corners below". Tailwind v4: rounded-l-* is physical, rounded-s-* is logical.
defects.mechanism: No component law — a design rule written as a comment on one caller instead of as a property of the component, so it protects one consumer and not the others (owner edict 5: root-level styling, never per-instance overrides).
defects.reproduction: Read MixSourceSelector.vue:199-203 against PaletteCard.vue:16-18; live class strings measured on /#/generate and /#/browse confirm the three divergent strategies.
defects.proposedCure: Give the component a radius contract of its own — corner posture derived from `orientation` using LOGICAL border-start-start-radius/border-end-start-radius, resolved from one `--strip-radius` defaulting to the card radius token. Then delete all three per-instance classes and the Mix wrapper's overflow-hidden/rounded-card. One law, one owner, three call sites that stop knowing about corners.

defects.defect: The 40px cross-axis measure is a raw Tailwind literal, isotropic across both postures, and non-relational: the strip's share of its host swings 33.3% → 21.3% → ~13% across three live hosts at the same viewport, none of it chosen.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:9-10 `w-10 h-full` / `h-10 w-full` = 40px fixed. Live: /#/browse PaletteCard 462×120 with strip 458×40 → 33.3% of card height; /#/extract PaletteCard 462.4×187.7 with strip 458.4×40.0 → 21.3%; /#/generate plate ~300 tall → ~13%. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 fixes the card anchor C = --card-pad-inline = --spacing(4) = 16px; 40 = 2.5C, not a φ rung (φ·C=25.9, φ²·C=41.9). §3.7: "Spacing is container-scaled from glass-ui tokens." PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §1: "Every element earns its scale... from its job relative to the local protagonist." Contrast PreviewStrip: `inline-size: 2.618rem /* one golden plate — φ² × 1em (F7) */; block-size: 1em`.
defects.mechanism: No component law — one magic number serves as both a band thickness and a rail width, which is the absence of a proportion decision rather than a wrong one.
defects.reproduction: The three live getBoundingClientRect measurements above, all at 1600×1000 CSS px, DPR 1.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the cross-axis measure from the card anchor as one token expressed once — `--strip-thickness: calc(var(--card-pad-inline) * var(--ratio-phi))` (≈25.9px) or the next glass-ui golden rung — and give the vertical posture its own named rung instead of reusing the horizontal number. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.7 frees the strip from the tap-target floor since it is non-interactive.

defects.defect: The strip's corner radius equals the card's OUTER radius (16px) instead of the inner radius (14px = 16 − 2px border), so every palette card shows a ~0.8–1.5px light card-edge crescent at each top corner — the edge line reads as a wedge, thicker through the arc than at the straight runs.
defects.evidence: Live: card {borderRadius 16px, borderTopWidth 2px, overflow visible}; strip {borderRadius "16px 16px 0px 0px", inset from card {left:2, top:2}}. Predicted radial excess at 45°: √2×((18−16/√2)−(16−14/√2)) ≈ 0.83px. Pixel scan of the device-scale capture (card outer corner (835,632.7); card-edge (208,201,194); strip color (224,92,120)): straight left edge y=655 → 834 bg | 835 edge | 836 edge | 837 COLOR (2px of edge); 45° diagonal → k0-3 bg | k4 blend | k5 edge | k6 blend | k7 COLOR (color begins ≈3.1–3.5px radially in). 12× crops: probe-corner-tl-x12.png, probe-corner-tr-x12.png.
defects.mechanism: No component law — concentricity is coincidental rather than structural because the radius is hard-coded by the caller with no knowledge of the host's border width.
defects.reproduction: Device-scale capture of /#/browse; pixel sample the diagonal from (835,633) vs the horizontal scan at y=655. Crops included beside the report.
defects.proposedCure: Once the radius is a component contract (D5), it resolves once as calc(var(--card-radius) - var(--card-border-width)) and concentricity becomes structural.

defects.defect: Zero motion: the strip hard-cuts on every content change while its own sibling specimen on the same plate is in the motion register. The index key will attach any future transition to the wrong segment.
defects.evidence: Live computed on strip and segments: transitionDuration "0s" (transitionProperty "all" is the CSS initial value, not an author rule), animationName "none". Sibling on the same plate: `class="... active:scale-95 transition-transform ..."` (GenerateControls.vue, measured class string). PaletteColorStrip.vue:15 `:key="i"`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6: "Color/opacity effects use the corresponding short effect curve; exit is shorter than entry" and "A scene swap preserves the specimen". §5.2 makes palette-color reorder a first-class mechanism.
defects.mechanism: Register non-membership — the strip never joined the motion register, on the one surface where the product's core verbs (regenerate / extract / mix) are expressed.
defects.reproduction: Click Regenerate on http://localhost:9000/#/generate — five segment colors replace in one frame with zero interpolation while the five dots below are animated. Computed styles above.
defects.proposedCure: One tokenised color transition on the segment from the existing effect-curve register, PRM-collapsed to 0s via animations.css:32 — and key on color identity rather than index so the transition attaches to the right element. Nothing new is invented; every neighbour is already in the register.

defects.defect: RTL silently reverses the palette's ordinal order; the on-screen strip and the exported SVG then mirror each other with no cue and no announcement.
defects.evidence: Live on /#/browse, real 6-color card: LTR color #1 at x=837.0 (leftmost), last at x=1218.6; after setting dir=rtl, color #1 at x=686.7 (rightmost), last at x=305.0; reversed:true; strip has no dir attribute. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1: "palette/release order | preserve explicit ordinal identity" and "CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance | render in LTR-isolated spans". PALETTE-CONTRACT.md Appendix W51 §6 emits rect x="0..N-1" ascending, unconditionally LTR.
defects.mechanism: Unowned state — a plain flex row inherits document direction; the strip is ordinal data, not chrome, and was never isolated.
defects.reproduction: document.documentElement.dir = 'rtl' on /#/browse, then read each segment's getBoundingClientRect().x — first color moves from leftmost to rightmost.
defects.proposedCure: Carry dir="ltr" on the strip root so ordinal identity matches the export byte contract exactly — the same isolation the constitution already mandates for hex, slugs and provenance. The card layout around it still follows document direction; only the ordinal rail is isolated.

defects.defect: The strip is rendered inside the Generate composition, which the constitution enumerates without it and explicitly rules out; the plate shows the same five colors twice (flat strip + WatercolorDot row). MixSourceSelector repeats the pattern. Two competing strip species are imported into one file with no rule distinguishing them.

The generated palette is a draft specimen, not a flat strip plus unrelated buttons." GenerateControls.vue:135 renders PaletteColorStrip as the plate face; :196-200 renders the WatercolorDot row of the same colors. For fairness: the strip IS constitutionally authorised on Browse/Library cards per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.
defects.mechanism: Register non-membership — the ruled specimen species for these workbenches is WatercolorDot; the strip is the un-ruled hard-rect color species that never joined it.
defects.reproduction: visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png shows the 40px strip at the plate head and five identical-color WatercolorDots ~190px below it.
defects.proposedCure: Remove the strip from the Generate plate and the Mix source rows — the WatercolorDot row is the ruled specimen in both. Where a compact single-line preview is genuinely wanted, PreviewStrip already exists and is already imported.

defects.defect: Three small contrivances: a redundant role="presentation" alongside aria-hidden; a dead Math.max(100/n, 0.5) guard unreachable for every valid palette; and six lines of prop documentation for a facility with no caller.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:4-5 (aria-hidden="true" already removes the subtree, so the role has no effect); :70 Math.max(100/n, 0.5) — PALETTE-CONTRACT.md §3 caps a palette at 50 colors so 100/n ≥ 2 always; :38-43 the weights doc comment.
defects.mechanism: Contrivance — owner edict 3 (KISS) and edict 2 (no dead dual paths).
defects.reproduction: Static: the 0.5 arm requires n > 200, which the palette contract forbids; the role has no ARIA effect on an aria-hidden subtree.
defects.proposedCure: Delete all three. The weights comment goes with the prop when D2's cure lands; historical provenance belongs in the tranche ledger, not a prop doc.

result.strongestDefect: D2 — the 8% weight floor has no n-guard, so the strip renders a confident, precise, false picture of palette dominance: at Extract's own maximum k=16 a color that is 41% of the image draws at 25.47%, and a color that is 100% of the image can never draw wider than 45.45%; at n=50 the ceiling is 20.33%. The weighted render is visually indistinguishable from the unweighted fallback it was built to replace (probe rows 3 vs 4), and the `weights` prop documenting the whole mechanism has zero consumers. D1 is graded BLOCKER on impact (total color loss under WHCM on a collapsed card that is also aria-hidden), but D2 is the strongest DESIGN defect: it is the one place the component's single job — be a truthful picture of the palette — is arithmetically betrayed.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. For completeness, the areas that survived interrogation with positive evidence (so the negative claims are load-bearing): idiomatic Vue 3.5 — reactive props destructure with defaults at :31-45, computed derived geometry, no defineModel/shallowRef hazard (edict 7 PASS); verbatimModuleSyntax — `import type { PaletteColor }` at :29 (edict 8 PASS); no god module — 72 lines, one job, no store reach, no side effects (edict 1 PASS); no back-compat shim; and the percentage-width arithmetic sums cleanly — measured 6 × 76.33px = 457.98px against a 458px strip, a 0.02px shortfall with no visible tail gap, so the naive sub-pixel-gap worry is NOT a real defect.

defects.defect: The <Checkbox> binding uses the radix-vue-era `:checked` prop and `@update:checked` emit, neither of which exists on @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 Checkbox (props: modelValue/defaultValue/disabled/value/id/class/asChild/as/name/required; emits: ["update:modelValue"]) nor on reka-ui CheckboxRoot (emits: ["update:modelValue"]). The component therefore never reflects the palette's current tags and never fires its toggle handler — it is 100% non-functional. Identically replicated at SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55; those are the only 2 <Checkbox> usages in the demo, so the defect rate for this primitive is 2/2 = 100%. Compounding: `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0 with zero errors, because Vue treats undeclared props and unhandled listeners as legal attr-fallthrough — the repo's strictest gate is structurally blind to glass-ui component-API drift.

GATE: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → `VUE_TSC_EXIT=0`, zero diagnostics. AGE: `git log -S'update:checked'` → a1060e5b 2026-03-26; radix-vue→reka-ui migration 8dc5d31c 2026-02-24.

defects.proposedCure: Not a two-site rename. Extract the checkbox loop — today hand-copied between TagEditPopover.vue:22-34 and SearchFilterBar.vue:50-56 — into a single owned `demo/palettes/tags/TagChecklist.vue` (props {catalog: Tag[]; modelValue: string[]}, emits update:modelValue, zero inject/api/etag). That makes it THE ONLY <Checkbox> in the repo, so the API can only be wrong in one place, and that place gets a mount test asserting aria-checked tracks the model. Structural guarantee = encapsulation + one test, not a stricter tsconfig (proven impossible). Separately relay upstream: a checkbox LIST bound to a value set is a design-system primitive and belongs in glass-ui (edict 4).

defects.defect: The component publishes a `trigger` slot inside `<PopoverTrigger as-child>` (an anchored-popover API) but its sole consumer, BrowsePane.vue:148-155, uses it as a fully-controlled detached dialog and passes no trigger content. reka-ui's Slot returns only Comment nodes for an empty slot, so no element is produced, PopperAnchor never registers a node, and PopperContent's `reference` is undefined — leaving `isPositioned` permanently false and the content pinned at its pre-measure hiding transform `translate(0, -200%)`, i.e. 200% above the viewport top, in a real browser as well as jsdom. Secondary: `rootContext.triggerElement` stays undefined, so reka's focus-return-on-close has no element to return focus to. This is a two-mode public API shipping only the mode it does not support (edict 2 dual path).
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:3-5 (`<PopoverTrigger as-child><slot name="trigger" /></PopoverTrigger>`); demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:148-155 (no slot content); node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Primitive/Slot.js (`firstNonCommentChildrenIndex === -1` → returns comments, no element); node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Popover/PopoverTrigger.js (wraps in PopperAnchor as-child; `rootContext.triggerElement.value = triggerElement.value`); node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Popper/PopperContent.js:196 `const reference = computed(() => props.reference ?? rootContext.anchor.value)` and :238 `transform: unref(isPositioned) ? unref(floatingStyles).transform : "translate(0, -200%)"`. EXECUTED PROBE: `TRIGGER ELEMENTS (aria-haspopup=dialog): 0` / `CONTENT PRESENT: true` / `POPPER WRAPPER STYLE: position: fixed; left: 0px; top: 0px; transform: translate(0, -200%); min-width: max-content;` — and with the trigger slot filled on the same component: `TRIGGER ELEMENTS: 1`.
defects.mechanism: component publishes a dual-mode surface (anchored-with-trigger AND detached-controlled); the live mode is unsupported by the underlying primitive and the supported mode is dead code — the component owns a shell whose anchor it cannot supply

defects.defect: `paletteETag` is implemented twice — once in the API, once hand-mirrored in the demo — and the demo copy sits directly in this component's import path. The same duplication runs one level up: FormattedPalette and the demo's Palette are two hand-written descriptions of one wire object that already disagree (updatedAt Date vs string; currentHash string|null vs string|undefined; tags required vs optional; voteCount required vs optional). Nothing generates the client contract from the server contract.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:46,74; demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:167-179 (`/** … mirroring the API's paletteETag() (api/src/middleware/etag.ts) */`) vs api/src/modules/palette/etag.ts:23-26 (`p.currentHash ?? p.updatedAt.toISOString()`); `ls api/src/middleware/etag.ts` → no such file; api/src/modules/palette/format.ts:14-48 vs demo/palettes/types.ts:14-63; `ls api/src/meta/` → empty, `grep -n openapi package.json api/package.json` → no matches. defects.reproduction: NONE (structural; both implementations quoted at file:line, the stale path verified absent, the absence of any generator verified by ls + grep).
defects.proposedCure: One home for the wire shape and its derived validators. Either generate the demo's `Palette` + `paletteETag` from the API module (api/src/meta/route-table.ts already exists as the mounted-route source of truth and the generated OpenAPI derives from it), or extract a tiny shared contract module consumed by both sides. defects.defect: A leaf presentational popover owns optimistic-concurrency policy: it derives the If-Match validator itself (a job useBrowsePalettes already does at :164/:192 because it owns the list), silently downgrades a lookup miss to RFC 7232 match-any via `undefined` → `saveTags(…, ifMatch = "*")`, emits the optimistic update BEFORE awaiting the save, and discards the PATCH response that carries the fresh validator. BrowsePane then re-caches the stale one by writing `{...target, tags}` back into remotePalettes. saveTags swallows every failure in `catch { console.warn }`, so a rejected write leaves the UI showing the new tags.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:73-77 (`const ifMatch = source ? paletteETag(source) : undefined;` … `emit("update:tags", updated); await tagEdit.saveTags(paletteSlug, updated, ifMatch);` — return value discarded); demo/palettes/useTagEdit.ts:51-55 (`ifMatch = "*"` default) and :64-67 (`catch (e) { console.warn(...); return undefined; }`); api/src/modules/palette/etag.ts:44 (`if (ifMatch.trim() === "*") return;` — the concurrency check is skipped); demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:164,192 (the same derivation, in its correct home); demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:312-320 (re-caches the stale updatedAt); api/src/modules/palette/service/crud.ts:178-193 (`$set = { updatedAt: new Date() }` always; currentHash bumped only when computeContentHash(name,colors) changes — never for a tags-only patch); api/src/modules/palette/etag.ts:5-7 (ETag falls back to updatedAt 'when currentHash is null, e.g. pre-version palette'); api/src/modules/palette/routes/crud.ts:139-142 (server returns the fresh ETag header nobody reads).
defects.mechanism: HTTP concurrency policy owned by a leaf UI component instead of the composable that owns the resource; a masking fallback (undefined→"*") disables the guarantee the surrounding comment claims to establish; the write's response — the only source of the next valid validator — is thrown away
defects.reproduction: Defects 1-4 (wrong home; silent "*" downgrade; discarded response; stale re-cache) are each CONFIRMED at file:line above. The end-to-end lost-update consequence is a HYPOTHESIS: it requires a row with currentHash === null so the ETag tracks updatedAt and flips on every tags PATCH, making the second toggle in one popover session 412 and be swallowed. createPalette (api/src/modules/palette/service/crud.ts:101-102) always sets currentHash, so the arm is reachable only on legacy pre-version rows; the local commons was unreachable (API down) so I could not seed it. Labelled a hypothesis; must not be reported as observed.
defects.proposedCure: The component should own none of this. Replace saveTags with `useTagAssignment.assign(palette: Palette, tags: string[]): Promise<Palette>` — derives the validator from the palette it is HANDED (no undefined, no "*" default, no global-list lookup), CONSUMES the returned palette, and republishes it into the browse list so the next validator is fresh. Delete the catch-and-warn: a failed save must surface and the optimistic emit must roll back. The popover then emits one intent (toggle(tagName)) and knows nothing about HTTP.

defects.defect: `getTags(): Promise<Tag[]>` is a type-lie the codebase has already discovered, and the compensating coercion lives at ONE of its TWO consumers. BrowsePane wraps allTags in an Array.isArray coercion with a comment explaining the object-shaped payload; TagEditPopover reads the same ref raw, so on an object payload `.length` is undefined, `undefined === 0` is false, the 'No tags available.' branch is dead, and the popover renders an unexplained empty box. Same family: the load lifecycle is triply called for one idempotent concern.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/api/colors.ts:14 (`export function getTags(): Promise<Tag[]>`); demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:210-220 — '// X9: coerce to an Array. `allTags` is typed `Tag[]` but the `/colors/tags` read can resolve an object-shaped payload … This computed guarantees an array.' with `return Array.isArray(tags) ? tags : Object.values(tags);`; demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:16 (`v-else-if="tagEdit.allTags.value.length === 0"`) and :23 (`v-for="tag in tagEdit.allTags.value"`) — no coercion. Load lifecycle: BrowsePane.vue:222-224 (onMounted loadAllTags) + TagEditPopover.vue:80-82 (watch) + :84-86 (onMounted) for one idempotent call guarded by useTagEdit.ts:37 (`if (loaded.value && !force) return;`).
defects.mechanism: producer/consumer inversion — a normalisation every reader must apply is written at one reader instead of at the single shared producer (useTagEdit.loadAllTags), so the guard is present or absent by accident of which file was touched last
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural; the asymmetry is proven at file:line — one consumer guards, the other does not — and the dead-branch arithmetic (`undefined === 0` is false) is total. Whether the object payload actually occurs on the wire I did not confirm, because either resolution yields a finding: the child is missing a needed guard, or the parent carries a contrivance to delete per edict 3.)
defects.proposedCure: Normalise once, in the producer: make demo/palettes/tags/api.ts `getTags()` total (return Object.values(payload) when it is not an array) so no consumer ever coerces again, and delete BrowsePane's availableTags computed. Fold the three load call sites into a single provided useTagCatalog with one idempotent load; replace the component's watch+onMounted pair with `watch(..., { immediate: true })` if a per-open refresh is still wanted.

result.strongestDefect: C-1 — every tag checkbox is bound to `:checked` / `@update:checked`, a prop/event pair that `@mkbabb/glass-ui@7`'s `Checkbox` does not declare (it declares `modelValue` / `update:modelValue`). Measured in real Chromium against the real component: applied tags render UNCHECKED (`checked="true"` leaks onto the `<button role="checkbox">` as a bogus DOM attribute while `aria-checked="false"` / `data-state="unchecked"`), and a click yields `emitted: []` with `saveTagsCalls: 0` while the tick visually appears (reka's uncontrolled internal state). `onToggle` — including the whole W5-13·F-9 captured-ETag block at lines 69-74 — is unreachable code. defects.defect: Optimistic `update:tags` emit with no rollback, over a `saveTags` that swallows every failure and returns undefined — which the caller discards. A failed save leaves the UI showing the tag applied while the server never received it, with no error surface anywhere.
defects.evidence: TagEditPopover.vue:76-77 (`emit("update:tags", updated); await tagEdit.saveTags(paletteSlug, updated, ifMatch);` — return discarded). demo/palettes/useTagEdit.ts:60-64 (`catch (e) { console.warn("Failed to update tags:", e); return undefined; }`). demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:312-320 writes the emitted tags into `pm.remotePalettes` and `tagEditPalette` synchronously on the emit.
defects.mechanism: two sources of truth for one row: an optimistic local guess is kept and the authoritative response is dropped, with the only failure channel being console.warn.
defects.reproduction: NONE — LATENT. Unreachable today because C-1 makes `onToggle` unreachable; it goes live the instant C-1 is cured. Labelled a hypothesis with a proven mechanism, not a measured failure.
defects.proposedCure: `saveTags` already returns the authoritative `Palette`. Await it and emit/fold the RETURNED palette; on `undefined`, surface the failure in the panel and leave the checkbox where it was. Better: move the whole read-modify-write into `useTagEdit` (which already owns the catalog and the commit) so the component emits an intent and never owns an optimistic copy.

defects.defect: The PATCH response is discarded, so the locally-held If-Match validator goes stale after every tag save. On a palette whose `currentHash` is null, the second tag toggle in a session sends a stale validator and is rejected 412 — then swallowed by C-3. Silent lost update.
defects.evidence: TagEditPopover.vue:69-77 captures `paletteETag(source)` from `pm.remotePalettes` and never folds the response back. demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:172-178 — `paletteETag = currentHash ?? updatedAt`. api/src/modules/palette/service/crud.ts:178 — `const $set = { updatedAt: new Date() }` on EVERY patch; crud.ts:188-194 — `currentHash` changes only when name/colors change, which a tags-only patch never does. api/src/modules/palette/etag.ts:5-7 documents the null-currentHash case as real; etag.ts:44-49 throws PreconditionFailedError (412) on mismatch.
defects.mechanism: two sources of truth for one row (same family as C-3): the optimistic guess is retained, the authoritative fresh `updatedAt` is thrown away, so every subsequent If-Match-guarded verb reading from `pm.remotePalettes` (rename / publish / unpublish, all of which take `paletteETag(palette)`) inherits a stale validator.
defects.reproduction: NONE — LATENT, blocked behind C-1. Mechanism proven by source. Would reproduce as: toggle two tags in a row on a pre-version palette (currentHash null) -> the second PATCH 412s and is silently dropped.
defects.proposedCure: Fold the returned `Palette` back into `pm.remotePalettes` in one write, replacing the optimistic guess. Delete the guess entirely — the response is the truth.

defects.defect: An object-shaped `/colors/tags` payload renders an EMPTY popover: `.length === 0` is false for an object, so the "No tags available." empty state is skipped and the `v-for` yields zero rows. The user sees a bare "Tags" heading over blank space.
defects.evidence: TagEditPopover.vue:16 (`v-else-if="tagEdit.allTags.value.length === 0"`). The sibling consumer of the SAME `pm.tagEdit.allTags` documents the hazard and defends: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:211-219 (`X9: coerce to an Array. ... the /colors/tags read can resolve an object-shaped payload`; `Array.isArray(tags) ? tags : Object.values(tags)`). Real-Chromium measurement (probeEdges()): with `allTags = ref({})` -> `{objectPayload: {renderedText: "Tags", showsEmptyState: false}}`.
defects.mechanism: defensive coercion in the wrong layer: the port returns an untrusted shape and each consumer guards (or doesn't) on its own — one consumer defends, the other doesn't, and that split IS the drift.
defects.reproduction: In a page on http://localhost:9000 : `(await import('.../probes/live-mount.ts')).probeEdges()` -> objectPayload.renderedText === "Tags", objectPayload.showsEmptyState === false.
defects.proposedCure: Coerce ONCE, in `useTagEdit` where the read lives — not per consumer. Best of all, make `getTags()` return `Tag[]` or throw, so no consumer needs a guard at all; a per-consumer `Array.isArray` fallback is exactly the masking fallback the standing edicts forbid.

result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but four negatives were proven and are recorded so a seventh seat does not born-RED them. result.strongestDefect: D5-01 — under `forced-colors: active` the colour commons shows no colours. `PaletteColorStrip` (the wall's specimen) is absent from `demo/styles/foundation.css`'s named colour-surface roster, so WHCM substitutes system colours into it and a 5-colour palette renders `stripDistinctBg: ["rgb(255,255,255)"]` — five identical white bands. Every decorative colour surface on the same page IS on the roster and keeps full saturation: the aurora ground, the empty plate's ghost trio, and the *duplicate* copy of the same swatches inside the expanded card, which renders `rgb(229,83,61)` for the very colour the wall above paints white. The roster's own header states its purpose (foundation.css:653-657): "the surfaces whose whole PURPOSE is to show a color — the actual content of a color tool — must survive WHCM's system-color substitution." The one surface that fails the policy is the content of the commons. Same roster is reused by `@media print` (foundation.css:830-841), so the specimen gets `printColorAdjust: "economy"` while decoration gets `"exact"` — the wall does not print, against foundation.css:793's declaration that "the palette IS a printable artifact".
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but six negatives were banked and are load-bearing for scope. (1) BrowsePane's own motion is sound: `<Transition name="vj-morph">` (:40) keys a sanctioned family defined centrally in demo/styles/animations.css:104-139 on `--duration-fast`/`--spring-snappy` (edict 6 satisfied), and the global guard at animations.css:184-193 (`transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on `*`) neutralises it under PRM. (2) It forces no layout: `vj-morph` can transition `max-height` via `--vj-morph-collapse`/`--vj-morph-expanded`, but BrowsePane sets neither, so both resolve `none` and `none→none` is not animatable — only opacity/transform animate. This also supplies the mechanism for pass 4's D4-06: the blunt guard caps `animation-duration`/`transition-duration` and structurally cannot reach PaneHeader's `animation-timeline: scroll()` motion, which is progress-driven not time-driven. defects.defect: Keyboard-activating the pagination trigger destroys focus and announces nothing. `More from the commons` sits in a `v-else-if` whose `v-if` sibling is the loading-skeleton block; when the request resolves faster than the branch swap settles, Vue re-creates the subtree as a NEW element and focus falls to `<body>`. The designed pagination skeleton never renders at all, and the newly-arrived cards are never announced.
defects.evidence: probe/p5-D-geometry.mjs arm B, Chromium, Enter on focused trigger. before: `{active:"BUTTON", activeName:"More from the commons", isBody:false, cards:3, trigger:1, loadingBlock:0, statusRegions:1}`. t+30/60/120/300/900/2500ms: `{active:"BODY", isBody:true, cards:6, trigger:1, loadingBlock:0, statusRegions:1}`. Three facts: focus BUTTON→BODY within 30ms, never recovers; `trigger:1` throughout (node replaced, not removed — so a `:disabled` patch would not fix it); `loadingBlock:0` at every frame (BrowsePane.vue:125-131's two `variant="developing"` skeletons never rendered once). `statusRegions:1` before and after, and the one region is My Palettes' own EmptyState.vue:28 `role="status"` — 3 palettes arrived on Browse with no announcement. Source: BrowsePane.vue:125-144. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 ("Request-bound skeletons exist only while real work is in flight") satisfied vacuously; §4.1 ("Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit").
defects.mechanism: Branch-swap identity loss: two mutually exclusive `v-if`/`v-else-if` siblings mean the trigger's DOM node cannot survive the loading transition, so focus has nowhere to persist. Compounded by the absence of any status region on the wall.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/p5-D-geometry.mjs`. Manually: Tab to `More from the commons`, press Enter, press Tab — next focus lands on the first control in the document, not the next control after the trigger.
defects.proposedCure: Pagination that replaces its own trigger must either keep the trigger's node identity stable across the loading swap (render one element and drive its busy state, rather than two exclusive branches), or move focus deliberately to the first newly-arrived card. Pair with the polite status region pass 2 D-20 already asked for so '3 more palettes' is announced instead of silently appended. The `loadingBlock:0` result also says the skeleton branch is dead weight on any fast responder — it should be latency-gated or deleted, not kept as an unreachable state.

defects.defect: The entity card's cartoon caster is clipped on its offset axis. PaletteCard adopts the producer `cartoon-surface` register — a three-layer caster offset to the lower-left (-3/-5/-7px X, +3/+5/+7px Y) — and explicitly declines `overflow-hidden` to protect it; PaletteCardGrid then sets `contain: content` and the card fills that box exactly, so the horizontal leg is deleted for every card and the last card loses both legs.
defects.evidence: probe/p5-D-clip.mjs, Chromium 1440x900, deviceScaleFactor 1. Geometry: `gridContain:"content"`; `cardBoxShadow: oklab(…/0.32) -3px 3px 0 0, oklab(…/0.26) -5px 5px 0 0, oklab(…/0.18) -7px 7px 0 0`; grid `{x:224,w:462}`, card0 `{x:224,w:462}` → `slackLeft=0.00`, `slackRight=0.00`; grid padding-box bottom 598.7 == last card bottom 598.7 → last-card bottom slack `0.00` against a 7px extent. Controlled two-sample pixel measurement, same frame/card/shadow: LEFT axis dx=-1,-2,-4,-6,-8,-12 all `rgb(244,183,213)` lum 198.1, identical to `paneGround` (14px left of grid) lum 198.1 → Δluminance 0.0 across 12px. BOTTOM gutter (12px gap-3, room inside the padding box) dy=+1,+3,+5,+7,+10 → lum 106.7, 139.3, 173.6, 203.5, 203.5 → Δluminance 96.8 over 7px, the three-layer caster resolving over its exact 3/5/7px steps. Source: PaletteCard.vue:9-19 (the 10-line comment declining overflow-hidden), PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 ("not cartoon casters stacked within casters"), §3 law 8.
defects.mechanism: Ancestor paint containment vs descendant offset register — two independently correct decisions in two files that cannot see each other. `contain: paint` clips descendant paint to the padding box (CSS Containment), and the plate is flush against that boundary on the axis its shadow is offset along.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/p5-D-clip.mjs` — writes evidence/D-p5-clip.json and D-p5-clip-wall.png.
defects.proposedCure: Not 'delete contain' — the containment is a real perf intent. Choose one: either the grid drops to `contain: layout style` (keeping layout isolation, losing the clip), or the card's register becomes a symmetric/inset caster that lives inside its own border box. `cartoon-surface` at PaletteCard.vue:19 and `contain: content` at PaletteCardGrid.vue:51 are two decisions that cannot both be right, and the current wall proves it by rendering two different shadow treatments on the same list (cards 1..n-1 keep a bottom rule, card n has nothing).

result.strongestDefect: LP5-1 — the published `@mkbabb/value.js` surface cannot write a hex colour. `serializeCssColor` (src/css/grammar.ts:289-311) emits 8 notations and has no hex arm and no options parameter; `grep -rn "toString(16)" src/` returns ZERO hits. The library PARSES `#4488cc` (measured) and holds the correct bytes (`toRgba8` → [68,136,204,255]) but stops one line short of the notation its own parser accepts. Consequence: five downstream hex writers exist, four of them different, INCLUDING glass-ui's own `oklchStopToHex` — i.e. the design system carries a colour-library capability because the colour library declined to publish it, which is the wrong direction along the inv-K-1 edge. This is the ROOT of the confirmed MiniColorPicker HSV fork (pass 1 L-6 / pass 2 LP2-4): the cure those passes prescribe ("delete both conversions, route through the library") is currently NOT WRITABLE — compose it and the last hop lands on `pickerColorToHex`, a demo module. Four prior CHALLENGE-L passes measured the fork's consequences (12–27% HSV divergence) without naming the missing export; `serializeCssColor` appears in zero of them.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this records only the negatives I proved rather than asserted (report §8): (1) edict-8 verbatimModuleSyntax is CLEAN — the subject's single type-only import is correct (`SearchFilterBar.vue:144 import type { Tag }`), MiniColorPicker has none; (2) NO deep-`src/` reach — the whole chain speaks only `@mkbabb/value.js/color` and `/css`, both real `exports` keys, so a real consumer could write every specifier (the T.W1 dogfood keystone holds; the public-surface defect is omission, not boundary violation); (3) NO dual value.js instance — glass-ui's dist imports value.js only by subpath, never the bare root, and the Vite self-alias set is generated from the same exports map, so one build serves both; (4) `.section-label` and `.scrollbar-thin` ARE consumed correctly from glass-ui, which sharpens LP5-3 (the component knows how to consume published utilities and declined to for the one carrying the focus ring); (5) named suspects `ActionBarLayer`/`useLayerTransition` and the three `useDark` stores are confirmed out of this chain; (6) the visual-audit matrix cannot see this component at all — `/#/browse` is captured with the popover closed in all 4 matrices, `overflowX 0`, `pageErrors 0`, and its 4 smallTapTargets all belong to PaletteSlugBar and the glass SearchBar.

defects.defect: NEW — the published library surface has no hex writer. `serializeCssColor` emits rgb/hsl/hwb/lab/lch/oklab/oklch/color() and omits hex; it takes no options argument, so there is no call-site seam either. The library parses hex and cannot print it. Five consumers wrote the missing line themselves, four of them differently, including glass-ui (a downstream package) which carries `oklchStopToHex` 'through value.js toRgba8'.
defects.evidence: src/css/grammar.ts:289-311 (the complete switch — no hex arm). `grep -rn "toString(16)" src/` → exit=1, ZERO hits. Measured: `node --input-type=module` against dist/ — serializeCssColor(convertColor(hsv(210,0.6666666666666669,0.8),'rgb')) → {"ok":true,"value":"rgb(68 136 204)"}; toRgba8 → [68,136,204,255]; parseCssColor('#4488cc') → ok, channels [68,136,204]. `grep -rn 'padStart(2, "0")' demo/ src/` → demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:215, demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue:103, demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useImageSampler.ts:33, demo/palettes/export/bytes.ts:31 (digest, correctly separate). node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/color/index.d.ts: `/** OKLCh stop → #rrggbb gamma hex through value.js toRgba8. */ export declare function oklchStopToHex(s: OklchStop): string;`
defects.mechanism: missing public surface — the published exports map stops one operation short of the notation its own parser accepts, so the capability is forced downstream and re-implemented per consumer; along the inv-K-1 edge the capability now lives on the CONSUMER side (glass-ui) rather than the producer (value.js)
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && grep -rn "toString(16)" src/ ; echo exit=$?   # → exit=1, zero hits. Then read src/css/grammar.ts:289-311: the switch has no hex case and the signature has no options parameter. Then: node -e "const p=require('./package.json');console.log(Object.keys(p.exports).join(' '))" → ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize — no hex writer in any of them.
defects.proposedCure: Publish the writer from the library beside its parser: `serializeCssColor(color, options?: { readonly format?: "functional" | "hex" }): Result<string, ColorIssue>`, hex arm routed through the existing toRgba8(color,{gamut:"clip"}) so gamut AND rounding policy are decided ONCE inside the failure-explicit boundary and returned as a Result like everything else. Then delete, in order: picker-color.ts:213 pickerColorToHex → one library call; MiniColorPicker.vue:85-105 and :110-125 (pass 1's L-6 cure becomes writable for the first time); useImageSampler.ts:33; glass-ui's oklchStopToHex → one library call, returning the capability to the producer side of the inv-K-1 edge (relay to the glass-ui BH inbox per the standing invariant). Pass 2's LP2-3 toRgba8 asymmetry then becomes a single-site fix.

result.strongestDefect: D-26 — `PaletteSlugBar.vue:19,:31` pass `variant="ghost"` to glass-ui `Button`, but glass-ui 7.0.0 has no `variant` axis at all (`grep -c variant node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js` → 0); the axis is `emphasis`, default `"secondary"`. The two edit-mode controls the design drew as ghosts render as filled secondary buttons, and `variant="ghost"` leaks to the DOM as a junk attribute. The producer's `loading` prop is also declined for four hand-rolled parts. This is the first finding across five runs that identifies the file as written against a producer API that no longer exists after the W44 glass-7 adoption — and it escapes the orphan: `ProfileSection.vue:60` carries the same dead `variant="outline"` and ships today.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative proof of soundness is owed. Recorded instead are the suspicions I measured and KILLED, which bound the finding set: (1) "the `mode=out-in` swap jumps because `min-h-9` under-reserves the form" — FALSE: the live `div.input-bar.search-seated` on the My Palettes pane measures exactly 36.0px against a 36.0px floor, and the Login pill measures 33.0px; both fit. The jump run-4 found comes from the pill arm wrapping to 45.28px, not the form arm, so a cure aimed at the form would miss. This refines run-4 D-24 from "magic number" to "a reservation fitted to whichever arm the author had on screen." (2) "`verbatimModuleSyntax` is violated" — FALSE: lines 131-145 import only values; there is no type-only import in the file to mis-declare, and `InstanceType<typeof SearchBar>` at :166 correctly relies on the value import. Edict 8 clean. (3) Genuinely well-made and named as such: `normalizeTokenInput` (:188-196) is a small pure function that correctly anticipates a real `ADMIN_TOKEN="..."` paste shape; reactive props destructure at :147 is the Vue 3.5 idiom; the three W5-a11y `aria-label`s (:24, :35, :84) plus `:aria-expanded`/`aria-haspopup` on the menu trigger satisfy PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-16's `…` clause; the `<Transition name="vj-morph">` is the correct family (animations.css:70-74 names "slug bar" explicitly) and is neutralised by the global reduced-motion guard at animations.css:184-192; the file is 243 lines and is not a god module (edict 1 clean).

The axis is `emphasis`, which defaults to "secondary", so both slug-edit controls render as FILLED secondary buttons where the design drew quiet ghosts, and `variant="ghost"` falls through $attrs onto the DOM as a junk attribute. The producer's `loading` prop is declined in favour of four hand-rolled parts (:23 :disabled, :24 aria-label swap, :26 Loader2, animate-spin).
